**Tuk**: Nobody pushed anybody. Hooray!  
**Elder Maud**: Hollins sleep on the left.  
**Chief Brack**: Drays sleep on the left of the left!  
**Nalu**: That’s the same place, silly. You’re all together.  

#### `q48-story`

_Night. Everyone sits by the campfire._  
_Two children reach for the last dumpling._  
_Grab! Pull! Oh no, a food fight!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, 1.G.A.3, ask): halves: one thing into two equal parts  
> **Nalu**: Oh dear. One dumpling, two children.  
> **Nalu**: How could they both have some?  
> - ✅ Cut it in half → Yes! Two halves. One for each. (Draw a circle in the air. Cut it down the middle.)
> - Throw it → Then nobody gets any! Cut it in half. Two halves, one each.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that cutting one thing into two equal halves lets two people share._

**Elder Maud**: Your great-great-grandpa took our ball!  
**Chief Brack**: Your great-great-grandma kicked it in the river!  
**Pemba**: Wait! I know a story about them!  
**Pemba**: They were twins! They played ball together.  
**Pemba**: They laughed so hard, the canyon cracked open!  
_Pemba looks at you. Don’t laugh! Keep a straight face!_  

**Choices**

- **Add: “They both sang badly!”**
    - **Chief Brack**: Drays sing badly!
    - **Elder Maud**: So do Hollins!
- **Nod slowly**
    - You nod. You don’t laugh. Well done!
- **Cough to hide a giggle**
    - Cough, cough! Pemba coughs too. Phew!

#### `q48-story-done`

**Elder Maud**: Twins! All this time.  
**Chief Brack**: Pass the dumplings, cousin.  
**Nalu**: (whispering) Pemba, that story isn’t true.  
**Pemba**: (whispering) But look. They’re sharing a blanket.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): real or make-believe  
> **Nalu**: Can laughing really crack a canyon?  
> - ✅ No, that’s pretend → Right. It’s a make-believe story. Make-believe is fun. It’s good to say so.
> - Yes → Laughing is fun. But it can’t crack rock. That part is make-believe.
> _For grown-ups: Your child told the difference between something real and something make-believe._


**Choices**

- **Tell them it was pretend**
    - **Elder Maud**: We guessed! But it’s a lovely story.
    - **Chief Brack**: We’ll keep it anyway.
- **Keep Pemba’s secret**
    - **Nalu**: Okay. But you’ll tell them one day, Pemba.
    - **Pemba**: I promise. After the dumplings.

#### `q48-complete`

_In the morning, both groups climb out together._  
_They talk and laugh. Which twin was taller?_  
**Pemba**: Look! They’re sharing socks now!  
_Chief Brack wears socks. He looks surprised. He likes them._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): making up after a fight  
> **Nalu**: The groups were cross. Now they are friends.  
> **Nalu**: How can we make up after a fight?  
> - ✅ Say sorry and share → Yes! Sorry, then share. Like the socks!
> - Stay cross forever → Staying cross feels heavy. Saying sorry and sharing feels better.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about ways to make up after falling out._

**Elder Maud**: Thank you, guide. Here is a hat for you.  
**Elder Maud**: And we’ll build a bridge. No more fighting!  
_By night, a rope bridge swings over the canyon._  

## Q49. The Secret Dance Party

- `q49-s1`: Give out 5 secret party notes. Don’t get caught! · _Wait until the headmaster looks at the board._
- `q49-s2`: Keep the party going! Tap on the beat. · _Tap when the drum ring closes. Stomp, clap, stomp, clap!_

#### `q49-school`

_Ding, ding! The school bell rings._  
_The children sit very still. Nobody smiles._  
**Kaito**: I came to this school once. The rules are the same.  
**Kaito**: No running. No humming. No being too happy.  
_A new boy comes in. He has a red headband._  
**Pemba**: Hi! I’m new! I’m, um, Kuzo!  
**The Headmaster**: In this school, we do not dance. We do not sing.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): good rules keep us safe  
> **Kaito**: Some rules help us. Which rule helps?  
> - ✅ “Walk inside, so nobody trips.” → Yes. That rule keeps us safe.
> - “Never, ever smile.” → That rule doesn’t help anyone. Good rules keep us safe and kind.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about why we have rules and what makes a good one._

**Rin**: (whispering) What is dancing?  
**Pemba**: Oh! Then we will have a party!  

**Choices**

- **Hide notes in lunch boxes**
    - **Kaito**: Sneaky! I like it. Am I allowed to like it?
- **Fold paper birds**
    - The paper birds fly over the headmaster. Swoosh!
- **Kaito can hand them out**
    - **Kaito**: Hi. Party. Cave. Tonight. Shh. Bye.
    - Everybody says yes!

#### `q49-school-done`

_You pass the notes out, one at a time._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count to 5  
> **Pemba**: Five notes for five friends. Count with me!  
> _(Count on one hand together.)_  
> **Pemba**: One, two, three, four, five!  
> Check: `edu:count:invites:5`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted five party notes on one hand._

**Rin**: A party in a cave? At night?  
**Pemba**: Yes! Bring your dancing feet!  
_The headmaster turns round. Everyone sits very still._  

#### `q49-party`

_The cave is full of children. They stand by the walls._  
_Your Nubbins bang on buckets. Bang! Bang! Bang!_  
**Pemba**: Dancing is easy. Feel the beat!  
**Rin**: My feet feel shy.  
**Kaito**: I don’t dance. I don’t think I can.  
**Pemba**: Everyone can dance. Watch the Nubbins!  
_The Nubbins stomp and clap. The children copy them._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): keep a beat and copy a pattern  
> **Pemba**: Copy the Nubbins: stomp, clap, stomp, clap!  
> _(Stomp and clap together. Keep the beat.)_  
> **Pemba**: What comes next? Stomp!  
> Check: `edu:clap:pattern:stomp-clap`
> _For grown-ups: Your child kept a steady beat and continued a stomp-clap pattern._

**Kaito**: Am I doing it? I think I’m doing it!  

#### `q49-party-done`

_Then the headmaster bursts in with a lantern._  
**The Headmaster**: WHAT is going on here?  
_The buckets stop. Everyone freezes._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): reading feelings on faces  
> _Look at the children’s faces. How do they feel?_  
> _(Wait for an answer.)_  
> - ✅ Worried → Yes. They are worried. Their eyes are wide.
> - Sleepy → Their eyes are wide open. Not sleepy! They feel worried. That’s okay to feel.
> _For grown-ups: Your child read other people’s faces to name a feeling._

_Kaito slowly puts his arms down._  

**Choices**

- **Everyone dance in front of Pemba**
    - Everyone dances at once. Pemba slips out the back.
- **Let Kaito speak**
    - **Kaito**: Sir, I followed every rule here. I was sad.
    - **Kaito**: Rules should help us. Not stop us being us.
    - **The Headmaster**: Hmm. Ten more minutes. Then home.
    - His foot taps along. Tap, tap. Pemba slips out.
- **Ask the headmaster to dance**
    - **The Headmaster**: I will not!
    - But his shoulders wiggle, just a bit. Pemba slips out.

_Outside, under the stars, the children laugh and laugh._  
**Rin**: We danced! We really danced!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): moving makes your heart beat faster  
> **Pemba**: Put your hand on your chest.  
> **Pemba**: Feel that thump-thump? That’s your heart.  
> **Pemba**: Dancing makes it beat faster. Moving keeps it strong!  
> _For grown-ups: Your child felt their heartbeat and heard that moving our bodies keeps our hearts strong._

**Pemba**: You were amazing. All of you!  
**Pemba**: You danced like shooting stars!  
**Kaito**: I don’t know what that means. But thank you.

## Q50. Uncle Tenzo’s Tea Stall

- `q50-s1`: Make 3 perfect cups of tea. · _Lift the kettle when the steam curls. Count slowly while the leaves soak._
- `q50-s2`: Give Mr Pell a cup of tea. · _Watch his face. A grumble means too hot. A sigh means just right._

#### `q50-open`

_A little tea stall stands by the pond. The kettle sings._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Welcome, Keeper! I used to be a general. Now I make tea.  
**Kaito**: He got up at four o’clock. He painted the sign twice.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Good tea is easy. Hot water. Then wait.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Not too short. Not too long. Just right.  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, do): count slowly to 5 to time something  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: The leaves are in. Now we wait and count.  
> _(Count slowly together, one to five.)_  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: One… two… three… four… five. Ready!  
> Check: `edu:count:steep:5`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted slowly to five to time the tea._

_Your Nubbin sniffs the tea tins. Sniff, sniff. Achoo!_  

**Choices**

- **Make jasmine tea first**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Lovely! Jasmine smells like flowers.
- **Make ginger tea first**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Bold! Ginger tea is spicy.
- **Ask Kaito which tea he likes**
    - **Kaito**: I don’t really like tea.
    - Uncle Tenzo gasps and holds the counter. Oh no!

#### `q50-open-done`

**Uncle Tenzo**: Three perfect cups! My heart is warm.  
**Kaito**: You burnt your tongue again, Uncle.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Ow. Yes. A little.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): hot drinks: blow and wait  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Tea is very hot. What should I do first?  
> - ✅ Blow on it and wait → Yes! Blow, blow. Wait a bit. Then sip.
> - Gulp it fast → Ow! Hot drinks can hurt your mouth. Blow on it and wait. Much better.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned to blow on a hot drink and wait before sipping._

**Uncle Tenzo**: I should have waited.  

#### `q50-grump`

_Here comes the first customer. He looks very grumpy._  
**Old Mr Pell**: Tea. Not fancy. Not flowery. No talking.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Of course. Please sit down.  
**Old Mr Pell**: The last tea I had tasted like old socks.  
**Kaito**: Then go back there!  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Nephew. A grumpy guest just needs a kind welcome.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): understanding a grumpy face  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Why might Mr Pell be grumpy?  
> - ✅ He’s tired or sad → Maybe. Grumpy faces can hide sad feelings. A kind hello can help.
> - He hates everyone → Hmm. Maybe he’s just having a hard day. A kind hello can help.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about the feelings that can hide behind a grumpy face._

**Kaito**: Is that a real saying?  
**Uncle Tenzo**: It is now.  

**Choices**

- **Give him jasmine tea**
    - **Old Mr Pell**: Flowery. I said no flowery.
    - He drinks it all. He asks for more!
- **Give him strong black tea**
    - **Old Mr Pell**: Hm. This tea is good and strong.
- **Ask what tea he drank as a boy**
    - **Old Mr Pell**: My mum made barley tea.
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: I have barley! I have everything!

#### `q50-grump-done`

**Old Mr Pell**: Hm. Not bad.  
_For Mr Pell, that is a great big smile!_  
_He counts his coins. He does not have enough._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): how many more (adding on)  
> _Tea costs 5 coins. He has 3 coins._  
> _How many more does he need?_  
> _(Count on together: four, five.)_  
> - ✅ 2 more → Yes! Three… four, five. Two more.
> - 1 more → Let’s count on: three… four. Then five. That’s two more!
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted on from 3 to 5 to find how many more coins were needed._

**Uncle Tenzo**: (quietly) It’s your stall today, Keeper. You choose.  

**Choices**

- **This cup is free today**
    - **Old Mr Pell**: I don’t want a present.
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: It is not a present. It is a hello for tomorrow.
    - **Old Mr Pell**: Hm. Tomorrow, then.
- **Kindly ask for the rest tomorrow**
    - **Old Mr Pell**: Fair. I’ll bring it tomorrow.
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Asking kindly is kind too.
- **Ask him to fix the wobbly stool**
    - **Old Mr Pell**: That stool wobbles. I noticed.
    - He fixes it with a folded leaf. No more wobble!

#### `q50-complete`

_By lunchtime the stall is full. Busy, busy!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): steam comes from very hot water  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: See the little cloud from the kettle?  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: That is steam. It comes from very hot water.  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Steam is hot too. Only grown-ups touch the kettle.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that very hot water makes steam, and that kettles are for grown-ups._

_Your Nubbins nap under the counter. Snore, snore._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Tea is just leaves and water. The rest is caring.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: The stall is yours, Keeper. I will visit a lot.  
**Kaito**: He’ll drink all the tea.  
_Kaito fills Mr Pell’s cup. Nobody asked him to!_  
_Uncle Tenzo smiles and smiles._  
**Old Mr Pell**: Same time tomorrow. Don’t be late.  

## Q51. Cactus Juice

- `q51-s2`: Take 3 little cactus pieces home to plant. · _Cut the small side pieces. Wear gloves. Spikes are sharp!_

#### `q51-desert`

_The desert is hot and sandy. Sand, sand, sand!_  
_Uh-oh. The water bottles are empty._  
**Nalu**: I’ll go and find water. Nobody eat anything strange!

_Nalu goes. Tuk looks at a fat green cactus._  
_He cuts it open. He drinks the juice. Slurp!_  
**Tuk**: Ooh! Best. Drink. EVER!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): never eat or drink plants you don’t know  
> **Pemba**: Should we eat or drink plants we don’t know?  
> - ✅ No. Ask a grown-up first → Yes! Some plants can make us poorly. Always ask a grown-up first.
> - Yes, if it looks tasty → Lots of plants look tasty but aren’t safe. Always ask a grown-up first.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned never to eat or drink a plant without asking a grown-up first._

**Pemba**: Tuk, why are you smiling at that rock?  
**Tuk**: It smiled first!  
_Tuk wobbles off across the sand. Wibble, wobble!_  

**Choices**

- **Say the cloud looks friendly**
    - **Tuk**: Thank you! Finally, someone who listens.
- **Take the cactus away**
    - **Tuk**: You can take the cactus. I still feel happy!
- _(left out in this band; plays as `cup`)_

#### `q51-desert-done`

_Nalu comes back with lots of water._

**Tuk**: Nalu! You look like a big talking fish!  
**Nalu**: Tuk! You made the rule! You wrote it down!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): worry can feel like cross  
> _Nalu is cross. Why?_  
> _(Wait for an answer.)_  
> - ✅ She was worried about Tuk → Yes. She was worried. Worry can come out as cross.
> - She doesn’t like fish → Ha! Maybe. But she was worried about Tuk. Worry can make us feel cross.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about the worry that can sit underneath a cross feeling._


**Choices**

- **Stick up for Tuk: he was thirsty**
    - **Nalu**: We were all thirsty. That’s why we had a rule.
    - **Tuk**: Thank you. Your face is a melon. A kind melon.
- **Agree with Nalu: he broke his rule**
    - **Tuk**: She’s right. I don’t like it when the fish is right.

#### `q51-cuttings`

**Nalu**: Drink this water, Tuk. Slowly.  
**Tuk**: This water isn’t fizzy. It’s just wet.  
**Nalu**: Water is just what you need, silly.  
_Look at the cactus. It is fat and spiky._  
**Nalu**: Let’s take some little pieces home. They grow easily!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): what plants need: a cactus  
> **Nalu**: What does a little cactus need to grow?  
> - ✅ Sun and a little water → Yes! Cactus plants love sun. They keep water inside their fat stems.
> - Lots of snow → Brr! Too cold for a cactus. Cactus plants need sun and a little water.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that plants need sun and water, and that a cactus stores water in its stem._

**Nalu**: Keep them far away from Tuk!

> - 2 → Let’s count them all: one, two, three. Three pieces!
> _For grown-ups: Your child added 1 and 2 to make 3._

**Nalu**: Off we go, back to the Grove.

**Tuk**: I don’t remember yesterday at all.

## Q53. The Fan Warriors

- `q53-s1`: Join the fan drill. Don’t drop your fan! · _Copy the warrior at the front. Open, sweep, close._
- `q53-s2`: Practise fan-blocks with Sumi. · _Block just as she moves. Let her come to you._

#### `q53-flattened`

_In the yard, warriors in green swish their fans._  
_Their faces are painted. They move all together._  
**Tuk**: Ha! Fan dancing! How cute!  
**Sumi**: We’re the fan-warriors. I’m Sumi. That was your last joke.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): teasing hurts feelings  
> _Tuk laughed at the fans. How might Sumi feel?_  
> - ✅ Not happy → Right. Teasing can hurt feelings. Tuk will learn that soon!
> - Very happy → Look at her face. She is not smiling. Teasing can hurt feelings.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about how teasing makes other people feel._

**Tuk**: Fans? Come on. I have a boomerang!  
**Sumi**: Want to try me?  
_Whoosh! Tuk is flat on his back. Bump!_  
**Tuk**: What just happened?

- **Ask about the river spirit**
    - **Ma Reedy**: She came at night, in the mist. With a lantern.

> _For grown-ups: Your child learned to tell a grown-up straight away when something is dangerous._

**Pemba**: A danger cloud! Big and clear!  
**Tuk**: Pemba, you clever little weather boy.  

#### `q58-clouds`

_Everyone stands in the square. Aunt Wen looks up._  
**Aunt Wen**: The clouds will speak! Hmm. That one looks like a duck.  
_Up high, Pemba and Puffin push the clouds. Whoosh!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, notice): wind moves clouds  
> **Pemba**: Wind is moving air.  
> **Pemba**: It pushes the clouds across the sky.  
> **Pemba**: Blow on your hand. That’s a tiny wind!  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that wind is moving air that pushes clouds along._

**Tuk**: We need one shape. A big, pointy mountain.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, do): shapes: triangle  
> **Tuk**: A mountain shape is a triangle. Three sides, three points.  
> _(Draw a triangle in the air. Count the sides.)_  
> **Tuk**: One, two, three. A triangle!  
> Check: `edu:tap:shape:triangle`
> _For grown-ups: Your child drew a triangle and counted its three sides._

**Nalu**: Tuk, we’re tricking them. Is that okay?  
**Tuk**: Hmm. You always ask good questions when I’m busy.  

**Choices**

- **Make a frowning volcano cloud**

## Q59. The Water Scroll

- `q59-s1`: Keep Captain Hake talking. · _Ask about everything on his ship. The bison whistle takes ages._
- `q59-s2`: Get away from the pirates down the river. · _Steer round the rocks. Your Swim Nubbins can push._

#### `q59-market`

_A pirate ship sits at the river market._  
**Captain Hake**: Step up! Treasures! No questions!  
**Pemba**: A whistle shaped like a bison! I want it!  
**Tuk**: It’s a stick with a hole in it.  
_Nalu goes still. She sees an old scroll._  
_It has pictures of water. Waves, drips and splashes._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS2-3, ask): water can freeze into ice and melt back  
> **Nalu**: Water can change. Very cold water freezes into…?  
> - ✅ Ice → Yes! Very cold water turns into hard ice. Warm the ice, and it melts back to water.
> - Sand → Not sand. It turns into ice. Warm the ice, and it melts back to water.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that water freezes into ice when very cold and melts again when warm._

**Nalu**: It’s a water scroll. It could teach me so much.  
**Captain Hake**: Two hundred gold coins, lady. Or your bison.  

**Choices**

- **Ask for a lower price**
    - **Captain Hake**: Two hundred! Final offer! Two hundred and ten!
    - **Tuk**: That’s not how it works.
- **Pretend to walk away**
    - **Captain Hake**: Fine! Nobody wants it! …Two hundred?
- **Ask where he got it**
    - **Captain Hake**: I found it. In a temple. On a shelf.

#### `q59-market-done`

_You turn round. Nalu walks fast to your boat._  
_The glass case is empty!_  
**Tuk**: Nalu! Did you just…?  
**Nalu**: Walk. Normally. Now.  
**Captain Hake**: Stop! After them!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): taking what isn’t ours is not okay  
> _Nalu took the scroll without paying._  
> _Taking things that aren’t ours is not okay._  
> _Even when we want them a lot._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that taking things that belong to someone else is wrong, even when we want them._


#### `q59-chase`

_You jump in your boat. The pirates come after you!_  
**Tuk**: You took it, Nalu!  
**Nalu**: The pirates took it first. I’ll give it back.  
**Pemba**: Are we pirates now? Can I have a hat?  
**Captain Hake**: And he never paid for the whistle!  
**Pemba**: Oh. Oops.  
_Your Swim Nubbins jump in. They push the boat. Splash, splash!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a push makes things move  
> **Pemba**: How do the Nubbins make the boat go?  
> - ✅ They push it → Yes! A push makes things move. A big push makes them go fast!
> - They sing to it → Singing is nice. But it won’t move a boat. A push makes things move!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that a push makes things move, and a bigger push makes them go faster._


**Choices**

- **Tell Nalu taking it was wrong**
    - **Nalu**: I know. I’ll make it right.
- **Ask Pemba to blow the whistle**
    - Toot! Far away, a sky bison turns his head.
- _(left out in this band; plays as `wrong`)_

#### `q59-chase-done`

_The pirate ship gets stuck. Crunch!_  
_It is stuck between two big rocks._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): position: between  
> _Where is the pirate ship stuck?_  
> - ✅ Between two rocks → Yes! A rock on this side. A rock on that side. The ship is between!
> - On top of a cloud → Ha! Look again. One rock here, one rock there. The ship is between them!
> _For grown-ups: Your child used the position word “between”._

**Captain Hake**: This isn’t over! Has anyone got a long stick?  
_Your boat sails on. Bye-bye, pirates!_  

#### `q59-complete`

_That night, Nalu practises with the scroll._  
_Swish! A ribbon of water snaps out and back._  
**Nalu**: I did it! I really did it!  
**Tuk**: Great. Now do the move where we don’t take things.  
**Nalu**: I’ll give the scroll back to the water villages. I promise.  
**Pemba**: And I’ll go back and pay for my whistle!  
**Nalu**: My tummy felt funny when I took it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): listening to your feelings  
> **Nalu**: Why did my tummy feel funny?  
> - ✅ You knew it wasn’t right → Yes. That feeling was telling me something. Listen to that feeling.
> - You ate too many snacks → Ha! Not this time. I knew it wasn’t right. Listen to that feeling.
> _For grown-ups: Your child noticed that our bodies can tell us when we have done something wrong._

_Your Swim Nubbin flicks its tail. A ribbon of water snaps!_

#### `q60-thief`

**Pemba**: That’s no bird. Birds don’t make neat piles.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> **Pemba**: How many peach stones? Let’s count.  
> _(Point to each stone and count.)_  
> **Pemba**: One, two, three. Three peaches gone!

> _For grown-ups: Your child counted three peach stones, pointing to each one._

**Lumi**: Chirrup!

_It grabs a peach and glides away. Whee!_  
**Pemba**: Let’s follow it. Gently!  

**Choices**

- **Run after it**
    - You run. It looks back. It thinks this is a game!
- **Leave a fruit out**
    - **Pemba**: Clever! It will come back for more.

#### `q60-thief-done`

_Up in an old temple, under the broken roof…_  
_…you find a nest! Fruit stones. Buttons. Your spoon!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): animal homes  
> **Pemba**: Where does the lemur live?  
> - ✅ In a nest, up high → Yes! A cosy nest up high, where it feels safe.
> - In the pond → Fish live in ponds. The lemur lives in a nest. Up high, where it feels safe.
> _For grown-ups: Your child matched an animal to its home._

**Pemba**: Oh. It lives up here all alone.  
**Lumi**: Chirr.  

#### `q60-friends`

_The temple is quiet and cold._  
_Old paintings show people laughing with lemurs._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what helps lonely feelings  
> **Pemba**: The lemur is lonely. What helps lonely feelings?  
> - ✅ A friend → Yes. A friend. And a little kindness.
> - Hiding → Hiding can make lonely feel bigger. A friend helps. Like us!

_Your Nubbin sits in the middle. It holds up a fruit._  
**Lumi**: …Chirr?

> - A hat → A hat would be funny! But it needs food, water and a safe home.

**Choices**

## Q61. Pemba Day

- `q61-s1`: Search the old records room for clues. · _The oldest papers are at the back. Your Nubbin can squeeze behind shelves._
- `q61-s2`: Show your clues at Pemba’s trial. · _Pick your best clue. Any clue will do!_

#### `q61-trial`

_Kettleby is having a party. Flags! Sweets!_  
_There is a big straw statue of a long-ago hero._  
_People bonk the statue with sticks. Bonk!_  
**Pemba**: That’s Avatar Kesh! She was like me, long ago.  
**Mayor Tibbs**: Long ago, Kesh made our Marshal Brag fall in the sea!  
**Mayor Tibbs**: So YOU are in trouble now!  
**Tuk**: He wasn’t even born then!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): fairness: blame only for what you did  
> _Is it fair to blame Pemba for something from long ago?_  
> - ✅ No, he didn’t do it → Right. It’s not fair to blame someone for what they didn’t do.
> - Yes → Hmm. Pemba wasn’t even born then. Blaming him isn’t fair.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about whether it is fair to blame someone for something they did not do._

_Two guards put Pemba in a cage. It has flags on it._  
**Nalu**: Let’s find out what really happened. Where are the old papers?  

**Choices**

- **Ask for a fair trial**
    - **Mayor Tibbs**: Of course! Fair, fast, and done by lunch.
- **Let Tuk do the talking**
    - **Tuk**: Mr Mayor. I will speak for Pemba.
    - **Mayor Tibbs**: Have you done this before?
    - **Tuk**: I’ve read a book.
- **Buy a party sweet**
    - It tastes of peppermint. Yum!

#### `q61-trial-done`

_You search the old records room. Dusty, dusty!_  
_Behind the oldest shelf, your Nubbin finds a scroll._  
_It has Marshal Brag’s own stamp on it._  
**Nalu**: It’s his diary! Look at this!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): diaries tell us about long ago  
> **Nalu**: A diary is a book about your days.  
> **Nalu**: People write down what they did and thought.  
> **Nalu**: Old diaries tell us about long ago.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard how old diaries and records tell us about the past._


#### `q61-evidence`

_The trial is in the square. Mayor Tibbs is the judge._  
_Mayor Tibbs is also everyone else. Hmm._  
**Nalu**: Brag wrote this: “I will take Kesh’s island.”  
**Tuk**: And this: “Note to self: get a bigger hat.”  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare sizes  
> **Tuk**: Brag had a big hat. He wanted a bigger one.  
> **Tuk**: Which is bigger: a hat or a house?  
> - ✅ A house → Yes! A house is much bigger. Even Brag’s hat wasn’t that big.
> - A hat → A hat fits on your head. A house fits you inside! The house is bigger.
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared the sizes of two familiar things._

_Someone takes off a Brag hat. They put it in the bin._  
**Mayor Tibbs**: He does sound a bit like a bully.  
**Nalu**: Kesh didn’t hurt anyone. She looked after her home.  
**Mayor Tibbs**: One more clue and I’ll be sure. Keeper?  

**Choices**

- **Show the stone that thanks Kesh**
    - **Mayor Tibbs**: “Thank you, Kesh, for our peace.” It was here all along!
- **Show the old map**
    - **Mayor Tibbs**: We were on her island! She was looking after us!
- **Say Pemba was kind all day**
    - **Mayor Tibbs**: That isn’t a clue. But it is very true.

#### `q61-evidence-done`

**Mayor Tibbs**: Pemba is not guilty! Let him out!  
**Pemba**: Hooray! Can I keep the flags?  
**Pemba**: Keeper? Should I say sorry for what Kesh did?  
**Pemba**: It wasn’t me. But it sort of was.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): sorry is for what we did; helping is for everyone  
> _We say sorry for things we did._  
> _We don’t have to say sorry for others._  
> _But we can always help make things better._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard the difference between saying sorry for our own actions and helping to fix things._


**Choices**

- **“It’s not your fault.”**
    - **Pemba**: Okay. I’ll just try to be kind.
- **“Not your fault. But you can help fix things.”**
    - **Pemba**: I like that! Fixing is better than blaming.
    - **Tuk**: Put that on a sign!

_The people make a new one. It looks like Pemba!_

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.C.6, ask): more and fewer  
> **Mayor Tibbs**: Here are 5 sweets and 2 sticks.  
> **Mayor Tibbs**: Are there more sweets or more sticks?  
> - ✅ More sweets → Yes! Five is more than two. Hooray for sweets!
> - More sticks → Let’s count. Sweets: five. Sticks: two. Five is more. More sweets!
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared two groups to find which has more._

**Pemba**: Best day ever!  
**Tuk**: You’re a party now. Don’t let it go to your head.

## Q62. Penguin Sledding

- `q62-s1`: Get Pemba out of the ice. · _Tap the glowing cracks. Cuddly Nubbins warm the ice._
- `q62-s2`: Make friends with a penguin. Slide down the hill! · _Give a fish first. Lean left and right to steer._

#### `q62-iceberg`

_Snow covers the Grove. Everything is white!_  
_By the frozen pond sits a giant block of ice._  
**Tuk**: Glowing ice? Not good news. Let’s leave it.  
**Nalu**: It’s Pemba! He sat so still all night, he froze!  
_Your Nubbin puts its paws on the ice._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-4, ask): warmth melts ice  
> **Nalu**: How can we melt the ice?  
> - ✅ Make it warm → Yes! Warmth melts ice. Ice melts back into water. Drip, drip!
> - Make it colder → Colder keeps ice frozen. Brr! Warmth melts ice. Drip, drip!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that warmth melts ice back into water._

_Under the ice, a blue arrow glows._  
**Nalu**: Please. Let’s help him.  

**Choices**

- **Tap it with a stone**
    - Tap! A thin crack zigzags across the ice.
- **Get your Nubbins to cuddle the ice**
    - The Nubbins snuggle close. They are warm. Drip, drip!
- **Hand Tuk his boomerang**
    - **Tuk**: Fine. But Pemba owes me a snack for this.

#### `q62-iceberg-done`

> - A big handful of snow → Brr! Snow would make him colder. A warm blanket and a hug will help.
> _For grown-ups: Your child noticed that a friend was cold and thought about what would help him._

**Pemba**: Penguins look warm. Can I ride one?

> **Nalu**: Penguins are birds. But they can’t fly.  
> **Nalu**: They swim very fast in the sea.  
> **Nalu**: And they slide on their tummies on the snow!  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that penguins are birds that cannot fly but swim and slide._

## Q63. King Rumbold’s Challenges

- `q63-s1`: Get the king’s key from the waterfall pool. · _A Swim Nubbin can dive for it. Or wait until noon._
- `q63-s2`: Find Biscuit the goat-yak. · _Listen for “baa”. Goat-yaks love high places and cabbages._
- `q63-s3`: Ride the stone slides down with King Rumbold. · _Lean into the bends. Duck under the letter slots!_

#### `q63-throne`

_Stonereach is a city cut into a cliff._

**King Rumbold**: If you fail, no pudding!

_The king laughs: HEE-HAW! Like a donkey!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): animal sounds  
> **Pemba**: Which animal says “hee-haw”?  
> - ✅ A donkey → Yes! Donkeys say hee-haw. Just like the king!
> - A cat → Cats say meow. Donkeys say hee-haw!
> _For grown-ups: Your child matched an animal to the sound it makes._

**King Rumbold**: Challenge one! My snack key is in the waterfall. Fetch it!  

**Choices**

- **Say yes to the challenge**
    - **King Rumbold**: Wonderful! Off you go! The fish nibble.
- **Ask why he needs the key**
    - **King Rumbold**: Because I am hungry! Why else?
- **Laugh with him**
    - You laugh. He laughs more. Your Nubbin brays too!

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): take away 1  
> **King Rumbold**: Three challenges. One is done. How many are left?  
> _(Hold up three fingers. Fold one down.)_  
> - ✅ 2 → Yes! Two left! Three take away one is two.
> - 3 → Let’s count the fingers still up: one, two. Two left!
> _For grown-ups: Your child took one away from three and found two._

**Tuk**: He didn’t even blink.  

#### `q63-pet`

**Tuk**: What kind of animal is Biscuit?  
**King Rumbold**: A goat-yak. Like a goat, and also like a yak.  
_Somewhere in the city, something goes BAA._  
**Tuk**: Let’s look from the top down. Pemba, take the roofs.  
**Pemba**: I love roofs!  
**King Rumbold**: Or think like Biscuit! Where would a goat go?  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): goats: climbers, and their babies are kids  
> **Pemba**: Goats are great climbers.  
> **Pemba**: They love high, rocky places.  
> **Pemba**: And a baby goat is called a kid!  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that goats are good climbers and that a baby goat is called a kid._

_Your Nubbin climbs the highest wall. It chews a leaf._

_Biscuit is on a roof! He’s eating a cabbage._  
_Down below, a voice wails. It sounds familiar._

**King Rumbold**: Oh dear. Biscuit ate someone else’s cabbage.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): making things right  
> **King Rumbold**: What should we do now?  
> - ✅ Say sorry and pay for it → Yes. Sorry, and here are some coins. Far below, a happy voice says thank you.
> - Run away → Hmm. That wouldn’t be fair. We say sorry and pay for it.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about how to make things right when something gets spoilt._


#### `q63-opponent`

**King Rumbold**: Challenge three! The last one. Pick who you face!  
_He points at a big guard. Then a rock beast. Then himself._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): first, second, third  
> **King Rumbold**: First the guard. Second the beast. Who is third?  
> - ✅ The king → Yes! I am third! Third and best!
> - The guard → The guard was first. I am third!
> _For grown-ups: Your child used the order words first, second and third._

## Q64. Kaito Says Hello

- `q64-s1`: Help Kaito practise what to say, three times. · _Pick the tip you think helps. Each try gets better._
- `q64-s2`: Stand next to Kaito while he asks to join. · _Stay by the campfire. Kaito feels braver with a friend._

#### `q64-rehearse`

_Behind a pillar, Kaito walks in circles. He talks to a rock._

**Kaito**: I want to ask Pemba if I can join his group.  
**Kaito**: But I get nervous. I get it all wrong.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when we feel nervous  
> _Kaito feels nervous. What can help?_

> - Never try at all → Then he can’t join his friends. Practice and slow breaths help.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named feeling nervous and two things that help: practice and slow breaths._

_Your Nubbin sits on the rock. It listens._  
**Kaito**: Pemba. Hello. I am a person. Now a good one. Probably.  

**Choices**

- **Say it’s a bit stiff**
    - **Kaito**: Stiff. Right. I can try less stiff.
- **Say it’s a good start**
    - **Kaito**: Really? Thank you.
    - It is a start. Starts are good.
- **Say: try smiling**
    - Kaito smiles. It looks a bit wobbly.
    - **Kaito**: Too much?

> - Long and muddled → Long and muddled is hard to follow. Short and kind. Got it.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about how to say something clearly and kindly._

**Kaito**: Short and friendly. Short and friendly.

## Q65. The White Lotus

- `q65-s1`: Learn the tile game with Uncle Tenzo. · _Flowers in the middle. Rocks at the edge. He will help you._
- `q65-s2`: Play a game of tiles with Uncle Tenzo. · _Save the lotus tile for last. Nothing can block it._

#### `q65-tiles`

_Rain pitters and patters on the leaves._  
_Under the big tree, Uncle Tenzo has a round board._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Keeper! Will you play with me? It’s no fun alone.  
_The tiles show flowers, rocks and wind._  
_One special tile shows a white lotus flower._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Flowers grow. Rocks block. Wind moves things.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.B.3, do): sort into groups  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Let’s sort the tiles into three piles.  
> _(Put flowers together, rocks together, wind together.)_  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Flowers here. Rocks there. Wind over there. Lovely!  
> Check: `edu:sort:tiles:flower-rock-wind`
> _For grown-ups: Your child sorted tiles into three groups by what they show._

**Uncle Tenzo**: The lotus does nothing. That’s why it matters most.  
**Kaito**: Uncle, that makes it more confusing.  
_Your Nubbin sniffs a flower tile. It’s wood. Oh._  

**Choices**

- **Ask him to teach you**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Gladly. Lesson one: don’t rush a tile.
- **Ask what the lotus does**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Patience. The quiet ones often matter most.
- **Ask if there are snacks**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Always! A game with no snacks is no fun.

#### `q65-tiles-done`

**Uncle Tenzo**: Good. You don’t rush. You look at the whole board.  
**Kaito**: He says that to everyone.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: I have never said it to you, nephew.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): taking turns  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: In a game, how do we play fairly?  
> - ✅ Take turns → Yes. My turn, then your turn. Waiting for your turn takes patience.
> - Everyone goes at once → Then the tiles get very muddled! We take turns. My turn, then your turn.
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised the idea of taking turns and waiting patiently._

**Kaito**: …Hm.  

#### `q65-game`

**Uncle Tenzo**: Now a real game. I won’t go easy. I’ll go medium.  
_The rain falls harder. Splish, splash!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, ask): plants need water  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Rain is falling. Who is happy about the rain?  
> - ✅ The plants → Yes! Plants need water to grow. Rain falls from clouds and gives them a drink.
> - The kettle → Ha! The kettle has enough water. Plants need rain to grow.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that plants need water, and that rain gives it to them._

_Kaito falls asleep against the tree. Snore._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Every tile matters. But no tile wins alone.  
**Uncle Tenzo**: If you lose, don’t sulk. You learned something.  
_Your Nubbins watch every move._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Hmm. Clever move. Did you mean it?  

**Choices**

- **Say you meant it**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Then I’m in trouble!
- **Say it was luck**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: Honest! I like honest players.
- **Point at your Nubbin**
    - **Uncle Tenzo**: A clever Nubbin! I should have known!

#### `q65-game-done`

_You put down your last tile._  
_Flowers bloom all over the board._  
**Uncle Tenzo**: You win! Fair and square! What a happy day!  
**Uncle Tenzo**: Look at the pattern you made.  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): patterns  
> **Uncle Tenzo**: Flower, rock, flower, rock, flower… what comes next?  
> - ✅ Rock → Yes! Flower, rock, flower, rock. A pattern!
> - Flower → Let’s say it again: flower, rock, flower… Rock comes next!
> _For grown-ups: Your child continued an AB pattern._

## LH1. Shalom, Ori!

> _(Your turn. Wave and say: sha-LOME!)_  
> **Ori**: Perfect! A big wave and a big shalom.

**Choices**

- **Ask me “ma shlomkha?” (the boy way).**

    - **You**: בְּסֵדֶר (beseder, “fine”)!
    - (Say it: beh-SEH-der.)
    - **Ori**: Beseder! That means OK. Fine!
- **Ask me “ma shlomekh?” (the girl way).**
    - **Ori**: מָה שְׁלוֹמֵךְ? (ma shlomekh?, “how are you?”)
    - (Say it: mah shlo-MEKH.)
    - **You**: בְּסֵדֶר (beseder, “fine”)!
    - (Say it: beh-SEH-der.)
    - **Ori**: Beseder! That means OK. Fine!
- **Either way. Just say shalom!**
    - **Ori**: Shalom, then! When I ask how you are, say בְּסֵדֶר (beseder, “fine”).
    - (Say it: beh-SEH-der.)
    - **You**: Beseder!
    - **Ori**: Perfect! You sound like my uncle.

> - Morning again → Morning comes back after the night. Evening, then night, then morning!
> _For grown-ups: Put the parts of the day in order: morning, evening, night._

- **Paint it big!**
    - **Ori**: Big! You can see it from the hill!
- **Paint it small and neat.**
    - **Ori**: Small and neat. Like a famous person’s name.
- **Paint it, then add a star.**
    - **Ori**: A star! A light next to “my light”!

#### `lh2-s3-done`

_On the tent, in fresh paint: אוֹרִי._  
**Ori**: That’s me! You helped paint my name.  
**Ori**: Nobody here has done that before.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): noticing how someone feels  
> _Look at Ori’s face. How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Happy and proud → Very happy. My name, on my tent, by my friend!
> - Cross → Look at his big smile. Ori feels happy!
> _For grown-ups: Looked at Ori’s face and named his feeling: happy and proud._

_The Wobbler turns round at last. It waves at the name._

**Ori**: Hebrew has twenty-two letters. You met alef!  
**Ori**: Hop along them, right to left!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): hopping in one direction

> **Ori**: Right to left. The Hebrew way!  
> Check: `edu:hop:stones:right-to-left`
> _For grown-ups: Hopped from right to left, the way Hebrew is written._

_The Wobbler hops too. Backwards, of course._

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): review: which way Hebrew goes  
> _The Wobbler is walking backwards again._

## LH3. Counting Plums

- `lh3-step1`: Help Fern count plums in Hebrew. · _Tap each plum as it goes in the basket. Say its number with Ori._
- `lh3-step2`: Play Ori’s “How Many?” football game. · _Watch each goal. Then tap the number. Ori helps if you get stuck._
- `lh3-step3`: Count ten stars with Ori. · _Go up the hill after dark. Tap a star to count it._

#### `lh3-s1`

_Fern’s plum trees are full. Plop! Plop!_  
**Fern**: I need ten plums in each basket. I keep losing count!  
**Ori**: I’ll help. I count in Hebrew!  
**Ori**: אַחַת (achat, “one”). שְׁתַּיִם (shtayim, “two”). שָׁלוֹשׁ (shalosh, “three”).  
_(Say them: ah-KHAT, SHTAI-yim, sha-LOSH.)_  
**Ori**: אַרְבַּע (arba, “four”). חָמֵשׁ (chamesh, “five”).  
_(Say them: AR-bah, kha-MESH. The “kh” is throaty, like “loch”.)_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5 in Hebrew  
> _(Hold up one finger for each plum.)_  
> **Ori**: Achat, shtayim, shalosh, arba, chamesh!  
> _(Say them again together, with your fingers.)_  
> **Fern**: Five plums! Halfway there!  
> Check: `edu:count:he:plums:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five plums in Hebrew (achat to chamesh), one finger for each._

**Fern**: Shtayim… it sounds like a sneeze!  
_The Wobbler catches the falling plums. Mostly with its face._  

**Choices**

- **I’ll count. You check.**
    - **Ori**: Deal! I’ll cheer every number.
- **Let Fern count. We’ll cheer.**
    - **Fern**: No pressure, then!
    - **Ori**: Big cheers! Achat!

#### `lh3-s1-done`

_Plop, plop, plop. The basket fills up._  
**Fern**: Ten plums! What is ten in Hebrew?  
**Ori**: עֶשֶׂר (eser, “ten”)! Ten is my favourite number.  
_(Say it: EH-ser. Hold up ten fingers!)_  
**Ori**: It’s my football shirt number.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): asking for help  
> **Fern**: I lost count, so I asked Ori for help.  
> **Fern**: What can you do when something is tricky?  
> - ✅ Ask a friend for help → Yes! Asking for help is brave and clever.
> - Give up → Let’s not give up. Asking a friend helps!
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking a friend for help when something is tricky._

_The Wobbler has a plum on its head. Nobody mentions it._  

#### `lh3-s2`

_Ori puts four jumpers on the grass. Two goals!_  
**Ori**: The game is called “How Many?” I shoot. You count!  
**Ori**: Big numbers now. שֵׁשׁ (shesh, “six”). שֶׁבַע (sheva, “seven”).  
_(Say them: SHESH, SHEH-vah.)_  
**Ori**: שְׁמוֹנֶה (shmone, “eight”). תֵּשַׁע (tesha, “nine”). And eser, ten!  
_(Say them: shmo-NEH, TEH-sha, EH-ser.)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): say the Hebrew numbers 6 to 10: call and response  
> **Ori**: I say shesh. You say shesh!  
> _(Ori says each number. Your child says it back.)_  
> **Ori**: Shesh! Sheva! Shmone! Tesha! Eser!  
> **Ori**: Perfect! You count like a referee.  
> Check: `edu:say:he:numbers:6-10`
> _For grown-ups: Repeated the Hebrew numbers six to ten (shesh to eser) after Ori._

_The Wobbler is in goal. It waves at the ball._  
**Ori**: I am very good at football. And very bad at losing.  
**Ori**: Ready? Achat, shtayim, shalosh, GO!  

**Choices**

- **Go easy on me!**
    - **Ori**: Never! …OK, a little bit. For one shot.
- **Bring it on!**
    - **Ori**: Now you sound like a footballer!

#### `lh3-s2-done`

_Ori scores ten goals. Eser!_  
_Then the ball bounces off the Wobbler’s tummy._  
_It rolls all the way down the grass. Into Ori’s goal!_  
**Ori**: The Wobbler scored one? Achat? ACHAT?  
**Ori**: Best of ten! Best of twenty!  
**Nova**: Ori.  
**Ori**: …בְּסֵדֶר (beseder, “OK”). Well played, Wobbler.  
_(Say it: beh-SEH-der.)_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): being a good sport  
> _Ori let in one goal. He feels cross._  
> _What can we say when a game ends?_  
> - ✅ Well played! → Well played. You’re right. That feels better.
> - I’m the best! → Hmm. That’s what I nearly said. “Well played” is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being a good sport: saying “well played” after a game, even when cross._

> **Ori**: We see stars at night, when the sky is dark.  
> **Ori**: In the day, the sun is too bright to see them.

    - **Ori**: The faint ones are brave. They shine anyway. Achat!

## LH5. Savta’s Letters

- `lh5-step1`: Look at a letter from Savta’s tin with Ori. · _Sit at the table with Ori. Tap the letter to hear it._
- `lh5-step2`: Draw a family tree with Ori. · _Draw a tree. Put a word sticker on each branch. Any way is right._
- `lh5-step3`: Tell Ori how a Nubbin feels. · _Look at the shy Nubbin by the gate. Is she happy, sad or tired?_

#### `lh5-s1`

_Pitter-patter. Rain. Ori opens his biscuit tin._  
**Ori**: Letters! They belong to my סַבְתָּא (savta, “grandma”).  
_(Say it: SAHV-tah.)_  
**Ori**: Hazel used to write to Savta. For forty years!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): letters, long ago and today  
> **Nova**: Long ago, people sent lots and lots of letters.  
> **Nova**: A letter can take days to arrive. I know. I carried some!  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that people have sent letters for a long time, and that a letter takes days to arrive._

_Ori reads one. “How is the מִשְׁפָּחָה (mishpacha, ‘family’)?”_  
_(Say it: meesh-pah-KHAH.)_  
_“Is the כֶּלֶב (kelev, ‘dog’) still stealing socks?”_  
_(Say it: KEH-lev. Woof!)_  
_In the corner of the letter: a game of noughts and crosses!_  
**Ori**: They played games by post? And Savta is LOSING?  

#### `lh5-s1-done`

**Ori**: Savta, mishpacha, kelev. You know them!  
_The Wobbler climbs onto the letter. It sits there like a cat._  
**Ori**: Just like a חָתוּל (chatul, “cat”)! Off, Wobbler!  
_(Say it: kha-TOOL. Miaow!)_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): animal sounds  
> **Ori**: A kelev says woof. What does a chatul say?  
> - ✅ Miaow! → Miaow! And purr, when it’s happy.
> - Moo! → Moo is a cow! A chatul says miaow.
> _For grown-ups: Matched animals to their sounds: a dog (kelev) says woof, a cat (chatul) says miaow._

**Ori**: Every letter has a game. Savta is behind. I’m very upset!  

#### `lh5-s2`

_Ori unrolls a long sheet of paper. He draws a tree._  
**Ori**: A family tree. My mishpacha! Savta at the top.  
**Ori**: Mum is אִמָּא (ima, “mum”). Dad is אַבָּא (aba, “dad”).  
_(Say them: EE-mah, AH-bah.)_  
**Ori**: I have an אָחוֹת (achot, “sister”) and an אָח (ach, “brother”).  
_(Say them: ah-KHOTE, AKH. A throaty “kh”!)_  

> **Lesson** (art, do): draw your own family

> **Ori**: Your grown-ups, your friends… and maybe a Nubbin or two!

> _For grown-ups: Drew a picture of their own family and named the people in it._

**Ori**: A friend who’s a boy is a חָבֵר (chaver).  
**Ori**: A friend who’s a girl is a חֲבֵרָה (chavera).  
_(Say them: khah-VER, khah-veh-RAH.)_  
**Nova**: Do I go on it? I just carry the letters.  

**Choices**

- **Nova goes on as a chavera.**
    - **Nova**: A chavera! I like that very much.
    - **Ori**: A big branch for Nova!
- **Ori goes on as a chaver.**
    - **Ori**: Me? On your tree?
    - **Ori**: …Chaver. Thank you. You’re on mine too.

    - **Ori**: A Nubbin branch! The Wobbler at the very top.

_Two trees, side by side. Ori’s family and yours._  
**Ori**: Ima, aba, ach, achot, chaver, chavera. All of them!

> **Ori**: I say it in English. You say it in Hebrew. Mum?

**Ori**: My achot will be cross you learned so fast. Good!  
**Ori**: And my ach borrows my football. Without asking!  
_The Wobbler drew itself on both trees. A circle with arms._  

#### `lh5-s3`

_The rain stops. Drip, drip. The Nubbins come out._  
**Ori**: Feelings! In Hebrew, they change for a boy or a girl.  
**Ori**: Boy: שָׂמֵחַ (sameach, “happy”). Girl: שְׂמֵחָה (smecha, “happy”).  
_(Say them: sah-MEH-akh, smeh-KHAH. Big smile!)_  
**Ori**: Boy: עָצוּב (atsuv, “sad”). Girl: עֲצוּבָה (atsuva, “sad”).  
_(Say them: ah-TSOOV, ah-tsoo-VAH. Sad face.)_  
**Ori**: Boy: עָיֵף (ayef, “tired”). Girl: עֲיֵפָה (ayefa, “tired”).  
_(Say them: ah-YEF, ah-yeh-FAH. Big yawn!)_  
_The shy one sits alone by the gate._  
**Ori**: She’s a girl, I think. מָה שְׁלוֹמֵךְ? (ma shlomekh?, “how are you?”)  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): feeling words in Hebrew, with faces  
> _(Say it: mah shlo-MEKH. That’s “how are you?” to a girl.)_  
> _(She’s a girl, so use the girl words.)_  
> _(Make a happy face and say: smeh-KHAH!)_

## LJ1. Konnichiwa, Hana!

- `lj1-step1`: Say hello to Hana at the gate. Say “konnichiwa”! · _Tap Hana and choose Greet. A little bow is lovely too._
- `lj1-step2`: Teach three Nubbins to bow when you say “konnichiwa”. · _Tap a Nubbin and say “konnichiwa”. Say it a few times. Nubbins learn by copying._
- `lj1-step3`: Say “oyasumi” (good night) to everyone. · _In the evening, tap each friend and choose Say, then “oyasumi”._

#### `lj1-s1`

_Bang! The gate swings open._  
_In runs a girl with a sketchbook. Nova follows, slowly._  
**Nova**: This is Hana. She raced me here!  
**Hana**: I won. By a lot.  
**Hana**: こんにちは (konnichiwa, “hello”)!  
_(Say it: kon-nee-chee-WAH. Your child says it back.)_  
_Hana bows. A quick little dip, then up again._  
**Hana**: はじめまして (hajimemashite, “nice to meet you”)!  
_(Say it: hah-jee-meh-MASH-teh. Say it slowly, together.)_  
**Hana**: We only say that the very first time we meet.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, do): greeting someone new with a bow  
> **Hana**: At home, we bow to say hello. And thank you. And sorry.  
> **Hana**: A deeper bow shows extra respect.  
> _(Stand up together. Bow and say: konnichiwa!)_  
> Check: `edu:bow:konnichiwa`
> _For grown-ups: Greeted Hana with konnichiwa (“hello”) and a small bow, and heard that in Japan people bow to greet, thank and say sorry._


**Choices**

- **Bow and say “konnichiwa”.**
    - You bow. Hana bows back, a bit lower.
    - **Hana**: Lower means I win. Probably.
- **Wave and say “konnichiwa”.**
    - **Hana**: A wave is friendly too!
    - **Hana**: Next time, add a tiny bow. Like this.
- **Say “hajimemashite” with a bow.**
    - **Hana**: Hajimemashite! The first-time word! Perfect!
    - **Hana**: Nova took three days to learn that.
    - **Nova**: Two days.

**Hana**: Do they want to learn? はい (hai, “yes”)!  
_(Say it: HAI. Nod your head.)_

_(Say it: EE-eh. Shake your head.)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): yes and no in Japanese  
> **Hana**: Silly questions! Answer hai or iie.  
> **Hana**: Is a Nubbin a teapot?  
> _(Your child answers: iie! Shake your head.)_

> _(Your child answers hai or iie. Both are fine!)_

> _For grown-ups: Answered silly questions with hai (“yes”) and iie (“no”), nodding and shaking their head._


#### `lj1-s2`

_Morning! Dew on the grass. Sparkle, sparkle._  
**Hana**: おはよう (ohayō, “good morning”)!  
_(Say it: oh-hah-YOH. Say it back to Hana.)_  
**Fern**: Good morning. Have a plum.  
**Hana**: ありがとう (arigatō, “thank you”)!  
_(Say it: ah-ree-gah-TOH. Say thank you to Fern.)_  
_Hana runs too fast. Bump! Over goes a round Nubbin._  
**Hana**: ごめんなさい (gomen nasai, “I’m sorry”)!  
_(Say it: go-men nah-SAI.)_  
**Fern**: That’s Dumpling. He copies everything.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying sorry after a bump  
> _Hana bumped Dumpling by mistake. What can she do?_  
> - ✅ Say sorry and help him up. → Yes! Gomen nasai, and a hand up. Better! Hana bows low. Dumpling copies, and lands on his face.
> - Run away. → Running away won’t help Dumpling. Say sorry, then help him up.
> - Pretend it didn’t happen. → Dumpling still feels bumped! Saying sorry helps him feel better.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about what to do after bumping someone by mistake: say sorry (gomen nasai) and help._


**Choices**

- **The shy one under the bench.**
    - You whisper: konnichiwa.
    - The shy one dips its head. Just a tiny bit.
    - **Hana**: Small bows count!
- **The bouncy one on the wall.**
    - Konnichiwa! The bouncy one bows. Boing! Off the wall!
    - **Hana**: Very keen. I like it.
- **The sleepy one in the sun.**
    - Konnichiwa! The sleepy one bows… slowly… and stays down.
    - **Hana**: Is it bowing? Or asleep?
    - **Fern**: Bit of both.

**Hana**: Arigatō, everyone! So good!  
_Then one more bow. Dumpling copies, late!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): 3 and 1 more make 4  
> _Three Nubbins bowed. Then Dumpling bowed too. How many bowed?_  
> _(Count on your fingers together.)_  
> - 3 → Three Nubbins, and Dumpling makes one more. One, two, three, four!
> - ✅ 4 → Four! Three Nubbins and one Dumpling.
> - 5 → Let’s count: one, two, three Nubbins. Dumpling makes four.
> _For grown-ups: Counted three bowing Nubbins and one more, and found that 3 and 1 more make 4._

**Hana**: Other way round, Dumpling!  
_He turns round. He bows again. Bump!_  
_Dumpling looks very pleased with himself._

_(Say it: kom-bahn-WAH. Wave to Luna!)_

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): times of day: morning and evening  
> _The sun is going down. Is it morning or evening?_  
> - ✅ Evening → Evening! The sun goes down in the evening. So we say konbanwa.
> - Morning → In the morning the sun comes up. Now it’s going down. That’s evening!
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that the sun goes down in the evening, when Hana says konbanwa (“good evening”)._

**Hana**: Bedtime word: おやすみ (oyasumi, “good night”).  
_(Say it: oh-yah-SOO-mee. Whisper it, soft and sleepy.)_  
**Hana**: Everybody gets an oyasumi. That’s the rule.

    - **Hana**: Everything is a race.

## LJ2. The Hiragana Pond

- `lj2-step1`: Find the painted stones and hop across. Say each sound! · _Start nearest the bank. Say ah, ee, oo, eh, oh as you hop._
- `lj2-step2`: Trace a shape in the sand by the pond. · _Tap the sand. Follow the numbered lines with your finger. No rush._
- `lj2-step3`: Help write Hana’s name in her sketchbook. Then draw a flower. · _Open the sketchbook. A grown-up can help you trace the two shapes._

#### `lj2-s1`

_Hana has painted shapes on the pond stones._

**Hana**: Ah. Ee. Oo. Eh. Oh.  
_(Say them after Hana: ah, ee, oo, eh, oh.)_  
**Hana**: Hop on the stones. Say each sound as you go.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): saying the five Japanese vowel sounds  
> _(You say a sound. Your child says it back and hops.)_  
> **Hana**: Ah! Ee! Oo! Eh! Oh!  
> Check: `edu:say:ja:vowel-sounds`

_On the last stone sits a frog. Fat and wet._

> - In a tree → Not in a tree! The frog is on the stone.

## LJ3. Counting Koi

- `lj3-step1`: Count the koi into the pond, from ichi to jū. · _Tap each fish as it swims in. Say the number with Hana._
- `lj3-step2`: Race Hana round the pond. Count the laps in Japanese. · _Start the race at the lap board. Say each lap number as you pass the post._
- `lj3-step3`: Count ten stars with Hana. Then find the moon. · _Go up the hill with Luna after dark. The moon is low, behind the plum trees._

#### `lj3-s1`

_Marina has two big buckets. Splash, splash!_  
**Marina**: New fish for the pond!  
**Hana**: こい (koi, “koi fish”)! They’re koi!  
_(Say it: KOY. It’s the same word in English!)_  
**Hana**: Let’s count them in. Hold up your fingers.  
**Hana**: いち (ichi, “one”), に (ni, “two”), さん (san, “three”)!  
_(Say it: EE-chee, NEE, SAHN. One finger at a time.)_  
**Hana**: よん (yon, “four”), ご (go, “five”)! A whole hand!  
_(Say it: YOHN, GO. Wiggle all five fingers!)_  
_Plop! Plop! The koi do not wait._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5 in Japanese  
> **Hana**: Count this bucket! Ichi, ni, san, yon, go!  
> _(Count on your fingers together. Five koi!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:ja:koi:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five koi in Japanese: ichi, ni, san, yon, go._


#### `lj3-s1-done`

**Marina**: Five more in this bucket.  
**Hana**: ろく (roku, “six”), なな (nana, “seven”), はち (hachi, “eight”)!  
_(Say it: ROH-koo, NAH-nah, HAH-chee. Copy Hana!)_  
**Hana**: きゅう (kyū, “nine”), じゅう (jū, “ten”)! Ten koi!  
_(Say it: KYOO, JOO. Show ten fingers!)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): tracing the kana shape い (i)  
> **Hana**: Ichi starts with this shape: い (i).  
> **Hana**: It says “ee”. Two little lines, like two koi.  
> _(Trace it: the long line on the left first, then the short one.)_  
> Check: `edu:trace:ja:i`
> _For grown-ups: Traced the Japanese shape い (i), the first shape of ichi (“one”)._

**Marina**: A little dramatic. But right.

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): counting actions: one, two, three  
> **Hana**: Run on the spot! One lap: ichi!

**Hana**: Loser feeds the さかな (sakana, “fish”).  
_(Say it: sah-KAH-nah. Make a fish face!)_

**Choices**

- **A fair start.**
    - **Byte**: Fair start. Nobody moves. Nobody. Hana.
    - **Hana**: I wasn’t moving. I was leaning.

    - **Hana**: I don’t need a head start!

_Clack! The last tile flips._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): losing kindly  
> _Hana didn’t win. What can she say?_  
> - ✅ “Good race!” → GOOD RACE, HANA! Again tomorrow? …Good race. Tomorrow I win.
> - “I’m the best!” → Hmm. That might make the others sad. “Good race!” is kinder.
> - “That was a practice one!” → There it is again. Feeling cross is OK. Then “good race!” helps.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about what to say after losing a race, and practised “good race!”._

> - ✅ It’s darker here. → Yes. Away from bright lights, the sky is darker. More stars show.
> - The stars came to see us. → A lovely idea! Really, it’s darker here. So we see more.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we can see more stars where the sky is darker, away from bright lights._

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): tracing the kana shape う (u)  
> **Hana**: Usagi starts with this shape: う (u).  
> **Hana**: It says “oo”. A little line on top, like an ear.  
> _(Trace it: the little line first, then the big curve.)_  
> Check: `edu:trace:ja:u`
> _For grown-ups: Traced the Japanese shape う (u), the first shape of usagi (“rabbit”)._

**Nova**: What’s that bird in the tree? It looks cross.  
**Hana**: A ふくろう (fukurō, “owl”). Owls always look cross.  
_(Say it: foo-koo-ROH. Hoo, hoo!)_  
**Hana**: It was a very kind owl.  

#### `lj5-s3`

_Clover sits in the grass with the Nubbins._  
**Hana**: うれしい (ureshii, “happy”)! That one is rolling about.  
_(Say it: oo-REH-shee. Make a happy face!)_  
**Hana**: かなしい (kanashii, “sad”). That one lost its ball.  
_(Say it: kah-NAH-shee. Make a sad face.)_  
_Plop! A frog lands on Hana’s shoe._  
**Hana**: かえる (kaeru, “frog”)! It’s a kaeru!  
_(Say it: kah-EH-roo. Ribbit!)_  
**Hana**: I’m not こわい (kowai, “scared”). Not at all.  
_(Say it: koh-WAI.) Hana is standing on a chair._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): it is OK to feel scared  
> **Clover**: It’s all right to be scared. Even of something small.  
> **Hana**: …Maybe I’m a little bit kowai.  
> _(Ask: what helps when you feel scared?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that it is all right to feel scared, and talked about what helps._


**Choices**

- **“It’s OK to be scared.”**
    - **Hana**: Thank you. It is OK. I’m staying up here, though.
- **Gently carry the frog to the pond.**
    - You cup the frog in your hands. Back to the pond.
    - **Hana**: Thank you. Really.
- **“Let’s look at it together.”**
    - You stand by the chair. The kaeru blinks. Hana blinks.
    - **Hana**: It’s got quite a nice face.

_(Say it: neh-MOO-ee. Do a big yawn!)_  
**Clover**: And you, Hana?

_(Say it: tah-NOH-shee. Do a happy wiggle!)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): feelings words in Japanese

## LJ6. Floating Lanterns

- `lj6-step1`: Sit with Hana by the stream. · _Hana is sitting by the stream. Tap her and choose Talk._
- `lj6-step2`: Help Hana make a lantern for her grandpa. · _Fold a lantern at Fern’s table. You can make one too. A grown-up can help write the name._
- `lj6-step3`: Float Hana’s lantern with her at dusk. Later, join the party! · _Go to the stream in the evening. Luna lights the lanterns. The party is back at the cottage._

#### `lj6-s1`

_Late summer. Hana sits by the stream. She is not drawing._  
_That means something is up._  
**Hana**: At home, there’s a special time in summer.  
**Hana**: Families remember the people in their family who have died.  
**Hana**: My family floats a paper lantern down the river for my grandpa.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, notice): families remember people in different ways  
> _(Tell your child: families all over the world remember people who have died.)_  
> _(Some tell stories. Some look at photos. Some float lanterns.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that Hana’s family floats a paper lantern in summer to remember her grandpa, and that families everywhere remember people in their own ways._

**Hana**: River is かわ (kawa, “river”). This stream is a little kawa.  
_(Say it: KAH-wah. Point to the water.)_  
**Hana**: The lantern has a ひかり (hikari, “light”) inside.  
_(Say it: hee-KAH-ree.)_  
**Hana**: This year I’m here. Could I float his lantern on your stream?  

**Choices**

- **“Yes! We’ll all come.”**
    - **Hana**: Really? Then I need paper. And sticks. And you, to help.
- **“Tell me about your grandpa.”**
    - **Hana**: He went fishing every week. He never caught anything.
    - **Hana**: He said that wasn’t the point. He taught me to run.
- **Sit next to her for a while.**
    - You sit together. The water goes by.
    - **Hana**: Thank you. That helped.

#### `lj6-s1-done`

_Hana is drawing again! Lanterns and tiny lights._  
**Hana**: And this is my grandma’s やま (yama, “mountain”).  
_(Say it: YAH-mah. Make a pointy mountain with your arms!)_  
**Hana**: In winter it has ゆき (yuki, “snow”) on top.  
_(Say it: YOO-kee. Shiver! Brrr!)_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): snow melts into water when it warms  
> **Hana**: When the spring sun warms the yuki on the yama, what happens?  
> - ✅ It melts into water. → Yes! Warm snow melts. It turns into water.
> - It turns into a snowman. → Only if you build one! Warm snow melts into water.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snow (yuki) melts into water when the sun warms it._

**Hana**: Everyone is coming tomorrow. Even Ember!  
**Nova**: Ember said “fine”, and asked what time. That’s a yes.  

#### `lj6-s2`

_Fern’s kitchen is full of paper, glue and sticks._  
**Fern**: The sticks are from the old plum き (ki, “tree”).  
_(Say it: KEE. Stand tall like a tree!)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): tracing the kana shape き (ki)  
> **Hana**: This shape is き (ki). It says “ki”.  
> **Hana**: All by itself, ki means tree!  
> _(Trace it: two lines across, one line down, then the curve.)_  
> Check: `edu:trace:ja:ki`
> _For grown-ups: Traced the Japanese shape き (ki), which on its own is the word for “tree”._

_Pixel fills a bucket with みず (mizu, “water”)._  
_(Say it: MEE-zoo. Splash!)_  
_The first lantern goes in. Glug. It sinks._  
**Pixel**: Paper gets soggy. Wood floats. Next one gets a wooden base.  
**Hana**: I write my grandpa’s name on mine. Slowly.  
**Hana**: You can make one too. For someone you remember, or love.  
_Hana writes very carefully. Nobody talks. Shh._  

**Choices**

- **Write the name of someone I remember.**
    - **Hana**: Write it big. So it shows from far away.
    - (A grown-up can help write the name.)
- **Write the name of someone I love.**
    - **Hana**: Yes. Grandpa would like that. Lanterns are for love too.
- **Ask Hana to help write the name.**
    - **Hana**: Say it slowly. I’ll write it, and you go over it.
    - (A grown-up can help too.)

#### `lj6-s2-done`

_Lanterns dry on the windowsill. A long row._  
**Hana**: Mine is the best one.  
**Fern**: It’s not a race, Hana.  
**Hana**: …You’re right. This one isn’t.  
_Pixel puts the test one in the mizu. It floats!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): what floats and what sinks  
> _The paper one sank. Which one floats?_  
> - ✅ The one with a wooden base. → Yes! Wood floats. The paper stays dry on top.
> - A paper one with no base. → That one went glug! The wooden base helps it float.
> _For grown-ups: Saw that a lantern with a wooden base floats, while soggy paper sinks._

_Pixel nods. Good._  

#### `lj6-s3`

_Dusk. Everyone walks to the stream with Hana._  
**Hana**: No あめ (ame, “rain”) tonight. Good!  
_(Say it: AH-meh. Pitter-patter with your fingers.)_  
**Luna**: I’ll light them. One at a time. No hurry.  
**Hana**: This one is for my grandpa.  
_Hana’s little hikari floats away. Slowly, slowly._  
**Hana**: He died. His body stopped working. It won’t start again.  
**Hana**: But I still love him. The lantern helps me remember him.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): remembering someone who has died  
> **Hana**: I feel a bit sad. And a bit happy. Both at once.  
> _(Say: it’s OK to feel sad and happy together.)_  
> _(Ask: who would you like to remember, or send love to?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard plainly what dying means, and that remembering, and feeling sad and happy at once, are all OK._

_A frog sits on the bank by Hana. It watches the lights._  
**Hana**: …You can watch too, frog.  

#### `lj6-s3-done`

_The lanterns float on the kawa. No ame. Just stars._  
**Hana**: ありがとう (arigatō). For doing this with me.  
_(Say it: ah-ree-gah-TOH. Say it back to Hana.)_  
_Later, at the cottage, Sparks shouts: PARTY!_  
**Hana**: Hello and good night words! Ohayō! Konnichiwa! Konbanwa! Oyasumi!  
_(Say them: oh-hah-YOH, kon-nee-chee-WAH, kom-bahn-WAH, oh-yah-SOO-mee. Bow each time!)_  
**Hana**: Hajimemashite! Hai! Iie! Gomen nasai!  
_(Say them: hah-jee-meh-MASH-teh, HAI, EE-eh, go-men nah-SAI.)_  
**Hana**: Now count the Nubbins in the front row!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 10 in Japanese  
> **Hana**: Ichi, ni, san, yon, go!  
> _(Say them: EE-chee, NEE, SAHN, YOHN, GO.)_  
> **Hana**: Roku, nana, hachi, kyū, jū!  
> _(Say them: ROH-koo, NAH-nah, HAH-chee, KYOO, JOO. A finger each!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:ja:nubbins:10`
> _For grown-ups: Counted ten Nubbins at Hana’s party in Japanese, from ichi to jū._

_The party goes on, up at the cottage._  
**Hana**: Food! Ringo, mikan, ichigo, momo, onigiri, obentō! Itadakimasu!  
_(Say them: REEN-go, mee-KAHN, ee-CHEE-go, MOH-moh, oh-nee-GEE-ree, oh-ben-TOH, ee-tah-dah-kee-MAS.)_
