_The crocodile lets go of the buffalo. It crawls back._  
_Thump! The log goes back on top of the crocodile._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): positions: on top and under  
> **Bu Wulan**: Where is the crocodile now?  
> - ✅ Under the log. → Yes! The crocodile is under. The log is on top.
> - On the log. → Look again. The log is on top. The crocodile is under it.
> _For grown-ups: Your child used the words on top and under._

**Kancil**: Buffalo, you may go home. Crocodile, stay where you started.  
_The buffalo walks home. Clip, clop._  

#### `lk05-complete`

_Kancil did not trick anyone this time. He just looked carefully._  
_A small girl asks: will the crocodile stay there forever?_  
**Bu Wulan**: No. Someone kind will come. I hope he says thank you then!  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Helping is kind. Saying thank you is kind too.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): being kind back to helpers  
> _(Ask: who helped you today? Did you say thank you?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about someone who helped them today._


## LK6. The Race with the Snails

- `lk06-s1`: Watch Kancil meet a snail. · _Sit on the bank when the lamp is lit._
- `lk06-s2`: Watch the big race. · _Help Siti put the snails along the screen._

#### `lk06-boast`

**Bu Wulan**: Kancil is very pleased with himself. Too pleased!  
**Kancil**: I am the cleverest! I am the fastest!  
_Here is a snail. Small and round and slow._  
**Kancil**: Ha! Snail, you are so slow!  
_A little boy looks at his feet. He feels sad._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): laughing at someone hurts  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: Is it kind to laugh at someone for being slow?  
> - ✅ No, it hurts. → Yes, it hurts. Look at the little boy. We can be kind instead.
> - Yes, it is funny. → Look at the boy. He is sad. Laughing at someone hurts.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about why laughing at someone for being slow is unkind._

**Snail**: I am slow. But I will race you, Kancil.  

#### `lk06-line`

_Wulan whispers to the snail. Shh!_  
**Mak Cik Siti**: That night, the snail tells all its cousins.  
_Snails come out from everywhere. Slow, slow, slow._  
_They carry their houses on their backs._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): snails carry their shells  
> **Bu Wulan**: A snail’s shell is its home. It goes everywhere with it.  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: A snail slides on one big foot. It leaves a shiny trail.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that a snail’s shell is its home and that it slides on one big foot._


#### `lk06-race`

_Siti puts ten snails along the river._  
**Kancil**: Ready? Go!  
_Kancil runs and runs. Then he stops._  
**Kancil**: Where are you, snail?  
**Snail**: Here I am! Just ahead of you!  
**Kancil**: Where are you now?  
**Snail**: Still ahead of you!  
_Kancil runs ten times. He is so tired! He gives up._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to ten  
> _(Count the snails on the screen together.)_  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: Ten snails! Each one waited in its place.  
> Check: `edu:count:snails:10`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted the ten snails along the riverbank._


#### `lk06-complete`

**Bu Wulan**: Ten snails. Not one of them ran!  
_The little boy smiles. He helped move the snails._  
**Bu Wulan**: Slow is not silly. Slow is just slow.  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Say it with me: Where are you? Here I am!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, notice): repeated lines in a story  
> _(Say it together: “Where are you?” “Here I am!”)_  
> **Bu Wulan**: Stories love words that come again and again.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child joined in with a line that repeats in the story._


## LK7. The Cucumber Garden

- `lk07-s1`: Watch the cucumber story. · _Sit on the bank when the lamp is lit._
- `lk07-s2`: Plant cucumber seeds by the screen. · _Take the seed pot by the lamp._

#### `lk07-garden`

**Bu Wulan**: This is my favourite story. Kancil and the cucumbers.  
**Bu Wulan**: Pak Tani is a farmer. Pak Tani means Mr Farmer.  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, notice): plants need water and light  
> **Bu Wulan**: Cucumbers need water and sun to grow.  
> _(Ask: what do plants need? Water and sun!)_  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that cucumber plants need water and sun to grow._

**Pak Tani**: Who ate my cucumbers?  
_Kancil creeps in. Nibble, nibble, crunch!_  
**Bu Wulan**: Pak Tani makes a scarecrow. It is very sticky!  
_Kancil pushes it. Stuck! He pushes again. Stuck again!_  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Wait! My grandma told it differently!  

#### `lk07-endings`

_Siti and Wulan whisper behind the screen._  
**Bu Wulan**: In the old story, Kancil tricks a dog and runs away.  
**Mak Cik Siti**: In the new story, Kancil says sorry.  
**Bu Wulan**: Both are stories. One is just older.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): stories change over time  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: Grandmas told stories long ago. We tell them today.  
> **Bu Wulan**: Each time, a story can change a little.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that old stories change a little each time they are told._


#### `lk07-sorry`

**Pak Tani**: Well, Kancil? What do you say?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): choosing kind words  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: What should Kancil say?  
> - Sorry. → Sorry is a good start. It means: I know I did wrong.
> - Can I help? → Helping fixes things. That is kind.
> - I won’t do it again. → A promise! That is kind too.
> _For grown-ups: Your child chose kind words for Kancil to say after doing wrong._

**Kancil**: I am sorry, Pak Tani. I took your cucumbers.  
**Kancil**: Can I help you plant more?  
_Pak Tani unsticks Kancil. One hoof. Two hooves._  
_They plant seeds together. Dig, drop, pat!_  

#### `lk07-complete`

_Siti and Wulan build a little fence for the vine to climb._  
_Your Nubbin plants seeds in a pot._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count objects one by one  
> _(Count the seeds into the pot together: one, two, three, four, five.)_  
> **Bu Wulan**: Five seeds! Maybe five little plants.  
> Check: `edu:count:seeds:5`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted five seeds into a pot, one at a time._

**Mak Cik Siti**: The old ending is clever. The new ending is kind.  
_Soon there is one small cucumber. Nobody eats it!_  

## LK8. The Tiger at the River

- `lk08-s1`: Watch Kancil meet the tiger. · _Sit on the bank when the lamp is lit._
- `lk08-s2`: Look into the still pond. · _Find a calm spot at the edge and look in._

#### `lk08-tiger`

**Mak Cik Siti**: Kancil walks by a still, quiet pool.  
_Here comes the tiger! Big and stripy._  
**Tiger**: A mouse-deer! Just right for supper!  
_Kancil is scared. But he takes a big breath._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): a big breath helps when we are scared  
> **Bu Wulan**: When you are scared, take a big breath. In... and out.  
> _(Take a big breath together.)_  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: A calm mind can think of a plan.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised a calming breath, like Kancil._

**Kancil**: Careful, tiger. A bigger tiger lives in this pool!  

#### `lk08-look`

**Tiger**: Show me this tiger!  
_The tiger looks in the pool._  
_There is a tiger in the water! It looks back at him._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, notice): still water shows a reflection  
> **Bu Wulan**: Still water is like a mirror. You can see yourself.  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: That tiger in the water is his reflection!  
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that still water works like a mirror._

**Tiger**: Grrr! Go away!  

#### `lk08-splash`

_The tiger roars. The water tiger roars too._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): above and below  
> **Bu Wulan**: The real tiger is on the bank. Where is the water tiger?  
> - ✅ Below, in the water. → Yes! Below, and upside down.
> - Up in a tree. → Not in a tree! Look down. He is below, in the water.
> _For grown-ups: Your child used the words above and below._

_Splash! The tiger jumps in the pool!_  
_Wulan flicks real water on the screen. Splish!_  
_The tiger climbs out. He is very wet!_  
**Tiger**: Where did that mouse-deer go?  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Kancil is home already!  

#### `lk08-complete`

_Your Nubbin looks into the pond._  
_Another Nubbin looks back! It waves. Wave, wave!_  
_Your Nubbin pokes the water. Plip! The picture wiggles away._  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Nobody was hurt. The tiger only got wet!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhyming words  
> **Bu Wulan**: Splash! What rhymes with splash?  
> - ✅ Crash! → Splash, crash! Yes, they rhyme.
> - Tiger. → Splash, tiger? No. Splash, crash! Splash, dash!
> _For grown-ups: Your child found a word that rhymes with splash._


## LK9. The Pit

- `lk09-s1`: Watch Kancil fall into a hole. · _Sit on the bank when the lamp is lit._
- `lk09-s2`: Help the elephant get out. · _Roll the logs from the woodpile._

#### `lk09-pit`

**Mak Cik Siti**: Kancil is running. He is not looking. Whoomp!  
_Kancil falls into a deep hole._  
**Kancil**: Help! I can’t get out!  
_Kancil jumps and jumps. He is too small._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): asking for help  
> **Bu Wulan**: Kancil is stuck. What can you do when you are stuck?  
> - ✅ Ask for help. → Yes! Ask for help. Call out, or tell a grown-up.
> - Hide. → Hiding keeps you stuck. Asking for help gets you out.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about asking for help when they are stuck._

_Thump, thump. Here comes the elephant!_  
**Elephant**: What are you doing down there, little one?  
**Kancil**: The sky is falling! This hole is the safe place!  
**Elephant**: Oh no! Make room!  

#### `lk09-out`

_The elephant climbs in. Thump!_  
_First, Kancil hops on its back. Next, on its head. Last, out!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): first, next, last  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: What did Kancil do first?  
> - ✅ Hopped on the back. → Yes! First the back, next the head, last out!
> - Climbed out. → That was last! First he hopped on the elephant’s back.
> _For grown-ups: Your child put the story in order: first, next, last._

**Kancil**: Thank you, Elephant!  
_But the elephant is still in the hole._  

#### `lk09-ending`

**Mak Cik Siti**: Oh dear. Poor Elephant is stuck.  
**Kancil**: Elephant, I am sorry! The sky is not falling. I will help!  
_Your Nubbin rolls logs to the screen. Roll, roll!_  
_The logs make a ramp. A slope to climb!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count objects to say how many  
> _(Count the logs together as they go down.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five, six!_  
> **Bu Wulan**: Six logs make a good ramp.  
> Check: `edu:count:logs:6`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted six logs to build a ramp._

_The elephant climbs out. Step, step, step!_  

#### `lk09-complete`

_Everyone is out of the hole. Everyone is safe._  
**Bu Wulan**: That was a tricky one.  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Kancil said sorry. Then he helped. That made it right.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): sorry and helping go together  
> **Bu Wulan**: Sorry is a word. Helping is doing. Both together are best.  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that saying sorry and then helping makes things right._

_Your Nubbin puts the elephant puppet in the box. Very gently._  

## LK10. The Night of Stories

- `lk10-s1`: Line up the Nubbins across the stream. · _Call your Nubbins to the water._
- `lk10-s2`: Count every crocodile! · _One hop, one crocodile. Count them all._

#### `lk10-line`

_It is the last night of summer. Everyone is here!_  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Kuih! Who wants kuih?  
**Bu Wulan**: And kue from me! Coconut, yum!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, notice): food from two countries  
> **Mak Cik Siti**: Kuih are little cakes from Malaysia.  
> **Bu Wulan**: Kue are little cakes from Indonesia. Nearly the same word!  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard about kuih and kue, little cakes from Malaysia and Indonesia._

**Pixel**: I made a second lamp. So everyone can see!  
_Tonight your Nubbin is Kancil. No puppet. Just itself!_  
**Bu Wulan**: Crocodiles! Line up, please!  
_The Nubbins float into the stream. Two lines, side by side!_  

#### `lk10-count`

**Mak Cik Siti**: We count my way first. Satu!  
_Your Nubbin hops. Everyone counts!_  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Dua, tiga, empat, lima, enam, tujuh...  
_At eight, the children shout: Delapan!_  
**Mak Cik Siti**: Lapan! Sembilan, sepuluh!  
_Ten more hops back on the other line. Squelch!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count to ten, twice  
> _(Count one line together, from one to ten.)_  
> _(Then count the other line. Ten and ten!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:crocodiles:20`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted one line of ten crocodiles, then the other._

**Bu Wulan**: Two lines of crocodiles! Hooray!  

#### `lk10-complete`

_The children sit on the bank, full of kuih and kue._  
**Mak Cik Siti**: What did Kancil learn this summer?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): thinking about what we learned  
> _(What do you think? Wait for an answer.)_  
> - Be clever. → Yes! Thinking hard helps when you are small.
> - Say thank you. → Yes! Kind words help a lot.
> - Don’t laugh at slow friends. → Yes. Slow is just slow. Be kind.
> _For grown-ups: Your child said what Kancil learned over the summer of stories._

**Bu Wulan**: We are leaving the screen by the pond. It lives here now.  
**Mak Cik Siti**: And we are staying for a while!  
_Your Nubbin makes the little puppet hop. One, two, three._  

## A2-1. Born from Stone

- `a02-01-s1`: Climb the painted mountain to the stone egg. · _Follow the smell of peaches uphill._
- `a02-01-s2`: Watch the stone egg hatch. · _Stay close to the egg._
- `a02-01-s3`: Look down from the clouds. · _Follow the gold light up._

#### `a02-01-page`

_Nova’s big book opens to a painted mountain._  
_Peach trees! A waterfall! Clouds like curly hair._  
_Whoosh! You and your Nubbin step into the picture._  
_Sniff, sniff. Everything smells of peaches._  
_At the top sits a big stone egg. It is taller than you!_  
_Your Nubbin walks round the egg. Round once. Round twice._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count to 2  
> _(Count the trips round the egg on your fingers. One. Two.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:laps:2`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted two trips round the egg._


**Choices**

- **Knock on the egg.**
    - Knock, knock! Something inside knocks back.
- **Sit down beside it and wait.**
    - You sit. Your Nubbin sits. The wind sits too.

#### `a02-01-page-done`

_A wind comes and leans on the egg. Push, push, push!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): wind is moving air that pushes  
> _Wind is air on the move. It can push leaves, kites and eggs._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that moving air can push things._


#### `a02-01-hatch`

_Crack! The egg breaks. A stone ball rolls out._  
_The ball unfolds into a little grey monkey._  
_He bows to the north. He bows to the south._  
_He bows to the east. He bows to the west._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, do): four directions: north, south, east, west  
> _(Stand up. Bow four ways with Monkey: north, south, east, west.)_  
> Check: `edu:point:compass:four-ways`
> _For grown-ups: Your child named the four compass directions._

**Monkey**: Ha! Who are you? You are very round for a rock.  
_Your Nubbin came out of an egg too. This is family!_  
**Monkey**: A cousin! You can have some of the view.  

#### `a02-01-hatch-done`

_Monkey’s eyes shine gold. Two beams of light shoot up high._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, notice): rhyming words: gold, old, cold  
> _Gold! Gold rhymes with old and cold. Can you think of another?_  
> _For grown-ups: Your child played with words that rhyme with "gold"._

_Far above, someone puts down his tea._  

#### `a02-01-heaven`

_The page lifts. Now you sit on a cloud, high up._  
**The Jade Emperor**: Two beams of light! Who is making a fuss?  
**A heavenly herald**: Only a little monkey, Majesty. Born this morning.  
**The Jade Emperor**: Let him play. Small things grow.  
_Your Nubbin leans over the cloud. It waves at a tiny grey dot._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): faraway things look small  
> _Monkey looks so tiny from the cloud. Why?_  
> - ✅ He is far away → Yes! Things that are far away look small.
> - He shrank → He did not shrink. Far-away things just look small. When he is close, he looks big again.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that faraway things look smaller._

_The tiny dot waves back!_  

#### `a02-01-complete`

_By evening, Monkey has learned to walk, then climb._  
_Next he eats peaches. Last he argues with the other monkeys._  
**Monkey**: Cousin! Tomorrow I will do something enormous.  
_He gives your Nubbin a peach. It is mostly bite marks!_  
_Your Nubbin holds it like treasure._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): sharing  
> _Your Nubbin has one peach, and Monkey has none. What is kind?_  
> - ✅ Share it → Yes! Sharing is kind. Now they both have some.
> - Eat it all → Then Monkey would be sad and hungry. Sharing is kinder. Your Nubbin shares.
> _For grown-ups: Your child chose sharing as the kind thing to do._

_Then your Nubbin breaks it in two and gives Monkey half._  

## A2-2. The Water-Curtain Cave

- `a02-02-s1`: Follow the stream to the waterfall. · _Walk up the stream with the monkeys._
- `a02-02-s2`: Jump through the waterfall. · _Dive in after Monkey._
- `a02-02-s3`: Join the monkeys’ feast. · _Sit down in the cave._

#### `a02-02-stream`

_It is a hot day. The monkeys splash in the stream._  
**An old gibbon**: Where does all this water come from?  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): streams come from rain on hills  
> _Where does the stream’s water come from?_  
> - ✅ Rain on the hills → Yes! Rain falls on the hills and runs down.
> - A big tap → No tap! Rain falls on the hills, and the water runs down. That is how a stream is born.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that streams are fed by rain running off hills._

_So everyone goes to look. Everyone means everyone!_  
_The stream ends at a waterfall. It hangs like a white curtain._  
**An old gibbon**: Who goes through the curtain and comes back? That one is king!  
**Monkey**: I will go! Rocks do not mind water.  
_Your Nubbin steps up beside him. It likes waterfalls._  

**Choices**

- **Tell them both to be careful.**
    - **Monkey**: Careful is for monkeys who are not going to be king.
- **Offer to count them in.**
    - **Monkey**: Yes! Count! Kings should start on a number.
    - You count: one, two, three. Monkey goes on two.

#### `a02-02-stream-done`

_Monkey crouches down. He shuts his eyes. He leaps!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, notice): syllables in "waterfall"  
> _Clap the word: wa-ter-fall. Three claps for three parts._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child clapped the three syllables of "waterfall"._


#### `a02-02-leap`

_Splash! Your Nubbin dives after him. You dive too._  
_The water thunders. Then it stops._  
_Behind the curtain it is dry! There is a cave._  
_Stone beds. Stone pots. Stone bowls._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.B.3, do): sort and count  
> _(Point to each kind. How many beds? Pots? Bowls? Count together.)_  
> Check: `edu:sort:cave-things:kind`
> _For grown-ups: Your child sorted cave things into kinds and counted each._

**Monkey**: Nobody lives here! It has a front door made of waterfall!  
_Your Nubbin tries every stone bed. They are all just right._  

#### `a02-02-leap-done`

_Monkey shoots out through the water, shouting._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, notice): sound is made by shaking  
> _A waterfall is loud. Loud sounds are big shakes in the air._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that sound comes from vibrations._

_Splash, splash, splash! Wet monkeys shoot in._  

#### `a02-02-king`

_The monkeys make him king. Hooray!_  
_Many feasts go by. Then one night, the king cries._  
**Monkey**: One day I will be old. One day I will stop.  
_Monkey is scared. His eyes are wet._  
_Your Nubbin climbs into his lap, to sit with him._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what helps when someone is scared  
> _Monkey is sad and scared. What helps?_  
> - ✅ A hug and a friend → Yes! Sitting close helps a lot.
> - Say hush → Saying hush does not help much. A hug and a friend do. That is what Nubbin gives.
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised comforting a scared friend._

**An old gibbon**: Some wise ones live for a very long time. Far away.  
**Monkey**: Then I will go and find them.  

**Choices**

- **Tell him growing old isn’t the worst thing.**
    - **Monkey**: You say that because you are not a king.
    - He keeps your Nubbin in his lap, though.
- **Tell him to go and find out.**
    - **Monkey**: Yes. That is the right answer!

#### `a02-02-complete`

_In the morning the monkeys build a raft._  
_They pile on fruit: one, two, three, four, five pieces._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _(Count the fruit on the raft together. One, two, three, four, five.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:fruit:5`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted five pieces of fruit._

_You and your Nubbin hop on too. Waving from shore is rude._  
**Monkey**: I will be back. And I will not ever have to stop.  
_The raft goes out over the big water. Everyone waves and waves._  

## A2-3. Lessons in Shape-Changing

- `a02-03-s1`: Visit Monkey’s teacher. · _Walk up to the cave with Monkey._
- `a02-03-s2`: Wait on the back step. · _Sit outside the back door._
- `a02-03-s3`: Watch Monkey under the pines. · _Stand in the yard._

#### `a02-03-lesson`

_High on a quiet mountain is a cave. A teacher lives there._  
**Master Subhuti**: A monkey. You shall be called Sun Wukong. You are mostly noise.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, notice): a name can have a meaning  
> _Wukong is a name. It has a meaning, like many names do._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that names often carry a meaning._

_Seven years go by. Monkey sweeps and sweeps the floor._  
**Master Subhuti**: I can teach you fortunes, or sitting still, or medicines.  
**Monkey**: Will any of them make me live for ever?  
**Master Subhuti**: No.  
**Monkey**: Then no, thank you.  
_The teacher taps Monkey three times on the head. Tap, tap, tap!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count to 3  
> _(Gently tap your own head three times. One, two, three.)_  
> Check: `edu:tap:head:3`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted three taps._

_He walks out with his hands behind his back. Monkey grins._  

**Choices**

- **Ask Monkey why he’s grinning.**
    - **Monkey**: Three taps. Come at the third watch of the night.
    - **Monkey**: Hands behind his back. Use the back door!
    - **Monkey**: It is a secret. Do not tell Cousin. It cannot keep one.
- **Work it out for yourself.**
    - Three taps. Hands behind the back. Monkey winks at you.

#### `a02-03-night`

_In the deep of the night, the back door opens a crack._  
_Monkey slips in. You sit on the step outside._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): night and day  
> _Monkey comes in the night. When is it dark outside?_  
> - ✅ At night → Yes! The sky is dark at night, with stars.
> - At lunch time → At lunch time the sun is high and bright. It is dark at night.
> _For grown-ups: Your child linked darkness to night-time._

_Your Nubbin falls asleep. Snore, snore, snore._  
_Years of nights go by. Then Monkey comes out, walking on air!_  
**Monkey**: I can be anything! And look at this!  
_He somersaults on a cloud. Whoosh! He is gone, then back._  

#### `a02-03-pine`

_The other students gather under the pine trees._  
**Monkey**: A pine tree? Easy!  
_Pop! Monkey is a pine tree. The students cheer._  
_Your Nubbin copies. It holds its arms up very still._  
**Master Subhuti**: Who is shouting in my yard?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): listening and feelings  
> _The teacher is cross. How does Monkey feel now?_  
> - ✅ Sorry and sad → Yes. He feels sorry. That is a big feeling.
> - Very proud → He was proud. But now he is sorry and sad. Feelings can change very fast.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named a changing feeling._

_Pop! The pine tree is a monkey again._  
**Master Subhuti**: Showing off makes trouble. Go home, Monkey.  

**Choices**

- **Tell the teacher Monkey meant no harm.**
    - **Master Subhuti**: I know. That is the trouble. He never means any.
- **Stay out of it.**
    - You stay out of it. Your Nubbin, still a pine tree, does too.

#### `a02-03-complete`

_Monkey bows to his teacher. All the way to the floor._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): bowing is a polite thing in China  
> _In China, a bow can mean thank you and respect._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that bowing can show thanks and respect._

**Monkey**: Hold on to my tail, Cousin’s keeper. I know a quick way.  
_One somersault. The world rolls by like a rug._  
_Then there are peaches again!_  
_Your Nubbin tumbles onto the grass. It beams. Again, please!_  

## A2-4. Havoc in Heaven

- `a02-04-s1`: Visit the heavenly stables. · _Go up to Heaven with Monkey._
- `a02-04-s2`: Look at the peaches in the garden. · _Walk among the trees._
- `a02-04-s3`: Watch Monkey at the feast. · _Go to the Jade Pool._

#### `a02-04-stables`

_Heaven gives Monkey a job. He looks after the horses._  
**Monkey**: A grand title! They must think a lot of me.  
_The horses grow fat and shiny. Your Nubbin rides one._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): what animals need  
> _The horses grow fat and shiny. What do horses need?_  
> - ✅ Grass, water and care → Yes! Food, water and care keep them well.
> - Only sweets → Sweets are not good for a horse. Horses need grass, water and care.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named what a horse needs to live._

**Monkey**: What rank is horse-keeper, exactly?  
_It is the smallest job in Heaven. Monkey throws down his hat._  
_He goes straight home, cross as a cat._  

#### `a02-04-stables-done`

**The Jade Emperor**: Give him the Peach Garden to look after. It will keep him busy.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): a big feeling needs a good job to do  
> _When we feel cross, a calm job can help, like digging, painting or walking._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that a calming activity can help with a cross feeling._


#### `a02-04-garden`

**The garden spirit**: So many trees, Great Sage! Seven rows of peaches.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 7  
> _(Count the rows of trees on your fingers. Seven!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:rows:7`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted seven rows of peach trees._

_Your Nubbin goes very still. It looks at the peaches._  
**Monkey**: Thank you. You may go. I will inspect the trees alone.  
_The spirit goes. Monkey climbs the oldest tree._  
_He eats the best peach, then the next best. Then he naps._  
_A ripe peach drops by your Nubbin’s feet. It glows a little._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a seed is inside the fruit  
> _Inside a peach is a big stone, and inside the stone is a seed._  
> _The seed can grow into a new peach tree._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that fruit holds a seed that can grow into a tree._


**Choices**

- **Hang the peach back on its branch.**
    - It will not stay. You put it gently at the foot of the tree.
    - Your Nubbin sighs from its toes, and lets it go.
- **Let your Nubbin sniff it, and no more.**
    - Sniff, sniff, sniff! It glows a little, then leaves it be.

#### `a02-04-banquet`

_Seven fairy maidens come to pick peaches._  
_(Count the maidens. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.)_  
_They tell Monkey who is invited. Everyone, except him._  
**Monkey**: Everyone?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): being left out and what to do  
> _Monkey was left out. How would that feel?_  
> - ✅ Sad and cross → Yes. Being left out feels sad and cross.
> - Happy → Most people feel sad when they are left out. Monkey felt sad and cross.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named the feelings that come with being left out._

_Monkey is hurt and cross. He makes the maidens freeze like statues._  
_Then he eats the whole feast, and the magic pills too._  
**Monkey**: Oh. That might have been a mistake.  
**Monkey**: Cousin! Home! Now!  

#### `a02-04-complete`

_Heaven sends its soldiers. Bonk! Bonk! Helmets ring like bells._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): loud and quiet sounds  
> _A helmet can ring like a drum._  
> _(Tap softly on the table. Now tap loudly. Can you hear the difference?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Your child noticed loud and quiet sounds._

**Monkey**: Equal to Heaven? I am better than equal. Tell them, Cousin.  
_Your Nubbin hides behind a rock. It would rather not._  
_The fairy maidens unfreeze at last and see the empty trees._

## A2-5. Under the Mountain

- `a02-05-s1`: Wait by the furnace door. · _Sit by the furnace._
- `a02-05-s2`: Talk with the Buddha. · _Stand near the Buddha’s hand._
- `a02-05-s3`: Sit with Monkey under the mountain. · _Climb down and sit by his hand._

#### `a02-05-furnace`

_Monkey is hard to stop. So Lord Lao puts him in a furnace._  
_For forty-nine days, the fire burns. Your Nubbin waits, like a good friend._  

> **Lesson** (health, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): staying back from fire  
> _The furnace is very hot. What do we do near a hot fire?_  
> - ✅ Stay well back → Yes! Hot things can burn. We stay well back.
> - Touch it → Ouch! Hot things burn. We stay well back from a fire.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned to stay well back from fire._

_Monkey hides in the one corner that is only wind._  
_Out he jumps! His eyes are two little suns._  
**Monkey**: Cousin! You waited. I am going to be rude to everyone.  
_He runs the length of Heaven. Generals tumble like skittles._  

#### `a02-05-furnace-done`

**The Jade Emperor**: Fetch the Buddha. Ask him, please, to come.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): asking for help is brave  
> _Even a big, strong emperor asks for help sometimes. That is wise._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that asking for help is wise._


#### `a02-05-palm`

_The Buddha comes in quietly. Everything goes quiet._  
**The Buddha**: What is it you want?  
**Monkey**: The big throne. It is my turn.  
**The Buddha**: Then jump out of my right hand, and it is yours.  
**Monkey**: Your hand is tiny! I go far in one somersault!  
_Monkey jumps onto the palm. Zoom! He is gone._  
_He flies to five pink pillars at the edge of the world._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count to 5 on your fingers  
> _(Hold up one hand. Count the five fingers, one by one.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:fingers:5`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted five fingers._

_He writes his name on the middle one. But look: the pillars are fingers!_  

**Choices**

- **When he lands, tell him gently: it was the hand all along.**
    - **Monkey**: Rubbish! I went to the end of the world.
- **Say nothing. Let the Buddha show him.**
    - You say nothing. The Buddha glances at you, and his face says thank you.

#### `a02-05-palm-done`

_The Buddha lifts his hand. On one finger is a name, in tiny writing._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): writing carries a message  
> _Someone wrote a name on the finger. Who wrote it?_  
> - ✅ Monkey did → Yes. Monkey wrote it, on a finger!
> - The Buddha did → The Buddha did not. Monkey did.
> _For grown-ups: Your child understood that writing records a message from a writer._

**Monkey**: That cannot be. I went…  

#### `a02-05-mountain`

_The Buddha turns his hand over. It becomes a mountain._  
_Monkey is under it. He is not hurt, only stopped._  
**The Buddha**: Feed him when he is hungry. Give him water when he is thirsty.  
**Monkey**: For how long?  
**The Buddha**: Until he has learned. Then someone will come.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): sitting with a friend who is sad  
> _Monkey is sad and stuck. How does your Nubbin help?_  
> - ✅ It stays beside him → Yes. Being there is a big help.
> - It runs away → It does not run away. It stays. Staying beside a sad friend helps.
> _For grown-ups: Your child saw that staying beside a sad friend is a help._

_Your Nubbin sits by his free hand. Monkey holds its foot._  

#### `a02-05-complete`

_The Queen Mother of the West brings a dish of peaches._  
**The Queen Mother of the West**: You stood by my trees and took nothing. This one is given.  
_Your Nubbin eats it slowly and glows like a lantern._  
**The Queen Mother of the West**: Keep the stone. Plant it where you will be glad to see it.  
_The page turns, and turns. Many years pass._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): plants grow from seeds, slowly  
> _A peach stone is a seed. It grows into a tree, slowly._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that some things in nature change very slowly._

_Moss grows on Monkey’s hand. Your Nubbin keeps its foot there._  

## A2-6. The Monk

- `a02-06-s1`: Walk with the monk to the edge of the land. · _Carry his luggage._
- `a02-06-s2`: Climb the mountain to the gold paper. · _Hold the staff and push._
- `a02-06-s3`: Wait by the road. · _Sit and let things calm down._

#### `a02-06-road`

_A monk comes along the road on a pale horse._  
_He has a bowl, a staff, a robe, and far too much luggage._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Good morning. Is this the road west?  
**Tang Sanzang**: I am Tang Sanzang. I must fetch books from India.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): the sun sets in the west  
> _The monk walks west. Where does the sun go down?_  
> - ✅ In the west → Yes! The sun sets in the west. The monk follows it.
> - In the east → The sun comes up in the east. It goes down in the west, where the monk is going.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that the sun sets in the west._

**Tang Sanzang**: You carry nothing. I carry everything. May I ask for help?  
_You take the luggage. Your Nubbin climbs on top of it._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): heavier and lighter  
> _Your Nubbin sits on the luggage. Is it heavier or lighter now?_  
> - ✅ Heavier → Yes! More weight on top makes it heavier.
> - Lighter → Not lighter. Your Nubbin adds weight. So it is heavier now.
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared a load with and without an extra weight._

**Tang Sanzang**: Thank you. You are my second disciple. I keep forgetting the horse.  

#### `a02-06-road-done`

_From the mountain ahead, a voice shouts. Loud!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): loud and quiet voices  
> _Is that a shout, or a whisper?_  
> - ✅ A shout → Yes! A shout is a big loud voice.
> - A whisper → A whisper is very quiet. This voice shakes leaves! That is a shout.
> _For grown-ups: Your child told a shout from a whisper._

_It shakes the leaves._  

#### `a02-06-seal`

**Monkey**: Master! You came! A lady told me to wait for a monk!  
_Monkey’s head sticks out of the mountain. There is grass in his ears._  
**Monkey**: Cousin! You are still here.  
**Tang Sanzang**: Oh dear. Are you a demon?  
**Monkey**: I am your disciple. Please peel the paper off the top.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): top and bottom  
> _Where is the gold paper? At the top, or the bottom?_  
> - ✅ At the top → Yes! Up at the top of the mountain.
> - At the bottom → Monkey is at the bottom, by the grass. The paper is at the top.
> _For grown-ups: Your child used the words top and bottom._

_The monk climbs. You hold his staff and push._  
_At the top is a strip of gold paper. He peels it, gently._  

#### `a02-06-seal-done`

_The mountain splits like bread. Monkey bounds out!_  
_He bows to the monk four times. Then he hugs your Nubbin._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying thank you  
> _Monkey bows to say thank you. What do we say when someone helps us?_  
> - ✅ Thank you → Yes! Thank you. Say it with Monkey.
> - Nothing → We can say something kind. Thank you makes a helper smile.
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised saying thank you._

**Monkey**: Right! Where are we going? India? Easy!  

#### `a02-06-band`

_Six robbers jump out of the trees. Boo!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 6  
> _(Count the robbers on your fingers. One to six.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:robbers:6`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted six robbers._

_Monkey chases them over three hills. Soon they are gone._  
**Tang Sanzang**: You frightened them! A monk must not do that.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): what to do instead of scaring people  
> _The monk says Monkey scared them. What could Monkey do instead?_  
> - ✅ Ask them to stop → Yes! Asking kindly can work too.
> - Scare them more → That would frighten them even more. Asking them to stop is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about a kinder way to stop trouble._

**Monkey**: I just helped, and this is the thanks?  
_Monkey somersaults away. The road is empty._  
_A kind old lady gives the monk a cap with a gold band._  
_Monkey comes back and puts it on. He likes it._  
_The monk says some quiet words. The band gets snug!_  
_Monkey hops round the road, holding his head._  

**Choices**

- **Ask the monk to stop.**
    - **Tang Sanzang**: Oh! Yes. I had no idea it was so strong.
    - **Tang Sanzang**: I will only use it when I must. I promise.
- **Wait. He’s stopping already.**
    - The monk stops at once. He looks as shaken as Monkey.

#### `a02-06-complete`

_Monkey tugs at the band. It will not come off._  
**Monkey**: Fine. I will behave. Mostly. Some of the time.  
**Tang Sanzang**: That is all anyone can promise.  
_You pick up the luggage. Your Nubbin climbs on._  
_The monk, Monkey, you, your Nubbin, and the horse go west._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _(Count them: monk, Monkey, you, Nubbin, horse. How many?)_  
> Check: `edu:count:travellers:5`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted five travellers._


## A2-7. The White Dragon Horse

- `a02-07-s1`: Walk to Eagle Grief Stream. · _Follow the rushing water._
- `a02-07-s2`: Talk with the lady with the vase. · _Stand by the water._
- `a02-07-s3`: Watch the dragon change. · _Stay by the bank._

#### `a02-07-stream`

_Eagle Grief Stream runs fast and green between steep rocks._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): streams flow downhill  
> _The stream rushes between the rocks. Which way does water run?_  
> - ✅ Downhill → Yes! Water runs down, from high to low.
> - Uphill → Water does not run uphill by itself. It runs downhill. That is why the stream is so quick!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that water flows downhill._

_The horse does not like it. Your Nubbin does not either._  
_Splash! A white dragon swoops up. It carries off the horse!_  
**Tang Sanzang**: My horse! How will I cross the world now?  
**Monkey**: I will get it back. Wait there.  
**Monkey**: It will not come out. Water is cheating.  
_Your Nubbin peeks into the stream. It sees a long white shape, sulking._  

#### `a02-07-stream-done`

**Monkey**: Local spirits say a lady put that dragon here.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): where a story happens  
> _Where are our friends now? In a cave, or by a stream?_  
> - ✅ By a stream → Yes! By Eagle Grief Stream.
> - In a cave → Not a cave this time. They are by a stream, with rushing water.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named the setting of the scene._

**Monkey**: I know which lady. I will fetch her.  

#### `a02-07-guanyin`

_A soft light comes over the water, like morning._  
_In it stands a lady with a vase and a willow branch._  
_You know her kind eyes. She was the old woman on the road!_  
**Monkey**: You gave him the band!  
**Guanyin**: I did. You are clever, Monkey. Clever ones need a friend beside them.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): willow trees grow by water  
> _Willow trees love water. They often grow beside streams and ponds._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that willow trees grow near water._

_Your Nubbin gives her a pebble, its very best gift. She smiles._  

#### `a02-07-dragon`

**Guanyin**: Prince Yulong, come up. The monk is on your bank.  
_The white dragon rises up, dripping and ashamed._  
**Prince Yulong**: I did not know who he was. I was hungry, and cross, and sad.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying sorry  
> _The dragon says he is sorry. Why does saying sorry help?_  
> - ✅ It shows you care → Yes! Sorry says: I know I was wrong.
> - It does not help → It does help. Sorry shows you care about the other person.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard why saying sorry helps._

**Guanyin**: Then be something better. Carry him all the way.  
_She touches him with the willow branch. He shrinks, and changes._  
_Now a white horse stands on the bank. He shakes his mane. Splash!_  

**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin give the horse its peach stone to sniff.**
    - The horse sniffs the stone and blows softly. A friendship begins.
- **Stroke his nose.**
    - He lets you. His nose is cool, like the inside of a river.

#### `a02-07-complete`

_Guanyin gives Monkey three willow hairs, for when he needs them._  
**Tang Sanzang**: A dragon. I am riding a dragon!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): the Chinese zodiac: Dragon is fifth, Horse is seventh  
> _In an old race, Dragon was fifth and Horse was seventh. Who was ahead?_  
> - ✅ Dragon was ahead of Horse → Yes! Fifth comes before seventh.
> - Horse was ahead of Dragon → Dragon was fifth, and Horse was seventh. So Dragon was ahead. Five comes before seven!
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared the order of two zodiac animals._

**Monkey**: Nobody at home will believe that. Get used to it.  
_The white horse carries the monk with great care._  

## A2-8. The Stolen Robe

#### `a02-08-hall`

_The monastery is rich. The abbot is very old._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.B.3, do): sort by colour  
> _(Sort the robes by colour: reds here, blues there. Count each pile.)_  
> Check: `edu:sort:robes:colour`
> _For grown-ups: Your child sorted robes into colour groups._

**Monkey**: My master has one better. Show him, master.

> - Hide under the bed → Hiding is not safe. Get out, stay low, and tell a grown-up.

- **Wake the monk. He would want to know.**
    - **Tang Sanzang**: Fire? Then everyone out. I do not care who started it.
    - Monkey groans, and blows the fire away from the beds.

> - ✅ A circle → Yes! A circle, round all the way.
> - A square → A square has four corners. This pill has none. It is a circle.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named a circle._

**The Black Bear**: A gift from my friend! How kind.

## A2-9. Pigsy

#### `a02-09-gao`

**Old Gao**: A strong young man came here three years ago.

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): which animal has a snout  
> _Big ears and a long snout. Which animal does that sound like?_  
> - ✅ A pig → Yes! A pig has a snout and big ears.
> - A bird → A bird has a beak, not a snout. Big ears and a snout sound like a pig.
> _For grown-ups: Your child matched body parts to an animal._

**Old Gao**: He keeps my daughter in the back house. Can you help?

**Tang Sanzang**: A what?

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, do): staying quiet and still  
> _(Put a finger on your lips. Hide as still as a mouse. Shh!)_  
> Check: `edu:hush:finger-on-lips`
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised staying quiet and still._

_The door blows open. In comes a round, bristly fellow with flowers._  
**Pigsy**: I brought flowers. Why are you so hairy tonight, my dear?

> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that plants need water and light._

**Pigsy**: The lady told me to wait for him! I got hungry while I waited.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): waiting is hard; calming ideas help  
> _Waiting is hard when you are hungry. What helps us wait?_  
> - ✅ Singing or counting → Yes! Singing, counting and deep breaths help.
> - Giving up → Giving up is easy, but waiting was worth it. Singing or counting makes waiting easier.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard calming ideas for waiting._


**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin give him back his flowers.**
    - **Pigsy**: You kept them! Oh, you good little thing. I like you.
- **Tell him there’s room on the road.**
    - **Pigsy**: Is there room for lunch on the road? That is the main thing.

#### `a02-09-complete`

_He walks back to Gao Village with his rake on his shoulder._  
**Tang Sanzang**: You shall be called Bajie. It means Eight Rules.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): the Pig is the last animal in the Chinese zodiac  
> _The Pig came last in the old race. Pigsy is a pig._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that the pig is the twelfth zodiac animal._

**Pigsy**: Pigsy for short. Everyone does.  
**Pigsy**: Keep my room for me, will you? Just in case.  
_Pigsy carries the luggage pole for a whole mile._  

## A2-10. Sandy

- `a02-10-s1`: Walk to the River of Flowing Sands. · _Follow the monk to the bank._
- `a02-10-s2`: Swim down to meet the river spirit. · _Follow your Nubbin into the water._
- `a02-10-s3`: Wait on the bank for Moksa. · _Sit and watch the water._

#### `a02-10-river`

_The River of Flowing Sands is wide, and the colour of weak tea._  
_A stone says not even a feather floats on it._  
_Your Nubbin drops a feather in. Plop! It sinks._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, do): sink or float  
> _(Try a leaf, a spoon and a stone in water. Sink or float?)_  
> Check: `edu:sort:things:sink-float`
> _For grown-ups: Your child sorted objects by whether they sink or float._

**Pigsy**: Well, that is that. Back to Gao Village!  
_A big blue-faced river spirit rises out of the water._  
_Monkey and Pigsy splash and bellow. They come up spitting sand._  

#### `a02-10-under`

_Your Nubbin slips into the river. You hold your breath and follow._  
_Down in the brown water, the river spirit sits alone._  
_He is not frightening here. He looks like he has waited a long time._  
**Sandy**: Every traveller wants to fight me or run away.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being kind to someone lonely  
> _Sandy is lonely. What does your Nubbin do to help?_  
> - ✅ Pats his knee → Yes! A pat says: I am here, friend.
> - Swims away → Your Nubbin does not swim away. A pat and a smile help a lonely friend.
> _For grown-ups: Your child saw a kind way to help someone who is lonely._

**Sandy**: I used to work in Heaven. I broke one crystal cup. One!  
_Your Nubbin pats his knee. He pats it back._  

#### `a02-10-under-done`

_You come up gasping. Big breath in!_  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): a slow, calming breath  
> _(Breathe in slowly, and out slowly, like blowing a feather. Twice.)_  
> Check: `edu:breathe:slow:in-out`
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised slow breathing._

_Monkey has somersaulted off to the South Sea to fetch help._  

#### `a02-10-moksa`

_Monkey comes back with Moksa. He carries a small red gourd._  
**Moksa**: Sha Wujing! The monk you were waiting for is on the bank. Come up.  
_The river spirit comes up. He kneels on the sand._  
**Sandy**: I did not know. He looks so ordinary.  
**Tang Sanzang**: I am very ordinary. That is rather the point.  
_Moksa puts the gourd on the water. It grows into a raft!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): a raft floats  
> _The gourd grows into a raft. Will a raft sink or float?_  
> - ✅ Float → Yes! A raft floats and carries us over the water.
> - Sink → A raft is made to float. It floats, so it carries us over.
> _For grown-ups: Your child predicted that a raft floats._


**Choices**

- **Offer Sandy the other end of the luggage pole.**
    - **Sandy**: Thank you. I like carrying things. You know where you are with a weight.
- **Help Sandy load the raft.**
    - He loads it neatly, heaviest at the bottom.
    - Pigsy sits on the lightest bit and calls it helping.

#### `a02-10-complete`

_The raft crosses the wide river in an afternoon._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Wujing. We shall call you Sandy.  
**Tang Sanzang**: Wukong, Bajie, Wujing, the horse, and you. I have the count right!  
_Now there are six of you, and the horse._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 6  
> _(Count the friends: monk, Monkey, Pigsy, Sandy, you, Nubbin. Six!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:pilgrims:6`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted six travelling friends._

_Sandy takes the back of the pole. You take the front._  

## A2-11. The Ginseng Fruit

- `a02-11-s1`: Visit the quiet temple. · _Walk in with the monk._
- `a02-11-s2`: Look at the tree in the garden. · _Go to the garden._
- `a02-11-s3`: Carry water to the tree. · _Pour it very gently._

#### `a02-11-temple`

_The temple is quiet and lovely. Its master is away._  
_Two young helpers look after it: Bright Moon and Pure Wind._  
**Bright Moon**: Our master said a monk would come. We must give him two fruits.  
**Pure Wind**: They ripen once in a very, very long time.  
_They bring two fruits on a dish. Each looks like a tiny sleeping baby._  
**Tang Sanzang**: No thank you. Please take them away.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying no politely  
> _The monk says no, kindly. What do we say instead of yuck?_  
> - ✅ No thank you → Yes! No thank you is polite and clear.
> - Yuck! → Yuck can hurt feelings. No thank you is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised saying no politely._

_So the helpers eat them in the kitchen. Pigsy listens at the wall._  
_He makes a small, hungry sound._  

#### `a02-11-tree`

**Pigsy**: Brother. Wise brother. Just three. One each. Nobody would notice.  
_Monkey knocks a fruit down. It sinks into the ground like water._  
_He knocks down three more. Monkey, Pigsy and Sandy eat one each._  
**Pigsy**: I did not taste it! I swallowed it whole!  
_The helpers count their fruit. They come back shouting._  
**Monkey**: Then nobody gets any!  
_Monkey pushes the whole tree over. Its roots come up out of the ground._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, notice): roots hold a tree and drink water  
> _Roots hold a tree in the ground._  
> _Roots drink water, too. A tree needs both._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that roots anchor a plant and take in water._


**Choices**

- **Tell the acolytes the truth: you saw it all.**
    - **Bright Moon**: Thank you. At least someone is honest.
    - Monkey glares at you. Then he stops glaring.
- **Go and kneel by the fallen tree.**
    - Its leaves are curling. Your Nubbin lies down beside the roots.

#### `a02-11-tree-done`

_The master comes home that night. He sweeps up all of you, gently._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): mending a mistake  
> _When we break something, we can help mend it. That is brave._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that fixing a mistake is brave and helpful._

**Master Zhenyuan**: Mend my tree, and I will let you go.  

#### `a02-11-mend`

_Monkey searches three islands for a cure. Nobody has one._  
_At last he goes to the South Sea. Guanyin comes with her vase._  
**Guanyin**: Bring water, in jade cups. Pour gently.  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, ask): plants need water  
> _The tree is drooping. What does it need most?_  
> - ✅ Water → Yes! Water helps a thirsty tree stand tall.
> - A hat → A hat is fun, but trees need water.
> _For grown-ups: Your child said that plants need water._

_You carry cup after cup. Your Nubbin has a very small cup._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): bigger and smaller cups  
> _Which holds more water: the big jade cup, or your Nubbin’s small cup?_  
> - ✅ The big cup → Yes! The big cup holds more.
> - The small cup → The small cup holds less. The big cup holds more.
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared how much two cups hold._

_It pours very slowly, and gets most of it in._  
_Guanyin sprinkles dew, and the tree stands up! Its leaves are green and glossy._  

#### `a02-11-complete`

**Master Zhenyuan**: That is the most trouble in a thousand years. Come and eat.  
_There is a feast. This time the monk eats one fruit._  
**Tang Sanzang**: It tastes like the first morning of spring.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words for tastes and seasons  
> _The monk says it tastes like spring morning. Is that fresh, or old?_  
> - ✅ Fresh → Yes! Fresh and new, like a new day.
> - Old → Spring mornings are fresh and new. That is the idea.
> _For grown-ups: Your child understood a describing phrase about taste._

_Master Zhenyuan and Monkey promise to be brothers._  
_Monkey looks a little shy, which is new._  

## A2-12. The White Bone Demon

- `a02-12-s1`: Watch the girl on White Tiger Ridge. · _Stay by the monk._
- `a02-12-s2`: Watch the old woman on the ridge. · _Stay by the monk._
- `a02-12-s3`: Choose who to believe. · _Think about what you saw, and tell your reason._
- `a02-12-s4`: Walk to the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. · _Go with Pigsy._

#### `a02-12-girl`

_White Tiger Ridge is bare rock and thin wind._  
_The monk is hungry. Monkey has gone to find fruit._  
_A girl comes with a basket of rice and noodles. She does not blink._  
**A stranger on the ridge**: Kind travellers! Please eat.  
_Your Nubbin hides behind your legs. It never hides from food._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): listening to a worried feeling  
> _Your Nubbin feels scared and hides. What can we do if something feels odd?_  
> - ✅ Tell someone we trust → Yes! Tell a grown-up or a friend.
> - Keep it secret → Secrets can make worried feelings bigger. Tell someone you trust.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that telling a trusted person helps with a worried feeling._

_Monkey comes back, takes one look, and taps her with his staff._  
_Poof! She flops like an empty coat. A cold puff floats away._  
**Tang Sanzang**: She was only a girl!  
**Monkey**: Look in the basket. No noodles. Only worms and frogs.  

#### `a02-12-girl-done`

_The monk says the quiet words. Monkey holds his head and says nothing._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character shows a feeling  
> _Monkey holds his head and goes quiet. How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Hurt and sad → Yes. His head hurts, and his heart feels hurt too.
> - Very happy → Not happy. He goes quiet because he feels hurt.
> _For grown-ups: Your child read a feeling from what a character does._


#### `a02-12-old-woman`

_An old woman comes up the path, leaning on a stick._  
**A stranger on the ridge**: Have you seen my girl? She went this way.  
_She does not blink either. Your Nubbin shakes against your ankles._  
_Monkey taps. The old woman folds away like paper._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Twice! In one morning!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count to 2  
> _(Count the visitors so far: a girl, an old woman. Two!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:visitors:2`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted two visitors._

**Monkey**: The same trickster. She keeps coming back.  

#### `a02-12-bones`

_An old man comes last, with prayer beads. He does not blink._  
_Monkey calls the mountain spirits to stand guard. Then he taps._  
_The old man folds up. Where he stood is a chalky heap of bones._  
**Monkey**: Bones. There is your trickster. Now do you believe me?  
**Pigsy**: He made them look like bones. It is a trick!  
**Tang Sanzang**: Three people, Wukong. I cannot walk beside that.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): friends can disagree, and listen  
> _When friends disagree, we can say what we saw. We can listen too._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that friends can disagree and still listen to each other._

**Tang Sanzang**: You carry our things. You have seen it all. What do you think?  

**Choices**

- **Believe Monkey. You saw your Nubbin hide.**
    - **You**: I believe him. My Nubbin hid from her three times.
    - **Tang Sanzang**: A Nubbin’s feelings are not proof. I am sorry.
    - **Monkey**: Thank you. Remember you said it.
- **Believe the monk. You can’t strike people on a hunch.**
    - **You**: Even if you are right, you cannot hit people because you are sure.
    - **Monkey**: I was not sure. I knew.
    - **Monkey**: Fine. Remember you said it, Cousin’s keeper.

#### `a02-12-bones-done`

_Monkey will not leave without a bow. He pulls three hairs and blows._  
_Three more Monkeys! Four Monkeys bow to the monk, all round him._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, do): one and three more make four  
> _(Hold up one finger, then three more. How many Monkeys? Four!)_  
> Check: `edu:add:monkeys:1+3`
> _For grown-ups: Your child added one and three to make four._

_Then Monkey is gone. Your Nubbin sits in the road, looking._  

#### `a02-12-return`

_Without Monkey, it goes badly. A yellow-robed trickster grabs the monk._  
**Pigsy**: I will have to fetch him. I will have to say sorry.  
**Pigsy**: I hate saying sorry. You come too. It is easier with two.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, notice): words that sound the same: too and two  
> _Listen: “You come too. It is easier with two.”_  
> _Too and two sound the same!_  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard two words that sound the same but mean different things._

_On the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, Monkey is king again._  
**Pigsy**: The trickster says you are just a jumped-up monkey.  
**Monkey**: He said that? Right.  
_Pigsy winks at you. It is the cleverest thing he has done._  

#### `a02-12-return-done`

_Monkey sends the trickster flying. The monk is a monk again, shaky._  
**Tang Sanzang**: I was wrong to send you away, Wukong. I am sorry.  
**Monkey**: I am scared of how strong I am, too, sometimes.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): it is okay to be scared  
> _Monkey says he is sometimes scared of his own strength. Is that okay?_  
> - ✅ Yes, it is okay → Yes. Even strong people feel scared. Saying so helps.
> - No → It is okay. Everyone feels scared sometimes, even Monkey.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that feeling scared is normal and okay to say._


#### `a02-12-complete`

_The monk takes Monkey’s hand in both of his._  
_It is the first time either of them has done that._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _(Count the hands: Monkey’s one hand, and the monk’s two. One, two, three!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:hands:3`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted three hands._

_Sandy picks up the back of the pole. You pick up the front._  
**Monkey**: Cousin’s keeper. I have not forgotten what you said.  
_Your Nubbin rides on his shoulder the rest of the day._  

## A2-13. The Magic Gourd

- `a02-13-s1`: Talk with Monkey in the pine wood. · _Listen to the rule._
- `a02-13-s2`: Wait at the cave and do not answer. · _Keep your mouth shut._
- `a02-13-s3`: Watch the gourd get swapped. · _Stay still and quiet._

#### `a02-13-rule`

_Two sly brothers, Gold Horn and Silver Horn, have caught the monk._  
_They have a magic gourd that calls your name._  
**Monkey**: If you answer, whoosh! You are inside.  
**Sandy**: So do not answer.  

> **Lesson** (health, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): stay with your grown-up  
> _A stranger calls your name. What do you do?_  
> - ✅ Stay close to my grown-up → Yes! Stay close and tell your grown-up.
> - Go and see → Do not go with someone you do not know. Stay close to your grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned to stay close to a trusted grown-up if a stranger calls._

**Monkey**: I answered a made-up name. It still got me!  
_Your Nubbin checks that its own mouth is shut._  

#### `a02-13-gourd`

_Silver Horn holds the gourd upside down at the cave mouth._  
**Silver Horn**: Little round one! Little Nubbin!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the syllables in "Nubbin"  
> _(Clap the name: Nub-bin. Two claps, two parts.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:nubbin`
> _For grown-ups: Your child clapped the two syllables of "Nubbin"._

_Your Nubbin blinks. It says nothing at all._  
**Silver Horn**: Answer me! It is rude not to answer!  
_He shakes the gourd. Then he looks at you._  
**Silver Horn**: You, carrying the luggage. Answer me!  

**Choices**

- **Keep your mouth shut, like your Nubbin.**
    - You say nothing. Your Nubbin looks up at you, very proud.
- **Start to say, “Who wants to know?”**
    - You begin “Who”, and the gourd pulls! Monkey tugs you behind a rock.
    - **Monkey**: What did I just say? What did I literally just say?

#### `a02-13-swap`

_While Silver Horn shouts, a little fly lands on his sleeve._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 6  
> _(A fly has six legs. Count them on your fingers. One to six.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:legs:6`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted six legs on a fly._

_A moment later, his gourd is swapped for a fake!_  
_Monkey stands on a rock with the real one, upside down._  
**Monkey**: Silver Horn!  
**Silver Horn**: What?  
_Whoosh! Monkey puts the stopper in._  

#### `a02-13-swap-done`

_Gold Horn goes the same way. Sandy unties the monk, and Pigsy, who grumbles._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being patient with a grumbler  
> _Pigsy grumbles while Sandy unties him. What is Sandy being?_  
> - ✅ Patient and kind → Yes! Sandy is patient. Grumblers need kind friends.
> - Cross → Sandy is not cross. He stays patient and kind.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named patience in a friend._


#### `a02-13-complete`

_An old man with a long white beard walks out of the clouds._  
**Lord Lao**: Those two are my helpers. They took my gourd. May I have it back?  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): giving things back to their owner  
> _The gourd belongs to Lord Lao. What is the right thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Give it back → Yes! Things go back to the one they belong to.
> - Keep it → It is not ours to keep. We give it back.
> _For grown-ups: Your child chose to return something to its owner._

**Monkey**: You might have kept a closer eye.  
**Lord Lao**: So might the Jade Emperor, on you. Yet here we all are.  
_He leads both brothers home, by the hand._

- `a02-15-s4`: Talk with the Buddha. · _Follow the Monkeys to the hall._

#### `a02-15-snatch`

_Bandits on the road again! Monkey is too rough, so he is sent away._  
_Everyone is tired. Pigsy goes for water, and Sandy follows._  
_Then Monkey comes back alone, with a cup of water._

_The monk sits up, dizzy but not hurt._  

#### `a02-15-twins`

_Sandy brings news. Monkey is on the Mountain, with a monk and a Pigsy._  
_At Guanyin’s island, Sandy finds the real Monkey, sulking._  
_Then the other one turns up. There are two Monkeys!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): same and different, two of something  
> _(How many Monkeys now? Point to each one. Two!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:monkeys:2`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted two Monkeys._

**Monkey**: Who are you? Why do you have my face?  
**Monkey**: Who are you? Why do you have my face?  
**Guanyin**: I cannot tell them apart.  
_Even the Jade Emperor’s mirror shows two, exactly the same._  
_Your Nubbin looks from one to the other. It cries, and that is okay._  

#### `a02-15-which`

_The two Monkeys tumble down. They land in front of the monk._  
_The monk looks at you, not at them._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Which one is my disciple?  
_Two staffs. Two gold bands. Both faces look at you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): it is okay to say "I don’t know"  
> _You cannot tell which is the real Monkey. What can you say?_  
> - ✅ I do not know → Yes! “I do not know” is a true and brave thing to say.
> - Guess loudly → A loud guess is not true knowing. “I do not know” is honest.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that "I don’t know" is an honest answer._

_Your Nubbin holds both tails, one in each paw._  

**Choices**

- **Point at the one on the left.**
    - **Monkey**: Ha! You see? The luggage-carrier knows me.
    - **Monkey**: Ha! You see? The luggage-carrier knows me.
    - They say it together, with the same grin.
    - **Tang Sanzang**: That settles nothing. I am sorry I asked.
- **Point at the one on the right.**
    - **Monkey**: There! Somebody with eyes at last.
    - **Monkey**: There! Somebody with eyes at last.
    - Both bow. Both bows are exactly as deep.
    - **Tang Sanzang**: That settles nothing. I am sorry I asked.
- **Say it plainly: “I can’t tell. I won’t pretend I can.”**
    - Both Monkeys open their mouths. Then neither says a word.
    - **Tang Sanzang**: Thank you. That is the first true thing anyone has said.
    - **Sandy**: Then we ask the one who does know.

#### `a02-15-named`

_The two Monkeys fight all the way to the Buddha’s hall._  
**The Buddha**: This one has six ears. He hears everything. He heard your story, Wukong.  
**The Buddha**: He wanted to be you. That is all.  
_The golden bowl comes down over the false Monkey, like a lid._  
_Under it is a small monkey with six ears, shaking._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 6  
> _(Count the six ears with your fingers. Real monkeys have two!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:ears:6`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted six ears._

_Monkey lifts his staff. Then he lowers it._  
**Monkey**: Go. Be yourself somewhere. It is harder, but it is yours.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): being yourself  
> _Being yourself is hard. But your own self is the best one._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that being yourself is worthwhile._


#### `a02-15-complete`

_The six-eared monkey runs off into the trees._  
_The luggage comes home, a bit dusty._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Wukong. Will you come back? Please?  
**Monkey**: Only if you say it twice.  
**Tang Sanzang**: Please.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): the word please  
> _What kind word did the monk say?_  
> - ✅ Please → Yes! Please. A small word with big power.
> - Goodbye → Not goodbye. The monk said please.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named a polite word._

_Your Nubbin lets go of its tail. It was the right one all along._  

## A2-16. The Flaming Mountains

- `a02-16-s1`: Talk with Princess Iron Fan. · _Hold out the red ribbon._
- `a02-16-s2`: Watch Monkey use the fan. · _Stand back from the flames._
- `a02-16-s3`: Carry the real fan. · _Hold it with Sandy._

#### `a02-16-ask`

_Ahead, the whole land looks like it is on fire. The Flaming Mountains!_  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): real red hills in China are very hot  
> _Real red hills in China are called the Flaming Mountains. They get very hot._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard about a real place in China._

_The only way over is a magic palm-leaf fan._  
_It belongs to Princess Iron Fan. She is Red Boy’s mum._  
**Princess Iron Fan**: You gave my son to that lady! He sweeps her floors!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): why someone is cross  
> _Princess Iron Fan is cross. Why?_  
> - ✅ She misses her son → Yes! She misses him, and missing someone can feel cross and sad.
> - She is hungry → Not hungry. She misses her son.
> _For grown-ups: Your child worked out why a character was upset._

**Monkey**: He is happy! He is learning!  
_She waves the fan once. Whoosh! Monkey flies far away, end over end._  
_Your Nubbin steps forward. It holds out the red ribbon._  

**Choices**

- **Tell her where your Nubbin found it.**
    - **Princess Iron Fan**: His. That is his. He was always losing it.
    - She holds it a long time.
    - She does not give you the fan, but she does not blow you away.
- **Let her take it without a word.**
    - She takes it and turns away. You hear her breathe out.
    - The door stays open.

#### `a02-16-ask-done`

_Monkey comes back. He turns into a tiny fly._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): rhyming words: fly and sky  
> _(Fly, sky! Can you think of another word that rhymes with fly?)_  
> Check: `edu:rhyme:fly:sky`
> _For grown-ups: Your child played with rhymes._

_He hops into her tea. After a fuss, she hands over a fan._  

#### `a02-16-fake`

_Monkey waves the fan at the edge of the flames._  
_The fire leaps up twice as high! His tail starts to smoke._  
**Monkey**: It is a fake! She gave me a fake!  
**Pigsy**: Run!  
_Everybody runs, and Pigsy runs fastest. Nobody has seen that before._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Wukong, your tail!  

> **Lesson** (health, ask): stop, drop and roll  
> _If clothes ever catch fire, what should we do?_  
> - ✅ Stop, drop and roll → Yes! Stop, drop, and roll. And tell a grown-up.
> - Run fast → Running makes a fire burn more. Stop, drop and roll. Tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned stop, drop and roll._


**Choices**

- **Pat out Monkey’s tail.**
    - **Monkey**: Thank you. That is my good tail. I only have the one.
- **Try very hard not to laugh.**
    - You fail. Your Nubbin fails too, rolling in the dust.
    - **Monkey**: Yes. All right. It was quite funny.

#### `a02-16-real`

_There is a long, silly business with disguises._  
_At last, Princess Iron Fan brings the real fan to the monk._  
**Princess Iron Fan**: Wave it forty-nine times. Then the fire goes out, and it rains.  
**Princess Iron Fan**: My boy would have wanted the fire. I think I want the rain.  
_The fan is huge. You and Sandy hold it, and Monkey swings it._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count in tens  
> _(Count ten waves with Monkey. Then ten more. Keep going: ten, twenty, thirty.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:waves:10`
> _For grown-ups: Your child counted by tens._

_Your Nubbin sits on your head and counts on its paws._  

#### `a02-16-real-done`

_Forty-nine waves, and the flames go out._  
_The first rain in a thousand years falls. Steam rises everywhere._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): rain on hot ground makes steam  
> _Rain on hot ground turns to steam. Steam is water in the air._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that hot water can become steam._


#### `a02-16-complete`

_You walk over the Flaming Mountains in the rain._  
_The ground is warm under your feet, and a little green._  
_Monkey gives the fan back to the princess. Everyone is surprised._  
**Princess Iron Fan**: Tell my son I kept his ribbon.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): a small kind act can open a door  
> _Why did the princess feel kinder at the end?_  
> - ✅ Your Nubbin was kind → Yes! A kind act, like the ribbon, can open a door.
> - She was tired → Not tired. Your Nubbin’s kind ribbon changed her heart.
> _For grown-ups: Your child saw how a kind act can change someone’s heart._

**Tang Sanzang**: We shall tell him.  

## A2-17. Cobweb Cave

- `a02-17-s1`: Visit the pretty cottage. · _Follow the monk quietly._
- `a02-17-s2`: Find where the web is tied. · _Follow a thread with your Nubbin._
- `a02-17-s3`: Help the monk out of the cave. · _Walk him to the mouth of the cave._

#### `a02-17-cottage`

**Tang Sanzang**: You have fetched every meal. Let me fetch one. Begging is my job.  
**Monkey**: Master, I really think…

> _(Count the seven spinners on your fingers.)_

#### `a02-17-cottage-done`

> _Spiders make silk from their own bodies. It is very thin, and very strong._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that spiders make strong silk._


#### `a02-17-web`

_The cottage is really a cave, and the cave is all web._

_Round three rocks, under a root, to a peg at the back._

**Sandy**: Everything that holds on has to hold on to something.

    - **Monkey**: There? That little one? Cousin, you are a genius.

#### `a02-17-out`

_Sandy unwraps the monk. He is dusty, and cross with himself, and fine._

_The seven spinners are seven spiders, scuttling for the cracks._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Leave them. Let them spin somewhere else.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being kind to small creatures  
> _The monk lets the spiders go. Why is that kind?_  
> - ✅ They have a right to live too → Yes! Small creatures matter too.
> - He was tired → He was tired, but he chose kindness.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that small creatures deserve kindness._

> Check: `edu:count:legs:8`

**Pigsy**: I have always said so. Nobody listens.

## A2-18. Vulture Peak

- `a02-18-s1`: Walk to Vulture Peak. · _Follow the green road._
- `a02-18-s2`: Cross the river in the boat. · _Take one small step._
- `a02-18-s3`: Talk with the Buddha and take the scrolls. · _Load the horse gently._

#### `a02-18-road`

_The page says you have walked for fourteen years._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): the real monk Xuanzang walked to India  
> _Long ago, a real monk called Xuanzang walked to India. It took years._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that the story grew from a real journey._

_The land ahead is green and quiet. People smile from their fields._  
**Tang Sanzang**: Is this it? Wukong, is this it?  
**Monkey**: That mountain there. You can stop worrying now.  
_The monk sits down in the road. He cries, and laughs, at once._  
_Your Nubbin climbs into his lap. Pigsy sits too._  

#### `a02-18-boat`

_A wide river lies between you and the mountain._  
_The only bridge is one slippery log._  
_A ferryman poles over in a boat with no bottom._  
_The water rushes through it. It looks very silly._  
**Tang Sanzang**: I cannot. It has no bottom.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): trying something new when scared  
> _The monk is afraid. What helps us try something new?_  
> - ✅ A friend, and one small step → Yes! A friend and one small step can help.
> - Run away → Running away is easy. One small step with a friend helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that a friend and a small step help with fear._

**Monkey**: You have walked fourteen years on trust. Try one more step.  
_The monk steps in. The boat holds him up, firm as stone._  

**Choices**

- **Step in after him.**
    - Your foot goes onto nothing, and the nothing holds. Your Nubbin hops in after.
- **Let your Nubbin go first.**
    - Your Nubbin hops in without a second thought. You follow it.

#### `a02-18-boat-done`

_On the far side, everyone feels light, like putting down a heavy pack._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): a big breath out

> Check: `edu:breathe:out:ahh`
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised a relaxing breath._


#### `a02-18-scriptures`

_The Buddha’s hall is full of light and very calm._  
**The Buddha**: You have come a long way. Rest, then take what you came for.  
_Disciples bring scrolls, bundle after bundle. You load the horse._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): paper and writing from China  
> _Paper was first made in China, long ago. It helped books spread._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that paper has a long history in China._

_Halfway down the mountain, a wind tears a bundle open. The pages are blank!_  
**Tang Sanzang**: Blank? After all this?  
**The Buddha**: The blank ones are truest. But people in the East need words.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): why we write words down  
> _Why do people need words on the pages?_  
> - ✅ So they can read them → Yes! Words let people read and remember.
> - To look pretty → Pretty is nice, but words are for reading and remembering.
> _For grown-ups: Your child said that writing lets us read and remember._

_New scrolls are full of writing. The monk gives his golden bowl as thanks._

> _(Count ten bundles on the horse, one to ten.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:bundles:10`
