## A2-19. The Eighty-First Hardship

- `a02-19-s1`: Swim with the old white turtle. · _Dive into the river._
- `a02-19-s2`: Carry the scrolls to the rock. · _Lay them in the sun._
- `a02-19-s3`: Bring the scrolls home. · _Walk to the city gate._

#### `a02-19-turtle`

_Far away, Guanyin reads a list of all the pilgrims’ hardships._  
_There were eighty. There ought to be eighty-one._  
**Guanyin**: One more, then. A gentle one.  
_At the River of Heaven, an old white turtle waits, smiling._  
**The old white turtle**: Welcome back. Did you ask the Buddha my question?  
**Tang Sanzang**: Oh no. I forgot. I am so sorry.  
_The turtle sinks slowly into the river. He is sad._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): how it feels to be forgotten  
> _How does the turtle feel when his question is forgotten?_  
> - ✅ Sad → Yes. He feels sad, because being forgotten hurts.
> - Happy → He is not happy. He is sad because he was forgotten.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named the feeling of being forgotten._

_Everyone goes into the water. Your Nubbin is delighted._  

#### `a02-19-turtle-done`

_Your Nubbin swims round the turtle, then sits on his shell._  
**The old white turtle**: No harm done. I only wanted to be remembered.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): turtles can live a very long time  
> _Some turtles and tortoises live for more than a hundred years._  
> _That is a long time to wait!_  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that some turtles live for a very long time._


#### `a02-19-rock`

_You haul the scrolls out and lay them on a flat rock to dry._  
_When you lift them, a few last pages stick to the stone._  
**Tang Sanzang**: No! We came all this way. Now they are not whole.  
**Monkey**: Nothing is whole, master. These are just honest about it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): nothing is perfect, and that is okay  
> _Nothing is perfect. Unfinished things can be good, and mistakes are okay._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that imperfect things can still be good._

**Monkey**: Maybe there is room for whoever reads them next.  

**Choices**

- **Try to peel the last pages free.**
    - You try, gently, but they stay put. The rock keeps a few words.
- **Leave them on the rock.**
    - You leave them. Your Nubbin pats the torn edges, kindly.

#### `a02-19-rock-done`

**Tang Sanzang**: Not quite complete. Yes. All right. That will do.  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, do): finish a story in your own way  
> _(Draw your own ending for the torn page. There is room!)_  
> Check: `edu:draw:picture:ending`
> _For grown-ups: Your child drew their own ending._


#### `a02-19-home`

_The city of Chang’an turns out to meet you._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): Chang’an is a real city, now called Xi’an  
> _Chang’an was a real city in China. Today it is called Xi’an._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that Chang’an was a real city._

_The pine trees by the gate all point east, the story says._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): the sun rises in the east  
> _The pines point east. Where does the sun come up?_  
> - ✅ In the east → Yes! The sun rises in the east, every morning.
> - In the west → The sun sets in the west. It rises in the east.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that the sun rises in the east._

_The emperor walks out. The scrolls are carried in with music._  
_Then the pilgrims are lifted back to Vulture Peak._  
_The Buddha gives each of them a new name. Monkey is a buddha now!_  
**Monkey**: A buddha in a headband looks silly. Take it off, master.  
**Tang Sanzang**: Touch your head, Wukong.  
_Monkey touches his head. The band is gone!_  

#### `a02-19-complete`

**Monkey**: Gone. It went when I stopped needing it.  
_His eyes are still little suns, but kinder, like the evening sun._  
**Monkey**: You believed me once, when nobody else did. I never forgot.  
**Tang Sanzang**: And you were right. I was afraid, and I called it careful.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): admitting you were afraid is brave  
> _The monk said he was afraid. Is that brave?_  
> - ✅ Yes, it is brave → Yes! Saying “I was afraid” takes courage.
> - No, it is silly → It is not silly. It is honest, and brave.
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard that admitting fear is brave._

_Monkey blows on a hair. It becomes a thin gold band, Nubbin-sized._

**Monkey**: And here, a little cloud, for when your Grove feels too big.

## A5-2. Sogolon

- `a05-02-s1`: Sit by the fire and hear a story. · _Find Balla at the fire._
- `a05-02-s2`: Walk with Sogolon to the king. · _Meet the hunters at the gate._

#### `a05-02-fire`

**Balla Fasséké**: Sit by the fire. This is a fire story.  
**Balla Fasséké**: A huge buffalo trampled the fields. Nobody could catch it.  
**Balla Fasséké**: Two brothers went to find it. On the road they met an old woman.  
**Balla Fasséké**: She was hungry. The brothers shared their food.  
**Balla Fasséké**: That was kind. So she told them how to win.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): sharing is a kind thing to do  
> _What did the brothers do that was kind?_  
> - ✅ They shared their food → Yes! Sharing is kind. And kindness came back to them.
> - They ate it all → The brothers didn’t eat it all. They shared it with the old woman.
> - They ran away → They didn’t run. They sat down and shared.
> _For grown-ups: Picked out sharing food as the kind act in the story._

**Balla Fasséké**: She asked for one thing. “Choose Sogolon. She is strong.”  
_Your Nubbin’s feet are warm by the fire._  
**Balla Fasséké**: Some say the old woman was the buffalo. Some say she was Sogolon’s aunt.  

**Choices**

- **Ask which one Balla believes.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: I believe the one I’m telling. That’s my job.
- **Say the brothers won by being kind.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: Yes! Keep that one.

#### `a05-02-fire-done`

_Out on the road, a dog barks. Woof!_  
_Another dog barks, woof! Then a third, woof!_  
**Balla Fasséké**: That’s them! Come on!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _(Bark three times together and count on your fingers.)_  
> _One, two, three!_

#### `a05-02-gate`

_Two dusty hunters come through the gate._  
_Between them walks a young woman. She is stooped, with very bright eyes._  
**The Elder Hunter**: We bring her to the king.  
_People come to look. Some stare, and some whisper._  
**Sogolon**: People look at me. It doesn’t stop me walking.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): being kind when others stare  
> _People stare at Sogolon. What could you do that is kind?_  
> - ✅ Walk beside her → A friend beside me. Good.
> - Stare too → Staring can hurt. Walking beside her says, “I’m with you.”
> - Hide behind a wall → Hiding doesn’t help her. Walking beside her does.
> _For grown-ups: Chose to walk beside someone being stared at, rather than stare._

**The Elder Hunter**: We offered her a donkey. She said it looked tired!  
**Sogolon**: It did look tired.  

**Choices**

- **Walk beside her.**
    - You walk beside her. Her shoulders relax.
    - **Sogolon**: A small round friend. I like odd company.
- **Offer to carry her bundle.**
    - **Sogolon**: No, it’s light. But thank you for asking.
    - Your Nubbin holds one corner anyway.

#### `a05-02-gate-done`

_Under the big tree, the court laughs. The king does not._  
**King Naré Maghan**: Doua. Do you remember what the hunter said?  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the beats in a name  
> _(Clap the parts of her name: So-go-lon.)_  
> _One, two, three claps. Sogolon has three parts!_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:sogolon`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the three syllables of “Sogolon”._

**Doua**: Every word, my king.

_The laughing stops all at once._  
**Sogolon**: I will. And please stop staring. I have only one head.

**Balla Fasséké**: She made them laugh with her, not at her!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): laughing with someone is different from laughing at them  
> **Balla Fasséké**: Laughing with someone is fun for everyone.  
> **Balla Fasséké**: Laughing at someone hurts. Sogolon showed the difference.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard the difference between laughing with and laughing at someone._


## A5-3. The Boy Who Couldn’t Walk

- `a05-03-s1`: Visit Sogolon’s house. Sit with her son. · _It is the small house at the back._
- `a05-03-s2`: Go with Sogolon to ask for leaves. · _Walk across the yard with her._

#### `a05-03-house`

_The page turns. A wedding, a baby, and seven years go by._  
_Sogolon’s son is seven. He crawls everywhere, and he watches everything._  
**Balla Fasséké**: His name is Mari Djata. He doesn’t talk much.  
_Your Nubbin sits in front of him. He pats its head, slowly._  
**Sogolon**: He doesn’t do that for many people. Your friend is honoured.  
**Balla Fasséké**: The old king died. His body stopped working, and it won’t start again.  
**Balla Fasséké**: I’m very sad. His older son, Dankaran, is king now.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what helps when someone is sad  
> _Balla is sad. What helps a sad friend?_  
> - ✅ Sit with them → Yes. Sitting close shows you care.
> - Tell them to stop → Sad feelings can’t be told to stop. Sitting close helps.
> - Run away → A friend stays close. Sit with them.
> _For grown-ups: Chose to sit with a sad friend. Heard plainly that the old king died._


**Choices**

- **Sit down in the dust with the boy.**
    - You sit. Nobody speaks.
    - He is not waiting. He is just looking, very hard.
- **Ask Sogolon if he’ll walk one day.**
    - **Sogolon**: He will walk when he walks.
    - **Sogolon**: I don’t pull up seedlings to make them grow.

#### `a05-03-house-done`

**Balla Fasséké**: Mark this, helper. He isn’t waiting to become someone.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): plants need water, sun and time; pulling does not help  
> **Sogolon**: A seedling needs water, sun and time.  
> **Sogolon**: If I pull it up, it dies. So I wait.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that plants need water, sunshine and time to grow._

**Balla Fasséké**: He is someone already. He is just not finished.  

#### `a05-03-leaves`

**Sogolon**: I need baobab leaves for supper. Sassouma has plenty.  
_Queen Sassouma sits under a baobab full of leaves._  
**Sogolon**: Sister, a handful of leaves, please.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds: b for baobab  
> _Baobab starts with a “b” sound. B, b, baobab!_  
> _Which word starts like baobab?_  
> - ✅ Ball → Yes! B, b, ball, and b, b, baobab.
> - Sun → Sun starts with “s”. Ball starts with “b”, like baobab.
> - Moon → Moon starts with “m”. Ball starts with “b”, like baobab.
> _For grown-ups: Matched the first sound “b” in baobab and ball._

**Sassouma Bérété**: Take them. My son picked them. He climbed up himself.  
**Sassouma Bérété**: Your son only crawls.  
_The women laugh. Sogolon takes the leaves, and she is hurt._  

**Choices**

- **Say nothing, and walk out beside Sogolon.**
    - You walk out beside her. She keeps her back straight.
- **Look Sassouma in the eye.**
    - You look at Sassouma. She looks back, cool and calm.
    - **Balla Fasséké**: She’ll remember your face.

#### `a05-03-leaves-done`

_At her door, Sogolon sits down. She cries, with her face in the leaves._  
_Her son crawls over. Your Nubbin leans on her other side._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): crying is allowed, and a hug or company helps  
> _Sogolon is sad, and it’s all right to cry._  
> _Her son and your Nubbin stay close. Being close helps._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that crying is allowed and that staying close helps._

**Sundiata**: Mother. Why are you crying?  
**Sogolon**: Because of leaves. Because of sharp words. Because of you, my son.  
**Sundiata**: Dry your eyes, Mother. Today I stand up.  
**Sundiata**: Ask the smiths for a rod of iron. The heaviest one.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 7  
> _(Hold up seven fingers.)_  
> _Sundiata crawled for seven years. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven._

> _For grown-ups: Counted to seven for the seven years Sundiata crawled._

## A5-4. The Iron Rod

- `a05-04-s1`: Run to the smiths with a message. · _The forges are by the river._
- `a05-04-s2`: Watch the boy stand. · _Stand with Balla at the edge of the crowd._
- `a05-04-s3`: Gather leaves for Sogolon. · _The leaves are round the baobab._

#### `a05-04-forge`

_The smiths’ street smells of smoke. Hammers ring: clang, clang!_  
_The master smith is big and quiet._  
**The Master Smith**: The heaviest rod we have ever made. For the crawling boy.  
**The Master Smith**: My father made it long ago. It waited for this day.  
_It is as long as two of you. It is dark as night._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-4, notice): fire makes iron hot and soft; cooling makes it hard again  
> **The Master Smith**: I put iron in the fire until it glows.  
> **The Master Smith**: Hot iron is soft, so I can shape it.  
> **The Master Smith**: When it cools, it is hard again.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that heat softens iron and cooling hardens it again._

**The Master Smith**: Smiths keep secrets, helper. And we are patient.  

**Choices**

- **Take hold of the rod with the helpers.**

- **Ask if a boy can really lift that.**
    - **The Master Smith**: No. That is the point.

#### `a05-04-forge-done`

> _Six helpers!_

_Half the children in town follow._

_The rod lies by Sogolon’s door. The crowd goes quiet._  
_The boy takes it in both hands. He pulls and pulls._  
_He is on his knees. Then on one foot._  
_Then he is standing! The rod bends like a bow._  
**Balla Fasséké**: He’s standing!  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): pushing and pulling  
> _(Put your hands together and push. Now pull them apart.)_  
> _Push, pull! Sundiata pulled to stand up._  
> Check: `edu:act:push-pull:hands`
> _For grown-ups: Tried pushing and pulling with their hands._

_Balla sings a praise song. The whole hill joins in._  
**Sogolon**: My son is standing.  

**Choices**

- **Look at Sogolon.**
    - Sogolon has her hands over her mouth. She waited seven years.

#### `a05-04-stand-done`

**Balla Fasséké**: Some tellers say it was a stick. Some say a branch.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): one story can be told in different ways  
> **Balla Fasséké**: Griots tell a story in different ways.  
> **Balla Fasséké**: The same story can have more than one telling.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that one story can be told in more than one way._

**Balla Fasséké**: I was there. It was iron. But I’ll tell the stick one too.

> - Basket one → Let’s count again: basket one has 3, basket two has 5. Five is more.

## A5-5. The Griot

- `a05-05-s1`: Watch Balla become Sundiata’s griot. · _Go to the hunters’ clearing._
- `a05-05-s2`: Help your Nubbin learn a tune. · _Sit your Nubbin at the balafon._

#### `a05-05-given`

_Sundiata is ten now. He hunts with the older boys._  
**Doua**: Every king has a griot. My son will be yours.  
**Sundiata**: I don’t need someone to sing at me.  
**Doua**: You need someone to remember you.  
**Balla Fasséké**: And I’ll tell you when you’re being a fool!  
**Sundiata**: Then stay close. I’ll need telling.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away to find the difference  
> _Sundiata stood at 7. Now he is 10._  
> _How many years later is that?_  
> - ✅ 3 years → Yes! Hold up 7 fingers, then 3 more to make 10.
> - 7 years → Start at 7 and count up: 8, 9, 10. Three years.
> - 1 year → Count up from 7: 8, 9, 10. That’s three years.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out that from age 7 to 10 is 3 years._


#### `a05-05-given-done`

_Sundiata and Balla shake hands, very seriously._  
_Then Sundiata gives him a playful push into the grass._  
_They both laugh._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): play is when everyone is laughing  
> _Friends can play and tease. It’s fine when both are laughing._  
> _If someone isn’t laughing, stop and say sorry._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that friendly play is when both are laughing; stop if someone isn’t._


#### `a05-05-lesson`

**Balla Fasséké**: If you’re my helper, your round friend is too.  
_He gives your Nubbin two beaters. They are very long._  
**Balla Fasséké**: You don’t hit the key. You ask it.  
_Your Nubbin asks. The key answers, round and low!_  
**Balla Fasséké**: There’s the hunters’ tune: quick and stamping.  
**Balla Fasséké**: Or Sogolon’s humming tune: slow and rocking.  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): fast and slow  
> _(Clap fast, like the hunters. Clap slow, like the humming tune.)_  
> _Fast, fast, fast. Slow… slow… slow._  
> Check: `edu:clap:tempo:fast-slow`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped a fast beat and a slow beat._

**Balla Fasséké**: Which one?  

**Choices**

- **The hunters’ tune.**
    - Balla plays it once: quick and stamping, like lots of feet.
    - Your Nubbin plays it back. Its feet stamp too.
    - **Balla Fasséké**: A tune for a crowd. You’ll never be lonely.
- **Sogolon’s lullaby.**
    - Balla plays it once. Slow, rocking, round and round.
    - Your Nubbin plays it back, very carefully.
    - **Balla Fasséké**: A tune for one person. They’ll think it’s just for them.

#### `a05-05-lesson-done`

_Your Nubbin plays its tune all evening._  
_By night it plays the whole tune without stopping._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): a pattern: what comes next  
> _The tune goes: low, high, low, high, low… What comes next?_  
> - ✅ High → Yes! Low, high, low, high, low, high is a pattern!
> - Low → Listen again: low, high, low, high, low… next is high.
> _For grown-ups: Continued a two-note pattern: low, high, low, high._

_Sogolon’s door is open. She sits just inside, listening._  

#### `a05-05-complete`

**Balla Fasséké**: Keep that tune. A tune you know by heart is a door.  
**Balla Fasséké**: I’ll tell you which door when we get there.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, do): first, next, last  
> _(Put three things in order: first, next, last.)_  
> _To learn a tune: first listen, next copy, last play it by heart._  
> Check: `edu:order:tune:first-next-last`
> _For grown-ups: Put the steps of learning a tune in order: listen, copy, play._

_Your Nubbin plays the first three notes. They’re still there._  

## A5-6. Exile

- `a05-06-s1`: Keep watch in the garden at night. · _Hide behind the vines._
- `a05-06-s2`: Say goodbye to Balla. · _Find him at the palace gate._
- `a05-06-s3`: Leave the town with Sogolon’s family. · _Meet them at the west gate._

#### `a05-06-garden`

_At night, nine old women creep into Sogolon’s garden._  
_They want to take her greens, and make Sundiata cross._  
_The garden is silver in the moonlight._  
_Sundiata stands up out of the vines._  
**Sundiata**: Grandmothers, you needn’t creep. Take what you like.  
**Sundiata**: These ones are better. Those are still green.  
_He fills their baskets. Your Nubbin brings a gourd each._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 9  
> _(Count the nine old women with your finger.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine!_  
> Check: `edu:count:women:9`
> _For grown-ups: Counted nine old women, one finger each._


#### `a05-06-garden-done`

**The Eldest of the Nine**: We came to make you cross. You made us ashamed instead.  
**The Eldest of the Nine**: From tonight, we watch over you.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, notice): a feeling word: ashamed  
> _“Ashamed” is a feeling word. It means you feel bad about something you did._  
> _Sundiata was kind, so the old women felt ashamed. Saying sorry helps._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what the feeling word “ashamed” means, and that kindness can change someone’s mind._


#### `a05-06-sent`

_In the morning, horses wait at the palace gate._  
**Dankaran Touman**: I send gifts to the king of Sosso. And a griot. Balla will go.  
**Sundiata**: You can’t take my griot!  
**Dankaran Touman**: I am king now, brother.  
_Balla touches Sundiata’s arm. Sundiata shakes, but stays._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): a good way to handle a big feeling  
> _Sundiata feels cross and sad. What helps a big feeling?_  
> - ✅ Slow, deep breaths → Yes. In… and out… Big feelings get smaller.
> - Hit something → Hitting hurts. Slow breaths help the feeling pass.
> - Hide and say nothing → Hiding can make it grow. Breathe, and tell someone.
> _For grown-ups: Chose slow breaths to handle a big feeling._

**Balla Fasséké**: Helper, listen. Remember it all for me. Then tell it back.  

**Choices**

- **Promise him.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: Good. Then I’m not leaving. I’m only going ahead.
- **Ask why he won’t say no.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: If I say no, there will be a fight. Sundiata isn’t ready.
    - **Balla Fasséké**: Sometimes going quietly is wise.

#### `a05-06-sent-done`

_Far down the road, Balla’s balafon answers with three more._

> _Three notes, and three more notes. How many notes in all?_  
> - ✅ 6 → Yes! 3 and 3 make 6.
> - 3 → That’s one group. Both together make 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6!
> - 9 → Let’s count: 1, 2, 3, then 4, 5, 6. Six notes.
> _For grown-ups: Added 3 and 3 to make 6 notes._

> _They leave by the west gate._  
> _Where does the sun go down: east or west?_  
> - ✅ West → Yes! The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
> - East → The sun comes up in the east. It goes down in the west.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the sun sets in the west._

**Kolonkan**: Walk quietly.  
_Sundiata looks back at the dark baobab._  
**Sundiata**: I’ll come back. Remember I said so.

    - You tie it in a corner of your cloth. It feels heavier all night.

> _Morning is a new start. The sun rises in the east._

## A5-7. Kingdom to Kingdom

- `a05-07-s1`: Watch Sundiata play wori. · _Sit by the game board._
- `a05-07-s2`: Listen to the king of Wagadou. · _Sit quietly at the back._
- `a05-07-s3`: Walk the long road with the family. · _Keep pace with Sogolon._

#### `a05-07-djedeba`

_The first king on the road loves games._  
**The King of Djedeba**: Play me at wori! Seeds into pits, round and round.  
_The board is carved wood with two rows of little pits._  
**Kolonkan**: The king is tricky, brother. Watch him closely.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.C.6, ask): more and fewer  
> _One pit has 4 seeds, and another has 7. Which pit has more?_  
> - ✅ The pit with 7 → Yes! Seven is more than four.
> - The pit with 4 → Count them: 4 stops sooner, and 7 goes on longer. Seven is more.
> _For grown-ups: Compared 4 seeds with 7 seeds and found which is more._

_Your Nubbin stares at the king’s hands._  
_Sundiata watches carefully. Then he starts to win._  

**Choices**

- **Count the seeds for Sundiata.**
    - You count under your breath, and Sundiata nods. He likes the company.
- **Let your Nubbin keep staring.**
    - The king feels uncomfortable. He hides his hands in his sleeves.

#### `a05-07-djedeba-done`

**The King of Djedeba**: You play well. You think before you move.  
**The King of Djedeba**: Stay the night. Then go on.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): taking turns  
> _In wori, you take turns. First me, then you._  
> _Waiting for your turn is a kind thing to do._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that taking turns is fair and kind._


#### `a05-07-wagadou`

_Wagadou is a very old kingdom. Its king is kind and careful._  
**The King of Wagadou**: Sit at my council. Learn how a king listens.  
_All day, people come: a farmer, a lady, two men with one goat._  
_The king listens to every one, even the goat men._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): being fair means listening to both sides  
> _Two men both say the goat is theirs. What does a fair king do?_  
> - ✅ Listen to both men → Yes. Everyone gets a turn to speak.
> - Pick one man → Picking quickly isn’t fair. Listen to both first.
> - Keep the goat → The goat isn’t the king’s. Fair means listening to both men.
> _For grown-ups: Chose to listen to both sides before deciding._

**Sundiata**: Why do you let them talk so long?  
**The King of Wagadou**: They came to be heard. Listening is how we keep people.  

#### `a05-07-wagadou-done`

_That night, Sundiata sits up late, thinking._  
**Sundiata**: Put that one near the top of the list for Balla.  
_(Think of the two men and their goat.)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhyming words  
> _Goat rhymes with… which word?_  
> - ✅ Boat → Yes! Goat and boat sound the same at the end.
> - Hen → Hen doesn’t sound like goat. Boat does: goat, boat!
> - Dog → Dog doesn’t rhyme with goat. Boat does: goat, boat!
> _For grown-ups: Found a word that rhymes with “goat”._


#### `a05-07-road`

_Months of road: thorn trees, dry river beds, a huge sky._  
_Sogolon walks slower every week. Nobody says so._  
**Manding Bory**: Djata, we could go faster!  
**Sundiata**: We go at my mother’s pace, so we all arrive.  
_Sundiata walks beside his mother. The whole family follows._  
**Kolonkan**: He used to be the slowest. Now he’s the one who waits.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): patience and waiting for others  
> _Why does Sundiata walk slowly?_  
> - ✅ So everyone arrives together → Yes. We go together.
> - Because he is tired → He isn’t tired. He walks slowly for his mother.
> - Because he is lost → He isn’t lost. He chooses to walk with his mother.
> _For grown-ups: Understood that Sundiata walks slowly so the whole family arrives together._


**Choices**

- **Offer to carry Sogolon’s water gourd.**
    - **Sogolon**: Thank you. My hands are glad.
- **Ask your Nubbin to play its tune.**
    - Your Nubbin taps its knees. The family walks to the beat.

#### `a05-08-army-done`

_Year by year, the king gives Sundiata more to lead._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): life long ago and today  
> _This was long ago. How did people travel far then?_  
> - ✅ On a horse or on foot → Yes! There were no cars then.
> - In a rocket → Rockets came much later. Long ago, people rode horses or walked.
> - In a car → Cars weren’t invented yet. People rode horses or walked.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that long ago people travelled by horse or on foot._


#### `a05-08-mat`

> _The sun moves across the sky all day. So the shade moves too._  
> _Sogolon’s shade moves round her as the day goes by._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the sun moves across the sky during the day, so shade moves too._

**Sogolon**: Sit with me. I like a quiet visitor.  
_Your Nubbin lies down against her side._  
**Sogolon**: I won’t see Niani again. I am old, and my body is tired.  
**Sogolon**: I carried him. I waited for him. I am proud, and tired.  
**Sogolon**: Tell Balla. Both are fine.  

**Choices**

- **Stay, and say nothing.**
    - You stay, and she closes her eyes. The shade moves.
    - She hums, very low, her grinding-stone tune.
- **Promise to tell Balla.**
    - **Sogolon**: Good. Make him laugh at the cattle bit.

#### `a05-08-mat-done`

_That night, Sogolon dies._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): when someone dies it is sad; being together helps

> _For grown-ups: Heard plainly that Sogolon died, that sadness is allowed, and that being together helps._

#### `a05-09-sosso-done`

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): sound words  
> _Balla pushes the old door. What sound does it make?_  
> - ✅ Creeeak! → Yes! Creeeak goes the old door.
> - Moo! → Moo is a cow! An old door goes creeeak.
> - Splash! → Splash is water! An old door goes creeeak.
> _For grown-ups: Remembered and said the sound word for an old door opening._


#### `a05-09-chamber`

_The room is dim. Owls sit on perches, watching._  
_Jars sit on shelves. Old crowns hang on the wall._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): owls sleep by day and wake at night  
> _Owls sleep in the daytime and wake up at night._  
> _They have big eyes to see in the dark. Whoo!_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that owls are awake at night and have big eyes._

_In the middle is a huge balafon, dark with age._  
**Balla Fasséké**: Oh, look at that.  
**Balla Fasséké**: A griot can’t see a balafon like that and not play it.  
**Balla Fasséké**: Your tune. Let’s hear it on a king’s balafon.  

#### `a05-09-chamber-done`

_Balla plays the hunters’ tune. It is enormous!_  
_Your Nubbin stamps, and the owls shuffle. Heavy feet climb the stairs._  
_Soumaoro fills the doorway, in a cloak the colour of iron._  

> **Lesson** (music, 1-PS4-1, notice): long keys make low sounds, short keys make high sounds  
> **Balla Fasséké**: This balafon is huge. Its long keys make deep, low sounds.  
> **Balla Fasséké**: Short keys make high sounds. Long is low. Short is high.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that long keys make low sounds and short keys make high sounds._

**Soumaoro Kanté**: That is a hunters’ tune. My father’s hunters played it when I was small.

**Soumaoro Kanté**: Hm.

_Balla bows and looks at you. He is not free, but he is fine._  

#### `a05-09-march`

_The page turns. Soumaoro’s soldiers leave Sosso._

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what to do when you are frightened  
> _Dankaran ran away because he was scared. What helps when you’re scared?_  
> - ✅ Tell someone, and get help → Yes. Telling someone you trust is brave.
> - Hide in the dark → Hiding alone can make it worse. Tell someone you trust.
> - Pretend nothing is wrong → Feelings need to be shared. Tell someone you trust.
> _For grown-ups: Chose to tell someone and get help when frightened._

**Balla Fasséké**: Manding has no king now.  
**Balla Fasséké**: Go back to Sundiata, helper. I’ll keep the tune going here.

**Balla Fasséké**: Remember that too.

## A5-10. The Call Home

- `a05-10-s1`: Help Kolonkan at her stall. · _Mind the stall with her._

#### `a05-10-market`

_Mema’s market is full of noise and colour._

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): we smell with our noses  
> _The man smells the leaves. Which part of you smells?_  
> - ✅ My nose → Yes! Sniff, sniff: the smell reminds him of home.
> - My toes → Toes can’t smell. Noses do!
> - My ears → Ears are for hearing. Noses smell.
> _For grown-ups: Named the nose as the part of the body we smell with._

**Messenger from Manding**: These are Manding leaves! Is Sogolon’s son here?  
**Kolonkan**: Sogolon’s daughter sells them.  
**Messenger from Manding**: Then he’s here! Manding needs him.

> _For grown-ups: Heard that stories have a beginning, a middle and an end._


#### `a05-13-cave`

_High in the hills, Sundiata stops at a cave._  
_Soumaoro’s black horse stands outside, cropping grass._  
**Sundiata**: He went in. Nobody has come out.  
_The cave is dark. Nothing makes a sound._  
**Balla Fasséké**: Some say he’s still in there. Some say he became stone.  
**Balla Fasséké**: Everyone agrees: he was never seen again.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): sound bounces back in a cave  
> _Call “hello” into a cave, and “hello” comes back._  
> _That is called an echo. Sound bounces off the hard walls._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sound bounces off cave walls and comes back as an echo._


**Choices**

- **Wait at the cave mouth a little while.**
    - You wait, and Sundiata waits too. Only a cool breath of air comes out.
- **Let your Nubbin play its tune into the cave.**
    - The tune comes back off the walls, the same and not the same.
    - **Balla Fasséké**: He loved music. That should be remembered too.

#### `a05-13-complete`

**Sundiata**: He was my greatest enemy. I don’t want him sung badly.  
**Balla Fasséké**: He won’t be. Not by me.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): being fair and gentle, even to those who were unkind  
> _Soumaoro was wrong to be unkind. But he loved music._  
> _Sundiata is gentle with the horse. The horse did nothing wrong._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that we can be fair and gentle, even about someone who was wrong._

_Sundiata leads the black horse down the hill._  
_He walks beside it. He does not ride._  

## A5-14. The Assembly

- `a05-14-s1`: Go to the great gathering. · _Walk with Balla to the wide clearing._
- `a05-14-s2`: Choose what Balla should remember. · _Find him where the griots sit._

#### `a05-14-assembly`

_At Kurukan Fuga, kings and peoples gather in a great ring._  
_There are more people than you can count. And so many drums!_  
**Fran Kamara**: Tabon gives its iron. Its people keep their own ways.  
**Fakoli**: The smiths give their skill. It stays theirs.  
**Sundiata**: Manding is one. A stranger is a guest. Nobody hurts a messenger.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): a kind rule: welcome guests  
> _One rule is “a stranger is a guest”._  
> _What do we do when a visitor comes?_  
> - ✅ Welcome them kindly → Yes! A guest is welcome.
> - Shut the door → A guest is to be welcomed, not shut out.
> _For grown-ups: Understood the rule that guests are welcomed kindly._

**Sundiata**: Every person matters. Even the smallest. Even one who crawled.  

#### `a05-14-assembly-done`

**Balla Fasséké**: Tellers still argue about the exact words said here.  
**Balla Fasséké**: The rules agreed here are remembered. They are called the Manden Charter.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): old rules are still remembered today  
> **Balla Fasséké**: That was about 800 years ago. People still remember these rules today.  
> **Balla Fasséké**: Griots still tell Sundiata’s story. It is a living story.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the rules and the story of Sundiata are still remembered about 800 years later._

_The ring roars. They name him Mansa, king of kings._  
_Kolonkan is crying happy tears._  

#### `a05-14-ask`

_At the edge of the ring, Balla tunes his balafon. He looks happy._  
**Balla Fasséké**: Sundiata made my family his griots for ever.  
_Your Nubbin climbs on the frame and sits, as it did on day one._  
**Balla Fasséké**: I’ll tell this story ten thousand times, a little different each time.  
**Balla Fasséké**: But there is one thing I’ll never leave out.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, notice): choosing what matters most, and saying why  
> _Every storyteller chooses what matters most._  
> _You are choosing too. There is no wrong answer._  
> _For grown-ups: Chose what matters most in a story, and heard there is no wrong answer._

**Balla Fasséké**: Helper, what should I never leave out?  

**Choices**

- **That it took him seven years to stand, and that was all right.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: Yes. I’ll tell the dust before the rod, and the years nobody hurried him.
- **That his mother was the strongest person in it.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: Sogolon. She goes in the first line, every time.
- **That Nana Triban chose to bring the secret.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: Yes. People forget her. I won’t.
- **That the enemy loved music.**
    - **Balla Fasséké**: The hardest to sing, and the truest. I’ll keep Soumaoro whole.

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): keep a steady beat  
> _(Stamp a steady beat with your feet. Stamp, stamp, stamp, stamp.)_

**Sundiata**: My hunting tune! The one they played when I came home.  
**Balla Fasséké**: In eight hundred years, children will still hear this. And they’ll argue about it!  
**Balla Fasséké**: A story that people argue about is a story that is alive.  
_He puts the little balafon in your arms._  
**Balla Fasséké**: Go home, helper. Remember us well.

## A6-1. Two Sinbads

- `a06-01-s2`: Sit on the bench in the shade by the big house. · _Sit down beside Sinbad by the gate._
- `a06-01-s3`: Go in and meet the old man of the house. · _Follow the helper through the courtyard._

#### `a06-01-street`

_A page in Nova’s atlas opens. A round city sits by a river._  
_You touch the river and, whoosh, you are in a busy lane!_  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Steady now! This basket has paper in it.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Paper is for writing. Clever people write books on it.  
_Your Nubbin rides on top of the paper rolls._

_(Point to each roll. Count them together.)_

> _For grown-ups: Counted five paper rolls, touching each one._

_One, two, three, four, five!_  

**Choices**

    - **Sinbad the Porter**: Thank you, friend! Now we carry together.
- **Ask what the scholars do with all this paper.**
    - **Sinbad the Porter**: They write and read. They make books about stars, and numbers, and medicine.

#### `a06-01-street-done`

_At the big library, a young man counts the rolls._  
_He pays Sinbad. Clink, clink!_

**Sinbad the Porter**: People come here to read, and write, and learn.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): a long time ago there were big libraries in cities  
> **Sinbad the Porter**: A very long time ago, people in Baghdad shared books here.  
> **Sinbad the Porter**: They shared what they knew. Sharing is a good thing to do.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that long ago there was a big library in a city called Baghdad where people shared books._


#### `a06-01-bench`

_Sinbad and you walk home. You stop by a big house._  
_Sinbad sits on a stone bench. He puts down his baskets._  
_Yum! You can smell warm food from the gate._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Somebody in there is eating lamb. I am going home to lentils!  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I carry heavy loads all day. It is not fair!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): name a feeling  
> _Sinbad’s face is scrunched up. His fists are tight. How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Cross. → Yes! Sinbad is cross. His face is scrunched. Cross is a feeling, and feelings are allowed.
> - Sleepy. → Not quite. Look at his scrunched face and his tight fists. Sinbad is cross.
> - Silly. → Not quite. Silly people giggle. Sinbad is scrunched up and growly. He is cross.
> _For grown-ups: Named a feeling (cross) from a face and body._

_Sinbad says this very loudly. A window opens up high._  
_Your Nubbin looks up at the window._  

**Choices**

- **Tell him to keep his voice down.**
    - **Sinbad the Porter**: Why? It is true, even in a whisper.
- **Say it isn’t fair.**
    - **Sinbad the Porter**: Thank you! I feel a little better.

#### `a06-01-bench-done`

_The gate opens. A helper in a neat turban looks out._  
**The Steward**: My master wants to meet the man who was talking.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sound of a name  
> _Sinbad starts with a “sss” sound. Which of these starts with “sss” too?_  
> - ✅ Sun. → Yes! Sss-sun and Sss-Sinbad start the same.
> - Moon. → Mmm-moon starts with “mmm”. Sinbad starts with “sss”. Sss-sun does too!
> - Boat. → Buh-boat starts with “buh”. Sss-sun starts like Sss-Sinbad!
> _For grown-ups: Matched the first sound “s” in Sinbad and sun._

**The Steward**: And his friend. And that.  
_(That is your Nubbin. It waves.)_  

#### `a06-01-hall`

_Inside, there is a courtyard with a fountain._  
_Then there is a long room with soft cushions._  
_An old man with a white beard sits at the end._  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Sit, sit! Eat first. Lamb is better than grumbling.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: You heard me grumble?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: The whole street heard! What is your name?  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Sinbad. Sinbad the porter.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Ha! I am Sinbad too. Sinbad the sailor.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): positions: on, under, beside  
> _Sinbad the porter sits on the very edge of a cushion._  
> _Is he sitting on the cushion, or under it?_  
> - ✅ On it. → Yes! He is on the cushion. (Pat a cushion near you.)
> - Under it. → Not under. A cushion is soft, but nobody sits under it! Sinbad is on the cushion.
> _For grown-ups: Used the position word “on” for where someone sits._

_The porter sits right on the edge of the cushion._

## A6-2. The Island That Moved

- `a06-02-s1`: Listen to the first story. Step into it. · _Sit on your cushion until the carpet turns to sea._
- `a06-02-s2`: Pick up sticks for the fire on the little island. · _Pick up sticks under the trees. Take them to the fire._
- `a06-02-s3`: Hold on to the washtub in the sea. · _Keep hold of the tub and kick._

#### `a06-02-telling`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: When I was young, I spent my money too fast.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: So I went to a city called Basra to take a ship.  
_The carpet turns blue. It starts to move!_  
_Now you are on a ship. It has a big triangle sail._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): name a triangle  
> _The ship’s big sail has three corners and three straight sides._  
> _What shape is it?_  
> - ✅ A triangle. → Yes! Three corners, three sides. A triangle! (Trace one in the air.)
> - A circle. → A circle is round with no corners. This sail has three corners. It is a triangle!
> - A square. → A square has four corners. Count the sail’s corners: one, two, three. A triangle!
> _For grown-ups: Named a triangle by counting its sides and corners._

_A young man leans on the rail. He grins at the sea._  
**Young Sinbad**: You are new! Good. Nobody else has heard my jokes.  

**Choices**

- **Ask to hear a joke.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: What is the difference between a merchant and a sailor?
    - **Young Sinbad**: About three days out of Basra!
- **Ask if he’s been to sea before.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Never! Isn’t it wonderful?

#### `a06-02-telling-done`

_Days and days of blue sea go by. Splash, splash!_  
_Then a sailor shouts, “Land!”_  
_A small green island. It is flat as a plate._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, notice): sea and land are different places  
> **Young Sinbad**: The sea is water, and the island is land.  
> **Young Sinbad**: Fish live in the sea, and trees grow on land.  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that sea and land are different places where different things live._


#### `a06-02-island`

**The Captain**: Everybody ashore! Wash your shirts. Back by evening!  
_The island feels soft and bouncy._  
**Young Sinbad**: Sticks for the fire! Let’s cook on dry land.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count sticks to 4  
> **Young Sinbad**: Four sticks make a good fire. Count them with me: one, two, three, four!  
> Check: `edu:count:firewood:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four sticks for the fire._

_The sailors light a fire. Somebody sings._  
_Your Nubbin sits down. Then it jumps up!_  
_The ground is warm. It is warm from underneath._  

**Choices**

- **Tell Sinbad the ground is warm.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: It is just the sun, friend. Have a date.
- **Kick sand over the fire.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Hey! That was our supper!

#### `a06-02-island-done`

_The island shakes. Wobble, wobble!_  
_All the little trees lean the same way._  
**The Captain**: It is not an island! It is a fish! Run!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): whales are big animals that breathe air  
> _It is a whale! Whales are very big animals. They live in the sea._  
> _Whales breathe air, like you. So they come up to the top to breathe._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a whale is a big sea animal that breathes air._


#### `a06-02-tub`

_The whale rolls over, slowly. A great eye opens._  
_Then it dives. Everyone falls into the sea!_  
**Young Sinbad**: Here! The washtub! Hold on!  
_Sinbad holds the tub, and you hold Sinbad. Your Nubbin holds your ear._  
_Far below, something sings one long, low note. Ooooo._  

> **Lesson** (music, ask): high and low sounds  
> _The whale sings a long, low note._  
> _Is a whale’s song high like a mouse, or low like a drum?_  
> - ✅ Low, like a drum. → Yes! Big animals often make deep, low sounds. Ooooo! (Hum it low.)
> - High, like a mouse. → Mice squeak high. The whale is huge, and its note is low. Ooooo!
> _For grown-ups: Linked a big animal with a low sound._

_Then it is quiet._  

**Choices**

- **Kick, hard.**
    - The tub spins round and round. Whee!
- **Float, and let the current take you.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Good thinking. The sea knows where it is going.

#### `a06-02-tub-done`

_A day goes by, then a night, then another day._  
_Bump! The tub hits sand._  
**Young Sinbad**: Land! Hooray!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): put events in order: first, next, last  
> _First there was a day. Next there was a night. What came last?_  
> - ✅ Another day. → Yes! A day, a night, then another day.
> - Another night. → Listen again: a day, a night, and then another day. That came last.
> _For grown-ups: Retold a short sequence in order._

**Sinbad the Sailor**: It was a very good fire.
