> _For grown-ups: Enjoyed a sound word (zzzzz) and made the sound._


#### `a06-04-leg`

**Young Sinbad**: She will fly at sunrise. We must go with her.  
_Sinbad unwinds his turban. It is very long._  
_You tie yourselves to one great toe, gently._  
**Young Sinbad**: Don’t pull. Don’t tickle. Don’t breathe.  
_At dawn, the bird spreads her wings. Whoosh, up you go!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): birds have wings and feathers  
> _Birds fly with wings and feathers._  
> _Their feathers are light, so the wind can lift them._  
> _(Flap your arms like wings.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that birds have wings and feathers, and flapped like a bird._


**Choices**

- **Look down.**
    - The island is a coin, then a crumb, then gone.
- **Shut your eyes.**
    - Your Nubbin keeps its eyes open for both of you.

#### `a06-04-leg-done`

_At noon, the bird lands on a high ridge._  
_You untie the turban. You are shaking, but you did it._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): being brave when scared  
> _You felt scared up high. Being brave means doing it while you feel scared._  
> _Take a big breath. In... and out. You were brave!_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that being brave means acting while scared, and tried a calming breath._


#### `a06-04-complete`

_The big bird flies back up into the sun._  
_A feather floats down. It is as long as you are tall!_  
_Your Nubbin catches it, and falls over._  
**Young Sinbad**: Keep it. Now people will believe you.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: That is not a chicken.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: longer and shorter  
> _The feather is as long as you are tall._  
> _Is it longer than your hand, or shorter?_  
> - ✅ Longer. → Yes! A feather as long as you is much longer than your hand. (Hold up your hand.)
> - Shorter. → Look again. It is as tall as you! That is longer than a hand.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a long feather with a hand using “longer”._


## A6-5. The Valley of Diamonds

- `a06-05-s1`: Walk down into the valley on tiptoe. · _Step on the bare stone between the sleepy snakes._
- `a06-05-s2`: Work out where the meat comes from. · _Watch the rim of the valley and the eagles._
- `a06-05-s3`: Ride the eagle up out of the valley. · _Hold on to Sinbad’s belt until the top._

#### `a06-05-valley`

_You look down into a deep, narrow valley. It sparkles like stars._  
**Young Sinbad**: Diamonds! Look how big they are!  
_Long snakes lie in the sun. They are fast asleep._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): snakes warm up in the sun  
> _Snakes lie in the sun to warm up._  
> _Their bodies do not make much heat._  
> _When the sun warms them, they feel good._  
> _Just like a cat on a warm wall._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snakes lie in the sun to warm up._

_You tiptoe down, between the snakes. Tip, tip, tip._  
_Your Nubbin tiptoes too. It does it very well._  

**Choices**

- **Hold your breath past the biggest snake.**
    - The snake opens one eye. It is not hungry, so it closes it again.
- **Go the long way round it.**
    - It takes an hour. Sinbad grumbles in a whisper.

#### `a06-05-valley-done`

_Something falls out of the sky. Splat, it is a big piece of meat!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the beats in a word  
> _Eagles carry the meat up. E-agle. Clap twice: ea-gle! Two claps._  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:eagle`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the two beats in “eagle”._

_Everyone stares at it. What is it doing here?_  

#### `a06-05-meat`

_More meat falls, splat, splat! Diamonds stick to it._  
_Men at the top throw it down. Eagles swoop and carry it up._  
**Young Sinbad**: If an eagle can lift that, it can lift me!  
_He ties himself under a big piece of meat._  
**Young Sinbad**: Take some stones! Quick!  
_By your foot is a small, clear stone._  
_It is as small as a lentil._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Eco.1.K-2, notice): we choose how much to take  
> _Sinbad wants lots of stones. You can take a little, or take none._  
> _Choosing is yours. Both are fine._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that we can choose how much to take; either choice is fine._


**Choices**

- **Take one small stone, for the porter.**
    - You put it in your pocket. It is warm from the sun.
    - **Young Sinbad**: Only one? You are madder than the fish!
- **Take nothing.**
    - You leave it where it lies. It goes on shining.
    - **Young Sinbad**: Nothing? Well, more for me.

#### `a06-05-meat-done`

_Your Nubbin climbs into Sinbad’s sash._  
_You hold on to his belt with both hands._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _One Sinbad. One you. One Nubbin. How many friends are holding on? Three!_  
> Check: `edu:count:friends:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three friends._


#### `a06-05-lift`

_An eagle swoops down and lifts the meat. Up you go!_  
_The snakes look as small as string._  
_At the top, a merchant bangs two pans._  
_The eagle lets go and flaps away._  
**A Diamond Merchant**: A man on my meat! And no diamonds!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): calming down  
> _The merchant was cross, and then he was calm. How? Sinbad spoke gently._  
> _A kind voice can help someone calm down. So can a big, slow breath._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a kind voice and slow breaths help us calm down._

**Young Sinbad**: Peace, friend. Here, take some stones.  
_The merchant stops shouting at once._  

#### `a06-05-lift-done`

**A Diamond Merchant**: Twenty years I threw meat. Nobody ever came up on it before!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): feeling words  
> _The merchant is very surprised. Which word means “very surprised”?_  
> - ✅ Amazed. → Yes! Amazed means very surprised. (Make big round eyes!)
> - Sleepy. → Sleepy is for bedtime. Amazed means very surprised.
> _For grown-ups: Matched a feeling word (amazed) to surprise._

_Sinbad grins. Your Nubbin grins too._  

#### `a06-05-complete`

_The carpet is a carpet again._  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I came home rich. I gave lots to people who needed it.  
_You put the little stone in the porter’s hand._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Nobody ever gave me a jewel. I will never sell it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): a gift from a friend feels special  
> **Sinbad the Porter**: A gift does not have to be big.  
> **Sinbad the Porter**: It can be tiny, and still mean so much.  
> **Sinbad the Porter**: It tells someone: I was thinking of you.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a small gift can mean a lot because it shows we thought of someone._

**Sinbad the Sailor**: Good. A stone you keep is worth more than one you sell.  

## A6-6. The Giant’s Island

- `a06-06-s1`: Look round the giant’s yard with the sailors. · _Look round the yard. Count everyone._
- `a06-06-s2`: Get everyone past the sleepy giant. · _Find something that makes people sneeze._
- `a06-06-s3`: Build rafts and sail away. · _Tie driftwood together on the beach._

#### `a06-06-castle`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: I will tell this story gently, for the little ones.  
_There is a storm._  
_Then an island, with a house as big as a hill._  
_In the yard there are cooking pots big enough to bath in._  
_Boom, boom, the ground shakes! A giant ducks in at the gate._  
_He has one big eye. He yawns and looks at his pots._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: bigger and smaller  
> _The giant’s pot is as big as a bath. Your cup is little._  
> _Which is bigger?_  
> - ✅ The pot. → Yes! The giant’s pot is bigger. The cup is smaller. (Make big hands, then small hands.)
> - The cup. → Think of a bath, and then a cup. The pot is much bigger!
> _For grown-ups: Compared big and small using “bigger” and “smaller”._

_Then he lies down across the gate, and falls fast asleep._  

**Choices**

- **Hide in a cooking pot.**
    - Your Nubbin is already in it. It is a very good pot.
- **Count the sailors, to be sure everyone is here.**
    - All here, and all very quiet. Shh!

#### `a06-06-castle-done`

**Young Sinbad**: He is asleep across the only way out.  
_Everyone whispers. Shh, shh._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): feeling scared and what helps  
> _The sailors feel scared. Their hearts go thump, thump._  
> _Staying together helps. So do slow breaths. Breathe in... and out._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that being scared is a feeling, and that staying together and breathing slowly help._


#### `a06-06-gate`

_The giant snores. It ruffles the sailors’ beards._  
**Young Sinbad**: Pepper! The cook has pepper. Giants sneeze like anyone.  
_Your Nubbin carries the bag to the giant’s nose, very quietly._  
_It tips the bag. The giant breathes in._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): a sneeze clears the nose  
> _Pepper tickles the nose. Then, atchoo! A sneeze blows the tickle out._  
> _Your body does this by itself. Atchoo! (Do a pretend sneeze.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sneeze is the body clearing a tickle from the nose._

_Atchoo! He sits up and his eye is full of tears._  
**Young Sinbad**: Now! Everybody out!  

**Choices**

- **Grab your Nubbin off the giant’s chin on the way past.**
    - You catch it. The next sneeze blows you both out of the gate!
- **Wait and go last, after the sailors.**
    - Everyone is out. You go last, with pepper in your hair.

#### `a06-06-gate-done`

_Behind you the giant sneezes, and sneezes, and sneezes._  
_Atchoo, atchoo, atchoo! Not one is aimed at anybody._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, notice): repeated sounds make a rhythm  
> _Atchoo, atchoo, atchoo! Repeating a sound makes a beat._  
> _Clap the beat with me: atchoo, atchoo, atchoo!_  
> _For grown-ups: Enjoyed a repeated sound and clapped its beat._


#### `a06-06-raft`

_On the beach the sailors tie driftwood together._  
**Young Sinbad**: Push! Push off!  
_The giant throws rocks. Splash, they land far away!_  
_You sail past the reef. The giant is tiny now._  
**Young Sinbad**: Nobody lost! Not one!  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): wood floats, stone sinks  
> _The sailors used driftwood for the raft. Why not stones? Which one floats?_  
> - ✅ Wood floats. → Yes! Wood floats on water. Stones sink. That is why rafts are made of wood.
> - Stones float. → Drop a stone in a pond, and plop! It sinks. Wood floats. That is why rafts are wood.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that wood floats and stones sink._


#### `a06-06-complete`

**Sinbad the Porter**: You sneezed a giant!  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Not me. Your friend’s little one did. I only ran.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: My daughter will like that one.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: That is how I tell it to children.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: It is the truest way I know.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): being gentle with little ones  
> **Sinbad the Sailor**: Some things are better told gently to little ones.  
> **Sinbad the Sailor**: Being gentle with little ones is a way of caring for them.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that we can be gentle with little ones and look after their feelings._


## A6-7. The Serpent

- `a06-07-s1`: Climb a tall tree before dark. · _Climb the nearest tall tree._
- `a06-07-s2`: Build a box of planks in the tree. · _Pull up the planks. Tie them round the branches._
- `a06-07-s3`: Wave to the ship on the sea. · _Wave something long from the top of the tree._

#### `a06-07-island`

_The rafts reach a second island. Everyone is very tired._  
_At dusk, a long hiss comes from the grass. Sssss._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): dusk: day turns to night  
> _Dusk is when the sun goes down. The sky gets dim, and then dark._  
> _Day turns to night, again and again. It happens every day._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that dusk is when day turns to night._

_A huge snake slides out. It is longer than a ship!_  
**Young Sinbad**: Up the trees, all of you!  
_You climb. Your Nubbin climbs faster._  
_The snake winds round the tree. It waits._  

**Choices**

- **Climb higher.**
    - The branches get thin. The snake cannot quite reach.
- **Stay where you are, and keep very still.**
    - The snake’s tongue flicks below your foot. Then it sinks away.

#### `a06-07-island-done`

**Young Sinbad**: Snakes can climb. We need a way to be safe.  
_Everybody looks at the broken raft planks._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): solving a problem together  
> _Sinbad has a big problem. What can friends do with a big problem?_  
> - ✅ Think of a plan together. → Yes! Friends can think together. Two heads are better than one.
> - Give up. → Giving up never fixes it. Friends can think of a plan together.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about solving a problem by planning together with friends._


#### `a06-07-box`

_Sinbad pulls up planks from the broken rafts._  
**Young Sinbad**: A box round us. With gaps to breathe.  
_You tie, and he ties. Your Nubbin holds each knot._  
_All night the snake goes round and round._  
_Nobody sleeps. Sinbad whispers about his round city._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count the sides of a box  
> **Young Sinbad**: Four planks make four sides. Count them: one, two, three, four!  
> Check: `edu:count:planks:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four sides of a plank box._


**Choices**

- **Ask what he’ll do when he gets home.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Never go to sea again.
    - **Young Sinbad**: I always say that.
- **Hum a Grove tune to your Nubbin.**
    - It helps. Even the snake goes still for a while.

#### `a06-07-box-done`

_At first light the snake gives up._  
_It pours itself away into the grass._  
_It does not come back._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): the sun rises in the morning  
> _Morning comes when the sun rises. Light fills the sky._  
> _Night turns into day. Dark goes, and light comes back._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the sun rises in the morning and night turns into day._


#### `a06-07-sail`

_A sail! A sail on the sea!_  
_Sinbad waves his long turban. Wave, wave, wave!_  
**The Captain**: Castaways! Up you come, all of you!  
**The Captain**: We have goods for a man we left on an island.  
**The Captain**: His name was Sinbad.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): find the letter S  
> _Ship starts with S. Sinbad starts with S. Sail starts with S too. Sss!_  
> Check: `edu:tap:letter:s`
> _For grown-ups: Found the letter S in ship, sail and Sinbad._

**Young Sinbad**: You did not!  
_Sinbad laughs and laughs._  

#### `a06-07-complete`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: Third voyage done. I swore, never again.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): count to 3 on fingers  
> _Three voyages so far! Hold up a finger for each one: one, two, three._  
> Check: `edu:count:fingers:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three voyages on fingers._

**Sinbad the Porter**: Never again?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Never again.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: How long did that last?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Long enough to get bored.  

## A6-8. The Strange Custom

- `a06-08-s1`: Listen to the fourth story from your cushion. · _Stay by the old man while he tells it._
- `a06-08-s2`: In the dark cave, find where fresh air comes from. · _Stand still. Feel the air on your face._
- `a06-08-s3`: Follow the little animal to the sea. · _Go where the striped animal goes._

#### `a06-08-telling`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: I will tell the fourth story from here. It is a sad one.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I sailed to a kind kingdom. I made saddles for their horses.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I married a lovely woman. I loved her very much.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Then she was ill, and she died. That means her body stopped working.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: It will not start again.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I held her hand at the end. I still remember her with love.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I was very, very sad.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Then a hard rule sent me down into a dark cave.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: All on your own?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Yes. I was frightened and sad, both at once.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what helps when we are very sad  
> _Sinbad was very sad. What helps when someone is very sad?_  
> - ✅ A hug, or a friend sitting close. → Yes. A hug helps. So does a friend sitting close. Sad feelings are allowed.
> - Pretending to feel fine. → Hiding sad feelings can make them heavy. A hug or a friend sitting close helps most.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about what helps when someone is very sad._


**Choices**

- **Put your hand on his.**
    - **Sinbad the Sailor**: Thank you. It was long ago. It is also tonight.
- **Let your Nubbin climb into his lap.**
    - It sits on his knee.
    - He rests a hand on its head, and goes on.

#### `a06-08-telling-done`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: Come in now, just for the dark part, and the light after it.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): opposites: dark and light  
> _Dark and light are opposites. Opposites are as different as can be._  
> _Dark and light. Big and small. Can you think of another pair?_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned the opposites dark and light, and thought of another pair._

_The lamps flicker. The porter holds his breath._  

#### `a06-08-dark`

_The carpet goes black. It is cold and quiet._  
**Young Sinbad**: Hello. You came. I did not want to ask anyone.  
_Sinbad is younger here. His voice is steady, but he is sad._  
_Your Nubbin turns its head to the left._  
_You feel a little air on your face. It smells of salt._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): we feel with our skin  
> _You feel air on your face. Which part of you feels the air moving?_  
> - ✅ My skin. → Yes! Your skin feels air, and warm, and cold. Air that moves like this is called a breeze.
> - My toes only. → Toes feel things, but the air is on your face. Skin all over can feel air moving.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that skin can feel moving air._


**Choices**

- **Take Sinbad’s hand and follow the draught.**
    - You walk slowly. He holds on tight.
- **Stay still and listen first.**
    - Far off, something small is scratching. It is alive, and not afraid.

#### `a06-08-dark-done`

_Something brushes your ankle._  
_It is a little animal with a striped face._  
_It knows where it is going._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): describing words  
> _The little animal has a striped face. Which word tells us about its face?_  
> - ✅ Striped. → Yes! Striped tells what its face looks like. Stripes, stripes!
> - Slowly. → “Slowly” tells how it moves. “Striped” tells what its face looks like.
> _For grown-ups: Picked out a describing word (striped)._


#### `a06-08-tunnel`

_The little animal slips into a crack in the rock._  
**Young Sinbad**: If it gets in and out, so can we.  
_The crack is tight, so you go sideways. Your Nubbin waits at each bend._  
_You hear the sea. You see grey light._  
_You come out on the shingle at the foot of a cliff._  
_Sinbad sits on the stones and cries. You sit beside him._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): crying is okay and a friend can sit beside you  
> _Crying is okay. Crying lets sad feelings out._  
> _You did not fix anything. You sat beside him. That helps a lot._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that crying is okay and that sitting beside a sad friend helps._


#### `a06-08-tunnel-done`

_Some days later a ship sees his fire on the stones._  
_The sailors take him home._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): helpers who look after others  
> _The sailors saw a fire and came to help._  
> _People who help others are called helpers._  
> _Can you think of a helper you know?_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard about people who help others, and thought of a helper they know._


#### `a06-08-complete`

_The lamps glow in the long room. The porter has stopped eating._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I am sorry about your wife.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Thank you. Nobody has said that for a long time.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what to say to someone who is sad  
> _The porter said sorry about the wife._  
> _What could you say to a sad friend?_  
> - ✅ “I am sorry you feel sad.” → Yes. Kind words show you care. A hug can help too, if they want one.
> - “Stop being sad.” → Sad feelings cannot just stop. Saying “I am sorry you feel sad” helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Practised a kind thing to say to someone who is sad._

**Sinbad the Porter**: I said a foolish thing on your bench.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: You said a true thing. It was half the truth.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Come back for the other half.  

## A6-9. The Roc’s Revenge

- `a06-09-s1`: Try to stop the merchants cracking the egg. · _Get to the white dome before the merchants._
- `a06-09-s2`: Hold on to a plank in the sea. · _Grab a plank. Keep your Nubbin close._

#### `a06-09-egg`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: The fifth voyage. I had my own ship by then.  
_There is an island, and a white dome. You know what it is._  
**Young Sinbad**: Do not touch it. I have met its mother!  
_The merchants laugh. They knock on the shell._  
_Crack! A big, fluffy chick tumbles out and shrieks._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-LS1-2, ask): parents look after their babies  
> _The big birds are the chick’s parents._  
> _What do bird parents do for their babies?_  
> - ✅ Keep them safe, and feed them. → Yes! Bird parents keep their babies safe and feed them. So do many animals.
> - Leave them alone. → Bird parents stay close. They keep their babies safe and feed them.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that parents look after their babies._

**Young Sinbad**: You fools!  

**Choices**

- **Help the chick into the shade of the rocks.**
    - It is as soft as a pillow.
    - It lets you push it, grumbling, into the shade.
- **Stand between the merchants and the chick.**
    - The merchants back away. One looks at the sky, and goes pale.

#### `a06-09-egg-done`

_Two huge shadows cross the island._  
_One, then two. The parents are home._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 2  
> _One shadow, two shadows. How many parents? Two!_  
> Check: `edu:count:shadows:2`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two shadows._


#### `a06-09-boulders`

_Sinbad gets everyone on the ship. It races away._  
_The big birds carry boulders in their claws._  
**Young Sinbad**: Hard over! Hard over!  
_Splash! The boulders crash into the sea._  
_The ship breaks into planks. You hold a plank, and your Nubbin holds you._  
_The big birds fly home to their chick. They were not being cruel._  
_They were looking after their baby._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): why someone is cross  
> _The big birds were upset because their baby was frightened._  
> _When we know why someone is cross, we can understand them better._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that people are often cross because they want to protect someone, and understanding that helps._


**Choices**

- **Shout for Sinbad.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Here! Over here! Swim to me!
- **Float, and save your breath.**
    - An hour later, Sinbad’s plank bumps into yours. He is very pleased.

#### `a06-09-boulders-done`

_A current carries you both along._  
_By evening there is an island. It has fruit and running water._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): what living things need  
> _The island has fruit and fresh water. Why is that good for people?_  
> - ✅ People need food and water. → Yes! People, animals and plants all need water. Animals and people need food too.
> - To play with. → Fun, but also something more. People need food and water to live.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that living things need food and water._


#### `a06-09-complete`

_The porter has brought his little daughter. She is asleep on the cushions._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: The merchants had it coming.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I knew, and I did not make them listen.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: You told them.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, SL.K.1, ask): good listening  
> _Listening is hard. What does a good listener do?_  
> - ✅ Looks at you and stays quiet. → Yes! Eyes on the speaker, and a quiet mouth. That is good listening.
> - Talks over you. → That makes it hard to hear! A good listener looks, and keeps quiet until it is their turn.
> _For grown-ups: Practised what good listening looks like._

**Sinbad the Sailor**: Telling is not the same as making someone listen.  

## A6-10. The Old Man of the Sea

- `a06-10-s1`: Help the little old man across the stream. · _Go to the stream where the old man sits._
- `a06-10-s2`: Find a way to make him let go. · _Watch what he reaches for. Look for a low branch._
- `a06-10-s3`: Help the sailors pick coconuts. · _Throw pebbles near the monkeys, never at them._

#### `a06-10-bank`

_By a stream sits a little old man in seaweed._  
_He does not speak. He points across the stream._  
**Young Sinbad**: He wants to be carried. Up you come, grandfather.  
_On the far bank, he does not get down!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): asking before you take  
> _The old man never asked. He just climbed up and would not get down._  
> _A good friend asks first: “May I?” And listens for the answer._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that asking before taking or climbing on someone is kind._

_He drums his heels, and points at a fig tree._  

**Choices**

- **Try to lift him off.**
    - His legs squeeze tighter. You stop at once.
- **Ask him politely to get down.**
    - He looks at you with bright black eyes. He points at another fig tree.

#### `a06-10-bank-done`

_Days pass like this._  
_The old man’s legs are long, and limp, and wrinkly._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): describing words  
> _The old man has long, limp, wrinkly legs._  
> _Which word means the opposite of long?_  
> - ✅ Short. → Yes! Short is the opposite of long. Long legs, short legs!
> - Wrinkly. → Wrinkly is about bumpy skin. The opposite of long is short.
> _For grown-ups: Matched the opposite of long (short)._

_He never gets down._  

#### `a06-10-fig`

**Young Sinbad**: I cannot lie down. He steers me by the ears.  
_Your Nubbin watches the old man’s hands. They always reach for fruit._  
_A fig tree has a low branch full of ripe fruit._  
_Your Nubbin points at the branch. Then it bends its knees._  
**Young Sinbad**: Walk under the branch. Then duck!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): under and over  
> _Sinbad will walk under the branch. Will he go over it, or under it?_  
> - ✅ Under it. → Yes! Under means below. He goes under the branch. (Put your hand under your chin.)
> - Over it. → Over means on top. Sinbad ducks, so he goes under the branch!
> _For grown-ups: Used the position word “under”._


**Choices**

- **Lead Sinbad under the low branch.**
    - The old man reaches up with both arms. His legs loosen.
- **Send your Nubbin to tickle his feet first.**
    - He squirms. Then he sees the figs, and his legs loosen.

#### `a06-10-fig-done`

**Young Sinbad**: Now!  
_Sinbad ducks. The old man hangs from the branch by both hands._  
_His mouth is full of fig._  
_He is quite surprised, and not hurt at all._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): sulking is a feeling too  
> _The old man feels cross and sulky. Sulking means feeling cross and going quiet._  
> _Nobody was hurt. He just needs time to calm down._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that feeling cross and sulky is a feeling and needs time to calm down._


#### `a06-10-coconuts`

_You run, and run, to the shore._  
_Sailors are picking coconuts. They are amazed that Sinbad got away._  
**A Coconut Gatherer**: Come with us. Watch how we do it.  
_The palm trees are tall and full of monkeys._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): animals live where they get what they need  
> _The monkeys live up in the palm trees. Why do monkeys like palm trees?_  
> - ✅ They find food and a safe place. → Yes! Animals live where they find food and a safe place. Palm trees have both.
> - To be near the sea only. → The sea is close by. But food and a safe place matter most.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that animals live where their needs are met._

_The sailors throw pebbles near the monkeys, carefully missing._  
_The monkeys throw coconuts back. Thud, thud!_  

**Choices**

- **Throw a pebble.**
    - A coconut comes back and lands in your arms. You win!
- **Let your Nubbin pull faces at them instead.**
    - It rains coconuts!
    - **A Coconut Gatherer**: We are keeping that one.

#### `a06-10-complete`

**Young Sinbad**: He was not wicked. He just found a good shoulder.  
_In the long room, the porter rubs his own shoulders._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I have carried men like that. I never put them down.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: You did. You got up from my bench and came in.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Hm.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): putting down a worry  
> _The porter put down his cross feelings and came in. That felt lighter._  
> _When you have a worry, telling a friend helps you put it down._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sharing a worry can make it feel lighter._


## A6-11. The River of Jewels

- `a06-11-s1`: Look along the beach for a way out. · _Follow the river along the beach._
- `a06-11-s2`: Build a raft from the broken ships. · _Gather planks and rope by the cave._
- `a06-11-s3`: Ride the raft through the mountain. · _Lie flat and hold on._

#### `a06-11-coast`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: The sixth voyage. I was an old fool by then.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I was not going to say so.  
_A ship is broken on a mountain beach. Wrecks lie all along it._  
**Young Sinbad**: Everything anyone ever lost is here. None of it is any use.  
_A river runs down the beach. It runs into a cave!_  
**Young Sinbad**: Water goes somewhere. A river always goes somewhere.  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): rivers flow downhill to the sea  
> _Rivers flow downhill. Most run all the way to the sea._  
> _Water always flows down, not up, like a ball rolling down a slope._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that rivers flow downhill._


**Choices**

- **Look up at the mountain road.**
    - It goes up into cloud, steep and bare. Sinbad looks back at the river.
- **Put your hand in the river.**
    - It is cold and quick. It tugs your fingers.

#### `a06-11-coast-done`

**Young Sinbad**: A raft, then. If the river goes in, it comes out.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): first, next, last  
> _Sinbad has a plan. First he builds a raft. What does he do next?_  
> - ✅ Rides it down the river. → Yes! First build, next ride, and last, come out the other side.
> - Eats a sandwich. → Yum, but not in his plan. First build, next ride the raft down the river.
> _For grown-ups: Put the steps of a plan in order._

_Sinbad looks at the planks along the beach._  

#### `a06-11-raft`

_You find planks and ropes from the broken ships._  
_The pebbles in the river are jewels! Red and blue and green._  
**Young Sinbad**: Nobody would believe me!  
_Your Nubbin picks up a green one. It puts it back._  
**Young Sinbad**: You and your friend are no good at being rich.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.B.3, do): sort by colour  
> _Put the red pebbles together. Put the blue together. Put the green together._  
> Check: `edu:sort:pebbles:colour`
> _For grown-ups: Sorted jewel pebbles by colour._


**Choices**

- **Help him tie the sack to the raft.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: If we sink, at least we sink impressively!
- **Ask if he’s ever been good at it.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: I am good at getting rich. Being rich is different.

#### `a06-11-dark`

_The cave swallows the raft. It gets dark._  
_You lie flat. Your Nubbin lies flat on top of you._  
**Young Sinbad**: Keep your head down. Think of something nice.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): thinking of something nice calms us  
> _When we feel nervous, we can think of something nice. A pond._  
> _A cosy bed. A friend._  
> _What is your something nice? (Wait for an answer.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Practised calming down by thinking of something nice._

_The rock glitters a little, like tiny stars._  
_Sinbad falls asleep, and so do you._  

**Choices**

- **Think of the Grove.**
    - You think of the pond and the fruit trees. It helps.
- **Think of the porter, waiting on his cushion.**
    - You can almost hear him: “I will mind the dates.”

#### `a06-11-complete`

_You wake to sunshine. The raft is tied to a bank by green fields._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Where did it come out?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Serendib. A great island, far from here.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): an island is land with water all around  
> _Serendib is an island. What is an island?_  
> - ✅ Land with water all round. → Yes! An island is land with water all around it. (Draw a little island with your finger.)
> - Water with land all round. → That is a lake! An island is land with water all around it.
> _For grown-ups: Learned what an island is._

**Sinbad the Porter**: You cannot stop there!  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I am old. I can stop where I like.  

## A6-12. Serendib

- `a06-12-s1`: Walk with the farmer to see the king. · _Walk through the fields to the palace._
- `a06-12-s2`: Tell the king about Baghdad. · _Sit with Sinbad in front of the king._
- `a06-12-s3`: Climb the great mountain to see the sunrise. · _Join the people on the steps at night._

#### `a06-12-bank`

**A Farmer of Serendib**: You came out of the mountain! Nobody does that.  
**Young Sinbad**: I did not mean to. I come from Baghdad.  
**A Farmer of Serendib**: Come with me. Our king will want to hear this.  
_Green rice fields step down the hills. Water shines in each one._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, notice): rice plants need water and light  
> **A Farmer of Serendib**: Rice plants love water.  
> **A Farmer of Serendib**: Their roots stand in it, and their leaves reach for the sun.  
> **A Farmer of Serendib**: Plants need water and light to grow big and green.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants need water and light, like rice in its watery fields._

_The trees smell of cinnamon when you rub them._  
_Your Nubbin rubs every tree. It arrives smelling like a pudding._  

**Choices**

- **Ask the farmer about the trees.**
    - **A Farmer of Serendib**: Cinnamon! It comes from tree bark. We sell it far away.
- **Ask about the water in the terraces.**
    - **A Farmer of Serendib**: It flows from field to field. Each farmer passes it on to the next.

#### `a06-12-bank-done`

_The palace is cool and open. Birds fly in and out._  
_The king is waiting. He is as curious as a boy._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): kings and leaders listen  
> _A good leader listens. The king wants to hear about other places._  
> _Listening to other people helps us learn._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that good leaders listen to others._


#### `a06-12-court`

**The King of Serendib**: Welcome! Sit. You came through the mountain?  
**Young Sinbad**: I did, your majesty. Not on purpose.  
**The King of Serendib**: Tell me about your Caliph. Is he fair?  
**Young Sinbad**: They say he walks the city to see how people live.  
**The King of Serendib**: A king who looks for himself. Good! I will write to him.  
**The King of Serendib**: You will carry my letter. You will be my messenger.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): greeting someone politely  
> _Sinbad is meeting a king._  
> _How can we greet someone new in a polite way?_  
> - ✅ Say hello, and smile. → Yes! Hello and a smile make people feel welcome. (Wave and smile.)
> - Look away and say nothing. → That could make them feel left out. A hello and a smile feel friendly.
> _For grown-ups: Practised greeting someone new politely._


**Choices**

- **Nudge Sinbad to accept.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: It would be an honour, your majesty.
    - Then he whispers to you, “What have I done?”
- **Let your Nubbin bow to the king.**
    - It bows so low it rolls over. The king laughs out loud!

#### `a06-12-peak`

_Before the ship sails, Sinbad climbs the great mountain._  
_Many people climb it, all night, to see the sun rise._  
**A Farmer of Serendib**: People come for different reasons. Everyone climbs the same steps.  
_The sun comes up, red, over the sea._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): respect for other people’s beliefs  
> _People believe different things, and that is okay. They can climb side by side._  
> _Being kind to people who are different from us is called respect._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that people believe different things and that respecting each other is kind._

_Everyone goes quiet. Your Nubbin sits very still on your foot._  

#### `a06-12-complete`

_The king gives Sinbad a letter, and gifts, and a ship home._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: A king who writes to another king, because a sailor washed up.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: That is how many friendships between countries begin.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): friendships can start in surprising ways  
> _A sailor washed up, and two kings became friends._  
> _Friendships can start in surprising ways. How did you meet a friend?_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that friendships can start in surprising ways, and remembered meeting a friend._

**Sinbad the Porter**: Did you swear again?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I did. That one nearly took.  

## A6-13. The Caliph’s Gift

- `a06-13-s1`: Take the king’s letter to the Caliph. · _Go into the palace and wait to be called._
- `a06-13-s2`: Sail with the wind to give the Caliph’s letter to the king. · _Board the ship at Basra when the wind turns._

#### `a06-13-palace`

_Sinbad comes home to the round city. He goes straight to the palace._  
_The court is full of scholars and busy clerks._  
**Harun al-Rashid**: Peace be upon you. You are the man who came out of a mountain?  
**Young Sinbad**: And upon you, peace. Through a mountain, yes.  
**Harun al-Rashid**: The King of Serendib has written to me. Please read it.  
**The Translator**: He has heard that you are fair.  
**The Translator**: He sends a ruby cup, and asks to be your friend.  
**The Translator**: It is in Arabic, and very good Arabic. Somebody there reads our books.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): people speak and write in different languages  
> _The translator helps people read a letter in a different language._  
> _What does a translator do?_  
> - ✅ Changes words from one language to another. → Yes! A translator turns words into another language, so people can understand.
> - Cooks the dinner. → Not that! A translator turns words into another language so people understand.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a translator helps people understand another language._

**Harun al-Rashid**: Then he shall have more books, and an answer. Sinbad, you will carry it.  

**Choices**

- **Ask the translator which languages they read at the House of Wisdom.**
    - **The Translator**: Greek, Persian, and many more.
    - **The Translator**: If a book exists, someone here wants to read it.
- **Let your Nubbin look into the ruby cup.**
    - It sees its own face, small and red. It is delighted.
    - **Harun al-Rashid**: The gift has found its true admirer.

#### `a06-13-palace-done`

_The Caliph sends books, and fine cloth, and a silver saddle._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _Books, cloth, and a saddle. Touch each gift and count: one, two, three!_  
> Check: `edu:count:gifts:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three gifts._

_Sinbad looks at the saddle. He says nothing._  

#### `a06-13-monsoon`

_At Basra, ships crowd the quay. They are all waiting for the wind._  
**The Captain**: For half the year the wind blows one way.  
**The Captain**: For half the year it blows the other way.  
**The Captain**: We sail out on one wind. We sail home on the other.  
_In the night the wind turns. In the morning every sail fills at once._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, notice): wind changes direction through the year  
> **The Captain**: Wind is moving air. It blows one way for months, and then it turns.  
> **The Captain**: Sailors learn the winds, like you learn your own street.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the wind can blow one way for months and then turn._

_Weeks of blue. Then green hills, and a king on the shore._  
**The King of Serendib**: Books! He sent me books!  

#### `a06-13-monsoon-done`

**The King of Serendib**: Go home safely, messenger. Tell your Caliph I am reading.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, notice): books and reading are for sharing  
> _Books can be shared across the sea._  
> _Someone far away reads the same words that you can read._  
> _Books connect people. What is your favourite book?_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that books can be shared and connect people._

_The king hugs his new books. He waves as the ship sails off._  

#### `a06-13-complete`

_On the way home, pirates take the ship. They carry everyone far away._  
_In a far town, Sinbad has to work for a rich merchant._  
_He is not allowed to leave._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: After all that? After the letter?  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: After all that. The sea never asked if I deserved it.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Come back for the next part. Sinbad is brave.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: And there is a kind choice in it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): it is okay to feel worried; Sinbad stays brave  
> _That is a hard bit. Feeling worried about it is okay._  
> _Sinbad is still brave. And the story is kind to him._  
> _A grown-up can give you a hug._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that feeling worried about a hard part of a story is okay, with reassurance._


## A6-14. The Elephant Hunter

- `a06-14-s1`: Sit in the tree by the elephants’ path. · _Climb up beside Sinbad before dawn._
- `a06-14-s2`: Go where the elephants take you. · _Hold on to Sinbad. Let the elephants lead._
- `a06-14-s3`: The master is at his gate. Decide what to tell him. · _Talk to the master at the gate._

#### `a06-14-tree`

**The Ivory Merchant**: You talk to kings? Good. Sit in the tree. When the elephants pass, shoot.  
**The Ivory Merchant**: I need ivory.  
_Every morning, you sit in the tree with Sinbad._  
_The herd walks past. An old elephant leads them._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count the calves  
> _Look at the little ones walking under their mothers._  
> _Count the calves: one, two, three, four!_  
> Check: `edu:count:calves:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four elephant calves._

_Every morning, Sinbad’s arrows land far away in the mud._  
**Young Sinbad**: I am the worst archer in the world. On purpose. Do not tell him.  

**Choices**

- **Promise not to tell.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Thank you. He is not a bad man. He just has a warehouse.
- **Count the calves in the herd.**
    - Four calves walk under their mothers. One looks up at you.

#### `a06-14-tree-done`

_Weeks go by, with mud and missed arrows._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): kindness to animals  
> **Young Sinbad**: I will not hurt the elephants. They have done nothing wrong.  
> **Young Sinbad**: They are somebody’s mums and babies.  
> _Being gentle to animals is kind._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that being gentle with animals is a way of being kind._

_The master grumbles, and buys more arrows._  

#### `a06-14-herd`

_One morning the herd stops by the tree. It is quiet._  
_The old elephant pulls the tree over, slowly and gently._  
_Sinbad falls. She catches him in her trunk, and sets him on her back._  
_You climb up too. Your Nubbin comes too._  
_They walk all day to a valley with a white floor._  
_It is full of old tusks and bones._  
_The old elephant sets you down, safe. The herd turns and goes._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-LS1-2, ask): elephants live in families led by an old female  
> _The herd followed the oldest elephant. Who leads an elephant family?_  
> - ✅ The oldest mother elephant. → Yes! An elephant herd is a family. The oldest female leads, and she remembers the way.
> - The smallest calf. → Calves follow their mothers. The oldest female leads, because she remembers the way.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that elephants live in families led by the oldest female._


#### `a06-14-herd-done`

**Young Sinbad**: Go to the town ahead. I twisted my ankle.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): what helps a hurt ankle  
> _Sinbad has a sore ankle. What helps a sore ankle get better?_  
> - ✅ Rest it, and ask a grown-up for help. → Yes! Rest, a cool cloth and a grown-up’s help make a sore ankle feel better.
> - Run and jump on it. → Ouch! That would hurt more. A sore ankle needs rest, and a grown-up’s help.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a hurt body part needs rest and a grown-up’s help._

**Young Sinbad**: You decide what he is told. I have done enough deciding for elephants.  

#### `a06-14-gate`

_The master meets you at his gate. He looks worried._  
**The Ivory Merchant**: The tree is down. Where is Sinbad?  
_Far behind you, the herd walks home in a long grey line._  
_Your Nubbin looks at the herd, then at you. It waits._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): both choices come from caring  
> _You can tell, and ask for a promise._  
> _Or you can keep the elephants’ secret. Both come from caring._  
> _Which feels right to you?_  
> _For grown-ups: Thought about a choice where both options come from caring._


**Choices**

- **Tell him, once he swears to take only the old tusks and never hunt again.**
    - **You**: There is a valley. Before I show you, you must promise.
    - **The Ivory Merchant**: I promise. On my children.
- **Keep the elephants’ secret.**
    - **You**: I do not know where he went.
    - **The Ivory Merchant**: He will come back. Where else would he go?

#### `a06-14-gate-done`

_That evening Sinbad limps through the gate._  
_He looks at you and the master. He understands, without a word._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): we can tell feelings without words  
> _Sinbad understood without words. How can we tell how people feel?_  
> - ✅ Look at their faces and bodies. → Yes! Faces, eyes and bodies show feelings, even when no one speaks.
> - We can never tell. → We can often tell! Faces, eyes and bodies show feelings.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that faces and bodies show feelings._


#### `a06-14-complete`

_The master takes his carts to the white valley._  
_He loads old tusks that were left behind._  
_On the road, the herd passes. The master bows his head to them._  
**The Ivory Merchant**: You are free, Sinbad. Go home.  
**Young Sinbad**: The elephants paid for my freedom. I want to remember that.  
**The Ivory Merchant**: Nobody in this town will hunt them again. I have promised.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-3, notice): we look after wild animals  
> _Elephants are wild animals. People can look after them by leaving them in peace._  
> _Many places make rules to keep elephants safe. That is called protecting them._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people can protect wild animals such as elephants._


## A6-15. Home

- `a06-15-s1`: Come home to Baghdad with Sinbad. · _Walk with Sinbad from the quay to the city._
- `a06-15-s2`: Walk the porter home to his street. · _Leave the great house with the porter and his daughter._

#### `a06-15-quay`

_The ship comes into Basra early. It sits low in the water._  
**Young Sinbad**: Home! Rich, early, and safe. That never happened before!  
_He walks in through the city gate. You are beside him._  
**Young Sinbad**: Seven voyages! And I promise you now: there is no eighth.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): what a promise is  
> _Sinbad makes a promise. What is a promise?_  
> - ✅ Saying you will do something, and doing it. → Yes! A promise is saying you will, and then doing it. Keeping a promise is trustworthy.
> - Saying something and forgetting. → A promise is something you really do. It helps people trust you.
> _For grown-ups: Learned what a promise is._

_For once, he keeps his promise._  

**Choices**

- **Say you believe him this time.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: So do I. That is new.
- **Ask how long it will last.**
    - **Young Sinbad**: Ha! Fair.
    - **Young Sinbad**: This time, for good. I have run out of things to be bored of.

#### `a06-15-street`

_The carpet is a carpet again. The old man smiles at his hands._  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I came home heavy that time. Porter, does your street have a fountain?  
**Sinbad the Porter**: There is a well at the far end. The women walk there all morning.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Then it has a fountain now.  
_Next morning, workmen are on his street with stone._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): a fountain shares water with everyone  
> _A fountain gives water to everybody in the street, big or small._  
> _Sharing things with everyone is fair._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a public fountain shares water fairly with everyone._

**The Porter’s Daughter**: Baba! They are building water! Right here!  

**Choices**

- **Ask the old man why.**
    - **Sinbad the Sailor**: Because a man complained on my bench, and he was right.
- **Promise the daughter you’ll come back for the first drink.**
    - **The Porter’s Daughter**: You have to! I will save you the first cup!

#### `a06-15-complete`

_Back in the long room, the old man opens a chest._  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: I have something for you and your little one.  
_It is a folded sail. It has a patch you have seen before._  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: From my first ship. Hang it where you can see the wind.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): wind pushes sails  
> _A sail catches the wind. What pushes a sailing ship?_  
> - ✅ The wind. → Yes! Wind pushes the sail, and the sail pushes the ship. Whooosh!
> - The sail by itself. → A sail needs the wind to push it. Without wind, a ship sits still.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that wind pushes a sail._

**Sinbad the Porter**: Then give me one more evening. Next time, you will hear mine.  
**Sinbad the Sailor**: Yours?  

## A6-16. The Porter’s Voyage

- `a06-16-s1`: Listen to the porter tell his own story. · _Sit in the long room with the household._
- `a06-16-s2`: Bring the storyteller’s cushion home. · _Step back through the page. Put the cushion where your Nubbins can sit._
- `a06-16-s3`: Tell your own story to the Grove. · _Sit on the storyteller’s cushion._

#### `a06-16-telling`

_It is the last evening. Everyone is in the long room._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I have never told a story. I have only carried a few.  
_He puts something on the low table. It is a small, clear stone._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: This is the first line of my story.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: A friend brought it from a valley.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I will never sell it.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: I am a porter. I carry paper, and I cannot read, so I listen.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, notice): a story has a beginning  
> _Every story starts somewhere. The porter began with the stone._  
> _A story has a beginning, a middle, and an end._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a story has a beginning, a middle, and an end._


#### `a06-16-telling-done`

**Sinbad the Porter**: And at the end, a herd walked home through the hills.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Nobody shot at them. Nobody ever will.  
**Sinbad the Porter**: The elephants were paid for in bones.  
_Nobody speaks. Then the old man claps, and everyone claps._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): sharing a story is brave  
> _The porter felt nervous. It takes courage to share a story._  
> _Clapping says, “well done!”_  
> _(Clap like the crowd. Clap, clap, clap!)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sharing a story takes courage and that clapping shows kindness._


#### `a06-16-grove`

**Sinbad the Sailor**: Take this cushion. I told from it, all seven nights.  
_It is round and faded. A tiny ship is sewn on it._  
**Sinbad the Porter**: Now he wants to listen, and he starts with me.  
_You step back through the page. The Grove’s evening is all round you._  
_Your Nubbin drags the cushion over the lawn._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-PS3-1, ask): shade is cooler than sunshine  
> _Under the fruit trees it is shady._  
> _Is the shade cooler or warmer than the sunny grass?_  
> - ✅ Cooler. → Yes! The leaves block the sun, so the shade stays cool.
> - Warmer. → The sun warms the grass it shines on. The leaves block it, so shade is cooler.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sunshine warms the ground and shade stays cooler._


**Choices**

- **Set it down by the pond.**
    - Where the water can listen too. Your Nubbin sits on it at once.
- **Set it down under the fruit trees.**
    - In the shade. Your Nubbin sits on it at once.

#### `a06-16-grove-done`

_One by one, your Nubbins come over the grass._  
_They sit in a ring round the cushion._

> _Touch each Nubbin as you count them. How many are in the ring?_  
> Check: `edu:count:nubbins:ring`
> _For grown-ups: Counted the Nubbins in the ring, touching each one._


#### `a06-16-tell`

_You sit on the cushion. All the little faces look up._  
_Nova sits down at the back of the ring._  
_You have never told a story either._  
_Your Nubbin sits on your foot, to help._  
_You take a breath. Then you begin._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, SL.K.1, notice): talking and listening in turns  
> _When one person tells, the others listen. Then it is someone else’s turn._  
> _Talking and listening in turns is how stories are shared._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that stories are shared by talking and listening in turns._


**Choices**

    - **You**: Once there was an island that was fast asleep...
    - Your Nubbin rolls onto its back, being the whale.
- **Begin with the porter on the bench.**

- **Begin with the elephants.**
    - **You**: Once there was a herd of elephants who wanted to be left alone...

**Nova**: A woman in Persia told stories to a king. One story each night.  
**Nova**: She told them until he learned to be kind.  
**Nova**: Persian, then Arabic, then French, then English. And now you, on a cushion.

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): stories travel from person to person  
> _Stories travel from place to place. How does a story travel?_

> - The story walks by itself. → Stories do not walk! People carry them, by telling them.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that stories travel because people tell them to each other._

- `a7-01-s2`: Help carry the marigolds into the house. · _Take the flowers from the cart. Bring them to Abuelita._
- `a7-01-s3`: Look at the family ofrenda. Meet Mamá Coco. · _Go to the altar at the end of the room. Look at the photos._

#### `a7-01-plaza`

_Nova’s atlas opens at a page of orange flowers and paper flags._  
_Whoosh! You and your Nubbin are in a town in Mexico._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): Mexico is a country, and many people there speak Spanish  
> _Mexico is a country. Many people there speak Spanish._  
> _(Find Mexico on a map or a globe, if you have one.)_

_Everyone carries marigolds. They are bright orange!_

_That is a festival. Families remember people who have died._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): say “hola”, hello in Spanish  
> **Miguel**: Hola! That means hello in Spanish. Say it with me!  
> _(Wave and say “Hola!”)_  
> Check: `edu:say:word:hola`
> _For grown-ups: Said hola, the Spanish word for hello._


**Choices**

    - **Miguel**: Then come and see our ofrenda! Abuelita’s is the best.
- **Ask who the man on the statue is.**
    - **Miguel**: That is Ernesto de la Cruz. He was a famous singer!
- **Let your Nubbin say hello.**
    - Your Nubbin hops onto the shoe box. Miguel laughs and laughs.

#### `a7-01-plaza-done`

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): what a dog needs to live

> - ✅ Food, water and a cosy home → Yes! Dante gets all three, and a lot of cuddles.
> - Only toys → Toys are fun! But Dante needs food, water and a home first.
> - Only sweets → Dante would love that! But dogs need proper food and water.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what a dog needs to live: food, water and a home._

**Abuelita**: There. Now the dog won’t think it’s a toy.  
**Abuelita**: These flowers are cempasúchil. Say it with me.  
**Abuelita**: Sem-pa-SOO-cheel. Clap for every beat!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the four syllables of cempasúchil  
> _Cem. Pa. Sú. Chil. Four claps!_  
> _(Clap with the beats. How many claps?)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:cempasuchil`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the four syllables of the Spanish word for marigold._

_They are bright, and they smell strong._  
_That helps loved ones who have died find their way home._  
_Your Nubbin carries one marigold, very proudly._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, ask): count the pieces to answer “how many?”  
> _(Point to each piece in turn.) How many pieces did Abuelita cut?_  
> - ✅ Three → Yes! One, two, three. A piece each.
> - Two → Let’s count again: one for you, one for Miguel, one for Nubbin. Three!
> - Five → Let’s count again: one, two, three. Three pieces.
> _For grown-ups: Counted three pieces of pan de muerto._

_The ofrenda is a family altar, with steps going up._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): an ofrenda is how a family remembers people they love  
> _An ofrenda is how a family remembers people who have died._  
> _They add photos, flowers, candles and favourite foods._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned what an ofrenda is, and how Mexican families use it to remember loved ones._

_Some photos are very old. One has a torn corner._  
_A man with a guitar was in that photo. His face is gone._  
**Miguel**: Mamá Imelda was sad about him. So our house has no music.  
_An old, old lady sits by the ofrenda. This is Mamá Coco._  
**Mamá Coco**: Who are you? Are you new?  

**Choices**

- **Take her hand and say your name.**
    - **Mamá Coco**: That’s a good name. I’ll try to keep it.
- **Sit beside her. Say nothing.**
    - You sit, and watch the candles with her. She pats your knee.
- **Lift your Nubbin up so she can see.**
    - **Mamá Coco**: Oh! You’re a funny one.

#### `a7-01-photo-done`

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): name the character in the story  
> _Mamá Coco asks about her papá. Who is she waiting for?_  
> - ✅ Her papá → Yes. Papá is the Spanish word for dad. She misses him very much.
> - Dante the dog → Dante is here already. She is waiting for her papá, her dad.
> - Abuelita → Abuelita is here too. Mamá Coco is waiting for her papá, her dad.
> _For grown-ups: Named the character in the story and learned papá, the Spanish word for dad._

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): tell a trusted grown-up about a worry  
> _Miguel has a secret that makes him worry. Who could he tell?_  
> - ✅ A grown-up he trusts → Yes. Telling a trusted grown-up shrinks a worry.
> - Nobody at all → Worries get heavy when we carry them alone. A grown-up can help.
> - Only the dog → Dante is a good listener! A grown-up can help too.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about telling a trusted grown-up when a secret feels worrying._

_Your Nubbin’s ribbon flutters, bright as a marigold._

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): calming down when you feel cross  
> _Abuelita is cross. What helps when we feel cross?_  
> - ✅ Breathe in and out slowly → Yes! In through your nose, out through your mouth. (Try it!)
> - Shout louder → Shouting makes cross feelings bigger. A slow breath helps them shrink.
> - Stamp and throw things → Things can get broken that way. A slow breath is gentler.
> _For grown-ups: Practised slow breathing as a way to calm down when cross._

> - A square → A square has four corners. This hole is round, a circle.
> - A triangle → A triangle has three corners. This hole is round, a circle.
> _For grown-ups: Named a circle._

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): finish a colour pattern  
> _Pink, green, pink, green, pink… What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Green → Yes! Pink, green, pink, green, pink, green.
> - Pink → Let’s say it slowly: pink, green, pink, green, pink… then green!
> - Blue → There’s no blue in this pattern. Pink, green, pink, green… green is next!
> _For grown-ups: Continued a pink and green colour pattern._

> _Alebrijes are real! Artists in Mexico make them from paper or wood._  
> _Then they paint them with bright colours and patterns._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that alebrijes are bright painted creatures made by artists in Mexico._

> - Push to the front → Pushing isn’t fair. Everyone gets a turn, in order.
> - Shout at the officer → Shouting makes it harder for everyone. Waiting calmly is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about waiting calmly for a turn._

> - A blanket → Blankets are for us. Plants need sun, water and soil.
