**The Snork Maiden**: Why is there a wardrobe?  
_In a puddle lies a pink shell with a curl._  
_You pick it up. You hold it to your ear._  
**Moomintroll**: It is waiting. It is listening for the sea, like us.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): a shell is an animal’s home  
> _The shell is empty. Who lived in the shell, a long time ago?_  
> - ✅ A small sea animal → Yes! A shell is a sea animal’s home. It grows with them.
> - A bird → Birds live in nests. Shells are homes for small sea animals.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a shell was an animal’s home._


#### `a09-08-seabed-done`

_You put the shell in your pocket._  
_It is pink, and curly, and very light._  
_It seems to want carrying._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): describing words  
> _The shell is pink, curly and light. What word tells us how it looks?_  
> - ✅ Curly → Yes! Curly. Describing words tell us what things are like.
> - Loud → A shell is not loud. Pink, curly and light are describing words.
> _For grown-ups: Picked out a describing word for how something looks._


#### `a09-08-complete`

_The sun goes down behind you._  
_Out on the seabed, the light comes from the sky, red and steady._  
**Snufkin**: We will go on in the dark. The comet lights the way.  
_Sniff counts his stilts, his pocket, his Nubbin, and you._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): the Sun goes down every evening  
> _The Sun goes down every evening, and comes up every morning._  
> _Day, then night, then day again._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the Sun sets each evening and rises each morning._


## A9-9. The Octopus

- `a09-09-s1`: Cross the deep part of the seabed. · _Keep to the ridge of rock. Stay away from the dark pool._
- `a09-09-s2`: Keep everyone together while the Snork Maiden helps. · _Hold the line on the ridge. Hold a light up if you can._

#### `a09-09-deep`

_The seabed dips down. The pools are dark and deep._  
_Everything is red in the comet’s light._  
**The Snork**: We keep to the ridge. Single file. That is a rule.  
**Moomintroll**: Not far now. I can almost smell the jam.  
_Moomintroll steps off the ridge to take a shortcut._  
_His stilt sinks into the edge of a dark pool._  
_The water in the pool moves, though there is no wind._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): rules keep us safe  
> _The Snork says: keep to the ridge._  
> _Why do we have a rule like that?_  
> - ✅ It keeps us safe → Yes! Rules are there to look after us. The ridge is the safe path.
> - To be bossy → The Snork can be bossy! But this rule is to keep everyone safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how rules keep people safe._


#### `a09-09-deep-done`

**Snufkin**: Moomintroll. Come back on the ridge. Slowly.  
_Snufkin’s voice is low and calm._  
_A calm voice helps a friend who is in a fix._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): a calm voice helps a friend feel steady  
> _When someone is in trouble, a calm voice helps them feel steady._  
> _Try it: say “slowly, slowly” in a soft voice._  
> _For grown-ups: Practised a calm, soft voice for helping a friend._


#### `a09-09-octopus`

_A long arm comes out of the pool. Then another._  
_An octopus lifts its head. It looks at him with one big, sad eye._  
_It has eight arms. One curls round Moomintroll’s stilt._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count eight arms  
> _An octopus has eight arms._  
> _(Count them on your fingers: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:octopus-arms:8`
> _For grown-ups: Counted to eight on the arms of an octopus._

**Moomintroll**: Help! I cannot pull free!  
_Sniff squeaks and hides behind the Hemulen._  
_The Snork Maiden grabs a lantern and runs._  
**The Snork Maiden**: Let him go!  
_She swings the lantern. Gold light flares on the rock._  

**Choices**

- **Hold your own light up behind her.**
    - You hold the pink shell up. It throws the light back.
    - The octopus blinks, and its arms open.
- **Grab Moomintroll’s paw and pull.**
    - You catch his paw. The Hemulen catches you.
    - The arms open, and everyone tumbles back in a heap.

#### `a09-09-octopus-done`

_The octopus slides back into its pool. Not a splash._  
_It was only curious, and a bit frightened by the lights._  
_Moomintroll is fine. He just stares at the Snork Maiden._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): animals can be scared too  
> _The octopus was curious and a little scared. Was it being mean?_  
> - ✅ No, it was scared and curious → Yes! Animals have feelings too. It wanted to be safe, just like us.
> - Yes, it was wicked → It never wanted to hurt anyone. It was curious and scared. We can be kind to animals.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how animals can feel scared and curious too._


#### `a09-09-complete`

**Moomintroll**: You saved me.  
**The Snork Maiden**: You saved me first. Now we are even.  
**Moomintroll**: I did not know you could do that.  
**The Snork Maiden**: Neither did I. I was too busy doing it.  
_Sniff and your Nubbin come out, surprised to be fine._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character feels  
> _Moomintroll says, “You saved me.” How does he feel about the Snork Maiden?_  
> - ✅ Thankful and amazed → Yes! He feels thankful, and amazed. Good word for feelings: thankful.
> - Grumpy → He is not grumpy. He is thankful. He is amazed she was so brave.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out how a character feels from what he says._


## A9-10. The Race Home

- `a09-10-s1`: Get off the seabed and on to the road home. · _Climb the shingle bank on the far side. Then keep walking._
- `a09-10-s2`: Hold on together when the wind comes. · _Get everyone behind the stone wall. Hold the nearest paw._
- `a09-10-s3`: Run the last bit to the valley. · _Down through the birch wood. You know the way._

#### `a09-10-road`

_You climb off the seabed in the morning._  
_The sky is red, even in the daytime._  
_The air is hot and still. The leaves hang down._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, notice): wind makes leaves move; still air does not  
> _When the air is still, leaves hang down._  
> _When the wind blows, they dance. Wind is air that moves._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wind is moving air, and that still air leaves leaves hanging._

**The Snork Maiden**: What day is it?  
**The Snork**: The seventh. I wish it was not.  
**Moomintroll**: We can do it! It comes in the evening.  
_Sniff walks a little faster._  

#### `a09-10-road-done`

_At a crossroads, a second Hemulen sits on a milestone._  
_He wears a big flowered dress and fans himself._  
**The Other Hemulen**: Cousin! What are you doing out on a day like this?  
**The Hemulen**: Walking very fast, cousin.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): beside means next to  
> _The second Hemulen sits on a milestone beside the road. What does beside mean?_  
> - ✅ Next to → Yes! Beside means next to. The stone is next to the road.
> - Far away → Beside means close. He is right next to the road.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the position word “beside”._


#### `a09-10-tornado`

_A great wind comes. Dust spins up in a column._  
**Snufkin**: Down behind the wall, everybody!  
_It picks up the other Hemulen, in his dress._  
_The dress fills up like a sail! He holds on to Moomintroll._  
_Then everyone holds on to everyone._  
**Snufkin**: Spread your skirts out wide! Like wings!  
_The Hemulen spreads his dress. You are gliding, all in a chain._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): moving the body like wings  
> _Let’s glide! Stretch your arms out wide like wings, and sway._  
> _(Hold on to the nearest hand, too.)_  
> Check: `edu:move:arms:wings`
> _For grown-ups: Moved arms wide like wings, practising balance and big movements._


**Choices**

- **Hold on tight to Sniff.**
    - Sniff has his eyes shut tight.
    - **Sniff**: Tell me when it is over.
- **Open your eyes and look down.**
    - Below, the whole country is spread out like a map.
    - At the river’s end, a green valley, and a tall blue house.

#### `a09-10-tornado-done`

_The wind sets you all down, gently._  
_One after another, like washing off a line._  
**The Other Hemulen**: My best dress. It has never been so useful.  
_(Say it together, like a drum: Hold on tight! Hold on tight!)_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, notice): a repeated line, a refrain  
> _A line we say again and again is called a refrain._  
> _Say it with me: Hold on tight! Hold on tight!_  
> _We are flying through the sky!_  
> _For grown-ups: Joined in a repeated line (a refrain), listening to its rhythm._


#### `a09-10-run`

_Everyone sits up in the meadow and counts._  
**The Snork**: Seven friends, a Nubbin and a cousin. Nobody missing!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count seven friends  
> _Count the friends together, on your fingers._  
> _Moomintroll, Sniff, Snufkin, the Snork Maiden, the Snork, the Hemulen, you._  
> Check: `edu:count:friends:7`
> _For grown-ups: Counted seven friends in the group._

_The comet fills a third of the sky now._  
**The Snork Maiden**: How far is it to the valley?  
**Moomintroll**: Over the hill and through the birch wood.  
_Snufkin pats his head. His hat has gone._  
_It is caught on a thistle, three steps away._  

**Choices**

- **Run and catch it.**
    - You grab it just as it lifts. It smells of woodsmoke.
    - **Snufkin**: Hold it for me. My hands are full of Sniff.
- **Let your Nubbin fetch it.**
    - Your Nubbin runs. The hat settles right over it.
    - The hat walks back. Snufkin laughs out loud.

#### `a09-10-run-done`

_Then you run, all of you, down through the birch wood._  
**Moomintroll**: There! There is the house! There is the smoke!  
_Moomintroll feels happy, and excited, and nearly home._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): naming feelings: excited, happy  
> _Moomintroll sees his house. How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Happy and excited → Yes! He feels excited. Feelings can have lots of names.
> - Sleepy and bored → Not this time! He is jumping up and down. Excited!
> _For grown-ups: Named a feeling (excited) from a character’s actions._


#### `a09-10-complete`

_The garden is empty and the house is shut._  
_A note is pinned to the door, in Mamma’s round writing._  
**Moomintroll**: It says: gone to the cave. Come quickly.  
**Sniff**: The cave! My cave!  
_The other Hemulen still holds his dress out, in case._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, notice): writing tells us things  
> _Mamma left a note, so everyone would know where she went._  
> _Writing can tell us things when nobody is there._  
> _(Point to some writing near you.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a note tells us something when the writer is not there._


## A9-11. The Cave

- `a09-11-s1`: Take everyone down to the cave on the shore. · _Use Sniff’s secret path. It is the quickest._
- `a09-11-s2`: Choose the one thing you bring into the cave. · _Moominmamma is at the cave mouth. Show her what you are carrying._
- `a09-11-s3`: Sit with Sniff in the dark. · _He is at the very back of the cave. Sit down beside him._

#### `a09-11-arrive`

_Sniff leads the way down his secret path, fast._  
_The cave mouth glows. Inside, there is a room!_  
_Blankets, lamps, a rocking chair, and the kitchen clock._  
**Moominmamma**: There you all are. More of you than went!  
_Moomintroll runs into her apron and stays._  
**Moominmamma**: There is cake. There is always cake, at the end of the world.  
**The Muskrat**: I brought my hammock. Nobody else thought of it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what makes a place feel safe  
> _Mamma made a cave feel safe. What can make a place feel safe?_  
> - ✅ Blankets, light, and people who care → Yes! Safe is a feeling. Cosy things and kind people make it.
> - Being all alone → Some people like quiet. But many feel safest with others who care.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what makes a place feel safe._


#### `a09-11-arrive-done`

_The kitchen clock says half past seven._  
_It ticks loudly. Everybody is listening._  
_The long hand points straight down, at six._  

> **Lesson** (maths, 1.MD.B.3, notice): half past: the long hand points to six  
> _Half past means half an hour after the hour._  
> _The long hand points straight down, to the six. Tick, tock!_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that half past means the long hand points to six._


#### `a09-11-door`

_Moominmamma stands at the cave mouth with a blanket._  
**Moominmamma**: A small cave. Many friends. One thing each, the thing you love.  
**Moominmamma**: The rest waits outside. It will be there in the morning.  
_You put down your things on the rock._  
_Three are left: the shell, the garnet, and your Nubbin._  
_Your arms are only so big._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Eco.1.K-2, ask): we choose when we cannot have everything  
> _Your arms only hold so much._  
> _What do we do when we cannot take everything?_  
> - ✅ Choose what we love most → Yes! Choosing means picking what matters most to you.
> - Take it all and drop it → Then things might break. Choosing carefully is wiser.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about choosing what matters most when we cannot have everything._


**Choices**

- **The shell with no sea in it.**
    - You bring the shell. Your Nubbin comes too, as Sniff’s one thing.
    - **Moominmamma**: It is waiting for something. Bring it in.
- **The garnet Sniff gave you to hold.**
    - You bring the garnet. Sniff sees, and pretends not to.
    - **Moominmamma**: Somebody has been generous.
- **Nothing but your Nubbin, held in both arms.**
    - You hold your Nubbin in both arms. The rest stays out.
    - **Moominmamma**: Yes. That is the right size for arms.

#### `a09-11-dark`

_The lamps go out one by one, to save oil._  
_The kitchen clock says twenty to nine._  
_Outside, the sky is red. It lies on the sand like a carpet._  
_A sound begins, far away, like the sky taking a breath._  
_Sniff is at the very back of the cave. You sit beside him._  
_He does not ask you anything this time._  
_In the dark his paw finds your hand and holds on._  
_Neither of you says a word. You wait, together._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, do): a held hand can help when we are worried  
> _Holding a friend’s hand can help a worry feel smaller._  
> _(Hold hands with the grown-up reading, and take three slow breaths.)_  
> Check: `edu:hold:hand:friend`
> _For grown-ups: Held a hand and breathed slowly, noticing how it helps with worries._


#### `a09-11-dark-done`

_The kitchen clock says eight forty-two._  
_The clock has gone on ticking, tick, tick, tick._  
_Time goes on, even when we wait._  

> **Lesson** (maths, 1.MD.B.3, notice): the clock hands move forward as time passes  
> _Half past seven, then twenty to nine, then eight forty-two._  
> _The clock’s hands creep round and round as time goes by._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that clock hands move on as time passes, reading three times in the story._


#### `a09-11-complete`

_Then there is light and noise._  
_Boom, rumble! The ground shakes, softly._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): sound words  
> _Boom! Rumble! Hush!_  
> _Some words sound like what they mean._  
> _Say them together, loud, then soft._  
> _For grown-ups: Joined in with sound words (boom, rumble, hush)._

**Moominmamma**: Hush now. Hush. Everyone is here.  
_Everyone is here._  

## A9-12. The Night It Missed

- `a09-12-s1`: Wait out the night in the cave. · _Stay where you are. It is nearly over._
- `a09-12-s2`: Go out in the morning and see the sea. · _Walk out of the cave mouth and down to the water._
- `a09-12-s3`: Say goodbye, and give Snufkin back his hat. · _Snufkin is at the gate with his pack. Bring the hat._

#### `a09-12-night`

_The roar goes over. It goes on a long time._  
_Then it is less. Then it is going away._  
**The Muskrat**: It seems to have missed.  
_The Snork Maiden laughs in the dark. Then everybody laughs._  
**Sniff**: Has it gone? Tell me exactly.  
**Moominpappa**: It brushed us with its tail, and went on its way.  
_The lamps come on. Moominmamma cuts the cake._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): real comets almost always pass by  
> _Real comets travel round the Sun on very long paths._  
> _They are far, far from us. Nearly always, they just pass by._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that real comets almost always just pass by, far away._


#### `a09-12-night-done`

_One by one, everybody falls asleep where they sit._  
_They are in a heap, like puppies._  
_It was a big night. Their bodies need rest._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sleep helps our bodies rest  
> _After a big, long day, what do bodies need?_  
> - ✅ Sleep and rest → Yes! Sleep lets our bodies and minds rest and grow strong.
> - More running → Running is fun, but after a big day we need rest. Sleep helps!
> _For grown-ups: Talked about sleep helping bodies rest after a long day._


#### `a09-12-dawn`

_In the morning, you wake with sand in your ear._  
_The light is not red. It is ordinary, yellow, wonderful._  
_The grey has gone off everything. The grass is green._  
_The sea is coming back, in long, slow, shining sheets._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): the tide: the sea goes out and comes back  
> _Real seas move in and out each day. We call that the tide._  
> _The sea goes out, and it always comes back._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the sea moves in and out each day, called the tide._

**Moomintroll**: It came back. Everything came back.  
**Snufkin**: Things mostly do.  

#### `a09-12-dawn-done`

_Your Nubbin runs down to the water._  
_It sits in the first wave. The sea comes home round it._  
**Sniff**: It is all right, then. I can tell, because it is doing that.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): feeling relieved  
> _Sniff feels all the worry go away. What do we call that feeling?_  
> - ✅ Relieved → Yes! Relieved. It is the breath-out feeling, after a worry.
> - Angry → Not angry. Sniff feels the worry lift. That is relieved.
> _For grown-ups: Named relief as the feeling after a worry has gone._


#### `a09-12-gate`

_Snufkin is at the gate with his tent on his back._  
_You hold out his hat._  
**Snufkin**: Keep it. I will find another.  
_He puts it on your head. It comes down over your eyes!_  
**Moominmamma**: Something to remember the house by.  
_She gives you a little blue stove._  
**Moominmamma**: Wherever you light it, people come home to it.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): one and one make two  
> _Snufkin gives you a hat. Mamma gives you a stove. How many gifts?_  
> - ✅ Two → Yes! One and one make two. Two gifts, and two thank-yous!
> - One → Count them: a hat is one, a stove is two. Two gifts!
> _For grown-ups: Added one and one to count two gifts._


#### `a09-12-gate-done`

_Snufkin is at the bend in the road._  
_He plays a few notes without looking back._  
_You play a few back._  
_He waves his hand over his head._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): call and response  
> _Snufkin plays, and you play back. Let’s do it._  
> _The grown-up hums three notes, and you hum them back._  
> Check: `edu:sing:call-and-response`
> _For grown-ups: Echoed a short tune back, practising call and response._


#### `a09-12-complete`

_The page begins to curl at the edges._  
**Moomintroll**: Will you come back? There is always a bed for you.  
**Sniff**: Bring the Nubbin. My pocket will be empty.  
_The blue house and the sea go flat and still._  
_You are back in the Grove, with a little blue stove._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, notice): a story has a beginning, a middle and an end  
> _This story is at its end. It began with a grey sea._  
> _In the middle, the friends travelled. At the end, everyone was home._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that stories have a beginning, a middle and an end._


## A10-1. The Chosen One

- `a10-01-s1`: Step onto the island. Listen to the story. · _Follow the children’s laughter._
- `a10-01-s2`: Hear the rest of the story. · _Sit with the children._
- `a10-01-s3`: Look after the baby turtle. · _Go down to the water._

#### `a10-01-page`

_Nova’s atlas opens. The page is blue, with a green island._  
_The paint turns to sand. Squish, squish! You are on a beach._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, 2-ESS2-2, notice): a map shows land and water; an island has water all round  
> _Nova’s page is a map. A map shows where land and water are._  
> _Green is land and blue is water. An island has water all round._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that maps show land and water, and what an island is._

_A big house has a roof and no walls. Children sit inside._  
_An old woman tells a story with her hands._  
**Gramma Tala**: Sit, sit! A guest! Your little one can sit on the end.  
_A small girl with lots of hair pats your Nubbin like a drum._  

#### `a10-01-page-done`

**Gramma Tala**: Now, where was I? The heart of the island!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): name where a story happens  
> _Where is this story? Point to your answer._  
> - ✅ On an island, by the sea → Yes! An island, with sand and palm trees.
> - In a snowy town → Not snow here! Look: sand, sea and palm trees. An island!
> - On the moon → Not the moon! We are on an island by the sea.
> _For grown-ups: Named the setting of the story: an island by the sea._


#### `a10-01-story`

**Gramma Tala**: Long ago there was only sea. Then an island came up out of it.  
**Gramma Tala**: The island had a heart. It made green things grow.  
**Gramma Tala**: A trickster took the heart. The island began to crumble.  
_Some children squeal and hide behind each other. The small girl leans in._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): naming a scared feeling and what helps  
> _Some children feel scared. What could help them?_  
> - ✅ A cuddle, and a grown-up nearby → Yes. A cuddle helps. Scared feelings get smaller.
> - Hide all alone → Hiding alone feels lonely. A cuddle works better.
> - Pretend not to be scared → It is fine to be scared. Say so, and ask for a hug.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about scared feelings and that a cuddle or a nearby grown-up helps._

**Chief Tui**: Mother, that is enough. The little ones will be scared.  
_Gramma Tala says her son is a good chief. He is also wrong._  

#### `a10-01-story-done`

_Gramma Tala picks up a stick and walks to the shore, humming._  
_You follow her._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): oral history: people tell stories out loud to remember the past  
> _Gramma Tala tells her story out loud. She learned it from her gramma._  
> _Long ago, people kept the past alive by telling stories._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that people kept the past alive by telling stories aloud._


#### `a10-01-turtle`

_The small girl has run to the beach. She frowns at something flat._  
_It is a baby turtle. It is trying to reach the sea._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): where sea turtles live and what they need  
> _The baby turtle wants to get home. Where does a sea turtle live?_  
> - ✅ In the sea → Yes! A sea turtle lives in the sea. It needs the water.
> - Up a tree → Not up a tree! A sea turtle swims, and its home is the sea.
> - In a house → Not in a house! Its home is the big blue sea.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sea turtle lives in the sea._

_Birds circle above. The girl holds a big leaf over it, like a roof._  

**Choices**

- **Send your Nubbin to walk beside the turtle.**
    - Your Nubbin waddles beside it, arms up. A very slow parade!
- **Wave the birds away.**
    - You flap your arms, and your Nubbin flaps its wings. The birds fly off.

#### `a10-01-turtle-done`

_The turtle reaches the foam. Splash! It is gone, and the girl claps._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): helping someone smaller  
> _The little girl helped the turtle. Helping feels good._  
> _Who could you help today?_  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed how good it feels to help someone smaller._


#### `a10-01-complete`

_The sea pulls back. It stands up in a wall of water!_  
_Fish hang in it like flecks in glass. The water leans down, gently._  
_It gives her a shell, then another shell. Then a green stone!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _(Count the gifts together on your fingers.)_  
> _A shell, a shell, a green stone: one, two, three. Three gifts!_  
> Check: `edu:count:gifts:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three gifts from the sea, one finger each._

**Chief Tui**: Moana! Where are you?  
_The water falls back. Gramma Tala picks up the green stone._  
_She keeps it safe in the shell at her neck._  
**Gramma Tala**: The sea picks who it picks. It never says why.  

## A10-2. The Reef

- `a10-02-s1`: Walk with Moana to the coconut trees. · _Go up to the grove._
- `a10-02-s2`: Go to the lagoon. The nets are empty. · _Find the fishermen._
- `a10-02-s3`: Go out to the reef with Moana. · _Wade out and be ready to pull._

#### `a10-02-coconuts`

_Moana is sixteen now. She is learning to be chief._  
**Moana**: You are Gramma’s guest! I knew you would come back.  
_A farmer holds out a coconut, cracked in half._  
_Inside it is black and soft. It should be white!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): plants need water, light and good soil to stay well  
> _Coconut trees need sun, water and good ground to grow._  
> _When a tree gets poorly, its fruit goes soft and dark._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what plants need to stay healthy._

**Coconut farmer**: Whole trees of them. Young trees too.  
**Moana**: Then we will plant a new grove. There is good ground over there.  

**Choices**

- **Dig the first hole for the new grove.**
    - **Coconut farmer**: A guest who digs!
    - Your Nubbin sits in the hole to check it is the right size.
- **Ask how long the trees have been sick.**
    - **Coconut farmer**: Since the rains. It walked this way, one tree at a time.
    - Moana looks past the island, at the sea.

#### `a10-02-coconuts-done`

**Moana**: That is one trouble. Next will be the fishing. It is always the fishing.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): noticing how someone else feels  
> _The farmer’s trees are poorly. How might he feel?_  
> - ✅ Worried → Yes. He is worried. He cares about his trees.
> - Silly → Not silly. His trees are poorly, so he feels worried.
> - Sleepy → Not sleepy! He is worried about his trees.
> _For grown-ups: Named a feeling (worried) for someone whose trees were poorly._


#### `a10-02-lagoon`

_The fishing canoes sit on the sand. Their nets are empty._  
**Old fisherman**: Every day, fewer fish. Today, none.  
**Moana**: Then we go out past the reef! The fish are out there.  
_The fishermen go quiet. The chief has walked up._  
**Chief Tui**: We do not cross the reef. It is our rule. It keeps us safe.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): rules help keep people safe  
> _The chief has a rule. Why might a rule like this help?_  
> - ✅ It keeps people safe → Yes. Rules can keep people safe. Moana will ask why.
> - To be cross → Not to be cross. A good rule helps keep people safe.
> - To spoil the fun → Not to spoil fun. A good rule is there to keep people safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why rules exist: to keep people safe._

_Your Nubbin senses a mood. It sits on Moana’s foot._  

#### `a10-02-lagoon-done`

_The chief walks away. Moana watches the reef._  
_Five canoes lie on the sand, with nothing in them._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _(Count the canoes with your finger.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five. Five empty canoes!_  
> Check: `edu:count:canoes:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five canoes, saying one number for each._

**Moana**: He never says why.  

#### `a10-02-breakers`

_Later, Moana pushes a small canoe out. Pua the pig sits in front._  
**Moana**: I am only going to look!  
_At the reef, the waves come in big and close. Whoosh! Whoosh!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, notice): coral reefs: tiny animals build a reef where fish live  
> _A reef is like a wall in the sea. Tiny coral animals build it._  
> _Lots of fish live in a reef. It is their home._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that tiny coral animals build reefs, and that fish make their homes there._

_The third wave tips the canoe over. Splash!_  
**You**: Moana!  
_You wade in. Your Nubbin paddles past you, fast._  
_Together you pull Moana and Pua to safety._  

#### `a10-02-breakers-done`

_Moana sits on the sand, by the canoe in two pieces. Pua sulks._  
**Moana**: Fine. Point taken.  
_Your Nubbin comes out of the sea with a spiral shell._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): hear the first sound of a word  
> _Say them slowly: sea, sand, sun. What sound do they all start with?_  
> - ✅ “s”, like a snake → Yes! S-s-sea, s-s-sand, s-s-sun. They all start with “s”.
> - “b”, like a ball → Listen again: sss-sea, sss-sand. They start with “s”.
> - “m”, like Moana → M starts Moana. Sea, sand and sun start with “s”.
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first sound, “s”, in sea, sand and sun._


#### `a10-02-complete`

**Moana**: Dad is right. I nearly drowned the pig.  
_She looks at the cut on her foot, not at the reef._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming feelings and what helps  
> _Moana feels let down. What could help her feel better?_  
> - ✅ Talk to Gramma or a friend → Yes. Talking to someone you trust helps.
> - Keep it all inside → Keeping it inside is heavy. Telling someone helps.
> - Be cross at the pig → Pua did nothing wrong! Talking to a friend helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps with a let-down feeling: telling someone you trust._

_Your Nubbin drops the spiral shell in your hand. You keep it safe._  
**Moana**: That is Gramma, round the point. She dances with the sea.  

## A10-3. Gramma Tala

- `a10-03-s1`: Find Gramma Tala dancing by the water. · _Walk round the point._
- `a10-03-s2`: Let Gramma teach your Nubbin one step. · _Stand in the shallows. Choose a step._
- `a10-03-s3`: Sit on the sand with Gramma and Moana. · _Sit beside Gramma Tala._

#### `a10-03-point`

_Round the point, the waves come in long and slow._  
_Gramma Tala dances at the edge of the water._  
_She moves like the sea: forward, then back. In, then out._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): waves come in and go out all day  
> _Watch the waves. They come in, and they go out._  
> _In, out. In, out. The sea keeps moving all day._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that waves move in and out all the time._

**Gramma Tala**: Do not stand there like a post. The sea does not bite!  
**Moana**: Gramma, you should not be out here alone.  
**Gramma Tala**: I have the sea, a guest and a round little thing with wings.  

#### `a10-03-point-done`

_Your Nubbin tries to copy her. It falls over. Plop!_  
**Gramma Tala**: Oh, that one has the makings!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): trying again after a wobble is brave  
> _Your Nubbin fell over and did not mind. It got up to try again._  
> _Trying again is brave. Every wobble helps you learn._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that falling over and trying again is a brave way to learn._


#### `a10-03-step`

**Gramma Tala**: Come here, small one. Feet in the water. Feel it pull?  
_Your Nubbin rocks a little each time the water goes out._  
**Gramma Tala**: I have two steps for a beginner. You get one today.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): copy a slow, gentle movement  
> _(Stand up. Sway side to side, slowly, like the sea.)_  
> _Swish, swish. Slow and soft. That is how Gramma moves._  
> Check: `edu:move:sway`
> _For grown-ups: Swayed slowly and gently, copying Gramma Tala’s movement._

**Gramma Tala**: Which shall it be?  

**Choices**

- **The stingray glide.**
    - **Gramma Tala**: Arms out wide and soft. Lean. Let the sea carry you.
    - Your Nubbin slides along the foam on one foot. Whee!
- **The wave step.**
    - **Gramma Tala**: Up on your toes when it comes in. Down when it goes.
    - Your Nubbin rises, sinks and rolls its arms. Right on the sea!

#### `a10-03-step-done`

**Gramma Tala**: There. That is yours now. A step is like a name. It stays.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the beats in a word  
> _(Clap the beats in each word.)_  
> _Wave and step: one clap each. Man-ta: two claps!_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:manta`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped syllables in wave, step and manta._


#### `a10-03-sand`

_Gramma sits on the sand. Moana sits beside her, and so do you._  
**Moana**: I tried to go past the reef. I nearly drowned Pua.  
**Gramma Tala**: I know. Wrong boat, wrong tide. Otherwise, very good.  
**Gramma Tala**: Safe is good. But safe is not the only thing.  
**Gramma Tala**: You have a big question in you. Go on. Ask it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): asking when you want to know something  
> _Moana has a big question. What can you do when you want to know?_  
> - ✅ Ask a grown-up you trust → Yes! Asking is brave. Good questions help us learn.
> - Never ask → Questions are good! Ask them. People like to help.
> - Guess and hope → Guessing is fine sometimes. But asking gets a real answer.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking a trusted grown-up when you want to know something._


#### `a10-03-sand-done`

**Moana**: Who are we? Where did we come from? Why do we never leave?  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): families have stories about long ago  
> _Moana wants to know where her people came from._  
> _Every family has stories about long ago. Ask a grown-up to tell you one._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that families have stories about the past, and was invited to ask for one._

**Gramma Tala**: Good. Get your guest. Bring a torch.  

#### `a10-03-complete`

_Gramma gets up. It takes three tries, and a hand from you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): helping someone kindly, without a fuss  
> _You gave Gramma a hand up, and nobody made a fuss._  
> _Quiet help is kind. It lets people feel strong, not silly._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that helping quietly, without a fuss, is a kind way to help._

_Your Nubbin walks up the beach, doing its step, a bit crooked._  
**Gramma Tala**: It will come. Everything good comes slowly.  

## A10-4. The Cave of Canoes

- `a10-04-s1`: Follow Gramma behind the waterfall. · _Carry the torch up the stream._
- `a10-04-s2`: Look at what is hidden in the cave. · _Go down the passage and look._
- `a10-04-s3`: Watch what the drum remembers. · _Stand back while Moana beats the drum._

#### `a10-04-falls`

_Gramma leads you up a stream. A waterfall tumbles down a cliff._  
**Gramma Tala**: The secret is behind the waterfall. Moana first, then our guest.  
_Moana steps through. You hear her gasp._  
_You follow. The water hits your head. Splash! Brr!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): words for where things are  
> _Where is the secret passage? Point to your answer._  
> - ✅ Behind the waterfall → Yes! Behind the waterfall. Moana went through the water.
> - On top of the waterfall → Not on top. It is behind the waterfall.
> - Beside a tree → Not beside a tree. The passage is behind the waterfall.
> _For grown-ups: Used a position word (behind) to say where the passage was._

_Behind the falls is a passage in the rock._  

#### `a10-04-falls-done`

_The torch makes the wet rock shine._  
_Your Nubbin’s emote ball glows too. It is company._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): a friend nearby helps you feel brave  
> _The cave is dark, and a bit spooky. But you are not alone._  
> _A friend nearby helps you feel brave. Who helps you feel brave?_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that having a friend close by helps us feel brave in the dark._


#### `a10-04-canoes`

_The passage opens into a huge cave. Blue light comes in from the sea._  
_Moana lifts the torch. The shapes in the dark are boats!_  
_They are great canoes, with two hulls each and sails folded up._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _(Count the canoes in the front row.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five. Five great canoes!_  
> Check: `edu:count:canoes:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five canoes, saying one number for each._

**Moana**: Whose are these? Nobody builds these any more!  
_Your Nubbin sits on a hull, under a very tall mast._  
_At the front is a great drum._  

**Choices**

- **Brush the dust off the nearest prow.**
    - Under the dust the wood is carved with waves, stars and tiny people.
- **Hold the torch high so Moana can see.**
    - Moana walks along, touching each hull, like counting heads.

#### `a10-04-canoes-done`

**Gramma Tala**: Bang the drum, Moana. It has been waiting for you.  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, notice): a drum makes sound when its skin shakes  
> _When Moana bangs the drum, the skin shakes. Shake, shake!_  
> _The shaking makes the sound you hear._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a shaking drum skin makes sound._


#### `a10-04-drum`

_Moana beats the drum. Boom! The sound goes all round the cave._  
_Then you are not in a cave. You are on the open sea!_  
_Great canoes sail all round, full of singing people._  
_A woman at a steering oar grins right at you._  
_They find an island, land and plant. Then they sail on._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): ancestors are family from long ago  
> _These people are Moana’s ancestors. Ancestors are family from long, long ago._  
> _They sailed from island to island, all across a huge ocean._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what ancestors are, and that Pacific peoples sailed between islands._

_Your Nubbin is doing its step without knowing it._  

#### `a10-04-drum-done`

_The drum stops ringing. You are in the cave again._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): clap a steady beat  
> _(Clap a slow, steady beat, like a drum.)_  
> _Boom, boom, boom. Keep it steady!_  
> Check: `edu:clap:beat:steady`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped a slow, steady beat._

_There is dust on your feet and sea sounds at the far end._  

#### `a10-04-complete`

**Moana**: They did not stay! They sailed on to every island. We did that!  
**Gramma Tala**: We did. Then the dark came, and the chiefs said, stay inside the reef.  
**Gramma Tala**: And we hid the boats and forgot. All but a few of us.  
_Gramma takes out the green stone with the spiral on it._  
**Gramma Tala**: This is the heart of Te Fiti, the mother island.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): remember what happened earlier in a story  
> _Gramma kept the green stone safe. Who gave it to Moana, long ago?_  
> - ✅ The sea → Yes! The sea gave it to her when she was very small.
> - Her dad → Not her dad. The sea gave Moana the stone, on the beach.
> - A turtle → The turtle went home to the sea. The sea gave her the stone.
> _For grown-ups: Remembered an earlier event in the story: the sea gave Moana the stone._

**Gramma Tala**: Someone must find Maui. He must put it back.  
**Moana**: I have to tell Dad. Right now!  

## A10-5. Setting Sail

- `a10-05-s1`: Stand by Moana while she tells the chief. · _Go to the meeting house._
- `a10-05-s2`: Sit with Gramma Tala in her house. · _Sit by her mat._
- `a10-05-s3`: Carry food and water to the hidden canoe. · _Take the bundles from Sina._

#### `a10-05-council`

_Moana runs into the meeting house with cobweb in her hair._  
**Moana**: Our people sailed! There are boats in a cave! We can find Maui!  
**Chief Tui**: The cave. She showed you.  
**Chief Tui**: We are not going past the reef.  
**Chief Tui**: When I was young, I went past the reef with my best friend.  
**Chief Tui**: The sea was rough. My friend died there. I came home alone.  
_For a moment he is just a man who has been afraid._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): naming a feeling and why  
> _Tui’s friend died at sea, so he fears for Moana. How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Sad and scared → Yes. He is sad about his friend, and scared for Moana.
> - Silly → Not silly. He feels sad and scared, because he loves her.
> - Hungry → Not hungry! He feels sad and scared.
> _For grown-ups: Named feelings (sad, scared) behind a worried parent’s rule._


#### `a10-05-council-done`

_A boy runs in, out of breath. Gramma Tala has fallen by the shore._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): tell what happened first, next and last  
> _First Moana told her dad. Next the boy ran in._  
> _What was the news the boy brought?_  
> - ✅ Gramma Tala has fallen → Yes. Gramma Tala has fallen. Moana will go to her.
> - The fish came back → Not that. The news was about Gramma Tala.
> - It is lunchtime → Not lunch. The news was that Gramma Tala has fallen.
> _For grown-ups: Followed the order of events and said what the news was._


#### `a10-05-bedside`

_Gramma lies on her mat. A healer sits beside her._  
_She is very small now. Her hands are cool._  
**Gramma Tala**: Do not fuss. I am very old, and very poorly.  
**Gramma Tala**: You must go. Tonight. Find Maui. Make him give it back.  
**Moana**: I cannot leave you. Not now.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): sad feelings are allowed, and hugs help  
> _Moana feels sad. It is hard when someone you love is very old._  
> _Feeling sad is allowed. A hug, a sit-down and a friend all help._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sadness is allowed and that hugs and company help._

**Gramma Tala**: I will be the bit of you that keeps going.  
_She puts the shell with the heart in it into Moana’s hand._  
**Gramma Tala**: And look after our guest. Guests are a big job.  

#### `a10-05-bedside-done`

**Gramma Tala**: Go on, my brave girl. I love you very much.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, SL.K.1, do): saying a kind thing out loud to someone you love  
> _(Tell a grown-up one kind thing about them.)_  
> _Kind words feel warm. Gramma’s words stay with Moana._  
> Check: `edu:say:kind-words`
> _For grown-ups: Said one kind thing to a loved one, as Gramma did._


#### `a10-05-pack`

_In Moana’s house, her mother Sina is packing food._  
**Sina**: Dried fish. Good coconuts. And water. Four gourds of water.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4  
> _(Count the water gourds on your fingers.)_  
> _One, two, three, four. Four gourds of water!_  
> Check: `edu:count:gourds:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four water gourds, one finger each._

**Sina**: I am not going to stop you. I am going to feed you.  
_She hugs Moana for a long time. Then she hugs you too._  
_You carry the bundles to the cave’s sea mouth, in the dark._  
_There the smallest canoe waits. It still looks enormous._  

**Choices**

- **Hold the canoe steady while she loads.**
    - You hold the hull still. By the third bundle her hands are steady.
- **Tell her what Sina said about water.**
    - **Moana**: I always forget water!
    - She counts the gourds out loud. Then once more, for her mum.

#### `a10-05-pack-done`

_You turn round, and your Nubbin is gone! So is Heihei the rooster._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): guess what might happen next  
> _Where might Nubbin and Heihei be hiding?_  
> - ✅ Inside the canoe → Yes! A good guess. Look at the canoe’s dark hull.
> - Up a palm tree → Maybe! But look at the canoe first. It is the best hiding place.
> - In Gramma’s house → Hmm. Gramma’s house is quiet. Check the canoe!
> _For grown-ups: Made a guess about what happens next in the story._


#### `a10-05-complete`

_Moana pushes the canoe off into the dark. The sail goes up crooked._  
_From under the deck comes a small cluck, and a small squeak._  
**You**: Wait! My Nubbin is in your boat!  
_You wade out. The sea lifts you gently onto the deck._  
**Moana**: Did the ocean just give me a passenger?  
_On the shore, a light goes out in Gramma Tala’s house._  
_Gramma Tala has died. Her body stopped working, and it will not start again._  
_Moana sees the light go, and she knows. She is very sad._  
_Under the canoe, a soft blue light glows. A big manta ray glides past._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): feelings after someone dies, and what helps  
> _When someone dies, we can feel sad, cross or scared. All are fine._  
> _A hug helps, and so does telling someone. Remembering them helps, too._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sad, cross and scared are all fine feelings after a death, and what helps._

_Moana wipes her eyes. She follows the glow._  

## A10-6. Maui

- `a10-06-s1`: Ride out the storm in the canoe. · _Bail water. Hold on tight._
- `a10-06-s2`: Meet the demigod on his rock. · _Walk up the beach._
- `a10-06-s3`: Get out of the cave. · _Climb up inside the stone figure._

#### `a10-06-storm`

_Day one is blue and easy. Your Nubbin and Heihei sit on deck._  
_On the second night a storm comes. Whoosh! Crash!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, notice): a storm has strong wind and heavy rain  
> _A storm has strong wind and heavy rain. The sea gets big and rough._  
> _After the storm, the weather goes calm again._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what a storm is like and that weather calms again._

**Moana**: Bail! Hold on to something!  
_You bail with a shell. Your Nubbin bails with its hands, and soaks you._  
_A huge wave rolls the canoe. Everything goes dark and loud._  

#### `a10-06-storm-done`

_You wake on a beach with sand in your mouth._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, do): sound words show what we hear  
> _(Say the storm’s sounds: whoosh, splash, crash!)_  
> _Sound words let us hear a story. What sound does the sea make?_  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-words:whoosh`
> _For grown-ups: Practised sound words (whoosh, splash, crash)._

_Your Nubbin is asleep on top of Heihei, who has not noticed._  

#### `a10-06-maui`

_A shadow falls on the beach. A huge man stands there, grinning._  
_Pictures of great deeds are drawn on his skin._  
**Maui**: Visitors! A thousand years on a rock, and now an audience!  
**Maui**: I am Maui. I pulled islands out of the sea. I slowed the sun.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): Maui is a hero in the stories of many Pacific peoples  
> _Many island peoples across the Pacific tell stories about Maui._  
> _In the stories he fishes up islands, slows the sun and brings fire._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that Maui is a hero in the stories of many Pacific island peoples._

**Maui**: And what is this? A coconut with opinions?  
**Moana**: My island is dying. You are coming with me to put it right.  

**Choices**

- **Thank him for the long days.**
    - **Maui**: See? Somebody was brought up properly.
    - Moana gives you a long look. You are meant to be on her side.
- **Keep your Nubbin behind your legs.**
    - Your Nubbin peeks out, and Maui peeks back. Nobody blinks first.

#### `a10-06-maui-done`

**Maui**: Thanks for the boat. I have waited a long time for one.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare sizes: bigger and smaller  
> _Look at Maui and your Nubbin. Who is bigger?_  
> - ✅ Maui is bigger → Yes! Maui is huge. Your Nubbin is tiny next to him.
> - The Nubbin is bigger → Look again. Maui is as big as a hill, and the Nubbin is smaller.
> - They are the same → Not the same! Maui is much bigger than your Nubbin.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two sizes and said which is bigger._


#### `a10-06-statue`

_Maui has shut you in a cave with a boulder._  
**Moana**: He is taking my boat!  
_Inside the cave is a huge stone Maui. It is hollow._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): calming down when you feel cross  
> _Moana feels cross. What can help when you feel cross?_  
> - ✅ Take a slow, deep breath → Yes. Big, slow breaths help the cross feeling get smaller.
> - Stamp and shout for hours → Stamping lets off steam, but slow breaths help most.
> - Hide away → Hiding does not fix it. A slow breath is a better start.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about calming down when cross: slow, deep breaths._

_Moana climbs up inside it. You climb after her._  
_At the top is a hole. Far below, a canoe sails away._  
**Moana**: Right.  
_She jumps, and so do you. Your Nubbin shuts its eyes, but falls anyway._  

#### `a10-06-statue-done`

_The sea catches you like a hand. It sets you on the deck._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): tell what happened first, next and last  
> _First Moana climbed. Next she jumped._  
> _What came last?_  
> - ✅ The sea set them on the canoe → Yes! Last, the sea set them gently on the deck.
> - They ate dinner → Not yet! Last, the sea set them on the canoe.
> - They flew home → No flying home. The sea set them on the canoe.
> _For grown-ups: Put events in order: climbed, jumped, landed on the canoe._


#### `a10-06-complete`

**Maui**: No, no. You cannot be on my boat!  
_He drops Moana over the side. The sea puts her back._  
_He does it again. The sea puts her back again._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 2  
> _(Count how many times the sea put Moana back.)_  
> _One time, two times. The sea put Moana back two times!_  
> Check: `edu:count:times:2`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two times, using fingers._

_He tries your Nubbin. The sea puts it back on his head._  
**Maui**: Fine! The ocean is on your side.  

## A10-7. The Kakamora

- `a10-07-s1`: Watch the strange boat come out of the fog. · _Stand at the stern._
- `a10-07-s2`: Get Heihei back from the pirates. · _Follow Moana across._
- `a10-07-s3`: Get the canoe away from the raft. · _Hold the sail line tight._

#### `a10-07-fog`

_Maui is steering. Moana counts that as a start._  
_A fog bank lies ahead. Out of it comes a sound of drums._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): fog is a low cloud that makes it hard to see far  
> _Fog is a cloud that sits low over the sea._  
> _In fog, it is hard to see far. Sailors go slowly and listen._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that fog is a low cloud that makes it hard to see._

_A raft comes out, made of many boats. Little round people crew it._  
_They wear coconut armour, with faces painted on the front._  
**Maui**: Kakamora! Pirates! They take everything they see.  
_Your Nubbin looks at them. They look at your Nubbin._  

**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin wave at them.**
    - Your Nubbin waves. Forty coconuts wave back, all at once.
- **Scoop your Nubbin up and hold it close.**
    - Across the water, several painted faces look hurt.

#### `a10-07-fog-done`

**Moana**: Why are they looking at it like that?  
**Maui**: They think it is one of theirs. A little one without a coconut.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): understand why characters act as they do  
> _Why do the Kakamora stare at Nubbin?_  
> - ✅ They think it is one of them → Yes. Round, small, and a bit lost. Just like them!
> - They are hungry → Not hungry. They think your Nubbin is one of theirs.
> - They want to race → Not a race. They think your Nubbin belongs with them.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out a character’s reason: the Kakamora thought Nubbin was one of theirs._


#### `a10-07-chase`

_Little darts stick in the deck. Pirates swarm aboard._  
_One pirate grabs Heihei and runs off with him._  
**Moana**: Heihei swallowed the heart! He thought it was a pebble!  
_Moana jumps to their raft. Your Nubbin jumps too._  
_The pirates let it through. One paints a face on its tummy._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): name a shape  
> _A coconut is round like a ball. Which flat shape is round?_  
> - ✅ A circle → Yes! A circle is round, like the front of a coconut.
> - A triangle → A triangle has three corners. A circle is round.
> - A square → A square has four corners. A circle is round.
> _For grown-ups: Named a circle as the round shape._

_Your Nubbin picks up Heihei and walks back. Nobody stops it._  

#### `a10-07-chase-done`

_Moana swings back on a rope. Your Nubbin clings to her back._  
_Heihei clings to your Nubbin. He is calmly eating a dart._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): animal sounds  
> _Heihei is a rooster. What sound does a rooster make?_  
> - ✅ Cock-a-doodle-doo! → Yes! Cock-a-doodle-doo! Do it with me!
> - Moo → Moo is a cow! A rooster goes cock-a-doodle-doo.
> - Woof → Woof is a dog! A rooster goes cock-a-doodle-doo.
> _For grown-ups: Matched an animal (rooster) with its sound._


#### `a10-07-escape`

**Maui**: Hold that line! Tighter! No, the other line!  
_You hold a rope that hums. The canoe leans and leaps._  
_The raft comes after you, drums going._  
_Moana points to a gap between two boats of the raft._  
**Moana**: There! Go between them!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): words for where things are  
> _Where does the canoe go? Point to your answer._  
> - ✅ Between the two boats → Yes! Between the two boats. Whoosh!
> - Over the top → Not over. The canoe goes between them.
> - Under the water → Not under! It goes between the two boats.
> _For grown-ups: Used a position word (between) to say where the canoe went._

_The canoe shoots through the gap. The raft comes unlashed._  

#### `a10-07-escape-done`

_The pirates drift off in the fog, drumming crossly._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): teamwork: each person has a job  
> _Maui steered and Moana pointed. You held the rope._  
> _Everyone had a job. Teams work best when everyone helps._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a team works when everyone has a job._


#### `a10-07-complete`

_Heihei coughs up the green stone. Moana washes it twice._  
**Moana**: Now you must help me. I saved your boat.  
**Maui**: My boat.  
**Maui**: A fire demon guards the heart. I need my hook to get past.  
**Maui**: My hook is at the bottom of the world.  
**Moana**: Then teach me to sail.  
_Your Nubbin still has a fierce face on its tummy._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, do): draw a face to show a feeling  
> _(Draw a face on paper. Make it happy, or fierce, or silly.)_  
> _Faces can show how we feel. How does yours feel?_  
> Check: `edu:draw:face:happy`
> _For grown-ups: Drew a face to show a feeling._


## A10-8. Wayfinding

- `a10-08-s1`: Learn to read the stars with your hand. · _Sit at the stern after dark._
- `a10-08-s2`: Feel the swell through the hull. · _Lie on the deck, one hand on the wood._
- `a10-08-s3`: Watch for the bird going home. · _At dusk, watch from the bow._

#### `a10-08-stars`

_Night falls clear. The sky is so full of stars it looks crowded._  
**Maui**: You want to sail? Start with the stars. Hold your hand out flat.  
_Moana holds out her hand, and so do you. Your Nubbin tries too._  
**Maui**: Stars come up in the same places, every night. Learn where.  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): stars rise and set in the same places each night  
> _Stars come up on one side of the sky and set on the other._  
> _They do it every night. Sailors use them like a map in the sky._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that stars rise and set in the same places, so sailors can steer by them._

**Maui**: Then you know which way you are going.  
**Moana**: That is it? That is the secret?  
**Maui**: That is night one. It takes years.  

#### `a10-08-stars-done`

_Moana checks her hand against the same star, again and again._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _(Hold out your hand. Count your fingers.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five. A whole hand is five fingers!_  
> Check: `edu:count:fingers:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five fingers on one hand._


#### `a10-08-swell`

**Maui**: Clouds hide the stars. Now what?  
**Maui**: Lie down. Put your hand on the hull. Shut your eyes. Be quiet.  
_The canoe lifts and falls, slow as breathing._  
**Maui**: That is the swell. Big, slow waves from far away.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): swells are long, slow waves  
> _(Lay your hand flat. Lift it up and down, slowly, like a swell.)_  
> _Swells are long, slow waves from far away. They keep coming the same way._  
> Check: `edu:move:swell`
> _For grown-ups: Felt a slow rise and fall, like an ocean swell, with their own hand._

**Maui**: Keep it at the same angle, and you keep your course.  
**Moana**: There! I can feel two swells!  

**Choices**

- **Feel for the second swell yourself.**
    - You wait. Then you feel it: a second, smaller lift.
- **Let your Nubbin try.**
    - Your Nubbin lies with its whole face on the wood. It falls asleep.

#### `a10-08-swell-done`

**Maui**: Huh. Not bad. Not good. Not bad.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): learning takes time and patience  
> _Moana did not learn it all in one go. Nobody does._  
> _Learning takes time. Being patient with yourself helps._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that learning something new takes time and patience._


#### `a10-08-birds`

_At dusk, Maui sits at the bow beside your Nubbin._  
**Maui**: In the morning, sea birds fly out from land. At dusk, they fly home.  
_A white bird crosses the red sky. It is in a hurry._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): some sea birds fly home to land at dusk  
> _The bird flies home at dusk. Which way is land?_  
> - ✅ The way the bird is flying → Yes! Follow the bird home, and you find land.
> - The way the bird came from → Not quite. At dusk the bird is heading home to land.
> - Nobody can tell → We can! The bird is going home. So land is where it goes.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that at dusk some sea birds fly home to land, which shows sailors where land is._

_Your Nubbin points with its whole arm. Then its whole body._  
**Maui**: Good. That way is land!  
**Moana**: Stars. Swells. Birds.  

#### `a10-08-birds-done`

_Moana takes the steering oar for the first time. Maui lets her._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): real sailors steered by stars, swells and birds  
> _Real sailors in the Pacific did this long ago._  
> _They used stars, swells and birds, and no maps. Some still learn it today._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that real Pacific sailors steered by stars, swells and birds long ago, and some still do._


#### `a10-08-complete`

_That night, Moana weaves strips of leaf left over from the sail._  
_In the morning there is a tiny woven sail on your Nubbin’s back._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): continue a pattern  
> _Weaving goes: over, under, over, under._  
> _What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Over → Yes! Over, under, over, under, over. A pattern!
> - Under → Close! Say it slowly: over, under, over, under... then over.
> - Jump → Jump is not in the pattern. Over, under, over, under, then over!
> _For grown-ups: Continued an over-under weaving pattern._

**Moana**: Every voyager needs a sail. Even a small one.  
_Your Nubbin spins to see it. Heihei spins too._  

## A10-9. Lalotai

- `a10-09-s1`: Climb the tall rock at the edge of the world. · _Climb the pillar, ledge by ledge._
- `a10-09-s2`: Find your way through the Realm of Monsters. · _Follow the glowing plants._
- `a10-09-s3`: Get the hook back from the crab. · _Keep Tamatoa talking._

#### `a10-09-pillar`

_A stone pillar stands alone in the sea. Its top is in the clouds._  
**Maui**: The way down is at the top. Yes. The way down is up.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): opposites  
> _Maui says, “The way down is up.” What is the opposite of up?_  
> - ✅ Down → Yes! Up and down are opposites. Silly way, but true here.
> - Over → Close, but not quite. The opposite of up is down.
> - Round → Not round. The opposite of up is down.
> _For grown-ups: Named the opposite of up (down)._

_Maui climbs it by being huge. Moana climbs with fingers and toes._  
_You climb behind her. Your Nubbin holds your heel._  
_At the top, Maui speaks old words, low and quiet._  
_The rock opens. Below is a long way down, and a glow._  

#### `a10-09-pillar-done`

**Maui**: Wait here. This is no place for a… Moana? Moana!  
_She has jumped, and so has your Nubbin. You sigh, and jump too._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): stopping to think before you act  
> _Moana jumped fast. What can you do before you jump into something new?_  
> - ✅ Look and think first → Yes. Look, think, then go. It keeps us safe.
> - Close your eyes and go → Looking first is safer. Look, think, then go.
> - Never try new things → New things are great! Just look and think first.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about looking and thinking before trying something new._


#### `a10-09-depths`

_You land on a big flower. It closes up a little, curious._  
_Lalotai is upside down. The sea is the sky here._  
_Below you, everything glows: purple, green and gold._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): some deep-sea animals make their own light  
> _Deep in the real sea it is very dark. The sun’s light cannot reach._  
> _Some animals there make their own light. They glow like tiny lamps._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that some deep-sea animals make their own light._

_Something with too many eyes blinks at you, and goes back to its crack._  
**Moana**: Maui’s hook is with something that loves shiny things.  
_Your Nubbin’s glowing ball floats above its head. Many eyes turn._  

#### `a10-09-depths-done`

_A trail of shiny things leads into a cave._  
_A shell, a bone, an earring, a golden canoe!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4  
> _(Count the shiny things on your fingers.)_  
> _A shell, a bone, an earring, a golden canoe. Four things!_  
> Check: `edu:count:treasure:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four shiny things, one finger each._


#### `a10-09-lair`

_Below is a crab as big as a house, covered in treasure._  
_A bone fish hook sits on the very top._  
**Tamatoa**: Visitors! Lunch does not usually knock.  
**Tamatoa**: Oh! What is that on the little round one? It glows!  
_Your Nubbin, worried, turns its ball into a question mark._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, notice): punctuation marks show feeling: ! and ?  
> _Nubbin’s ball can be a question mark. That means, “I am not sure.”_  
> _It can be an exclamation mark! That means, “Wow!”_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what question marks and exclamation marks mean._

**Tamatoa**: It does tricks!  

**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin show off its ball.**
    - Heart, spiral, plain ball, exclamation mark. Tamatoa claps his claws.
- **Ask Tamatoa about his shell.**
    - **Tamatoa**: Since you ask. Every piece is a story. Let me start at the bottom.

#### `a10-09-lair-done`

_Behind him, Moana climbs his shell and lifts off the hook._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): crabs have a hard shell and claws  
> _Real crabs have a hard shell on the outside, and two claws._  
> _Most crabs walk sideways. The shell keeps their soft body safe._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that crabs have a hard shell and two claws, and walk sideways._


#### `a10-09-complete`

**Tamatoa**: Wait! That is mine. Everything here is mine!  
_Moana throws the hook to Maui. He catches it._  
_Tamatoa topples onto his back, with his legs waving._  
**Tamatoa**: Somebody turn me over! I am never undignified!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming a feeling  
> _Tamatoa is stuck on his back. How might he feel?_  
> - ✅ Embarrassed and cross → Yes. He feels embarrassed. Proud crabs hate looking silly!
> - Calm and sleepy → Not calm. He is waving his legs and shouting.
> - Very hungry → Maybe a bit! But mostly he is embarrassed and cross.
> _For grown-ups: Named feelings (embarrassed, cross) for a character stuck on his back._

_A warm geyser carries you all up into the real sky._  
_Your Nubbin’s painted face washes off in the sea._  

## A10-10. The Hook

- `a10-10-s1`: Watch Maui try to change shape. · _Stay well back on the deck._
- `a10-10-s2`: Sit with Maui while he talks. · _Sit near him. Do not push._
- `a10-10-s3`: Help Maui find his hawk. · _Steer into the wind._

#### `a10-10-practice`

**Maui**: Back in business! Hawk!  
_Flash! Where Maui was, a fish flaps on the deck._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): where animals live  
> _Maui turned into a fish. Where do fish live?_  
> - ✅ In water → Yes! Fish live in water. They breathe with gills.
> - In trees → Not trees. Fish live in water.
> - In beds → Not beds! Fish live in water: the sea, rivers and ponds.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that fish live in water._

**Maui**: Hawk!  
_Flash! Now a pig. Your Nubbin and Pua would get on._  
**Maui**: A thousand years without it. Hawk!  
_Flash! A hawk with a shark’s head flops into the sea._  

#### `a10-10-practice-done`

_Maui climbs back aboard as himself. He sits down hard at the stern._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): a new feeling word: frustrated  
> _Maui is frustrated. That means cross, because something will not work._  
> _Say it with me: frus-trat-ed. Have you ever felt frustrated?_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned the feeling word “frustrated” and linked it to their own experience._


#### `a10-10-story`

_Nobody speaks for a long time. You all sit near Maui._  
**Moana**: Are all your tattoos things you did?  
**Maui**: Every one. I earned every one.  
**Maui**: When I was a baby, my first family did not keep me.  
**Maui**: So I gave people gifts. So they would want me.  
**Moana**: The gifts were kind. But nobody has to earn being loved.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): you are loved just for being you  
> _Moana is right. Nobody has to earn love._  
> _Every child is loved just for being them, not for what they do._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that every child is loved just for being themselves._


**Choices**

- **Pass him the water gourd.**
    - He takes it, holds it, and does not give it back.
- **Say nothing. Sit a little closer.**
    - Your Nubbin climbs into Maui’s lap and stays there.

#### `a10-10-story-done`

_Maui does not answer. But he does not turn his back again._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how characters respond to events  
> _Maui stayed close this time. What does that show?_  
> - ✅ He felt a little better → Yes. Being listened to helped Maui feel a little better.
> - He wanted a nap → Maybe, but mostly he felt a little better being listened to.
> - He was cross → He was sad, not cross. Staying close shows he felt a bit better.
> _For grown-ups: Understood how a character’s actions show his feelings._


#### `a10-10-hawk`

**Moana**: Try again. Not because you have to. Because you can.  
**Maui**: …Hawk.  
_A flash. A softer flash this time._  
_A great hawk lifts off and climbs in a wide spiral._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): hawks have wide wings and ride the wind  
> _A hawk has wide, strong wings. It can ride the wind without flapping._  
> _That is how it glides high up, in big circles._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that hawks have wide wings and glide on the wind._

**Moana**: Look at him go!  
_You steer into the wind. Your Nubbin throws its arms up, as if flying._  

#### `a10-10-hawk-done`

_The hawk dives, pulls up, and lands on the mast. It is grinning._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): words for where things are  
> _Where did the hawk land?_  
> - ✅ On top of the mast → Yes! On top of the mast. High above the deck.
> - Under the canoe → Not under. The hawk landed on top of the mast.
> - Beside the sun → Not beside the sun! On top of the mast.
> _For grown-ups: Used a position word (on top of) for where the hawk landed._


#### `a10-10-complete`

**Maui**: Did you see? The roll at the end? I did a roll!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): practice helps you get better  
> _Maui tried again and again, until the hawk came._  
> _Practice, and kind friends, help us get better at hard things._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that practice and kind friends help us improve at hard things._

**Moana**: We saw. The fish saw too.  
_He teaches her steering and the shapes of waves. He is a good teacher._  
_That evening, Moana steers alone. Maui sleeps._  

## A10-11. Te Kā

- `a10-11-s1`: Sail up to the dark islands at night. · _Keep watch from the bow._
- `a10-11-s2`: Get the canoe away from the fire. · _Bail and hold the sail._
- `a10-11-s3`: Stand by while Maui and Moana talk. · _Stay on deck._

#### `a10-11-barrier`

_A ring of black islands lies across the sea, smoking._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS1-1, notice): many Pacific islands began as volcanoes under the sea  
> _Many real islands in the Pacific began as volcanoes under the sea._  
> _Hot rock came up, cooled, and built the island, bit by bit._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that many Pacific islands began as volcanoes and grew slowly._

**Maui**: The island is behind them. Te Kā guards the way. Let me go first.  
**Moana**: I know the swell now. There is a gap.  
_The ash moves. A giant of rock and fire stands up._  
_Your Nubbin hides under the deck with Heihei. Very sensible._  

#### `a10-11-barrier-done`

_Te Kā roars. It is the sound of a mountain having a bad day._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): what to do when something feels too big and scary  
> _Something loud and scary is near. What can you do?_  
> - ✅ Stay safe and tell a grown-up → Yes. Stay safe, and tell a grown-up. Scared is fine.
> - Run at it → Running at something scary is not safe. Tell a grown-up.
> - Pretend it is not there → Pretending does not help. Tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what to do when scared: stay safe and tell a grown-up._


#### `a10-11-gap`

_Moana turns for the gap. Maui, as a hawk, leads Te Kā away._  
_Te Kā swats at him. He swerves and dives._  
**Moana**: Nearly there!  
_Te Kā’s hand comes down. Maui blocks it with his hook. Crack!_  
_The wave throws the canoe far out into the dark sea. Nobody is hurt._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _(Count who is on the canoe.)_  
> _Moana, you, Nubbin, Heihei and Pua. Five! Everyone is safe._  
> Check: `edu:count:crew:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five friends on the canoe._


**Choices**

- **Grab the sail line.**
    - You get the line and keep it. The sail tears but stays on.
- **Grab Heihei, who has wandered out again.**
    - You catch Heihei by the tail. He gives you a funny look.

#### `a10-11-gap-done`

_The sea goes quiet. The sail is torn, and Te Kā’s glow sinks._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): wind pushes a sail and waves push a boat  
> _Wind pushes a sail, and the boat moves. Waves can push a boat too._  
> _Strong wind and big waves push hard. That is how the sail got torn._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wind pushes sails and waves push boats._


#### `a10-11-crack`

_Maui holds his hook. A crack runs through it._  
**Maui**: I told you to turn back. Look at it.  
**Moana**: We can fix it. We will try again.  
**Maui**: One more hit and it is gone. And then who wants me?  
**Moana**: That is not true. You know it is not.  
**Maui**: I am sorry. Good luck.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what friends can do after an argument  
> _Maui and Moana argued. What can friends do afterwards?_  
> - ✅ Say sorry and listen → Yes. Sorry and listening help friends feel close again.
> - Never speak again → Never speaking keeps hurt going. Sorry and listening help.
> - Pretend it did not happen → Pretending does not fix hurt. Sorry and listening do.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about repairing an argument with sorry and listening._

_A hawk lifts off the stern and flies north._  

#### `a10-11-crack-done`

_Moana watches him get smaller. Then he is gone._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): explain what is happening in a story  
> _Why does Maui get smaller and smaller?_  
> - ✅ He is flying far away → Yes! The farther away he flies, the smaller he looks.
> - He is shrinking → He is not shrinking. He is flying far away.
> - He is hiding → Not hiding. He is flying away, so he looks small.
> _For grown-ups: Explained that things look smaller when they are farther away._

_Moana sits at the bow with the green stone. She does not cry._  
**Moana**: I cannot do this. I am not enough.  
_She holds the stone out. The sea takes it, gently._  
_You do not say anything. You sit beside her._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): sitting beside someone helps  
> _You did not fix Moana’s sad feeling. You sat beside her._  
> _Sitting beside someone is a kind way to help._

_Your Nubbin comes out and sits beside you too._

## A10-12. The Manta Ray

- `a10-12-s1`: Watch the light under the water. · _Look over the side._
- `a10-12-s2`: Watch the manta. Let your Nubbin answer. · _Bring your Nubbin to the side._
- `a10-12-s3`: Listen to Gramma’s song. · _Sit with Moana and Gramma._

#### `a10-12-light`

_Late at night, a soft blue light comes up under the canoe._  
_It is a manta ray, glowing, circling the hulls._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): manta rays are huge, gentle fish that glide  
> _A real manta ray is a very big flat fish. It has wide wings._  
> _It is gentle. It glides through the water and eats tiny sea food._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that manta rays are huge, gentle, gliding fish._

_At the stern sits Gramma Tala, as if she was always there._  
**Gramma Tala**: Well. You are a long way past the reef.  
**Moana**: Gramma?  
**Gramma Tala**: I told you I would come back as one of those.

> - Things we lose → Not lost things. The things we learn with love stay.
> - Only toys → Not just toys. What we learn with love stays with us.
> _For grown-ups: Understood a character’s message: what we learn with love stays with us._

> - Having a new hat → Hats are nice! But remembering love helps most.

## A10-13. Te Fiti

- `a10-13-s1`: Run the dark islands again. · _Hold the sail while Moana steers._
- `a10-13-s2`: Look at where the green island should be. · _Climb the mast._
- `a10-13-s3`: Walk the path behind Moana. · _Choose how you go._

#### `a10-13-run`

_This time Moana sails the swell: left, right, left, right._  
_Te Kā’s fire falls where the canoe was, not where it is._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): continue a pattern  
> _Moana sails: left, right, left, right._  
> _What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Left → Yes! Left, right, left, right, left. A pattern!
> - Right → Close. Say it slowly: left, right, left, right... then left.
> - Up → Not up. Left, right, left, right, then left!
> _For grown-ups: Continued a left-right pattern._

**Moana**: Hold it! Now let go! Now!  
_You let go. The canoe spins round a rock, as if dancing._  
_A hawk drops from the sky. It becomes Maui, with his cracked hook._  
**Maui**: Told you to let me go first.  
**Moana**: You came back!  

#### `a10-13-run-done`

**Maui**: Go! I will hold her!  
_His hook meets Te Kā’s fist and breaks. He stands firm._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): coming back to help is brave  
> _Maui had left. Then he came back to help._  
> _Coming back is brave. Friends can start again._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that coming back to help a friend is brave._


#### `a10-13-spiral`

_Moana climbs the mast. You climb after her._  
_Where the green island should be, there is only a hollow in the sea._  
_On Te Kā’s chest is a mark: a spiral._  
_It is the same spiral as on the green stone. And your shell._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): name a shape  
> _What shape is on the stone, the shell and Te Kā’s chest?_  
> - ✅ A spiral → Yes! A spiral goes round and round, and in.
> - A square → A square has four corners. This one goes round and round: a spiral.
> - A star → Not a star. It goes round and round: a spiral.
> _For grown-ups: Named a spiral shape seen on three objects._

**Moana**: Oh.  
**Moana**: She is Te Fiti, without her heart.  

#### `a10-13-spiral-done`

_Moana climbs down. She holds up her hand to the open water._  
_The sea parts. A path of wet sand opens, straight to Te Kā._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): say who a character really is  
> _Moana knows a secret now. Who is the fiery giant, really?_  
> - ✅ Te Fiti, without her heart → Yes! The giant is Te Fiti. She lost her heart.
> - A big crab → Not a crab. The spiral shows it: the giant is Te Fiti.
> - A storm cloud → Not a cloud. The giant is Te Fiti, missing her heart.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out who a character really is from a clue (the spiral)._


#### `a10-13-walk`

_Moana walks down the path through the sea._  
_Te Kā sees her and comes roaring down. Moana keeps walking._  
_You step onto the wet sand. Your heart goes like a drum._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): a gentle way to meet someone upset  
> _Te Kā is not bad. She is hurting, and hurting can look scary._  
> _How can you go to someone upset, gently?_  
> - ✅ Slowly, with open hands → Yes. Slow and open says, “I am a friend.”
> - Shouting back → Shouting adds noise. Slow and open hands is gentler.
> - Running away → Sometimes a grown-up is needed. Slow and open is gentle.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about a gentle approach to someone upset: slow, with open hands._


**Choices**

- **Carry the spiral shell in your open hand.**
    - You hold out the little spiral shell on your palm.
    - Te Kā sees the same spiral. The roar goes quieter.
- **Say, out loud, that you remember her.**
    - **You**: We remember you. All the green. We remember who gave it.
    - Your voice is small against the fire. It carries anyway.
- **Just keep walking, slowly, hands open.**
    - You say nothing. You walk slowly with your hands open.
    - Your Nubbin walks beside you, step for step.

#### `a10-13-walk-done`

_Te Kā stoops, enormous. Fire runs off her like water._  
**Moana**: I see the spiral. I know you. You have waited a long time.  
_Moana touches her forehead to Te Kā’s. The giant goes very still._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): the meaning of a new word  
> _The giant goes very still. What does still mean?_  
> - ✅ Not moving → Yes! Still means not moving at all. Calm and quiet.
> - Very fast → Not fast. Still means not moving.
> - Very loud → Not loud. Still means not moving, and quiet.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that “still” means not moving._

_Moana sets the green stone into the spiral on Te Kā’s chest. It fits._  
_The fire goes out. Moss grows, then ferns, then flowers._  
_The giant softens into a green woman lying down._  
_She becomes an island again. Green, and more green, and more._  
_Te Fiti opens her eyes. She looks at Moana, you, and your Nubbin._  
_She gives Maui his hook, mended and new._  
**Maui**: I am sorry for what I took.  
_Te Fiti smiles. The sea around her goes clear and full of fish._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-3, notice): clean, clear water helps coral reefs and fish; plants need soil, water and light  
> _When the sea is clean and clear, coral and fish do well._  
> _Plants grow when they have soil, water and light. We can look after them._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that clean water helps reefs and fish, and what plants need._
