_Pooh walks off humming. He is thinner now._  
**Rabbit**: He will be back. I need a wider door.  
_Rabbit looks at the empty hall. He almost misses the legs._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): a good friend waits with you  
> _For a whole week, friends sat and waited with Pooh._  
> _Waiting with someone is a way of saying, I care about you._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sitting and waiting with a friend shows you care._


## A11-3. The Woozle

- `a11-03-s1`: Follow Pooh round the trees after the mystery tracks. · _Walk round the spinney in the snow. Do not tell the secret yet._
- `a11-03-s2`: Watch from the oak with Christopher Robin. · _Climb the big oak and keep quiet._

#### `a11-03-tracks`

_It is a snowy day. Piglet sweeps snow off his step._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS2-3, notice): snow is frozen water  
> _Snow is water that has frozen into tiny, soft crystals._  
> _When the sun comes out, snow melts back into water. Drip, drip._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snow is frozen water and melts when it warms up._

_Pooh goes past, round and round in a circle._  
**Piglet**: Pooh, why do you go round and round?  
**Pooh**: I am following something. Paw prints!  
**Piglet**: A Woozle?  
**Pooh**: It might be. Woozles are hard to tell from the front.  
_Your Nubbin puts its feet carefully in the snow._  

**Choices**

- **Tell them the little prints are your Nubbin’s.**
    - **Pooh**: Yes, yes. Do keep up.
    - Nobody listens. They are too busy tracking.
- **Say nothing. Let it play out.**
    - You say nothing. It feels like carrying a full cup.
- **Let your Nubbin go round once more.**
    - Round goes your Nubbin. Now there is one more set of prints.

#### `a11-03-tracks-done`

_Round they go. Round and round._  
_Every time, there are more tracks._  
_(Point to the footprints. Count them: one, two, three.)_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count footprints to 3  
> _Pooh’s prints. Piglet’s prints. Your Nubbin’s tiny prints._  
> _One, two, three sets. Each friend makes their own._  
> Check: `edu:count:footprints:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three sets of footprints, one for each walker._


#### `a11-03-count`

**Pooh**: Look! Two Woozles now. And one little one.  
**Piglet**: I just remembered something I meant to do. Bye!  
_Up in the oak, Christopher Robin sits very still._  
**Christopher Robin**: Do not say anything. It is better when he finds out himself.  
_Pooh puts his foot in a print. It fits!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): testing an idea: does my foot fit the print?  
> _Pooh tries his foot in the print. How does he find out?_  
> - ✅ He tries it and sees if it fits → Yes! Trying it is a clever way to find out.
> - He guesses → Guessing is a start. Trying his foot is how he really finds out.
> _For grown-ups: Saw that testing an idea (does the foot fit?) is a way of finding out._

**Pooh**: Oh.  
_Piglet looks at your Nubbin’s feet. He goes pink._  

#### `a11-03-count-done`

_Christopher Robin climbs down from the tree._  
**Christopher Robin**: Oh, Pooh. Whose footprints do you think those are?  
**Pooh**: My own. I have been following my own feet.  
**Christopher Robin**: There is no better bear anywhere.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): feeling silly is fine; friends are kind  
> _Pooh felt a little silly. Everybody feels silly sometimes._  
> _Christopher Robin did not laugh at him. He said something kind._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that feeling silly is ordinary and kind friends stay kind._


#### `a11-03-complete`

**Pooh**: Being silly is hungry work. Is it lunch?  
_Pooh and Christopher Robin go home._  
_Piglet walks a long way round your Nubbin. Then a shorter way._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: a long way and a short way  
> _First Piglet goes a long way round. Then a short way. Which is shorter?_  
> - ✅ The second way → Yes! The second way is shorter. Piglet is less worried now.
> - The first way → The first way was long. The second way is shorter, and closer.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a long path and a short path, and saw Piglet grow less worried._

**Piglet**: I knew it was not a Woozle. Mostly.  
_Your Nubbin holds out a paw. Piglet shakes it, twice._  

## A11-4. Eeyore’s Tail

- `a11-04-s1`: Find out what is wrong with Eeyore. · _He is in the thistly corner of the Forest._
- `a11-04-s2`: Go with Pooh to ask Owl. · _Owl lives high in a tree, behind a grand door._
- `a11-04-s3`: Hold the tail straight while Christopher Robin nails it on. · _Carry the tail back. Hold it where Christopher Robin points._

#### `a11-04-gloomy`

_Eeyore is a grey donkey. He stands in the thistles, all by himself._  
**Pooh**: Good morning, Eeyore.  
**Eeyore**: Good morning. If it is. Which I doubt.  
**Pooh**: What is the matter?  
**Eeyore**: Nothing. Nobody minds.  
_Pooh walks round Eeyore. Then round again._  
**Pooh**: Eeyore! Where is your tail?  
**Eeyore**: It is gone. That explains a great deal.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): how a sad friend feels, and what helps  
> _Eeyore is sad. What could help him?_  
> - ✅ Sit with him and help look → Thank you. That helps a bit.
> - Tell him not to be sad → Feelings do not just go away. Sitting with him helps more.
> - Walk away → Eeyore is lonely. Staying close helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being with a sad friend and helping._


**Choices**

- **Promise you will help find it.**
    - **Eeyore**: Kind of you. Do not trouble. Somebody is using it, I expect.
- **Sit with him for a moment first.**
    - You sit in the prickly thistles beside him.
    - Eeyore notices, and does not say so. That is his thank you.
- **Look behind the thistles.**
    - Your Nubbin looks behind the thistles and under a stone. No tail.

#### `a11-04-gloomy-done`

**Pooh**: I shall find your tail, Eeyore. Me. Pooh.  
**Eeyore**: Thank you, Pooh. You are a real friend.  
_Eeyore’s ears lift, just a little._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): thistles are prickly to keep animals off  
> _Thistles have sharp prickles all over._  
> _The prickles help the plant. Most animals do not want to nibble it._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that thistle prickles help protect the plant._


#### `a11-04-owl`

_Owl lives high in a tree, behind a grand door._  
_There are two signs by the door. They are spelled in Owl’s own way._  
**Owl**: Ah, Pooh. How do you do?  
**Pooh**: Eeyore has lost his tail. How do I find it?  
**Owl**: There is a Proper Way. First, one Puts Up a Notice.  
**Pooh**: I am only a small bear. Big words make my head go fuzzy.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, L.2.4, ask): asking what a word means  
> _Pooh does not know the big words. What can he do?_  
> - ✅ Ask Owl what the word means → Quite right. “Notice” just means a sign.
> - Pretend he knows → Asking is brave and clever. Owl is happy to explain.
> _For grown-ups: Saw that asking what a new word means is a good thing to do._

**Owl**: It means: the thing to do.  
_Your Nubbin is not listening. It stares at the bell-pull._  

#### `a11-04-owl-done`

**Pooh**: Owl, that bell-pull. Where did you get it?  
**Owl**: I found it on a bush. It came away in my wing.  
**Pooh**: It is Eeyore’s! It is his tail!  
_(Point to the grey tail with a tuft at the end.)_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): looking closely finds things  
> _Your Nubbin did not listen to the long words. It looked closely._  
> _Looking carefully is how scientists find answers._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that looking closely helps us find answers._


#### `a11-04-nail`

_You carry the tail carefully, as if it might wake._  
_Christopher Robin has a little hammer and one tiny nail._  
**Christopher Robin**: Hold it straight. There. Eeyore, this will not hurt.  
**Eeyore**: Do not mind me.  
_Tap, tap. Eeyore does not flinch, but your Nubbin does, twice._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count the taps: 2  
> _Tap, tap. (Tap the table with me.)_  
> _One tap, two taps. The tail is on tight._  
> Check: `edu:count:taps:2`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two taps of the hammer while a tail was fixed on._

**Eeyore**: Hm. It works. Not that anyone asked.  
_Swish, swish! Eeyore swishes his tail, and he is happy._  

#### `a11-04-nail-done`

**Eeyore**: Thank you, Pooh. And the one with the bow.  
_Eeyore swishes his tail. Swish._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, notice): sound words: swish  
> _Swish is a sound word. It sounds like what it does._  
> _(Swish your arm like a tail: swish, swish!)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard and acted out the sound word swish._

_He is glad. He would rather you did not mention it._  

#### `a11-04-complete`

_Pooh walks home. He feels he has done a Good Deed._  
_He is ready for a little something by eleven o’clock._  
**Pooh**: Owl knows ever such a lot. But your Nubbin looked at the bell-pull.  
_Your Nubbin looks proud._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): everyone is good at something different  
> _Owl is good at long words. Your Nubbin is good at looking._  
> _Everybody is good at something. It all helps._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that everyone has different things they are good at._


## A11-5. The Very Deep Pit

- `a11-05-s1`: Help Pooh and Piglet dig a deep pit by the Six Pine Trees. · _Dig where Pooh points._
- `a11-05-s2`: Keep the lantern steady while Pooh checks the honey. · _Walk with Pooh and hold the lantern still._
- `a11-05-s3`: Let Piglet meet the “Heffalump”. Do not explain. · _Stay by the pit with the lantern._

#### `a11-05-dig`

**Christopher Robin**: I saw a Heffalump today. I think.  
**Piglet**: A Heffalump! Pooh, what do we do?  
**Pooh**: We catch it in a Very Deep Pit, by the Six Pine Trees.  
_Piglet digs and Pooh watches. You do most of it._  
_Your Nubbin moves one pebble a very long way._  
**Piglet**: What do Heffalumps like?  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count the pine trees: 6  
> _The Six Pine Trees stand in a row. (Point and count them.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five, six. Six pine trees!_  
> Check: `edu:count:pine-trees:6`
> _For grown-ups: Counted six pine trees by pointing at each one._

**Pooh**: Honey.  

**Choices**

- **Ask what they will do once it is caught.**
    - **Pooh**: Be very polite to it, I expect.
    - **Piglet**: Oh, d-dear.
- **Dig a little step in one side, in case.**
    - **Piglet**: A step? For the Heffalump?
    - **You**: For anyone who falls in by mistake.
    - **Pooh**: Very sensible.
- **Check it is deep enough.**
    - You climb in. It comes up to your chin!

#### `a11-05-dig-done`

_Pooh fetches his very last jar of honey._  
_He lowers it into the pit. Down, down, down._  
_He looks at it for a long time._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): honey keeps for a very long time  
> _Honey is made by bees, and it keeps for a very long time._  
> _That is why Pooh’s last jar will still be good tomorrow._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that honey keeps for a very long time._


#### `a11-05-night`

_That night Pooh cannot sleep._  
**Pooh**: I will see if the honey is still there. Hold the lantern?  
_You walk with the lantern. Your Nubbin stays in the light._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): position words: inside and outside  
> _Your Nubbin stays in the circle of light. Is it inside, or outside?_  
> - ✅ Inside → Yes! Inside the light. Outside, it is dark.
> - Outside → Look again. It stays inside the light, where it can see.
> _For grown-ups: Used the position words inside and outside._

_Pooh climbs down into the pit and licks the honey._  
**Pooh**: Mmff. Mmff mff.  
_The jar is stuck on Pooh’s head!_  

**Choices**

- **Hold the lantern steady and wait.**
    - You hold it steady. It trembles once, because you giggle.
- **Try to pull the jar off.**
    - It will not come. This will have to be a morning job.

#### `a11-05-night-done`

_Pooh climbs out somehow._  
_He wanders off in the grey morning, with the jar on his head._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, ask): sounds are muffled inside a jar  
> _Pooh talks inside the jar. Do his words sound loud and clear?_  
> - ✅ No, they sound muffled and boomy → Yes! A jar changes how a voice sounds.
> - Yes, clear as a bell → Not quite. In a jar the voice sounds muffled and boomy.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a voice sounds different inside a jar._

**Pooh**: Mmff mmm mmff.  

#### `a11-05-morning`

_At first light, Piglet comes to look._  
_A big round head walks round the pit. Roar!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): shapes: round is a circle  
> _The big head is round. Which shape is round?_  
> - ✅ A circle → Yes! A circle is round, like the jar on Pooh’s head.
> - A square → A square has corners. A round shape is a circle.
> _For grown-ups: Named a round shape: a circle._

**Piglet**: Help! A Heffalump! It has Pooh’s honey!  
_Piglet runs to Christopher Robin._  
_You stay with the lantern. You do not explain._  
_The jar bangs on a root and breaks. There is Pooh!_  
**Piglet**: …Oh. It was Pooh.  

#### `a11-05-morning-done`

_Piglet goes home to bed. He has a headache._  
_Pooh goes home to breakfast._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): being scared is fine; checking helps  
> _Piglet got a big fright. Frights make hearts go thump._  
> _A deep breath helps. So does looking again, slowly._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that being frightened is normal and slow breaths and a second look help._

_Your Nubbin keeps one piece of the jar._  

#### `a11-05-complete`

**Pooh**: I thought I might be a Heffalump. It was echoey in there.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, notice): funny stories: a mix-up  
> _A mix-up! Piglet saw a bear in a jar and thought Heffalump._  
> _Stories make us laugh when someone gets the wrong idea._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed how a mix-up makes a story funny._

**Christopher Robin**: You were a bear in a jar. That is better.  
**Pooh**: Then who is the Heffalump?  
_Everyone looks at your Nubbin. It looks behind itself._  

## A11-6. Eeyore’s Birthday

- `a11-06-s1`: Find out why Eeyore is sadder than usual. · _He is by the stream, looking at the water._
- `a11-06-s2`: Go with Pooh and Piglet to fetch presents. · _Carry the honey pot for Pooh._
- `a11-06-s3`: Choose what your Nubbin gives Eeyore. · _There is no wrong present. Nothing at all is a choice._

#### `a11-06-stream`

_Eeyore stands by the stream. He looks at himself in the water._  
**Eeyore**: Even the one in the water looks glum.  
**Pooh**: Good morning, Eeyore.  
**Eeyore**: Is it? It would be just like it.  
**Eeyore**: It is my birthday. Not that it matters.  
**Pooh**: Your birthday!  
**Eeyore**: You can tell by the presents. All none of them.  
_Pooh looks left and right. No presents._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, ask): zero means none  
> _Eeyore has “all none” of the presents. How many is that?_  
> - ✅ Zero. None at all → Yes! Zero means none. Eeyore has no presents yet.
> - One → One would be a present. “None” means zero: nothing at all.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that none means zero._

**Pooh**: Wait here, Eeyore.  

#### `a11-06-presents`

_Pooh has a pot of honey. Piglet has a green balloon._  
_Your Nubbin carries a thistle in both paws._  
_Pooh sits down. He peeks in the pot, just to see._  
_Lick, lick, lick. The pot is empty!_  
**Pooh**: Bother. I ate my present.  
**Pooh**: But a pot is useful! I will give Eeyore a Useful Pot.  
_Piglet runs to be first, and trips. He lands on the balloon._  
_Bang! Now it is a bit of damp rag._  
**Piglet**: Oh, d-dear.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a balloon is full of air that pushes out  
> _A balloon is full of air. The air pushes out on the rubber._  
> _Squash it too hard, and bang! The air rushes out._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that squashing a balloon too hard makes it burst._


#### `a11-06-presents-done`

_Your Nubbin looks at the pot, the rag and the thistle._  
_The pot is empty, the rag is floppy, and the thistle is prickly._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, notice): describing words for how things feel  
> _Empty, floppy, prickly: these are describing words._  
> _They tell us how a thing feels. Can you think of one more?_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned describing words for how things feel._

_(Touch your arm. Is it soft or prickly?)_  

#### `a11-06-gift`

**Piglet**: Happy birthday, Eeyore. I brought a balloon.  
**Eeyore**: A balloon? For me?  
**Piglet**: It burst. I am so sorry.  
**Pooh**: I brought a Useful Pot. To put things in.  
**Pooh**: There is nothing in it. That is what makes it useful.  
_Eeyore puts the damp rag in the pot, and takes it out. In again!_  
**Eeyore**: It goes in and out. Fancy that.  
_Nobody has seen Eeyore happy before. Nobody speaks._  
_Now it is your Nubbin’s turn. It can give something, or nothing._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): a gift does not have to be big  
> _A present does not have to be big, or new, or shiny._  
> _A ribbon is a gift. So is a thistle. So is sitting beside someone._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a gift can be small, or just time spent together._


**Choices**

- **Your Nubbin gives Eeyore its blue ribbon.**
    - Your Nubbin tugs its blue bow undone. It lays the ribbon at Eeyore’s feet.
    - **Eeyore**: Christopher Robin tied that. I know what it says.
    - **Eeyore**: I shall keep it somewhere safe. In the pot.
- **Your Nubbin gives him the thistle it carried.**
    - Your Nubbin holds out the thistle. Its paws are sore from carrying it.
    - **Eeyore**: The good sort. Purple on top. Somebody carried that far.
    - **Eeyore**: I shall not eat it today. I shall keep it.
- **Nothing. You both just sit with him.**
    - You sit on the bank. Your Nubbin sits beside you.
    - Pooh and Piglet go home, but you stay. The afternoon goes slowly.
    - **Eeyore**: Nobody has done that before. Sat. Without wanting anything.

#### `a11-06-gift-done`

_By evening Eeyore still puts the rag in and out of the pot._  
_In, out, in, out, in, out._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, notice): repeated words and actions in a story  
> _In, out. In, out. In, out. The story repeats it._  
> _Repeated words are fun to say together. (Say “in, out” with a clap.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that repeated words and actions make a story fun to say._

_He looks almost cheerful._  

#### `a11-06-complete`

_Christopher Robin arrives with a cake. First he cuts it in half._  

> **Lesson** (maths, 1.G.A.3, ask): two equal parts are halves  
> _The cake is cut into two equal parts. What is each part called?_  
> - ✅ A half → Yes! Two equal parts. Each one is a half.
> - A whole → The whole is all of it. One of two equal parts is a half.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that two equal parts are halves._

_Then more slices, one for everyone. Eeyore gets the most icing._  
**Eeyore**: A pot, a balloon, and cake. People will say I am spoiled.  
**Pooh**: Will they?  
**Eeyore**: No. But they could.  
_Pooh gives you an empty pot too. Eeyore adds a bit of balloon._  

## A11-7. Kanga and Baby Roo

- `a11-07-s1`: Listen to Rabbit’s plan about the newcomers. · _Rabbit has a meeting by his front door._
- `a11-07-s2`: Make sure Roo has a nice time. · _Run alongside Rabbit. Keep Roo company._
- `a11-07-s3`: Go and see how Piglet is getting on. · _Kanga’s house is by the Sandy Pit._

#### `a11-07-plan`

_A Kanga and a baby Roo are new in the Forest._  
**Rabbit**: Who said she could come? She keeps her baby in her pocket!  
**Pooh**: Where should it ride?  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-LS1-2, notice): kangaroo mothers carry their babies in a pouch  
> _Real kangaroos have a pouch, like a pocket, on their tummy._  
> _A baby kangaroo is called a joey. The pouch keeps it safe and warm._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that mother kangaroos carry their babies in a pouch._

**Rabbit**: Here is my plan. We borrow Roo for a game of hide.  
**Rabbit**: Piglet hops in the pocket, so Kanga does not notice.  
**Piglet**: V-very small. Yes.  
_Your Nubbin looks at you. You look at Rabbit._  

**Choices**

- **Say it is a bad plan.**
    - **Rabbit**: It is a good plan. It has Steps.
    - You cannot stop a plan with Steps.
- **Ask what happens to Roo.**
    - **Rabbit**: He stays at mine. Briefly. He will be safe.
    - You will be there too.
- **Say nothing, and go along.**
    - You go along. Someone should be there who is not part of the plan.

#### `a11-07-plan-done`

**Rabbit**: Look after Roo on the way, Keeper.  
**Rabbit**: Happy Roos stay quiet.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): tell your grown-up before you go anywhere  
> _Roo is going off with Rabbit. Who should Roo tell first?_  
> - ✅ His grown-up, Kanga → Yes. Always tell your grown-up where you are going.
> - Nobody → Grown-ups worry. Telling them keeps you safe.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to tell a grown-up before going off anywhere._

_(Whisper “Quiet Roo.” Now whisper louder, then quieter.)_  

#### `a11-07-swap`

_By the Sandy Pit, Kanga teaches Roo to jump._  
_Pooh keeps her busy with a long, long story._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): kangaroos hop on strong back legs  
> _Real kangaroos have very strong back legs._  
> _They hop to get about, boing, boing, boing. Roo is learning how._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that kangaroos hop on strong back legs._

_Rabbit lifts Roo into a pillowcase. Piglet hops in Kanga’s pocket._  
_You run alongside._  
**Roo**: Is this a game? It smells of carrots!  
**Roo**: Can your Nubbin come too?  

**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin ride with Roo.**
    - Your Nubbin climbs in. Roo giggles all the way.
- **Count the trees with Roo as they go by.**
    - **Roo**: One, two, lots, lots, lots, home!
- **Tell Roo a story.**
    - **Roo**: Is there a Roo in it?
    - **You**: There is now.
    - **Roo**: Make him jump a lot.

#### `a11-07-swap-done`

_At Rabbit’s, Roo hops off the step. Hop!_  
_Rabbit pretends not to count the hops._  
_He counts them anyway._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count hops to 5  
> _Hop! Roo hops again. (Hop with me and count.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five hops. Whew!_  
> Check: `edu:count:hops:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five hops, one number for each._


#### `a11-07-bath`

_At Kanga’s house, Kanga has noticed. Kangas always notice._  
**Kanga**: Bath time, Roo dear.  
_She says it to Piglet. She looks right at him._  
**Piglet**: I am not Roo! I am Piglet!  
**Kanga**: Of course you are, dear.  
_Splash! Kanga scrubs him and gives him some medicine._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): only a grown-up gives you medicine  
> _Medicine helps a body get well. Take it only from a grown-up._  
> _Never take medicine by yourself, even if it looks like a sweet._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that only a trusted grown-up should give medicine._

_Kanga winks at you. She knows, and she is enjoying herself._  
_Piglet escapes and runs home._  

#### `a11-07-bath-done`

_Kanga collects Roo from Rabbit’s. She smiles._  
_She knew all along._  
**Rabbit**: I was only borrowing.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): ask first before borrowing  
> _What could Rabbit do next time, before borrowing Roo?_  
> - ✅ Ask Kanga first → Yes. Asking first is kind and fair.
> - Do it quietly → Quiet is not the same as kind. Asking is better.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that asking first is the kind and fair way to borrow._


#### `a11-07-complete`

**Rabbit**: Well. She can stay. Roo jumps very well.  
_Rabbit is friendly now. A bit stiffly, like a new shoe._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): being kind to someone new  
> _Rabbit was cross at first, because Kanga and Roo were new._  
> _Being friendly to newcomers helps them feel they belong._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that being friendly to newcomers helps them belong._

**Roo**: Can I go in the pillowcase again?  
**Kanga**: Thank you for watching him, dear.  

## A11-8. The Expotition

- `a11-08-s1`: Join Christopher Robin’s Expotition to the North Pole. · _He is outside his house in his Big Boots._
- `a11-08-s2`: Help get Roo out of the stream. · _Take the other end of Pooh’s pole._
- `a11-08-s3`: Help Christopher Robin mark the spot. · _Push the pole into the bank._

#### `a11-08-setoff`

_Christopher Robin puts on his Big Boots. That means an Adventure!_  
**Christopher Robin**: We are going on an Expotition, to find the North Pole.  
**Pooh**: What is the North Pole?  
**Christopher Robin**: A thing at the North. You will know it when you see it.  
_Everyone comes: Rabbit, Kanga, Roo, Owl, Piglet. Eeyore comes last._  
**Eeyore**: Nobody told me. Well, somebody did. Not properly.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): including everyone and telling them the plan  
> _Eeyore was told about the Expotition, but not properly._  
> _Being left out feels sad. Telling everyone the plan helps them belong._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that telling everyone the plan helps them feel included._

**Rabbit**: Single file!  
_Your Nubbin marches in line, between Pooh and Piglet._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): first and last in a line  
> _(Look at the line.) Who is at the very end?_  
> - ✅ Eeyore → Yes! Eeyore comes last, at the back.
> - Christopher Robin → He is at the front. Eeyore is last, at the back.
> _For grown-ups: Used first and last to describe a line of friends._


**Choices**

- **Walk at the back with Eeyore.**
    - **Eeyore**: Someone has to be at the back. It might as well be me.
- **Walk at the front with Christopher Robin.**
    - **Christopher Robin**: Good. You can look out for the Pole.
- **Look out for Ambushes.**
    - You find two gorse bushes, a log and Owl.

#### `a11-08-roo`

_By a pool in the stream, everyone has lunch._  
_Roo falls in with a splash, and the water carries him off._  
**Roo**: Look, Kanga! I am swimming!  
_Your Nubbin does not mind water. It paddles beside him._  
_Pooh holds a long pole across the stream. You hold the other end._  
_Roo bumps the pole and holds on. You lift him out._  

> **Lesson** (health, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): water safety: reach, do not jump in  
> _Nubbins do not mind water. People should be careful._  
> _If a friend falls in, stay on the bank._  
> _Reach with a pole, and shout for a grown-up._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned to reach with a pole and call a grown-up if someone falls in water._


#### `a11-08-roo-done`

**Roo**: Did you see me swimming? Did you?  
**Kanga**: We did, dear. Now come and be dried.  
_The stream keeps running, down, down, down._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): streams flow downhill and carry things along  
> _A stream always runs downhill. Whoosh!_  
> _It carries leaves, sticks, and Roo. Water pushes things along._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that streams flow downhill and carry things with them._


#### `a11-08-pole`

**Christopher Robin**: Pooh, do you know what you are holding?  
**Pooh**: A pole. A wet one.  
**Christopher Robin**: It is the North Pole! You found it!  
**Pooh**: Oh!  
_Christopher Robin pushes it into the bank._  
_He writes a sign on it. The spelling wobbles._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, notice): spelling can wobble; sound it out  
> _Christopher Robin wrote the sign by listening to the sounds._  
> _Pole is spelled P-O-L-E. He might write P-O-L, and that is fine._  
> _Sounding out is how we all start._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wobbly spelling is fine when you sound a word out._

**Eeyore**: My tail has been in the pool ten minutes. It is numb.  
**Christopher Robin**: Oh, Eeyore. Let me dry it.  

#### `a11-08-pole-done`

_Everyone walks home in a long happy line._  
_Roo is asleep on Kanga._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): the real North Pole is at the top of the world  
> _The real North Pole is at the very top of the Earth._  
> _It is covered in ice and it is very, very cold._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the real North Pole is a cold place at the top of the world._

_Pooh walks very upright. That is how discoverers walk._  

#### `a11-08-complete`

**Christopher Robin**: This is the spare pole. Every Expotition needs a hat-stand.  
_It is shorter, and it has a forked top._  
**Pooh**: Did I really discover it?  
**Christopher Robin**: You did.  
**Pooh**: I thought it would be bigger. But it is very nice.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, do): on top of, under, beside  
> _Hang a hat on the forked pole._  
> _Is the hat on top of the pole, or under it?_  
> _(Put something on top of something, then under it, then beside it.)_

## A11-9. Surrounded by Water

- `a11-09-s1`: Find out where Piglet is, in all this rain. · _Watch the flood from the high bank._
- `a11-09-s2`: Help Pooh get the message to Christopher Robin. · _Paddle the wash-tub beside the Floating Bear._
- `a11-09-s3`: Sail the Brain of Pooh to Piglet’s tree. · _Keep your tub beside the umbrella._

#### `a11-09-rain`

_Rain, rain, rain. It rains all day and all night._  
_The stream grows big. It spills over its banks._  
_Low places fill first. Water runs downhill._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): weather words: flood  
> _What do we call it when a stream spills over its banks?_  
> - ✅ A flood → Yes, a flood! Lots of rain made the water too big for the stream.
> - A drought → A drought is no rain at all. This is a flood: too much water.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the word flood and what it means._

_Piglet’s house is in a beech tree. Water is all around._  
**Piglet**: Everyone else will be fine. I am just small and wet.  
_He writes HELP and his name. He corks it in a bottle._  
_You are up on the high bank. You see the bottle float by._  

#### `a11-09-rain-done`

_You follow the bottle along the bank._  
_Bob, bob, bob. It floats all the way to Pooh._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, notice): a corked bottle has air in it, so it floats  
> _A closed bottle is full of air. The air helps it float._  
> _Some things float. Some things sink. A stone sinks._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a bottle with air inside floats._

_He is sitting on a branch above his own front door._  

#### `a11-09-bear`

**Pooh**: A bottle with a letter! I can only read the P.  
**Pooh**: P is for Pooh. So it must be for me!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): the first sound and letter of a name  
> _Pooh starts with P. Which other friend starts with P too?_  
> - ✅ Piglet → Yes! Piglet and Pooh both start with P. Puh, puh!
> - Owl → Owl starts with O. Piglet starts with P, like Pooh.
> _For grown-ups: Matched a name to the first letter and sound P._

_Pooh puts his big empty jar on the water._  
_It tips over, so he tries again, sitting on top. It floats!_  
**Pooh**: This is the Floating Bear. Mostly it floats.  
_You find a wash-tub in a bush. You paddle with your hands._  
_Your Nubbin rides on your head, nice and dry._  

**Choices**

- **Paddle close enough to grab him.**
    - Twice the Floating Bear tips. Twice you push it back up.
- **Tow him with a bit of string.**
    - **Pooh**: A tow! Like a proper ship. I shall sit very still.

#### `a11-09-bear-done`

_You bump into the hill where Christopher Robin lives._  
_It is an island now. A boy stands on it._  
_(Point to the water all round the hill.)_  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): an island is land with water all round  
> _An island is land with water all the way round it._  
> _On a map, islands are bits of land, with blue all round._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that an island is land surrounded by water._


#### `a11-09-umbrella`

**Christopher Robin**: Piglet is stuck in his tree. We need a boat.  
**Pooh**: Your umbrella is a bowl turned over. A bowl is a sort of boat.  
_Christopher Robin opens it. He sets it on the water._  
_It floats, wobbles, and holds. Pooh climbs in too._  

> **Lesson** (science, 3-5-ETS1-2, notice): a bowl shape floats because it holds air  
> _A bowl shape pushes water aside, so it can float and carry things._  
> _Pooh had a clever idea: use what you have to build a boat._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a bowl shape can float and used a clever idea to solve a problem._

**Christopher Robin**: I name this ship the Brain of Pooh. It was your idea.  
**Pooh**: The Brain of Pooh. Oh.  
_You paddle beside them. Your Nubbin is the lookout._  

#### `a11-09-umbrella-done`

_Piglet is at his window. He is very small and very wet._  
_He sees the Brain of Pooh. He jumps up and down._  
**Piglet**: Pooh! Christopher Robin! You came!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): friends come when you ask for help  
> _Piglet was scared. He sent a message asking for help._  
> _Asking for help was brave. Friends came, because he asked._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that asking for help is brave and friends come._


#### `a11-09-complete`

_Piglet climbs down into the umbrella. It holds three, just._  
**Piglet**: I knew someone would come.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): add one more: 2 and 1 makes 3  
> _Two friends are in the umbrella. Piglet climbs in. How many now?_  
> - ✅ Three → Yes! Two and one more makes three.
> - Two → Two was before Piglet. Add Piglet: one, two, three!
> _For grown-ups: Added one more to two to make three._

**Christopher Robin**: It was Pooh’s idea. All of it.  
**Pooh**: Was it? I must have more of them.  
_Your Nubbin sneezes. It is the driest thing for miles._  

## A11-10. The Long Table

- `a11-10-s1`: Help Owl tell everyone about the party. · _Go round the Forest and tell everyone in short words._
- `a11-10-s2`: Set the long table. Save Eeyore a seat at the end. · _Lay a plate at each place. Then put a cushion on the last chair._

#### `a11-10-invites`

**Christopher Robin**: Owl, tell everyone there is a party. It is for Pooh.  
**Owl**: Very good. I shall Announce it.  
_Owl flies off. You go too, to say it in shorter words._  
_At the Gloomy Place, Owl tells Eeyore._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): clear messages use short, simple words  
> _Which is easier to understand? “Party for Pooh!” or a very long, fancy sentence?_  
> - ✅ “Party for Pooh!” → Yes! Short, clear words help everyone hear the news.
> - The long, fancy one → Long words can get lost. Short ones are easier to hear.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that short, clear words make a message easy to understand._

**Eeyore**: A party. For me. Better late than never.  
**Owl**: No, it is for…  
_But Eeyore has turned away to think._  

**Choices**

- **Tell Eeyore it is for Pooh.**
    - **Eeyore**: Is it. Well. I shall come anyway, if I am wanted. Which I doubt.
- **Tell him there will be a seat for him.**
    - **Eeyore**: A seat. At the end, I expect.
    - **You**: Wherever you like.
    - **Eeyore**: The end. I like the end. You can see who is leaving.

#### `a11-10-table`

_Christopher Robin makes a long table in the open air._  
_You lay the plates. Your Nubbin puts a leaf on each one._  
**Rabbit**: Owl at the top. Then Kanga. Then me.  
_One chair is left at the very end._  
_You put a cushion on it, and a card that says EEYORE._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, do): one plate for each friend  
> _Put one plate for each friend, down the long table._  
> _One plate, one friend. One plate, one friend. No one gets left out._  
> Check: `edu:place:plates:one-each`
> _For grown-ups: Matched one plate to each friend, one to one._

**Eeyore**: A place at the end. With my name on.  
**Eeyore**: The cushion is a nice touch.  

#### `a11-10-table-done`

**Christopher Robin**: This party is for what somebody did, and we all know who.  
_Eeyore half stands, to make a speech._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, notice): the first letter of a name: E for Eeyore  
> _The card on the end chair says EEYORE. It starts with E._  
> _Here E says “ee”, like the start of Eeyore. (Can you find an E?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Linked the first letter E to the first sound in Eeyore._

_Then Christopher Robin gives Pooh a present._  
_Eeyore sits down again._  

#### `a11-10-complete`

_Pooh’s present is a Special Pencil Case._  
_Inside are pencils marked B, HB and BB._  
_Pooh cannot write. But he looks at every pencil._  
**Eeyore**: Pencils. When I was young we had sticks.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): leaving a place for everyone  
> _Eeyore had a place at the party, with a cushion and his name._  
> _Saving a place for everyone, even the quiet ones, helps them feel they belong._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that saving a place for everyone makes people feel they belong._

_Walking home, Pooh and Piglet are quiet. It is a friendly quiet._  

## A11-11. A House for Eeyore

- `a11-11-s1`: Help Pooh and Piglet build Eeyore a house. · _Carry sticks to Pooh Corner._
- `a11-11-s2`: Go with Christopher Robin and Eeyore to look for his missing house. · _Walk Eeyore through the snow to Pooh Corner._
- `a11-11-s3`: Let Eeyore work it out his own way. · _Stand back and let Eeyore look._

#### `a11-11-snow`

_It is snowing. The Forest is white and soft._  
_Pooh hums a snow hum. It gets longer as it goes._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): weather words: snow  
> _What is falling from the sky in this story?_  
> - ✅ Snow → Yes, snow! Soft, white and cold.
> - Rain → Rain is wet drops. This is snow: soft, white flakes.
> _For grown-ups: Named the weather in the story: snow._

**Pooh**: Eeyore has no house. Everybody has one except him.  
**Piglet**: We could build him one, at Pooh Corner. Out of sticks.  
_A heap of sticks lies on the far side of the wood._  
_You carry sticks. Your Nubbin carries one, the long way round._  
**Piglet**: It is a very good house. Eeyore will be pleased.  

**Choices**

- **Make the doorway wide enough for a donkey.**
    - You make it wider. Pooh likes wide doors, ever since Rabbit’s.
- **Put a roof on, in case.**
    - **Piglet**: In case of snow? It is snow already.
    - **You**: In case of more.
    - **Piglet**: Oh. Yes.
- **Let your Nubbin choose the last stick.**
    - It picks a crooked one. It looks right, somehow.

#### `a11-11-snow-done`

_The house stands at Pooh Corner. It is a little lopsided._  
_Snow settles on the roof, which is shaped like a triangle._  
_(Draw a triangle in the air: three sides, three corners.)_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, notice): a triangle has three sides and three corners  
> _A triangle has three straight sides and three corners._  
> _A sloping roof like a triangle lets snow slide off._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a triangle has three sides and three corners._


#### `a11-11-missing`

_At Christopher Robin’s door, Eeyore stands in the snow._  
**Eeyore**: It is snowing. I built a house. Now it is not there.  
**Christopher Robin**: Where was it?  
**Eeyore**: By the wood. A house of sticks. It has gone.  
_You think of a heap of sticks. Uh-oh._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): a funny feeling in your tummy can mean a mistake  
> _Your tummy feels funny. That can be a worry feeling._  
> _It may mean we made a mistake. We can put it right._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a funny tummy feeling can mean we have made a mistake and can put it right._

**Christopher Robin**: Let us go and look.  
_You walk with them through the snow._  

#### `a11-11-missing-done`

_At Pooh Corner stands a house of sticks._  
_Pooh and Piglet are admiring it._  
_Snow is on the roof. Inside, it is dry._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, notice): a house keeps us warm and dry  
> _A house has walls and a roof. They keep out snow and wind._  
> _Animals have homes too. Birds have nests. Rabbits have burrows._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that homes keep people and animals warm and dry._


#### `a11-11-wind`

**Eeyore**: There. That is my house. It is here. And I built it there.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): position words: here and there  
> _(Point to something near you. Now something far away.) Which one is here?_  
> - ✅ The near one → Yes! Here is near. There is far away.
> - The far one → The far one is there. Here is near, close to you.
> _For grown-ups: Used the position words here (near) and there (far)._

**Eeyore**: The wind must have moved it.  
_Pooh and Piglet look at you. You say nothing, which is the kind thing._  
**Eeyore**: It is better here. Not so draughty.  
**Christopher Robin**: It is a lovely house, Eeyore.  
**Eeyore**: Somebody somewhere must like me.  

#### `a11-11-door`

_Eeyore goes in. He comes out again, to look at his door._  
_On the latch is a blue ribbon, tied in a bow._  
**Eeyore**: It keeps the door from banging. Useful. Like a Friend.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): small kind things can last a long time  
> _The ribbon was a small gift. Eeyore found a use for it._  
> _A small kind thing can go on helping for a long, long time._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a small kind gift can keep helping for a long time._


#### `a11-11-complete`

_Pooh and Piglet walk home in the snow._  
**Piglet**: Pooh. Did we take Eeyore’s house?  
**Pooh**: We did. And then we gave it back, in a better place.  
**Piglet**: I think that counts.  
_Your Nubbin walks in Pooh’s footprints all the way. Hop, hop._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: big and small footprints  
> _(Look at the footprints.) Whose feet are bigger: Pooh’s, or your Nubbin’s?_  
> - ✅ Pooh’s → Yes! Pooh’s feet are bigger. That is why your Nubbin hops.
> - Your Nubbin’s → Your Nubbin’s feet are small. Pooh’s are bigger, so it hops.
> _For grown-ups: Compared big and small footprints._


## A11-12. A Bouncy Visitor

- `a11-12-s1`: Find out what is making that noise at Pooh’s door. · _You are staying the night at Pooh’s. Open the door._
- `a11-12-s2`: Help Tigger try honey, haycorns and thistles. · _Go from Pooh’s to Piglet’s to Eeyore’s._
- `a11-12-s3`: Take Tigger to Kanga’s for one last try. · _Kanga’s house is by the Sandy Pit._

#### `a11-12-night`

_In the night, at Pooh’s house, there is a noise._  
_It is a growly, wobbly noise. A pleased sort of noise._  
**Pooh**: Is it you?  
_It is not. Pooh opens the door._  
**Tigger**: Hello! I am Tigger. I have just come!  
_Tigger has orange and black stripes. Orange, black, orange, black._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): a stripe pattern: what comes next?  
> _Tigger’s stripes go orange, black, orange, black. What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Orange → Yes! Orange, black, orange, black, orange! Patterns repeat.
> - Green → Green is not in the pattern. After black comes orange again.
> _For grown-ups: Continued an orange and black stripe pattern._

_He has a fight with the tablecloth. He wins._  
_He bounces your Nubbin. Your Nubbin bounces back._  

**Choices**

- **Offer to help find Tigger some breakfast.**
    - **Tigger**: Breakfast! Tiggers like everything for breakfast. Probably.
- **Put the tablecloth back.**
    - You put it back. Tigger watches it, in case it starts again.
- **Ask Tigger where he came from.**
    - **Tigger**: From over there. From just now. Is there breakfast?

#### `a11-12-night-done`

_In the morning, Pooh sets out a pot of honey._  
_The very best kind._  
_The night is over. The sun is up._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): day and night  
> _At night it is dark, and many of us sleep._  
> _In the morning the sun comes up, and it is day again._  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed the change from night to morning._


#### `a11-12-breakfast`

_Tigger takes a big mouthful of honey._  
**Tigger**: Yuck. It sticks to my whiskers.  
_Pooh tries to look sorry. He has the rest himself._  
_At Piglet’s, Tigger tries a haycorn._  
**Tigger**: They are all corners. Tiggers do not do corners.  
_At Eeyore’s, Tigger tries a thistle._  
**Tigger**: Ow! Prickly! That is a punishment!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): describing words: sticky and prickly  
> _Honey sticks to everything. A thistle pricks. Which word means ow, it pricks?_  
> - ✅ Prickly → Yes! Prickly. Sharp little points.
> - Sticky → Sticky is the honey. The thistle is prickly.
> _For grown-ups: Used the describing words sticky and prickly._

**Eeyore**: Some of us eat them every day. We hardly complain.  

#### `a11-12-breakfast-done`

**Pooh**: Only Kanga is left. She might have something.  
_Tigger has tried three things. Honey, haycorns, thistles._  
_(Hold up three fingers. One more try!)_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count the tries to 3  
> _First honey. Next haycorns. Last thistles._  
> _One, two, three tries. Tigger is a brave eater._  
> Check: `edu:count:breakfast-tries:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three tries and used first, next and last._


#### `a11-12-malt`

_At Kanga’s house, Roo is having his medicine._  
**Roo**: Do I have to? It is brown and sticks to the spoon.  
**Kanga**: Just one spoonful, dear. It makes you big and strong.  
_Tigger sniffs. He takes the whole spoonful!_  
**Tigger**: That is it! That is a Tigger breakfast!  
**Roo**: He can have mine! Always!  
**Kanga**: Then he had better stay. I will fetch another spoon.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): different living things eat different food  
> _Pooh likes honey. Eeyore eats thistles. Tigger likes malt._  
> _Real animals eat different foods too. Bees drink flower juice. Donkeys eat plants._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that different animals eat different foods._


#### `a11-12-malt-done`

_So Tigger lives at Kanga’s from then on._  
_He has malt for breakfast, dinner and tea._  
_He tried and tried until he found what suited him._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, notice): keep trying until you find what suits you  
> _Tigger did not give up after honey. Or haycorns. Or thistles._  
> _Trying again is a brave thing to do. Soon he found his breakfast._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that trying again until you find what suits you is brave._

## A11-13. The Search for Small

- `a11-13-s1`: Get your orders from Captain Rabbit. · _Rabbit has a list and a pencil._
- `a11-13-s2`: Search by the Six Pine Trees, where the old pit is. · _Walk with Pooh. Mind the pit._
- `a11-13-s3`: Help everyone out of the pit, and look closely at Pooh. · _Take one of Pooh’s paws._

#### `a11-13-orders`

_Rabbit is busy, and likes it. He has a list._  
**Rabbit**: Small is missing. One of my friends. A very small beetle.  
**Pooh**: What does Small look like?  
**Rabbit**: Small.  
**Pooh**: Ah. That helps.  
**Rabbit**: Look under things. That is called being Thorough.  
_Your Nubbin looks under a leaf at once._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: which is smaller?  
> _Which is smaller: a beetle, or a bear?_  
> - ✅ A beetle → Yes! A beetle is tiny. A bear is much bigger.
> - A bear → A bear is big. A beetle is smaller. Smaller still: Small!
> _For grown-ups: Compared two animals by size._


**Choices**

- **Salute.**
    - **Rabbit**: Good. Someone here understands organisation.
- **Ask how small, exactly.**
    - **Rabbit**: Smaller than that. No. Smaller.
- **Start looking straight away.**
    - Your Nubbin is already under a stone.

#### `a11-13-pit`

_Pooh walks along thinking about honey._  
_You remember the old pit. A moment too late._  
_Whump! Pooh is gone._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): things fall down: gravity pulls  
> _Pooh walks into the pit and falls. What pulls him down?_  
> - ✅ Gravity, a pull towards the ground → Yes! Gravity pulls everything down.
> - Piglet → Poor Piglet is only underneath. Gravity did the pulling.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that gravity pulls things down._

**Piglet**: Help! Something fell on me! A Heffalump!  
**Pooh**: It is only me.  
_You look over the edge. Pooh is in the pit._  
_Piglet is under Pooh._  
**Piglet**: I was searching. Under things.  

#### `a11-13-pit-done`

_Christopher Robin comes to the edge of the pit._  
_He looks. Then he sits down to laugh._  
_Pooh and Piglet laugh too, after a bit._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): laughing with someone, not at them  
> _When everyone laughs together, it feels warm._  
> _Laughing at someone can hurt. Laughing with them is kind._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard the difference between laughing with and laughing at someone._


#### `a11-13-small`

**Christopher Robin**: Out you come. Take my hand, Pooh. Keeper, take his paw.  
_You heave. Up comes Pooh, and up comes Piglet._  
_Your Nubbin climbs up Pooh to help. It stops and stares._  
_A tiny beetle sits in Pooh’s fur._  
**Christopher Robin**: Pooh! You found Small!  

> **Lesson** (science, do): a beetle has six legs  
> _Look closely at Small. A beetle is an insect. Every insect has six legs._  
> _(Count them on your fingers: one, two, three, four, five, six.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:beetle-legs:6`
> _For grown-ups: Learned that insects have six legs and counted to six._

**Pooh**: Where was he?  
**Christopher Robin**: On you.  

#### `a11-13-complete`

**Rabbit**: Found! By my search. Well done, me.  
_Small says nothing, being a beetle._  
**Pooh**: I found him without looking. That is the easiest way.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): working together to find a friend  
> _Rabbit, Pooh, Piglet, Christopher Robin and you all helped._  
> _When friends go looking together, things get found._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that friends can find things together._

_Your Nubbin looks under every leaf on the way home._  

## A11-14. Up a Tree

- `a11-14-s1`: Follow Tigger and Roo into the Forest. · _They went to the tall pines with a bag of sandwiches._
- `a11-14-s2`: Hold one corner of the tunic while Tigger jumps. · _Pull your corner tight. Do not let go._

#### `a11-14-climb`

_Tigger takes Roo for a walk, with malt sandwiches._  
**Roo**: Can Tiggers climb trees?  
**Tigger**: Tiggers are the best tree-climbers!  
_Up goes Tigger, with Roo on his back. Whoosh!_  
_Then Tigger looks down. He looks for a long time._  
**Tigger**: Up is easy. Down is not their best thing.  
**Roo**: We are stuck! Is it lovely? We are up a tree!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): asking for help when you cannot get down  
> _Tigger cannot get down. What is a good thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Call for help → Yes! Calling for help is the safe thing to do.
> - Jump → Jumping could hurt. Calling for help is safer.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to call for help rather than jump when stuck up high._


**Choices**

- **Call up that help is coming.**
    - **Tigger**: Good! Tiggers are not worried. But do hurry.
- **Send your Nubbin up to sit with them.**
    - Your Nubbin climbs to the lowest branch, and sits there for company.
- **Run for Christopher Robin.**
    - You run. Pooh and Piglet are already coming.

#### `a11-14-climb-done`

_Soon everyone stands at the bottom of the pine._  
_They all look up._  
_(Point up. Point down. Up is high. Down is low.)_  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): cats climb up easily and need help down  
> _Cats do this too. They climb up fast, and then find coming down hard._  
> _Their claws curve the wrong way for going down. They need a little help._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that cats climb up easily but may need help coming down._


#### `a11-14-tunic`

_Christopher Robin holds out his tunic, like a sheet._  
_Everyone takes a corner._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, do): a square has four corners  
> _The tunic is flat and square. (Point to each corner.)_  
> _One, two, three, four corners. Four friends hold four corners._  
> Check: `edu:count:corners:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted the four corners of a square._

**Christopher Robin**: Pull it tight, Keeper. Pooh, yours is sagging.  
**Pooh**: It is not sagging. It is having a little sit-down.  
_Roo jumps, boing! He bounces out, and in again._  
_Tigger thinks about jumping for a long, long time._  
_You hold your corner. Your arms ache, but you do not let go._  
_Then Tigger jumps, all at once._  

#### `a11-14-tunic-done`

_Crash! Everyone falls in a heap._  
**Eeyore**: Thank you. I was quite comfortable down here.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): waiting for someone to feel brave  
> _Tigger needed a long time to feel brave. You waited. You did not rush._  
> _Being patient with a friend is a way of being kind._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that being patient while a friend feels brave is kind._

_Eeyore is at the bottom of the heap. He is fine._  

#### `a11-14-complete`

**Tigger**: Did you see me? Tiggers can jump out of trees. Easily.  
**Christopher Robin**: Let us say it is a thing they do with help.  
_Christopher Robin puts his tunic back on._  
_It has a Tigger-shaped stretch now._  
_Your Nubbin cannot get down its branch either. It has to be lifted._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): what happened first, next and last  
> _Tigger climbed up first. Then he got stuck. What happened last?_  
> - ✅ He jumped into the tunic → Yes! First up, next stuck, last jump!
> - He flew home → Tigger cannot fly. Last, he jumped into the tunic.
> _For grown-ups: Put the events of a story in order: first, next, last._


## A11-15. The Note on the Door

- `a11-15-s1`: Go with Rabbit to Christopher Robin’s house. · _Rabbit is off to tell Christopher Robin what to do._
- `a11-15-s2`: Ask Owl what the note means. · _Take the note to Owl’s tree._
- `a11-15-s3`: Ask Eeyore, who has been learning something with sticks. · _Eeyore stands over three sticks._

#### `a11-15-note`

_Rabbit wakes up feeling important._  
**Rabbit**: I shall tell Christopher Robin what to do today.  
_But Christopher Robin is not at home._  
_A note is pinned to his door. The spelling wobbles._  
**Rabbit**: Backson? What is a Backson? Gone out with a Backson?  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): sound out a word: back-son  
> _Sound it out slowly: back… son. What does it sound like?_  
> - ✅ Back soon → Yes! Back soon! Christopher Robin spelled it by sound.
> - A big animal → Say it slowly again: back… son. It sounds like back soon.
> _For grown-ups: Sounded out a wobbly word and found it said back soon._

**Rabbit**: I must ask Owl. Owl can read.  

**Choices**

- **Read the note again, slowly.**
    - You read it again, and it is no clearer. Some notes are like that.
- **Ask Rabbit if he has ever seen a Backson.**
    - **Rabbit**: Certainly not. But that is what a Backson would want me to say.
- **Let your Nubbin sniff the note.**
    - Your Nubbin sniffs it. It smells of breakfast and pencil.

#### `a11-15-owl`

**Owl**: Ah. Let me see.  
_Owl reads the note upside down. Then the right way up._  
**Owl**: A perfectly ordinary message. He has gone out with a Backson.  
**Rabbit**: What does a Backson look like?  
**Owl**: Large, I should think.  
**Owl**: I know my days. Tuesday. T, U, E… there is an S somewhere.  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): the order of the days of the week  
> _Owl is trying to spell Tuesday. Which day comes after Tuesday?_  
> - ✅ Wednesday → Yes! Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.
> - Monday → Monday comes before Tuesday. After Tuesday comes Wednesday.
> _For grown-ups: Named the day after Tuesday._

_Your Nubbin cannot spell anything. It looks at Owl with respect._  

#### `a11-15-owl-done`

**Rabbit**: Eeyore might have seen it. He sees most things.  
_Owl does not always spell every word right._  
_Nobody does. That is how we learn._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, notice): mistakes help us learn  
> _Owl is clever, and still gets some words wobbly._  
> _Mistakes are not bad. They help us learn, one try at a time._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that mistakes help us learn._


#### `a11-15-a`

_Eeyore stands over three sticks on the ground._  
_Two lean together at the top. One goes across the middle._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): making the letter A out of lines  
> _The letter A is made of three lines. Two lean together at the top._  
> _One goes across the middle. Make an A with three sticks, or three fingers._  
> Check: `edu:build:letter:A`
> _For grown-ups: Built the letter A from three lines._

**Eeyore**: Do you know what that is? An A! I made it.  
**Rabbit**: Of course it is an A. Everybody knows that.  
_Rabbit says it airily. Eeyore’s ears go down._  
**Eeyore**: Christopher Robin taught me. He goes out in the mornings now, to learn things.  
**Rabbit**: Learn? Then the Backson is… oh.  
_Rabbit stands very still. It is the first time today he is not busy._  

#### `a11-15-a-done`

**Eeyore**: Somebody has to look after the A. In case he forgets it.  
_Eeyore’s ears are up again._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying something kind about someone’s work  
> _Eeyore is proud of his A. What is a kind thing to say?_  
> - ✅ Well done, Eeyore! → Yes! Kind words help someone feel proud.
> - That is easy → Easy things can still be hard to learn. “Well done” is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Chose kind words to say about a friend’s work._

_He is proud of his A. He worked hard on it._  

#### `a11-15-complete`

_Christopher Robin comes home at lunchtime, with ink on his fingers._  
**Christopher Robin**: Hello! Did you see my note? I said I would be back soon.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, notice): wobbly spelling is how we start writing  
> _Back soon. We could read it, even with wobbly letters._  
> _Everyone starts to write by listening for sounds. Wobbly spelling is a good start._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wobbly spelling is a good way to start writing._

_He is. Rabbit walks home slowly, thinking about mornings._

## A11-16. Sticks on the Bridge

- `a11-16-s1`: Watch Pooh invent a game on the bridge. · _Pooh is on the little wooden bridge with a fir-cone._
- `a11-16-s2`: Play the stick game with everyone on the bridge. · _Drop your stick on “now”. Run to the other side._
- `a11-16-s3`: Help Pooh wash Eeyore to the bank. · _Help lift the big stone. Drop it beside Eeyore, not on him._

#### `a11-16-cone`

_Pooh crosses the bridge with a fir-cone._  
_He trips over nothing, and plop! The cone falls in the river._  
**Pooh**: Bother.  
_He runs to the other side. The cone comes out from under the bridge!_  
**Pooh**: I dropped it on that side. It came out on this one.  

> **Lesson** (science, ask): which way a stream flows  
> _Pooh drops the cone on one side. Where does it come out?_  
> - ✅ On the other side, with the water → Yes! The stream carries things along, under the bridge.
> - Back where it started → Not quite. A stream flows one way, and carries the cone with it.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a stream carries things in the direction it flows._

_He drops two cones at once, a big one and a small one._  
_That is how the stick game begins._  

#### `a11-16-game`

_Soon everyone plays: Pooh, Piglet, Rabbit, Roo, you and your Nubbin._  
**Christopher Robin**: Everybody drop on “now”. Then run to the other side.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): fair rules: everyone starts together  
> _Everybody drops on “now”. Nobody gets a head start._  
> _Starting together is a fair rule. Fair rules help everyone enjoy the game._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that starting together is a fair rule in a game._

_Your Nubbin drops its stick. Then it drops itself in, too!_  
_It swims beside its stick, nudging it, enjoying the wet._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): the middle of a stream flows fastest  
> _Near the bank, the stream is slow. In the middle, it is fast._  
> _Whoosh! A stick in the fast middle wins._  
> _(Drop one near the edge, one in the middle.)_  
> Check: `edu:drop:stick:middle-of-stream`
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a stream flows fastest in the middle, so a stick there wins._

**Roo**: That is not fair! Can I do that?  
**Christopher Robin**: No, Roo.  
**Pooh**: I think it is fair. Nothing says you cannot go with your stick.  
_Your Nubbin’s stick comes out first. It shakes itself all over Piglet._  
**Piglet**: Woozles shake like that. I am nearly sure.  

**Choices**

- **Let it count.**
    - **Pooh**: It counts. It is my game, so I say.
- **Say it should not count.**
    - **Pooh**: Then it won the next best thing, which is getting wet on purpose.
- **Drop your own stick and run.**
    - Your stick comes out last. Some sticks like the view.

#### `a11-16-eeyore`

_Something big and grey floats out from under the bridge._  
_It is Eeyore, on his back, upside down. He looks calm._  
**Eeyore**: Do not mind me. I am upside down in a river. It is restful.  
**Christopher Robin**: Eeyore, what are you doing there?  
**Eeyore**: Floating. Not by choice.  
**Pooh**: A big stone makes a wave. A wave pushes him to the bank.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: heavier and lighter  
> _The stone is very big. Is it heavier than a leaf, or lighter?_  
> - ✅ Heavier → Yes! The stone is heavy. That is why it takes three to lift.
> - Lighter → A leaf is light. The stone is heavier. It takes three to lift.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a stone and a leaf: heavier and lighter._

_You help Pooh lift the stone. Your Nubbin pushes from underneath._  
**Pooh**: Now!  
_Splash! A great wave rolls Eeyore over, and he walks out._  

#### `a11-16-bounced`

**Eeyore**: I was bounced. Into the river. Tigger bounced me.  
_Tigger arrives. He says he only coughed._  
_Everyone looks at Tigger. Tigger looks at the sky._  
**Tigger**: Just a cough. A big Tigger cough.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying sorry when you have bumped someone  
> _Eeyore got bounced into the river. What would help him feel better?_  
> - ✅ Tigger says, “Sorry, Eeyore” → Yes! A real sorry helps someone feel seen.
> - Everyone looks away → Looking away does not help. A kind sorry does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how saying sorry helps someone feel better._

**Eeyore**: Some coughs are bouncier than others. That is all I am saying.  

#### `a11-16-complete`

_Afterwards everyone plays again, Eeyore too, dripping._  
_He wins twice and says it does not count._  
**Pooh**: The best thing about this game is you can play for ever.  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, do): first, second and last  
> _Drop three sticks. Watch them come out._  
> _Which comes out first? Which is second? Which is last? (Point to each.)_  
> Check: `edu:order:sticks:first-second-last`
> _For grown-ups: Put three sticks in order: first, second and last._

_Your Nubbin watches the water go under. Same water, new water._  
**Christopher Robin**: You could have a bridge like this at home. Any stream will do.  

## A11-17. A Game in the Mist

- `a11-17-s1`: Hear Rabbit’s plan, and choose whom to walk with. · _Your choice decides where you are when the mist comes down._
- `a11-17-s2`: Get through the mist. · _Stay close to whoever you are with. Listen._

#### `a11-17-plan`

**Rabbit**: Tigger is very bouncy. He bounces on everybody.  
**Rabbit**: Here is my plan. A game of hide-and-seek, in the mist.  
**Pooh**: Why?  
**Rabbit**: So Tigger has a quiet rest. We hide, and he seeks.  
**Piglet**: That is not very kind.  
_A mist is coming up from the river, white and soft._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, notice): mist is tiny drops of water in the air  
> _Mist is tiny drops of water floating in the air near the ground._  
> _It is like a soft, low cloud. It makes things hard to see._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that mist is tiny drops of water in the air._

**Tigger**: A walk! Tiggers love walks!  

**Choices**

- **Go with Rabbit.**
    - **Rabbit**: Good. Someone sensible. Keep up, and keep quiet.
- **Stay with Tigger.**
    - **Tigger**: Hooray! Tiggers like company.

#### `a11-17-plan-done`

_Into the mist they go. Rabbit leads._  
_Tigger bounces round the outside of everybody._  
_The Forest goes soft and white._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): a plan should be kind to everyone  
> _Piglet said the plan was not very kind. He was right to say so._  
> _A good plan asks: how would I feel?_  
> _If it would make a friend lonely, it is not kind._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a good plan is kind to everyone, and it is okay to say when it is not._


#### `a11-17-mist`

_At the top of the Forest, in a hollow, Rabbit whispers, “Now!”_  
_They duck behind a bank. Tigger bounces on, with you._  
**Tigger**: Where is everybody? Hello?  
**Tigger**: They must be lost. Poor things.  
_At Kanga’s, Pooh and Piglet arrive, damp. Rabbit is not with them._  
**Tigger**: Tiggers never get lost. I will fetch him!  
_He bounces into the white. You follow, holding your Nubbin close._  

> **Lesson** (health, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): if you are lost, stay still and call out  
> _If you are lost, here is the rule: stop, stay put, and call out._  
> _Do not wander off. A grown-up will find you faster if you stay still._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned the safety rule: if lost, stop, stay put and call out._


#### `a11-17-found`

_You hear a small voice in a hollow, saying, “Hello?” Very bravely._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): in mist we hear further than we see  
> _In the mist it is hard to see. What helps you find a friend?_  
> - ✅ Listening → Yes! Ears help when eyes cannot see far.
> - Running fast → Running can get you more lost. Listening helps you find a friend.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that listening helps when it is hard to see._

**Tigger**: Rabbit! There you are! Tiggers are good at finding!  
_Rabbit comes out. For once, he has no plan._  
**Rabbit**: Tigger. Oh, Tigger. I am glad to see you.  

#### `a11-17-complete`

_Tigger takes everyone home, bouncing, by a short way._  
**Rabbit**: He is still very bouncy. Too bouncy.  
_Rabbit says it quietly. He does not quite mean it any more._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, notice): characters can change in a story  
> _First Rabbit was cross with Tigger. Now he is glad of him._  
> _In stories, characters can change. (Make a cross face. Now a glad face.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a character changed from cross to glad._

**Tigger**: Tiggers do not get lost. Tiggers find.  

## A11-18. A Very Grand Thing

- `a11-18-s3`: Help Eeyore find a new house for Owl. · _Follow Eeyore through the Forest._

#### `a11-18-wind`

_It is a very windy day. Piglet’s ears stream out behind him._

> _A breeze is a soft wind. A blustery day has big, gusty puffs._  
> _A gale is a very strong wind. Today is blustery._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned the weather words breeze, blustery and gale._

**Piglet**: What if a tree fell on us, Pooh?

**Owl**: My house is on its side. This has never happened.  

**Choices**

- **Look for a way out.**

    - **Piglet**: Th-thank you. I am not frightened. My hand is.

#### `a11-18-wind-done`

_Everyone looks at Piglet._

> _In a strong, blustery wind, where is the safest place to be?_  
> - ✅ Indoors, away from trees → Yes! Trees can drop branches in a strong wind.
> - Under a big tree → Careful! Branches can fall. Stay indoors, away from trees.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to stay indoors and away from trees in strong wind._

_(Point to the smallest friend.)_

> _Piglet feels scared, and he goes anyway. What does brave mean?_  
> - ✅ Doing it even when you feel scared → Yes! Piglet was brave. Brave is not the same as not scared.
> - Never feeling scared → Everyone feels scared sometimes. Brave means going on anyway.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that being brave means acting even when you feel scared._

> _Different animals live in different places. Squirrels, birds, and owls too._
