## A11-19. The Rissolution

- `a11-19-s1`: Go to the meeting Rabbit has called, and sign the Rissolution. · _Everyone is at Pooh Corner. Sign at the bottom, any way you like._
- `a11-19-s2`: Take the Rissolution to Christopher Robin. · _Walk with everyone to his door._

#### `a11-19-meeting`

_Soon Christopher Robin will be somewhere else, most of the time._  
_Nobody says so. But everybody knows._  
_Everyone feels sad. Sad is allowed._  
**Rabbit**: A Meeting has been called. By me. Eeyore has written a poem.  
**Eeyore**: A Rissolution. Do not expect much.  
_Eeyore reads it. It rhymes in places, and it says: we will miss you._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, notice): poems often rhyme  
> _Eeyore’s poem rhymes in places. Rhymes are words that end the same way._  
> _Moon and spoon rhyme. Pot and lot rhyme. What rhymes with cat?_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that poems often rhyme and gave rhyming words._

_Nobody laughs. Even Tigger stands still._  
**Piglet**: It is a very good poem, Eeyore.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when you feel sad about a goodbye  
> _Everyone feels sad. What could help?_  
> - ✅ Make something kind, together → Yes! Making a poem for him was a loving thing.
> - Pretend not to be sad → Sad feelings need room. Sharing them, or making something, helps.
> - Hide away → Being together helps more. Friends can be sad together.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about feeling sad and what helps: sharing and making something kind._

**Rabbit**: Now everybody signs their name at the bottom.  

**Choices**

- **Sign your name.**
    - You sign it, in your best letters, under Piglet’s.
- **Let your Nubbin sign with a paw.**
    - Your Nubbin presses an inky paw down. Crooked, and its own.
- **Help Pooh with his letters.**
    - **Pooh**: P, O, O, H. It looks right. It looks like me.

#### `a11-19-signed`

_Tigger signs next to you. His T bounces off the edge._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): the first letter of a name: T for Tigger  
> _Tigger signs his name. Which letter does Tigger start with?_  
> - ✅ T → Yes! T for Tigger. Tuh, tuh, Tigger!
> - P → P is for Pooh and Piglet. Tigger starts with T.
> _For grown-ups: Matched Tigger’s name to its first letter, T._

**Tigger**: Is he coming back? He is. Isn’t he?  
_Nobody answers. Tigger bounces once, very small._  
_(Grown-up: you can say, “I do not know, but he loves you all.”)_  

#### `a11-19-scroll`

_Rabbit rolls up the scroll. A blue ribbon is already round it._  
**Eeyore**: I kept it in my pot. It is a Friend ribbon. He will know.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): keeping a gift safe shows it mattered  
> _Eeyore kept the ribbon safe in his pot, all this time._  
> _Keeping a gift safe is a way of saying: you matter to me._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that looking after a gift shows the giver they matter._

_Everyone walks to Christopher Robin’s door._  
_Nobody wants to go first._  
_Eeyore goes first, because it is his poem._  
**Christopher Robin**: What is this?  
**Eeyore**: A Rissolution. From all of us. You read it.  
_Christopher Robin reads it to the end, and all the names._  
**Christopher Robin**: Thank you. All of you.  

#### `a11-19-scroll-done`

_Then everyone goes quietly, one by one, until only Pooh is left._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, notice): one by one: counting down to one  
> _One by one means one at a time. (Hold up five fingers.)_  
> _Fold them down: five, four, three, two, one. One is left: Pooh._  
> _For grown-ups: Counted down from five to one, one at a time._

_You wait by the gate with your Nubbin._  
_Nobody asked you to. It seems the right place to be._  

#### `a11-19-complete`

_After a while Christopher Robin comes out. Pooh is with him._  
**Christopher Robin**: We are walking to the top of the Forest. Come some of the way?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): how to say goodbye kindly  
> _A friend is going somewhere new. What is a kind thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Tell them you will remember them → Yes! Telling someone you will remember them is a lovely gift.
> - Say nothing at all → Words, a hug or a card can help. Saying you will remember is best.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about kind ways to say goodbye to a friend._

_Your Nubbin is already on its feet._  

## A11-20. The Ring of Trees

- `a11-20-s1`: Walk with Christopher Robin and Pooh to the top of the Forest. · _Walk a little way behind them, up to the ring of trees._
- `a11-20-s2`: Wait at the edge of the circle while they talk. · _Stay at the edge. This part is theirs._

#### `a11-20-climb`

_Christopher Robin and Pooh walk up through the Forest._  
_You walk a little way behind, with your Nubbin._  
**Christopher Robin**: Pooh. Of all the things there are, what do you like best?  
**Pooh**: Coming to yours. And you saying there is honey.  
**Christopher Robin**: I like that too. But best of all is doing Nothing.  
**Pooh**: What does Nothing look like?  
**Christopher Robin**: It is going out for no reason. And the whole day is yours.  
**Pooh**: Oh. I do that a lot.  
_At the top is a ring of trees, sixty-something of them._  
_Nobody can count them. It changes every time._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count a circle: mark where you started  
> _In a circle, there is no first one and no last one._  
> _Tie a ribbon on one tree. Count round till you reach the ribbon._  
> Check: `edu:count:trees:circle`
> _For grown-ups: Learned to count a circle by marking where you started._


**Choices**

- **Count the trees.**
    - You count sixty-three, then sixty-four. Your Nubbin gives up at four, content.
- **Do not count them. Just look.**
    - You just look. It seems a place that would rather not be counted.

#### `a11-20-knight`

_At the edge of the circle, you stop. Your Nubbin sits down._  
_Christopher Robin and Pooh go into the middle, and sit._  
_They talk about kings and queens, and a place called Brazil._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): Brazil is a country in South America  
> _Brazil is a real place on the map. It is in South America._  
> _A map shows where places are. (Can you find the top of a map?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Brazil is a country in South America._

_Pooh listens. He does not mind not knowing._  
**Christopher Robin**: Pooh. Stand up.  
_Christopher Robin touches Pooh’s shoulders with a stick._  
**Christopher Robin**: Arise, Sir Pooh. Knight of the Forest, and my truest friend.  
_Then he is quiet for a long time, looking at the trees._  
**Christopher Robin**: Pooh, will you remember me? Always?  
**Pooh**: I will. I promise.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): a promise is words you keep; remembering is how love stays  
> _A promise is something you say and then keep._  
> _Remembering someone is a way of keeping them close, wherever they are._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a promise is kept and that remembering keeps people close._

**Christopher Robin**: If I am not here so much, it is not because of you.  
**Pooh**: I shall know. Even if I do not know why.  

#### `a11-20-knight-done`

_Christopher Robin laughs, and jumps up, and holds out his hand._  
_Pooh takes it._  
**Christopher Robin**: Come on, Pooh.  
**Pooh**: Where?  
**Christopher Robin**: Anywhere.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): quiet time with a friend helps us feel calm  
> _Doing Nothing together is a lovely way to rest._  
> _Quiet, slow time helps our bodies feel calm and our hearts feel full._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that quiet time with a friend helps us rest and feel calm._


#### `a11-20-complete`

_Christopher Robin and Pooh walk off together._  
_You do not follow. This part is theirs._  
_Christopher Robin gave back the blue ribbon. Your Nubbin ties it on a tree._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, ask): a marker shows where you started counting  
> _The ribbon is on the first tree. Why is that handy for counting?_  
> - ✅ It shows where we started → Yes! When we get back to the ribbon, we know we are done.
> - It makes the tree pretty → Pretty, yes! But the best reason: it marks where we started counting.
> _For grown-ups: Understood that a marker shows where counting started._

_A boy and his Bear are playing in that ring of trees._  
_The page closes gently, like a door nobody bangs._  
_You are back in the Grove, with the atlas on your knee._  
_By the stream is a little bridge. A blue ribbon is on its rail._  

## A12-1. The Troll’s Mirror

- `a12-01-s1`: Climb the stairs and meet Grandmother. · _Touch the page. Then go up the attic stairs._
- `a12-01-s2`: Hold the candle for Grandmother’s shadow-show. · _Stand by the wall. Keep the candle still._
- `a12-01-s3`: Watch the troll’s mirror break. · _Keep the candle steady to the end of the show._

#### `a12-01-arrive`

_Nova’s atlas opens at a page made of cut paper._  
_Rooftops! Chimneys! Two attic windows, side by side._  
_You climb a steep wooden stair with your Nubbin._  
**Grandmother**: There you are, lodger. Your bed is by the chimney.  
**Grandmother**: Mind your head on the beam. Everyone bumps it.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): above and below  
> _Where is the beam? Above your head, or under your feet?_  
> - ✅ Above my head → Yes! Look up. The beam is above you.
> - Under my feet → Look up! The beam is above your head. Mind it.
> _For grown-ups: Practised the position words above and below._

_Across the gutter, a boy and a girl wave. They are Kay and Gerda._  
**Grandmother**: And what is this? It is not a cat.  

**Choices**

- **Tell her it’s a Nubbin.**
    - **Grandmother**: A Nubbin! It can have the end of the bed.
- **Say it’s your friend.**
    - **Grandmother**: Good. Friends are worth a bed.
- **Let your Nubbin bow.**
    - Your Nubbin bows. Boing! It nearly tumbles down.
    - **Grandmother**: Manners. It can stay.

#### `a12-01-arrive-done`

**Grandmother**: That is Kay and Gerda. They live across the gutter.  
**Grandmother**: Each evening there is a story. You hold the candle.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying yes to helping  
> _Grandmother asks you to hold the candle. What do you say?_  
> - ✅ Yes, I will help! → Thank you. Helping is a kind thing to do.
> - No, that is boring. → It might be fun! Helping makes a story go well.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying yes when someone asks for help._


#### `a12-01-show`

_Late summer. Kay and Gerda climb across the gutter._  
_Grandmother has black paper and long scissors. Snip, snip, snip!_  
**Grandmother**: Hold the candle high. Now the wall is a stage.  
_A paper troll steps onto the wall. He holds a thin mirror._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, ask): shadows need light  
> _The troll is a shadow on the wall. What makes a shadow?_  
> - ✅ Paper that blocks the candle light → Yes! The paper blocks the light. That makes a dark shape.
> - Nothing at all → Something blocks the light. Try it: hold your hand in front of a lamp.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a shadow is made when something blocks light._

**Grandmother**: His mirror made good things look small.  
**Grandmother**: And it made ugly things look big.  
**Kay**: I’d like to look in it.  
**Gerda**: I wouldn’t.  

#### `a12-01-show-done`

_Grandmother does the troll’s voice. It is deep and pleased._  
**The Troll**: Ha! See how small good things look in my mirror!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words for feelings  
> _How does the troll feel? Pleased, or sad?_  
> - ✅ Pleased → Yes. He is pleased with his wicked mirror.
> - Sad → Listen to his big laugh. He is pleased, not sad.
> _For grown-ups: Named a character’s feeling from the way he sounded._


#### `a12-01-shards`

**Grandmother**: The troll had a school. His pupils took the mirror everywhere.  
**Grandmother**: Then it slipped from their hands. Crash!  
_Grandmother opens her fingers. Paper snips fall like snow._  
**Grandmother**: It broke into more pieces than people. Some were as small as sand.  
**Grandmother**: A piece in your eye makes things look wrong.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): comparing sizes  
> _Which is smaller: a grain of sand, or a big snip?_  
> - ✅ A grain of sand → Yes! A grain of sand is tiny, tinier than any snip.
> - A big snip → A big snip is bigger. The grain of sand is the smaller one.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two sizes: smaller and bigger._

**Grandmother**: A piece in your heart makes it cold.  
**Kay**: And then what?  
**Grandmother**: Then you need someone to come and fetch you.  

**Choices**

- **Brush the snips off Gerda’s sleeve.**
    - You brush them off. Gerda checks her other sleeve, twice.
- **Catch a snip as it falls.**
    - You catch one. It is only paper. You look at it a long time.
- **Ask who comes to fetch you.**
    - **Grandmother**: Whoever loves you most. They are stubborn about it.

#### `a12-01-shards-done`

_The troll laughs on the wall. Grandmother blows out the candle._  
_In the dark, something glints once. Then it is gone._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, notice): no light, no shadows  
> **Grandmother**: Whoosh, the candle is out. No light means no shadows.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that we need light to see, and that shadows need light too._


#### `a12-01-complete`

_Later you lie in the bed by the chimney._  
_Two small rose trees bloom in the dark across the gutter._  
_Your Nubbin curls up on your feet._  
_Rain begins to fall. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the syllables  
> _(Clap along: pit, ter, pat, ter. Four claps!)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:pitter-patter`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the parts of the words pitter-patter._


## A12-2. Two Windows

- `a12-02-s1`: Water the roses in the gutter boxes. · _Climb out to the gutter with the watering can._
- `a12-02-s2`: Warm a coin and melt a peephole in the frosty window. · _Warm a coin on the stove. Press it on the glass._
- `a12-02-s3`: Look out of your window that night. · _Wait quietly at your peephole._

#### `a12-02-roses`

_In the morning you see two attics. Their roofs nearly touch._  
_A gutter runs between them. Peas hang over the boxes._  
_In each box grows a rose tree. Together they make an arch._  
**Gerda**: You’re tallest. Water the top of the arch. Not too much!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): what plants need  
> _What do roses need to grow?_  
> - ✅ Water and sunshine → Yes! Water and sunshine make roses grow.
> - Only sweets → Roses like water and sunshine. Not sweets!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants need water and light to live._

**Kay**: Gran says the roses will last until we’re old.  
_Your Nubbin tries to help. It sits in the watering can._  

**Choices**

- **Water the top of the arch.**
    - Drip, drip! A drop falls on Kay’s head. He pretends not to notice.
- **Give the peas a bit extra.**
    - **Gerda**: See? They are cheering up.
    - **Kay**: They look the same.
- **Lift your Nubbin out of the can.**
    - Your Nubbin comes out dripping. Gerda dries it. All is forgiven.

#### `a12-02-roses-done`

**Gerda**: In winter we can’t climb across.  
**Gerda**: We go down all our stairs and up all the others.  
**Kay**: It takes years!  
**Gerda**: It takes two minutes.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): longer and shorter  
> _Which way is shorter? Across the gutter, or down all the stairs?_  
> - ✅ Across the gutter → Yes! The gutter is the short way. It takes no time.
> - Down all the stairs → The stairs are the long way. The gutter is shorter.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a short path with a long path._


#### `a12-02-frost`

_Winter comes. Ice ferns grow on the windows._  
_Kay and Gerda warm copper coins on the stove._  
_They press a coin on the glass. The ice melts into a round hole._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-4, ask): warm things melt ice  
> _What melts the ice on the window?_  
> - ✅ A warm coin → Yes! Warm things melt ice.
> - A cold spoon → A cold spoon keeps ice icy. A warm coin melts it.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that something warm melts ice._

_Through the hole, a bright eye looks across the snow._  
**Grandmother**: Look at the white bees swarming in the snow.  
**Kay**: Do they have a queen?  
**Grandmother**: They do. Some nights she looks in at windows.  
**Kay**: I’d put her on the hot stove! She would melt.  

**Choices**

- **Tell Kay that’s unkind to a guest.**
    - **Kay**: She isn’t a guest. She’s weather.
- **Ask Grandmother if she has seen her.**
    - **Grandmother**: Once or twice, through the glass. Not close.
- **Look out of your own peephole.**
    - Snowflakes whirl past by the thousand. One seems to look back.

#### `a12-02-frost-done`

_Grandmother smooths Kay’s hair._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): kind wishes  
> _Kay wished the queen would melt. Is that a kind wish?_  
> - ✅ No, it isn’t kind → Right. Unkind wishes make hearts cold. Kind words keep them warm.
> - Yes, it is kind → Hmm. Wishing someone harm is not kind. Kind words keep hearts warm.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why a kind wish is better than an unkind one._

_She tells a story about a goose instead._  

#### `a12-02-night`

_That night you can’t sleep. Your Nubbin looks out the peephole._  
_Across the gutter, Kay stands on a chair at his window._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): seasons and weather  
> _Snow is falling. Which season is it? Summer, or winter?_  
> - ✅ Winter → Yes! Snow comes in the cold winter.
> - Summer → Summer is warm. Snow comes in winter.
> _For grown-ups: Linked snow to winter weather._

_A big snowflake lands on the flower box. It grows!_  
_It grows into a tall lady made of ice and starlight._  
_She is lovely and cold. Her eyes shine like stars._  
_She looks in at Kay. She waves her hand. Come!_  

**Choices**

- **Knock on your window.**
    - You knock hard. Kay jumps down.
    - The lady is gone. A big white bird flies past.
- **Call Kay’s name.**
    - You call his name. Kay jumps down.
    - The box is empty. Something white flies by, like a big bird.
- **Pull your Nubbin back from the glass.**
    - Your Nubbin is cold right through. It snuggles into your shirt.
    - Kay jumps down. A white bird passes. The box is empty.

#### `a12-02-night-done`

_You sit up until morning._  
_The frost on your window has grown into ferns._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS2-3, notice): frost is ice  
> **Grandmother**: Frost is ice. Water from the air freezes on the cold glass.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that frost is ice that grows on very cold glass._


#### `a12-02-complete`

**Kay**: It was a dream. I dreamed a lady on the box.  
**Gerda**: I dreamed you stood on a chair.  
**Kay**: Well, I wasn’t.  
_Grandmother looks at Kay a little longer than usual._  
_Then the thaw comes. The swallows come back. The roses wake up._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): spring follows winter  
> _The swallows are back and the snow has melted. Which season is it?_  
> - ✅ Spring → Yes! After winter comes spring.
> - Winter → Winter is cold and snowy. Melting snow and swallows mean spring.
> _For grown-ups: Named spring as the season that follows winter._


## A12-3. The Splinter

- `a12-03-s1`: Sit under the rose arch with Kay and Gerda. · _Climb to the gutter. Take the spare stool._
- `a12-03-s2`: Put the rose box straight again. · _Lift the box. Press the earth round the roots._
- `a12-03-s3`: Go out in the snow with Kay. · _Follow Gerda down to the street._

#### `a12-03-arch`

_It is summer. The roses are the best ever._  
_Gerda sings a rose hymn. Kay sings it back._  
_They look at a picture book of animals. Kay does the noises._  
**Kay**: That is an elk. It goes like this.  
**Gerda**: It does not!  
_The church clock begins to strike five._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, ask): count the bongs  
> _Bong, bong, bong, bong, bong. How many bongs did the clock make?_  
> - ✅ Five → Yes! One, two, three, four, five. Five o’clock!
> - Three → Let’s count again: one, two, three, four, five. Five bongs.
> _For grown-ups: Counted five bongs of a clock._

**Kay**: Ow! Something stung my heart. And my eye!  
_You see a glint, smaller than a grain of sand. It is gone._  

**Choices**

- **Look in Kay’s eye.**
    - You look gently. There is nothing there, you think.
- **Hold Kay’s hand.**
    - His hand is warm. Then it is not quite so warm.
- **Call Grandmother.**
    - Grandmother peers in. She finds nothing at all.
    - **Grandmother**: Blink. Again. There. Gone.

#### `a12-03-arch-done`

**Kay**: It’s gone. I think it’s gone.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming feelings  
> _Kay says “Ow!” and looks sad. How does Kay feel?_  
> - ✅ Hurt and worried → Yes. Hurt and worried. It is fine to feel that.
> - Very happy → Look at his face. He is hurt and worried, not happy.
> _For grown-ups: Named a friend’s feelings: hurt and worried._

_It hasn’t gone._  

#### `a12-03-kick`

**Gerda**: Kay? Are you all right?  
**Kay**: Stop crying! It looks silly!  
**Kay**: These roses are ugly. They have worms.  
_He kicks the box. Two roses fall over the edge._  
_You reach for him. But you can’t pull a splinter out of a heart._  
_Kay slams his window. Gerda holds her book close._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): helping a sad friend  
> _Gerda is sad. What helps a sad friend?_  
> - ✅ Sit close and be kind → Yes. Sitting close helps a lot.
> - Tell her to stop crying → That does not help. Sitting close and listening does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what really helps a sad friend._

**Gerda**: He said it is a baby book.  

**Choices**

- **Fetch the two roses back for Gerda.**
    - You fish them back. Gerda puts them in a cup of water.
- **Knock on Kay’s window.**
    - Kay opens it. He pulls a horrible face at you.
    - Then he shuts it.
- **Say nothing. Straighten the box together.**
    - You lift the box together. Your Nubbin pats the earth flat.

#### `a12-03-kick-done`

_The rose tree has lost two flowers and a bit of bark._  
_Roses forgive that, if you leave them be._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): plants can recover  
> **Grandmother**: Give a rose water and sun, and it grows new flowers.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a plant with water and light can grow back._


#### `a12-03-glass`

_All autumn, Kay is clever and unkind. He copies Grandmother’s voice._  
_Everyone laughs. But he copies Gerda too, only the parts that hurt._  
_When snow comes, he runs out with a big glass._  
_He catches snowflakes on his sleeve._  
**Kay**: Look, Gerda! Look how perfect they are!  
_Under the glass each flake is a six-pointed star._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count how many  
> _(Point to the star’s arms and count them. One, two, three, four, five, six!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:snowflake-arms:6`
> _For grown-ups: Counted the six arms of a snowflake._

**Gerda**: Real flowers smell of something.  
**Kay**: That’s what is wrong with them.  

**Choices**

- **Look in the glass.**
    - You look. The flake is lovely, but it feels cold and flat.
- **Throw a snowball at Kay.**
    - Splat! Kay almost laughs. Then he brushes it off, bored.
- **Stand by Gerda.**
    - You stand by Gerda. Your Nubbin leans on her boot.

#### `a12-03-glass-done`

**Kay**: I’m allowed in the big square tomorrow. Gran said.  
**Gerda**: Gran said maybe.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): what “maybe” means  
> _Gran said “maybe”. Does maybe mean yes?_  
> - ✅ No. Maybe means not sure yet → Right. Maybe means we will see.
> - Yes, it means yes → Not quite. Maybe means not sure yet.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that “maybe” means not sure yet._


#### `a12-03-complete`

_That evening Gerda sits on her stool in the cold._  
**Gerda**: He’s still in there. Something is in front of him.  
_You sit down next to her on Kay’s stool._  
_You wait with her. Waiting together is a kind of help._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, do): calm and wait together  
> _(Sit beside a grown-up. Take ten slow breaths together.)_  
> Check: `edu:breathe:slow:10`
> _For grown-ups: Practised sitting calmly beside someone and breathing slowly._


## A12-4. The Big Sledge

- `a12-04-s1`: Follow Kay to the great square. · _Go to the square. Keep Kay in sight._
- `a12-04-s2`: Run after the white sledge. · _Run! Keep going to the town gate._
- `a12-04-s3`: Watch from the hill. · _Stay on the hill. You can’t reach them from here._

#### `a12-04-square`

_Kay comes past with big gloves and his sledge on his back._  
**Kay**: I’m going to the big square!  
**Gerda**: Go with him, please. Keep an eye on him.  
_The square is busy. Bold boys tie sledges to farmers’ carts._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): staying safe on sledges  
> _The boys tie their sledges to moving carts. Is that safe?_  
> - ✅ No, it isn’t safe → Right. A cart can pull you too fast. A little hill is much safer.
> - Yes, it’s safe → A moving cart can pull you too fast. A little hill is safer.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why it is not safe to hitch a sledge to a moving cart._

_A great white sledge comes in. The driver wears white fur._  
_The white driver watches only Kay._  

**Choices**

- **Shout to Kay to stay put.**
    - **Kay**: Mind your own business, lodger!
    - He doesn’t look round. He watches the white sledge.
- **Push through to get hold of his cord.**
    - There are too many boys. The square is suddenly very wide.
- **Pick up your Nubbin. It has gone very still.**
    - It stares at the white sledge. It feels cold, like at the window.

#### `a12-04-square-done`

_Kay holds his cord. He ties a careful knot, tongue between his teeth._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): sledges slide on snow  
> _Which is better for sledging, snow or grass?_  
> - ✅ Snow → Yes! A sledge slides well on smooth snow.
> - Grass → Grass is bumpy and stops a sledge. Smooth snow lets it slide.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sledge slides best on smooth snow._


#### `a12-04-chase`

_The white sledge circles again. Kay ties his sledge to it. Off he goes!_  
_Faster, into the next street. Faster!_  
_The driver nods to Kay kindly, as if they are old friends._  
_You run. Your Nubbin runs ahead. You scoop it up and run faster._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): in front and behind  
> _Your Nubbin runs ahead. Is it in front of you, or behind?_  
> - ✅ In front of me → Yes! It is in front of you.
> - Behind me → Behind is at your back. Your Nubbin is in front, running ahead.
> _For grown-ups: Practised the position words in front and behind._

_Out through the town gate. The snow comes down thick and white._  
**Kay**: Stop! I want to get off!  
_You lose them. Then, from a hill, you see the sledge has stopped._  

#### `a12-04-chase-done`

_The driver stands up. Under the snow is a tall lady, pale and sparkling._  
_It is the lady from the window. It is the Snow Queen._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): who is in the story  
> _Who is driving the white sledge?_  
> - ✅ The Snow Queen → Yes. The lady from the window is the Snow Queen.
> - Grandmother → Grandmother is at home. The driver is the lady from the window.
> _For grown-ups: Named a character from the story._


#### `a12-04-kiss`

**The Snow Queen**: We have come a long way. You are shivering.  
**The Snow Queen**: Creep in under my fur.  
_She wraps Kay in her white bearskin. He sinks in like a snowdrift._  
**The Snow Queen**: Are you still cold?  
_She touches his forehead. It is colder than ice._  
_Now Kay does not feel cold at all._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): all feelings are allowed  
> _Is it okay to feel cold, or sad, sometimes?_  
> - ✅ Yes. All feelings are okay → Yes. Feelings are part of being alive. Sad, cross and cold are fine.
> - No. We should feel nothing → Feelings are allowed. A hug or a friend helps with the hard ones.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how all feelings, even sad ones, are okay._

_Gerda, Grandmother, the roses: Kay forgets them. But you do not._  
_The sledge rises over the forest. A big white moon comes out._  

**Choices**

- **Call his name, as loud as you can.**
    - The wind blows your voice back towards the town, to Gerda.
- **Stand and watch until they’re gone.**
    - You watch till the sledge is a speck, then a star, then nothing.

#### `a12-04-kiss-done`

_You walk back in the dark. The town gate is still open._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): the Moon in the night sky  
> _The Moon shines in the night sky. Its shape changes each month._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the Moon is seen at night and changes shape through the month._

**Gerda**: Then he isn’t lost. He has been taken. That is different.

**Gerda**: No. He hates water. He would never go near the river.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character responds  
> _Everyone says Kay is gone. What does Gerda think?_  
> - ✅ He can still be found → Yes. Gerda keeps hoping, and she will go and look.
> - They are right → Gerda does not agree. She believes Kay can still be found.

## A12-5. The Red Shoes

- `a12-05-s1`: Sit with Gerda through the long winter. · _Find Gerda on her stool by the gutter._
- `a12-05-s2`: Go down to the river with Gerda at dawn. · _Walk with Gerda to the boats in the rushes._
- `a12-05-s3`: Jump into the boat after Gerda. · _Run along the bank and jump!_

#### `a12-05-winter`

_It is a long, dark winter. People stop saying Kay’s name._  
_Only Gerda says it._  
_Then spring comes. The sun is warm on the gutter again._  
**Gerda**: Some people say Kay has died.  
_The sunshine does not believe it. Neither do the swallows._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): signs of spring  
> _The swallows are back. What else says it is spring?_  
> - ✅ Warm sun and new flowers → Yes! Warm sun and new flowers are signs of spring.
> - Snow and ice → Snow and ice come in winter. Spring has warm sun and flowers.
> _For grown-ups: Named signs of spring: warm sun, flowers and returning birds._

**Gerda**: I don’t believe it either.  

**Choices**

- **“Nor do I.”**
    - **You**: Nor do I.
    - **Gerda**: Good. That makes three of us, and the swallows.
- **Remind her: the sledge went north.**
    - **Gerda**: North. Then I will go north. I’ll ask the river first.
- **Sit with her and say nothing.**
    - You sit a long time. A swallow lands and looks at you both.

#### `a12-05-winter-done`

**Gerda**: I’m going to give the river my red shoes.  
**Gerda**: Kay never saw them. They are my best thing.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, ask): a pair is two  
> _Gerda has a pair of red shoes. How many shoes make a pair?_  
> - ✅ Two → Yes! A pair is two. One for each foot.
> - Three → Count her feet: one, two. A pair of shoes is two.
> _For grown-ups: Counted the two shoes in a pair._


#### `a12-05-river`

_At dawn Gerda puts on her new red shoes._  
_She kisses sleeping Grandmother and goes out._  
_You go with her to the river. Your Nubbin is under your arm._  
**Gerda**: River, did you take my friend? I’ll give you my red shoes.  
_The little waves nod. She throws the shoes in._  
_Splash! The waves bring them straight back._  
**Gerda**: I didn’t throw them far enough.  
_There is a boat in the rushes. She climbs in._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): water safety  
> _Who should be with a child near deep water?_  
> - ✅ A grown-up → Yes. A grown-up keeps children safe near water.
> - Nobody → Always have a grown-up near deep water. It keeps you safe.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to stay with a grown-up near deep water._


**Choices**

- **Stay on the bank. It’s her gift to give.**
    - You stay on the bank. It is hers to give.
- **Tell her to be careful.**
    - **Gerda**: I am being careful. Careful and quick.

#### `a12-05-river-done`

_She throws the shoes from the end of the boat._  
_The boat isn’t tied. It slides out of the rushes._  
**Gerda**: Oh!  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): rivers flow downhill to the sea  
> _Rivers flow downhill. They carry things along, all the way to the sea._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that rivers flow downhill towards the sea._


#### `a12-05-boat`

_The boat is already a step from the bank, and gliding._  
_Your Nubbin jumps first. You jump after it._  
_Thump! You land in the bottom of the boat._  
**Gerda**: You came. You didn’t have to.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): being a loyal friend  
> _Gerda is glad you came. What does a good friend do?_  
> - ✅ Helps, and stays close → Yes. A good friend helps and stays close.
> - Goes away when it’s hard → A good friend stays and helps, even when it is hard.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what a good friend does when things are hard._

_The red shoes float behind. They can’t catch up._  

**Choices**

- **Look for an oar.**
    - No oar. Only a can, some rope and an apple. Your Nubbin eats it.
- **Reach for the red shoes.**
    - You stretch over the side. Your fingers brush one shoe. The river takes it.
- **Sit back and let the boat take you.**
    - You sit back. Gerda sits beside you in her stockings.

#### `a12-05-boat-done`

_The banks are lovely: flowers and old trees._  
_Three sheep and two cows graze on the slopes._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add within 10  
> _Three sheep and two cows. How many animals altogether?_  
> - ✅ Five → Yes! Three and two make five.
> - Four → Count them: one, two, three sheep, then four, five cows. Five!
> _For grown-ups: Added three and two to make five._

_There isn’t a single person anywhere._

> _(Point to something red. Now point to something blue.)_  
> Check: `edu:point:colours:red-blue`
> _For grown-ups: Named and pointed to red and blue._

## A12-6. The Garden That Forgets

- `a12-06-s1`: Meet the old woman of the cherry house. · _Let her pull the boat in. Go inside._
- `a12-06-s2`: Spend the summer in the garden. · _Explore the flower beds. Follow your Nubbin._
- `a12-06-s3`: Ask the flowers about Kay. · _Talk to the roses, then the other flowers._

#### `a12-06-cherries`

_An old woman comes out. She wears a big hat with painted flowers._  
**The Old Woman**: You poor little thing. How did you get on this wide river?  
_She pulls the boat in with her stick. She is strong._  
_She gives you cherries, as many as you like._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away within 10  
> _You have three cherries. Your Nubbin eats one. How many are left?_  
> - ✅ Two → Yes! Three, take away one, leaves two.
> - Three → Your Nubbin ate one! Three take away one leaves two.
> _For grown-ups: Took one away from three to make two._

**The Old Woman**: Kay? He hasn’t come by. Don’t be sad. Eat your cherries.  
_She combs Gerda’s hair with a golden comb. Gerda grows sleepy._  
_She isn’t wicked. She just always wanted a little girl._  

**Choices**

- **Have another cherry.**
    - It is the best cherry ever. You forget the second best.
- **Ask her the way north.**
    - **The Old Woman**: North? Nobody goes north. Have a cherry.
    - You forget your question halfway through the cherry.
- **Give a cherry to your Nubbin.**
    - Your Nubbin tucks it in your pocket. One eye stays on the comb.

#### `a12-06-cherries-done`

_While you doze, the old woman goes into the garden._  
_She points her stick at the rose bushes. They sink into the ground._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): roots live under the ground  
> _Plants have roots under the ground. Roots drink water for the plant._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that plants have roots that drink water under the ground._


#### `a12-06-garden`

_The garden has every flower, from every season, all at once._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): flowers bloom in different seasons  
> _In a real garden, snowdrops come in late winter. Roses come in summer._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that different flowers bloom in different seasons._

_Gerda plays here all day. She has stopped asking about Kay._  
_You can’t remember what day it is._  
_Your Nubbin keeps digging at one bare patch by the wall._  
_One day the old woman’s painted hat lies on the bench._  
_Gerda sees a rose painted on the hat._  
**Gerda**: Roses! Where are the roses? There are none here!  

**Choices**

- **Show her where your Nubbin has dug.**
    - You show her the bare patch. Your Nubbin sits tall beside it.
- **Search with her.**
    - You search bed by bed. Your Nubbin sits on a bare patch.

#### `a12-06-garden-done`

_Gerda sits by the bare patch and cries. Her tears fall on the earth._  
_A rose bush comes up, in full flower!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): plants drink water  
> _Gerda’s tears fall on the earth. What do plants drink?_  
> - ✅ Water → Yes! Plants drink water through their roots.
> - Milk → Plants drink water. Milk is for people, not plants!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants take in water through their roots._


#### `a12-06-flowers`

**Gerda**: I’ve been so long! Do you know where Kay is?  
**The Roses**: He isn’t here. We were underground, and he wasn’t there.  
**Gerda**: Thank you!  
_Gerda asks the other flowers, one by one._  
_Each flower is dreaming its own story. None is about Kay._  
**The Bindweed**: There is a castle, and a girl on the balcony. That is my story.  
**Gerda**: Is it about Kay?  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): who a story is about  
> _Is the bindweed’s story about Kay?_  
> - ✅ No. It is about a castle and a girl → Yes. Every flower has its own story.
> - Yes, it is about Kay → Listen again: a castle and a girl on a balcony. Not Kay.
> _For grown-ups: Said who and what a story was about._

**The Bindweed**: It’s my story. It is not about anybody else.  

**Choices**

- **Ask the snowdrop.**
    - **The Snowdrop**: Two girls on a swing blow bubbles. Each bubble is a world. Pop!
    - **Gerda**: A lovely story. But no help.
- **Ask the buttercup.**
    - **The Buttercup**: A granny in a sunny yard. Her granddaughter comes home. That’s enough.
    - **Gerda**: Poor Gran. She is at home without us.
- **Ask the narcissus.**
    - **The Narcissus**: I can see myself! How lovely I smell!
    - **Gerda**: That isn’t about Kay. That isn’t about anyone.

#### `a12-06-flowers-done`

**Gerda**: It’s no good. They only know their own stories.  
**Gerda**: I have to go. I’ve stayed too long.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): keeping a promise to a friend  
> _Gerda remembers her friend. What does she do next?_  
> - ✅ Keeps looking for Kay → Yes. She does not give up on her friend.
> - Stays in the garden → She could stay, but she wants to find Kay. So she goes.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about not giving up on a friend._

> _Leaves turn yellow and fall. Which season is it?_  
> - ✅ Autumn → Yes! Leaves fall in autumn.
> - Spring → In spring, new leaves come out. Falling yellow leaves mean autumn.

#### `a12-07-hedge`

> - Paws → Paws are for cats. A raven flies with wings.
> _For grown-ups: Named wings as the part a bird flies with._

_Gerda tells him everything. Has he seen Kay?_  
**The Raven**: It might be Kay. It might be!

**The Raven**: She has read every newspaper in the world.  
**The Raven**: And forgotten them all again. That is how clever she is.  

**Choices**

    - **The Raven**: Politely! A rare thing. I will go on at once.
- **Ask how a raven knows all this.**
    - **The Raven**: My sweetheart at the palace is tame. She tells me everything. I tell everybody.
- **Let your Nubbin say hello.**
    - Your Nubbin bows. The raven bows lower, so as not to be outdone.

#### `a12-07-hedge-done`

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): what a character wants  
> _What does the princess want? Someone who can…_  
> - ✅ Talk back → Yes! She wants someone who can really talk to her.
> - Stand very still → No, no. Standing still is the boring part. She wants someone who can talk.
> _For grown-ups: Said what a story character wants._


#### `a12-07-boots`

**The Raven**: The papers said: any young man may come and talk to her.  
**The Raven**: Crowds came! But at the silver guards, they went quiet.  
**The Raven**: On the third day came a little fellow, marching up.  
**The Raven**: His eyes shone like yours. His clothes were shabby.  
**Gerda**: That was Kay! I’ve found him!  
**The Raven**: His boots creaked all over the hall. He was not afraid.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhyming words  
> _Which word rhymes with creak? Squeak, or boat?_  
> - ✅ Squeak → Yes! Creak and squeak rhyme.
> - Boat → Say them: creak, squeak. They end the same. Boat does not.
> _For grown-ups: Found a word that rhymes with creak._

**The Raven**: He came to hear how clever she was. They liked each other.  

**Choices**

- **It must be Kay.**
    - **Gerda**: It must be. Kay was always clever. He could do sums in his head.
- **Plenty of boys have creaky boots.**
    - **Gerda**: Not like Kay’s.

> - Run in anyway → Running in could spoil the plan. Waiting calmly is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about waiting calmly when asked._

> - Four → One went dark. Four take away one leaves three.

> _For grown-ups: Heard that a mix of foods is better than too many sweets._

**Gerda**: Goodbye! Goodbye!  
_Gerda keeps her hands in the muff. Your Nubbin keeps them warm._  

## A12-9. The Robber Girl

- `a12-09-s1`: Ride the golden coach through the dark forest. · _Keep your head down when the coach stops._
- `a12-09-s2`: Go into the robbers’ castle. · _Follow the robber girl in, past the dogs._
- `a12-09-s3`: Answer the robber girl. She wants your Nubbin. · _Choose what to say. Either answer is kind and honest._

#### `a12-09-forest`

_The road goes into a dark forest. The golden coach shines like a torch._  
_Robbers jump out, shouting, “Gold!”_  
_The coachman and footmen run off and hide. Nobody is hurt._  
_A girl pushes the old robber woman aside._  
**The Robber Girl**: She’s mine. She can play with me and sleep in my bed.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): people are not possessions  
> _The robber girl says, “She’s mine!” Can a person belong to someone else?_  
> - ✅ No. People belong to themselves → Yes. Friends choose each other. Nobody owns a friend.
> - Yes, if you want them → Wanting someone is not owning them. A friend is free to choose.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why a person cannot be owned, and a friend is chosen._

_The robber girl is Gerda’s size, with black eyes that look almost sad._  
_Gerda tells her everything. The robber girl puts her hands in the muff._  
**The Robber Girl**: What’s this? It’s warm. It’s alive!  

**Choices**

- **Tell her it’s your Nubbin.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: A Nubbin. Never heard of one. I like it.
- **Let Gerda explain.**
    - **Gerda**: It’s the lodger’s. It kept my hands warm.
    - **The Robber Girl**: Has it, now.

#### `a12-09-forest-done`

_The robber girl keeps one hand in the muff the whole way._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): living bodies make heat  
> _Your Nubbin is warm because living bodies make their own heat._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that living bodies make their own warmth._


#### `a12-09-castle`

_The coach stops in a cracked old castle yard. Crows fly out._  
_Big dogs leap up. They don’t bark._  
_In the hall, soup bubbles in a big pot on a fire._  
**The Robber Girl**: You’ll sleep with me and my animals.  
_In her corner, about a hundred pigeons sleep on perches._  
**The Robber Girl**: Those wood pigeons would fly off if not tied. And here’s old Bae.  
_A reindeer is tied to the wall by a copper ring._  
_She has a long knife, kept in a crack in the wall._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sharp things are for grown-ups  
> _The robber girl has a sharp knife. Who should use a sharp knife?_  
> - ✅ A grown-up → Yes. Sharp knives are for grown-ups. Children ask for help.
> - Any child → Sharp knives can hurt. Ask a grown-up to help you.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sharp knives are for grown-ups to use._


**Choices**

- **Ask her to put the knife away.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: No.
    - But she puts it in the wall, close by. A kind of yes.
- **Stroke Bae’s nose.**
    - Bae lowers his head. His nose is soft. His eyes are tired.

#### `a12-09-castle-done`

**The Robber Girl**: Tell me about Kay again. The warm thing stays where I can see it.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count to a hundred by tens  
> _(Count the pigeons in tens: ten, twenty, thirty, all the way to a hundred.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:tens:100`
> _For grown-ups: Counted to one hundred by tens._


#### `a12-09-keep`

_She holds out both hands, the way she did to the muff._  
**The Robber Girl**: I want that one. It’s warm. It’s mine now.  
**Gerda**: It isn’t yours. It isn’t mine either.  
**The Robber Girl**: I didn’t ask you.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): asking, and saying no kindly  
> _Who gets to decide what happens to your Nubbin?_  
> - ✅ You and your Nubbin → Yes. You decide together. And you can say no kindly.
> - The robber girl → She can ask. But you and your Nubbin decide.
> _For grown-ups: Practised the idea that you can say no kindly, and that asking is not the same as taking._

_Your Nubbin looks at you. It waits to see what you will do._  
_The robber girl’s hands are chapped. There is a scar on one knuckle._  

**Choices**

- **“No.” Plainly and kindly.**
    - **You**: No.
    - **The Robber Girl**: No?
    - **You**: No. A Nubbin is not a thing to keep. It stays with me.
    - She stares. Then she shrugs, as if she meant to lose.
    - **The Robber Girl**: Fine. Keep your warm thing.
- **“You can hold it for one night.”**
    - **You**: You can hold it tonight. In the morning it comes back to me.
    - **The Robber Girl**: One night?
    - She holds your Nubbin in both hands, very carefully.
    - **The Robber Girl**: One night. Fine.
    - Your Nubbin snuggles on her shoulder and falls asleep.
    - She looks as if nobody has ever done that before.

#### `a12-09-keep-done`

_The robber girl falls asleep with an arm round Gerda, and snores._  
_Gerda lies awake and stares at the pigeons. You stare at Gerda._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): lonely people want friends  
> _Some people are lonely. They can act grumpy, but they just want a friend._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that grumpy behaviour can hide loneliness._


#### `a12-09-complete`

_By the fire the robbers sing. The old robber woman does a somersault._  
_Bae stands in the dark with his copper ring on, looking at the door._  
_The pigeons shuffle and murmur on their perches._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): animal sounds  
> _The pigeons murmur. What sound does a pigeon make?_  
> - ✅ Coo, coo → Yes! Coo, coo, coo.
> - Moo, moo → Moo is a cow! A pigeon says coo.
> _For grown-ups: Matched an animal to its sound._

_Only the robber girl sleeps. She sleeps like someone who has won._  

## A12-10. The Reindeer

- `a12-10-s1`: Listen to the wood pigeons in the night. · _Lie still in the straw. Listen._
- `a12-10-s2`: In the morning, ask Bae the way north. · _Talk to Bae while the robber girl listens._
- `a12-10-s3`: Go with Gerda and Bae. · _Help tie Gerda on, then climb up behind her._

#### `a12-10-pigeons`

**The Wood Pigeons**: Coo, coo. We have seen little Kay.  
**Gerda**: What? What did you say?  
**The Wood Pigeons**: A white hen pulled his sledge. He sat in the Snow Queen’s carriage.  
**The Wood Pigeons**: She flew low over the forest and breathed on us. We were cold.  
**Gerda**: Where was she going?  
**The Wood Pigeons**: North, we think, where there is always snow. Ask the reindeer.  
**Bae**: Snow and ice! It’s glorious. You can run free in great shining valleys.  
**Bae**: The Snow Queen’s strong castle is far north, on an island called Spitsbergen.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): north is up on a map  
> _Bae says north. On most maps, which way is north? Up, or down?_  
> - ✅ Up → Yes! On most maps, north is at the top.
> - Down → Down is south. On most maps, north is at the top.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that north is usually at the top of a map._

**Gerda**: Oh, Kay. Little Kay.  

**Choices**

- **Whisper to Bae: do you know the way?**
    - **Bae**: Know it? I’d find it eyes shut. I’d go, but for this ring.
- **Hold Gerda’s hand in the dark.**
    - You find her hand in the straw. She holds on tight.
- **Hush them before the robber girl wakes.**
    - The robber girl stirs. Everyone is quiet until she snores again.

#### `a12-10-pigeons-done`

_Nobody sleeps much after that, except the robber girl and one very old pigeon._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when you are worried at bedtime  
> _Gerda can’t sleep. What helps when we are worried at bedtime?_  
> - ✅ A cuddle and slow breaths → Yes. A cuddle and slow breaths help worries get smaller.
> - Lying awake and worrying → That makes worries bigger. A cuddle and slow breaths help.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about calming down when worried at bedtime._


#### `a12-10-morning`

_In the morning Gerda tells the robber girl what the pigeons said._  
**The Robber Girl**: The far north. Bae, do you know the way?  
**Bae**: Do I know? I was born there. Ask a fish about the river!  
_His eyes shine. He shakes his big antlers._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): reindeer mums and dads both grow antlers  
> _Reindeer are special deer. Mums and dads can both grow big antlers._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that both male and female reindeer can grow antlers._

**The Robber Girl**: The men are all out. Only Mother is here, and she naps at noon.  
**The Robber Girl**: Then I’ll do something for you.  

**Choices**

- **Thank her.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: Don’t thank me yet. I might change my mind.
- **Ask her why.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: Because I want to. That is why I do everything.

#### `a12-10-morning-done`

_At noon the old robber woman has a nap, chin on chest._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds  
> _Which word starts with the sound “s”? Sleep, or nap?_  
> - ✅ Sleep → Yes! S, s, sleep. It starts with s.
> - Nap → Nap starts with n. S, s, sleep starts with s.
> _For grown-ups: Found a word that starts with the sound s._


#### `a12-10-free`

_The robber girl goes to Bae. She does not look at you._  
**The Robber Girl**: Don’t think this is for you. I was going to anyway.  
**The Robber Girl**: Bae, I’m untying you. Carry this girl to the Snow Queen’s.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): fairness: letting someone go home  
> _Bae wants to go home. Is it kind to let him go?_  
> - ✅ Yes. He wants to go home → Yes. It is fair and kind to let someone go home.
> - No. Keep him tied → Bae is tired and wants his home. Letting him go is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about fairness: letting an animal go home._

_Bae leaps for joy. The robber girl lifts Gerda onto his back._  
**The Robber Girl**: Here are your boots. I’m keeping the muff. It’s too pretty.  
**The Robber Girl**: Take Mother’s big mittens. They reach your elbows.  
**The Robber Girl**: Two loaves for the road. And don’t cry. Look happy!  
**Bae**: Climb on behind her, lodger. You weigh less than a sack of salt.  
**The Robber Girl**: Run! And look after her!  

**Choices**

- **Wave goodbye to the robber girl.**
    - You wave. She doesn’t wave back, but she watches until you are gone.
- **Nod to her, as one equal to another.**
    - You nod. She nods back, once, hard, like shutting a box.

#### `a12-10-free-done`

_Bae runs over stumps and bushes, through forest and plains._  
_Above you the sky flares green and white._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): the northern lights  
> _The northern lights are glowing colours, high in the far north sky._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the northern lights glow in the sky near the far north._

**Bae**: Those are my old lights! Look at them flash!  

#### `a12-10-complete`

_You ride north day and night. Two loaves, then one, then none._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away within 10  
> _There were two loaves. You eat one. How many are left?_  
> - ✅ One → Yes! Two take away one leaves one.
> - Two → You ate one! Two take away one leaves one.
> _For grown-ups: Took one away from two to make one._

_Gerda’s hands are in great mittens. Your Nubbin rides inside her coat._  
**Gerda**: Is it much further?  
**Bae**: Yes. But we’re nearer than we were.  

## A12-11. The Sámi Woman

- `a12-11-s1`: Find the little house in the snow. · _Follow Bae towards the smoke and lamplight._
- `a12-11-s2`: Get warm while Bae tells his story. · _Sit by the lamp and eat what you are given._
- `a12-11-s3`: Carry the message on the dried fish. · _Take the fish from the Sámi woman. Keep it safe._

#### `a12-11-hut`

_Bae stops at a little house. Its roof comes down to the snow._  
_The door is low. You crawl in. Your Nubbin goes in on its belly._  
_Inside, by lamplight, a woman is frying fish._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): the Sámi people today  
> _The Sámi are real people of the far north. They live there today._  
> _Many live in towns. Some herd reindeer._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Sámi are a living people of the far north, in towns and as reindeer herders._

_A reindeer, a cold girl and a lodger crawl in. She stays calm._  
**The Sámi Woman**: Well. Come in. Shut the cold out. Mind the pan.  
_Gerda is too cold to speak. The woman rubs her hands by the lamp._  

**Choices**

- **Help rub Gerda’s feet.**
    - You rub Gerda’s feet while the woman does her hands. Warm comes back.
- **Mind the pan.**
    - You turn the fish. The woman nods: right side, right moment.

#### `a12-11-hut-done`

**The Sámi Woman**: There. Fingers are coming back. Toes next.  

> **Lesson** (health, notice): warming up when very cold  
> _When very cold, go inside and warm up slowly, with a warm drink._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard how to warm up gently when very cold._


#### `a12-11-lamp`

_Bae tells his own story first. Then he tells Gerda’s._  
**The Sámi Woman**: You’ve been tied up a long while. Hold still.  
_She checks Bae’s legs and neck, quickly and gently._  
**The Sámi Woman**: My son has our herd out on the winter grass. I know tired reindeer.  
_She feeds you fish and broth. She fetches Bae a heap of lichen._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): what reindeer eat  
> _Bae is a reindeer. What does the woman fetch for him to eat?_  
> - ✅ Lichen → Yes. Reindeer love lichen, which grows on rocks and trees.
> - Fish → Fish is for us. Reindeer eat lichen, which grows on rocks and trees.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that reindeer eat lichen._

**The Sámi Woman**: You’ve a long way to go, to where the Snow Queen is.  
**Gerda**: Do you know where she is?  
**The Sámi Woman**: I know her weather. She lights up the sky every evening, further north.  

**Choices**

- **Ask about her herd.**
    - **The Sámi Woman**: Big enough. My son knows each one by its face.
- **Thank her for the food.**
    - **The Sámi Woman**: It’s only fish. You’d do the same, if I came to your door.
- **Help feed Bae his lichen.**
    - Bae eats from your hands, softly, then all at once.

#### `a12-11-lamp-done`

**The Sámi Woman**: My friend further north knows that country better than I do.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): kindness to strangers  
> _The woman gave strangers food and a warm seat. That was…_  
> - ✅ Kind and generous → Yes. Sharing with people who need help is kind.
> - Silly → Helping someone who is cold and hungry is kind, not silly.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being kind to people who need help._


#### `a12-11-fish`

**The Sámi Woman**: I’ve no paper. I’ll write it on a fish.  
_She writes careful lines on a dried fish and hands it to you._  
**The Sámi Woman**: Look after that. Don’t let the reindeer eat it. Don’t eat it yourself.  
_She ties Gerda onto Bae with her own knots, which are better._  
_She gives you a rolled-up reindeer skin._  
**The Sámi Woman**: To sit on, wherever you end up sitting. Snow is colder from underneath.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a skin keeps the cold out  
> _Why sit on a reindeer skin, and not straight on the snow?_  
> - ✅ The skin keeps the cold out → Yes. The thick fur keeps the cold of the snow away.
> - The snow is too soft → Snow is soft, but cold. The thick fur keeps the cold away.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that thick fur stops the cold of the snow reaching you._

_She doesn’t say how she knows. She knows the country._  

**Choices**

- **Put the fish inside your coat.**
    - You tuck it in. It smells of fish, and so will you.
- **Ask why she thinks you’ll be sitting.**
    - **The Sámi Woman**: Everyone who goes north ends up waiting for someone.

#### `a12-11-fish-done`

**The Sámi Woman**: Go well. Come back this way after. I’ll want to know how it ends.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): beginning and end of a story  
> _Which comes first in a story: the beginning, or the end?_  
> - ✅ The beginning → Yes! Beginning, then middle, then end.
> - The end → The end comes last. First comes the beginning, then the middle.
> _For grown-ups: Put the beginning, middle and end of a story in order._


#### `a12-11-complete`

_Bae runs on into the night. The lights burn blue all night._  
**Gerda**: She didn’t ask for anything. Not even our names.  
_The fish letter is warm in your coat. Your Nubbin sniffs it, hopefully._  
**Bae**: Not far now. Further than you’d like, but not far.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): north on the map  
> _Her friend lives further north. Is that nearer the cold, or the warm?_  
> - ✅ Nearer to the cold → Yes. Further north is colder, with more snow.
> - Nearer to the warm → Warm lands are in the south. Further north is colder.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that going further north means colder places._


## A12-12. The Finnish Woman

- `a12-12-s1`: Deliver the fish letter. · _There is no door. Knock on the chimney._
- `a12-12-s2`: Listen while Bae asks the Finnish woman for help. · _Sit in the heat and listen._
- `a12-12-s3`: Ask the Finnish woman if you should go with Gerda. · _Ask her in the corner, before Bae sets off._

#### `a12-12-chimney`

_The Finnish woman’s house has no door. Bae knocks on the chimney._  
_A voice says, come down. Inside, it is so hot the air shimmers._  
_The Finnish woman is small, with rolled-up sleeves and very wise eyes._  
**The Finnish Woman**: Boots off, mittens off, coat open, or you’ll cook!  
_She puts a block of ice on Bae’s head. He looks so relieved._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-4, ask): ice takes heat away  
> _Bae is too hot. A block of ice makes him feel…_  
> - ✅ Cooler → Yes! Ice is cold. It takes the heat away.
> - Hotter → Ice is very cold. It makes Bae feel cooler.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that ice is cold and cools something hot._

_You give her the fish. She reads it three times._  
_Then she pops it in the soup pot. She never wastes anything._  

**Choices**

- **Watch the letter go in the soup.**
    - It goes in with a respectful plop. Your Nubbin watches the pot.
- **Ask for a block of ice for yourself.**
    - **The Finnish Woman**: Ha! Here. You’re cooking too. Everybody does, the first time.

#### `a12-12-chimney-done`

**The Finnish Woman**: Well. So you’re the ones. Sit.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): dress for the weather  
> _It is very hot inside. What should you take off?_  
> - ✅ My coat and mittens → Yes! Take off warm things when you are hot.
> - Nothing at all → You would get too hot. Take off your coat and mittens.
> _For grown-ups: Chose to take off warm clothes when too hot._


#### `a12-12-power`

_Bae tells his story, then Gerda’s. The Finnish woman says nothing._  
**Bae**: You are so clever. Can you give her the strength of twelve men?  
**The Finnish Woman**: The strength of twelve men! Much good that would do her.  
_She takes Bae to a corner and puts fresh ice on his head._  
**The Finnish Woman**: Kay has a splinter in his heart and glass in his eye.  
**The Finnish Woman**: They must come out, or he will never be himself again.  
**The Finnish Woman**: I can’t give her more than she has. Look how much that is!  
**The Finnish Woman**: People help her. Animals carry her. She has come this far barefoot.  
**The Finnish Woman**: It is in her heart. She loves someone, all the way through.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): strength comes from caring  
> _Where does Gerda’s strength come from?_  
> - ✅ From her loving heart → Yes. Love and kindness make her strong. No magic needed.
> - From a magic drink → No magic. Her caring heart is her strength.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how love and kindness give us strength._


#### `a12-12-power-done`

_Gerda, by the stove, hasn’t heard a word. She sleeps in the heat._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): warm clothes for snow  
> _It is snowing outside. What should Gerda wear: boots and mittens, or a swimsuit?_  
> - ✅ Boots and mittens → Yes! Boots and mittens keep her warm in the snow.
> - A swimsuit → Brrr! A swimsuit is for the beach. Boots and mittens for snow.
> _For grown-ups: Chose warm clothes for snowy weather._


#### `a12-12-ask`

_You go to the corner. You ask: should you go with Gerda?_  
**The Finnish Woman**: No.  
**The Finnish Woman**: Two miles on, by the Snow Queen’s garden, stands a red-berried bush.  
**The Finnish Woman**: Take her as far as the bush. Then stop. Then wait.  
**The Finnish Woman**: Some doors only open for one person.  
_She looks at you, as if checking you are the waiting sort._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): waiting well  
> _The Finnish woman asks you to wait. What helps with waiting?_  
> - ✅ Slow breaths and counting → Yes. Slow breaths and counting make waiting easier.
> - Running about → Running about is hard to do while waiting. Slow breaths help.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about ways to wait calmly._


**Choices**

- **“How long?”**
    - **The Finnish Woman**: As long as it takes. That is the only length waiting comes in.
- **“And if she doesn’t come out?”**
    - **The Finnish Woman**: Then you will still have waited. That is worth something. But she will come.
- **Nod. You understand.**
    - **The Finnish Woman**: Good. Most people argue.

#### `a12-12-ask-done`

**The Finnish Woman**: Now go. Put her down at the bush. Let the reindeer come straight back.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): long and short distances  
> _The bush is two miles away. Which is longer, two steps or two miles?_  
> - ✅ Two miles → Yes! Two miles is much, much longer.
> - Two steps → Two steps is tiny. Two miles is much longer.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two steps with two miles._


#### `a12-12-complete`

_The Finnish woman lifts sleeping Gerda onto Bae. Off he runs!_  
**Gerda**: Oh! My boots! My mittens!  
_Bae doesn’t dare stop. He runs through the hard cold._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): reindeer hooves spread on snow  
> _Reindeer have wide hooves. They spread out on the snow, like snowshoes._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that reindeer have wide hooves that help them walk on snow._

_You look back once. The little hot house is a spark, then nothing._  

## A12-13. The Bush with Red Berries

> _For grown-ups: Talked about how crying is okay when we feel sad._

    - **You**: Go on, then.

- **Count the berries again.**
    - So many berries! Your Nubbin points at one you missed.
- **Hum Gerda’s rose tune, under your breath.**
    - You hum quietly. Your Nubbin hums it back, a beat behind.
- **Just sit.**
    - You just sit. It turns out you are good at it.

#### `a12-13-wait-done`

_Your feet go numb, and come back, and go numb again. You stay._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): keeping your word  
> _Why do you stay at the bush, even when it is hard?_  
> - ✅ Because I said I would → Yes. Keeping your word is a big thing.
> - Because it is easy → It isn’t easy! You stay because you said you would.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keeping a promise even when it is hard._


#### `a12-13-complete`

_Night comes. The stars come out thick as frost._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): stars are there in the day too  
> _Stars shine by day too. The Sun’s glare hides them._  
> _At night, we can see them._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that stars are there by day but hidden by the Sun’s brightness._

_Far away, tiny Gerda is still walking. Something moves towards her._  
_You stand up on the skin to see. You do not step off it._  
_You hold your Nubbin tight and stay where you are._  

## A12-14. The Snowflake Guards

- `a12-14-s1`: Watch Gerda from the bush. · _Stand on the reindeer skin and look out._
- `a12-14-s2`: Watch what Gerda does. · _Keep watching. Don’t look away._

#### `a12-14-guards`

_Gerda is a dark speck on the white._  
_Towards her run the snowflakes, along the ground._  
_The nearer they get, the bigger they grow._  
_Some are like spiky hedgehogs. Some are like fat little bears._  
_They are the Snow Queen’s guards. They make a ring round Gerda._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): name a shape  
> _The guards make a ring round Gerda. What shape is a ring?_  
> - ✅ A circle → Yes! A ring is a circle.
> - A triangle → A triangle has three corners. A ring goes round and round: a circle.
> _For grown-ups: Named a circle as the shape of a ring._


**Choices**

- **Shout to her.**
    - You shout. The cold drops your voice in the snow a yard away.
- **Take one step off the skin.**
    - You take one step. Then you remember the Finnish woman. You step back on.
- **Hold your Nubbin tight.**
    - You hold it. It holds you. You both keep watching.

#### `a12-14-guards-done`

_Gerda stops. She doesn’t run._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): stop and breathe when scared  
> _When we feel frightened, what can we do first?_  
> - ✅ Stop and take a slow breath → Yes. A slow breath helps us feel calmer.
> - Run away fast → Running can make it scarier. Stopping and breathing helps first.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about stopping and breathing when frightened._


#### `a12-14-prayer`

_Gerda folds her hands and says the prayer Grandmother taught her._  
_You can’t hear it from here, and you don’t need to._  
_It is so cold her breath comes out like smoke._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): you can see your breath when it is cold  
> _On a cold day, you can see your breath. It makes a little cloud._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that breath makes a little cloud on a cold day._

_The smoke turns into small bright figures with helmets and spears._  
_There are more with every breath she takes._  
_They clear the road ahead of her._  
_They stroke her hands and feet. She feels the cold less._  
_She walks on, quickly and bravely._  

#### `a12-14-prayer-done`

_They go with her to the gate. Then they fade, like breath on glass._  

> **Lesson** (science, do): breath fogs cold glass  
> _(Breathe on a cold window. See the little cloud? Watch it fade.)_  
> Check: `edu:breathe:window:fog`
> _For grown-ups: Breathed on cold glass and watched the mist fade._


#### `a12-14-complete`

_The palace gate is made of cutting winds. Gerda says her evening prayer._  
_The winds drop, as if they have gone to sleep._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): we see what wind moves  
> _We can’t see wind. How do we know it is blowing?_  
> - ✅ Things move, like leaves and flags → Yes! We see what the wind moves.
> - We can’t know → We can! Leaves, flags and snow all move when the wind blows.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we can tell wind is blowing by what it moves._

_She goes in. The gate closes. The winds get up again._  
_You sit back down on the reindeer skin._  
_Now there is nothing to watch but the walls._  

## A12-15. The Ice Puzzle

- `a12-15-s1`: Watch the Snow Queen fly south. · _Look through the clear patch in the frost, then up at the sky._
- `a12-15-s2`: Watch Kay at his puzzle. · _Keep looking through the clear patch in the frost._

#### `a12-15-south`

_Your Nubbin breathes on the frozen crust. The frost clears like a window._  
_The atlas shows you the next page: inside the palace, a little earlier._  
_The halls are drifted snow. Cold winds are the windows._  
_Northern lights shine on them. They are huge and empty._  
_The Snow Queen stands in the greatest hall, ready to go._  
**The Snow Queen**: I’m off to the warm lands.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): north and south  
> _The queen goes to the warm lands. Which way? South, or north?_  
> - ✅ South → Yes! The warm lands are south of the cold north.
> - North → North is even colder. The warm lands are to the south.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that warmer places lie to the south of the cold north._

**The Snow Queen**: Make the word while I’m gone, and I’ll give you the world.  

**Choices**

- **Look up as she passes.**
    - She flies over the bush, high up, a long white streak heading south.
- **Keep your head down.**
    - A long white shadow crosses the snow. The berries rattle on the bush.

#### `a12-15-south-done`

_In the great hall Kay is alone. He is the only thing that moves._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): opposites  
> _The hall is empty. What is the opposite of empty?_  
> - ✅ Full → Yes! Full is the opposite of empty.
> - Cold → Cold is the opposite of hot. The opposite of empty is full.
> _For grown-ups: Found the opposite of the word empty._


#### `a12-15-puzzle`

_In the hall is a frozen lake, cracked into a thousand pieces._  
_The Snow Queen calls it the Mirror of Understanding._  
_Kay sits on it. He is blue with cold, and does not notice._  
_He pushes flat, sharp pieces of ice about. He fits them together._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, do): find a triangle  
> _(Look around the room. Find a triangle. Triangles have three corners.)_  
> Check: `edu:tap:shape:triangle`
> _For grown-ups: Found and named a triangle._

_To Kay, the shapes are the most important thing in the world._  
_He makes words. But one word he cannot make._  
**Kay**: Nearly. It just needs one more piece.  
_It doesn’t. He sits and thinks until he creaks, stiff and still._  

**Choices**

- **Say his name, out loud, to nobody.**
    - **You**: Kay.
    - He can’t hear you. Someone should say it, so you did.
- **Look away for a moment.**
    - You look at the red berries. It helps a bit. Then you look back.
- **Keep watching.**
    - You keep watching. Your Nubbin watches the way it watches an egg.

#### `a12-15-puzzle-done`

_Then a small figure in stockings comes in through the gate of winds._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): bravery  
> _Gerda is scared, and she comes in anyway. What is that called?_  
> - ✅ Being brave → Yes! Being brave means doing it even when you feel scared.
> - Being silly → It is not silly. It is being brave, even when scared.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that bravery means acting even when you feel scared._


#### `a12-15-complete`

_Gerda walks into the empty hall. It takes her a long time._  
_Kay does not look up. He is counting pieces._  
_Your Nubbin holds its breath. So do you._  
_Over the palace the northern lights go quiet._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): loud and quiet  
> _The lights go quiet. Which is quieter, a whisper or a shout?_  
> - ✅ A whisper → Yes! A whisper is very quiet.
> - A shout → A shout is loud. A whisper is quiet.
> _For grown-ups: Compared loud and quiet sounds._


## A12-16. Gerda’s Tears

- `a12-16-s1`: Watch Gerda find Kay. · _Watch through the clear patch in the frost._
- `a12-16-s2`: Watch Kay come back. · _Keep watching. This is the part you waited for._
- `a12-16-s3`: Watch the ice spell the word. · _Watch the pieces of ice on the lake._

#### `a12-16-found`

_Gerda sees him. She knows him at once._  
_She runs and throws her arms round his neck._  
**Gerda**: Kay! It’s you! I’ve found you!  
_Kay sits quite still. He is stiff and cold. He doesn’t know her._  
_Gerda cries, the way you cry at the end of a very long way._  
_Her warm tears fall on his chest and reach his heart._  
_They thaw the ice. The little splinter melts, as if it never was._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-4, ask): warm things melt ice  
> _Gerda’s tears are warm. What does warm do to ice?_  
> - ✅ It melts it → Yes! Warm melts ice. Her warm tears melt the cold.
> - It makes it bigger → Warm things make ice melt away, not grow. Drip, drip!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that something warm melts ice._

_Kay looks at her._  

**Choices**

- **Stand up on the skin.**
    - You stand up. Your Nubbin climbs onto your shoulder to see.
- **Stay perfectly still.**
    - You don’t move. You don’t want to break anything, even from far away.

#### `a12-16-found-done`

_Gerda sings the rose hymn. You know the tune, and hum along._  

> **Lesson** (music, RL.2.4, do): keep a steady beat  
> _(Hum a slow tune and clap a steady beat together.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:beat:slow`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped a steady beat to a hummed tune._


#### `a12-16-tears`

_Kay bursts into tears. The grain of glass washes out of his eye._  
_He blinks. He sees her._  
**Kay**: Gerda? It’s you! Where did I go? How long have I been away?  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): long and short times  
> _Which is longer: a day, or a year?_  
> - ✅ A year → Yes! A year is much longer than a day.
> - A day → A day is short. A year has many, many days in it.
> _For grown-ups: Compared the length of a day and a year._

_He looks round the hall as if for the first time._  
**Kay**: It’s so cold in here. It’s so big and empty.  
_He holds Gerda. She laughs and cries at once. So do you._  

**Choices**

- **Cheer.**
    - You cheer out loud, alone in the far north. Your Nubbin squeaks.
- **Sit down hard on the skin.**
    - Your legs go wobbly. You sit on the skin and laugh.

#### `a12-16-tears-done`

_Even the pieces of ice begin to move._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): describing words  
> _The ice is dancing. Which word fits best: sparkly, or soggy?_  
> - ✅ Sparkly → Yes! Dancing ice is sparkly.
> - Soggy → Soggy is wet and floppy. Dancing ice is sparkly.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a describing word that fits the picture._


#### `a12-16-word`

_It is such a glad moment that the ice dances round them._  
_When it is tired, it lies down in the shape of a word._  
_It is the word Kay could not make: ETERNITY._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): the letter E  
> _(The word starts with the letter E. Draw a big E in the air!)_  
> Check: `edu:trace:letter:e`
> _For grown-ups: Recognised and traced the letter E._

_Kay didn’t make it. It made itself when he stopped trying and was glad._  
_Gerda hugs him. His cheeks go pink. His eyes shine like hers._  
_He is well and strong again._

    - **You**: Eternity.

#### `a12-16-word-done`

_Kay and Gerda take hands and walk out of the great palace._

> _You waited for Kay. What does waiting for a friend show?_

> - That we have nothing to do → You waited because you care. That is what it shows.
