## A12-17. The Road Home

- `a12-17-s1`: Meet Bae back at the bush. · _Stay by the bush. Bae is coming back._
- `a12-17-s2`: Go south past the Finnish woman’s house and the Sámi woman’s. · _Stop at both houses on the way._
- `a12-17-s3`: Meet the rider in the forest. · _Walk on into the green forest._

#### `a12-17-doe`

_Bae is back at the bush. He has brought a young doe._  
_She gives the children her warm milk to drink._  
**Bae**: I said I’d come straight back. I never said I’d stay away.  
**Kay**: Hello, lodger. I’m sorry about the face I pulled at you.  
_He means the horrible face at the window. He remembers, and he is ashamed._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): accepting an apology  
> _Kay says sorry. What can you say back?_  
> - ✅ “Thank you. It’s okay.” → Thank you. That makes me feel better.
> - “I’m still cross.” → That’s fair. I’ll try to make it up to you.
> _For grown-ups: Practised answering an apology kindly._

**Gerda**: He’s really back. He’s cross about his feet, which is how I know.  

**Choices**

- **Tell Kay it was a very good impression.**
    - **Kay**: It was, wasn’t it. I won’t do it again. Probably.
- **Hug them both.**
    - You hug them both. Your Nubbin gets squashed in the middle and doesn’t mind.
- **Wrap them in the reindeer skin.**
    - You wrap the skin round them. They look like one small, pleased bundle.

#### `a12-17-doe-done`

_Bae and the doe carry them south. You walk beside them._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add within 10  
> _Two reindeer and two children. How many altogether?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! Two and two make four.
> - Three → Count on your fingers: two reindeer, then two children. Four!
> _For grown-ups: Added two and two to make four._


#### `a12-17-south`

_First you stop at the Finnish woman’s hot little house._  
_The children warm up. She gives Gerda back her boots and mittens._  
**The Finnish Woman**: I told you she would come. You waited well. Most people fidget.  
_Then on to the Sámi woman. She has sewn new clothes for both children._  
_She has her sledge ready._  
**The Sámi Woman**: Well. You’re back, and there are two of them. That is how it ends.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): what happened first  
> _Which house came first: the Finnish woman’s, or the Sámi woman’s?_  
> - ✅ The Finnish woman’s → Yes! First the hot little house, then the Sámi woman’s.
> - The Sámi woman’s → Let’s remember: first the Finnish woman’s house. Then the Sámi woman’s.
> _For grown-ups: Put two story events in order._

_She drives you south herself, to the edge of her country._  
_There the first green is coming through the snow._  
**The Sámi Woman**: Go well, all of you. Even the one who wanted to eat my letter.  

**Choices**

- **Thank her for everything.**
    - **The Sámi Woman**: It was only fish and a skin. Keep the skin.
- **Say goodbye to Bae.**
    - **Bae**: Goodbye, lodger. You sit well. I’ve never seen anyone sit so well.
    - He touches his nose to your Nubbin and turns for home.

#### `a12-17-south-done`

_Bae and the doe run north, side by side, into the snow._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): the Sámi languages  
> _The Sámi people have their own languages. There are several._  
> _In North Sámi, “good day” is “buorre beaivi”._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that the Sámi have their own languages, and one greeting in North Sámi._


#### `a12-17-rider`

_Birds sing. The forest has green buds. A horse comes out of it._  
_On it rides a girl in a red cap. It is the robber girl!_  
**The Robber Girl**: I got bored at home. I’m off to see the world.  
_Two wood pigeons ride on her saddle, tied by the leg._  
**The Robber Girl**: So this is Kay. Was he worth running to the world’s end?  
**Gerda**: How are the prince and princess? And the ravens?  
**The Robber Girl**: The prince and princess went abroad. The old raven died.  
_The raven’s body stopped working. He was very old._  
**The Robber Girl**: His sweetheart wears a black thread on her leg, to remember him.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): when someone dies, and remembering  
> _When someone dies, their body stops working, and it does not start again._  
> _It is okay to feel sad. We can remember them, and talk about them._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what death means in plain words, and that sadness and remembering are okay._


**Choices**

- **Say you’re sorry about the raven.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: Don’t be. He had a good job and all the scraps he wanted.
- **Admire her red cap.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: It’s a good cap. You can’t have it.

#### `a12-17-rider-done`

_As she rides off, she tosses something small and red over her shoulder._  
_It lands on your Nubbin’s head: a little red cap._  
**The Robber Girl**: Robbers always have two of everything!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): saying thank you  
> _The robber girl gives your Nubbin a cap. What can you say?_  
> - ✅ Thank you! → Don’t mention it. I mean it. Don’t.
> - Nothing at all → Hm. You could say thank you. It’s nice to hear.
> _For grown-ups: Practised saying thank you for a gift._

_Kay and Gerda walk on, hand in hand. It is spring._  
_Your Nubbin wears its red cap at a slant._  
_Somewhere ahead, church bells are ringing._

> _A bell rings when it shakes very fast. Shaking makes sound._

## A12-18. Summer

- `a12-18-s1`: Walk home into the town. · _Follow the church bells to Grandmother’s door._
- `a12-18-s2`: Sit by the roses with Kay and Gerda. · _Climb out to the little stools under the rose arch._

#### `a12-18-bells`

_The church bells ring. You know the high towers. It is the town._  
_You go through the streets to Grandmother’s door and up the stairs._  
_Everything is where it was. The clock says tick, tick._  
_But Kay and Gerda notice something. They have grown up._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): growing taller  
> _Kay and Gerda have grown. What happens to children as they grow?_  
> - ✅ They get taller → Yes! Children grow taller as time goes by.
> - They get smaller → Children get taller as they grow. That is why the door seems low.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that children grow taller over time._

**Kay**: Was the door always this low?  
**Gerda**: We have been gone a long time.  

**Choices**

- **Duck under the beam, out of habit.**
    - You duck. Kay, who never had to before, bumps his head, and laughs.
- **Listen to the clock.**
    - Tick, tick. It kept going all the time. Someone kept winding it.

#### `a12-18-bells-done`

_The window is open. Gutter roses bloom and grow in at the window._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): our senses: smell  
> _The roses smell sweet. What do you smell with?_  
> - ✅ My nose → Yes! You smell with your nose. Sniff, sniff!
> - My elbow → Not your elbow! You smell with your nose. Sniff, sniff!
> _For grown-ups: Named the nose as the body part for smelling._


#### `a12-18-roses`

_Two little stools sit under the arch. Kay and Gerda are too big now._  
_The Snow Queen’s cold halls have faded, like a dream after breakfast._  
_Grandmother sits in the sun, reading aloud from her old book. She reads slowly._  
_Kay and Gerda understand the old rose hymn, all at once._  
_They are grown up, and they are children too, in the place that counts._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): staying yourself as you grow  
> _You grow tall on the outside. What can stay the same on the inside?_  
> - ✅ Your kind, playful heart → Yes. Your kind heart can stay with you always.
> - Your shoes → Ha! Shoes get too small. Your kind heart stays with you.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what stays the same inside as we grow._

_And it is summer: warm, glorious summer._  

**Choices**

- **Sit on the gutter’s edge beside them.**
    - You sit with your feet over the boxes. Grandmother nods and reads on.
- **Fetch the watering can.**
    - You water the arch. A drop lands on Kay. He pretends not to notice.

#### `a12-18-roses-done`

**Grandmother**: There you are, lodger. I kept your room.  
**Grandmother**: I thought you’d want it back, after.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): who did what in the story  
> _Who kept your room all this time?_  
> - ✅ Grandmother → That’s right. I did. Rooms like yours are worth keeping.
> - The robber girl → Not the robber girl! It was me, your Grandmother.
> _For grown-ups: Recalled which character kept the room._

## A13-1. The Piece of Wood

- `a13-01-s1`: Step into the brown-ink page, and out of the rain. · _Touch the page. Find the open door with sawdust on its step._
- `a13-01-s2`: Stay in Master Cherry’s shop. Keep your Nubbin out from under their feet. · _Stand by the bench. Two old men are about to argue._

#### `a13-01-page`

_Nova’s atlas opens. The page is all brown ink._  
_A hill town. A long white road. The sea at the bottom._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): Italy is a country shaped like a boot; Tuscany is in the middle  
> _This page is in Italy. Italy is a country shaped like a boot._  
> _(Trace a boot in the air.)_  
> _The hill town is in Tuscany, in the middle._  
> _For grown-ups: Met Italy, a country shaped like a boot, and Tuscany, the part in the middle._

_This story begins with a piece of wood. Just wood!_  
_The ink turns to rain. Splash! You and your Nubbin get wet._  
_One door is open. It smells of warm pine. In you go._  
**Master Cherry**: Come in! Shut the weather out. Mind the shavings.  
_Master Cherry has a nose like a ripe red cherry._  
**Master Cherry**: I will make a table leg from this old log.  
_He lifts his axe._  
**A Small Voice**: Ow! Not so hard!  

#### `a13-01-page-done`

_Master Cherry looks under the bench. He looks up the chimney._  
**Master Cherry**: Did you say that? Nobody said that!  
**Master Cherry**: I imagined it. It was only the weather.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): wood comes from trees, and a tree grows a ring each year  
> _Wood comes from trees. This log was once part of a tree._  
> _Each year a tree grows one new ring inside._  
> _More rings means an older tree._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wood comes from trees, and that each year a tree grows one ring._


#### `a13-01-plane`

_Master Cherry gives the log a whack._  
**A Small Voice**: Ow! That hurt!  
_He sits down on the floor. Then he tries his plane._  
**A Small Voice**: Stop it! You are tickling!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds: log starts with the sound l  
> _The log says “Ow!” The word log starts with the sound l, l, l._  
> _Which word starts the same? Lamp, or hat?_  
> - ✅ Lamp → Yes! L, l, lamp. L, l, log.
> - Hat → Hat starts with h, h, h. Lamp starts with l, l, l, just like log.
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first sound of a word (l for log and lamp)._

_In comes a little old man in a bright yellow wig._  
**Geppetto**: Good morning, Master Antonio. I want to carve a puppet.  
**A Small Voice**: Good idea, Polendina!  
_Geppetto goes red. He thinks Master Cherry said it!_  

**Choices**

- **Tell Geppetto it was the log.**
    - **Geppetto**: A log said that? Now I have heard everything.
- **Keep out of it. It is their argument.**
    - You keep out of it. Not for long!

#### `a13-01-plane-done`

_The two old men shout and tug. They swap wigs by mistake!_  
_Then they swap back and shake hands._  
_Master Cherry gives Geppetto the log. It bounces on his toe._  
_Then it is peace, and the rain has stopped._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): making up after a quarrel  
> _The two old men were cross. How did they make friends again?_  
> - ✅ They shook hands. → Yes. Shaking hands, or a hug, or sorry, can mend a quarrel.
> - They shouted more. → More shouting makes it worse. They stopped, and shook hands. That helped.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how to make up after a quarrel._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count three things in a room

> _How many things is that? (Count on your fingers.)_

> _For grown-ups: Counted three things in a room._

**Geppetto**: It keeps me warm if I do not think about it.

**Geppetto**: Ha. It may stay. It is the warmest thing in the house.  

## A13-2. Geppetto Carves a Puppet

- `a13-02-s1`: Hold the lamp while Geppetto carves. · _Stand at his elbow. Watch the nose._
- `a13-02-s2`: Help Geppetto teach the puppet to walk. · _Hold one wooden hand. Mind the door._

#### `a13-02-carve`

_Geppetto rolls up his sleeves. He looks at the log._  
**Geppetto**: I shall call him Pinocchio.  
_Geppetto smiles. It is a good name for a pine puppet._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, L.2.4, notice): pinocchio means pine nut in Italian  
> **Geppetto**: Pinocchio is a real Italian word. It means a pine nut.  
> **Geppetto**: Pine nuts are tiny seeds. They hide in pine cones.  
> **Geppetto**: And this puppet is made of pine!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that pinocchio is the Italian word for a pine nut._

_He carves the hair, then the eyes. The eyes look back!_  
**Geppetto**: Wooden eyes, why are you looking at me?  
_He carves the nose. It grows. And grows!_  
_He carves the mouth. It sticks out its tongue._  

**Choices**

- **Point out that the nose is growing.**
    - **Geppetto**: I know. I have decided not to notice.
- **Keep the lamp steady and say nothing.**
    - You hold the lamp still. Geppetto works faster.

#### `a13-02-carve-done`

_Geppetto carves the hands. They grab his yellow wig!_  
**Geppetto**: Pinocchio! Give that back!  
_Pinocchio gives it back. His eyes are laughing._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): naming a feeling: Geppetto is cross but also fond  
> _Geppetto shouts. But is he really very angry?_  
> - ✅ A little cross, and a little fond. → Yes! Sometimes we feel two things at once.
> - Only very angry. → He is cross. But look, he is smiling a bit. Two feelings together!
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that people can feel two feelings at once._


#### `a13-02-legs`

_Geppetto carves the legs and feet._  
_The first thing the feet do is kick his nose. Bonk!_  
_You hold one wooden hand. Geppetto holds the other._  
_One step. Two steps. Then Pinocchio is running!_  
**Pinocchio**: I have LEGS!  
_Clack, clack, clack! Out of the door and down the street._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, ask): clapping beats and counting steps  
> _Clack, clack, clack! That is three clacks. Can you clap three?_  
> - ✅ Clap, clap, clap! → Yes! One, two, three. Three clacks!
> - Clap, clap. → Let us try again. Clack, clack, clack. One, two, three.
> _For grown-ups: Counted three steps by clapping._

**Geppetto**: Catch him! Catch him!  

#### `a13-02-street`

_At the bottom of the street, a carabineer catches him by the nose._  
_Geppetto arrives, out of breath._  
_Pinocchio lies down on the stones and will not walk._  
_The crowd thinks the old man is being unkind to the puppet._  
**Carabineer**: You, old man. You can come with me.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, L.2.4, notice): babbo is the Tuscan word for dad  
> _Geppetto is Pinocchio’s babbo._  
> _In Tuscany, children say babbo for dad. Say it with me: bab-bo._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned the Italian word babbo, for dad._


#### `a13-02-complete`

_So it is Geppetto who is led away. He is sad._  
**Geppetto**: I worked so hard. I should have thought.  
_Your Nubbin hops out of the cap. The street is empty._  
_Pinocchio runs home across the fields, fast as a hare._  
_The room under the stairs is very quiet._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when a room feels empty and quiet  
> _The room feels lonely. What helps when you feel lonely?_  
> - ✅ Cuddle a friend or a toy. → Yes. A cuddle helps. So does telling someone.
> - ✅ Telling a grown-up. → Yes. Telling someone you trust helps too.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about what helps when we feel lonely._


## A13-3. The Talking-cricket

- `a13-03-s1`: Find what is going cri-cri-cri in the dark. · _Listen along the wall by the hearth._
- `a13-03-s2`: Listen to the Talking-cricket. Then see what happened at the hearth. · _Hear him out. Then go and look._

#### `a13-03-cri`

_Pinocchio shuts the door and sighs. A whole room, all his!_  
**Pinocchio**: Mine. The chair, the table, the painted fire.  
_Then, a small sound. Cri, cri, cri._  
**Pinocchio**: Who is that?  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): sound words: cri, cri, cri  
> _A cricket goes cri, cri, cri. Can you make the sound?_  
> _What sound does a dog make? A duck?_  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-word:cri`
> _For grown-ups: Made animal and sound words, like cri, cri, cri._

_Your Nubbin’s ears go straight up._  

#### `a13-03-cri-done`

_On the wall climbs a big cricket. He looks very grand._  
**The Talking-cricket**: I am the Talking-cricket. I have lived here a hundred years.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): where a cricket lives and what it does  
> _Crickets chirp by rubbing their wings. Where do real crickets live?_  
> - ✅ In grass, and in cosy cracks. → Yes! They hide in grass, under stones and in warm cracks.
> - In the sea. → Not the sea. Crickets live on land, in grass and in cosy cracks.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that crickets live in grass and cracks and chirp with their wings._


#### `a13-03-cricket`

**The Talking-cricket**: Listen, Pinocchio. Be kind to your babbo. Go to school.  
**Pinocchio**: I would rather chase butterflies.  
**The Talking-cricket**: Then you will be sorry.  
_Pinocchio picks up a mallet and throws it. He is not really aiming._  
_Thump! The cricket tumbles off the wall, into the ash._  
**Pinocchio**: Oh! I did not mean to!  
_(The cricket is only dazed. He is a very tough old cricket.)_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): what to do after hurting someone by accident: check they are all right  
> _The mallet bumped the cricket. What should Pinocchio do now?_  
> - ✅ Go and check he is all right. → Yes. When we hurt someone, we go and see if they are all right.
> - Pretend nothing happened. → Pretending does not help. Going to check, and saying sorry, does.
> _For grown-ups: Practised what to do after an accident that hurts someone: check, and say sorry._


**Choices**

- **Look in the hearth for the cricket.**
    - You look in the ash. Your Nubbin finds him! Squeak!
    - **The Talking-cricket**: I am not hurt. I am cross. Cross, not hurt.
    - You carry him to the hedge on a leaf. He is safe.
    - **The Talking-cricket**: Thank you, kind friend.
- **Wait. Give the cricket a little time.**
    - You wait. Later you see a tiny track in the ash.
    - It goes to the crack under the door. The cricket walked away, grumbling.

#### `a13-03-cricket-done`

_The room is quiet. Pinocchio rests his chin on his fists._  
**Pinocchio**: Anyway. I am hungry.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming a feeling: hungry, and also a little sorry  
> _Pinocchio’s tummy is rumbling. But is he feeling something else too?_  
> - ✅ A little sorry. → Yes. He is sorry, and he cannot say it yet.
> - Only hungry. → He is hungry. But his quiet face looks a little sorry too.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed a feeling that is hiding behind another one._


#### `a13-03-complete`

_Night comes. Pinocchio’s tummy rumbles like a small dog._  
**Pinocchio**: Is there any supper? Somewhere?  
_Your Nubbin curls up against your boot._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): day and night: it gets dark at night  
> _Night comes when our side of the Earth turns away from the Sun._  
> _The Sun is still there. We just cannot see it._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that night comes as our side of the Earth turns away from the Sun._

_Outside, the wind is getting up._  

## A13-4. The Flying Egg

- `a13-04-s1`: Help Pinocchio look for something to eat. · _Try the cupboard, the drawers and the heap in the corner._
- `a13-04-s2`: Watch Pinocchio cook his egg. · _Stand back from the pan._
- `a13-04-s3`: Go with Pinocchio into the storm, to the village. · _Keep your Nubbin under your coat._

#### `a13-04-hungry`

_Pinocchio runs to the pot on the fire. His nose goes right through!_  
**Pinocchio**: Painted. Even the soup is painted.  
_He tries the drawers. A button. A cork. A bent nail._  
_Your Nubbin digs in the heap in the corner._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.B.3, do): sort things into groups: things you can eat and things you cannot  
> _Button, cork, nail. Can you eat any of them? No!_  
> _Sort them: how many things can we eat? None!_  
> Check: `edu:sort:drawer-things:edible`
> _For grown-ups: Sorted objects into things we can eat and things we cannot._


**Choices**

- **Dig with your Nubbin.**
    - You dig too. It is not grand, but it is company.
- **Tell Pinocchio there is sure to be something.**
    - **Pinocchio**: There had better be. I am empty all the way through.

#### `a13-04-hungry-done`

_In the heap is something round and white. An egg!_  
**Pinocchio**: An egg! I will fry it!  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-LS1-2, ask): eggs come from hens, and a chick grows inside  
> _Who laid the egg? A hen! And what might grow inside a hen’s egg?_  
> - ✅ A chick! → Yes! A chick grows inside, with its mother hen keeping it warm.
> - A fish. → Fish eggs are in the water. A hen’s egg can grow a chick.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a chick can grow inside a hen’s egg._


#### `a13-04-egg`

_He puts a pan on the brazier. The water steams._  
_He cracks the egg. Out pops a fluffy chick!_  
**The Chick**: Thank you, Pinocchio, for helping me out. Good evening!  
_The chick flies out of the window and away._  
**Pinocchio**: Oh. The cricket was right. I wish I had not run off.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): saying what you wish you had done differently  
> _Pinocchio wishes he had stayed home. What could he do now?_  
> - ✅ Say sorry, and try again. → Yes. Saying sorry and trying again is brave.
> - Hide under the bed. → Hiding feels safe for a bit. But sorry and trying again help more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying sorry and starting again._


#### `a13-04-egg-done`

_Outside, the wind is a storm. Pinocchio puts his cap on._  
**Pinocchio**: There is a village. Someone will give me bread. I will ask nicely.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): a polite way to ask: please and thank you  
> _Pinocchio says he will ask nicely. Nice words are please and thank you._  
> _Say them with me: please. Thank you._  
> _For grown-ups: Practised polite words for asking: please and thank you._


#### `a13-04-storm`

_The night is black. Thunder rumbles over the hills._  
_Every window in the village is shut tight._  
_Pinocchio pulls a doorbell, again and again._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, do): weather words: thunder, lightning, wind, rain  
> _Point to what you can hear in a storm._  
> _Rumble, rumble: thunder! Whoosh: wind! Pitter-patter: rain!_  
> Check: `edu:name:weather:storm`
> _For grown-ups: Named weather words and sounds in a storm._

**Old Man in a Nightcap**: What do you want at this hour?  
**Pinocchio**: A bit of bread, please.  
**Old Man in a Nightcap**: Wait there.  
_Splash! He tips a basin of water over Pinocchio’s head._  

#### `a13-04-storm-done`

_You walk home together, dripping._  
_Your Nubbin is dry under your coat._  
_Pinocchio puts his wet feet on the brazier. He falls asleep._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-PS3-1, ask): a hot fire dries wet things and can burn wood  
> _Pinocchio’s feet are wet. What dries them faster, something warm or something cold?_  
> - ✅ Something warm. → Yes. Warmth dries things. But wood must not get too close to a fire!
> - Something cold. → Cold is slow. Warm air dries things faster. A fire is very warm, so we keep wood far from it.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that warmth dries wet things, and that wood must stay away from a fire._


#### `a13-04-complete`

**Pinocchio**: Babbo!  
_He jumps up, and falls on his face._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): being kind to someone who made a mistake  
> _Pinocchio’s feet are gone. Will Geppetto be kind or cross?_  
> - ✅ Kind. He loves Pinocchio. → Yes. Geppetto will be kind, and he will mend the feet.
> - Cross, and walk away. → He might be a bit cross. But watch, he stays and helps.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about being kind to someone who has had an accident._

## A13-5. Three Pears

- `a13-05-s1`: Let Geppetto in. · _Give Geppetto a hand over the window sill._
- `a13-05-s2`: Help with breakfast: three pears, peeled. · _Do not throw the peel away. You will see._
- `a13-05-s3`: Wait at the window while Geppetto goes out into the snow. · _Keep the room warm. Watch the road._

#### `a13-05-window`

**Pinocchio**: Babbo, I cannot open the door! My feet are gone!  
_Geppetto climbs in through the window. It is a small window!_  
_You lean out and take his arm. Up he comes._  
**Geppetto**: Now, you young— Oh. Oh, my boy. Your feet.  
_He came to scold. He looks at the feet, and hugs him instead._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): choosing kindness over scolding when someone is hurt  
> _Geppetto wanted to scold. Then he hugged. Why did he change?_  
> - ✅ He saw Pinocchio needed help. → Yes. When someone needs help, a hug comes first.
> - He forgot he was cross. → He did not forget. He chose to be kind first. That is a strong thing to do.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about choosing kindness first when someone needs help._


#### `a13-05-window-done`

**Pinocchio**: I am so hungry, Babbo.  
_Geppetto takes three pears from his pocket. It is his own breakfast._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count three pears  
> _Point and count the pears. One, two, three._  
> _Three pears. How many is that? Three!_  
> Check: `edu:count:pears:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three pears._

_He holds them out and says nothing about it._  

#### `a13-05-pears`

**Pinocchio**: Peel them for me, please. I only like them peeled.  
_Geppetto peels all three. He puts the peel and cores aside._  
_Pinocchio gobbles up all three pears. Munch, munch, munch!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a pear has seeds in its core, and seeds grow into trees  
> _The core of a pear has little brown seeds._  
> _A seed can grow into a pear tree!_  
> _It needs soil, water and sun._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a seed in a pear’s core can grow into a tree._

**Pinocchio**: I am still hungry.  
**Geppetto**: I have only the peel and the cores.  
_Pinocchio looks at them for quite a while._  

**Choices**

- **Ask Geppetto if he has eaten.**
    - **Geppetto**: Me? Oh yes. Ages ago.
    - His tummy rumbles loudly. He talks over it.
- **Put the peel and cores on a plate for later.**
    - You put them on a plate. The plate waits.

#### `a13-05-pears-done`

_A minute later the peel is gone, and the cores too._  
**Pinocchio**: I feel very well now.  
**Geppetto**: You see? It does not pay to be too fussy.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): sharing: Geppetto gave away his own breakfast  
> _Geppetto gave away his breakfast. What is that called?_  
> - ✅ Sharing. It is kind. → Yes! Sharing is giving some of what you have to someone else.
> - Being silly. → It is not silly. It is sharing, and it is one of the kindest things there is.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about sharing: giving some of what you have to someone else._


#### `a13-05-snow`

_Geppetto makes new feet for Pinocchio. They are his best yet._  
_From the scraps, he starts a little wooden Nubbin for you._  
**Geppetto**: I will finish it tomorrow. There is always tomorrow for small things.  
_He makes Pinocchio a paper suit with flowers on it, and bark shoes._  
**Pinocchio**: But I need a spelling-book for school.  
_Geppetto has no money. He puts on his old patched coat and goes out._  
_It is snowing._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a coat keeps you warm by holding your body’s warmth in  
> _A thick coat holds your warmth close, like a hug._  
> _In snow, a coat helps a lot._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a warm coat keeps our own body warmth in._


#### `a13-05-coat`

_Geppetto comes home in the snow. He has a new spelling-book._  
**Pinocchio**: Babbo, where is your coat?  
**Geppetto**: I sold it. I was too warm.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character feels from what he says and does  
> _Geppetto said “I was too warm.” But it was snowing!_  
> _Why did he say that?_  
> - ✅ So Pinocchio would not feel bad. → Yes. He gave something up, and he did not want Pinocchio to worry.
> - Because he was hot. → It was snowy! He was kind, and he did not want Pinocchio to worry.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out why a character said something kind that was not quite true._

_Pinocchio hugs him tight. He understands._

> _Atchoo! A sneeze clears tickles out of your nose._  
> _We sneeze into our elbow, like this. (Show how.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sneeze clears the nose and practised sneezing into an elbow._

> - The pile of two. → Count them: five logs, then two logs. Five is more.

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): helping a friend, even when it is hard  
> _Pinocchio spoke up for his friend. What was that?_  
> - ✅ Brave and kind. → Yes! It takes courage to stand up for a friend.
> - Silly. → Not silly. It was brave and kind, and it saved Harlequin.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about standing up for a friend._

_Fire-eater’s nose twitches. Atchoo! Atchoo! Atchoo!_  

#### `a13-07-harlequin-done`

**Fire-eater**: Oh, very well! Nobody burns tonight.

> _Let us dance with the puppets! Clap and stamp to a steady beat._  
> _Clap, clap, stamp. Clap, clap, stamp._  
> Check: `edu:clap:beat:dance`
> _For grown-ups: Danced and clapped to a steady beat._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Eco.1.K-2, ask): choosing: money can buy a coat or a toy, but not both

> _We cannot buy both. We have to choose._

> - The toy. → A toy is fun. But Babbo is cold. When we cannot have both, we choose what matters most.

## A13-8. The Fox and the Cat

- `a13-08-s1`: Walk home with Pinocchio and his five gold pieces. · _Watch who you meet on the road._
- `a13-08-s2`: Stop for supper at the Inn of the Red Craw-fish. · _Pinocchio is paying. He does not know yet._

#### `a13-08-road`

_On the road you meet a lame Fox and a blind Cat._  
**The Fox**: Good day, Pinocchio.  
**Pinocchio**: How do you know my name?  
**The Fox**: I know your babbo. I saw him shivering at his door.  
**Pinocchio**: Look! Five gold pieces. I am buying Babbo a coat!  
_The Fox stretches out his lame leg._  
_The Cat opens his eyes, then shuts them._  
_Nobody sees but you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): staying safe with people you have just met: check with a grown-up you trust  
> _A stranger knows your name and wants your money. What should you do?_  
> - ✅ Say no, and tell a grown-up I trust. → Yes! Always check with a grown-up you trust first.
> - Give it to them. → Not yet! Strangers can be tricky. Check with a grown-up you trust first.
> _For grown-ups: Practised staying safe: check with a trusted grown-up before trusting someone new._


**Choices**

- **Warn him. The Cat opened its eyes.**
    - **Pinocchio**: Shame on you. He is blind!
    - **The Cat**: We forgive you, traveller.
- **Say nothing yet, and watch the Fox.**
    - The Fox sees you watching. He smiles with all his teeth.

#### `a13-08-road-done`

**The Fox**: Would you like to make five gold pieces into a thousand?  
**The Fox**: Plant a coin in the Field of Miracles.  
**The Fox**: A tree will grow with gold on it!  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, ask): plants grow from seeds, not coins; they need soil, water and sun  
> _Can a gold coin grow into a tree? What grows into a tree?_  
> - ✅ A seed! → Yes! A seed, with soil, water and sun.
> - A gold coin. → Coins are metal. They cannot grow. Only a seed can, with soil, water and sun.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that trees grow from seeds, not from coins._

_A white blackbird calls to Pinocchio not to listen._  
_The Cat leaps. The blackbird flies away safe._  

#### `a13-08-inn`

_At night you reach the Inn of the Red Craw-fish._  
_The Cat orders lots and lots of fish. The Fox orders chicken._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): fish live in water and breathe with gills  
> _The Cat ordered fish. Where do fish live?_  
> - ✅ In the water. → Yes! Fish live in water and breathe with gills.
> - Up in the trees. → Birds live in trees. Fish live in water, and breathe through gills.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that fish live in water and breathe through gills._

_Pinocchio is too excited to eat. He has a walnut._  
**Pinocchio**: Tonight a seed. Tomorrow a tree!  

**Choices**

- **Ask who is paying for all this.**
    - **The Fox**: Paying? Among friends? What a question!
- **Wrap Pinocchio’s leftover bread for his pocket.**
    - You tuck the bread in his pocket. He will be glad of it later.

#### `a13-08-inn-done`

_At midnight the innkeeper knocks. The Fox and Cat have gone ahead._  
**Innkeeper**: They said you would pay. One gold piece.  
_Pinocchio pays. He had five gold pieces. Now he has four._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, do): take away one from five: 5 − 1 = 4  
> _Pinocchio had five gold pieces. He paid one._  
> _Take one away. How many are left? Count: four!_  
> Check: `edu:count:gold-left:4`
> _For grown-ups: Took one away from five to make four._


#### `a13-08-complete`

_The night is very dark. Something rustles in the hedge._

**Pinocchio**: Not you. I am not listening.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when the dark feels scary  
> _Pinocchio hears a noise in the dark. What helps when you feel scared?_  
> - ✅ Stay close to a friend. → Yes. Stay near someone safe.
> - ✅ Tell myself it is only the dark. → Yes. Breathe slowly, and remind yourself you are safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when the dark feels scary._

_He walks faster. There is only dark in the hedge._  

## A13-9. The Assassins

- `a13-09-s1`: Keep close to Pinocchio on the dark road. · _Stay on the road._
- `a13-09-s2`: Run after Pinocchio across the fields. · _Follow the clack of his feet. Jump the ditch._

#### `a13-09-sacks`

_Behind you, two shapes in black sacks hop along._  
**Pinocchio**: Robbers!  
_Pinocchio pops the gold under his tongue, quick as a squirrel._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): squirrels hide food to eat later  
> _Squirrels hide nuts in the ground and in trees._  
> _They find them later, in winter._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that squirrels store food to eat later._

**The Taller Sack**: Give us your gold!  
_Pinocchio cannot answer. His mouth is full of gold!_  
**The Shorter Sack**: Hand it over, or else!  
_One sounds just like a Fox with a cold._  

**Choices**

- **Grab a stick and stand with him.**
    - You grab a stick. A sack takes it politely. You land in the ditch.
    - Your Nubbin hops in after you.
- **Pick up your Nubbin and shout for help.**
    - You shout till the hills shout back. Nobody comes.

#### `a13-09-sacks-done`

_A sack grabs Pinocchio’s chin. Chomp! Pinocchio bites hard._  
_The sack yowls just like a cat, and lets go._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhymes: chin and pin  
> _Chin. Does it rhyme with pin, or with sock?_  
> - ✅ Pin! → Yes! Chin, pin. They rhyme.
> - Sock. → Chin, pin: same ending sound. Sock is different.
> _For grown-ups: Found a rhyme: chin and pin._

_Pinocchio hops over the hedge and runs._  

#### `a13-09-chase`

_He runs across the fields. You run after him._  
_There is a muddy ditch. Pinocchio jumps over it. So do you!_  
_The sacks jump too, and land in the middle. Splash!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): position words: over, under, in the middle  
> _Pinocchio jumps OVER the ditch. The sacks land IN the ditch._  
> _Is the ditch under you when you jump?_  
> - ✅ Yes! I am over it. → Yes! Over the ditch means above it. Hop to show it.
> - No, it is beside me. → When you jump, the ditch is under you. You are over it.
> _For grown-ups: Used position words: over, under and in._

_Far off there is a little white house. Pinocchio knocks._  
**Pinocchio**: Help! Open up! Please!  
_A girl with blue hair opens the window. She has her eyes shut._  
**The Fairy**: Nobody is home. I am only waiting.  
_The window closes softly._  

#### `a13-09-chase-done`

_The sacks catch Pinocchio at the door. They shake him._  
_They hang him by his paper jacket from the Big Oak._  
_He dangles like a coat on a peg. He is not hurt._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): asking for help when you are stuck  
> _Pinocchio is stuck on a branch. What can he do?_  
> - ✅ Call for help. → Yes. Calling for help is clever, not silly.
> - Stay quiet. → If we are stuck, we can call for help. Someone will hear.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking for help when stuck._

**The Taller Sack**: We will be back in the morning.

## A13-11. The Nose

- `a13-11-s1`: Get Pinocchio to take his medicine. · _He will bargain. Sugar first, then the glass._
- `a13-11-s2`: Stay while the Fairy asks about the gold. · _Stand where he can see you._

#### `a13-11-medicine`

**The Fairy**: Drink this, and you will be well in a day or two.  
**Pinocchio**: Is it sweet or bitter?  
**The Fairy**: Bitter. But it is good for you.  
**Pinocchio**: Then I want a lump of sugar first.  
_Crunch! He eats the sugar. He pushes the glass away._  
**Pinocchio**: Another lump. Then I will drink it. Probably.  
_In come four black rabbits, walking on their back legs._  
**Black Rabbit**: We heard you were not taking your medicine.  
**Pinocchio**: Give me the glass! Quick!  
_Gulp! He drinks it all. The rabbits go out, grumbling._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): take medicine only from a grown-up who looks after you, and as they say  
> _The Fairy gave Pinocchio his medicine. Who gives you medicine?_  
> - ✅ A grown-up who looks after me. → Yes. Only take medicine from a grown-up you trust.
> - I find it myself. → Never take medicine by yourself. Ask the grown-up who looks after you.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to take medicine only from a trusted grown-up._


#### `a13-11-medicine-done`

_In a few minutes Pinocchio jumps out of bed. He is well!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, do): add one more: 1 lump of sugar + 1 more = 2  
> _Pinocchio ate one lump of sugar. Then he asked for one more._  
> _One lump, and one more. Count them: one, two lumps!_  
> Check: `edu:add:sugar-lumps:2`
> _For grown-ups: Added one more to one to make two._

_Puppets get ill quickly, and well quickly._  

#### `a13-11-nose`

**The Fairy**: Now. Where are the four gold pieces?  
**Pinocchio**: I lost them.  
_That is a fib. His nose grows two fingers longer!_  
**Pinocchio**: I lost them in the wood.  
_His nose grows again. It bumps the bed and the window._  
**The Fairy**: Fibs are found out quickly, my boy.  
_He cannot get through the door. His nose is too long!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): honesty: telling the truth, even when it is hard  
> _Pinocchio fibbed. What is better to do?_  
> - ✅ Tell the truth. → Yes! The truth is easier to carry than a fib.
> - Fib again. → Another fib makes it grow more! The truth is better, and nobody needs to feel ashamed.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about telling the truth, even when it is hard, without shame._


**Choices**

- **Laugh, kindly. You cannot help it.**
    - **Pinocchio**: It is not funny!
    - It is a little funny. In a minute even he thinks so.
- **Tell him the coins are in his pocket. He knows.**
    - **Pinocchio**: They are in my pocket.
    - His nose stops growing. That is a start.

#### `a13-11-nose-done`

_Pinocchio cries for a while. The Fairy lets him._

_Tap, tap, tap! They peck his nose back to size._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): woodpeckers tap on trees with strong beaks to find food and make homes  
> _Real woodpeckers tap on trees. Tap, tap, tap!_  
> _Their strong beaks help them find bugs and make a home._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned how a woodpecker’s beak helps it find food and make a home._

> _For grown-ups: Talked about fairness and why punishing a person who was robbed is not fair._

> _Grapes grow on a vine. Whose grapes are these?_  
> - ✅ The farmer’s. We should ask first. → Yes! We always ask before we take something that is not ours.
> - Anyone’s. → They belong to the farmer, who grew them. We ask first.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking before taking what belongs to someone else._

_He is over the wall before you can speak._  

## A13-14. The Guard Dog

- `a13-14-s1`: Go after Pinocchio into the vineyard. · _Watch where you put your feet._
- `a13-14-s2`: Keep watch with Pinocchio by the hen-house. · _Sit in the dark. Be quiet when the visitors come._

#### `a13-14-trap`

_Pinocchio reaches for a grape. Snap! A trap closes on his ankles._  
_It does not hurt. He is made of wood._  
_But it will not let go._  
**Pinocchio**: Help! Get it off!  
_At dark, a farmer comes with a lantern._  
**The Farmer**: So you are the one who has been at my hens.  
**Pinocchio**: No! I only wanted two bunches of grapes!  
**The Farmer**: My old dog Melampo died this morning. He was very old.  
**The Farmer**: You can be my watchdog tonight.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): owning up and saying sorry  
> _Pinocchio took grapes that were not his. What should he say now?_  
> - ✅ I am sorry. I should have asked. → Yes! Owning up and saying sorry is brave.
> - It was not me. → The truth is better. Say sorry, and put it right.
> _For grown-ups: Practised owning up and saying sorry._


**Choices**

- **Tell the farmer he is only a hungry puppet.**
    - **The Farmer**: Then he will be a hungry watchdog. It is one night.
    - **The Farmer**: The kennel is dry.
- **Help Pinocchio settle into the kennel straw.**
    - You shake out the straw. Pinocchio sits there, the saddest dog in Tuscany.

#### `a13-14-trap-done`

_The farmer puts a brass collar on Pinocchio, on a long chain._  
**The Farmer**: If thieves come, bark. Goodnight.  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-2, notice): dogs hear and smell much better than people, which helps them guard  
> _Real dogs are good guards. They hear tiny sounds and smell very well._  
> _A dog’s nose is much better than ours._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that dogs have very good hearing and sense of smell._

**Pinocchio**: The cricket said this would happen.  

#### `a13-14-martens`

_Around midnight, four long little shapes slip out of the dark._  
_They are martens. They smell of hens._  
**Marten**: Good evening, Melampo.  
**Pinocchio**: I am not Melampo.  
**Marten**: You look reasonable. Keep quiet, and we will share the hens.  
**Pinocchio**: Oh yes. Go right in.  
_One by one, they go into the hen-house._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count four martens going in  
> _Four martens go into the hen-house. Count them as they go in._  
> _One, two, three, four!_  
> Check: `edu:count:martens:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four martens one by one._

_Pinocchio shuts the door. He rolls a stone against it._  
_Bow-wow! Bow-wow! Bow-wow!_  

#### `a13-14-martens-done`

_The farmer runs out in his nightshirt, with a lantern._  
_He puts all four martens in a sack._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): some animals are awake at night: owls, bats, martens  
> _The martens came at night. Which animal is also awake at night?_  
> - ✅ An owl. → Yes! Owls and bats come out at night.
> - A butterfly. → Butterflies sleep at night. Owls and bats are up at night.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that some animals, like owls and bats, are awake at night._

**The Farmer**: Well done, dog! Well done, boy. Whatever you are.  

#### `a13-14-complete`

**The Farmer**: And Melampo, all those years. Did he take hens off them?  
_Pinocchio knows the answer. He looks at the empty kennel._  
**Pinocchio**: Melampo was a good old dog. Let him keep his good name.  
**Pinocchio**: It costs nothing.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): speaking kindly about someone who is not there  
> _Pinocchio kept quiet about the old dog’s tricks. Was that kind?_  
> - ✅ Yes. Kind words cost nothing. → Yes. Choosing kind words is a gift.
> - No. He should have told. → Telling the truth matters. But kind words, said gently, can be true and kind.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about choosing kind words about others._

_The farmer lets him go. He gives you grapes for the road._  

## A13-15. The Stone and the Pigeon

- `a13-15-s1`: Go with Pinocchio to the Fairy’s white house. · _Through the wood, past the Big Oak._
- `a13-15-s2`: Follow the Pigeon to the sea. · _You take the coast road. Hurry._

#### `a13-15-stone`

_Pinocchio runs to the Big Oak. The little white house is gone._  
_There is only grass, and a small white stone with words on it._  
**Pinocchio**: What does it say? I cannot read. I sold my book.  
_You kneel by the stone. Your Nubbin brushes leaves off it._  
**Pinocchio**: Read it. Please.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first letters: P for Pinocchio  
> _Pinocchio’s name starts with P, p, p. Which word starts with P too?_  
> - ✅ Pear! → Yes! P, p, pear. P, p, Pinocchio.
> - Bell. → Bell starts with b. Pear starts with p, like Pinocchio.
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first letter of Pinocchio’s name: P, like pear._


**Choices**

- **Read it exactly as it is written.**
    - **You**: “Here the girl with blue hair waited for her little brother Pinocchio.”
    - **You**: “He did not come. She went away, missing him.”
    - Pinocchio sits down on the grass, very suddenly.
- **Read it gently, and say it in small pieces.**
    - **You**: It says she waited for you. Then she had to go away.
    - **Pinocchio**: Read the rest, please.
    - **You**: “…and she went away, missing him.”
    - Pinocchio sits down on the grass, very suddenly.

#### `a13-15-stone-done`

_He cries all night. The hills cry back in echoes._  
**Pinocchio**: Little Fairy, come back. Where is Babbo?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): it is all right to cry; hugs and telling someone help  
> _Pinocchio is very sad, and he is crying. Is it all right to cry?_  
> - ✅ Yes. Crying is okay. → Yes. Crying lets sadness out. A hug helps too.
> - No. Be brave. → Being brave includes crying. It is all right. A hug helps.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that crying is all right and that a hug or telling someone helps._


#### `a13-15-pigeon`

_In the morning a great Pigeon circles down._  
**The Pigeon**: Do you know a puppet called Pinocchio?  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): pigeons can find their way home and carry messages  
> _Real pigeons can find their way home from far away._  
> _Long ago, people used them to carry messages._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that pigeons find their way home and once carried messages._

**Pinocchio**: It is me!  
**The Pigeon**: Your babbo is by the sea.  
**The Pigeon**: He is building a little boat to look for you.  
**Pinocchio**: Babbo! Can you take me?  
**The Pigeon**: Climb on my back. Traveller, it is the coast road for you.  
_Off they go over the trees. You walk all day._  

#### `a13-15-pigeon-done`

_At dawn you come out on the shore._  
_A crowd points out to sea. A tiny boat is rowing._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): the shore is where land meets sea; Tuscany’s sea is on its west side  
> _The shore is where the land meets the sea._  
> _Tuscany is in the middle of Italy. Its sea is on the west side._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the shore is where land meets sea, and that Tuscany’s sea is to the west._

_Pinocchio is on a rock, waving his cap._  

#### `a13-15-complete`

**Pinocchio**: Babbo! BABBO! It is me!  
_The little old man waves back._  
_A big wave hides the boat from view._  
**Pinocchio**: I will help him!  
_Pinocchio jumps in. Wood floats, so he swims like a fish._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, do): wood floats; some things sink  
> _Wood floats. A stone sinks. Sort these: wood, stone, leaf, key._  
> _Floaters: wood and leaf. Sinkers: stone and key._  
> Check: `edu:sort:float-or-sink:wood`
> _For grown-ups: Sorted things into floaters and sinkers and learned that wood floats._


## A13-16. The Island of Busy Bees

- `a13-16-s1`: Cross to the island and find Pinocchio. · _A fishing boat will take you. Look for the puppet asking for a penny._
- `a13-16-s2`: Help carry the water home. · _Pinocchio takes one can. Your Nubbin tries the other._
- `a13-16-s3`: Walk Pinocchio to the island school. · _He has promised. Walk beside him._

#### `a13-16-island`

_A fishing boat takes you over. This is the Island of Busy Bees._  
_Everyone here is busy. Pinocchio is very hungry._  
_He asks everyone for a penny._  
**Coalman**: Help me pull my coal cart, and I will give you forty pennies.  
**Pinocchio**: Pull a cart? I am not a donkey!  
_A bricklayer says he can carry bricks for his supper._  
**Pinocchio**: Bricks are heavy. Look at my arms.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): everybody’s work matters, and we respect people who do it  
> _The coalman and the bricklayer both work hard. Are their jobs important?_  
> - ✅ Yes. Every job helps. → Yes! Coal heats homes. Bricks build them. We say thank you to workers.
> - No. They are just jobs. → Every job helps someone. Coal keeps us warm. Bricks build our homes.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why every job matters and why we respect workers._


**Choices**

- **Carry a hod of bricks yourself, to show him.**
    - You carry them. They are heavy. Your Nubbin carries one brick, proudly.
- **Tell him work is not the end of the world.**
    - **Pinocchio**: It is the end of the morning. That is worse.
    - But he watches the coal cart go. He might follow.

#### `a13-16-island-done`

_Along the street comes a little woman, carrying two cans of water._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count two cans  
> _The woman carries two cans. Count them: one, two._  
> Check: `edu:count:cans:2`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two cans of water._


#### `a13-16-water`

**Pinocchio**: Good woman, may I have a drink?  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): all living things need water  
> _Pinocchio drinks water. Who else needs water to live?_  
> - ✅ Plants, animals and people. → Yes! Everything alive needs water.
> - Only fish. → Fish need water. So do plants, animals and you!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that all living things need water._

**A Little Woman**: Drink. Then carry a can home for me, and I will give you bread.  
_Pinocchio picks up the can. It is as big as he is!_  
_Your Nubbin tries the other can. Splash! Into a puddle._  
_At her house, he eats bread and a cream sweet._  
**Pinocchio**: You have blue hair. Like her. Just like her!  
_The little woman only smiles._  
**Pinocchio**: It is you! You grew up!  
**The Fairy**: Then call me mother, if you like.  

#### `a13-16-water-done`

**Pinocchio**: Why did you grow, and I did not?  
**Pinocchio**: I am the same as the day I was carved.  
**The Fairy**: Puppets do not grow. They stay as they were made.  
**Pinocchio**: I am tired of being wood! I want to be a boy!  
**The Fairy**: You can be. But nobody can earn it for you.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): growing takes time and trying, and nobody can do it for you  
> _Children grow by trying, a little every day. What can you try today?_  
> - ✅ Something new, a little bit. → Yes! A little try every day helps us grow.
> - Nothing. I will wait. → Waiting is fine sometimes. But a little try helps us grow.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about growing by trying a little each day._


#### `a13-16-school`

**Pinocchio**: I will be good. I will go to school.  
**The Fairy**: If you are good, I think you will see Babbo again.  
_Next morning he goes to school. He is the only wooden boy in forty._  
_The boys hang their caps on his nose!_  
_He puts up with it for a morning. Then they all like him._  
_The teacher praises him. He is first through the door._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the beats in a word: puppet, school, teacher  
> _Clap the beats in the word puppet: pup-pet. Two claps!_  
> _School has one clap. Teacher has two: teach-er._  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:puppet`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the beats (syllables) in puppet, school and teacher._


#### `a13-16-school-done`

_The atlas turns a page. A whole school year goes by._  
_Pinocchio comes top in the tests._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, notice): a year has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter  
> _A school year goes through all four seasons._  
> _Spring, summer, autumn, winter. Then spring again._  
> _For grown-ups: Named the four seasons in order._


#### `a13-16-complete`

**The Fairy**: I am pleased with you. Go on like this.  
**Pinocchio**: I will. You will see.  
_He means it, at the time._  
_Your Nubbin has been to school too._  
_It can sit still for nearly a minute._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps you sit still and listen  
> _Your Nubbin is learning to sit still. What helps you sit still and listen?_  
> - ✅ A slow breath. → Yes. Breathe in slowly, and out. Try it now.
> - ✅ Wiggling my toes quietly. → That helps too! Little quiet wiggles can keep you calm.
> _For grown-ups: Practised calm breathing and quiet ways to stay still._


## A13-17. The Dog-fish Trick

- `a13-17-s1`: Go down to the beach with Pinocchio and the schoolboys. · _Keep up. They are running._
- `a13-17-s2`: Keep clear of the fight on the beach. · _You cannot stop it. Watch the books._
- `a13-17-s3`: Get Alidoro out of the sea. · _Wade in from the shallows._
- `a13-17-s4`: Find Pinocchio along the shore. · _Look for smoke coming out of a cave._

#### `a13-17-lure`

**Schoolboy**: Pinocchio! The Terrible Dog-fish is on the beach! Come and see!  
**Pinocchio**: After school. We will go after school.  
**Schoolboy**: After school he will be gone!  
_The boys are already running._  
_Pinocchio looks at the school. Then at the road to the sea._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): it is all right to say no when friends push you to break a promise  
> _The boys want Pinocchio to skip school. What can he say?_  
> - ✅ No, thank you. I will go after school. → Yes! Saying no kindly takes courage.
> - Yes, let us go. → That is what he does. But we can say no kindly, and keep a promise.
> _For grown-ups: Practised saying no kindly when friends push you._


**Choices**

- **Tell him: school first, the beach after.**
    - **Pinocchio**: After! Everything is after!
    - He runs. You follow, because somebody should.
- **Go with him. You want to see the Dog-fish too.**
    - You go. It is a silly idea. The sun is out.

#### `a13-17-lure-done`

_At the beach the sea is flat and empty, smooth as a plate._  
_There is no Dog-fish. There never was._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): wind makes waves on the sea  
> _The sea is flat today. What makes waves on the sea?_  
> - ✅ Wind. → Yes! Wind blows over the water and makes waves.
> - Fish. → Big fish can make ripples. But most waves come from wind.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that wind makes waves on the sea._


#### `a13-17-fight`

**Schoolboy**: Ha! You came! You make us look bad, being good.  
_Somebody pushes somebody. Soon there is a fight._  
_They throw their school books. The books splash into the sea._  
_The fish nibble a page and swim off._  
_A big book hits a boy called Eugene on the head. He sits down._  
_Everyone runs. Except Pinocchio. He wets his hanky in the sea for Eugene’s head._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): a kind rule: hands are for helping, books are for reading  
> _The boys threw books. What is a kind rule for hands and books?_  
> - ✅ Hands are for helping. → Yes! Hands help. Books are for reading, not throwing.
> - Throw the books. → Throwing can hurt someone. Hands are for helping. Books are for reading.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about a kind rule: hands are for helping._


#### `a13-17-fight-done`

**Eugene**: Ow. Who threw the sums?  
_Eugene sits up. He has a bump like half an egg._  
_He is all right._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): a cold cloth helps a bump; tell a grown-up if you bump your head  
> _Eugene has a bump on his head. What helps? And who do you tell?_  
> - ✅ A cold cloth, and tell a grown-up. → Yes! A cool cloth helps, and a grown-up should always know.
> - Nothing. Keep playing. → A bump on the head needs a rest. A cool cloth helps, and tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a cold cloth helps a bump, and that we tell a grown-up about a bump on the head._

_Two carabineers come down the beach. They see a wooden boy and a book._  
_Pinocchio runs. They let their dog off after him._  

#### `a13-17-alidoro`

_The dog is a big mastiff called Alidoro._  
_Pinocchio throws himself into the sea. Alidoro goes in after him._  
_Alidoro cannot swim. Splash, glug, splash!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, do): sound words: splash, glug, plop  
> _Splash! Glug! Plop! Those are sound words._  
> _Say them in a big voice, then a small voice._  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-words:splash`
> _For grown-ups: Said sound words: splash, glug and plop._

**Alidoro**: Help! Pinocchio! Save me!  
**Pinocchio**: If I save you, will you promise not to chase me?  
**Alidoro**: I promise! Anything!  

#### `a13-17-alidoro-done`

_Pinocchio swims back and catches Alidoro by the tail._  
_You wade in and take the other end._  
_Out comes the dog, like a wet carpet._  
**Alidoro**: You saved me. I do not forget a thing like that.  
_He shakes himself all over you, and trots off home._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): kindness comes back around  
> _Pinocchio helped the dog who chased him. What do you think the dog feels?_  
> - ✅ Thankful. → Yes! Thankful. And kindness often comes back around.
> - Cross. → He was in trouble. Now he is thankful. Kindness often comes back around.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being thankful, and about kindness coming back around._


#### `a13-17-fisher`

_Round the point there is a cave with smoke in it._  
_A fisherman is frying fish. He is green all over, even his beard!_  
_He has a net of fish. In the middle is Pinocchio._  
**The Green Fisherman**: Mullet, in the pan. Bream, in the pan. And what are you?  
**Pinocchio**: I am a puppet!  
_He rolls Pinocchio in flour from head to foot._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): flour is made by grinding grains like wheat; bread is made from flour  
> _Flour is made from grains, like wheat._  
> _People grind the grains to a soft powder._  
> _Then bakers use flour to make bread._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that flour is ground from grains like wheat and is used to bake bread._

**Pinocchio**: I am not a fish! Fish do not wear shoes!  

#### `a13-17-fisher-done`

_A big dog bounds into the cave. It is Alidoro, dry now._  
_He gently takes Pinocchio in his teeth, and is gone._  
**Alidoro**: Now we are even.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.C.6, ask): even means the same: one rescue each  
> _Pinocchio saved Alidoro. Alidoro saved Pinocchio. One rescue each._  
> _Is that more for one, or the same?_  
> - ✅ The same. We are even. → Yes! One and one. The same. Even!
> - More for Pinocchio. → One rescue each. That is the same, and that is what even means.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two groups and found them equal: even._


#### `a13-17-complete`

_Pinocchio goes to the Fairy’s house, floury as a loaf._  
_The Snail who keeps the door looks out of the top window._  
_It takes her nine hours to come down! Pinocchio falls asleep on the step._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): snails are slow because they glide on one muscly foot over a trail of slime  
> _Snails are slow. They glide on one soft foot._  
> _A trail of slime helps them slide. See the shiny path?_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a snail glides on one foot over a trail of slime._

**The Fairy**: Tomorrow you will stop being a puppet. You will be a boy.  
**Pinocchio**: Tomorrow? Really? I will invite everybody!  

## A13-18. The Land of Toys

- `a13-18-s1`: Go with Pinocchio to invite his friends. · _The last one on his list is the hardest to find._
- `a13-18-s2`: Find Pinocchio in the Land of Toys. · _Look anywhere there is noise._
- `a13-18-s3`: Stay near Pinocchio in the circus ring. · _Watch the lady in the box above the ring._

#### `a13-18-candlewick`

_The last friend on the list is Candlewick, thin and pale as a candle._  
_You find him at midnight, in a doorway, with a bundle._  
**Candlewick**: I am going to the Land of Toys! No schools. No books. Just holidays.  
**Pinocchio**: I cannot. I promised the Fairy.  
_A silent coach comes down the road, pulled by donkeys in white boots._  
_A Little Man drives it. He is as round and shiny as butter._  
**The Little Man**: Climb up, my dears. There is always room, for boys.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): play and learning both matter; a good day has some of each  
> _The Land of Toys has only play. What is a good day made of?_  
> - ✅ Some play, and some learning. → Yes! Play is great, and learning helps us grow. A good day has both.
> - Only play. → Play is wonderful. But a bit of learning and rest makes a good day.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about balance: a good day has play, learning and rest._


**Choices**

    - **Pinocchio**: That was ages ago! I will only stay a day.
    - He climbs up anyway.
- **Take his hand and turn him towards home.**
    - He lets you for three steps. Then he runs, and climbs up.

> _Donkeys carry loads and pull carts._  
> _They are gentle and strong._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a donkey is a strong farm animal with long ears._

_Poor boy, it says. Take care._

> - ✅ Soft and hairy. → Yes! Soft and hairy. Good describing words.
> - Hard and bumpy. → Donkey ears are soft and hairy. Hard and bumpy is like a stone.

> _Can you find a circle near you? A plate? A wheel?_

_A lady in a box has a locket with a puppet’s picture._  
_He tries to call to her. Out comes a bray!_  
_He catches his leg on a hoop. After that, he limps._

#### `a13-18-sea`

_Pinocchio swims away, laughing._

_Ahead, Pinocchio swims for a white rock._  
_A little goat with blue wool bleats at him._  
_Behind him, the sea rises._  
_A great head comes out, with a mouth like a cave._  
_It is the Terrible Dog-fish. It breathes in._  
_In goes Pinocchio, and in goes the sea. In go you!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a dog-fish is a kind of shark; the biggest shark eats only tiny food  
> _A dog-fish is a kind of shark._  
> _Real dog-fish are small, as long as a grown-up’s arm._  
> _The biggest shark is as long as a bus._  
> _It eats only tiny sea creatures!_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a dog-fish is a small shark, and that the biggest shark eats tiny food._


## A13-19. The Terrible Dog-fish

- `a13-19-s1`: Find your way through the dark inside the Dog-fish. · _Follow the faint light, far off._
- `a13-19-s2`: Go to the old man at the table. · _You know who it is. Let Pinocchio go first._
- `a13-19-s3`: Light the way to the Dog-fish’s mouth. · _Your Nubbin carries the candle. Walk softly._

#### `a13-19-belly`

_It is dark and wet in here. It smells of fried fish._  
**Pinocchio**: Help! Is anyone here?  
**The Tunny**: Only us unfortunates.  
**The Tunny**: I am a Tunny. I was swallowed too.  
**Pinocchio**: I am a puppet. And that is a traveller, and a Nubbin.  
_Far away, down the dark, there is a little light._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, ask): we need light to see  
> _It is very dark inside. Why can we see the little light far away?_  
> - ✅ Because it is a light in the dark. → Yes! We see things when there is light.
> - Because it is loud. → Light is not a sound. We see because of light.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we can see because of light._


**Choices**

- **Head for the light.**
    - You start towards it. Your Nubbin goes first. It has the best eyes.
- **Ask the Tunny how big the Dog-fish is.**
    - **The Tunny**: Very big. I never counted the tail.
    - You decide to head for the light.

#### `a13-19-belly-done`

_The light is a candle, stuck in a green glass bottle._  
_At the table sits an old man, white as snow._  
_He is eating a tiny fish._

> _On the table: a candle, a bottle, a fish. Count them: one, two, three._  
> Check: `edu:count:table-things:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three things on a table._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): naming a feeling: relief and joy when you find someone you missed  
> _Pinocchio found his babbo. How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Happy, and relieved. → Yes! Happy and relieved. Both feelings together.
> - Cross. → Not cross. Look, he is hugging him. Happy and relieved.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feelings of joy and relief at finding someone you missed._

**Geppetto**: Hush. You are here.  
**Geppetto**: This is my last candle. When it goes out, we are in the dark.  
**Pinocchio**: Then we must get out. I can swim. I am wood.  
**Pinocchio**: I will carry you.

> _Geppetto says ciao. It is an Italian word for hello and for goodbye._  
> _Say it with me: chow!_

_Your Nubbin climbs on his shoulder._  
_He laughs for the first time in two years._

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): stars are far-away suns that we see at night  
> _Look! Stars! Stars are suns, very far away._  
> _We only see them at night, when our side of the Earth is dark._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that stars are far-away suns that we see at night._

_You climb over the soft tongue, quietly._  
**Pinocchio**: Babbo, climb on my back. Hold on tight.

_You try again, very quietly. Then you all jump into the sea._

_It is the Tunny! He swims up beneath them both, like a boat._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): asking for help, and helping, when someone is tired  
> _Pinocchio is too tired. What can he do?_  
> - ✅ Ask for help. → Yes! Asking for help is brave. And the Tunny came.
> - Try even harder alone. → Trying is good. But when we are too tired, we ask for help.

## A13-20. The Wheel and the Chair

- `a13-20-s1`: Walk with Pinocchio and Geppetto, and find shelter. · _Go slowly. Somebody is begging by the road._
- `a13-20-s2`: Stand by Pinocchio while he speaks to the Talking-cricket. · _Let him say it himself._
- `a13-20-s3`: Help Pinocchio earn a glass of milk at the water-wheel. · _A hundred buckets for one glass. Count with him._
- `a13-20-s4`: Keep Pinocchio company through the winter. · _He works every day now. The pennies are for a new coat._

#### `a13-20-road`

_Geppetto can hardly stand. You walk slowly up the road._  
_By the road sit a thin Fox with no tail, and a Cat._  
_The Cat cannot see now. Really cannot._  
**The Fox**: Oh, Pinocchio! Have pity on two poor creatures!  
**Pinocchio**: Goodbye, you cheats. You fooled me once. You will not fool me twice.  
_He walks on, holding his babbo up._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): you can be kind and careful at the same time  
> _The Fox and Cat tricked Pinocchio. Now they are hungry._  
> _What could kindness look like?_  
> - ✅ Share a little, and stay careful. → Yes. You can be kind and careful together.
> - Walk by without a word. → Walking on is safe. Kindness might share a little, and stay careful.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being kind and careful at the same time._


**Choices**

- **Give the Cat a crust from your pocket.**
    - You put a crust in the Cat’s paw. You say nothing.
    - **The Cat**: Thank you, Pinocchio. You were always the kind one.
    - Pinocchio’s ears go red. Nobody says anything.
- **Walk on with Pinocchio.**
    - You walk on. Behind you, the Fox says it was only the wind.

#### `a13-20-road-done`

_At the end of a lane is a little straw hut._  
_A sign on the door says PULL THE CORD. So Pinocchio does._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): signs tell us what to do: pull the cord  
> _A sign has words that tell us what to do. This one says PULL._  
> _Where else do you see signs? On a road? A shop?_  
> Check: `edu:read:sign:pull-the-cord`
> _For grown-ups: Talked about signs and how words on them tell us what to do._

_Inside, on a beam, sits the Talking-cricket._  

#### `a13-20-hut`

**The Talking-cricket**: Oh, my Pinocchio.  
**Pinocchio**: Oh, my dear little Cricket!  
**Pinocchio**: I am sorry about the mallet. Please forgive me.  
**The Talking-cricket**: I forgive you. I only wanted to remind you.  
**The Talking-cricket**: Be kind to everyone you can. Then someone may be kind to you.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character changes: the mallet then, sorry now  
> _At first Pinocchio threw a mallet at the cricket. What does he do now?_  
> - ✅ He says sorry. → Yes! He has changed. Saying sorry is hard, and he did it.
> - He throws another. → He does not! He has grown kinder. He says sorry.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed how a character changes from the start of a story to the end._


#### `a13-20-hut-done`

_Pinocchio lays his babbo on the straw._  
_Geppetto is so weak he can only smile._  
**Pinocchio**: Milk. He needs milk. I will get him some.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): milk comes from animals like cows and goats  
> _Milk comes from animals, like cows and goats._  
> _Milk is a good drink to help us grow strong._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that milk comes from animals like cows and goats._


#### `a13-20-wheel`

_The gardener, Giangio, has milk at a penny a glass. Pinocchio has no penny._  
**Giangio**: Then turn my water-wheel. A hundred buckets, and you can have a glass.  
_Pinocchio turns the wheel and you count. Ten, twenty, thirty!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count to 100 by tens  
> _Count with Pinocchio by tens. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty._  
> _Sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred!_  
> Check: `edu:count:by-tens:100`
> _For grown-ups: Counted by tens up to one hundred._

_At a hundred buckets he is wet right through._  
**Giangio**: My donkey turned that wheel before. He is very old and tired.  
_In the stable, a donkey lies on straw. He opens his eyes._  
**Candlewick**: Pinocchio. It is me. Candlewick.  
**Pinocchio**: Candlewick! Oh, Candlewick.  
_Candlewick puts his head in Pinocchio’s lap. Then Candlewick dies._  
_That means his body stopped working, and it will not start again._  
_It did not hurt._

**Giangio**: Why cry over a donkey?  
**Pinocchio**: He was my friend. We sat at the same desk.  
_Your Nubbin sits by his head. So do you, for a while._  
_Being sad is all right. Remembering him is a way to love him still._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): sadness when a friend dies is allowed; sitting together and remembering help  
> _Pinocchio is very sad about his friend. What helps when we are sad?_  
> - ✅ Sit with a friend, and remember him. → Yes. Sitting together and remembering helps.
> - Pretend we are not sad. → Sad is allowed. A hug and a memory help more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about feeling sad when a friend dies, and what helps._


#### `a13-20-coat`

_The atlas turns its pages slowly now._

_He looks after Geppetto as if Geppetto were the puppet._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Eco.1.K-2, ask): saving means keeping some money for later; giving is another choice  
> _Pinocchio saved pennies in a jar. What is saving?_  
> - ✅ Keeping some for later. → Yes! And he chose to give his savings away. That is a kind choice.
> - Spending it all now. → Spending is fun. Saving keeps some for later, as he did.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that saving means keeping some for later, and thought about giving._

_One morning, a Snail crosses the road to him. It takes a while._

**Pinocchio**: Take her this. I do not need a coat. It was too warm anyway.  
**The Snail**: I will go as fast as I can.

> _Pinocchio gave away his coat money. How does it feel to give something kind?_  
> - ✅ Warm inside. → Yes! Giving can feel warm, even when we have less.
> - Sad. → Sometimes a little. But often giving feels warm inside.

#### `a14-01-gate`

    - Your Nubbin trots in. Telemachus laughs.

> - Silly → He is not feeling silly. He is quiet and looking at the spears. He feels sad.

**Telemachus**: Come this way, away from the noisy men.

> _The bird flew up through a hole in the roof._  
> _Which way does smoke from a fire go?_  
> - ✅ Up → Yes. Warm air goes up and takes the smoke with it. That is why the roof has a hole.
> - Down → Smoke floats up, not down. The warm air carries it up and out of the hole.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that smoke and warm air rise._

**Telemachus**: That was no ordinary traveller!

> _When Phemius plucks a string, it wobbles._  
> _The wobble is the sound! (Wiggle your fingers like a string and hum: mmmm.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a plucked string wobbles and that the wobble makes sound._

> - Hat → Hat starts with h, h, h. Lamp starts with l, l, l, just like loom.

**Telemachus**: Ask Antinous. He loves to tell that story.

## A14-2. The Assembly

- `a14-02-s1`: Stand behind Telemachus at the big meeting. · _Stand behind his father’s seat._

#### `a14-02-assembly`

_The men of Ithaca meet in the meeting-place._  
_Telemachus sits in his dad’s seat. You stand behind him._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): taking turns: one person speaks at a time  
> _Only the person holding the staff may talk. Why?_  
> - ✅ So everyone takes turns → Yes. One person talks, and everyone else listens. Then it is the next person’s turn.
> - So it looks pretty → It does look grand, but the real reason is turns. The staff shows whose turn it is.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a speaker’s staff was a way of taking turns._

_Some men laugh. Telemachus feels very small._  

**Choices**

- **Pick up the staff and give it back.**
    - He takes it and holds it tight.
- **Look kindly at the man who laughed.**
    - The man stops laughing for a moment.
- **Stay right behind him.**
    - Telemachus stands up a little straighter.

#### `a14-02-assembly-done`

> _Antinous says it is not his fault. What could he say instead?_  
> - ✅ I am sorry. I will go home. → Yes. Saying sorry and putting things right is brave.
> - It is your fault! → Blaming someone else does not help. Saying sorry does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying sorry instead of blaming someone else._

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): first, next, last: what happened in order  
> _In the day, Penelope wove the cloth. Then night came._

> - She sang a song → She did not sing. At night she took the cloth apart, bit by bit.

> - 2 rows → Taking away makes fewer, not more. 1 take away 1 leaves none.

> _What gives us light in the daytime?_

> - The Moon → The Moon shines at night. In the day, the Sun gives us light.

## A14-3. Nestor and Menelaus

- `a14-03-s1`: Land at Pylos and ask old Nestor for news. · _Walk up the beach to the feast._

#### `a14-03-pylos`

_A sandy beach, at sunrise. People are having a big feast._  
**Telemachus**: I feel nervous. What if I say the wrong thing?

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when you feel nervous  
> _Telemachus feels nervous. What can help him feel braver?_  
> - ✅ A slow, deep breath → Yes. Breathe in slowly, and out slowly. (Try it together.)
> - Run away → Running away does not help the nervous feeling go. A slow breath does.
> _For grown-ups: Practised a calming breath for nervous feelings._

_Nestor is very, very old. He is kind._

**Telemachus**: Please, do you know where my dad is?  
**Nestor**: I am sorry. I do not know. Menelaus might.  

**Choices**

- **Ask who might know.**
    - **Nestor**: Menelaus. My son will drive you to Sparta.
- **Ask if there is any hope.**
    - **Nestor**: There is always hope with your dad.
- **Let your Nubbin sit by the old king.**
    - Nestor pats it gently, like a grandchild.

#### `a14-03-pylos-done`

_After the feast, Mentor turns into a big sea-eagle._

_The people on the beach are praying quietly._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): be quiet and kind when others are praying  
> _The people are praying on the beach. What should a good guest do?_  
> - ✅ Stay quiet and kind → Yes. Being quiet shows you respect what matters to them.
> - Shout and run about → Shouting would spoil it for them. A good guest stays quiet and kind.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to be quiet and respectful when others are praying._

_You stand back and keep quiet._

    - **Telemachus**: Yes, I am. Is my dad alive?

#### `a14-03-sparta-done`

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, ask): waiting patiently  
> _Telemachus must wait all night for news. What can he do while he waits?_  
> - ✅ Eat and rest → Yes. Resting helps us wait. Morning will come.
> - Ask and ask again → Asking again and again makes waiting feel longer. Resting is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about waiting patiently by resting._
