## A14-4. Calypso’s Island

- `a14-04-s1`: Walk to Calypso’s cave. · _Follow the young man with golden sandals._
- `a14-04-s2`: Find Odysseus on the shore. · _Go down to the rocks above the beach._
- `a14-04-s3`: Help him build the raft. · _Carry the pegs to the shore._

#### `a14-04-ogygia`

_A quiet island far across the sea._  
_There are trees, and four springs, and soft green meadows._  
_Owls and sea birds nest in the trees._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): animals live where they find what they need  
> _Birds nest in these trees. Why do birds like this island?_  
> - ✅ It has water, food and trees → Yes. Animals live where they find water, food and a safe home.
> - It has no trees → There are lots of trees! Birds nest in trees. They need a safe home.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that animals live where they find water, food and shelter._

_A young man with golden sandals lands beside you._  
**Hermes**: I am Hermes. I carry messages. Walk with me.  
_In a cave, a woman sits weaving and singing._  
_She is Calypso. She gives you bread and figs to eat._  
**Hermes**: Zeus says: let the man go home.  
**Calypso**: I am sad. But I will let him go.  

**Choices**

- **Thank Calypso for the figs.**
    - **Calypso**: You are welcome, little guest.
- **Ask Hermes where Odysseus is.**
    - **Hermes**: On the shore. He is always on the shore.

#### `a14-04-ogygia-done`

_Hermes goes away over the sea._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): in old Greek stories, Hermes carried messages  
> _In the old Greek stories, Hermes carried messages for the king of the gods._  
> _Some people in Greece still honour these gods today._  
> _We tell their stories with care._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that in old Greek stories Hermes carried messages, and that some people still honour these gods._

_Calypso puts down her loom. She goes to find Odysseus._  

#### `a14-04-shore`

_A man sits on a rock above the beach._  
_He looks at the sea. He is crying, very quietly._  
**Odysseus**: I miss my home. I miss it so much.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): name homesickness and say what helps  
> _Odysseus misses home. That feeling is called homesick. What can help?_  
> - ✅ Talk about home with a friend → Yes. Sharing a feeling makes it lighter. A hug helps too.
> - Hide the feeling → Hiding a feeling can make it heavier. Talking helps.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feeling of being homesick and talked about what helps._

**Odysseus**: Every morning I come here and look at the sea.  
_Your Nubbin sits beside him and looks at the sea too._  

**Choices**

- **Sit with him and say nothing.**
    - You sit together. The sea goes in and out.
- **Ask him about home.**
    - **Odysseus**: My son was a baby. Now he is a man.
- **Tell him you met his son.**
    - **Odysseus**: My son? Is he tall? Tell me!

#### `a14-04-shore-done`

_Calypso comes down the beach._  
**Calypso**: Do not cry. I will let you go.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count to seven on your fingers  
> _Odysseus stayed here for seven years._  
> _(Count to seven on your fingers together.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:years:7`
> _For grown-ups: Counted to seven on fingers._

**Calypso**: Build a raft. I will give you food and a fair wind.  
**Odysseus**: Promise it, please.  
**Calypso**: I promise. I am sorry you are sad.  

#### `a14-04-raft`

_Odysseus cuts down trees with a bronze axe._  
_You carry the pegs. Your Nubbin carries one, so proudly._  
_He works four days. Now there is a raft with a sail._  
**Calypso**: Stay with me, and nothing bad will ever happen.  
**Odysseus**: I want to go home. My family is there.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): home is where people who love you are  
> _Odysseus could stay safe here, but he wants to go home. Why?_  
> - ✅ His family is there → Yes. Home is where the people who love us are.
> - He is bored → Not bored. He misses his family, and his family misses him.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why home matters: the people who love us._

**Odysseus**: Would you stay, little guest?  

**Choices**

- **Say, “No. Home.”**
    - **Odysseus**: Home. Yes. That word says it all.
- **Say, “I do not know.”**
    - **Odysseus**: That is an honest answer.
- **Say, “Not if nothing ever happens.”**
    - **Odysseus**: Yes! Safe is not the same as happy.

#### `a14-04-raft-done`

_On the fifth day, he sails._  
_At night he steers by the stars._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): stars shine at night  
> _Stars shine at night._  
> _In the day, the Sun is too bright to see them._  
> _Sailors use stars to find their way. (Point up and say: twinkle, twinkle.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that stars shine at night and that sailors steer by them._

_You watch the island get small, and then it is gone._

> - ✅ Sand → Yes! Land and sand rhyme. Land, sand, hand.
> - Sea → Sea ends in ee. Land ends in and, just like sand.
> _For grown-ups: Found a rhyme for land (sand)._

#### `a14-05-storm-done`

_The biggest wave breaks the raft apart._

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): holding on and breathing when scared  
> _You feel scared in the big waves. What can help?_  
> - ✅ Slow breaths, and holding a friend → Yes. Breathe slowly, and stay close to a friend.
> - Squeezing your eyes shut and stopping → Stopping does not help. Slow breaths and a friend do.
> _For grown-ups: Practised slow breaths and staying close to a friend when scared._

_He ties the scarf round him, and swims. You follow._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add two days and two nights  
> _Two days and two nights. How many is that: 2 and 2?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! 2 and 2 make 4. (Hold up four fingers.)
> - Two → Two is only the days. Add the two nights: 2 and 2 make 4.
> _For grown-ups: Added 2 + 2 to make 4._

**Odysseus**: Land! I could cry with joy!

#### `a14-05-olives`

**Odysseus**: I am too cold by the river. I will go up into the woods.  
_Two olive bushes grow from one root._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): plants need water and sunlight  
> _The olive bushes are green and alive. What do plants need to grow?_  
> - ✅ Water and sunlight → Yes. Plants drink water and love sunlight. That is how they grow.
> - Toys → Toys are for children! Plants need water and sunlight.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants need water and sunlight to grow._

_Under them, dry leaves make a soft bed._

_You and your Nubbin snuggle in too._

- **Keep watch for a while.**

- **Pile more leaves over him.**
    - He is already asleep.
- **Sleep.**
    - You sleep. It is the first sleep in three days.

#### `a14-05-complete`

_Athena pours sleep over his eyes, so he can rest._  
_Up the hill, a princess has a dream._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sleep helps our bodies rest  
> _Odysseus is very tired. Why do we need sleep?_  
> - ✅ So our bodies can rest and grow → Yes. Sleep gives our bodies a rest, and helps us grow.
> - So we can be grumpy → Sleep makes us less grumpy! Our bodies rest and grow.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sleep gives our bodies rest and helps us grow._

## A14-6. Nausicaa

- `a14-06-s1`: Help with the washing at the river. · _Carry the clothes to the washing pools._

#### `a14-06-river`

_A mule-cart comes down the road, piled high with clothes._

_You splash and tread the clothes in the pools._

> **Lesson** (science, K-PS3-1, ask): the Sun dries wet things  
> _The wet clothes lie on the pebbles in the Sun._  
> _What will happen to them?_  
> - ✅ They will dry → Yes. The Sun warms the clothes and the water goes up into the air.
> - They will get wetter → The Sun does not make things wetter. It makes them warm and dry.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Sun’s warmth dries wet clothes._

_The girls eat lunch, then play ball._  
**Nausicaa**: Catch!  

**Choices**

    - You catch it and throw it back. She laughs.
- **Let your Nubbin catch it.**
    - Your Nubbin catches it and falls over backwards.
- **Drop it, for fun.**
    - Everyone laughs. Being bad at ball is fun here!

#### `a14-06-river-done`

_Nausicaa throws the ball. It lands in the deep water._

> _(Clap the four beats together.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:nausicaa`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the four syllables in the name Nausicaa._

_Everyone shrieks!_  
_In the bushes, the leaves wiggle. Someone gets up._  

#### `a14-06-bushes`

_A man steps out of the bushes. He is covered in salt._  
_The maids run away. Nausicaa stays._  
**Odysseus**: Hello, lady. Please may I have some clothes and some food?  
_He stays far back and asks politely._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): polite words and gentle manners  
> _The man asks in a gentle voice. Which word is a polite one?_  
> - ✅ Please → Yes. Please and thank you are kind words that help people feel safe.
> - Give me → Give me can sound bossy. Please makes a request kind.
> _For grown-ups: Practised polite words (please) and gentle manners._


**Choices**

- **Say he is a good man.**
    - **Nausicaa**: Then he is welcome here.
- **Hold out a clean cloak.**
    - He takes it and bows to you.
- **Stay back. It is her choice.**
    - **Nausicaa**: You look like a man who has had bad luck.

#### `a14-06-bushes-done`

**Nausicaa**: Come back! Give him clothes and food!  
_He washes the salt off in the river._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): washing keeps us clean and healthy  
> _Odysseus washes the salt off. Why do we wash with water and soap?_  
> - ✅ To get clean and keep healthy → Yes. Washing gets rid of dirt and germs.
> - To get dirty → Washing makes us clean, not dirty.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that washing keeps us clean and healthy._

_When he comes back, he looks clean and tall._  

#### `a14-06-road`

**Nausicaa**: Follow the cart to the town fields.  
**Nausicaa**: Then wait in the quiet grove.  
**Nausicaa**: Then ask for the palace. Then go to my mother.  
**Nausicaa**: She sits by the fire. Be polite to her.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): first, next, last in directions  
> _First, follow the cart. Next, wait in the grove._  
> _What is last: ask for the palace, or go home?_  
> - ✅ Ask for the palace → Yes. First the cart, next the grove, last the palace.
> - Go home → Odysseus is trying to get home! The last step is to ask for the palace.
> _For grown-ups: Put directions in order: first, next, last._


#### `a14-06-road-done`

_You wait in the quiet grove until sunset._  
_Odysseus talks quietly to Athena, all alone._  
_You walk a little way off to give him room._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): giving someone space  
> _Odysseus wants to talk alone. Why is it kind to give him room?_  
> - ✅ Some things are private → Yes. Giving a friend space shows you respect them.
> - So you can run away → Not to run away. Giving room is a kind way to say: this is yours.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about giving a friend space as a kind thing to do._

#### `a14-08-cave`

_A cave high above the sea. It is full of cheeses._

**Polyphemus**: Who are you? Why are you in my cave?  
_You are shut in. Your Nubbin’s heart goes thump, thump._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when you are scared  
> _Your Nubbin is scared. What can help when you feel scared?_  
> - ✅ A slow breath, and a hug → Yes. Breathe in slowly and out slowly. Hold someone safe.
> - Pretending you are not scared → It is fine to be scared. Say so, then breathe slowly.
> _For grown-ups: Practised a slow breath and a hug when scared._


**Choices**

- **Hide your Nubbin inside your tunic.**
    - You tuck it in. It feels safe.
- **Stand next to Odysseus.**
    - He stands between you and the fire.

> _What is the problem Odysseus must solve: the big stone, or a lost toy?_  
> - ✅ The big stone → Yes. The stone blocks the door. A plan must get them past it.
> - A lost toy → No toy is lost. The problem is the big stone.
> _For grown-ups: Named the problem to solve (the big stone) before making a plan._

> - Lamp → Lamp starts with l, l, l. Nest starts with n, just like Nobody.
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first sound of a word (n for Nobody and nest)._

> - Shout as loud as you can → Shouting can make a cross feeling bigger. A slow breath is better.

## A14-9. The Bag of Winds

- `a14-09-s1`: Stay a while on the floating island. · _Go up to the hall inside the bronze wall._
- `a14-09-s2`: Keep watch on the bag. · _Stay near the silver thread._
- `a14-09-s3`: Go back and ask again. · _Follow Odysseus to the hall._

#### `a14-09-aeolia`

_A floating island, with a wall of bronze._  
_Aeolus keeps all the winds. He lives here with his twelve children._  
**Aeolus**: Tell me about Troy! Tell me everything!  
_Odysseus tells stories for a whole month._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): wind is moving air  
> _Wind is air that moves. Can you see the wind, or only feel it?_  
> - ✅ Feel it, and see what it moves → Yes. We cannot see air, but we see leaves and sails move.
> - See it like a ball → Air is invisible. We see what the wind moves, like leaves.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that wind is moving air we can feel but not see._

**Aeolus**: Now you can go home. Here is a bag of winds.  
_He ties the bag with a silver thread._  
**Aeolus**: Do not open it. Not ever.  

**Choices**

- **Say, “We will not.”**
    - **Aeolus**: Good guest. Off you go.
- **Ask what is inside.**
    - **Aeolus**: Every wind there is, but one.
- **Let your Nubbin sniff the bag.**
    - Its ears blow straight back!

#### `a14-09-aeolia-done`

_The west wind fills the sail._  
_Odysseus steers the ship all by himself._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count aloud to nine  
> _Odysseus steers for nine days and nine nights._  
> _(Count to nine together: one, two, three, up to nine.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:aloud:9`
> _For grown-ups: Counted aloud to nine._


#### `a14-09-bag`

_On the tenth day, you see home!_  
**Odysseus**: That is home! I can see the smoke!  
_He is so tired, he falls asleep._  
**A Sailor**: What is in that bag? I want to look.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): ask before opening what is not yours  
> _The sailors want to open the bag. What should they do first?_  
> - ✅ Ask, or wait for Odysseus → Yes. Ask first. Things that are not ours are not ours to open.
> - Open it quickly → Opening it quickly could cause trouble. Ask or wait first.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking before opening something that is not yours._

**A Sailor**: Just one little peek!  

**Choices**

- **Say, “It is only the winds.”**
    - **A Sailor**: Of course! Move over.
- **Try to wake Odysseus.**
    - He mumbles about goats. He does not wake.
- **Sit on the bag.**
    - Two sailors gently lift you off.

#### `a14-09-bag-done`

_They untie the silver thread. Whoosh!_  
_Every wind comes out at once._  
_The ship spins round. Home gets small, then it is gone._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): soft breezes and strong winds are different  
> _A little breeze is gentle. What is a very strong wind like?_  
> - ✅ Loud and wild → Yes. A strong wind is loud and can push big things.
> - Quiet and still → A still day has no wind. A strong wind is loud and wild.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a gentle breeze and a very strong wind._

_Odysseus wakes. He lies down with his cloak over his face._  

#### `a14-09-again`

_The winds blow you back to the floating island._  
**Odysseus**: My crew opened the bag. Please help us again.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): saying sorry and owning a mistake  
> _The sailors opened the bag, and that was a mistake._  
> _What is a good thing to say?_  
> - ✅ I am sorry. I will make it right → Yes. Sorry, and trying to put it right, is brave.
> - It was not me → Blaming others does not help. Saying sorry does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying sorry and owning a mistake._

**Aeolus**: No. I cannot help you now.  
_Nobody offers you dinner. It is the first shut door._  

**Choices**

- **Go quietly.**
    - At the door, a little girl gives your Nubbin a fig.
- **Ask once more, for the crew.**
    - **Aeolus**: No. I am sorry. No.

#### `a14-09-complete`

_No wind now. They row, day after day._  
_Big grumpy giants chase them out of a harbour. Only one ship gets away._  
**Odysseus**: I was so close to home. I could see the smoke.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): opposite words: close and far  
> _Odysseus was close to home. What is the opposite of close?_  
> - ✅ Far → Yes! Close and far are opposites. Near, far.
> - Soon → Soon is about time. The opposite of close, near, is far.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that close and far are opposite words._

**Odysseus**: Close is harder than far.

#### `a14-10-woods`

_A woody island, with smoke over the trees._  
_Some sailors went to look. They did not come back._  
**Odysseus**: I will go and see. You can come too.  
_On the path stands Hermes, with a wand._

_It has a dark root and a white flower._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): roots hold a plant in the ground  
> _The flower has a root under the ground. What does a root do?_  
> - ✅ Holds the plant and drinks water → Yes. Roots hold a plant in the soil and drink water.
> - Makes the flower smell → Roots hold the plant and drink water. The petals make the smell.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that roots hold a plant in the ground and take in water._


**Choices**

> _Your Nubbin hides, and peeks out. How does it feel?_  
> - ✅ A bit nervous, and a bit curious → Yes. It can feel two ways at once.
> - Sleepy → Sleepy ones do not peek. Your Nubbin feels nervous and curious.
> _For grown-ups: Named mixed feelings (nervous and curious) from a character’s actions._

> - Go away → Go away is not kind. Thank you is.

## A14-11. The House of the Dead

- `a14-11-s1`: Sail to the edge of the world. · _Wait under the willows._
- `a14-11-s2`: Stay near while the misty people come. · _Sit quietly under the willows._
- `a14-11-s3`: Sit with him afterwards. · _Stay under the willows until he comes back._

#### `a14-11-edge`

_This part of the story is sad and gentle. You can stop any time._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): sad stories are allowed  
> _If a story makes you sad, that is all right. It means you care._  
> _You can have a cuddle, or take a slow breath._  
> _You can tell a grown-up how you feel._  
> _For grown-ups: Was told that feeling sad at a sad story is fine, and that a cuddle, a breath or talking can help._

_The ship sails to a misty land at the edge of the world._  
_Odysseus goes on alone to do something important._  
**Odysseus**: Wait here by the trees, with the little one.  
_You sit under a willow with your Nubbin on your lap._  
_The page is grey, like paper left out in the rain._  

#### `a14-11-edge-done`

_Then they come: shadowy, misty people, from long ago._  
_They make a sound like birds far away._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): sound words  
> _Birds go tweet, tweet._  
> _(Tweet softly like a bird far away.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-word:tweet`
> _For grown-ups: Said a sound word (tweet) softly, like a faraway bird._

_They do not frighten you. They are only sad._  

#### `a14-11-shades`

_A wise old man comes first. He cannot see, but he knows many things._  
**Tiresias**: Be careful at home, Odysseus. It will not be easy.  
_Then a woman comes out of the mist._  
**Odysseus**: Mum? Is it you?  
_Odysseus’s mum has died. That means her body stopped working._  
_It will not start again. She is a memory in the mist._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when someone is sad  
> _Odysseus is very sad about his mum. What helps when we are sad?_  
> - ✅ A hug, and someone beside us → Yes. We can be sad and still be loved. We can always remember the people we love.
> - Pretending we are not sad → It is all right to feel sad. A hug and a friend beside us help most.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when we are sad: a hug and a friend, and remembering people we love._

**Anticlea**: I missed you, my son. I love you very much.  
**Anticlea**: Your wife and son are waiting for you.  

#### `a14-11-shades-done`

_Odysseus tries to hug her. His arms go through the mist._  
**Odysseus**: Mum, why can’t you stay?  
**Anticlea**: I cannot, my child. Go back to the light.  
**Anticlea**: Remember me. Tell your wife about me.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): telling stories keeps people remembered  
> _Odysseus’s mum says, remember me. How can we remember someone we love?_  
> - ✅ Tell stories about them → Yes. When we tell stories about someone, they stay in our hearts.
> - Forget them → We do not have to forget. Telling stories keeps them close.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that telling stories helps us remember people we love._


#### `a14-11-after`

_The misty people go back down._  
_Odysseus walks to the willows and sits beside you._

_Your Nubbin looks at you, as if to ask what to do._  
_You remember what Hazel did. She just sat beside someone._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): sit beside a sad friend  
> _Odysseus is sad. What helps a sad friend most?_  
> - ✅ Sit beside them, quietly → Yes. You do not need words. Being there helps.
> - Tell them to cheer up → Cheer up can feel hard for a sad friend. Sitting beside them is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sitting quietly beside a sad friend is a kind way to help._


**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin climb into his hands.**

## A14-12. The Sirens

- `a14-12-s1`: Hear Circe’s advice. · _Walk with them along the shore._
- `a14-12-s2`: Let him put wax in your ears. · _Sit on the bench and keep still._
- `a14-12-s3`: Watch him at the mast as the ship rows past. · _Stay on the bench. You will not hear a thing._

#### `a14-12-advice`

_Circe takes Odysseus aside._  
**Circe**: Some women sing beautiful songs by the sea.  
**Circe**: Sailors who listen forget to go home.  
**Circe**: Put soft wax in your friends’ ears. Then they cannot hear.  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, ask): soft wax keeps sound out  
> _Wax is soft and squashy._  
> _With wax in your ears, does the world sound louder or quieter?_  
> - ✅ Quieter → Yes. The wax fills up your ears, so less sound gets in.
> - Louder → Wax makes sound softer, not louder. It blocks the way into your ears.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that wax in the ears blocks sound, so the world sounds quieter._

**Circe**: If you want to listen, your friends can tie you to the mast.  
_Odysseus promises to be careful._  

**Choices**

- **Ask if you need wax too.**
    - **Circe**: Yes, little guest. And the small one.
- **Ask Odysseus why he wants to listen.**
    - **Odysseus**: I am curious. I always have been.

#### `a14-12-advice-done`

_In the morning, Circe waves goodbye._  
_A fair wind pushes the ship out to sea._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhyming words  
> _Ship rhymes with a word. Which one: trip or ball?_  
> - ✅ Trip → Yes! Ship and trip rhyme. Ship, trip, dip.
> - Ball → Ball ends in all. Ship ends in ip, like trip.
> _For grown-ups: Found a rhyme for ship (trip)._


#### `a14-12-wax`

_The wind drops. The sea is flat like a plate._  
_Odysseus makes a soft cake of wax with his warm hands._  
**Odysseus**: Ears, everyone! Even you, little guest.  
_He puts wax in the sailors’ ears._  
_Then in your ears, and in your Nubbin’s. The world goes quiet._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count six ears  
> _You, Odysseus and your Nubbin each have two ears._  
> _(Count all the ears together: one, two, three, four, five, six.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:ears:6`
> _For grown-ups: Counted six ears (three friends with two ears each)._

_The sailors tie Odysseus to the mast._  

#### `a14-12-wax-done`

_Your Nubbin keeps touching its ears, in case they have gone._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): protect your ears from very loud sounds  
> _Very loud noise can hurt our ears. What can we do?_  
> - ✅ Cover our ears, or go away from it → Yes. Covering your ears protects them.
> - Make it louder → Louder would hurt more. Cover your ears and move away.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to protect ears from very loud noise._


#### `a14-12-sirens`

_A green meadow slides past. Two women sit and sing._  
_You hear nothing at all._  
_Odysseus pulls at the ropes._  
_His friends keep rowing, all together._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): working together  
> _The sailors row all together. Why is it good to work together?_  
> - ✅ We can do big things as a team → Yes. Together, the sailors get past safely.
> - It is not good → Teams can do things nobody can do alone.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how teamwork helps people get big jobs done._

_They tie the rope tighter, just as he asked._  
_Soon the meadow is far behind._  

**Choices**

- **Keep looking at him.**
    - He sees you, and it helps him hold on.
- **Look away, at the sea.**
    - The sea is flat and blue.
- **Hold your Nubbin’s paws over its ears.**
    - It puts its paws over your ears too.

#### `a14-12-sirens-done`

_The men take the wax out of their ears, and untie him._  
**Odysseus**: They sang so sweetly! They sang high, like birds.  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): high and low sounds  
> _A bird tweets high. A big drum goes boom, low. Which sound is high?_  
> - ✅ The bird → Yes. A bird’s tweet is high, and a drum’s boom is low.
> - The drum → A drum goes boom, which is low. A bird’s tweet is high.
> _For grown-ups: Told a high sound (a bird) from a low sound (a drum)._


#### `a14-12-complete`

_He rubs his sore wrists._  
**Odysseus**: Was it quiet on your side?  
**You**: Very.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): opposite words: quiet and loud  
> _Very quiet. What is the opposite of quiet?_  
> - ✅ Loud → Yes! Quiet and loud are opposites.
> - Little → Little is about size. The opposite of quiet is loud.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that quiet and loud are opposite words._

**Odysseus**: Quiet is peaceful. I am glad you are safe.  

## A14-13. Scylla and Charybdis

- `a14-13-s1`: Watch the strait as he steers by the cliff. · _Stay low on the bench and keep rowing._
- `a14-13-s2`: Land on the island of the Sun. · _Go ashore, and keep away from the cows._
- `a14-13-s3`: Hold on to the fig tree. · _Grab the tree and hang on._

#### `a14-13-strait`

_Two big rocks stand on each side of a narrow strait._  
_On one side, the sea swirls round and round, down a deep hole._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): water swirls when it is squeezed through a narrow place  
> _Water can swirl round and round when it is squeezed through a narrow place._  
> _(Swirl your finger in the air, round and round.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that water swirls when squeezed through a narrow place._

_On the other side, a scary shape hides in a cave._  
**Odysseus**: Row close to the cliff. Do not look up. Row!  
_The sailors duck low and row hard._  
_Some of the sailors are lost. That means they died._  
_That is very sad, and Odysseus is sad too. You hold hands._  

#### `a14-13-strait-done`

_The strait opens out. Behind you, the sea swirls and roars._  
_Ahead is a green island, with cows on it._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): animal sounds  
> _A cow goes moo. Which animal goes baa?_  
> - ✅ A sheep → Yes! Sheep go baa, cows go moo.
> - A dog → Dogs go woof. Sheep go baa.
> _For grown-ups: Matched animals to their sounds (cow: moo, sheep: baa)._


#### `a14-13-island`

_It is the island of the Sun, with fat cows._  
**Odysseus**: We sail past. We do not touch the cows.  
**Eurylochus**: We are tired and hungry. Let us stop!  
_They stop, and promise not to touch the cows._  
_The wind blows the wrong way for a month. The food runs out._  
_Odysseus goes to ask the gods for help, and falls asleep._  
_The sailors are very hungry._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): keeping a promise even when it is hard  
> _The sailors promised not to touch the cows, but they are hungry._  
> _What is a good thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Keep the promise, and ask for help → Yes. Keeping a promise is brave, and a friend can help us find another way.
> - Break the promise → Breaking a promise can cause trouble. Asking for help is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keeping a promise even when it is hard, and asking for help._


**Choices**

- **Go and find Odysseus.**
    - He is asleep in a hollow. You shake him awake.
- **Stay and talk to the crew.**
    - **Eurylochus**: We are too hungry!
    - Nobody listens.
- **Stand with the cows.**
    - The men walk round you, politely.

#### `a14-13-island-done`

_Odysseus comes back. The hungry sailors have eaten some of the cows!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): day and night  
> _The Sun goes down, and then it is dark. When is it dark?_  
> - ✅ At night → Yes. The Sun shines in the day. At night, we see the stars.
> - At lunchtime → At lunchtime, the Sun is up high. It is dark at night.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that it is light in the day and dark at night._

_He cries out. Far above, the Sun is sad too._  

#### `a14-13-fig`

_Six days the sailors eat. Then they sail._  
_A black cloud comes, and a big storm hits the ship._  
_The ship breaks apart, and the sailors die._

_You cling to the mast. All night the wind carries you back._  
_At dawn you are at the swirl again._  
_Odysseus grabs a fig tree and hangs on. You hold his hand._  
_You can only hang on, and wait._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count aloud to ten  
> _Count while you hang on, to make the time go faster._  
> _(Count to ten together, nice and slow.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:aloud:10`
> _For grown-ups: Counted aloud to ten._


**Choices**

- **Hang on.**
    - Your arms are tired. Odysseus talks about goats, so you do not let go.
- **Count, to make it go faster.**
    - You count and count. Odysseus counts with you.
- **Look at Odysseus.**
    - He is calm. You decide to believe him.

#### `a14-13-fig-done`

_When evening comes, the wood comes back up._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): before clocks, people told time by the Sun  
> _Long ago, people told time by the Sun._  
> _When the Sun is high up, is it noon or night?_  
> - ✅ Noon → Yes. When the Sun is high, it is the middle of the day.
> - Night → At night, the Sun is gone. High in the sky means noon.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that long ago people told time by where the Sun was in the sky._

_Odysseus drops onto the wood, and you follow._  
_He paddles away with his hands._  

#### `a14-13-complete`

_Nine days he drifts, until he reaches an island._  
_The page turns back. You are in the hall again._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): who tells the story  
> _Who told all those adventures to the people in the hall?_  
> - ✅ Odysseus → Yes! Odysseus told them. A story can sit inside another story.
> - The loom → Looms do not talk. Odysseus told the stories.
> _For grown-ups: Told who the storyteller is in a story told inside a story._

**Odysseus**: That is my story. I do not like to tell it twice.  
_Nobody speaks for a long time._  
**Alcinous**: Tomorrow you go home, with gifts from all of us.  

## A14-14. Home Asleep

- `a14-14-s1`: Sail with the Phaeacians to Ithaca. · _Sit in the stern beside him._
- `a14-14-s2`: Stay with him when he wakes. · _Wait on the sand beside him._

#### `a14-14-ship`

_The ship sails fast and smooth, all night._  
_Odysseus sleeps on a rug. He has earned it._  
_You sit beside him and watch the stars._  
_Before dawn, you see a dark shape: an island._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): an island has water all around it  
> _Ithaca is an island. What is all around an island?_  
> - ✅ Water → Yes. An island is land with water all around it.
> - Sand only → There may be sand, but what is all around is water.
> _For grown-ups: Recalled that an island is land with water all around it._

_It is Ithaca, his home._  

**Choices**

- **Pull his cloak up over his shoulder.**
    - He does not wake. He mumbles about a dog.
- **Watch the stars.**
    - The dawn star comes up. The ship sails into harbour.
- **Sleep too.**
    - You dream of a gate, and someone lifting and pushing it.

#### `a14-14-ship-done`

_In the bay, an olive tree grows beside a cave._  
_Bees keep honey there._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-2, ask): bees visit flowers  
> _Bees make honey. What do bees visit to get food?_  
> - ✅ Flowers → Yes. Bees drink nectar from flowers, and carry pollen too.
> - Rocks → Rocks have no nectar. Bees visit flowers.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that bees visit flowers to collect nectar._

_The sailors lay Odysseus gently on the sand, still asleep._  
_They leave his gifts under the olive tree, and go._  

#### `a14-14-harbour`

_He wakes in the mist. He does not know where he is._

> _The island is called Ithaca. It has three beats: Ith-a-ca._  
> _(Clap the three beats together.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:ithaca`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the three syllables in the word Ithaca._

_Odysseus is so happy. But he tells the shepherd a made-up story._  
_The shepherd smiles, and turns into Athena._  
**Athena**: You cannot help being clever, Odysseus. Look! Your harbour, your tree, your hill.  
_Odysseus kneels and kisses the ground._  
**Athena**: Bad guests are in your house. Keep who you are secret, for now.  
_She touches him with her wand. He is an old beggar!_  
**The Beggar**: Well. Nobody will know me now.  
**The Beggar**: You told me once to keep my name. I am keeping it now.  

#### `a14-14-harbour-done`

_Together you hide his gifts in a cave: gold, bronze and cloth._

> _(Count the three gifts on your fingers together.)_

_She is gone. The beggar leans on his staff._

**The Beggar**: I fell off that rock when I was six!

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): two feelings at once: happy and lonely  
> _Odysseus is home, but he cannot tell anyone. Which words fit how he feels?_  
> - ✅ Happy and a little lonely → Yes. You can feel two feelings at once.
> - Only cross → He is happy to be home, and a little lonely. Both are true.
> _For grown-ups: Named two feelings at once (happy and lonely) for a character._


## A14-15. The Swineherd

- `a14-15-s1`: Go to the swineherd’s hut. · _Climb the track to the stone yard._
- `a14-15-s2`: Help Eumaeus with the pigs. · _Pour the acorns and herd the piglets._
- `a14-15-s3`: Be there when Telemachus comes home. · _Stay in the hut when the dogs go quiet._

#### `a14-15-hut`

_On a hill, a yard with stone walls._  
_There are pig houses, and four big dogs._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count four dogs  
> _There are four big dogs in the yard._  
> _(Count the four dogs together: one, two, three, four.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:dogs:4`

_The dogs rush at the old beggar, barking!_

**Eumaeus**: Oh, old man! Come in. Sit down. Eat first.  
_He gives you the best food he has._  
**The Beggar**: Thank you, friend.  
**Eumaeus**: Everyone is welcome here, even when I have little.  

**Choices**

- **Say, “He might still be alive.”**
    - **Eumaeus**: Many say that. I stopped believing.
- **Ask Eumaeus about his master.**
    - **Eumaeus**: He was kind. He gave me this hut.
- **Eat, and let the beggar talk.**
    - **The Beggar**: He will come home. This very year.
    - **Eumaeus**: I will believe it when I see it.

#### `a14-15-hut-done`

**The Beggar**: He will come home, between the old moon and the new.  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): the Moon changes shape  
> _The beggar said, between the old moon and the new._  
> _Is the Moon always the same shape?_  
> - ✅ No. It changes shape → Yes. Sometimes round and full, sometimes a thin slice.
> - Yes, always round → The Moon seems to change, from a thin slice to a big round circle.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Moon seems to change shape over the month._

**The Beggar**: If he comes, give me a cloak.  
**Eumaeus**: Ha! No, old man. Eat.  

#### `a14-15-pigs`

_At evening, the pigs come home to their pens._  
**Eumaeus**: Help me pour the acorns. Mind the big one.  
_Your Nubbin herds the piglets into the wrong pen._  
**Eumaeus**: Not that one. That one. There!  
_The night is cold and wet. The beggar shivers._  
_Eumaeus finds him a warm cloak._  
_Then Eumaeus goes out into the rain, to sleep by the pigs._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): caring for others, even when it is cold and wet  
> _Eumaeus gave his guest a warm cloak._  
> _Then he went out in the rain to mind the pigs. Why?_  
> - ✅ Because he cares for his guest and his pigs → Yes. He looks after everyone in his care, even when it is cold and wet.
> - Because he likes rain → He gave his guest the cloak, and went out to mind the pigs. He cares for them all.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about kindness: looking after others, even when it is uncomfortable._


**Choices**

- **Go out with Eumaeus.**
    - The pigs are warm and smelly. He makes room for you.
- **Stay inside with the beggar.**
    - **The Beggar**: Look at him go. For his pigs!
- **Offer Eumaeus your cloak.**
    - **Eumaeus**: Keep it, guest. I am used to the rain.

#### `a14-15-pigs-done`

_In the hut, the beggar lies under the borrowed cloak._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a cloak keeps your own warmth in  
> _A thick cloak keeps you warm._  
> _Does it make heat, or hold in your own heat?_  
> - ✅ It holds in your own heat → Yes. A cloak holds your own body’s warmth close.
> - It makes a fire → A cloak does not make fire. It holds your warmth in.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that clothes keep us warm by holding in our own body warmth._

_He lies awake, watching the door._  

#### `a14-15-son`

_One morning, the dogs do not bark. They whine with joy._  
_It is Telemachus, home from Sparta!_  
_Eumaeus kisses his head and his hands._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): happy tears are real  
> _Eumaeus is so glad he kisses Telemachus’s head._  
> _Can people cry when they are happy?_  
> - ✅ Yes. Happy tears are real → Yes. Tears can come when we are very happy, too.
> - No. Tears are only sad → Tears can be happy tears. Many people cry when they are glad.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people can cry happy tears._

**Telemachus**: I came here first. Is my mum all right?  
**Eumaeus**: She is still waiting for you.  
_Someone stands at the edge of the yard._  
_The beggar goes out to her._  
_When he comes back, he is tall, in clean clothes._  
**Odysseus**: I am your father. I came home.  

#### `a14-15-son-done`

_Telemachus and his dad hug and cry._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhyming words  
> _Dad rhymes with glad. Which word rhymes too: sad or tree?_  
> - ✅ Sad → Yes! Dad, glad and sad all rhyme.
> - Tree → Tree ends in ee. Dad, glad and sad all end in ad.
> _For grown-ups: Found rhymes for dad (glad, sad)._

_You and your Nubbin sit on the wall, and let them be._  

#### `a14-15-complete`

**Odysseus**: Tell nobody yet.  
**Telemachus**: There are lots of bad guests, and only two of us.  
**Odysseus**: Two, and the guest. That makes three.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add two and one  
> _Two of them, and one guest. How many is that?_  
> - ✅ Three → Yes! 2 and 1 make 3. (Hold up three fingers.)
> - Two → Two is only Odysseus and his son. Add the guest: 2 and 1 make 3.
> _For grown-ups: Added 2 + 1 to make 3._

_Three friends, and Athena helping._  

## A14-16. Argos

- `a14-16-s1`: Walk into town with Eumaeus and the beggar. · _Carry the bag down the track to the spring._
- `a14-16-s2`: Stop at the gate, by the heap. · _Stand at the gate with them._
- `a14-16-s3`: Sit with Argos in the sun. · _Sit beside the heap and stay._

#### `a14-16-road`

_Eumaeus and the beggar walk to town. You carry the bag._  
_At the spring, a goatherd sees you._  
_He is rude and unkind to the beggar._  
_The beggar does not hit back. He stays calm._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what to do when someone is unkind  
> _Someone is unkind to you. What can you do?_  
> - ✅ Walk away, and tell a grown-up → Yes. Walking away and telling a grown-up keeps you safe.
> - Be unkind back → Being unkind back makes more trouble. Walk away and tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Learned what to do when someone is unkind: walk away and tell a grown-up._

**Eumaeus**: One day the master will come home.  
_Your Nubbin stares at the goatherd until he is out of sight._  

#### `a14-16-road-done`

_The house comes into sight._  
_You hear a lyre, and smell meat cooking._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): ears hear and noses smell  
> _You heard the lyre and smelled the meat. What did you use?_  
> - ✅ Ears and nose → Yes. Ears hear, and noses smell.
> - Toes → Toes are for walking. Ears hear, and noses smell.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we hear with our ears and smell with our noses._


#### `a14-16-gate`

_Outside the gate is a heap, and on it lies an old dog._  
_He is thin, and nobody looks after him now._  
**Eumaeus**: That is Argos. He was the best hunting dog.  
_The old dog lifts his head. His nose twitches._  
_He knows! After twenty years, he knows his master._  
_His ears go flat and his tail wags. He cannot get up._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words that show feelings: a wagging tail  
> _Argos’s tail wags and his ears go flat. What does a wagging tail show?_  
> - ✅ He is happy → Yes. A wagging tail shows a dog is glad. Argos is so glad to see his friend.
> - He is cross → A cross dog growls. Argos is wagging, which shows he is happy.
> _For grown-ups: Read a dog’s body language: a wagging tail shows he is glad._

_The beggar cannot go to him, or everyone will know._  
_The beggar whispers one word, so only the dog hears._  
**The Beggar**: Nobody.  
**Eumaeus**: Come on, old man.  
_They go in through the gate. He does not look back._  

#### `a14-16-gate-done`

_You stay at the gate with your Nubbin. Somebody should._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): what a dog needs  
> _Argos is old and thin. What does a dog need to stay healthy?_  
> - ✅ Food, water and a soft bed → Yes. A pet needs food, water, a safe bed, and someone who loves them.
> - Only a heap → A heap is not a good bed. A dog needs food, water and a soft bed.
> _For grown-ups: Learned what a dog needs: food, water and a soft bed._


#### `a14-16-sit`

_You sit beside the heap in the warm sun._  
_Your Nubbin goes up to the old dog, gently._  
_Argos sniffs it. He puts his head down._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): dogs have a very good sense of smell  
> _Argos sniffs. A dog’s nose is very, very good._  
> _How did Argos know his friend?_  
> - ✅ By his smell → Yes. A dog remembers smells for a very long time.
> - By his shoes → The beggar wears rags! Argos knew him by his smell.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a dog knows loved people by smell, because its nose is very good._

_Your Nubbin lies against his side._  
_His tail moves once more in the dust._  
_His eyes are on the gate. He is very tired._  

**Choices**

- **Scratch behind his ears.**
    - His eyes half close. He likes it.
- **Just sit with him.**
    - You just sit. That is enough.
- **Tell him, quietly, that his friend is home.**
    - **You**: He is home. You were right.
    - Argos sighs, a long, happy sigh.

#### `a14-16-sit-done`

_Argos puts his head down on his paws._  
_Argos has died. His body has stopped working, and will not start again._  
_He waited twenty years, and saw his friend come home._  
_Your Nubbin stays by his side for a long time._  
_It is all right to be sad. We can remember him._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when a pet dies  
> _When a pet dies, we feel sad. What can help us?_  
> - ✅ Remembering him, and being with people who care → Yes. Telling stories about him and having a hug helps.
> - Pretending it did not happen → Pretending does not help. Remembering and hugs do.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that after a pet dies it helps to remember and be with people who care._


#### `a14-16-complete`

_Later, Eumaeus finds you there._  
**Eumaeus**: He was a good dog.  
_Together you carry Argos under an olive tree._  
_Your Nubbin pats the earth flat, softly._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): people long ago remembered loved animals  
> _Long ago in Greece, people put up stones for animals they loved._  
> _We can remember our pets too, with a picture or a story._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people long ago made memorial stones for loved animals._


## A14-17. The Scar

#### `a14-17-hearth`

_Night. The noisy men have gone home._  
_Penelope sits by the fire._  
**Penelope**: Who are you, stranger?

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a fawn is a baby deer  
> _The brooch had a fawn on it. A fawn is a baby animal._  
> _Which animal?_  
> - ✅ A deer → Yes. A fawn is a baby deer. A baby dog is a puppy.
> - A pig → A baby pig is a piglet. A fawn is a baby deer.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a fawn is a baby deer._

_Penelope cries. She made that cloak herself._  
**The Beggar**: He is near. He will be home this year.  

**Choices**

- **Look at the beggar’s eyes.**
    - His eyes are dry. He is holding back his tears.
- **Pass Penelope a cloth for her eyes.**
    - **Penelope**: Thank you. You are a kind guest.
- **Let your Nubbin sit at Penelope’s feet.**
    - It leans on her ankle. She pats it, without looking.

#### `a14-17-hearth-done`

**Penelope**: You are my guest. Nurse, please wash this man’s feet.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): washing a guest’s feet was a kind welcome  
> _Long ago, a host had a guest’s tired feet washed. Why was that kind?_  
> - ✅ It makes tired feet clean and cool → Yes. It shows the guest is welcome and cared for.
> - It makes feet muddy → The washing makes feet clean and cool, which feels lovely.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that washing a guest’s feet was a kind welcome in Greece long ago._

**The Beggar**: Only an old nurse, please.  

#### `a14-17-scar`

_Eurycleia brings a basin of warm water._  
_She washes his foot and leg._  
_She feels a scar on his leg. She knows it!_  
_The scar is from when he was a boy._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): a scar is where a cut has healed  
> _A scar is where a cut has healed._  
> _What does your body do when you get a cut?_  
> - ✅ It mends itself → Yes. Your body grows new skin to mend the cut. The scar is where it mended.
> - Nothing → Your body works hard to mend a cut, all by itself.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the body mends a cut, and a scar is where it healed._

_She drops his foot, and splash! The water spills._  
**Eurycleia**: You are Odysseus! I know you!  
_The beggar gently holds her hand._  
**The Beggar**: Shh. Nobody must know yet.  

**Choices**

- **Mop up the spilt water.**
    - You mop it quickly. Penelope does not turn round.
- **Watch Penelope.**
    - She is looking into the fire, very still.
- **Keep still and say nothing.**
    - Eurycleia nods at you. You nod back.

#### `a14-17-scar-done`

**Eurycleia**: I will keep your secret.  
**The Beggar**: Thank you, nurse.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): a secret that worries you should be told to a grown-up  
> _A surprise secret can be fun. What if a secret makes you feel worried?_  
> - ✅ Tell a trusted grown-up → Yes. A worrying secret should always be shared with a grown-up you trust.
> - Keep it to yourself → A worried feeling is too big to carry alone. Tell a trusted grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to tell a trusted grown-up about a secret that makes you worried._


#### `a14-17-dream`

**Penelope**: I had a dream, stranger.  
**Penelope**: I keep twenty geese. A big eagle came.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count by tens to twenty  
> _Penelope has twenty geese._  
> _(Count by tens together: ten, twenty.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:by-tens:20`
> _For grown-ups: Counted by tens to twenty._

**Penelope**: Then the eagle spoke: I am your husband, home again.  
**The Beggar**: The eagle told you himself.  
**Penelope**: I will set a test tomorrow: a bow and twelve axes.  

#### `a14-17-dream-done`

_Penelope cries until she falls asleep._  
_The beggar lies on the porch. He cannot sleep._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when worries keep you awake  
> _Worries can keep us awake. What can help?_  
> - ✅ Slow breaths, and a cuddle → Yes. Slow breaths and a cuddle help worries get smaller.
> - Thinking about the worry harder → That makes it bigger. Slow breaths and a cuddle work better.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that slow breaths and a cuddle help when worries keep you awake._


#### `a14-17-complete`

_In the night, the beggar feels cross._  
_His heart growls like a dog guarding her puppies._

> _A mother dog guards her puppies. Why does she do that?_  
> - ✅ To keep them safe → Yes. Animal parents look after their babies and keep them safe.
> - To play → She guards them to keep them safe, because they are small.

## A14-18. The Bow

- `a14-18-s1`: Help carry the axes into the hall. · _Bring the axes, two at a time._
- `a14-18-s2`: Watch the men try the bow. · _Stand where you can see the bow and the door._
- `a14-18-s3`: See the beggar string the bow. · _Watch from beside his stool._

#### `a14-18-axes`

_It is a feast day. The noisy men come early._  
_Penelope brings down the great bow._  
**Penelope**: Whoever can string this bow and shoot through twelve axes, I will go with.  
_Telemachus lines up the axes in a straight row._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count twelve axes  
> _There are twelve axes in a straight row._  
> _(Count them together, up to twelve.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:axes:12`
> _For grown-ups: Counted twelve axes in a row._

_You carry them in, two at a time._  
**Telemachus**: I will try first.  
_He nearly does it. Then his dad shakes his head, so he stops._  

**Choices**

- **Nod at Telemachus.**
    - **Telemachus**: I am not strong enough yet. Let someone else try.
    - He sits near his father.
- **Pass the bow along to the men.**
    - It is very heavy. The string hums when you touch it.
- **Watch the beggar.**
    - The beggar looks at the bow like an old friend.

#### `a14-18-axes-done`

_The men line up to try the bow, one at a time._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): taking turns is fair  
> _The men take turns. Why is taking turns fair?_  
> - ✅ Everybody gets a go → Yes. Taking turns means everyone gets a go.
> - Only one person plays → With turns, everybody plays. That is why it is fair.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why taking turns is fair._


#### `a14-18-suitors`

_The first man tries. He cannot bend the bow._  
_Many men try. They are all red in the face._  
_In the yard, the beggar talks to Eumaeus._  
_He shows him his scar. Eumaeus is so happy, he hugs him._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words that show feelings  
> _Eumaeus is shaking and hugging. Which word names how he feels?_  
> - ✅ Happy → Yes. Eumaeus is so happy that he shakes.
> - Bored → A bored person yawns. Eumaeus is hugging and shaking, so he is happy.
> _For grown-ups: Named a character’s feeling (happy) from what he does._

**The Beggar**: Tie the yard gate shut, my friend.  
_Eumaeus ties it with a rope._  

**Choices**

- **Stand by the hall door with Eumaeus.**
    - He is shaking. He says he has never been so happy.
- **Stand by the beggar’s stool.**
    - He puts a hand on your shoulder.
- **Keep your Nubbin close.**
    - You hold it tight. It is going to get loud.

#### `a14-18-suitors-done`

_Antinous says it is a holy day. They will try again tomorrow._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): holy days and festivals are special days  
> _A holy day is a special day._  
> _People in Greece long ago held feasts for their gods, with music and games._  
> _Many people today have special days too._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a holy day is a special day, with feasts, music and games._


#### `a14-18-string`

**The Beggar**: May I try the old bow?  
**Antinous**: You? A beggar? Be quiet!  
**Penelope**: It is not kind to be rude to a guest.  
**Telemachus**: Mother, go upstairs. I will see to this.  
_Eumaeus gives the bow to the beggar._  
_He strings it as easily as a lyre._  
_He plucks the string. It sings sweetly._  

> **Lesson** (music, 1-PS4-1, notice): a plucked string sings  
> _The bow’s string sings when it is plucked, like a lyre string._  
> _(Pluck the air, and hum a note.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a plucked string wobbles and sings._

_He shoots an arrow. It goes through all twelve axes!_  
**The Beggar**: Your guest has not shamed you, Telemachus.  

#### `a14-18-complete`

_The hall is silent._  
_Telemachus stands by his father._  
_The beggar stands tall. He is not stooping now._  
_You hold your Nubbin tight. It is very quiet._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): a slow breath calms a racing heart  
> _Your heart goes thump, thump. What helps it calm down?_  
> - ✅ A slow breath → Yes. Breathe in slowly, and out slowly. (Try it together.)
> - Holding your breath → Holding your breath makes it feel louder. Slow breaths calm it.
> _For grown-ups: Practised a slow breath to calm a racing heart._


## A14-19. The Hall Cleared

- `a14-19-s1`: Stand behind him in the doorway. · _Stay just behind the doorstep._
- `a14-19-s2`: Stay in the doorway as Athena comes. · _Stay in the doorway. Do not run._
- `a14-19-s3`: Help tidy the hall. · _Collect the cups from under the tables._

#### `a14-19-threshold`

_He throws off his rags, and steps onto the stone doorstep._  
_Telemachus and Eumaeus stand beside him._  
_His first arrow knocks the cup from Antinous’s hand._  
**Odysseus**: You ate my food. You were not kind guests.  
**Eurymachus**: We are sorry. We will pay it all back.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): it is fair to ask before taking  
> _The men ate food that was not theirs. What should they have done first?_  
> - ✅ Asked, and said please → Yes. Asking first is fair and kind.
> - Taken it quickly → Taking without asking is not fair. We should ask first.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that it is fair to ask before taking._

**Odysseus**: No. This is my house.  

**Choices**

- **Stand with Telemachus.**
    - He is trembling. So are you, but you stay.
- **Slip out and untie the gate rope.**
    - You leave the yard gate open, so there is a way out.
- **Put your Nubbin behind you.**
    - It puts its paws on the backs of your knees.

#### `a14-19-threshold-done`

_Eurymachus shouts. Everyone moves at once._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): staying safe in a busy, pushing crowd  
> _Everyone is pushing at once. In a busy crowd, what keeps you safe?_  
> - ✅ Stay close to a grown-up you know → Yes. Hold on to a grown-up you know, and stay beside them.
> - Run off on your own → Running off alone in a crowd is not safe. Stay close to a grown-up you know.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that in a busy crowd it is safest to stay close to a grown-up you know._


#### `a14-19-aegis`

_Then someone else stands in the doorway: old Mentor, who is really Athena._  
_A swallow flies up to the roof._  
_A great shield makes everyone afraid._  
_The bad guests run away, whoosh! Over the wall and down the road._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, do): sound words  
> _The bad guests ran away: whoosh!_  
> _(Say whoosh, whoosh, whoosh and run on the spot.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-words:whoosh`
> _For grown-ups: Said a sound word (whoosh) and moved to it._

_Odysseus lets them go. Nobody is hurt._  
_They do not come back._  

#### `a14-19-aegis-done`

_The hall is empty. The swallow is gone._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): birds fly to warm places in winter  
> _Swallows are birds. In winter, where do swallows fly to stay warm?_  
> - ✅ To warm places, far away → Yes. Many birds fly far away to warm places for the winter.
> - Into the sea → Swallows cannot live in the sea. They fly to warm places on land.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that many birds fly far away to warm places in winter._

**Telemachus**: They are gone. Really gone.  

#### `a14-19-clean`

_Eurycleia runs in, ready to cheer._  
**Odysseus**: Do not cheer. Be kind.  
_Under a table, the singer Phemius hides, shaking._  
**Odysseus**: Come out. You are safe.  
_Everyone helps tidy the hall._  
_You collect cups from under the tables._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add one more  
> _You find five cups. Your Nubbin finds one more. How many cups?_  
> - ✅ Six → Yes! 5 and 1 make 6. (Hold up five fingers, then one more.)
> - Four → One more makes more, not less. 5 and 1 make 6.
> _For grown-ups: Added 5 + 1 to make 6._


**Choices**

- **Stack the cups by the door.**
    - You stack them in a neat tower.
- **Help the maids with the stools.**
    - The maids work quickly and quietly.
- **Sit with the shaking singer a while.**
    - You sit with Phemius. He hums to calm his hands.

#### `a14-19-clean-done`

_The hall is clean. The fire burns bright._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): helping together  
> _Everyone helped tidy the hall. Why is it good to help together?_  
> - ✅ The job gets done, and friends feel happy → Yes. Helping together makes a big job small.
> - So nobody has to help → When everybody helps, the job is quicker and kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how helping together makes a big job small._

_Eurycleia goes to wake Penelope._  

#### `a14-19-complete`

**Odysseus**: You stood in my door. Guest-friend.  
_He gives you the great bow, with no string._  
**Odysseus**: A friend gave it to me. Keep it over your door.  
**Odysseus**: Remember you have a friend on Ithaca.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): hosts and guests gave gifts to show friendship  
> _In Greece long ago, hosts and guests gave each other gifts._  
> _A gift said, we are friends. What gift could you give a friend?_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that long ago hosts and guests gave gifts to show friendship._


## A14-20. The Olive-Tree Bed

- `a14-20-s1`: Wait in the hall while Penelope comes down. · _Sit on the step and keep out of the way._
- `a14-20-s2`: Stay while she tests him. · _Keep still by the hearth._
- `a14-20-s3`: Go with him to his father’s orchard. · _Walk out to the farm in the hills._

#### `a14-20-hall`

**Eurycleia**: Wake up! He is home!  
**Penelope**: Why do you wake me? I was sleeping so well.  
_Penelope sits across from him, and does not speak._  
**Telemachus**: Mother, why do you not hug him?  
**Penelope**: I must be sure it is really him.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, ask): ask a question when you are not sure  
> _Penelope wants to be sure._  
> _What is a good thing to do when you are not sure?_  
> - ✅ Ask a question → Yes. Asking a question helps us find out what is true.
> - Guess quickly → Guessing can go wrong. Asking a question helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking a question when you are not sure._

_Odysseus smiles. He knows her._  

**Choices**

- **Sit down on the step, out of the way.**
    - This part is theirs. You are only here to see it.
- **Look at Penelope.**
    - She looks at him slowly, like checking every stitch.
- **Hold your Nubbin still.**
    - It wants to run to them, but you hold it.

#### `a14-20-hall-done`

_He goes to bathe. Athena makes him tall and strong._  
_His hair curls like hyacinth petals._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sound of a word  
> _Hyacinth starts with the sound h, h, h._  
> _Which starts the same: hat or fish?_  
> - ✅ Hat → Yes! H, h, hat. H, h, hyacinth.
> - Fish → Fish starts with f, f, f. Hat starts with h, just like hyacinth.
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first sound of a word (h for hyacinth and hat)._


#### `a14-20-bed`

**Odysseus**: Make me a bed out here. I will sleep alone.  
**Penelope**: Move the bed out of our room.  
_Odysseus goes pale._  
**Odysseus**: Nobody could move that bed! I built it round a living olive tree.  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): roots hold a tree in the ground  
> _The bed is built round a living olive tree._  
> _Why can you not move a tree?_  
> - ✅ Its roots hold it in the ground → Yes. Roots grow deep and hold a tree tight.
> - It is too sleepy → Trees are not sleepy. Their roots hold them in the ground.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that roots hold a tree in the ground._

**Odysseus**: That was our secret.  
_Penelope runs to him and hugs him._  
**Penelope**: I had to be sure it was you.  
_They hug and cry._  
**Odysseus**: Penelope. It is me. It is Odysseus.  
_He says his own name out loud, at home._  

#### `a14-20-bed-done`

_You leave them by the fire, quietly._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): the olive tree and Athena: Athens is named for her  
> _In the old story, Athena gave a city its first olive tree._  
> _The city is named Athens, for her._  
> _People in Greece still grow olives today._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned the old story that Athens is named for Athena, who gave it an olive tree._


#### `a14-20-orchard`

_In the morning, you walk to Laertes’s farm._  
_Laertes is digging round a young tree._  
**Odysseus**: Old man, your garden is lovely. But you look sad.  
**Laertes**: I had a son once. I think he has died.  
**Odysseus**: Father, it is me. I came home.  
**Laertes**: Show me a sign.  
**Odysseus**: You gave me thirteen pear trees and ten apple trees.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count ten apple trees  
> _Ten apple trees grow in the orchard._  
> _(Count ten on your fingers together.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:trees:10`
> _For grown-ups: Counted ten apple trees on fingers._

_Laertes hugs his son._  

**Choices**

- **Count the pear trees.**
    - Thirteen, still. Some are very old.
- **Fetch the old man a stool.**
    - Laertes sits, and holds his son’s hand.
- **Let your Nubbin carry his gloves.**
    - It lays them on the wall, one at a time.

#### `a14-20-orchard-done`

**Laertes**: Now everything will be well.  
_But angry families come up the road._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): talking and listening settles a quarrel  
> _Two groups are angry. What is a kind way to settle a quarrel?_  
> - ✅ Talk and listen → Yes. Talking and listening can turn a quarrel into peace.
> - Shout louder → Shouting makes a quarrel bigger. Talking and listening helps.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that talking and listening can settle a quarrel._


#### `a14-20-complete`

_Athena steps between the two sides._  
**Athena**: Stop. Make peace, and keep it.  
_Thunder rumbles and the spears go down. Everyone goes home._  
**Penelope**: Take my loom, guest.  
_Telemachus brings an olive cutting in wet cloth._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): a cutting needs water to grow  
> _The olive cutting is wrapped in wet cloth. Why does it need water?_  
> - ✅ So it can grow roots → Yes. With water, a cutting grows roots and becomes a new tree.
> - So it can swim → A cutting does not swim. Water helps it grow roots.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a cutting needs water to grow roots and become a new tree._

**Odysseus**: Plant it by your water.  
_You are home, with the atlas on your knee._  
_Your Nubbin holds the corner of a very large loom._  

## A15-1. The Grey Prairie

- `a15-01-s1`: Step into the grey page and find the little house. · _Touch the page. Then walk across the flat grass to the one house._
- `a15-01-s2`: Help Uncle Henry and Aunt Em get ready for the storm. · _Look at the dark sky. Then help at the little door in the floor._
- `a15-01-s3`: Ride the storm in the house. Then step out of the page. · _Hold on to your Nubbin. When the page curls, step through._

#### `a15-01-page`

_Nova’s book opens at a grey page._  
_Grey grass. Grey sky._  
_One little grey house._  
_Long ago the house was painted. The sun and rain rubbed it off._  
_You step in. The dry grass goes crunch, crunch._  
_There are no hills. No trees._  
_Just sky._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): flat land is called a prairie  
> _Look all around. Is this land flat, or bumpy with hills?_  
> - ✅ Flat → Yes! Flat all the way to the sky. Wide, flat, grassy land is a prairie.
> - Bumpy → Look again. No hills here! It is flat. Flat grassland is a prairie.
> _For grown-ups: Described a place: a prairie is wide, flat, grassy land._

_A small black dog runs up. Woof, woof!_  
**Dorothy**: I am Dorothy. This is Toto.  
_Toto sniffs your Nubbin. Your Nubbin sniffs Toto._  

**Choices**

- **Tell her your name.**
    - **Dorothy**: What a nice name!
- **Ask why everything is grey.**
    - **Dorothy**: The sun and wind are rough on it.
- **Let your Nubbin play with Toto.**
    - They race round you and tumble in the dust. Giggle!

#### `a15-01-page-done`

**Dorothy**: Come and meet Aunt Em. Follow me and Toto!  
_Dorothy’s dress is pale. The grass is brown._  
_The house is grey._  
_Toto starts with the sound t. Say it: t, t, Toto!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): first sound of a name  
> _(Say t, t, Toto together. Then think of another t word: tree, toe, ten.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:first-sound:t`
> _For grown-ups: Practised hearing and saying the first sound of a name._


#### `a15-01-storm`

_Dark clouds roll in. The wind goes whoo, whoo!_  
**Uncle Henry**: A big storm is coming, Em!  
_The grass bends flat. Whoosh!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): wind is moving air  
> _What do we call air that moves? (Point to the bending grass.)_  
> - ✅ Wind → Yes! Wind is air that moves. It bends the grass.
> - Rain → Rain falls from clouds. Air that moves is wind. Whoo!
> - Snow → Snow is cold and white. Air that moves is wind. Whoo!
> _For grown-ups: Named wind as moving air and saw what it does._

**Aunt Em**: Dorothy! Into the cellar, now!  
_A cellar is a little room under the floor._  
_Toto hides under the bed. Dorothy kneels down for him._  

**Choices**

- **Hold the trap door open for her.**
    - You hold it tight. The floor shakes.
- **Reach under the bed for Toto.**
    - You grab his collar and pass him up. Safe!
- **Grab your Nubbin first.**
    - Your Nubbin is in your arms. It is shaking.

#### `a15-01-storm-done`

_The wind screams. The house shakes._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): go to a safe place in a storm  
> **Aunt Em**: When a big storm comes, we go to a safe place inside.  
> **Aunt Em**: A cellar is safe. So is a room with no windows.  
> _(Ask your grown-up: where is our safe place?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that in a big storm we go to a safe place inside, and talked about ours._

_Then the house turns round and round._  
_It lifts up, up, up, like a balloon._  
**Dorothy**: Hold tight, Toto!  

#### `a15-01-cyclone`

_The house floats high. Inside, it is quiet._  
_It rocks like a cradle. Rock, rock, rock._  
_Toto peeks out of the trap door. Uh-oh!_  
_Dorothy catches him and pulls him back._  
**Dorothy**: That is enough adventure for one little dog.  
_Dorothy lies down to sleep. Toto cuddles close._  
_You stay awake with your Nubbin._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4  
> _Count who is in the house: Dorothy, Toto, you, your Nubbin._  
> _(Count on your fingers. One, two, three, four!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:travellers:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four travellers, matching one number to each._

_A gap opens in the page. You see green grass!_  

**Choices**

- **Step through the gap with your Nubbin.**
    - You step out. Bump!
    - The house lands behind you.
- **Take a last look at Dorothy, asleep.**
    - She sleeps with one arm round Toto. You step through.

#### `a15-01-cyclone-done`

_You land on soft green grass._  
_Everything is bright. Green trees._  
_A blue brook. Singing birds._  
_Your Nubbin rolls over and over. Wheee!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming a feeling about something new  
> _Dorothy lands in a brand new place. How might she feel?_  
> - ✅ Surprised → Yes! Surprised, and maybe a bit scared. New places can feel big.
> - Bored → Not bored! Her eyes go wide. A new place is a big surprise.
> _For grown-ups: Named a feeling a character might have in a new place._


#### `a15-01-complete`

**Dorothy**: Oh my! Where did Kansas go?  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, do): finding and naming a colour  
> _The page was grey. Now it is full of colour!_  
> _Tap three blue things._  
> Check: `edu:tap:colour:blue`
> _For grown-ups: Hunted for one colour in a picture and named it._

_Little people in blue walk up, slowly._  
_They stop and stare at the house._  
_Two silver shoes poke out under one corner._  
_Only your Nubbin sees them._  

## A15-2. The Council with the Munchkins

- `a15-02-s1`: Say hello to the little people and the old woman in white. · _Walk round the house to where they are waiting._
- `a15-02-s2`: Ask the way home. Watch the old woman’s hat. · _Watch the hat while she counts._
- `a15-02-s3`: Help Boq lay the tables for the night. · _Carry the blue dishes from the shelf to the long tables._

#### `a15-02-council`

_Little people in blue gather round. Their hats have tiny bells._  
_An old woman in white bows to Dorothy._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): finding east on a map  
> _The Munchkins live in the east. The sun comes up in the east._  
> _Which way is east?_  
> - ✅ Where the sun comes up → Yes! East is where the sun comes up. The Munchkins are that way.
> - Where it goes to bed → That is west. East is where the sun wakes up!
> _For grown-ups: Linked east with sunrise on a story map._

**The Witch of the North**: Welcome, my dear. You have set these people free.  
**Dorothy**: I did not do anything!  
**The Witch of the North**: Your house did. Look under the corner.  
_Only two silver shoes are left._  
_The very old Witch has dried up, like a puddle in the sun._  
**A Munchkin**: We are free! Hooray!  
**The Witch of the North**: The silver shoes are yours now.  

**Choices**

- **Tell Dorothy to try them on.**
    - **Dorothy**: They fit exactly!
- **Tell her to be careful with them.**
    - **The Witch of the North**: Wise. Know a charm before you use it.
- **Let your Nubbin sniff the shoes.**
    - Sniff, sniff, achoo! Your Nubbin sits on them.

#### `a15-02-council-done`

**Dorothy**: Please, can you help me get home to Aunt Em?  
**Dorothy**: She will be so worried.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): asking for help when you are worried  
> _Dorothy is worried. What does she do?_  
> - ✅ Asks for help → Yes. Asking is brave and it helps. Now we can work it out.
> - Hides → Hiding keeps the worry big. Asking helps, and Dorothy asked.
> _For grown-ups: Saw that asking for help is a good way to deal with a worry._

**The Witch of the North**: Ah. That is hard.  
**The Witch of the North**: Let me think.  

#### `a15-02-slate`

**A Munchkin**: Desert to the east. Desert to the west.  
**A Munchkin**: Nobody crosses.  
_The old woman takes off her hat. She counts: one, two, three._  
_The hat turns into a slate. Chalk letters appear._  
_They tell Dorothy to go to the Emerald City._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): first letter of a word  
> _The slate says Emerald City. Emerald starts with the sound eh._  
> _(Say eh, eh, Emerald. It starts with the letter E.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:first-sound:e`
> _For grown-ups: Heard the first sound of Emerald and met the letter E._

**The Witch of the North**: Keep to the road of yellow bricks. It will take you there.  
_She kisses Dorothy on the forehead. A round mark shines._  

**Choices**

- **Ask if she will kiss you too.**
    - **The Witch of the North**: You carry your own luck, visitor. Share it.
- **Look closely at the mark.**
    - It shines softly, like a coin in a well.
- **Hold your Nubbin up to say goodbye.**
    - She taps its nose. It goes cross-eyed, proud as can be.

#### `a15-02-slate-done`

_She spins round three times on her left heel._  
_Pop! She is gone._  
_Toto barks at the empty place._  
_Tinkle, tinkle. The tiny hat bells ring._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, do): steady beat  
> _The bells go tinkle, tinkle, tinkle, tinkle._  
> _(Clap a steady beat with them. Clap, clap, clap, clap!)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:beat:bells`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped a steady beat along with a sound._


#### `a15-02-boq`

_You walk along the yellow road. Evening comes._  
_A big house. A big feast._  
_Boq waves hello._  
**Boq**: Welcome, Sorceress! Welcome, little friend!  
**Dorothy**: I am only Dorothy.  
**Boq**: Then you are a kind witch. That is best.  
**Boq**: Now: the tables!  
**Boq**: Five tables. Blue plates only!  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _Count the tables with Boq: one, two, three, four, five._  
> _(Point to each table. Say one number for each.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:tables:5`

> - The cups → Look again. The cups are the paler ones. The plates are darker.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two shades of one colour: darker and paler._

## A15-3. The Scarecrow

- `a15-03-s1`: Help lift the Scarecrow down from his pole. · _Climb into the cornfield. Hold the pole steady._
- `a15-03-s2`: Help the Scarecrow find his feet. · _Walk beside him on the yellow bricks. Catch him if he tips._
- `a15-03-s3`: Sit by the road and listen to Dorothy talk about Kansas. · _Sit on the bank with them while Dorothy eats her bread._

#### `a15-03-pole`

_A big cornfield. High on a pole stands a Scarecrow._

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): straw is light and soft  
> _The Scarecrow is made of straw._  
> _Is straw heavy and hard, or light and soft?_  
> - ✅ Light and soft → Yes! Straw is light and soft. That is why he is easy to lift.
> - Heavy and hard → Not straw! Rocks are heavy and hard. Straw is light and soft.
> _For grown-ups: Described a material: straw is light and soft._

_He winks!_  
**The Scarecrow**: Good morning. Would you lift me down, please?  
_Someone must hold the pole steady._  

**Choices**

- **Hold the pole steady.**
    - You hold tight. Dorothy lifts him down.
- **Stand underneath, ready to catch him.**
    - Flump! He lands on you.
    - Like a big, soft pillow.

#### `a15-03-pole-done`

**The Scarecrow**: Thank you! I feel much more like a person.  
_He stretches. He yawns._  
_He falls flat on his face!_

> **The Scarecrow**: Walking is hard at first. Try standing on one foot.  
> _(Stand on one foot and count to 3. Then switch feet!)_  
> Check: `edu:stand:one-foot:balance`
> _For grown-ups: Practised balancing on one foot, as the Scarecrow learns to stand._

_He gets up. He falls over sideways._  
_Flop!_  

#### `a15-03-feet`

**The Scarecrow**: Then I shall come. What a comfort!

_A hole! Plop!_  
_He falls down._  
_Step. Step._  
_Another hole! Plop!_  
_Then a brick gets in the way. Bump!_

> _How many times did he fall? Plop, plop, bump._  
> _(Count: one, two, three!)_

    - **The Scarecrow**: An arm! Just the thing.

    - Your Nubbin walks slowly. He copies every step.

#### `a15-03-feet-done`

_First he can only fall._  
_Next he can take small steps._

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): first, next, last  
> _What did the Scarecrow do last?_  
> - ✅ Walked nearly straight → Yes! First he fell, next he stepped, last he walked.
> - Fell down → That was first! Last, he walked in a nearly straight line.
> _For grown-ups: Put three story events in order: first, next, last._

**Dorothy**: Even if home is plain, it is where my people are.  
**Dorothy**: Nowhere else is home.  
**The Scarecrow**: I see. Home is where the people you love are.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): what makes a place feel like home  
> _What makes a place feel like home to you? (Wait for an answer.)_  
> - ✅ The people there → Yes. Home is the people you love, not the paint.
> - The things in it → Things are nice. But the people matter most.
> - The smell of food → A lovely answer. Food made with love feels like home.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what makes a place feel like home._

> _Corn grows in open fields. Which grows in the woods?_  
> - ✅ Trees → Yes! Lots of trees grow in woods.
> - Corn rows → Corn likes open fields. Woods have trees.
