## A15-4. The Tin Woodman

- `a15-04-s1`: Follow the groaning sound into the forest. · _Leave the road where the trees are thickest. Listen._
- `a15-04-s2`: Find the oil-can in the Woodman’s cottage. · _Look on the shelf for the can with the long thin spout._
- `a15-04-s3`: Oil the Woodman’s joints, one after another. · _Start with his neck. Then his arms. Then his legs._

#### `a15-04-groan`

_In the forest, someone groans. Mmmm._  
**Dorothy**: Who is that?  
_A man made of tin stands still. His axe is up high._  
**The Tin Woodman**: Mmm. I got wet in the rain.  
**The Tin Woodman**: Now I am stuck.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): rain can make metal rusty  
> _Rain made his joints rusty. What can make metal rusty?_  
> _Rain or sunshine?_  
> - ✅ Rain → Yes. Water on metal makes rust. Rusty parts get stuck.
> - Sunshine → Not sunshine. Wet makes rust. Rusty parts get stuck.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that water can make iron rusty, and rusty parts stick._

**The Tin Woodman**: Please oil me. The oil-can is in my cottage.  

**Choices**

- **Say you will fetch it.**
    - **The Tin Woodman**: Thank you. Mind the step.
- **Ask how it happened.**
    - **The Tin Woodman**: The rain. I forgot to shelter.
    - **The Tin Woodman**: That is all.

#### `a15-04-groan-done`

_The cottage is just through the trees._  
_You hurry. Your Nubbin is at your heels._  
**The Tin Woodman**: Thank you for stopping to look.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): helping a friend who is stuck  
> _The Woodman was stuck for a year. You stopped to help._  
> _What do we do for a friend who is stuck?_  
> - ✅ Stop and help → Yes! Stopping to help is kind.
> - Walk past → Walking past leaves them stuck. Stopping to help is kind.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about stopping to help someone who is stuck._


#### `a15-04-cottage`

_The cottage is small and tidy._  
_On a shelf stand three oil-cans._  
_One is big and square. One is small and round._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): biggest and smallest  
> _Point to the biggest oil-can._  
> - ✅ The big square one → Yes! The big square can is the biggest.
> - The small round one → That one is the smallest. The big square can is biggest.
> _For grown-ups: Compared sizes: biggest and smallest._

_One has a long thin spout._  
_Your Nubbin looks up at them._  

**Choices**

- **Take the one with the long spout.**
    - It will reach the joints. It sloshes.
    - It is full.
- **Take the big square one, to be sure.**
    - The big one is empty. You take the full one.
- **Look at the picture a little longer.**
    - A girl, drawn in pencil, smiles. You take the can and go.

#### `a15-04-cottage-done`

_You run back through the trees._  
_You still see the pencil picture in your mind._  
_The girl in it has a kind face._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, do): drawing a face  
> _Draw a face like the one in the picture._  
> _Two eyes, a nose, a smile._  
> Check: `edu:draw:face:smile`
> _For grown-ups: Drew a simple face, naming the parts._


#### `a15-04-oil`

**Dorothy**: Where shall we start?  
_You start with his neck. Drip, drip._  
_His head turns. Creak, creak._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, ask): oil helps parts slide  
> _The joints are stuck. What does the oil do?_  
> - ✅ Helps them slide → Yes! Oil helps parts slide, so they can move.
> - Makes them stickier → The other way! Oil helps parts slide.
> _For grown-ups: Saw how oil can fix a stuck joint._

_Then his arms. They go down at last._  
**The Tin Woodman**: Ahh. Thank you.  
**The Tin Woodman**: Now my legs, please.  

**Choices**

- **Do his legs.**
    - Drip, drip. He takes three steps for fun.
- **Give his jaw another drop first.**
    - **The Tin Woodman**: Ah. Much better.
- **Oil everything you can find, twice.**
    - He shines like a new kettle!

#### `a15-04-oil-done`

_First you oiled his neck._  
_Next you oiled his arms._  
_Last you oiled his legs._  
**The Tin Woodman**: Thank you. One more year and I would be a statue.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): first, next, last  
> _What did you oil first?_  
> - ✅ His neck → Yes! First the neck, next the arms, last the legs.
> - His legs → Legs came last. First was the neck.
> _For grown-ups: Retold three steps in order._


#### `a15-04-complete`

**The Tin Woodman**: Where are you all going?  
**Dorothy**: To the Emerald City, to see Oz.  
**The Tin Woodman**: May I come? I want a heart.  
**The Scarecrow**: I want brains.  
_The Woodman taps his chest. Clong._  
_It is empty._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being kind  
> **The Tin Woodman**: A heart helps me be kind. What is one kind thing to do?  
> - ✅ Help a friend → Yes! Helping is kind.
> - ✅ Share a snack → Yes! Sharing is kind too.
> - Take a toy → That makes people sad. Helping and sharing are kind.
> _For grown-ups: Named kind actions._

_Dorothy hands you the oil-can. It is yours to carry now._

> - Nothing → Saying sorry helps the hurt feeling go away.

> - No, just sleepy → Look at its trembling paws. It was scared and did it anyway. That is brave.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the word brave: doing something even when scared._

**The Cowardly Lion**: Oh! It is not afraid of me.

## A15-7. The River and the Stork

- `a15-07-s1`: Tie the logs into a raft. · _Tie each log to the next with a double knot._

> - ✅ Float → Yes! Wood floats on water. That is why rafts work.
> - Sink → Wood floats! Rafts are made from it because it floats.
> _For grown-ups: Predicted that wood floats and a raft will work._

- **Your Nubbin taught you. It chews them.**
    - Your Nubbin chews the next knot. You tie it again.

> - ✅ Downhill → Yes! Rivers flow downhill, towards the sea.
> - Uphill → Water runs down, not up. Rivers flow downhill.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that rivers flow downhill._

> _What does the Stork use to fly?_  
> - ✅ Wings → Yes! Wings. Her big wings push the air.
> - Fins → Fins are for fish. Birds fly with wings.
> - Wheels → Wheels are for carts. Birds fly with wings.
> _For grown-ups: Named wings as the body part birds use to fly._

_Your Nubbin sees her first. It stands up tall._

    - She looks. It is not a fish.
    - She stays to talk.

> - Help now! → That sounds bossy. Say please, will you help?

> - A fib → Fibs grow bigger and bigger. The truth is better.

> - ✅ The roots → Yes! Roots hold the tree in the ground and drink water.
> - The leaves → Leaves are on the branches. Roots grow under the ground.
> _For grown-ups: Named a tree part: roots grow under the ground._

**The Scarecrow**: Well! How rude.  
**The Scarecrow**: I will try another tree.  
**The Tin Woodman**: Let me go first.  
_The Woodman holds a big branch back._  
_The tree shakes crossly and lets him by._  
**The Cowardly Lion**: Only the first row grabs. They guard the wood.  

**Choices**

- **Keep right behind the Woodman.**
    - A branch reaches for you, finds his axe, and thinks again.
- **Tuck your Nubbin inside your coat.**
    - A branch pats you all over, finds nothing, and gives up.

#### `a15-17-trees-done`

_Behind the first row, the trees are only trees._  
_Everyone gets through. The Scarecrow is last, very ruffled._  
_Tree rhymes with bee._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): rhyming words  
> _Tree rhymes with a word. Which one: bee, or dog?_  
> - ✅ Bee → Yes! Tree and bee end with the same sound.
> - Dog → Dog does not sound like tree. Bee does!
> _For grown-ups: Found a rhyming word for tree._


#### `a15-17-wall`

_A high white wall stands beyond the wood. It is smooth like a plate._  
_The Woodman makes a ladder. You all climb up and over._  
_The other side is a land of china. The houses and people are china._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away 1 from 4  
> _A cow has four legs. One leg broke off._  
> _How many legs are left?_  
> - ✅ Three → Yes! Four take away one leaves three.
> - Two → Count: one, two, three. Three legs are left.
> - Four → One broke off. So there are three left.
> _For grown-ups: Subtracted within 10: four take away one._

**The China Milkmaid**: Look what you have done! Her leg is off!  
**Dorothy**: I am very sorry. Please forgive us.  

**Choices**

- **Pick up the cow’s leg and hand it back.**
    - **The China Milkmaid**: Well. Thank you.
    - **The China Milkmaid**: You might have broken it worse.
- **Say sorry too, as small as you can.**
    - You crouch down small and say sorry. The milkmaid sniffs.

#### `a15-17-wall-done`

_The milkmaid leads her cow away on three legs._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): china and where the name comes from  
> _Long ago, people in China made very fine plates and cups from baked clay._  
> _Now those pretty plates and cups are called china._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that china dishes are named after the people in China who made them first._

**The China Princess**: If I fall, I might break.

**The China Princess**: Here we walk and talk and do as we like.  
**The China Princess**: Out there we would go stiff and still, like a jug on a shelf.

_One comes to the fence. Your Nubbin touches noses with it._  
_Your Nubbin looks at your pocket. It wants the lamb so much._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): where someone is happiest  
> _Where is the lamb happiest: in its own field, or in a pocket?_  
> - ✅ In its own field → Yes. Home is where a lamb can run and play.
> - In a pocket → A pocket is cosy. But the lamb is happier free in its own field.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what a living thing needs to be happy, not just safe._


**Choices**

    - You tuck it in your pocket. Your Nubbin keeps a paw on it.
- **Put it back in its field.**
    - You gently lead your Nubbin away. The lamb bleats once, tiny.
    - Your Nubbin looks back three times. Then it walks close to you.

> _A china plate has a pattern: blue, white, blue, white. What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Blue → Yes! Blue, white, blue, white, blue. The pattern repeats.
> - White → White came last. Next comes blue.
> _For grown-ups: Continued a repeating AB colour pattern._

#### `a15-18-council`

_Past the tall grass is a forest of great old trees._  
**The Cowardly Lion**: What a forest. I could live here for ever.  
_In a clearing, hundreds of animals are talking at once._

**The Tiger**: King of Beasts! We need you.  
**The Tiger**: A giant spider chases and frightens us.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): spiders have eight legs  
> _A spider has eight legs. Count them on your fingers._  
> _(One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight!)_

> _For grown-ups: Learned that spiders have eight legs and counted them._

_Your Nubbin presses against your legs again._

    - His mane is up. You cannot tell if it is courage or worry.
- **Pick up your Nubbin.**
    - Its heart goes fast. So does yours.

#### `a15-18-council-done`

**The Cowardly Lion**: If I deal with this spider, will you have me for your King?  
**The Tiger**: Gladly. All of us.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): a fair leader  
> _The animals want a King._  
> _What makes a good leader: kind and fair, or loud and bossy?_  
> - ✅ Kind and fair → Yes! A good leader is kind and fair to everyone.
> - Loud and bossy → Bossy leaders make others unhappy. Kind and fair is best.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what makes a fair leader._

**The Cowardly Lion**: Then wait here.  

#### `a15-18-wait`

**The Cowardly Lion**: Look after my friends. I will go before I think about it.  
_He goes into the trees alone._  
_Your Nubbin starts after him. Then it comes back and sits down._  
**Dorothy**: He was so scared of the ditch. And now this.  
**The Tin Woodman**: I think courage was inside him all the time.  
_You wait. The forest is very quiet._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when you wait and worry  
> _You are waiting for a friend and feeling worried. What helps?_  
> - ✅ Sit together → Yes! Sitting with a friend makes waiting easier.
> - ✅ Slow breaths → Yes! Slow breaths help worries get smaller.
> - Run off → Staying together is better. Sit and breathe slowly.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when you are waiting and worried._


**Choices**

- **Sit down and wait, with your Nubbin in your lap.**
    - Your Nubbin climbs onto your lap. You wait the way you wait for anyone.
- **Stand at the edge and watch the trees.**

#### `a17-02-granny`

_Granny comes with rags and a bucket._

> - Run away and hide alone. → That is a big worry to carry alone. Laughing with a friend can help it feel smaller.
> - Stay still and say nothing. → Staying still is fine for a moment. But telling a friend, or laughing together, helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Thought of calming ways to feel braver: laughing and being with someone._

**Mei**: I will laugh. I am good at it!  
_Kanta shouts, “Your house is haunted!” and runs away._

## A17-3. The Bath in the Storm

- `a17-03-s1`: Help shut the rain shutters before the storm. · _Pull each wooden shutter along until the house is closed._
- `a17-03-s2`: Wait in the main room while the family has their bath. · _Sit by the low table. Join in when Mr Kusakabe calls._
- `a17-03-s3`: Sit on Granny’s step and watch the hill. · _Go home through the hedge. Sit on the step and look up._

#### `a17-03-shutters`

_The wind gets up. Whoosh!_  
_The rice fields go silver._  
**Granny**: Go and help with the shutters.  
**Mr Kusakabe**: One is stuck. Can you help?  
_You lift it a little. Slide!_  
_It runs all the way along._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, ask): a stuck thing may move when we lift and push in a better way  
> _The shutter is stuck. What can we try?_  
> - ✅ Lift a little, then push. → Yes! Trying a new way solves a stuck problem.
> - Walk away. → Then the shutter stays stuck. Trying a new way, like lift and push, can fix it.
> - Pull the wrong way harder. → Harder is not always better. Lifting a little and pushing works best.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a new way of lifting and pushing to solve a stuck shutter._

_The boards creak. The house groans like a ship._  
**Mr Kusakabe**: The house is only stretching, Mei. Old houses do.  

#### `a17-03-shutters-done`

**Mr Kusakabe**: Stay till the wind drops. The bath is nearly hot.  
_Your Nubbin sits by the stove. Rattle!_  
_The shutters jump._  
_Creak! Bang!_  
_The house makes lots of noises._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, do): sound words that copy noises: creak, rattle, bang  
> _The old house is noisy! Say the sounds with me._  
> _(Say them in a big voice: creak, rattle, bang.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-words:creak`
> _For grown-ups: Said sound words that copy noises: creak, rattle and bang._


#### `a17-03-bath`

_The family has a bath at the back. You wait in the main room._  
_A gust hits the house. Bang!_  
_The lamp swings._  
**Mei**: Dad! I heard something!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): telling a trusted grown-up when we feel scared  
> _Mei heard a noise and felt scared. What did she do?_  
> - ✅ She told her dad. → Yes! Telling someone you trust is a good thing to do.
> - She hid and said nothing. → Hiding can feel safe, but the worry stays big. Mei told her dad, and that helped.
> - She ran out into the storm. → That would not be safe. Mei told her dad. Telling a grown-up is a safe, brave thing.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that telling a trusted adult helps when we feel scared._

**Mr Kusakabe**: Do you know what to do? Laugh, as loud as you can!  
_From the back comes a big, silly laugh. Ha ha ha!_  

**Choices**

    - You laugh. It sounds so silly, you laugh more.
- **Tickle your Nubbin.**
    - Your Nubbin squeaks and rolls. Everyone laughs.
- **Try to laugh. Out comes a honk.**
    - **Mei**: Do it again!

#### `a17-03-bath-done`

_The wind blows on. Inside, nobody minds any more._

> _A warm bath makes you clean. It makes you sleepy too._  
> _When you sleep, your body rests and grows._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a warm bath cleans us, and that sleep helps our bodies rest and grow._

> _Look at the Moon. It does not make its own light._  
> _The Sun lights it up, like a torch shining on a ball._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Moon shines because the Sun lights it._

## A17-4. The Hospital

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a bicycle goes faster downhill and needs more push uphill  
> _Which way is easier on a bike: down the hill, or up?_  
> - ✅ Down the hill. → Yes! The hill helps you roll, whoosh! Uphill needs lots of push.
> - Up the hill. → Uphill is hard work. Pedal, pedal, puff! Down the hill is easier. The hill helps you roll.
> _For grown-ups: Compared riding downhill and uphill: downhill is easier._


**Choices**

- **Race them to the top.**
    - Mr Kusakabe wins by a wheel. Then he puffs.
- **Ride slowly and let them win.**
    - Mei shouts happily all the way down.

> _(Clap three times: hos, pi, tal.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:hospital`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the three syllables in the word hospital._

**Mrs Kusakabe**: Come here, both of you.  
_Mei climbs on the bed. Satsuki holds her mum’s hand._  
**Mrs Kusakabe**: The nurses and doctors are looking after me. I am getting better.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): naming the feeling of missing someone, and what helps  
> _Mei and Satsuki miss their mum. What helps when we miss someone?_  
> - ✅ A big hug. → Yes! A hug is a good help.
> - ✅ Talking about them. → Yes! Talking about someone helps too.
> - Pretend we do not miss them. → Missing someone is a real feeling. It is okay to have it. A hug or a chat about them helps.
> _For grown-ups: Named missing someone as a real feeling, and chose hugs and talking as help._


#### `a17-04-room-done`

> _Nurses, doctors, good food and sleep help too._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that rest, food and caring helpers all help a body get well._

> _The family wants a quiet moment together. What does the Keeper do?_

> - Go back in and chatter. → Chattering would break their quiet moment. Waiting outside gives them space.

## A17-7. Kanta’s Umbrella

_Rain! It comes all at once._

_Satsuki bows to the statue. You bow too._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): Jizo statues watch over children and travellers; we ask politely and are respectful  
> _The small statue is called Jizo. He watches over children and travellers._  
> _Satsuki asks politely. Being polite is a way of showing respect._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned about Jizo, who watches over children and travellers, and how Satsuki shows respect._

#### `a17-07-rain-done`

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): a cloth umbrella keeps rain out because water cannot get through it  
> _Which keeps the rain off best?_  
> - ✅ Umbrella cloth. → Yes! Rain cannot get through cloth that is made for rain.
> - A sponge. → A sponge soaks water up. Umbrella cloth keeps rain out.
> - A net. → Water runs right through a net. Umbrella cloth keeps rain out.
> _For grown-ups: Compared materials and chose the one that keeps rain out._

**Satsuki**: Mei.  

#### `a17-07-return`

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): saying thank you in a gentle way that does not embarrass someone  
> _How can they thank shy Kanta kindly?_  
> - ✅ Leave a kind note. → Yes! A note lets him feel proud, not shy.
> - Shout it in the street. → That would make him very shy. A quiet note is gentler.
> - Say nothing at all. → Then he would not know they are grateful. A kind note says thank you gently.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a gentle way of saying thank you to someone who is shy._

**Satsuki**: Keeper, what do we do?

    - The note says Thank you. Next day it is gone.
- **Give it to Granny.**
    - **Granny**: He did, did he? The daft boy.
- **Let Satsuki give it back.**
    - **Satsuki**: Thank you. It was very kind.
    - **Kanta**: S’all right.

- `a18-01-s1`: Step into the painted page. Knock at the merchant’s house. · _Touch the page. Then walk up to the wooden house._

#### `a18-01-house`

_The atlas opens to a painted page. It is yellow and black._  
_Pop! You step inside. A wooden house, with snow at its edges._  
_A big man in a fur hat opens the door._  
**The Merchant**: Come in! A friend of Nova’s can stay with us.  
**The Merchant**: My wife is poorly. We walk softly here.  
_A little girl peeks round his knee. She has a long plait._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): first sound of a name  
> **The Merchant**: This is my girl, Vasilisa. Vvv-asilisa.  
> _(Say the first sound together: vvv. Now try: van, vase, vine.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:first-sound:v`
> _For grown-ups: Said the first sound of a character’s name (v) and thought of other words that start with it._

**Vasilisa**: What is it? Does it eat?  

**Choices**

- **Say it is a Nubbin. It eats everything.**
    - **Vasilisa**: Everything? Even burnt porridge?
    - Your Nubbin nods. Burnt bits are the best bits.
- **Let your Nubbin say hello.**
    - Your Nubbin sits on her shoe. She goes very still.
- **Ask her name first.**
    - **Vasilisa**: Manners say you go first. But I will tell you anyway.

#### `a18-01-house-done`

**Vasilisa**: I am Vasilisa. I will be kind to guests. Mostly.  
**The Merchant**: Go and wash your hands, Vasilisa.  
_She goes up slowly. She keeps looking back at your Nubbin._  
_The house is made of big logs, laid one on another._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): long ago, houses were often made of wood  
> _This house is made of logs. Where do logs come from?_  
> - ✅ Trees → Yes! Long ago, many houses were built from tree logs.
> - Clouds → Not clouds. Logs come from trees. A forest gave this house its walls.
> - The sea → Not the sea. Logs come from trees, cut from the forest.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that long ago many houses were built from logs, which come from trees._


#### `a18-01-counterpane`

_That evening, a soft voice calls Vasilisa._  
_You walk her to the bedroom door. You wait there._  
_Her mother sits up in bed. Her blanket is made of bright scraps._  
**Vasilisa’s Mother**: Vasilisa, I am very poorly. I will not get better.  
_She takes out a little doll with a red scarf._  
**Vasilisa’s Mother**: This doll is my love, in a small shape. Keep her close.  
**Vasilisa’s Mother**: When you need help, give her food first. Then ask her.  
**Vasilisa’s Mother**: Tell nobody about her, and she will help you.  
**Vasilisa**: Food first. Then ask. Tell nobody.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming a big feeling  
> _Vasilisa’s mother is very poorly. How might Vasilisa feel?_  
> - ✅ Sad and scared → Yes. Vasilisa feels sad and scared. Those feelings are allowed.
> - Silly and giggly → Not giggly. Look at her face. She is sad and scared.
> - Hungry for pie → Not pie. Her heart is heavy. She is sad and scared.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feelings (sad and scared) that someone has when a person they love is very ill._

_Her mother looks at you. She does not send you away._  

**Choices**

- **Stay by the door.**
    - You stay. Your Nubbin sits on your foot and keeps still.
- **Step back and give them room.**
    - Through the gap, her mother lays a hand on Vasilisa’s head.
- **Nod: you will look after her.**
    - **Vasilisa’s Mother**: Thank you. She will need a friend.

#### `a18-01-complete`

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what helps someone who is sad  
> _Vasilisa is very sad. What helps a sad friend?_

> - Say stop crying → Crying is allowed. Sitting beside them helps much more.
> - Walk away → A sad friend feels better when someone stays. Sit beside them.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sitting beside a sad friend is a good way to help, and that crying is allowed._

## A18-2. Little Doll, Eat

- `a18-02-s1`: Follow Vasilisa down to the cellar with a candle. · _Take the candle from the kitchen shelf and go after her._
- `a18-02-s2`: Hold the light while Vasilisa feeds the doll. Keep still. · _Keep the candle steady. Don’t speak._
- `a18-02-s3`: Learn how to set out the food. Make Vasilisa a promise. · _Lay the food in a row in front of the doll. Then answer Vasilisa._

#### `a18-02-supper`

_Days pass. People bring pies, then go home._  
_At supper, Vasilisa eats almost nothing._  
_The best bits go into her apron: a crust, an egg, a honey cake._  
**The Merchant**: Eat, little one. You are getting thin.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): bodies need food and water to be strong  
> _Vasilisa is not eating much. What does a body need to feel strong?_  
> - ✅ Food and water → Yes! Good food and water give a body energy to play, work and grow.
> - Only pie → Pie is yummy. But a body needs many foods, and water too.
> - Nothing at all → Everybody needs food and water. Without them we feel weak.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what a body needs to feel strong: food and water._

**Vasilisa**: I am eating, Father. Look!  
_She chews a tiny bit of turnip. Then she slips away._  
_Your Nubbin looks at you. It saw the honey cake too._  

**Choices**

- **Take the candle and follow her.**
    - The cellar door is open a crack. Below, a very small voice.
- **Finish your supper, then follow.**
    - You finish. Then you take the candle down after her.
    - She was waiting in the dark for somebody with a light.

#### `a18-02-supper-done`

**Vasilisa**: Oh! It is you. Shut the door. Properly, it sticks.  
_You shut it properly. Thud! It does stick._  
_Door. Floor. They sound the same at the end._

_The food is gone. Your Nubbin leans in, and the cake is gone too!_

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): how to help a sad friend

> - Say hurry up → Sad feelings need time. Staying close and listening helps.
> - Go away → Going away leaves a sad friend alone. Stay close and listen.
> _For grown-ups: Practised choosing to stay close and listen when a friend is sad._

## A18-3. The Widow

- `a18-03-s1`: Meet the merchant’s new wife and her daughters. · _Wait in the yard when the cart comes in at the gate._
- `a18-03-s2`: Get up before dawn. See how the work is getting done. · _Go out to the garden before anyone else is up._
- `a18-03-s3`: Help Vasilisa look busy when her stepmother comes round. · _When the back door opens, give Vasilisa something to be doing._

#### `a18-03-cart`

_The atlas turns a page. It is spring, and the birches are green._  
**The Merchant**: I have found a new wife. She has two daughters.  
_A cart rolls in, piled with trunks. Three people sit on top._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): heavier and lighter  
> _The trunks are huge. The hatbox is tiny._  
> _Which is heavier to carry?_  
> - ✅ The big trunk → Yes! The big trunk is heavier. The hatbox is light.
> - The tiny hatbox → Look again. The big trunk is much heavier. The hatbox is light.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two objects by weight: the big trunk is heavier, the little hatbox lighter._

**The Stepmother**: So this is the house. And this is the girl.  
**The Elder Sister**: She is very pretty.  
**The Younger Sister**: Too pretty. It is not fair!  
**The Stepmother**: Pretty fades, my loves. Sun and wind and work will see to that.  
_Vasilisa curtsies and says nothing. One hand is in her pocket._  

**Choices**

- **Offer to carry a trunk.**
    - **The Stepmother**: The guest may carry all of them.
    - You carry them all. Your Nubbin carries a hatbox, eyes shut.
- **Stand beside Vasilisa.**
    - You stand beside her. The stepmother looks past you.

#### `a18-03-cart-done`

**The Stepmother**: Vasilisa will do the garden, the water, the stove and the floors.  
**The Elder Sister**: And we will do the sitting down.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words and voices that show feelings  
> _The elder sister says it in a sneery voice. How does she sound?_  
> - ✅ Unkind → Yes. A sneery voice sounds unkind. Words and voices show feelings.
> - Kind → Listen again. A sneery voice is not kind. It sounds unkind.
> - Sleepy → Not sleepy. A sneery voice sounds unkind.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed how a voice and words can show a feeling, such as unkindness._

_Vasilisa curtsies again. In her pocket, something small is very still._

_Smoke curls from the kitchen chimney. The stove is hot._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): plants need water and light  
> _The garden beds are full of plants. What do plants need to grow?_  
> - ✅ Water and sunlight → Yes! Plants drink water and use sunlight to grow.
> - Only sweets → Plants do not eat sweets. They need water and sunlight.
> - Nothing at all → Every plant needs water and sunlight to grow.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants need water and sunlight to grow._

**Vasilisa**: Shh! I fed the doll and asked. She said sleep, so I did.  
_In the cabbage bed, the doll pulls up the last dandelion._  
_Your Nubbin helps, and they tumble backwards. Pop! It comes out._  
_Vasilisa puts the crown on your Nubbin. The morning begins._

_Vasilisa keeps a happy secret. It keeps her safe._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): happy secrets and secrets that scare you  
> _A happy secret is fine. It is like a surprise party._

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sun safety  
> _Working in the sun all day can make skin hot and sore. What helps?_  
> - ✅ A hat, shade and water → Yes! A hat, a shady rest and a drink keep you safe.
> - Nothing at all → Too much sun can hurt. A hat, some shade and water help.
> - A big winter coat → Too hot! A hat, some shade and water are better.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a hat, shade and water help keep us safe when we are out in the sun._

**The Elder Sister**: She was picking flowers! She has pollen on her nose!  
**The Stepmother**: Where is your hoe, girl? Where is your bucket?

    - She swings it as if it were full. A very good act.

> - One person does everything → That is not fair. One person gets worn out. Sharing is fair.

#### `a18-04-years`

_The atlas turns many pages. Whoosh, like birds taking off._  
_The birches are twice as tall now. The swing is too small._  
_Vasilisa comes down the path. She is grown up, taller than you._

_Your Nubbin walks round her twice, puzzled._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): taller and shorter  
> _Vasilisa was small. Now she is tall._  
> _Who is taller now, you or Vasilisa?_  
> - ✅ Vasilisa → Yes! She is taller than you now. She has grown.
> - You → Look again. Vasilisa has grown. She is taller than you now.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two heights and saw that a person who has grown is taller._

**Vasilisa**: I am glad. Everything else changes. It is nice when something stays.

**Choices**

    - **Vasilisa**: Young men. For me.
    - **Vasilisa**: Not for my sisters.

    - **Vasilisa**: Still there. She says hello.
    - The doll did not say it. Vasilisa is being kind.

#### `a18-04-years-done`

_Behind her, down at the gate, somebody is knocking._  
_Knock, knock, knock! Wood makes a sound when it is tapped._

> _(Tap a table softly. Then tap it hard._  
> _Which sound is louder?)_

> _For grown-ups: Tapped softly and hard and heard that harder taps make louder sounds._


#### `a18-04-gate`

_At the gate stands a young man in a clean shirt._  
**The Stepmother**: Who is it for? Not for my girls?  
_He goes pink. He says Vasilisa’s name._  
**The Stepmother**: Go home. The youngest does not marry before the elders.  
**The Stepmother**: That is the custom in this house.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): a custom is a way people always do things  
> _A custom is something a family does again and again. Which is a custom?_  
> - ✅ Saying goodnight every evening → Yes! Goodnight every evening is a custom. People keep customs for years.
> - Dropping a spoon once → Dropping a spoon was an accident. A custom happens again and again.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a custom is something a family or village does again and again._

_He goes. The next young man does not get a word in._

#### `a18-04-last`

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being kind to someone who is disappointed

> - Laugh at him → Laughing hurts. A kind word helps a sad person.
> - Pretend not to see → He is sad, and you can see it. A kind word helps.
> _For grown-ups: Chose kindness towards someone who is disappointed._

_Your Nubbin holds the gate with both paws, as if that could help._

> - In a hot desert → Too hot and dry. Birches like cool lands with snowy winters.

**The Elder Sister**: Everybody says a hut stands in there.

> - Pretend you do not miss them → Missing someone is allowed. Holding something of theirs helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how holding a keepsake or talking about someone helps when we miss them._


#### `a18-05-errand`

**The Stepmother**: Vasilisa. We need bark and mushrooms. Go deep into the wood.

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): never eat wild mushrooms without a grown-up who knows  
> _Wild mushrooms can make you very ill._

> - Taste a tiny bit → Never taste wild mushrooms. They can make you ill. Ask a grown-up.
> - Give one to a friend → Not to a friend either. Ask a grown-up who knows.
> _For grown-ups: Learned never to eat wild mushrooms and to ask a knowledgeable grown-up._

_Vasilisa touches her pocket. Then she turns, sure of the way._

## A18-6. One Candle

- `a18-06-s1`: Sit with the family for an evening of work by one candle. · _Take your place at the table, near the candle._
- `a18-06-s2`: See what happens to the candle. · _Stay at the table. It is about to go dark._
- `a18-06-s3`: Set out the doll’s supper in the dark, the way Vasilisa taught you. · _Feel for the napkin. Lay the food in a row. Then wait._

#### `a18-06-evening`

_An autumn evening. Rain taps the window._  
**The Stepmother**: Work, all of you. Lace for you. A stocking for you. Vasilisa, spin.  
_She puts out every fire. The lamp, the stove, all of them._  
**The Stepmother**: One candle is enough.  
_One candle on the table, and four people round it._  
_Your Nubbin keeps trying to sit on the warm bit._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): candle flames are hot: keep back and tell a grown-up  
> _A candle flame is hot. What should we do near a candle?_  
> - ✅ Keep back, and tell a grown-up → Yes! Flames are hot. Keep back and tell a grown-up.
> - Touch the flame → Ouch! Never touch a flame. Keep back and tell a grown-up.
> - Blow on it close up → Too close is not safe. Keep back and tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Learned to keep away from a candle flame and to tell a grown-up._

_Vasilisa’s spindle turns and turns. Her thread is thin and even._

    - She nearly smiles. Then she remembers to be cross.
- **Keep your Nubbin off the candle.**
    - You lift it off the table three times. Then you just hold it.

> _A nod can mean yes. A head shake can mean no._

> - Yes, that is fair → Look again. One person did nothing wrong. That is not fair.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about fairness: it is not fair to send one person into danger and then blame them._

## A18-7. The Three Riders

- `a18-07-s1`: Walk through the birch wood all night with Vasilisa. · _Keep close behind her and turn when she turns._
- `a18-07-s2`: Stand still and let the riders go by. · _Step off the path at dawn, and again at sunrise._
- `a18-07-s3`: Reach the clearing at dusk. Let the last rider pass. · _Keep to the edge of the clearing. Hide your Nubbin if it wants hiding._

#### `a18-07-night`

_All night you walk. There is no path, but Vasilisa is sure._  
_Twice an owl floats over. Once something big passes, far away._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): owls are awake at night  
> _An owl floats over in the dark. When is an owl awake?_  
> - ✅ At night → Yes! Owls are awake at night. They sleep in the day.
> - Only at breakfast → Owls do their hunting at night. They sleep in the day.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that owls are awake at night._

_The cold comes down. Your breath makes little clouds._  
**Vasilisa**: Talk to me. Anything. Then I will not hear the wood.  
**Vasilisa**: If you hear hooves, stand still. Let them pass.  
_Near the end of the dark, you hear hooves._  

**Choices**

- **Tell her about your gran’s garden.**
    - You whisper about the Grove, the pond, and a gran who grew things.
    - **Vasilisa**: She sounds like Mother. Not to look at.
    - **Vasilisa**: In the hands.
- **Count the birches with her.**
    - You count up to four hundred and twelve. Vasilisa says thirteen.
    - Your Nubbin sneezes. That makes fourteen.
- **Hold her hand and say nothing.**
    - Her hand is cold and holds on hard. Then it warms.

_Your Nubbin holds its breath, to be safe._

> _Do it three times.)_

#### `a18-07-white`

_A rider comes at a walk, all in white, on a white horse._  
_He passes. The sky goes from black to grey, then to milk._  
**Vasilisa**: Morning! He brought the morning. Or it followed him.  
_The birds start. One, then all of them._  
_Then a rider all in red, on a red horse. He trots by._  
_The sun rises. Everything goes red, then gold, then bright day._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): the order of the day: dawn, sunrise, daytime  
> _The sky was dark, then grey, then gold. What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Daytime → Yes! After the sun rises it is daytime.
> - Night time → Night comes later. After the sun rises it is daytime.
> _For grown-ups: Put the parts of the day in order: dark, dawn, sunrise, daytime._

**Vasilisa**: White, then red. Somebody is counting out the day.

    - **Baba Yaga**: Never seen one of you. I have seen everything, so that is something.

**Baba Yaga**: Same rules for you as for her. Work, and you go home.

## A18-9. Supper for Ten

- `a18-09-s1`: Help Vasilisa carry Baba Yaga’s supper to the table. · _Bring dish after dish out of the great white stove._
- `a18-09-s2`: Decide who has your crust. · _There is one crust and a long day tomorrow. Choose._

#### `a18-09-supper`

_Out of the stove come pots, and pots, and pots._  
_Vasilisa carries, you carry, and your Nubbin carries a spoon._  
_Soup, pork, pies, porridge, a goose, and three big jugs._  
**Baba Yaga**: More! Look in the back. There is always something at the back.  
_She eats like the wind crossing a field. All of it!_  
_Your Nubbin watches the goose go. It looks very sad._  
**Baba Yaga**: Ah. Better. That is what an old woman needs.  
_She leaves a little soup, a crust and a tiny scrap of pork._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.C.6, ask): more and fewer  
> _Baba Yaga ate a mountain of food. Vasilisa has a tiny bowl._  
> _Who has more?_  
> - ✅ Baba Yaga → Yes! Baba Yaga had much more. Vasilisa has very little.
> - Vasilisa → Look again. Baba Yaga ate a mountain. Vasilisa has just a little.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two amounts of food and said which was more._

**Baba Yaga**: That is yours, girl. And a crust for you, since you carried.  

#### `a18-09-supper-done`

_Baba Yaga climbs on the stove and pulls a quilt over her._  
_She snores like a saw going through a log. Zzzrrr!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, do): sounds are made by shaking  
> _Every sound is made by something shaking._  
> _(Touch your throat and hum. Feel the tickle?)_  
> _That tickle is your voice shaking!_  
> Check: `edu:hum:throat:feel`
> _For grown-ups: Felt their throat shake while humming, learning that sound comes from vibrations._


#### `a18-09-crust`

_Vasilisa takes her supper into the corner behind the stove._  
_You hear the napkin. Two small lights come on, and her supper is gone._  
**Vasilisa**: She needed it more. She has to work tomorrow.  
_Vasilisa is very pale. She has not eaten since yesterday._  
_Your crust sits on the table. It is the only food left._  
_Your Nubbin climbs up and looks at the crust. It does not touch it._  
_Tomorrow will be very long._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, notice): there is no wrong choice; caring for others and for yourself  
> _There is no wrong choice here._  
> _Sharing with others is a kind way to care. Looking after yourself matters too._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sharing food is a way to care, and that looking after yourself matters as well._


**Choices**

- **Give it to your Nubbin.**
    - You break it small. Your Nubbin eats every crumb, looking at you.
    - Feed them first, says Gran Hazel. You are hungry, but it feels right.
- **Give it to the doll, for Vasilisa.**
    - **Vasilisa**: For her? But it is yours!
    - **You**: She works for two tomorrow. She should eat for two.
    - The doll’s lights come on, brighter than before.
- **Eat it yourself. Tomorrow is long.**
    - You eat it. It is very dry, and then it is gone.
    - Your Nubbin curls up on your feet anyway. That is kind.

#### `a18-09-crust-done`

_The fire in the stove sinks to red._  
_Vasilisa curls up on the bench with one hand in her pocket._  
_A crust can be shared, and broken in half._

> _(Fold a paper in half. Two equal parts!)_  
> _Each part is called one half._  
> Check: `edu:fold:paper:halves`
> _For grown-ups: Folded paper into halves and saw two equal parts._

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): first, next, last  
> _Which job comes last: sweeping the yard, cooking dinner, or sifting oats?_  
> - ✅ Sifting the oats → Yes! First the yard and hut, next dinner and linen, last the oats.
> - Sweeping the yard → Sweeping comes first. The oats are last.
> - Cooking dinner → Dinner is the middle job. The oats are last.
> _For grown-ups: Listened to a list of jobs and named the one that comes last (first, next, last)._

**Baba Yaga**: If it is not done when I come back, we shall see.

## A18-10. The First Day

- `a18-10-s1`: Keep close while Vasilisa asks the doll what to do. · _Stay by the warm stove and listen._
- `a18-10-s2`: Help with the yard, the hut and the oats while Vasilisa sleeps. · _Sweep, scrub and sift. The doll is working too._
- `a18-10-s3`: Stand by while Baba Yaga looks over the work. · _Wait in the yard as the night comes down._

#### `a18-10-night`

_When the snoring is steady, Vasilisa takes the doll out._

_There is no food left to give. The two little lights come on anyway._  
**Dollet**: Lie down and rest. A good sleep makes you strong.  
**Dollet**: Things look better when you wake.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sleep helps our bodies  
> _Sleep is good for us. What does a good sleep do?_  
> - ✅ Gives us energy and helps us grow → Yes! Sleep gives our bodies energy and helps us grow.
> - Makes us hungry for pie → Not pie. Sleep gives us energy and helps us grow.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sleep gives the body energy and helps children grow._

**Vasilisa**: That is what Mother used to say. The same thing.  
_She lies down on the bench. She is asleep in a blink._  

**Choices**

- **Do as the doll says, and sleep.**
    - You lie down by the stove. The doll keeps watch for all of you.

## A18-11. The Second Day

- `a18-11-s1`: Hear what the second day’s work is. · _Listen to Baba Yaga before she goes out._
- `a18-11-s2`: Help get the earth out of the poppy seeds. · _Work at the barn table. Your Nubbin can help._
- `a18-11-s3`: Watch Baba Yaga find no fault, a second time. · _Wait in the yard as night falls._

#### `a18-11-list`

**Baba Yaga**: Up! Today the same jobs. And one thing more.  
_She drags a sack across the floor. It is full of tiny poppy seeds._

**Baba Yaga**: Somebody did this to me once. Somebody always does.  
**Baba Yaga**: Get every speck of earth out. I will know.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a sieve sorts small from big  
> _A sieve is a bowl with tiny holes. What does a sieve do?_  
> - ✅ Lets small bits fall through → Yes! Small bits fall through. Bigger bits stay in the sieve.
> - Makes things bigger → A sieve does not grow things. Small bits fall through the holes.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sieve lets small bits fall through while larger bits stay behind._

_She whistles, her mortar comes, and she is gone._  
**Vasilisa**: Every speck. You cannot even see which are specks.

    - **Vasilisa**: I will ask her first.

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): guess, then try: black and white paint make grey

#### `a18-11-oil`

_Baba Yaga comes down in her mortar and goes straight to the barn._  
_She sniffs the seeds. She sniffs the earth. Twice._

**Baba Yaga**: Servants of mine! Take the poppy and press it. I want oil by morning.  
_Three pairs of hands come out of the dark and take the sack._  
**Baba Yaga**: You helped, did you not. I can see it on your sleeves.  
**Baba Yaga**: I pay for work. Here.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): work deserves fair pay  
> _Baba Yaga pays for work._  
> _Is it fair to pay someone who worked for you?_  
> - ✅ Yes. Work deserves thanks and pay → Yes! Fair people pay or thank those who work for them.
> - No. Work should be free → Work takes effort. It is fair to pay or thank people who work.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about fairness: someone who works for us should be paid or properly thanked._

_She hands you a tiny cracked mortar and pestle._  
**Baba Yaga**: Too small for flying. Plant something in it.  

**Choices**

    - **Baba Yaga**: Do not thank me. It is pay.
    - **Baba Yaga**: Pay is not a present.
    - But for a moment she looks pleased.
- **Ask whether it ever flew.**
    - **Baba Yaga**: Once. A very short way. Into a pond.
    - She does not explain. You do not ask again.

#### `a18-11-oil-done`

_By morning there is a jar of golden poppy oil on the table._  
_Nobody saw it arrive._

> _Poppy seeds do this. So do sunflower seeds!_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that some seeds, like poppy and sunflower seeds, contain oil that can be pressed out._

## A18-12. Questions

- `a18-12-s1`: Stand by Vasilisa while Baba Yaga eats. Listen. · _Keep quiet at the table. Vasilisa will speak._
- `a18-12-s2`: Decide whether to ask a question of your own. · _Think about what Baba Yaga just said about questions._
- `a18-12-s3`: Hear how Vasilisa answers Baba Yaga’s question. · _Stay near the door. It may be time to go quickly._

#### `a18-12-supper`

_Baba Yaga eats and eats. Vasilisa stands by, as still as a post._  
**Vasilisa**: Granny, may I ask you some questions?  
**Baba Yaga**: Ask, then. Mind you pick good ones.  
**Vasilisa**: A rider in white went by. Who was he?  
**Baba Yaga**: That was my bright day.  
**Vasilisa**: And a rider all in red?  
**Baba Yaga**: That was my red sun.  
**Vasilisa**: And one all in black, at your gate?  
**Baba Yaga**: My dark night. All three are mine, and faithful.  
_Vasilisa thinks of the hands. She shuts her mouth._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): old tales are told in many places  
> _This tale is very old. People told it aloud for hundreds of years._  
> _Baba Yaga is in Ukrainian, Belarusian, Polish and Russian stories too._  
> _Each place tells her a little differently. Stories travel with people._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that this old tale, and Baba Yaga, are told in many places, each a little differently._


#### `a18-12-supper-done`

**Baba Yaga**: Is that all? Nothing else?  
_Bright day, red sun, dark night. A pattern of three!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, do): repeated lines and patterns of three  
> _(Say it with me: bright day, red sun, dark night.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:repeat:three`
> _For grown-ups: Said a pattern of three phrases aloud, noticing the rhythm of repetition._


#### `a18-12-question`

**Vasilisa**: That is all, Granny. Too many questions are not always good.  
**Baba Yaga**: Good girl. You only ask about outside my yard, not inside it.  
_Baba Yaga turns her wet-stone eyes on you._  
**Baba Yaga**: And you? Anything you want to know?  
_You think of the hands. They are waving in your head._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): polite questions and private things  
> _Which is a polite question: Will it be cold tomorrow?_  
> _Or what is in your private box?_  
> - ✅ Will it be cold tomorrow? → Yes. A question about the weather is polite.
> - What is in your private box? → A private box is private. Questions about the weather are polite.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a polite question and recognised that some things are private._


**Choices**

    - You open your mouth. Vasilisa steps on your foot, hard.
    - **You**: …About the weather. Will it be cold tomorrow?

- **Ask nothing. Shake your head.**
    - **Baba Yaga**: Wise. Wiser than you look.
- **Ask about the birches.**
    - **You**: Why are the birches white?
    - **Baba Yaga**: So my bright day has something to shine on. Next.

## A18-13. The Lantern on a Stick

- `a18-13-s1`: Walk home through the dark wood by the lantern’s light. · _Keep inside the circle of light and walk where it shines._
- `a18-13-s2`: Stay with Vasilisa when she wants to throw the lantern away. · _Wait beside her at the edge of the wood._
- `a18-13-s3`: Carry the lantern the last stretch, so Vasilisa’s arms can rest. · _Take the stick, hold it out in front, and walk to the house._

#### `a18-13-dark`

_The night wood is different. The lantern makes a small round room of light._  
_You walk inside the room of light._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, do): light cannot pass through your hand: shadows  
> _(Shine a torch on a wall. Hold your hand in front._  
> _See the shadow?)_  
> _Light cannot go through your hand. So the dark patch is a shadow._  
> Check: `edu:make:shadow:hand`
> _For grown-ups: Made a hand shadow and saw that light cannot pass through a hand._

_Your Nubbin walks ahead, at the edge of the light. It is not afraid._

**Vasilisa**: Look! It is not frightened at all. How is it not frightened?  
**Vasilisa**: Mother said: a fed child sleeps. A hungry one sees wolves.  
_You walk all night and all the next day. The light never goes out._  

#### `a18-13-dark-done`

_At dusk on the second day you see the stepmother’s house._  
_There is no light in it at all._  
_Long ago there were no electric lights. Homes used candles, lamps and fires._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): how people lit their homes long ago  
> _Long ago, before electric lights, how did people light their homes at night?_  
> - ✅ With candles, lamps and fires → Yes! Candles, lamps and fires lit the evening.
> - With a plug in the wall → Plugs came much later. Long ago, it was candles, lamps and fires.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that before electric lights, homes were lit by candles, lamps and fires._


#### `a18-13-throw`

_At the edge of the wood Vasilisa stops. Her arms are shaking._  
**Vasilisa**: I cannot take it into the house. I will throw it in the ditch.  
**Vasilisa**: They have fire by now. They will not need it.  
_She lifts the stick to throw. Your Nubbin covers its eyes._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): stop, breathe, then choose  
> _Vasilisa feels like throwing it away. What helps when a feeling is very big?_  
> - ✅ Stop, breathe, then choose → Yes. Stop, breathe, then choose. That is what Vasilisa does.
> - Do it fast without thinking → Fast can lead to a mistake. Stop, breathe, then choose.
> - Shout at someone → Shouting hurts others. Stop, breathe, then choose.
> _For grown-ups: Practised a calming way to handle a big feeling: stop, breathe, then choose._

**The Skull**: Please do not throw me away.  
_The voice is dry as leaves, and not unkind._  
**The Skull**: Take me to your stepmother’s house. That is where I am wanted.  
**Vasilisa**: Oh.  

**Choices**

- **Tell her to do as it says.**
    - **Vasilisa**: Yes. All right. It did nearly say please.
- **Say nothing. It is her choice.**
    - You wait. Vasilisa looks at the lantern.
    - It looks back.
    - **Vasilisa**: All right. Home.

#### `a18-13-throw-done`

_She lowers the stick. Her arms tremble._  
_The light shakes on the snow._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): tired muscles need rest  
> _When we hold something up for a long time, our muscles get tired._  
> _(Hold your arms out straight and count to ten.)_  
> _(Now shake them out and rest.)_  
> Check: `edu:hold:arms:rest`
> _For grown-ups: Felt muscles tire from holding arms out and learned that resting helps._


#### `a18-13-carry`

**You**: Give it to me. Just to the gate.  
_You take the stick. It is lighter than you thought, and warm._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): heavier and lighter  
> _The lantern on its stick is light._  
> _Which is lighter: the stick, or a big stone?_  
> - ✅ The stick → Yes! A big stone is heavy. The stick is lighter.
> - The big stone → A big stone is very heavy. The stick is lighter.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two objects and said which is lighter._

_Vasilisa shakes out her arms. She walks beside you._  
_The lantern looks at the dark house. Its eyes get brighter._  
**The Skull**: Nearly there.  
_Your Nubbin climbs on your shoulder to see._  

**Choices**

- **Hold it steady, far out in front.**
    - You hold it far out. The light goes ahead like a carpet.
- **Ask the lantern how it is.**
    - **The Skull**: Busy. It has been long since anybody asked.
    - It says no more. You do not ask again.

#### `a18-13-carry-done`

_At the gate you give the stick back to Vasilisa._  
_It should be her who carries it in._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): help, then step back so the other person can finish  
> _You helped, and then you stepped back._  
> _A kind helper lets a friend finish what they started._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a kind helper steps back and lets the other person finish._


#### `a18-13-complete`

_The house is dark from top to bottom._

_Your Nubbin stands close against your leg._  
_The door flies open before you reach it._

## A18-14. No Fire

- `a18-14-s1`: Bring the lantern into the house with Vasilisa. · _Follow her through the door._
- `a18-14-s2`: Stay by the cold stove with Vasilisa through the long night. · _Sit by the hearth. Don’t leave her on her own._
- `a18-14-s3`: Help Vasilisa lay the lantern to rest and lock up the house. · _Dig under the birch by the gate. Then walk her to the road._

#### `a18-14-door`

**The Stepmother**: You! You came back. And you have fire!  
_For the first time, she is pleased to see Vasilisa._  
**The Elder Sister**: We have had no light since you left. None.  
**The Younger Sister**: We fetched fire three times. Each time it went out at the door.  
**The Stepmother**: Never mind that. Put it on the table. It will do for a lamp.  
_Vasilisa sets the lantern on the table, facing the room._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): fire needs air to burn  
> _A fire needs air to burn._  
> _Cover a candle with a jar, and it runs out of air._  
> _Never play with fire. Only grown-ups light or put out flames._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that fire needs air, and that only grown-ups handle flames._


**Choices**

- **Stand next to Vasilisa, by the door.**
    - You stand by her. The stepmother looks at the lantern.
    - It looks at her.
- **Keep your Nubbin close.**
    - You hold your Nubbin to your chest. It does not want to look.

#### `a18-14-door-done`

_The stepmother moves to the stove. The lantern’s eyes follow._  
_She moves to the window. They follow her there too._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, do): positions: by the stove, at the window  
> _(Where is she now? Point to the stove._  
> _Now point to the window.)_  
> Check: `edu:point:position:stove-window`
> _For grown-ups: Used position words (by the stove, at the window) and pointed to each place._


#### `a18-14-stare`

**The Stepmother**: Turn it round! Turn it to the wall!  
_Vasilisa turns it. The light still shines at the stepmother._  
**The Elder Sister**: It is looking at me! Mother, it is looking at me!  
_The sisters hide in the cellar. The light finds them._  
_They climb to the loft. The light finds them there._  
_Nobody is hurt. There is only a steady light, and three people running._  
_Vasilisa sits by the cold stove. You sit beside her._  
**Vasilisa**: I did not want this. I only went for fire.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): naming mixed feelings: sorry and upset  
> _Vasilisa did not want anyone frightened. How does she feel?_  
> - ✅ Sorry and upset → Yes. She feels sorry and upset, though she did nothing wrong.
> - Proud and bossy → Look at her face. She is sorry and upset.
> - Sleepy and silly → Not silly. Her heart is heavy. She feels sorry and upset.
> _For grown-ups: Named mixed feelings (sorry and upset) in a character who did nothing wrong._


**Choices**

- **Sit with her, and say nothing.**
    - You sit with her. It is a very long night.
    - You stay for all of it.
- **Put your sleeve over her eyes.**
    - She leans on your shoulder with your sleeve over her eyes. Soon she sleeps.
- **Tell her it was not her doing.**
    - **You**: You went for fire. That is all you did.
    - **Vasilisa**: I know. Will you stay up with me anyway?

#### `a18-14-stare-done`

_Some time before dawn, the back door opens and shuts._  
_Three times. Then the house is quiet._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): ways to rest when you are worried  
> _It is a worrying night. What helps you rest when you are worried?_  
> - ✅ A cuddle and slow breaths → Yes. A cuddle and slow breaths help a worried body rest.
> - Shouting → Shouting does not help us rest. A cuddle and slow breaths do.
> _For grown-ups: Chose calming ways to rest when worried: a cuddle and slow breaths._


#### `a18-14-morning`

_In the morning the house is empty. The shawl and boots are gone._  
_Footprints go off down the lane in the snow. They do not come back._  
**Vasilisa**: They are gone. I did not hate them. I never did.  
_The lantern sits on the table, dim, as if it were tired._  
**Vasilisa**: It did its job. It should rest in the ground, under a tree.  
_You dig under the birch by the gate. Your Nubbin digs too._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): marking a special place with a stone or tree  
> _People put things to rest kindly._  
> _A stone or a tree can mark the place._  
> _Marking a place helps us remember._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that people mark special places with a stone or a tree, to remember them._


**Choices**

- **Set a flat stone on top.**
    - You set a flat stone over the place. Vasilisa nods.
- **Ask if she wants to say something.**
    - **Vasilisa**: Thank you for the light. That is all.
    - **Vasilisa**: That is enough.

#### `a18-14-morning-done`

_Vasilisa locks the door._  
_She hangs the key on a string round her neck._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): longer and shorter  
> _The string is long. The key is short._  
> _Which is longer?_  
> - ✅ The string → Yes! The string is longer. The key is shorter.
> - The key → Look again. The string is longer than the key.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two lengths and said which is longer._

_She does not look back at the house._  

#### `a18-14-complete`

**Vasilisa**: I will go to town and wait for Father. He said spring.  
_You walk with her down the lane, and then towards the town._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): a slow beat and a fast beat  
> _(March on the spot to a steady beat: slow, slow, slow.)_  
> _(Now fast, fast, fast!)_  
> Check: `edu:march:beat:slow-fast`
> _For grown-ups: Marched to a steady beat, slow and then fast._

_Halfway, she feeds the doll some bread. The little lights glow, even in daylight._

**Dollet**: Go on, Vasilisa. It is not far now.  

## A18-15. The Loom

- `a18-15-s1`: Find Vasilisa somewhere to stay in town. · _Knock at the little house at the end of the last lane._
- `a18-15-s2`: Find an old comb, a shuttle and a horse’s mane for the doll. · _Ask round the town: the barber, the weaver’s widow, the stable._
- `a18-15-s3`: Help bleach the linen on the spring grass. · _Spread the linen on the meadow and keep it damp._

#### `a18-15-town`

_The town is fences and smoke and dogs._  
_At the end of the last lane is a little house with one window._  
_An old woman answers. She has flour on her hands._  
**The Old Woman**: A girl on her own, and a… whatever that is. Come in.  
**Vasilisa**: I wait for my father, far away. May I stay? I will work.  
**The Old Woman**: Stay. I have a bench and a stove and a rude cat.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): welcoming someone new  
> _The old woman welcomes a stranger._  
> _What is a kind way to welcome someone new?_  
> - ✅ Say hello and make room → Yes! Hello and a place to sit make a stranger feel welcome.
> - Shut the door → A shut door says go away. Hello and a place to sit are kinder.
> - Ignore them → Ignoring makes people feel lonely. Say hello and make room.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a kind way to welcome a newcomer._

_The cat looks at your Nubbin. Your Nubbin looks at the cat._  

**Choices**

- **Offer to fetch the water.**
    - **The Old Woman**: Two pails, then. Mind the dog.
    - **The Old Woman**: He is worse than the cat.
- **Introduce your Nubbin to the cat.**
    - Your Nubbin sits beside the cat. After a long time, the cat allows this.

#### `a18-15-town-done`

**Vasilisa**: Granny, I cannot sit idle. Please buy me flax to spin.  
_Flax is a plant with tall, thin stems and blue flowers._  
_Its stems hold long, strong fibres. Fibres can be spun into thread._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): plant fibres can be spun into thread and cloth  
> _Flax is a plant. Its fibres can be spun._  
> _What can thread be woven into?_  
> - ✅ Cloth → Yes! Thread is woven into cloth. Flax makes a cloth called linen.
> - Soup → Not soup. Thread is woven into cloth. Flax makes linen.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that flax is a plant whose fibres are spun into thread and woven into linen cloth._


#### `a18-15-loom`

_Vasilisa spins through the dark days. Her thread is fine as hair._  
**The Old Woman**: Lovely. But no loom here will take thread so fine.  
_That night Vasilisa takes a crust to the cellar. You hold the light._  
_The doll eats, and its lights come on. It talks to Vasilisa, low._  
**Vasilisa**: She wants an old comb, a shuttle and a horse’s mane.  
**Vasilisa**: Will you find them? I cannot ask Granny for a horse’s mane.  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, do): a repeating pattern: over, under, over, under  
> _A loom weaves thread over, under, over, under. That is a pattern._  
> _(Weave your fingers in the air and say it: over, under, over, under.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:pattern:over-under`
> _For grown-ups: Said and acted out a repeating pattern (over, under) like weaving._


**Choices**

- **Go out first thing and ask round.**
    - The barber has a comb. The weaver’s widow has a shuttle.
    - The stableman cuts a mane.
- **Send your Nubbin to the stable.**
    - Your Nubbin comes back with a long switch of mane.
    - The horse did not mind.

#### `a18-15-loom-done`

_By morning there is a loom in the corner, small and neat._  
_Nobody heard it being made._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, do): first, next, last: how flax becomes cloth  
> _Flax becomes cloth in steps. First, we pull the flax._  
> _Next, we spin it into thread._  
> _Last, we weave the thread into cloth._  
> _(Say it with me: pull, spin, weave.)_  
> Check: `edu:order:flax:pull-spin-weave`
> _For grown-ups: Put three steps in order (pull, spin, weave) using first, next and last._

_Your Nubbin falls asleep in the heap of combed flax._  

#### `a18-15-bleach`

_All winter Vasilisa weaves. By spring there is a roll of linen._  
**The Old Woman**: Now it wants the sun. Out on the grass with it.  
_You spread it on the new grass, a long white road through the green._  
_Every hour you sprinkle it. The sun works on it._  
_It gets whiter by the day._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): sunlight can lighten cloth  
> _Sunlight can fade colours and make cloth whiter._  
> _That is why washing hung in the sun can look so bright._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sunlight can lighten cloth, which is why linen was bleached in the sun._

_Your Nubbin lies at the edge with one paw on the linen._  
**Vasilisa**: I made this myself. Well, with her, and with you carrying.  

**Choices**

- **Take a turn with the watering can.**
    - You sprinkle it end to end. A little rainbow follows, then gives up.
- **Lie in the grass beside it and watch the sky.**
    - You lie down beside the linen. For one afternoon, nobody has to do anything.

#### `a18-15-bleach-done`

**The Old Woman**: Whiter than snow. Finer than anything. I have never seen the like.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): feeling proud of work done together  
> _Vasilisa made the linen with help. How does she feel?_  
> - ✅ Proud → Yes! Proud, and thankful for the help.
> - Cross → Not cross. She looks happy. She feels proud.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feeling of pride in work done with others._


#### `a18-15-complete`

_All winter the old woman has whittled by the stove._  
_Now she puts a lantern shade in your hands. It is carved birch._  
_It has two round eye holes. It looks like a kind, sleepy face._  
**The Old Woman**: For the light that brought her home. A friendly one.  
_Put a candle inside, and the eyes glow warm._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): wood blocks light; carved holes let it through  
> _Wood stops the light. The carved holes let it through._  
> _So bright spots glow on the wall. Only grown-ups use carving knives._  
> _(Shine a torch through a colander. Can you see the spots of light?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wood blocks light while carved holes let it through, and looked at spots of light through a colander._


## A18-16. Twelve Shirts

- `a18-16-s1`: Walk with the old woman to the palace with the linen. · _Carry the roll. She does the talking._
- `a18-16-s2`: Help make up the twelve shirts. · _Sit at the window with Vasilisa, where the light is best._
- `a18-16-s3`: Stand with Vasilisa when the Tsar asks to meet the seamstress. · _Walk her to the palace. She is shaking._

#### `a18-16-palace`

**Vasilisa**: Sell it, Granny. Keep the money for both of us.  
**The Old Woman**: Sell cloth like this? No. It is a gift, or it is nothing.  
_You walk to the palace. The old woman carries her linen like treasure._  
_She walks under the windows. A window opens, and a man looks out._  
_He is the Tsar, in his slippers._  
**The Tsar**: What do you have there, old mother?  
**The Old Woman**: A wonder. I will show it only to you.  
_He holds the linen up. The light goes through it._  
**The Tsar**: What do you want for it?  
**The Old Woman**: Nothing. It is a gift.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): a gift is given freely  
> _The old woman gives the linen as a gift. What is a gift?_  
> - ✅ Something given freely, asking nothing back → Yes! A gift is given freely, with nothing asked back.
> - Something you swap for money → That is selling. A gift is given freely.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the difference between a gift (given freely) and something sold._


**Choices**

- **Bow, as everyone else does.**
    - You bow. Your Nubbin bows too and slides off the linen.
- **Keep your Nubbin off the linen.**
    - You catch your Nubbin as it reaches for a corner. The Tsar laughs.

#### `a18-16-palace-done`

_The Tsar thanks her and sends her home with presents._  
_A Tsar is the old word for a ruler, a bit like a king._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): the word Tsar  
> _In this tale, what is a Tsar?_  
> - ✅ A ruler, like a king → Yes! A Tsar is a ruler, a bit like a king.
> - A baker → Not a baker. A Tsar is a ruler, like a king.
> - A horse → Not a horse. A Tsar is a ruler, like a king.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the meaning of the word Tsar (a ruler, like a king) from the story._


#### `a18-16-shirts`

_A man from the palace knocks. He holds the linen and looks worried._  
**The Old Woman**: Nobody at court can sew it. Can she make it into shirts?  
**Vasilisa**: Yes. Tell him yes.  
_She sews twelve shirts at the window where the light is best._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to twelve  
> _(Count the shirts together, one to twelve: twelve shirts!)_  
> Check: `edu:count:shirts:12`
> _For grown-ups: Counted to twelve to find how many shirts there are._

_You thread her needles. Your Nubbin sorts the buttons into rows._  
_The doll works at night. In the morning there is one more seam done._  

#### `a18-16-shirts-done`

_Twelve shirts lie folded on the table, white as first snow._  
_Vasilisa rubs her tired eyes._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): rest your eyes when doing close work  
> _Sewing is close work. It tires the eyes._  
> _Use good light. Look far away sometimes, and rest your eyes._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard how to rest tired eyes after close work: good light, looking far away, resting._

_The old woman carries the shirts to the palace._  

#### `a18-16-tsar`

_The Tsar puts on one shirt. He sends for the seamstress._  
**Vasilisa**: Me? At the palace? Like this?  
**The Old Woman**: Like that. Wash your face. It is a very good face.  
_On the steps she touches her pocket, then takes her hand out, steadier._  
**The Tsar**: You made these? All of them?  
**Vasilisa**: Yes, Majesty. With help.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): honesty and sharing the thanks  
> _Vasilisa says: with help. Why is that a good thing to say?_  
> - ✅ It is true, and it shares the thanks → Yes. Honest people share the thanks with those who helped.
> - It makes the shirts bigger → Not bigger. It is honest, and it shares the thanks.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about honesty: saying who helped, and sharing the thanks._

**The Tsar**: Then I do not want to let you go. Would you mind very much?  
**Vasilisa**: I would not mind at all.  

**Choices**

- **Cheer, out loud, in a palace.**
    - You cheer. Your Nubbin runs round the throne room twice.
- **Just squeeze her hand.**
    - You squeeze her hand. She squeezes back so hard it hurts, and laughs.

#### `a18-16-tsar-done`

_Bells ring, and somebody throws grain. Your Nubbin eats a good deal of it._

## A19-1. This Is Berk

- `a19-01-s1`: Sail to Berk. Find a place to sleep. · _Walk up the jetty to Hiccup and Gobber._
- `a19-01-s2`: Pump the bellows. Keep the forge fire hot. · _Push long and slow. Push, push, push._
- `a19-01-s3`: Help Hiccup wheel his machine out. · _Take the back end, and push._

#### `a19-01-arrive`

_Your boat bumps into a grey island. It is cold and rainy._  
_This is Berk. Berk is made up, a place in a story._  
_But real Vikings lived on islands like it, long ago._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): an island has water all round it  
> _(Point to the sea.) Land with sea on every side is called what?_  
> - ✅ An island → Yes! An island. You can sail all the way round it.
> - A hill → A hill is a bump of land. An island has sea all round.
> - A pond → A pond is a little pool. An island has sea all round.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that an island is land with water all around it, and that Berk is a made-up island._

**Hiccup**: Hello! I am Hiccup. I live here.  
_A big man comes down the jetty. He has a hook for a hand._  
**Gobber**: I am Gobber. What is that little round one?  
_Your Nubbin waves a stubby wing. Gobber waves his hook._  

**Choices**

- **Tell him it’s a Nubbin.**
    - **Gobber**: A Nubbin! Never heard of one. It cannot be dangerous.
- **Let your Nubbin wave a wing at him.**
    - Your Nubbin waves. Gobber waves his hook back, very politely.
- **Say nothing at all.**
    - **Hiccup**: Good idea. Gobber likes a mystery.

#### `a19-01-arrive-done`

**Gobber**: You need a job. Come and work at my forge.  
_A forge is where people make things out of iron._  
**Hiccup**: It is warm in there. Come on up!  
_Over the forge is a cosy loft. That is your bed._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): first sounds: h  
> _(Say it with me: h-h-hammer, h-h-hook, h-h-Hiccup.)_  
> _They all start with the same sound: h._  
> Check: `edu:say:first-sound:h`
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first sound h in hammer, hook and Hiccup._


#### `a19-01-raid`

_Horns toot in the night. Dragons are stealing sheep!_  
**Gobber**: Bellows! Pump, pump, pump! Make the fire hot!  
_You push the bellows. Whoosh, the fire gets bigger!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): a fire needs air to burn  
> _(Puff on your hand. Whoosh, can you feel the air?)_  
> **Gobber**: Bellows push air at the fire. Air makes it burn hot.  
> Check: `edu:blow:air:hand`
> _For grown-ups: Felt moving air on their hand and learned that a fire needs air, which is why a forge has bellows._

_Your Nubbin sits on the anvil. Bang, bang, and it covers its ears!_  
**Hiccup**: I want to help out there. But everyone says stay in here.  
**Gobber**: Out there you might get hurt. In here you are safe.  
_Hiccup sighs. Then he gets on with his work._

_Your arms feel like jelly._

**Hiccup**: It is heavy. Please, can you help me push?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): helping a friend who asks  
> _Hiccup needs a hand. What is a good thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Say yes and help → Thank you! Many hands make it easy.
> - Walk away → That is a bit lonely for me. Helping is kinder.
> - Hide → Hiding will not move my machine. A helper will!
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how a good friend helps when asked._

#### `a19-01-launcher-done`

_Out into the lane you go._  
_Creak, creak, creak go the wheels._  
_Round and round, the wheels turn._  
_A wheel is the shape of a circle._

## A19-2. The Night Fury

- `a19-02-s1`: Watch the sky with Hiccup. See where the shot goes. · _Stay by the machine and look at the stars._
- `a19-02-s2`: Run down the hill with Hiccup. · _Hide behind the torch posts in the square._
- `a19-02-s3`: Stand next to Hiccup while he talks to his dad. · _Stay close. You do not have to say anything._

#### `a19-02-shot`

_It is a dark night. Torches glow on the hill._  
_Wheeeee! A high whistle flies through the sky._  
**Hiccup**: That is the dragon nobody sees. Shh. Watch the stars.  
_You look up. The stars twinkle, and something dark hides a few._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): we see stars at night  
> _(Point up.) At night, what twinkles in the dark sky?_  
> - ✅ Stars → Yes! Stars. They are always there. We see them best when it is dark.
> - The Sun → The Sun shines by day. At night we see the Moon and stars.
> - A rainbow → Rainbows come in the day, when sun and rain meet. At night: stars!
> _For grown-ups: Named the stars as what we see twinkling in the night sky._

**Hiccup**: There! I will aim, and fire!  
_Zoom, the ropes fly up! Something falls behind the ridge._  
**Hiccup**: I hit it! Did anyone see?  
_You saw. Your Nubbin saw, too._  

**Choices**

- **Tell him you saw it.**
    - **Hiccup**: You saw it! Somebody saw it. Good.
- **Point to where it fell.**
    - You point at the dark ridge. Hiccup learns the spot, like a map.
- **Ask if he’s sure.**
    - **Hiccup**: Yes. It fell. Things only fall like that if something is wrong.

#### `a19-02-shot-done`

_Crack! A wooden post snaps behind you._  
_Something big has landed on the cliff._  
_It is red and bumpy. It does not look happy._  
_It is wide awake, and it has seen you._  

> **Lesson** (music, 1-PS4-1, do): high sounds and low sounds  
> _(Make a high whistle. Now make a low rumble.)_  
> _The night whistle was high. The big red dragon’s grumble is low._  
> Check: `edu:make:sound:high-low`
> _For grown-ups: Made a high sound and a low sound and compared them._


#### `a19-02-chase`

_The big red dragon sniffs the air. Run!_  
**Hiccup**: Not that one! Run! Running is good!  
_You run down the hill. Thump, thump, thump!_  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): our heart beats faster when we run  
> _(Put a hand on your chest.) When we run, what does our heart do?_  
> - ✅ Beats faster → Yes, thump-thump-thump! It pumps blood to your legs to help them run.
> - Stops → Your heart keeps going. It beats faster to help your legs run.
> - Goes to sleep → It stays awake. It beats faster when you run, then slows down to rest.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the heart beats faster during running and slows when we rest._

_Your Nubbin runs through Hiccup’s legs. Twice!_  
**Hiccup**: Left! No, the other left! Behind the post!  
_You hide. A giant man steps out and shoos the dragon away._  
_The dragons fly off. The night goes quiet._  

#### `a19-02-chase-done`

_The giant man is Stoick. He is Hiccup’s dad._  
**Stoick**: Hiccup.  
**Hiccup**: Hi, Dad.  
_Hiccup’s shoulders go down. He looks small._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): naming a feeling in someone else  
> _How do you think Hiccup feels?_  
> - ✅ Worried and a bit sad → Yes. His shoulders went down, and that tells us how he feels.
> - Very silly and giggly → Not quite. Look at his face and shoulders: he looks worried.
> - Sleepy → It is late, but his face is worried, not sleepy.
> _For grown-ups: Read a character’s body language to name a feeling._

_Stoick is the chief. He is big and very tired._  
**Hiccup**: I hit a dragon! Up on the cliff!

**Stoick**: I have a village to feed. Winter is coming.  
**Hiccup**: I know what I saw.  
_Some people laugh. Hiccup looks at his feet._  
**Gobber**: This is our new helper. And a little hatchling.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, do): tell what happened in order: first, next, last  
> _(Let us tell it in order. First, Hiccup shot at the dark.)_  
> _Next, something fell. Last, nobody believed him._  
> _(Say it together: first, next, last.)_  
> Check: `edu:order:story:first-next-last`
> _For grown-ups: Retold part of the story in order, using first, next and last._


**Choices**

    - He is not unkind. He is just very busy tonight.
- **Say nothing. Stand next to Hiccup.**
    - You stand close. He can tell you are there.
    - **Hiccup**: Thanks.

> _It had a fire in the middle. People met there to talk and eat._

**Stoick**: I will take the ships and find the dragons’ home.

**Hiccup**: Oh dear.

#### `a19-03-docks`

_All day you carry things to the ships._

_The ships are made of wood. Wood floats on water._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): wood floats and stones sink  
> _Wood floats. Which of these would float on the water?_  
> - ✅ A wooden spoon → Yes! Wood floats, so a wooden spoon would bob along.
> - A stone → Plop! A stone sinks, because it is heavy for its size.
> - An iron nail → Plop! A nail sinks too, and wood is the one that floats.
> _For grown-ups: Sorted things that float from things that sink, starting with wood._

**Stoick**: Listen to Gobber, Hiccup.  
**Hiccup**: I will.

- **Stand with Hiccup until the sails are gone.**
    - You stand with him until there is only grey water.

> - Being all alone → That makes it feel bigger. A friend nearby is better.
> - Pretending to feel fine → It is all right to feel sad. Saying so helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when you miss someone: a hug and a friend._
