## A19-4. The Bound Dragon

- `a19-04-s1`: Search the woods for what fell. · _Follow Hiccup. Look for broken trees._
- `a19-04-s2`: Stay with Hiccup. Keep back and watch. · _Stand at the top of the rise._
- `a19-04-s3`: Walk back to the village with Hiccup. · _Take the long way round, through the woods._

#### `a19-04-woods`

_The woods are wet and grey. Hiccup has a map with crosses._  
**Hiccup**: Nothing here. Nothing here. Nothing here.  
_A branch swings back and bonks him. Your Nubbin ducks._  
_Then you stop. A pine tree is snapped in two._  
_The ground has a long, dark scratch in it._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-2, ask): animals leave signs behind  
> _(Point to the scratch.) What signs might an animal leave when it passes?_  
> - ✅ Footprints and broken twigs → Yes, footprints, scratches and broken twigs! Hiccup is a good tracker.
> - Nothing at all → Look! The scratch and the broken tree are signs that something came this way.
> - A rainbow → A rainbow is made by sun and rain. Animals leave footprints and twigs.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that animals leave signs such as footprints, scratches and broken twigs._

**Hiccup**: That is where it came down!  
_Something is breathing on the other side of the hill._  

#### `a19-04-bound`

_A black dragon lies in the ropes. It is very still._  
_Hiccup takes out his knife. He holds it up._  
**Hiccup**: This is what Vikings do.  
_The dragon opens one green eye. It looks tired._  
**Hiccup**: I cannot. I did this to you.  
_Hiccup cuts the ropes instead. Snip, snip, snip._  
_The dragon jumps up and roars. Then it flies off._  
_Your Nubbin is scared. It hides behind a stump and shakes._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what helps a scared friend  
> _Your Nubbin is scared. What helps a scared friend?_  
> - ✅ Stay close and be gentle → Yes. Staying close and being gentle makes a scared friend feel safe.
> - Shout at it → Shouting makes scared feelings bigger. Gentle is better.
> - Walk far away → A scared friend needs someone near. Stay close and be calm.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how to help a scared friend: stay close, be gentle and calm._


**Choices**

- **Scoop your Nubbin up and run.**
    - You scoop it up and walk away fast.
    - It holds on tight, and so do you. You are both very scared.
- **Crouch where you are, and let it come to you.**
    - You crouch low and wait, one hand flat on the ground.
    - It takes a long time. Then a small shape snuggles your knee.

**Hiccup**: I could not. Why could I not?

_A calm heart has a slow, steady beat._  

> **Lesson** (music, 1-PS4-1, do): a slow beat and a fast beat  
> _(Clap a slow, steady beat. Now clap a fast one.)_

> _For grown-ups: Clapped a slow beat and a fast beat and noticed which feels calmer._


#### `a19-04-walk`

_You walk back to the village together._  
**Hiccup**: Please keep a secret for me.  
_He stops. Your Nubbin looks up at him._  
**Hiccup**: I do not know why I did not do it.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): a good friend keeps a promise  
> _Hiccup trusts you. What does a good friend do with a promise?_  
> - ✅ Keep it → Yes. A kept promise shows you can be trusted. If a secret ever worries you, tell a grown-up you trust.
> - Forget it → A promise is something to remember. A good friend remembers.
> - Tell it to everyone → That would not be keeping it. A friend keeps promises safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keeping a promise to a friend, and telling a trusted grown-up about any secret that worries you._

_The arena horn blows. School is starting._  
**Hiccup**: Oh good. My favourite.  

**Choices**

- **Promise you won’t tell.**
    - **Hiccup**: Thank you. Really.
    - You carry the promise carefully all day.
- **Ask him why he didn’t.**
    - **Hiccup**: I will tell you when I know. Is that all right?
    - You say it is.

> _Baby ducks follow their mother in a line. Lambs stay close to their mums._

## A19-5. Dragon Training

- `a19-05-s1`: Go to the arena for dragon school. · _The arena is the stone pit with the chain roof._
- `a19-05-s2`: Hand out the shields. · _Run a shield to each young Viking._
- `a19-05-s3`: Watch the round. Stay by the wall. · _Stay near the gate, where Gobber can reach you._

#### `a19-05-arena`

_The arena is a stone pit. It has a roof of chains._  
**Gobber**: Dragon school! Lesson one: be careful.  
_Five young Vikings stand in the middle._  
**Astrid**: I am Astrid. Stay out of my way.  
**Fishlegs**: I am Fishlegs! Is that a hatchling?  
**Snotlout**: I am Snotlout. Remember my name.  
**Ruffnut**: I am Ruffnut. He is Tuffnut.  
_Hiccup creeps in last, in a helmet too big for him._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, do): count to 5, then add one  
> _(Count on your fingers: Astrid, Fishlegs, Snotlout, Ruffnut, Tuffnut.)_  
> _Five! Then Hiccup comes in, and five and one more is six._  
> Check: `edu:count:vikings:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five young Vikings, then added one more to make six._


#### `a19-05-arena-done`

_It does its fiercest face. Grrr!_  
_A twin pats it on the head._

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the parts of a word  
> _(Clap the parts: Fish-legs. Two claps!)_  
> _(Now Hic-cup. Two claps again!)_

> _For grown-ups: Clapped the two parts of names such as Fish-legs and Hic-cup._


#### `a19-05-shields`

**Gobber**: Behind this door is a Gronckle. Everyone needs a shield!  
_You run along with shields in your arms._  
_The door bangs. Out rolls a round brown dragon!_  
**Fishlegs**: A Gronckle! It eats rocks!  
_The twins tug on one shield. Tug, tug, tug!_  
**Ruffnut**: It is mine.  
**Tuffnut**: I touched it first.  
_Now there is one shield left, and two people with none._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): sharing fairly by taking turns  
> _One shield and two people. What is a fair way to share?_  
> - ✅ Take turns → Yes. Taking turns is fair, because each person gets a go.
> - Grab it fast → Grabbing is not fair. The slow one never gets a go.
> - Snap it in half → Then nobody has a good shield! Turns work better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about a fair way to share one thing between two people: taking turns._

    - **Fishlegs**: Thank you! Hiccup, stand behind me. I am very wide.
- **Prop it by the wall, for your Nubbin.**

    - **Gobber**: Ha! The hatchling has the best plan of all.

> _That rock was very hot. What is safe to do near hot things?_  
> - ✅ Stay back and tell a grown-up → Yes. Hot things can burn, so stay back and get a grown-up.
> - Touch it to check → Ouch! Never touch to check: stay back and tell a grown-up.
> - Poke it with a stick → That is not safe. Stay back and tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about staying back from hot things and telling a grown-up._

> - ✅ Take a deep breath and say how she feels → Yes. Breathing slowly and using words helps a cross feeling get smaller.
> - Stomp on Hiccup’s toes → Ouch! Cross is a fine feeling, but hurting someone is not.

## A19-6. The Cove

- `a19-06-s1`: Follow Hiccup along the dragon’s trail. · _Follow the broken twigs to a crack in the rocks._
- `a19-06-s2`: Sit at the edge of the cove. Watch quietly. · _Sit further back than Hiccup. Keep still._

#### `a19-06-trail`

_Hiccup follows a trail of broken twigs._  
**Hiccup**: It is walking. Why is it walking?  
_The trail ends at a crack between two rocks._  
_You squeeze through. Your Nubbin walks right through._  
_Inside is a cove, a round hollow with a lake._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, notice): animals live where they find food, water and shelter  
> _This cove has water, fish and high rock walls._  
> _Animals live where they find food, water and a safe place._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that animals live where their needs are met: food, water and shelter._

_Something black zooms past the lake!_  

#### `a19-06-cove`

_The dragon runs and flaps. Up, up, and plop, down!_  
_It tries again, and again. Plop!_  
**Hiccup**: Look at its tail.  
_It should have two tail fins, but one is torn off._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): take one away from two  
> _A tail has two fins, and one is torn off. How many are left?_  
> - ✅ One → Yes! Two take away one leaves one.
> - Two → Two would be the whole set. One is torn off, so one is left.
> - None → There is still one whole fin. Two take away one is one.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out that two take away one leaves one._

**Hiccup**: That was my ropes. It cannot steer.  
_Hiccup sits on a rock and starts to draw._  
_You sit further back, so the dragon has space._  

**Choices**

- **Watch the dragon.**
    - It tries the lake and snaps at fish. It misses them all.
- **Watch Hiccup.**
    - He rubs out a line and draws it again, slower.
- **Watch your Nubbin.**
    - Your Nubbin peeps at the dragon from behind your ankle.

#### `a19-06-cove-done`

_The dragon looks right at Hiccup._  
_Hiccup drops his charcoal._  
_It rolls away, down into the cove._  
_Nobody moves. Everybody keeps calm._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, do): keeping still and calm  
> _(Be still as a stone. Count to five, slowly.)_  
> _Still and slow. That is how you stay calm near a shy animal._  
> Check: `edu:keep:still:count-5`
> _For grown-ups: Practised keeping their body still and calm while counting to five._

**Hiccup**: They are not angry eyes. I keep drawing them angry.  

> **Lesson** (art, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): how eyes show feelings in a drawing  
> _(Look at the picture.) Which eyes make a face look kind?_  
> - ✅ Big, round eyes → Yes! Big round eyes look gentle.
> - Eyes with low, pointy eyebrows → Those make a face look cross. That is my mistake!
> - Eyes shut tight → Shut eyes look sleepy. I want it awake and kind.
> _For grown-ups: Looked at how drawn eyes can make a face look kind or cross._

## A19-7. The Knife

- `a19-07-s1`: Carry a basket of fish to the cove. · _The basket is by the forge door. It leaks!_
- `a19-07-s2`: Wait at the cove. Stay low and still. · _Do not move towards the dragon._

#### `a19-07-basket`

_Before dawn, Hiccup packs a basket of fish._  
**Hiccup**: The dragon cannot catch anything. It must be hungry.  

> **Lesson** (health, K-LS1-1, ask): food gives us energy to grow and play  
> _The dragon is hungry. Why do animals and people need food?_  
> - ✅ Food gives us energy to grow and play → Yes. Food is fuel for our bodies.
> - Food makes us disappear → Ha, no! Food helps us grow bigger and stronger.
> - We do not need food → Everyone needs food and water to live and grow.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why people and animals need food: it gives energy to grow and play._

**Gobber**: Where are you going with my fish?  
**Hiccup**: Dragon school! Extra studying.  
_The basket is heavy and it leaks. You carry it between you._  
_Plip, plip. Drips fall behind you all the way._  
_At the cove, Hiccup takes a big breath and climbs down._  

#### `a19-07-knife`

_Hiccup tips the fish onto the stones._  
_The dragon comes out low and fast. Then it stops._  
_It is looking at the knife on Hiccup’s belt._  
**Hiccup**: Oh. That.  
_Hiccup takes out the knife slowly. Plop, it goes in the lake!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): showing a friend you mean no harm  
> _Hiccup throws the knife away. What does that tell the dragon?_  
> - ✅ I will be gentle → Yes. It says “I mean no harm”, so now the dragon feels safer.
> - I am cross → No. A cross person would keep the knife, but throwing it away is gentle.
> - I am hungry → Hiccup is not hungry. He wants the dragon to feel safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how putting something dangerous down shows a friend you mean no harm._

_The dragon sits back. Its ear flaps go up._  
_Then it eats. Munch, munch, munch._  

**Choices**

- **Put your own hands where it can see them.**
    - You rest your open hands on your knees. The dragon glances, then eats.
- **Look away, at the water.**
    - You look at the water. You hear munching, and nothing else.
- **Keep a hand on your Nubbin.**
    - Your hand rests on its back. It is warm and calm.

#### `a19-07-name`

_When the fish is gone, the dragon coughs up half a fish._  
**Hiccup**: Thank you. That is very kind.  
_Hiccup eats it and gags. Yuck!_  
_The dragon smiles. There are no teeth at all!_  
_Then teeth pop out. And fold back in again._  
**Hiccup**: Teeth that fold away! I will call you Toothless.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): first sounds: t  
> _(Say it with me: t-t-Toothless, t-t-teeth, t-t-tail.)_  
> _They all start with t!_  
> Check: `edu:say:first-sound:t`
> _For grown-ups: Listened for the first sound t in Toothless, teeth and tail._


**Choices**

- **Laugh.**
    - You laugh, and Hiccup laughs. Toothless looks from one to the other.
- **Keep a straight face.**
    - **Hiccup**: You are very polite. He did just sick on me.
- **Say the name suits him.**
    - **Hiccup**: It does, does it not? A Night Fury called Toothless!

#### `a19-07-complete`

_Toothless lets you stay till noon._  
_He does not let anyone touch him. But he does not leave._  
**Hiccup**: Gobber will want his basket back.  
**Hiccup**: I will say a dragon ate it.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away within 10  
> _(Picture five fish in the basket.) If Toothless eats two, how many are left?_  
> - ✅ Three → Yes! Five take away two leaves three.
> - Two → Two is how many he ate. Five take away two leaves three.
> - Five → That is how many we started with. After two are eaten, three are left.
> _For grown-ups: Took 2 away from 5 and found 3 left._

_You carry the empty basket home. It smells of fish._  

## A19-8. The Hand

- `a19-08-s1`: Watch what Toothless does with the stick. · _Stay at the edge of the sand._

#### `a19-08-lines`

_By day four, Toothless lets Hiccup sit closer._  
_Hiccup draws Toothless in the sand with a stick._  
_Toothless picks up a branch. He draws, too!_  
_Round and round the cove he goes. Loops and lines everywhere._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): curly, straight and zigzag lines  
> _(Draw a curly line in the air. Now a straight one, and a zigzag.)_  
> _Toothless drew loops. What lines can you make?_  
> Check: `edu:draw:lines:curly-straight`
> _For grown-ups: Drew curly, straight and zigzag lines in the air._

**Hiccup**: Is that me? It is very bold.  
_Hiccup is in the middle of the scribble._  
_If he steps on a line, Toothless growls. If he lifts his foot, purr._  
_So Hiccup steps over each line, one at a time._  

**Choices**

- **Step through the lines after him.**
    - You step carefully over every line. Toothless watches you.
- **Stay outside the lines.**
    - You stay outside the drawing. Toothless seems to like that.

#### `a19-08-hand`

_Hiccup comes out of the last line. Toothless is very close._  
_Hiccup lifts his hand slowly. Toothless wrinkles his nose._  
_Hiccup stops. He does not pull back, and he does not push forward._  
_Then he shuts his eyes and turns his face away._  
_He holds out his open hand, and waits._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, do): waiting quietly and calmly  
> _(Hold out your hand and wait quietly. Count to ten, slowly.)_  
> _Slow, calm people make animals feel safe. Ask a grown-up before touching one._  
> Check: `edu:wait:quietly:count-10`
> _For grown-ups: Practised waiting quietly and calmly, and heard to ask a grown-up before touching an animal._

_Nobody moves. A drip falls from the rock._  
_Then Toothless pushes his nose into Hiccup’s hand._  
**Hiccup**: Oh!  

#### `a19-08-near`

_Toothless looks past Hiccup, at you and your Nubbin._  
**Hiccup**: Stay still. Let him choose.  
_Toothless walks across the sand._  
_Your Nubbin does not hide. It is not scared._  
_Toothless bends his big head down. Sniff, sniff, sniff._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): we smell with our nose  
> _Toothless goes sniff, sniff. What do we smell with?_  
> - ✅ Our nose → Yes! Sniff, sniff, noses are for smelling.
> - Our toes → Toes are for wiggling! We smell with our nose.
> - Our elbows → Elbows bend, but they cannot smell. Noses can.
> _For grown-ups: Named the nose as the part of the body we smell with._

_Your Nubbin sniffs back. Then it bumps its forehead on his nose._  
**Hiccup**: He likes it! He does not like anybody.

_Hiccup sits down in the sand, grinning._

**Hiccup**: Nobody ever sat still long enough to see.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): words that rhyme  
> _Hiccup sat still. Which word rhymes with still?_  
> - ✅ Hill → Yes! Still and hill sound the same at the end.
> - Dog → Dog does not rhyme with still. Still and hill do!
> - Cat → Cat does not rhyme with still. Still and hill do!

## A19-9. The Tail Fin

- `a19-09-s1`: Hold the lamp while Hiccup works. · _Keep it steady and quiet._
- `a19-09-s2`: Watch the first flights. · _Stand at the edge of the lake._
- `a19-09-s3`: Help Hiccup make a pedal. · _Hammer the stirrup flat at the anvil._

#### `a19-09-forge`

_At night, Gobber snores upstairs. Honk-shoo, honk-shoo._  
_Hiccup lights a lamp. You hold it for him._  
**Hiccup**: Lower. A bit left. Perfect.  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, ask): we see when there is light  
> _You are holding the lamp. Why does Hiccup need it?_  
> - ✅ So he can see in the dark → Yes! Light lets us see. Without it, the night is too dark.
> - So he can make a noise → A lamp does not make noise. It makes light so I can see.
> - So the leather can sleep → Ha! No. The lamp lights up my work.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we see things when there is light._

_He cuts leather and stitches a new tail fin for Toothless._  
**Hiccup**: Toothless cannot steer with one fin. So I will steer the other.  
_A board creaks. Gobber calls down the stairs._  
**Gobber**: Who is up? What are you making?  
_You hold the lamp very still._  

**Choices**

- **“It’s a saddle. For my Nubbin.”**
    - **Gobber**: A saddle for the hatchling! Ha! Southern folk are mad.
    - He goes back to bed. Hiccup grins at you.
- **“It’s a new kind of shield.”**
    - **Gobber**: Looks like a saddle.
    - **Hiccup**: A saddle-shaped shield. For sitting on.
    - **Gobber**: Bed. Both of you.
- **Blow out the lamp.**
    - You blow out the lamp. Gobber grumbles and goes back to bed.

#### `a19-09-strap`

_At the cove, Toothless sniffs the new fin._  
_He sniffs the saddle. He sniffs Hiccup._

_Hiccup climbs on. Toothless spreads his wings._  
_Up they go, round they go, and splash! Into the lake._  
_They try again. Splash, into the lake again!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 2  
> _(Count the splashes with me.)_  
> _Splash, one, and splash, two! Two splashes._  
> Check: `edu:count:splashes:2`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two splashes._


**Choices**

- **Cheer anyway.**
    - **Hiccup**: Thank you! That was nearly flying!
- **Wade in and help fish him out.**
    - You wade in. Toothless climbs out and shakes water all over you.
- **Keep your Nubbin out of the water.**
    - Your Nubbin wants to dive in. You gently hold it back.

#### `a19-09-strap-done`

**Hiccup**: He turns before I tell him.  
**Hiccup**: I need to know when he wants to turn.  
_Hiccup is listening with his eyes._  
_A friend can tell us things without any words._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): friends show feelings with their face and body  
> _How can a friend tell us a feeling without words?_  
> - ✅ With their face and body → Yes. A smile, a wag or a frown can tell us a lot.
> - They cannot → They can! Faces and bodies say lots without a word.
> - Only by shouting → Shouting is loud, but faces and bodies tell us softly, too.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how friends show feelings with their face and body, not only with words._


#### `a19-09-pedal`

_Back at the forge, Hiccup draws a pedal._  
_A pedal is pushed with a foot. Then the fin opens._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): pushing makes things move  
> _(Press your foot down on the floor, like a pedal.)_  
> _A push moves things. Hiccup’s foot pushes the pedal, and the fin opens._  
> Check: `edu:press:pedal:foot`
> _For grown-ups: Pressed a foot down like a pedal and heard that a push can make something move._

**Hiccup**: Hammer it flat. Flatter!  
_Bang, bang, bang! Your Nubbin brings a bucket of water._  
_At the cove they go up again._  
_This time they miss the lake. Up they go, over the sea!_  

#### `a19-09-pedal-done`

_They come back an hour later._  
_They are wet through, with windy hair._  
_They are both wearing the same big grin._

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): dry clothes and warmth help when we are wet and cold  
> _Hiccup is wet and cold. What helps?_  
> - ✅ Dry clothes and a warm blanket → Yes. Dry and warm is just right.
> - More cold water → Brrr! More water makes you colder.
> - Nothing → Something helps a lot: dry clothes and a cosy blanket.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how dry clothes and warmth help when we are wet and cold._

> _Friends who each do a part have a special name. What is it?_  
> - ✅ Teamwork → Yes, teamwork! Each one does a part.
> - Hiding → Hiding is staying out of sight. Helping each other is teamwork.
> - A race → A race is who is first. Helping each other is teamwork.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the word teamwork: friends each doing a part._

#### `a19-10-grass`

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, ask): plants need water and light  
> _Grass grows by the cove. What do plants need to grow?_  
> - ✅ Water and sunlight → Yes, water and sunlight! That is why the cove’s grass is green.
> - Only toys → Ha! Toys are fun, but plants need water and sunlight.
> - Only music → Music is lovely, but plants need water and sunlight.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants need water and light to grow._

_The Gronckle sniffs it. Then it rolls on its back like a puppy!_  
**Fishlegs**: That is not in the book!  
**Hiccup**: I read ahead?

_Hiccup blinks. Everyone is cheering._  
_Gobber looks surprised. Fishlegs looks surprised._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, do): a word for a feeling: surprised  
> _(Show me a surprised face, with wide eyes and an open mouth!)_  
> _Surprised is the feeling when something happens that you did not expect._  
> Check: `edu:show:face:surprised`
> _For grown-ups: Made a surprised face and learned the feeling word surprised._


#### `a19-10-eel`

_Day after day, Hiccup calms every dragon._  
_A Nadder rears up. Hiccup holds up a smoked eel, and it shies away._  
_A Gronckle corners Fishlegs. Hiccup scratches its chin, and it flops down happy._  
_The village comes to watch. They cheer for Hiccup!_  
**Astrid**: Where does he go every afternoon?  
_Astrid has caught your elbow. She wants an answer._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): when we cannot tell a secret, we can say so  
> _You cannot share Hiccup’s secret. What is a good thing to say?_  
> - ✅ “I cannot say. Please ask him.” → Yes. That is honest and kind, and it does not tell a fib.
> - Make up a fib → A fib makes trust wobbly. Saying “I cannot tell you” is honest.
> - Run away → Running does not help. A calm “I cannot say” does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being honest when you cannot share something: say so kindly._


**Choices**

- **Tell her he goes fishing.**
    - **Astrid**: Fishing? Hmm.
    - She lets go. She does not quite believe you.
- **Tell her to ask him herself.**
    - **Astrid**: I did. He said he goes for walks.
- **Shrug.**
    - **Astrid**: Fine. I will find out.
    - It is not a threat. It is more of a plan.

#### `a19-10-fleet`

_Stoick laughs a big laugh. He lifts Hiccup right off his feet._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): taller and shorter  
> _Stoick lifts Hiccup up high. Who is taller, Stoick or Hiccup?_  
> - ✅ Stoick → Yes! Stoick is the taller one, as big as a door.
> - Hiccup → Hiccup is shorter. That is why Stoick can lift him up.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two people and said which is taller._

**Stoick**: I always knew it was in you.  
_Hiccup smiles. But it is a wobbly smile._

## A19-11. The Flight

- `a19-11-s1`: Deal with Astrid at the cove. · _She is on the path down to the cove._
- `a19-11-s2`: Watch Toothless take Astrid flying. · _Watch from the cove. The sky is theirs this time._
- `a19-11-s3`: Wait at the cove for the last of the light. · _Stay on the sand. Toothless will decide._

#### `a19-11-astrid`

_Astrid follows Hiccup to the cove._

**Astrid**: A Night Fury!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): a fright makes our heart beat fast  
> _Astrid got a fright. What does our body do?_  
> - ✅ Our heart beats fast and we jump → Yes, thump-thump! Our body wakes up fast to keep us safe.
> - We turn into a rock → Ha, no! We jump, and our heart beats fast.
> - Nothing happens → Something does! Our heart beats fast and we may jump.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a fright makes the heart beat fast and the body jump._

**Hiccup**: No! He is my friend. Astrid, this is Toothless.  
_Astrid looks at Toothless. She looks at you._  
_Then she turns and runs towards the village._  
**Hiccup**: Oh dear. That is very bad.  

**Choices**

    - You step into the path. Astrid stops.
- **Sit down on the path, where she has to pass.**
    - You sit down in the middle of the path. Astrid nearly trips over you.
- **Leave it to Hiccup.**
    - You stay where you are. It is Hiccup’s secret.

#### `a19-11-astrid-done`

_He sets her down on top of a tall pine tree._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): taller and shorter  
> _Astrid sits on a pine tree. Which is taller, the tree or Astrid?_  
> - ✅ The pine tree → Yes! The pine is much, much taller.
> - Astrid → Astrid is tall, but the pine tree is much taller.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a tree and a person and said which is taller._

**Astrid**: Get me down from here!  
**Hiccup**: Let me show you. Then you can decide.  

#### `a19-11-spin`

_Astrid climbs on behind Hiccup. She is stiff as a plank._

_Whoosh, up they go! Then round and round._  
_Toothless dips them down and spins them. Wheee!_  
**Astrid**: Sorry! Make him stop!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sit down and wait when dizzy  
> _After spinning, the world wobbles, and that is called dizzy. What helps?_  
> - ✅ Sit down and wait → Yes. Sit still, and the wobble goes away.
> - Spin some more → More spinning makes dizzy worse. Sit down and wait.
> - Run very fast → Running when dizzy can make you fall. Sit and wait.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that when we feel dizzy, sitting down and waiting helps._

_Toothless stops. He glides up, slow and smooth._

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character’s feeling changes  
> _At first Astrid was cross. How does she feel now?_  
> - ✅ Happy → Yes. Her feeling changed from cross to happy.
> - Sleepy → She does not look sleepy. She said it was amazing.
> - Hungry → She might be hungry later! Right now she is happy.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed how a character’s feeling changed after something happened._


#### `a19-11-turn`

_Off they go, low over the water, in the last of the sun._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): night comes after day  
> _The sun is going down. What comes after the day?_  
> - ✅ Night → Yes. The sun goes down and it gets dark, and then it is night.
> - Breakfast → Breakfast is in the morning. After the day comes night.
> - Summer → Summer is a season. After day comes night.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about night coming after day as the Sun goes down._

_Your Nubbin’s ball glows like a lantern._  
_When they land, it runs to you and sits on you._

> - ✅ Yes, find out first → Yes. Looking and listening first helps us decide well.
> - No, decide right now → Deciding too fast can be a mistake. Finding out first is wise.

## A19-12. The Nest

- `a19-12-s1`: Fly out with Hiccup, Astrid and Toothless. · _Hold on tight at the back of the saddle._
- `a19-12-s2`: See where the dragons are going. · _Stay low and quiet. Toothless does the flying._
- `a19-12-s3`: Fly home quietly. · _There is nothing to do but hold on._

#### `a19-12-fog`

_Next evening, Astrid is at the cove first._  
_Toothless looks at you. He has not agreed to this._  
_But he lowers his shoulder anyway._  
_You climb on. Your Nubbin is buttoned in your coat._  
_Up you go, into a cloud. The cloud turns to fog._  
_Fog is a cloud that touches the ground or the sea._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): fog is tiny drops of water  
> _You are flying in fog. What is fog made of?_  
> - ✅ Tiny drops of water → Yes! Fog is a cloud of tiny water drops, low down.
> - Smoke → Smoke comes from fire. Fog is tiny drops of water.
> - Cotton wool → It looks fluffy, but fog is tiny drops of water.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that fog is made of tiny drops of water._

_Dragons come out of the fog, all flying the same way._  

**Choices**

- **Hold your Nubbin tighter.**
    - You fold your arms round your coat. Your Nubbin snuggles under your chin.
- **Keep your eyes open.**
    - You keep your eyes open. Somebody should see this.
- **Hold on to Astrid’s belt.**
    - **Astrid**: Good. Do not let go.

#### `a19-12-pit`

_The fog opens. A mountain sits in the sea._  
_The dragons fly in through a crack in its side. So do you._  
_Inside it is huge, hot and red._  
_In the middle is a pit full of mist._  
_One by one, the dragons drop fish and sheep into it._  
**Hiccup**: They are not eating it. Why not?  
_Something big and scary rumbles in the mist._  
**Astrid**: They are not stealing for themselves. They are scared of that!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): what to do when scared  
> _Even big dragons can feel scared. What can we do when we are scared?_  
> - ✅ Hold on to a friend and say so → Yes. Saying “I am scared” and holding on to a friend helps.
> - Pretend we are not → Pretending keeps the scared feeling inside. Saying so helps.
> - Never tell anyone → Telling a friend or a grown-up makes scared feelings smaller.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying you are scared and holding on to a friend._

_Toothless turns. Out, out, back into the fog._

**Astrid**: We have to tell the village about the nest.  
**Hiccup**: Please wait. They will find Toothless.  
**Astrid**: That big dragon is dangerous.  
**Hiccup**: Give me time. I will think of something.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): when friends disagree, listen to both  
> _Astrid and Hiccup disagree. What helps when two friends disagree?_  
> - ✅ Listen to both and take turns talking → Yes. Listening to both sides is fair.
> - Whoever shouts loudest wins → Shouting is not fair. Taking turns to talk is.
> - Walk away and say nothing → Walking off leaves the problem. Taking turns to talk helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about listening to both sides when friends disagree._

_Astrid looks at the back of his head. Toothless flies gently._

- **Reach past Astrid and touch Hiccup’s shoulder.**

- **Say they’re both right.**
    - **Astrid**: That is the hard part.
    - Nobody says any more, all the way home.

## A19-13. The Final Exam

- `a19-13-s1`: Take your place at the arena gate. · _Stand with Gobber. Hiccup will pass you._

- `a19-13-s3`: Stay with Hiccup as the ships go out. · _Go down to the jetty with him._

#### `a19-13-stands`

_All of Berk is at the arena. It is very noisy._  
_Somebody is selling smoked fish on sticks._  

> **Lesson** (music, 1-PS4-1, do): loud sounds and soft sounds  
> _(Clap loudly, like a big crowd. Now clap very softly.)_  
> _A crowd is loud. A whisper is soft._  
> Check: `edu:clap:loud-soft`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped loudly and softly and compared the sounds._

**Stoick**: My son is going to be a hero today!  
_You stand at the gate with Gobber._  
_Hiccup walks into the pit in his too-big helmet._  
_He looks at you. He has an idea._  

**Choices**

- **Wish him luck.**
    - **Hiccup**: Thanks. I will need it.
- **Tell him he doesn’t have to do this.**
    - **Hiccup**: I do. But not the way they think.
- **Just nod.**
    - You nod, and he nods back. That is enough.

#### `a19-13-hand`

_The gate opens. A Monstrous Nightmare comes out._  
_Hiccup puts down his shield, his knife and his helmet._  
**Hiccup**: It is all right. I will not hurt you. Look. Nothing.  
_He holds out his hand and turns his face away._  
_The dragon calms down. Everyone is quiet._  
**Stoick**: Enough! Get him out!  
_Stoick bangs the bars with his hammer. CLANG!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-3, ask): quiet and calm are kind to animals  
> _The loud noise scared the dragon. What is kinder to a scared animal?_  
> - ✅ Being quiet and calm → Yes. Quiet, calm people help animals feel safe.
> - Banging louder → Louder noises scare animals even more.
> - Shouting at it → Shouting scares animals. Quiet and calm is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that loud noises frighten animals and that quiet, calm people help them feel safe._

_The loud noise frightens the dragon. Far off, a whistle comes closer._  

#### `a19-13-chain`

_Toothless crashes in through the roof. He stands in front of Hiccup._  
_He pushes the Nightmare back into its pen._  
**Hiccup**: Go, Toothless! Go!  
_He stays by Hiccup. The Vikings catch him with ropes._  
_Hiccup tells his dad about Toothless. Stoick is upset and says something unkind._  
_Then he turns his back. Hiccup feels very small and very sad._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): what helps when someone says something unkind  
> _Hiccup feels hurt by unkind words. What helps?_  
> - ✅ Tell someone you trust how you feel → Yes. Telling a friend or a grown-up helps the hurt get smaller.
> - Say unkind things back → That hurts more people. Telling someone you trust is better.
> - Hide the feeling forever → Hidden feelings get heavy. Sharing them helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps after unkind words: telling someone you trust._

_Next day, the ships sail. Toothless is chained on the front one._  
_Hiccup stands on the jetty. His hands are empty._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): families can be cross and still love each other  
> _Families and friends can be cross with each other and still care._  
> _Mending it takes time. Saying sorry helps._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people who care about each other can fall out, and that time and saying sorry help to mend it._


## A19-14. What Astrid Asked

- `a19-14-s1`: Find Hiccup, and sit with him. · _He is on the cliff over the harbour. You do not have to say anything._
- `a19-14-s2`: Listen while Astrid asks her question. · _Stay where you are when Astrid comes._

#### `a19-14-cliff`

_Hiccup sits on the cliff over the empty harbour._  
_He hugs his knees. You sit down near him._  
_You do not ask him anything. You just stay._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): sitting quietly with a sad friend helps  
> _Hiccup is sad. Do we always have to talk to help?_  
> - ✅ No. Sitting close and quiet can help → Yes. Just being there says “I care”.
> - Yes, we must always talk → Not always. Sometimes just staying near is the kindest.
> - We should run away → A sad friend needs us near. Staying helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how just sitting near a sad friend can help._

_Your Nubbin sits between you, facing the sea._  
**Hiccup**: Everything was going so well.  
**Hiccup**: He came to help me. Now they have him.  

**Choices**

- **Stay where you are.**
    - You stay. Some things only need someone not to leave.
- **Move a little closer.**
    - You move closer. He does not look up, but he relaxes a little.
- **Give him the dried fish from your pocket.**
    - He laughs, once. He takes it.
    - **Hiccup**: You learned that from Toothless.

#### `a19-14-astrid`

_Astrid sits down next to Hiccup. She is quiet at first._  
**Astrid**: In the woods, you could have hurt him. Why did you not?  
**Hiccup**: I am not sure.  
**Astrid**: That is not an answer. Why?  
_Hiccup looks at his hands for a long time._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, SL.K.1, ask): in a talk we ask, then listen  
> _Astrid asked a question. What did she do next?_  
> - ✅ She waited and listened → Yes. Asking, then waiting and listening, is how a good talk works.
> - She walked away → She stayed. She sat and waited for his answer.
> - She sang a song → No song. She sat quietly and listened.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a good conversation means asking, then waiting and listening._

**Hiccup**: He was scared. I know that kind of scared. I could not hurt him.  
**Astrid**: So he is scared and chained to a ship. What now?

_Then at the arena and the pens._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4  
> _(Point to four pens, or four dots on the page.)_  
> _One, two, three, four! Four dragons in four pens._

#### `a19-14-complete`

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, ask): to solve a problem, first say what the problem is  
> _Toothless is chained. What is the first step to solving a problem?_  
> - ✅ Say what the problem is → Yes. Name the problem, then make a plan and try it.
> - Pretend it is not there → A problem does not go away if we hide. Name it first.
> - Hope it fixes itself → Hoping is nice, but naming the problem and making a plan is better.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the first step in solving a problem is saying what the problem is._

## A19-15. Training Dragons

- `a19-15-s1`: Meet the others at the arena pens. · _Go round to the pens at the back._
- `a19-15-s2`: Help match each rider to a dragon. · _Watch which way each dragon looks._
- `a19-15-s3`: Fly after the ships with the young riders. · _Ride behind Fishlegs on the Gronckle. Hold on._

#### `a19-15-pens`

_The arena is empty. The dragons sit in their pens._  
_Astrid has brought the others._  
**Snotlout**: If this is a trick, I am too good-looking to eat.  
**Ruffnut**: Nobody eats you. You are mostly elbows.  
**Tuffnut**: And hair.  
**Hiccup**: Nobody is getting eaten. I want you to meet them properly.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): meeting someone new politely  
> _What is a polite way to meet someone new?_  
> - ✅ Say hello gently and ask first → Yes. Gentle and slow is polite, with people and with animals.
> - Grab them → Grabbing is rude and can frighten them. Gentle is better.
> - Shout as loud as you can → Shouting can frighten. A soft hello is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about meeting someone new politely, gently and slowly._

**Fishlegs**: Meet them? We have been trying to beat them!  

#### `a19-15-hands`

_Hiccup opens the Nadder’s pen. It has every spike up._  
**Hiccup**: Hand out. Slow. Look away. Do not grab. Let it choose.  
_Astrid goes first. She holds out her hand and looks away._  
_The Nadder puts its nose into her palm._  
_Now it is your turn to help. Who goes with who?_  
_The Nightmare likes noise, so it gets Snotlout._  
_The Zippleback has two heads, so the twins share it._  
_That leaves the Gronckle and Fishlegs._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, ask): count to 4  
> _Nadder, Nightmare, Zippleback, Gronckle. How many dragons are there?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! One, two, three, four: four dragons.
> - Two → Count again: Nadder, Nightmare, Zippleback, Gronckle. Four!
> - Six → Count again with me: one, two, three, four. Four dragons.
> _For grown-ups: Counted four dragons._


**Choices**

- **Bring Fishlegs to the Gronckle.**
    - Fishlegs holds out a shaky hand. The Gronckle leans her head on him.
    - **Fishlegs**: She likes me! She actually likes me!
- **Let the Gronckle choose.**
    - The Gronckle waddles straight past everyone. She sits on Fishlegs’s feet.
    - **Fishlegs**: She picked me! Nobody picks me first!

#### `a19-15-hands-done`

_Fishlegs is crying. They are happy tears._  
_Nobody laughs. Not even Snotlout._  
_People cry when they are sad. People cry when they are very happy, too._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): all feelings are allowed, even happy tears  
> _Fishlegs cries happy tears. Is it all right to cry when we are happy?_  
> - ✅ Yes. All feelings are allowed → Yes. Happy tears are real tears, and every feeling is allowed.
> - No, never → We can cry when sad and when very happy. It is all right.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that crying when happy is fine and all feelings are allowed._

_Fishlegs has a friend at last._

_There are no saddles. They use rope and blankets._

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): hold on tight when riding high up  
> _You are riding high up on a dragon. What keeps you safe?_  
> - ✅ Hold on tight → Yes. Hold on with both hands, and sit nice and still.
> - Let go and wave → Not up high! Hold on tight.
> - Wiggle all about → Wiggling is wobbly. Sit still and hold on.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about holding on tight and sitting still to stay safe when riding._

**Astrid**: Which way did the ships go?

#### `a19-16-mountain`

_The ships have found the mountain. The Vikings hammer at the rock._  
_Toothless is chained on the front ship. He sees you coming._  
_The rock cracks wide. Then everyone stops cheering._  
_Out comes the big scary one, as big as a hill._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS1-1, notice): water, ice and time can crack rock  
> _Real rock can crack, too. Water freezes in a crack and pushes it wider._  
> _It happens very slowly, over many winters._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that rock can crack slowly when water freezes in its cracks._

**Gobber**: That is not a dragon. That is a mountain with a temper.  
_Its fire makes the ships hot and smoky. Everyone must get off!_  
**Stoick**: Everyone off! Get to the rocks!  

#### `a19-16-draw`

_The young riders swoop in. The Vikings on the beach gasp._

**Fishlegs**: Big head, small eyes! It cannot see well to the sides!  
**Hiccup**: Then be noisy on its left side!  
_The riders fly round its head, like gulls round a ship._  
_Fishlegs sets you down. Your job is to help people off the ships._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): helpers: who helps in a hard time  
> _Everyone is helping people off the ships. Who does the helping first?_  
> - ✅ Everyone who can, together → Yes. In a hard time, many hands help.
> - Only the chief → The chief helps, but so do the riders, Gobber and you.
> - Nobody → Everyone helps. That is how people get safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how everyone helps together when people need to get to safety._


**Choices**

- **Help Gobber down first.**
    - **Gobber**: Mind the leg! It is not my first, but it is a good one.
- **Send your Nubbin to look for anyone hiding.**
    - Your Nubbin finds a young Viking behind a barrel.
    - You get her off together. She hugs your Nubbin all the way down.
- **Go to Stoick.**
    - **Stoick**: Not me! Them! Get them off first!
    - So you do. He comes off last.

#### `a19-16-chain`

_The front ship is slipping into the sea. Toothless is still chained._  
_Hiccup pulls at the chain with both hands._  
_The ship slides off the rocks. Hiccup and Toothless go in the water!_  
_Stoick runs past you. He wades in, up to his chest._  
_It is a long wait._  
_Stoick comes up with Hiccup. Toothless climbs out onto the rocks._  
**Stoick**: Hiccup. I was wrong. I am sorry, son.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): a good sorry says what you did wrong  
> _Stoick said sorry. Which is the best sorry?_  
> - ✅ “I was wrong. I am sorry.” → Yes. A good sorry says what was wrong, and means it.
> - “Sorry, but it was your fault.” → That is not a real sorry. A good sorry does not blame.
> - “Whatever.” → “Whatever” does not mend anything. A good sorry does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what a good apology sounds like: says what was wrong and means it._

**Hiccup**: Me too, Dad.

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how a character shows care with words  
> _Stoick tells Hiccup to come back. What does that tell us?_  
> - ✅ He loves Hiccup and wants him safe → Yes. “Come back” is a loving thing to say.
> - He is cross → He sounds soft, not cross. “Come back” means he cares.
> - He wants a sandwich → Ha, no! “Come back” tells us he cares.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out what a character’s words show about how he feels._

## A19-17. The Fall

- `a19-17-s1`: Watch from the beach as Hiccup leads the big one away. · _Stand on the beach with the others and look up._
- `a19-17-s2`: Wait for the smoke to clear. · _There is nothing to do but wait. Do it as best you can._
- `a19-17-s3`: Find them. · _Go into the burnt place where the smoke is thinning._

#### `a19-17-up`

_From the beach you watch Hiccup and Toothless climb._  
_They are a tiny black speck against the cloud._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): high and low  
> _Hiccup is in the sky and you are on the beach. Who is higher?_  
> - ✅ Hiccup → Yes! Hiccup is high up, and you are down low.
> - You → You are on the beach, down low. Hiccup is up high.
> _For grown-ups: Compared high and low positions: the rider up in the sky and the child on the beach._

_The big one spreads its wings and follows._  
**Gobber**: What is the boy doing?  
**Astrid**: He is leading it up, away from us.  
_Everyone on the beach looks up. Your Nubbin peeps through its paws._  
_The speck and the big shadow go into the cloud._  

#### `a19-17-dive`

_For a long time there is only cloud._  
_Then a high whistle. It comes down, down, down._  
_Toothless dives out of the cloud, wings tucked in._  
_At the last moment he opens his wings and turns. The big one cannot._  
_Far along the beach, you see a flash and a puff of smoke._  
**Stoick**: Hiccup!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): slow breaths help us wait  
> _Waiting is very hard. What helps us wait?_  
> - ✅ Slow breaths, and holding a friend → Yes. Slow breaths and a hand to hold make waiting easier.
> - Jumping about → Jumping is tiring. Slow breaths calm us down.
> - Giving up → Waiting is hard, but slow breaths and a friend help us keep going.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when waiting is hard: slow breaths and a friend._


**Choices**

- **Run towards the smoke.**
    - You start to run, but the heat stops you. Gobber’s hook catches your collar.
    - **Gobber**: Wait for the smoke to clear.
- **Hold your Nubbin and wait.**
    - You hold your Nubbin and wait. It is the hardest thing here.
- **Go with Stoick.**
    - You follow Stoick’s broad back into the thinning smoke. He knows the way.

#### `a19-17-shore`

_The smoke thins. There is black rock and a curled-up dragon._  
_Toothless’s new tail fin is burnt._  
**Stoick**: Son? Hiccup?  
_Toothless opens one green eye. Slowly he opens his wings._  
_Wrapped inside, like a cloak, is Hiccup. His chest goes up and down._  
**Stoick**: He is alive!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): feeling words: relieved  
> _Stoick says “He is alive!” How does he feel?_  
> - ✅ Very relieved and happy → Yes. Relieved means a big worry has gone away.
> - Bored → Not bored! His worry has gone, and he is very happy.
> - Sleepy → He might be sleepy later. Right now he is relieved.
> _For grown-ups: Learned the feeling word relieved, when a big worry goes away._

_Stoick pats Toothless’s head. It is how you say thank you._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): staying close shows you care  
> _Your Nubbin keeps watch beside a friend who is resting. What does that say?_  
> - ✅ “I care about you” → Yes. Staying close says “I care” without any words.
> - “I am bored” → Not bored. Staying close shows love.
> - “I want to play” → It is a time for quiet. Staying close shows care.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how staying close to a resting friend shows care._

_Toothless pads over. He puts a whole silver fish at your Nubbin’s feet._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): patience: waiting kindly  
> _Toothless took a long time to trust. What did Hiccup do?_  
> - ✅ Waited, quietly and kindly → Yes. Waiting kindly is how trust grows.
> - Grabbed him → Grabbing frightens. Waiting kindly works better.
> - Shouted at him → Shouting frightens. Waiting quietly works better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how patience and kindness help trust grow._

_Your Nubbin is so proud. It does not eat the fish._  
_The sea goes grey and you are home. The saddle smells of fish._  

## A20-1. The Bright One

- `a20-01-s1`: Step into the grey and gold page. Find Frigg’s hall. · _Touch the page. Then go in at the door._
- `a20-01-s2`: Carry Frigg’s cloak up the hill. · _Follow the path up to the pale hall._
- `a20-01-s3`: Sit with Baldr while your Nubbin sleeps. · _Sit on the bench. There is no hurry._

#### `a20-01-page`

_Nova’s atlas opens at a grey and gold page._  
_This is a very old story, from a land called Iceland._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS2-2, ask): Iceland is an island: land with water all around  
> _Iceland is an island, far away to the north._  
> _(Point to the sea on the page.) What is all around an island?_  
> - ✅ Water → Yes! An island has water all the way around it.
> - Sand → Some islands have sand. But water goes all the way around.
> - A fence → No fence. The sea is what goes all the way around.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Iceland is an island, with sea all around it._

_A man named Snorri wrote it down, long, long ago._  
_His book tells one way the story goes._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): books were made by hand long ago  
> _Snorri wrote with a pen, on pages made of calfskin._  
> _There were no printers. Every book was made by hand._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that Snorri wrote the stories in a handmade book long ago._

_Some people still honour these gods today._  
_Whoosh! The page goes soft, and you step inside._  
_This is Frigg’s hall. Her spindle goes whirr, whirr, whirr._  
**Frigg**: Come in, guest. This is Fensalir. Will you run errands for me?  
**Fulla**: Can the little one carry things?  
_Your Nubbin holds up both arms. Yes!_  

**Choices**

- **Bow to Frigg, nice and low.**
    - Frigg bows back, just as low.
    - **Frigg**: Guests and hosts bow the same, in this house.
- **Say your name.**
    - **Frigg**: A good name. I will remember it.
- **Ask what to carry first.**
    - **Fulla**: Oh, I like this one!

#### `a20-01-page-done`

**Frigg**: The first errand is easy. Take this cloak up the hill to my son.  
**Fulla**: The hall is called Breidablik. You cannot miss it.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the parts of a name  
> _Let’s clap the name. Brei - da - blik._  
> _(Clap three times.)_  
> _Three claps, three parts. (Now try Fen - sa - lir.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:breidablik`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the syllables in Breidablik and Fensalir._


#### `a20-01-hall`

_Breidablik stands high on a hill. Its roof is pale as the sky._  
_A man sits at a long table, mending a strap._  
_He is so kind and so glad that he seems to shine._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, ask): we see things when there is light  
> _Baldr’s light fills the hall, so we can see everything._  
> _What do we need to see?_  
> - ✅ Light → Yes! We see things when there is light.
> - Quiet → Quiet is nice for sleeping. But to see, we need light.
> - Cold → Cold does not help us see. Light does.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we need light to see._

**Baldr**: You came from my mother. I know her cloak.  
**Baldr**: Put it down, and sit. Everyone who climbs should rest.  
_Your Nubbin sits in his light. Blink._  
_Blink. Then it tips over, fast asleep._  
**Baldr**: Shh. The small ones do that. Let it sleep.  

#### `a20-01-hall-done`

_Your Nubbin is fast asleep in the brightest patch of floor._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sleep helps bodies rest and grow  
> _Little ones need lots of sleep. Why?_  
> - ✅ It helps their bodies rest and grow → Yes! Sleep is how little bodies rest and grow.
> - It makes them noisy → Not noisy! Sleep helps bodies rest and grow.
> - They do not need it → Everybody needs sleep. It helps bodies rest and grow.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why sleep matters for growing bodies._

**Baldr**: Stay till it wakes. I would like the company.  

#### `a20-01-sit`

_You sit on the bench. Baldr mends his strap._  
_Stitch, stitch._  
**Baldr**: Everyone climbs up here with a question.  
**Baldr**: I like the part of the day when I listen.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): being kind by sitting quietly beside someone  
> _A friend is quiet and does not want to talk. What can we do?_  
> - ✅ Sit beside them → Yes. Sitting close shows we care, even with no words.
> - Shout at them → Shouting is too loud. Sitting quietly beside them is kinder.
> - Run away → Staying close is kinder. Sit beside them.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about staying close to a quiet friend._

**Baldr**: Ask me something. Or don’t.  

**Choices**

- **Ask why he shines.**
    - **Baldr**: I do not know. I have never been anything else.
- **Ask about his brothers.**
    - **Baldr**: Hödr. He cannot see, but he hears everything.
- **Just sit.**
    - So you sit. Baldr sits too.
    - Nobody says a word.
    - **Baldr**: That was a good question.

#### `a20-01-complete`

_Your Nubbin wakes when the light moves across the floor._  
**Baldr**: It will follow me now. The small ones do.  
_He folds the cloak and puts it on the bench._  
**Baldr**: Tell my mother I will wear it.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): on and under  
> _Baldr put the cloak on the bench._  
> _Is it on the bench, or under it?_  
> - ✅ On the bench → Yes! On means on top. The cloak is on the bench.
> - Under the bench → Under means below. The cloak is on top, so it is on the bench.
> _For grown-ups: Used the words on and under for where things are._

_On the way down, your Nubbin keeps looking back._  

## A20-2. Bad Dreams

- `a20-02-s1`: Take lamp oil up to Baldr. · _Fulla has the jar. Carry it up the hill._
- `a20-02-s2`: Walk down with Baldr to tell the gods. · _Go with Baldr and wait by the door._
- `a20-02-s3`: Help in the hall while the gods talk. · _Feed the fire. Fill the cups. Or just listen._

#### `a20-02-oil`

_It is late. Fulla holds a jar of lamp oil._  
**Fulla**: His lamp burns all night. Take this up to him?  
_Baldr sits at his table. His cup has gone cold._  
**Baldr**: Oh, it is you. I am glad it is you.  
**Baldr**: I keep having a bad dream. I go down a long road.  
**Baldr**: It makes me worried. I have not told anyone.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): telling someone when you are worried  
> _Baldr is worried. What could help him?_  
> - ✅ Tell someone he trusts → Yes. Telling someone helps. It is hard alone.
> - Keep it a secret → Secrets make a worry feel bigger. Telling helps.
> - Pretend it is not there → I tried that. The dream stayed. Telling helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about telling someone you trust when you are worried._

_Your Nubbin climbs up beside him and sits very close._  

**Choices**

- **Say a dream is only a dream.**
    - **Baldr**: I keep telling myself that. It is hard to believe.
- **Say he should tell the others.**
    - **Baldr**: Yes. You are right. It is worse alone.
- **Sit and wait.**
    - You sit. He puts his hand on your Nubbin’s head.

#### `a20-02-oil-done`

**Baldr**: In the morning I will tell them all. Walk with me?  
_He sleeps a little. The lamp stays lit, and you keep watch._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): the sun comes up in the morning  
> _The lamp is lit because it is night. When does the sun come up?_  
> - ✅ In the morning → Yes! The sun comes up in the morning, and the dark goes.
> - At bedtime → At bedtime it is getting dark. The sun comes up in the morning.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about night and morning._


#### `a20-02-telling`

_In the morning the gods meet in their great hall._  
_Baldr tells them about the road, and the bad dream._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds  
> _Baldr starts with the sound buh. Which word starts with buh too?_  
> - ✅ Bear → Yes! Buh-buh-bear. Baldr and bear both start with buh.
> - Fox → Fox starts with fuh. Baldr starts with buh, like bear.
> - Hare → Hare starts with huh. Baldr starts with buh, like bear.
> _For grown-ups: Matched words by their first sound (b for Baldr and bear)._

**Thor**: A dream is only smoke. Show me the trouble and I will fix it.  
**Odin**: Not every trouble is easy to see.  
**Frigg**: Then we will find it. Whatever it is.  
_The talk goes on and on. You find a stool by the door._  

#### `a20-02-telling-done`

_The talk goes on all morning, and into the night._  
_You carry three cups to the table. Then two more._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add 3 and 2  
> _You carried three cups, then two more. How many cups is that?_  
> - ✅ Five → Yes! One, two, three, four, five. Five cups.
> - Four → Let’s count: one, two, three, four, five. It is five.
> - Six → Let’s count: one, two, three, four, five. Five cups.
> _For grown-ups: Added 3 and 2 using cups._

_You listen to everything._  

#### `a20-02-council`

_The hall gets dark. The fire is low._  
**Thor**: We could stand round him, day and night.  
**Odin**: Then he would live in a ring of spears. No.  
**Baldr**: I would rather not. I would miss people.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): who we like to be with  
> _Baldr would miss people. Who do you like to be with?_  
> _(Wait for an answer.)_  
> - My family → Family is a good answer. Being together feels safe.
> - My friends → Friends are a good answer. Being together feels happy.
> - My pet → A pet is a good answer. Being together feels cosy.
> _For grown-ups: Named the people and pets they like to be with._

**Frigg**: Then I will ask. Everything in the world will promise not to hurt him.  
**Thor**: Everything? That is a great deal of everything.  
**Frigg**: Then I had better start early.  

**Choices**

- **Build the fire up.**
    - You build up the fire. Odin nods at you.
- **Fill the cups.**
    - You fill the cups. Thor’s hands are steady now.
- **Sit by the door and listen.**
    - You sit by the door and listen.

#### `a20-02-complete`

_By dawn the gods have a plan._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): what happens first, next and last  
> _Let’s tell it in order. First, Baldr told his dream._  
> _Next, the gods made a plan. What will they do last, tomorrow?_  
> - ✅ Walk and ask the whole world → Yes! First the dream, next the plan, last the walk.
> - Go to sleep for a year → No, they have work to do. Last comes the walk.
> - Have a big party → Not a party. Last comes the walk, to ask the world.
> _For grown-ups: Put the story in order: first, next, last._

**Frigg**: Tomorrow we walk. We will ask the whole world.  
**Baldr**: Mother, you do not have to.  
**Frigg**: I know.  
_Your Nubbin falls asleep. You carry it down the hill._  

## A20-3. The Oaths

- `a20-03-s1`: Walk with Frigg while she asks the fire, the water and the stones. · _Keep one step behind Frigg._
- `a20-03-s2`: Carry Frigg’s asking to the animals and birds. · _Go over the meadows and along the edge of the wood._
- `a20-03-s3`: Let your Nubbin make its own promise. · _Bring your Nubbin to Frigg on the step._

#### `a20-03-asking`

_Frigg walks out at first light. Fulla, you and your Nubbin follow._  
_She asks the fire. The flames lie down low._  
_She asks the water. It goes still as glass._  
_She asks the iron. Every blade on the wall rings._  
_She asks the stones and the trees, one by one._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, do): sorting materials: stone, wood, iron, water  
> _Frigg asked iron, stone, wood and water. (Point to each one in the picture.)_  
> _Which of these is hard and strong: iron, or water? (Tap the hard one.)_  
> Check: `edu:sort:materials:hard-or-soft`
> _For grown-ups: Compared materials: hard iron and stone, and flowing water._

**Frigg**: Everything can be asked. It only takes time.  
_Past an old oak, you see a tiny green sprig. It has two leaves._  
_Your Nubbin stops to look. Frigg walks on._  

#### `a20-03-asking-done`

**Frigg**: The animals and birds now. My feet are tired. Will you carry my asking?  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): asking for help, and saying yes  
> _Frigg is tired and asks for help._  
> _Is asking for help a good thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Yes, it is brave and sensible → Yes. Asking for help is a good thing. Thank you.
> - No, we should do it all alone → Doing it all alone is very hard. Asking is wise.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how asking for help is a good thing to do._


#### `a20-03-beasts`

_You carry Frigg’s asking over the meadows._  
_The hare thumps the ground. The bear lies down flat._  
_The reindeer lowers her antlers to the grass._  
_The birds all fly up in one big cloud, and come down again._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): animals live where their needs are met  
> _Birds live in trees and nests. What do birds need from trees?_  
> - ✅ A safe place to rest and make a nest → Yes! Trees give birds a safe home.
> - A swimming pool → Not a pool! Birds use trees for homes and nests.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that trees are homes for birds._

_Your Nubbin tugs your sleeve. Nobody has asked it._  

#### `a20-03-promise`

_Frigg sits on the step. Your Nubbin walks up to her._  
_It stands up as straight as it can._  
**Fulla**: Oh. It wants to be asked.  
**Frigg**: Of course. Everything should be. Come here, little one.  
**Frigg**: Will you promise not to hurt my son?  
_Your Nubbin thinks about it very seriously._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): keeping a promise  
> _A promise is something we say, and then we do._  
> _What do we do with a promise?_  
> - ✅ Keep it → Yes. We keep our promises. It is how friends trust us.
> - Forget it → Forgetting can hurt a friend. We try to keep promises.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what a promise means and keeping it._


**Choices**

- **Let it put its paw in Frigg’s hand.**
    - Your Nubbin puts its paw in her hand.
    - **Frigg**: That will hold.
- **Let it bow, like the hare.**
    - It bows so low it nearly topples.
    - **Frigg**: Twice promised!
- **Promise for it.**
    - **Frigg**: No. Let it promise for itself.
    - Your Nubbin nods hard, three times. Frigg nods back.

#### `a20-03-complete`

_By evening, everything has promised._  
_Fire, water, iron, stones and trees all said yes._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 5  
> _Let’s count the promises on your fingers. Fire._  
> _Water. Iron._  
> _Stones. Trees._  
> _(Count each one. How many did you get?)_  
> Check: `edu:count:promises:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five things on their fingers._

**Frigg**: Everything has promised. Everything I could think of.  
_Frigg gives you her spindle. Your Nubbin falls asleep on the step._  

## A20-4. The Game

- `a20-04-s1`: Go with the gods to the Thing-field. · _Follow the crowd to the ring of stones._
- `a20-04-s2`: Join the game, or watch from the edge. · _Thor will give you a pebble. You can say no._
- `a20-04-s3`: Find Hödr outside the ring. Tell him what is happening. · _Walk round the outside of the stones._

#### `a20-04-field`

_The Thing-field is a wide green place with a ring of stones._  
_Baldr stands in the middle. The gods throw things at him, for fun._  
_A stone bumps his shoulder. Plop!_  
_It lands in the grass._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): sound words  
> _The stone goes plop! Which one is a sound word?_  
> - ✅ Plop → Yes! Plop is a sound word. It sounds like what it is.
> - Grass → Grass is a thing. Plop is the sound word.
> _For grown-ups: Found a sound word (plop) in the story._

_Nothing can hurt him, because everything promised._  
**Thor**: Your turn, brother! Stand still!  
_Thor’s big stone stops. Then drop!_  
_It falls to the ground._  
_Everyone laughs. Baldr laughs the most._  

#### `a20-04-field-done`

_Your Nubbin finds the edge of Baldr’s light._  
_It lies down in it like a cat in a sunbeam._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-PS3-1, ask): sunlight warms  
> _Cats and Nubbins love a sunbeam. Why is a sunny spot cosy?_  
> - ✅ Sunlight makes it warm → Yes! Sunlight warms the ground, so it feels cosy.
> - Sunlight makes it cold → Sunlight warms things up. That is why it feels cosy.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sunlight makes things warm._


#### `a20-04-turn`

**Thor**: Guest! Here is a pebble for you to throw.  
_It is small and smooth. Baldr smiles._  
**Baldr**: Go on. It only tickles.  
_Outside the ring a tall man stands alone, with his hands empty._  
**Fulla**: That is Hödr, Baldr’s brother. He cannot see to throw.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): choosing, and watching is fine too  
> _You may throw, or watch. Is it all right to say, “I will watch”?_  
> - ✅ Yes, watching is fine → Yes. You can choose to watch, and that is fine.
> - No, you must join in → You never have to join in. Choosing to watch is fine.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about making a choice, and that it is fine to watch._


**Choices**

- **Throw the pebble, gently.**
    - Your pebble bumps his knee and rolls back. Everyone cheers.
- **Give it back. Watch from the edge.**
    - **Thor**: Fair enough. Somebody should keep the score.
- **Let your Nubbin have the throw.**
    - It rolls the pebble to Baldr’s feet. He hands it back.
    - **Baldr**: A draw!

#### `a20-04-hodr`

_You walk round to where Hödr stands. He turns his head._  
**Hödr**: You are the guest. I know your footsteps.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): we hear with our ears  
> _Hödr cannot see, but he hears the laughing. What do we hear with?_  
> - ✅ Our ears → Yes! Ears hear sounds. (Touch your ears.)
> - Our knees → Not knees! (Touch your ears.) Ears are for hearing.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we hear with our ears, and can still know things without sight._

**Hödr**: Tell me what they are doing. I can hear laughing.  
_So you tell him about Thor’s big stone, and your Nubbin asleep._  
**Hödr**: Thank you. I like to know what is funny.  

#### `a20-04-hodr-done`

**Hödr**: Come and tell me the next good one.  
**Hödr**: You tell it better than they do.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): a story has a beginning, middle and end  
> _Every story has a first part._  
> _What comes first in your day: waking up, or going to bed?_  
> - ✅ Waking up → Yes! First you wake up. Bed comes at the end.
> - Going to bed → Bed comes last. First, we wake up.
> _For grown-ups: Put parts of a day in order, as a story has a beginning and an end._


#### `a20-04-complete`

_The game goes on till the light goes. Nobody is hurt._  
_Baldr puts his arm round his brother._  
**Baldr**: Did you hear Thor’s big stone go drop?  
**Hödr**: I heard everything. The guest told me the rest.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): including everyone in the game  
> _The guest told Hödr what he could not see._  
> _How does this help him join in?_  
> - ✅ He can be part of the fun → Yes! Telling someone helps them be part of things.
> - It does not help → It does help. Telling Hödr lets him share the fun.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about including a friend who cannot see._

_Your Nubbin follows them home, holding Hödr’s bootlace._  

## A20-5. The Old Woman

- `a20-05-s1`: Fetch water for Fensalir. · _Take the pails to the spring and carry them back._
- `a20-05-s2`: Sit by the fire while Frigg talks with the traveller. · _Wind the wool, and stay in the room._

#### `a20-05-water`

_You fetch water. You take two pails._  
_Your Nubbin takes a thimble._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): which holds more  
> _You carry pails, and your Nubbin carries a thimble. Which holds more water?_  
> - ✅ The pail → Yes! The pail is big, so it holds more. The thimble holds a drop.
> - The thimble → The thimble is tiny. The pail is bigger, so it holds more.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a pail and a thimble to see which holds more._

_At the door stands an old woman, wrapped in shawls._  
_You can only see her hands._  
**Fulla**: A traveller! Bring the water in.  
_Your Nubbin looks at her. Then it hides behind your legs._  
_It has never done that before._  

#### `a20-05-talk`

_Frigg gives the old woman the best seat, and a cup of water._  
**The Old Woman**: What are the gods doing at the Thing-field, lady?  
**Frigg**: Playing. Nothing can hurt my son. Everything promised.  
**The Old Woman**: Everything? Every single thing?  
**Frigg**: Every thing but one little sprout. It was too young to ask.  
_The old woman puts her cup down very carefully._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): feeling unsure, and what helps  
> _Your Nubbin hid behind your legs. It felt unsure._  
> _What helps when we feel unsure?_  
> - ✅ Stay close to a friend or a grown-up → Yes. Staying close helps. Feeling unsure is allowed.
> - Pretend we are fine → It is fine to feel unsure. Staying close helps more.
> - Run off alone → Staying close to someone safe helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about feeling unsure and staying close to someone safe._

**The Old Woman**: Too young. Yes. Very wise.  

**Choices**

- **Keep winding the wool.**
    - You keep winding, round and round.
- **Look up at the old woman.**
    - You look up. She smiles under the shawls.
    - Then it is only shawls.
- **Pick up your Nubbin.**
    - You hug your Nubbin. It stops shaking.

#### `a20-05-talk-done`

_The old woman thanks Frigg, and goes out of the door._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds  
> _Door starts with the sound duh. Which word starts with duh too?_  
> - ✅ Dog → Yes! Duh-duh-dog. Door and dog both start with duh.
> - Cat → Cat starts with kuh. Door starts with duh, like dog.
> - Hen → Hen starts with huh. Door starts with duh, like dog.
> _For grown-ups: Matched words by first sound (d for door and dog)._

_You look down the path. It is empty both ways._  

#### `a20-05-complete`

**Frigg**: An odd guest. She asked a lot of questions.  
**Fulla**: I will bolt the door tonight.  
_Your Nubbin sits by the door, looking out towards the old oak._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, notice): mistletoe grows on another tree  
> _The green sprout on the old oak is mistletoe. It is a real plant._  
> _Mistletoe grows on a branch of another tree._  
> _It drinks water from the tree. Its green leaves make food._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that mistletoe is a green plant that grows on another tree’s branch._


## A20-6. Hödr

- `a20-06-s1`: Go back to the Thing-field. · _Walk to the ring of stones. Hödr is standing apart._
- `a20-06-s2`: Run for the ring. · _Run as fast as you can._
- `a20-06-s3`: Sit with Hödr. · _Stay beside him outside the ring._

#### `a20-06-field`

_A quiet word first: in this part, Baldr dies. It is told gently._  
_The game is on again. The ring is full of laughing._  
_Hödr stands outside the ring, with empty hands._  
_A cloaked someone comes up beside him._  
_You see only a hand, holding something green._  
**A Voice**: Why are you not throwing? Everyone else is.  
**Hödr**: I cannot see him. I have nothing to throw.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): fair play: everyone gets a turn  
> _Hödr wants a turn too. Is it fair to leave someone out?_  
> - ✅ No, everyone should get a turn → Yes. Fair means everyone gets a turn.
> - Yes, leave him out → That is not fair. Fair means everyone gets a turn.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about fairness: making sure everyone gets a turn._

**A Voice**: Here is a sprig. I will guide your arm.  
_It is a trick. Your Nubbin knows the sprig, and starts to run._  
**Hödr**: Thank you. I want to be in the game.  

#### `a20-06-fall`

_The hand turns Hödr’s arm. You run, but the field is wide._  
_Hödr throws the sprig._  
_Baldr falls down, and does not get up._  
_He has died. His body has stopped working, and it will not start again._  
_Nobody laughs. The field is very quiet._  
_The gods cry so hard that nobody can find any words._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): crying is allowed when we are very sad  
> _When someone we love dies, we feel very sad. Crying is allowed._  
> _Crying helps. So does a hug, and sitting together._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that crying is allowed when we are sad, and that hugs and company help._

_Your Nubbin runs past them all, to Hödr. It sits by his feet._  

#### `a20-06-hodr`

**Hödr**: What happened? Why is it quiet?  
_Nobody can answer. The gods are crying too hard._  
_Your Nubbin leans against his legs._  
**Hödr**: You are there. Please tell me.  
_So you tell him, kindly and plainly. He goes very still._  
**Hödr**: I only wanted to be in the game.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words for feelings  
> _Hödr’s voice is small and low. Which word tells how Hödr feels?_  
> - ✅ Sad → Yes. Hödr feels sad. His voice sounds sad too.
> - Silly → Silly is a giggly feeling. Hödr feels sad.
> - Sleepy → Sleepy is a yawny feeling. Hödr feels sad.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a word for a character’s feeling (sad)._

_Someone tricked him. It was not his fault._

- **Sit down next to him.**
    - You sit in the grass beside him. After a while he sits too.
- **Hold his hand.**
    - You hold his hand. He holds on tight.
- **Tell him someone tricked him.**
    - **Hödr**: I felt a hand on mine. It does not help yet. Stay anyway.

_The gods stay at the Thing-field. It is a place of peace._  
_Hödr sits in the grass. Only you and your Nubbin go to him._  
**Fulla**: Bring him to Fensalir. Frigg says nobody should sit alone tonight.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what helps someone who is very sad  
> _Hödr is very sad. What helps someone who is very sad?_  
> - ✅ Stay with them → Yes. Staying with someone shows we care.
> - Leave them alone → Being alone feels lonely. Staying with them is kinder.
> - Tell them to stop → Sad feelings need time. Staying close helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about staying with a sad friend._

> - A tiny push → A tiny push is too small for a heavy ship.

> - Hit someone → Hitting hurts people. A slow breath helps better.
> - Shout at everyone → Shouting is too much. A slow breath helps better.

> - Nothing at all → Try again. Hum, and touch your throat. It buzzes. That is a vibration.

> - At the shore → The shore has sand, pebbles and sea. Trees are in the woods.

- **Take the road through the woods.**

> - It gets bigger → It does not grow. Warm sunshine melts ice into water.
> - It turns to stone → Frost does not turn to stone. Warm sunshine melts it into water.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that warmth melts frost into water._

> - A fish → Fish live in water. Bats and bears shelter in caves.
> - A whale → Whales live in the sea. Bats and bears shelter in caves.

> - A puddle → A puddle is wet, full of water. A rock in the sun is dry.
