#### `a20-13-house`

_The gods know who tricked Hödr. It was Loki, and he has run away._  
_They find a house high on a mountain, with a door in every wall._  
**Thor**: Four doors. So he could watch every way at once.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4  
> _A door in every wall. (Count the doors: one, two, three, four.)_  
> _Four doors. One for each wall of the house._  
> Check: `edu:count:doors:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four doors._

_The house is empty. By the fire there is a little heap of ash._  
**Odin**: He was making something. He burned it when he saw us.  
_Below the mountain a waterfall tumbles into a deep pool._  

#### `a20-13-ash`

_Kvasir, the wisest god, kneels by the ash and looks._  
_It is the shape of a net. Nobody has made one before._  
**Odin**: He will be in the water. So we will make a net too.  
_The gods sit down and make a net, knot by knot._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): over and under, like weaving a net  
> _A net has cords that cross: over, under, over, under._  
> _(Wiggle your fingers over and under, like making a net.)_  
> Check: `edu:weave:net:over-under`
> _For grown-ups: Moved their fingers over and under, as in weaving._

**Thor**: Hold still, small one. You are not the fish.  
_It is the first smile since the Thing-field._  

**Choices**

- **Hold the cord steady.**
    - You hold it steady through every knot.
- **Tie some knots yourself.**
    - You tie a row of knots. Thor checks every one.
- **Untangle your Nubbin first.**
    - You untangle your Nubbin. It watches with its arms folded.

#### `a20-13-falls`

_This is Franang’s Falls. A salmon lies in the pool below._  
_It is Loki._  
_Thor wades in with the net. You hold one end on the bank._  
_You drag it down the river. The salmon slips away._  
_You drag it again. This time the salmon leaps!_  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, notice): salmon live in rivers and leap up waterfalls  
> _Real salmon are river fish. They swim up rivers to lay their eggs._  
> _They leap right up waterfalls on the way._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that real salmon swim up rivers and leap waterfalls._

_Thor catches it by the tail. Splash!_  
_The old book says that is why salmon have thin tails._  

#### `a20-13-falls-done`

_In Thor’s hand the salmon is a man again, wet and still._  
_He says nothing at all._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): putting things right after a wrong thing  
> _Loki did a wrong thing. What can a person do after a wrong thing?_  
> - ✅ Say sorry, and make it right → Yes. Saying sorry and making it right is brave.
> - Pretend it did not happen → The wrong thing is still there. Saying sorry is braver.
> - Blame someone else → Blaming is not fair. Saying sorry is braver.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying sorry and putting things right._


#### `a20-13-complete`

_The gods take Loki away down the mountain._  
_Your Nubbin looks at you, as if it has a question._  
**Odin**: Go home to Fensalir, guest. What happens next is ours to do.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): rules keep people safe  
> _Rules help keep people safe. Who helps make the rules at home or school?_  
> - ✅ Grown-ups, and we can help too → Yes. Grown-ups make rules, and we can help.
> - Nobody → Somebody always helps make them. Grown-ups, and we can too.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about who makes rules and why rules keep us safe._

_The page turns, the way pages do._  

## A20-14. The Bowl

- `a20-14-s1`: Follow the stair down under the earth. · _Take the steep stair, and keep your Nubbin close._
- `a20-14-s2`: Stay near Sigyn and her bowl. · _Go nearer, or stay where you are._
- `a20-14-s3`: See what happens when the bowl is full. · _Stay still. It will not take long._

#### `a20-14-cave`

_Under the earth there is a cave, with three flat stones._  
_Loki is held still on the stones, because of the wrong thing he did._  
_Drops fall from the rock above him, slow and steady._  
_A woman kneels by him with a bowl. It is Sigyn, his wife._  
_The bowl catches the drops. Her arms are tired._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): above and below  
> _The drops fall from above. Where is the bowl: above the drops, or below?_  
> - ✅ Below → Yes! The bowl is below the drops, to catch them.
> - Above → Above means higher up. The bowl is below the drops.
> _For grown-ups: Used above and below to say where things are._

_Your Nubbin holds on to your leg._  

#### `a20-14-bowl`

_You go nearer._  
_Sigyn knows who you are: the guest who asked at the cave._  
_She looks at the bowl, and nothing else._  
**Sigyn**: You asked so nicely, in the cave. Everyone heard.  
**Sigyn**: I do not ask anything of you. Please do not ask me.  
_The bowl fills, drop by drop._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): offering help with a hard job  
> _Sigyn is doing a hard job, with love._  
> _What can we do for someone doing a hard job?_  
> - ✅ Ask if they need help → Yes, asking if they need help is a kind thing to do.
> - Tell them it is boring → That would not be kind. Asking if they need help is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about offering help to someone doing a hard job._

_Your Nubbin sits at the edge of the lamplight._  

#### `a20-14-shake`

_The bowl is full. Sigyn must take it away to empty it._  
_A drop falls on Loki. He shakes, and the earth shakes too!_  
_Wobble, wobble. Then Sigyn is back, and it is still._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS1-1, notice): earthquakes are real: the ground moves  
> _Iceland has real earthquakes. The ground is made of huge pieces._  
> _The pieces slowly move, and sometimes the ground shakes._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the ground is made of huge pieces that move, so earthquakes are real._

_The old book says Sigyn stays with him, all that time._  
_Your Nubbin holds on to you with both arms._  

**Choices**

- **Hold your Nubbin close.**
    - You hold it close. It was shaking, and then it is not.
- **Stay a bit longer, for Sigyn.**
    - You stay. Sigyn lifts one hand, just for a moment.
- **Go back up the stair.**
    - You go up into the cold air. The earth is quiet.

#### `a20-14-complete`

_You climb up out of the earth into a grey evening._  
_The wind smells of snow._  
_The page turns. It is white from edge to edge._  
_Your Nubbin pulls your cloak round you both. You step onto the snow._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): sound words  
> _Snow goes crunch, crunch. Which word sounds like what it is: splash, or table?_  
> - ✅ Splash → Yes! Splash sounds just like water. Crunch sounds like snow.
> - Table → Table is just a name. Splash sounds like what it is.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a sound word (splash) over an ordinary word._


## A20-15. The Fimbulwinter

- `a20-15-s1`: Cross the long white plain. · _Keep the wind at your back. Walk to the dark trees._
- `a20-15-s2`: Find the two who are hiding in the wood. · _Look for trodden snow._
- `a20-15-s3`: Keep Líf and Lífthrasir company. · _Sit in the hollow with them._

#### `a20-15-plain`

_Now comes a great winter, called the Fimbulwinter._  
_Snow blows from every side. The sun is pale and gives no warmth._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-2, ask): winter days are short in the far north  
> _In the far north, winter days are short._  
> _Is the sun up for a long time, or a short time?_  
> - ✅ A short time → Yes! In midwinter, Iceland has only a few hours of daylight.
> - A long time → In winter the sun is up only a few hours in the far north.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that winter days are short in the far north._

_Three winters come, one after another, with no summer between._  
_You walk with your head down. Your Nubbin rides in your cloak._  
_Ahead, through the white, there is a dark line of trees._  

#### `a20-15-holt`

_The wood is called Hoddmímir’s Holt. Under the trees, the wind cannot find you._  
_Two people sit under a big tree, in one blanket._  
**Líf**: Oh! Someone. I thought nobody was left.  
**Lífthrasir**: We are Líf and Lífthrasir. We live on dew.  
**Líf**: It is not much. But it is enough.  
_Your Nubbin climbs out and sits between them, under the blanket._  
**Lífthrasir**: It is warm. Can it stay?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): welcoming someone new  
> _Líf and Lífthrasir welcome a new friend. How can we welcome someone new?_  
> - ✅ Say hello and make room → Yes! Saying hello and making room helps someone feel welcome.
> - Look away → Looking away feels lonely. Hello and a bit of room feel welcoming.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how to welcome someone new._


#### `a20-15-company`

_So you stay in the wood. Every morning you lick dew off the leaves._  
_Every night you sit close, under one blanket and your cloak._  
_Your Nubbin shares itself out: a night by each of you._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): two and two make four  
> _Two people were in the hollow. Then you and your Nubbin joined._  
> _How many now?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! Two and two make four.
> - Three → Let’s count: Líf, Lífthrasir, you, Nubbin. One, two, three, four.
> - Two → Two were there, then two more came. Count them: four.
> _For grown-ups: Added two and two to make four._

**Lífthrasir**: We used to have names for the days. We stopped.  
**Líf**: Tell us something. Anything that is not snow.  

**Choices**

- **Tell them about your valley.**
    - **You**: There is a pond, and a gate that sticks.
    - **Lífthrasir**: A gate that sticks. That sounds like a good home.
- **Tell them about the bright hall.**
    - You tell them about Baldr’s light, and your Nubbin asleep on the boards.
    - **Líf**: Then there was a light once. Good.
- **Just sit close.**
    - You sit close. Lífthrasir leans his head on your shoulder.

#### `a20-15-company-done`

**Líf**: You stayed. Nobody stays anywhere any more.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): staying with friends in hard times shows we care  
> _You stayed with Líf and Lífthrasir. What does staying show?_  
> - ✅ That we care → Yes. Staying with someone shows that we care.
> - That we are bored → Staying shows we care, and it feels good to be cared for.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how staying with friends shows care._


#### `a20-15-complete`

_One morning the dew tastes different._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS2-3, notice): what dew is  
> _Dew is tiny drops of water on leaves and grass in the morning._  
> _It forms when the night air cools._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that dew is tiny drops of water that form when the air cools._

**Lífthrasir**: Something is coming. I can feel it in the roots.  
**Líf**: Not here, though. It will not come here. Will it?  
_Your Nubbin climbs to the edge of the wood and looks out._  

## A20-16. The Twilight

- `a20-16-s1`: Look out from the edge of the wood. · _Climb the roots where your Nubbin is._
- `a20-16-s2`: Wait at the edge of the wood until it is over. · _Stay with Líf and Lífthrasir. Nothing will reach the trees._

#### `a20-16-edge`

_From the edge of the wood you can see a very long way._  
_Far, far away, something is happening at the end of the world._  
_Tiny wolves run across the sky._  
_A dark ship comes slowly over the sea._  
_There is a figure at its front, who never turns._  
_Far off there is a red glow, like a sunset in the wrong place._  
_None of it comes near. Your Nubbin holds on to a root._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): near and far  
> _Which is near: the root in Nubbin’s arms, or the far-off ship?_  
> - ✅ The root → Yes! The root is near. The ship is far away.
> - The ship → The ship is far away. The root is near.
> _For grown-ups: Used near and far to compare distances._


#### `a20-16-wait`

_Líf and Lífthrasir come up beside you. They look at your face._  
**Líf**: Is it coming here?  
**You**: No. Not here.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when we feel scared  
> _Líf and Lífthrasir feel scared. What helps when we feel scared?_  
> - ✅ Hold a hand and breathe slowly → Yes. A hand to hold and slow breaths help.
> - Hide all alone → Being with someone helps more. Hold a hand and breathe slowly.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about holding a hand and slow breathing when scared._

**Lífthrasir**: Then we will wait. We are good at waiting.  
_The light changes. The noise far off gets less, and then it is gone._  

**Choices**

- **Hold Líf’s hand.**
    - You hold Líf’s hand. Her fingers are cold, then warm.
- **Tuck your Nubbin in your cloak.**
    - It puts one eye out, to keep watch with you.
- **Keep watching, so someone does.**
    - You keep watching. It is hard, but someone should.

#### `a20-16-complete`

_Then it is quiet._  
_A new quiet, like a room when everyone has gone home._  
_The snow stops._  
**Líf**: Is it over?  
_Your Nubbin sniffs. The air smells of salt, and of something green._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words for smells  
> _Your Nubbin smells the air. Which word describes a smell: sweet, or loud?_  
> - ✅ Sweet → Yes! Sweet can describe a smell. Loud is for sounds.
> - Loud → Loud is for sounds. Sweet can describe a smell.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a word that describes a smell._


## A20-17. The Green Earth

- `a20-17-s1`: Walk out of the wood into the new land. · _Follow Líf and Lífthrasir._
- `a20-17-s2`: Go to the old ground where the gods’ halls stood. · _Walk across the fields to the grassy plain._
- `a20-17-s3`: Look in the grass for the gods’ old game pieces. · _Search the long grass round the old stones._

#### `a20-17-green`

_The sea goes down._  
_The land comes up, wet and new, green as a first leaf._  
_There are fields already. Corn grows in them, and nobody planted it._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, notice): plants grow from seeds that need water and light  
> _In real life, plants grow from seeds. Seeds wait in the soil._  
> _They grow when they get water and sunshine._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that seeds wait in the soil and grow with water and sunshine._

_Líf and Lífthrasir walk out from the trees, holding hands. Then faster._  
**Líf**: Grass! Feel it!  
**Lífthrasir**: And the sun. It is warm again.  
_Your Nubbin runs into a field and lies down flat in the sun._  

#### `a20-17-old-ground`

_Where the gods’ halls stood there is grass, with old stones showing through._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): places change over time  
> _Long ago, people built halls to meet in. Now grass grows over the stones._  
> _Places change over time. Old things can be remembered._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that places change over time, and old things can be remembered._

_People are gathering: the gods’ grown sons, Vídarr and Váli, Módi and Magni._  
_Módi and Magni carry their father’s hammer between them, gently._  
**Vídarr**: Guest. Sit with us. There is time for everything.  
_Then two more come up the road from the quiet hall._  
_It is Baldr, and Hödr with him!_  
_Baldr’s light is just as it was._  
_Your Nubbin is running before you can stand._  

#### `a20-17-old-ground-done`

_Your Nubbin runs into Baldr’s light and falls asleep in it, at once._  
_It has been trying to get back there all this time._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, do): a slow, sleepy clapping beat  
> _Let’s clap a slow, sleepy beat for your Nubbin. Clap, rest._  
> _Clap, rest._  
> _(Clap four slow claps, with a quiet rest between each.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:lullaby:slow`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped a slow, steady beat._


#### `a20-17-pieces`

_The brothers sit on the grass, and talk about old things._  
**Baldr**: Do you remember the Thing-field? Thor’s big stone that went drop?  
**Hödr**: I remember the guest telling it. Better than you did.  
_In the long grass, your hand finds something small and cold._  
_It is a gold game piece! There are more in the grass._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 6  
> _Let’s count the gold pieces in the grass. (Point to each one.)_  
> _One, two, three, four, five, six. Six gold pieces!_  
> Check: `edu:count:game-pieces:6`
> _For grown-ups: Counted six game pieces, pointing at each._

**Vídarr**: They were ours, before. Now they are anybody’s.  

**Choices**

- **Give the first piece to Baldr.**
    - **Baldr**: Ha! I always lost with this one.
- **Give the first piece to Hödr.**
    - Hödr feels the shape of it.
    - **Hödr**: A little horse. I always wanted to be the horse.
- **Set it on the grass between them.**
    - You set it between the brothers. They both reach for it, and laugh.

#### `a20-17-complete`

_The sun goes over the new land. The talk goes on, slow and easy._  
_Hödr turns his face to you. You are sitting beside him._  
**Hödr**: You rode to fetch my brother, and you asked for him in the cave.  
**Hödr**: Thank you for trying.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): trying to help is worth it  
> _Hödr says thank you for trying._  
> _Is trying to help worth it, even if it does not work?_  
> - ✅ Yes, trying shows we care → Yes. Trying shows that we care.
> - No, only winning counts → Trying matters too. It shows that we care.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why trying to help matters, even when it does not work out._

_Before you go, Baldr gives you a sprig with two leaves._  
**Baldr**: Too young to ask, once. It is older now. Keep it for me.  
_Your Nubbin wakes in his light, then comes back to you on its own._  
_Líf and Lífthrasir walk out together into the morning._  
_You are back in the Grove. There is a gold piece in your pocket._  

## A22-1. The Candle’s Story

- `a22-01-s1`: Step into the painted page and hear how the candle began. · _Touch the candle in the window. Then sit at the edge of the painted bed._
- `a22-01-s2`: Walk into the valley and meet the family. · _Climb the hill from the market to the house with green shutters._

#### `a22-01-story`

_A big book opens. It shows tall green mountains._  
_A candle glows in one window. You step into the picture._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, do): find Colombia’s mountains and seas  
> _This is a real place. It is a country called Colombia._  
> _It has tall mountains. It has sea on two sides._  
> _(Point to the tall green mountains in the picture.)_  
> Check: `edu:point:mountains:colombia`
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Colombia is a real country in South America, with tall mountains and sea on two sides._

_It is night, long ago. Abuela sits by a little girl in round glasses._  
**Abuela Alma**: Come in. Listen too. Mirabel loves this story.  
**Abuela Alma**: Long ago, we had to leave our home. It was not safe.  
_Abuela and Pedro walked for days with three babies._  
_Trouble was far behind them, small as a thread._  
**Abuela Alma**: At a river, Pedro stayed behind so we could cross.  
**Abuela Alma**: Pedro died that night. I miss him every day.  
**Abuela Alma**: Then a candle lit, and a warm house grew around us.  

**Choices**

- **Keep listening.**
    - You sit very still. The little girl holds her blanket tight.
- **Ask about Pedro.**
    - **Abuela Alma**: Pedro was kind. He was brave. He was a funny dancer.
    - Abuela smiles a little. Her eyes are wet.

#### `a22-01-story-done`

**Abuela Alma**: Every child in this family gets a gift one day.  
**Abuela Alma**: Tomorrow is yours, Mirabel.  
**Mirabel**: What will it be?  
**Abuela Alma**: Sleep, and see.  
_Mirabel feels excited and nervous, both at once._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming two feelings at once  
> _Mirabel feels excited and nervous. Can we feel two feelings together?_  
> - ✅ Yes, we can → Yes! Feelings can mix, like colours. Both are okay to feel.
> - No, only one → It can feel like one, but often two come together. Both are okay.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about feeling excited and nervous at the same time._


#### `a22-01-casita`

_The page turns. It is morning, ten years later._  
_A market is full of noise. Up the hill is a house._  
_It has white walls and green shutters. The shutters open by themselves!_  
_A young woman in round glasses runs down the steps._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the three beats of abuela  
> _Abuela is Spanish for grandmother. Say it with me: a-bue-la._  
> _(Clap each beat: a, bue, la. That is three claps.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:abuela`
> _For grown-ups: Learned that abuela is Spanish for grandmother and clapped its three syllables._

**Mirabel**: Hello! You are the traveller. Abuela said you would come.  
_The floor tiles clack, like a dog wagging its tail._  
**Mirabel**: That is Casita. Casita, be nice. We have a guest.  
_A shutter taps your shoulder, very gently._  
**Mirabel**: I am Mirabel. I do not have a gift. It is fine.  

**Choices**

- **Say you are the traveller.**
    - **Mirabel**: Great! You are in the blue room. The house likes guests.
- **Point out your Nubbin is travelling too.**
    - **Mirabel**: Oh, hello! Antonio will love you.
- **Ask what the list is for.**
    - **Mirabel**: Tonight is Antonio’s gift night. Everything must be just right.

#### `a22-01-lamp`

_Abuela meets you in the courtyard. She is tall and straight._  
_You have a little lamp. Its glass is dark._  
**Abuela Alma**: Nobody in this house walks in the dark. Come.  
_She lights your lamp from the candle in the window._  
_The flame is gold and steady. It is very kind of her._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, ask): we need light to see  
> _Your lamp is dark, then lit. What does a lit lamp help us do?_  
> - ✅ See in the dark → Yes! We see things when there is light.
> - Hear far away → Light helps our eyes, not our ears. We see when there is light.
> - Smell flowers → Light helps our eyes. A lamp helps us see in the dark.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we see things when there is light._

_Your room is small and blue. It has a window over the valley._  
_Your Nubbin sits on the windowsill and looks out._  
_Downstairs there are three sounds. Laughing, cooking, and shouting about chairs._

> _(Count with me: laughing is one, cooking is two, shouting is three.)_

## A22-2. The Family

- `a22-02-s1`: Go down to the market with Mirabel. · _Follow Mirabel down the hill to the square._
- `a22-02-s2`: Meet the rest of the family at the house. · _Go back up the hill and say hello in the courtyard._
- `a22-02-s3`: Eat in the kitchen with Julieta and Agustín. · _Follow the smell of arepas to the kitchen._

#### `a22-02-market`

_It is market morning. There are oranges, bread and sacks of coffee beans._  
**Mirabel**: Quick tour! Everyone in my family has a special gift.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): coffee grows on mountain bushes  
> _Those sacks hold coffee beans. Where does coffee grow here?_  
> - ✅ On bushes in the mountains → Yes! Coffee grows on bushes on the mountain slopes in Colombia.
> - In the sea → Not in the sea. Coffee grows on bushes on the mountain slopes.
> - In the sky → Not in the sky. It grows on bushes, high on the mountains.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that coffee grows on bushes in the mountains of Colombia._

_Luisa walks by. She carries two donkeys, one on each shoulder!_  
**Luisa**: Hi! Can’t stop. The church is crooked.  
_Tía Pepa has a little grey cloud above her head._  
_Plip, plip, plip! It rains on her onions._  
**Tío Félix**: Don’t worry, my love. We have umbrellas!  

**Choices**

- **Tell Tía Pepa the cloud is fine.**
    - **Tía Pepa**: It is fine, isn’t it?
    - The cloud turns into a small, pleased rainbow.
- **Ask Félix how he copes.**
    - **Tío Félix**: Umbrellas! And I tell her she is lovely, which is true.
- **Check on your Nubbin.**
    - Your Nubbin has found the goat. They are deciding to be friends.

#### `a22-02-market-done`

_Mirabel has ticked three things on her list._  
_She ticks one more. Then she nearly walks into a post._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add one more: 3 and 1 make 4  
> _Three ticks, and one more tick. How many ticks now?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! Three and one more is four.
> - Three → Let’s count: one, two, three, and one more. That is four.
> - Five → Let’s count again: one, two, three, four. Four ticks.
> _For grown-ups: Added one to three and got four._

**Mirabel**: Next, my cousins. Hold on tight!  

#### `a22-02-cousins`

_In the courtyard, flowers pop up! Pink, red and yellow._  
**Mirabel**: My sister Isabela grows flowers. Everyone loves her.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): what makes you you  
> _Camilo can look like anyone. What makes you you?_  
> - ✅ My own smile, laugh and heart → Yes! Nobody has your smile, your laugh and your heart. That is you.
> - My hair only → Hair is just one bit. Your smile, laugh and heart are you too.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what makes each person themselves._

**Isabela**: Hello, guest. How nice.  
_A girl in a pale dress whispers to herself. That is Dolores._  
**Dolores**: You sneezed in the market. Bless you.  
_A boy turns into Mirabel! Then Félix!_  
_Then himself. That is Camilo._  
**Camilo**: I can do your face. Stand still!  

**Choices**

- **Stand still.**
    - Camilo looks hard. Then you are looking at yourself, a little taller.
    - **Camilo**: I improved you. You are welcome.
- **Don’t stand still.**
    - **Camilo**: Fair. People hate it. Mostly my sisters.

#### `a22-02-kitchen`

_In the kitchen, Julieta is cooking arepas. They smell warm and buttery._  
**Julieta**: You look hungry. Sit down and eat.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): wash hands before eating  
> _Julieta says, wash your hands before you eat. Why do we do that?_  
> - ✅ To wash away germs → Yes! Soap and water wash germs away, so we stay well.
> - To make our hands cold → Not for cold. We wash to wash germs away and stay well.
> - So the arepa jumps → Ha! No. We wash to wash germs away and stay well.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that washing hands with soap and water washes germs away._

_An arepa is a round corn cake. This one has melted cheese inside._  
_Yum! Your tummy feels full and happy._  
**Agustín**: Welcome! Don’t mind the bee on my nose.  
_At the end of the house is a tower with a dark door._  
_Nobody looks at it. Everybody talks about chairs._  

**Choices**

- **Ask about the tower.**
    - **Mirabel**: That is nobody. Nobody is up there. It is just a room.
    - Julieta puts another arepa on your plate. That is an answer too.
- **Let it go.**
    - You let it go. Mirabel gives you a small, thankful look.
- **Watch your Nubbin.**
    - Your Nubbin looks up at the tower.
    - A small grey face looks back, then hides.

#### `a22-02-complete`

_All day, Mirabel hangs lanterns. She carries chairs._  
_She ties ribbons._  
_Nobody asks her to. She does it anyway._  
**Mirabel**: It is fine. Somebody has to do the not-magic jobs.  
_She smiles, but her smile looks small._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): a feeling can hide behind “fine”  
> _Mirabel says, “It is fine.” But her smile looks small._  
> _How does she feel?_  
> - ✅ A little sad → Yes. Her words say fine, but her small smile shows sad.
> - Very silly → Look at her small smile. She feels a little sad.
> - Sleepy → Her small smile shows a feeling. She feels a little sad.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a face and a voice can show a feeling the words hide._

_Your Nubbin leans on her ankle. Lean, lean, lean._  

## A22-3. Antonio’s Door

- `a22-03-s1`: Find Antonio before his gift night. · _Look in the nursery, and under the bed._
- `a22-03-s2`: Walk Antonio up to his door. · _Climb the stairs two steps behind Mirabel and Antonio._

#### `a22-03-hiding`

_It is evening. Everyone wears their best clothes and holds a candle._  
**Tía Pepa**: Where is Antonio?  
_You find him under the bed. He is five, and he is scared._  
**Antonio**: What if I do not get a gift?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what helps a scared friend  
> _Antonio is scared. What helps a scared friend?_  
> - ✅ Staying close and listening → Yes! A friend who stays close and listens helps a lot.
> - Shouting at him → Shouting makes scared feelings bigger. Staying close helps.
> - Leaving him alone → Alone can feel worse. Staying close and listening helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how to help a scared friend: stay close and listen._

_Mirabel lies flat on the floor, so her face is by his._  
**Mirabel**: Then you get to be you. That is the best thing in this house.  
**Antonio**: You did not get one.  
**Mirabel**: No. I did not. And I am still me.  

**Choices**

- **Hold out your hand.**
    - Antonio looks at your hand. Then he takes Mirabel’s.
    - That is just right.
- **Let your Nubbin go under first.**
    - Your Nubbin wriggles under the bed. Antonio giggles before he can stop.
- **Wait.**
    - Nobody hurries him. A small hand comes out and finds Mirabel’s sleeve.

#### `a22-03-hiding-done`

**Antonio**: Will you walk me? Both of you?  
**Mirabel**: All the way to the door.  
_Antonio’s heart goes thump, thump, thump. Let’s help it slow down._  

> **Lesson** (health, CASEL: Self-management, do): slow breaths calm a worried body  
> _(Breathe in slowly through your nose. Breathe out like blowing a candle.)_  
> _(Do it three times with Antonio: in, out; in, out; in, out.)_  
> Check: `edu:breathe:slowly:3`
> _For grown-ups: Practised three slow breaths to calm a worried body._


#### `a22-03-door`

_The stairs are full of family, holding candles._  
_A new door glows softly. It has no picture yet._  
_Mirabel holds Antonio’s hand. You walk behind._  
_Halfway up, Mirabel slows down. You see a memory._  
_Long ago, a little Mirabel stood at a glowing door. The door went dark._  
**Abuela Alma**: Whatever happens, you are loved, little one.  
_Then it is now. Antonio touches his door, and it glows!_  
_A toucan lands on his head. A jaguar and capybaras come out!_  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a bird has wings and a beak  
> _Which of these animals has wings and a big beak?_  
> - ✅ The toucan → Yes! A toucan has wings to fly and a big beak to eat fruit.
> - The jaguar → A jaguar has paws and fur, not wings.
> - The capybara → A capybara has no wings. The toucan has wings and a big beak.
> _For grown-ups: Told a bird from other animals by its wings and beak._

**Antonio**: I can hear them! They are talking!  
_Everyone cheers. Mirabel cheers the loudest, for a long time._  

**Choices**

- **Cheer with Mirabel.**
    - You cheer with her. When she stops, you stop too.
- **Look at Mirabel.**
    - She catches you looking and smiles hard. Her glasses are steamy.

#### `a22-03-door-done`

_The jaguar sniffs your Nubbin. Sniff, sniff, sniff!_  
_Your Nubbin sniffs back. Then it trills._  
_Trrrill!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sound: sniff and snore start with sn  
> _Sniff starts with “sn”. Which word starts the same way?_  
> - ✅ Snore → Yes! Snore and sniff both start with sn.
> - Toucan → Toucan starts with t. Snore starts with sn, like sniff.
> - Jaguar → Jaguar starts with j. Snore starts with sn, like sniff.
> _For grown-ups: Matched words that begin with the same first sounds._

**Antonio**: She says it smells like a garden. Your Nubbin says you snore!

- `a22-04-s2`: Help Mirabel show the family the cracks. · _Stand on the landing by the candle with Mirabel._

#### `a22-04-party`

_The party is loud and bright. There is music and dancing._  

> **Lesson** (music, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, do): clap a steady beat  
> _A musician plays a tiple. That is a small guitar from Colombia._  
> _(Clap a steady beat with the music: one, two, three, four.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:beat:party`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped a steady beat and met the tiple, a small Colombian guitar._

_Luisa holds up the piano, so people can dance under it!_  
_Mirabel slips to the quiet edge. You follow._  
**Mirabel**: I am happy for him. I really am.  
_A crack runs up the wall by her hand. Crrrack!_  
_Cracks race across the tiles, towards the candle._  
_The candle’s flame shakes and shrinks._  
**Mirabel**: Oh no. The candle!  
_Mirabel runs. You run after her._  
_Nobody else looks down._  

**Choices**

- **Follow the cracks.**
    - You watch the cracks. They race ahead, and they all go one way.
- **Keep up with Mirabel.**
    - You stay at her elbow, through a crowd that keeps smiling.

#### `a22-04-party-done`

_You reach the landing with her. The cracks reach it with you._  
_The floor tiles make a pattern: red, blue, red, blue._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): a colour pattern: what comes next  
> _Red, blue, red, blue. What colour comes next?_  
> - ✅ Red → Yes! Red, blue, red, blue, red. The pattern repeats.
> - Blue → Blue came just before. After blue, the pattern goes back to red.
> - Yellow → There is no yellow tile. The pattern repeats: red comes next.
> _For grown-ups: Continued a repeating colour pattern._


#### `a22-04-cracks`

**Mirabel**: Everybody! The house is in danger! Look at the cracks!  
_The music stops. Everyone looks up._  
_But the wall is smooth. The tiles are whole._  
_Casita mended them._  
**Abuela Alma**: Mirabel. What cracks?  
_Mirabel points. There is nothing there._  
**Abuela Alma**: Everything is fine. Music, please!  
_The music starts again. Nobody looks at Mirabel._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): how it feels when no one believes you  
> _Nobody believes Mirabel. How does she feel?_  
> - ✅ Lonely and worried → Yes. A friend who stays beside her helps.
> - Very happy → Look at her face. She feels lonely and worried.
> - Sleepy → She is wide awake, and she feels lonely and worried.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feelings of someone who is not believed: lonely and worried._


**Choices**

- **Say you saw them too.**
    - You say, “I saw them.” Abuela looks at you, polite and closed.
    - **Abuela Alma**: Our guest is tired. It was a long journey.
- **Say nothing, and stay by Mirabel.**
    - You stand beside her. It is not much, but she is not alone.

#### `a22-04-lamp`

_Your lamp has a gold flame. Abuela lit it._  
_The flame shakes, just like the candle._  
_Then it goes still, when the candle does._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): moving air makes a flame wobble  
> _In the real world, what makes a candle flame wobble?_  
> - ✅ Moving air, like a breeze → Yes! A breeze or a puff makes a flame dance.
> - A song → Not a song. Moving air, like a breeze, makes a flame wobble.
> - A colour → Not a colour. Moving air, like a breeze, makes a flame wobble.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that moving air makes a flame wobble._

**Mirabel**: Yours too! You saw it!  
_She squeezes your wrist, then lets go._

**Mirabel**: Night night, Antonio.  
_Your Nubbin hops up and sleeps on her bed._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): sleep helps our bodies rest and grow  
> _What does your body do while you sleep?_  
> - ✅ It rests and grows → Yes! Sleep helps your body rest and grow.
> - It runs a race → No race! While you sleep, your body rests and grows.
> - It eats lunch → Lunch is for when we are awake. Sleep helps us rest and grow.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sleep helps the body rest and grow._


## A22-5. Abuela’s Prayer

- `a22-05-s1`: Follow the light on the landing at midnight. · _Creep out to the banister and stay out of sight._
- `a22-05-s2`: Decide how you will help Mirabel: eyes, ears or hands. · _Choose the job you like best. All three help._

#### `a22-05-prayer`

_Late at night, a soft light shines on the landing._  
_Mirabel hides behind the banister. You hide too._  
_Abuela stands by the candle. A painting hangs beside it._  
_It shows a young man with a kind face. It is Pedro._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): families remember people with pictures and stories  
> _Abuela keeps a painting of Pedro. How do families remember people?_  
> - ✅ With pictures and stories → Yes! Pictures and stories keep people close in our hearts.
> - They never talk about them → Talking about people we miss helps. Pictures and stories keep them close.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how families remember people with pictures and stories._

**Abuela Alma**: Pedro, something is wrong. I can feel it.  
**Abuela Alma**: Tell me what to do, and I will do it.  
_The candle does not answer. Abuela goes to bed._  
**Mirabel**: She is scared. I have never seen her scared.  

**Choices**

    - That helps.
- **Look at the painting.**

#### `a22-05-plan`

**Mirabel**: Nobody else sees the cracks. So I will fix it.

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): ears are for hearing  
> _Mirabel says, ears. Which part of you hears sounds?_  
> - ✅ Ears → Yes! Ears hear. Eyes see. Hands touch.
> - Eyes → Eyes help us see. Ears help us hear.
> - Hands → Hands help us touch. Ears help us hear.
> _For grown-ups: Matched ears to hearing, eyes to seeing and hands to touching._


**Choices**

    - **Mirabel**: Yes! Two people looking. We start in the morning.
    - She gives you a drawing of the whole house.
- **Be the ears: make friends with Dolores.**
    - **Mirabel**: Dolores hears everything. Be kind to her.
    - From two floors away, a small voice says, “Thank you.”
- **Be the hands: help Luisa with her loads.**
    - **Mirabel**: Luisa carries so much. Let’s help her.
    - Outside, something very heavy is put down very gently.

**Mirabel**: Partners. Secret partners.  
_Your Nubbin holds out its hand. She shakes that too._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): share four things in twos  
> _There are four donkeys. Luisa carries two at a time._  
> _How many trips?_  
> - ✅ Two trips → Yes! Two donkeys, then two more. Two trips.
> - One trip → One trip is only two donkeys. Two and two make four, so two trips.
> - Four trips → She can carry two at once. Two and two make four: two trips.
> _For grown-ups: Split four into two groups of two._

**Luisa**: Hi. Can’t talk. Donkeys, then the bridge.

_Luisa goes still. Then she laughs too loudly._  
**Luisa**: I am fine. I am the strong one. Nothing cracks on me.

    - **Luisa**: You?

#### `a22-06-loads-done`

_By noon, the bridge is mended. The church is a bit to the left._  
_Luisa sits down on a wall. She is very tired._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): tired muscles need rest and water  
> _Luisa worked hard all morning. What does her body need?_  
> - ✅ Rest and water → Yes! Rest and water help tired muscles feel better.
> - More hard work → Hard work makes muscles more tired. They need rest and water.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that tired muscles need rest and water._

_Luisa does not move her foot._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what to say to a tired friend  
> _Luisa is tired, but she is afraid to stop. What can we say?_  
> - ✅ Rest. I will stay with you → Yes! A friend who stays gives a good rest.
> - Work harder → That would make her more tired. “Rest, I will stay” is kinder.
> - Go away → That would make her feel alone. “Rest, I will stay” is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being kind to a tired friend._

_Your Nubbin snores, very softly._  
**Luisa**: Before Tío Bruno went away, he saw something about the house.  
**Luisa**: Nobody talks about it. It is still in his room.

> - A bird → Not a bird. A butterfly begins as a caterpillar.

> _For grown-ups: Learned to drink water and rest after hard work._

> - Pounce even harder → Hard pouncing can hurt. Ask first, then play gently.
> - Run away → Running away is not asking. A kind question comes first.
> _For grown-ups: Practised asking a friend before playing, so play stays kind._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): noticing an uneasy feeling and telling a trusted grown-up  
> _Your tummy feels funny near Scar. What can you do?_  
> - ✅ Tell a grown-up you trust → Yes. A funny tummy is a clue. A trusted grown-up can help.
> - Pretend it is nothing → Better to listen to that funny feeling. Tell someone you trust.
> _For grown-ups: Practised noticing an uneasy feeling and deciding to tell a trusted adult._

> **Lesson** (science, K-PS3-1, ask): shade is cooler because something blocks the sun  
> _The ledge is cool and shady. Why?_  
> - ✅ The rock blocks the sunlight → Yes. When something blocks the light, we get shade, and shade is cooler.
> - The sun is asleep → The sun is still up. The rock is in the way, so it is shady.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that shade happens when something blocks sunlight, and it is cooler._

_Simba’s eyes go round and shiny._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): tell a trusted adult about a secret that makes you uneasy  
> _Scar says: “Keep it secret from your dad.”_  
> _What is the wise thing to do?_  
> - ✅ Tell a grown-up you trust → Yes. A secret that gives you a funny tummy is one to tell.
> - Keep it secret → Careful. Secrets that make us uneasy should be told to a trusted grown-up.

> - Bigger → Look again. Mufasa’s print is bigger than all of Simba. Simba’s is smaller.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two sizes using bigger and smaller._

**Mufasa**: Simba, you did not listen. That was not safe.

#### `a23-09-chase`

_The page turns to a gorge. A gorge is a deep, rocky valley._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): it is okay to be very sad; what helps  
> _When someone we love dies, we feel very sad. That is okay._  
> _A hug helps. So does crying, telling someone, and sitting together._  
> _Sad feelings get easier to carry when someone is beside us._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard plainly that a death makes us sad, that sad is okay, and that company helps._

_Zazu has bumped his wing on the rocks. You scoop him up and follow._

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, ask): plant parts help the plant survive  
> _Why do some plants have thorns?_  
> - ✅ To stop animals eating them → Yes! Thorns are a plant’s way of saying “please don’t nibble me”.
> - To look pretty → They do look sharp, not pretty. Thorns help plants stay safe.
> - To catch the rain → Rain falls on leaves, not thorns. Thorns keep nibblers away.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that thorns protect plants from being eaten._

_Beyond the thorns there is only dry sand._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): making a hard choice between two kind things  
> _Both choices are kind. What helps when it is hard to choose?_  
> - ✅ Stop, breathe, and think who needs you most → Yes. A slow breath and a think help us choose well.
> - Pick without thinking → Quick picks can be fine, but a big choice deserves a slow think.
> _For grown-ups: Practised pausing to think when choosing between two kind options._

## A23-13. The Wind

- `a23-13-s1`: Get through the night after Nala’s news. · _Keep going. Stay with whoever needs you most tonight._
- `a23-13-s2`: Watch where the wind goes. · _Keep still, and follow the dust with your eyes._

#### `a23-13-ridge`

_Simba climbs a bare ridge. You climb after him._  
_The sky is huge. Every star is out._  
**Simba**: My dad died. I think it was my fault.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): comforting someone who blames themselves  
> _Simba thinks it was his fault. What can you tell him?_  
> - ✅ It was not your fault → Yes. Simba was only a cub, and it was not his fault. Hearing that helps.
> - It was your fault → No. It was not Simba’s fault. He was only a cub.
> - Do not be sad → Telling someone not to be sad does not work. Telling them the truth, kindly, does.
> _For grown-ups: Practised comforting someone who blames themselves for something that was not their fault._

_He throws himself down on the ridge with a thump._  

**Choices**

- **Sit down next to him and wait.**
    - You sit beside him. He does not tell you to go.
- **Tell him it was not his fault.**
    - He says you did not see. That is true.
    - You say it anyway.

#### `a23-13-ridge-done`

_A puff of dust and fur lifts from the ridge._  
_The wind catches it._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): wind pushes light things  
> _Wind pushes light things: dust, leaves, feathers and fur._  
> _Heavy things, like stones, stay where they are._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that wind moves light things but not heavy ones._


#### `a23-13-wind`

_First the green place. Then the desert._  
_Last, the home plain._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): follow places in order on a journey  
> _The fur floats over the green place, then the desert, then the home plain._  
> _Which place is last?_  
> - ✅ The home plain → Yes. The green place first, the desert next, the home plain last.
> - The desert → The desert comes in the middle. The home plain is last.
> _For grown-ups: Put places in order on a journey: first, next, last._

_Your Nubbin watches until it is only a dot._  
**Simba**: What are you looking at?  
_The wind smells of dust and, faintly, of home._  

**Choices**

## A23-14. Look Harder

- `a23-14-s1`: Watch Rafiki find Simba in the green place. · _Stay back among the ferns. Rafiki has his own way of doing this._
- `a23-14-s2`: Follow Rafiki through the roots to the still pool. · _Keep up with him. Duck under the roots and listen for his stick._

#### `a23-14-find`

_In the morning, Simba sits alone by the trees._  
_Rafiki walks up and sits down beside him._  
_He says nothing at all._  
**Simba**: What do you want?  
**Rafiki**: Nothing. I am sitting.  
**Rafiki**: You can sit too.  
_Simba moves away. Rafiki moves too, and sits again._  
**Rafiki**: I am not following you. I am sitting next to you.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): sitting beside someone helps them feel less alone  
> _Rafiki just sits beside Simba. How does that help?_  
> - ✅ Simba feels less alone → Yes. Sitting beside someone, even quietly, tells them they are not alone.
> - It does not help → It does! Being near a kind friend helps a sad feeling.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that quiet company helps someone feel less alone._


**Choices**

- **Stay back in the ferns.**
    - You stay where you are. This one is not yours to do.
- **Let your Nubbin go and sit with them too.**
    - It sits on Simba’s other side. He gives up and stays.

#### `a23-14-find-done`

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): above and below  
> _Rafiki goes under the root. Is he above the root or below it?_  
> - ✅ Below it → Yes! Under means below. He ducks beneath the root.
> - Above it → Above means on top. Under means below.
> _For grown-ups: Used the position words above and below._

_Simba goes after him. So do you._  

#### `a23-14-pool`

_The trees open on a small round pool._  
_The water is perfectly still._  
**Rafiki**: Look down. Into the water.

_Rafiki touches the water. Ripples spread out in circles._

**Rafiki**: You carry him with you, in your memory.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): we can remember people we love after they have died  
> _When someone we love has died, we can still remember them._  
> _We can say their name, tell stories, and look at pictures._  
> _That keeps them close._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that we can keep someone we love close by remembering them._

_Your Nubbin sees only itself, with a red mark on its brow._  

**Choices**

- **Look into the pool yourself.**
    - You see your face, and a grey sky moving fast.
- **Keep watching Simba.**
    - Simba holds his breath. He does not want the water to move.

#### `a23-14-clouds`

_A wind comes. The clouds pile up and turn._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): clouds are made of tiny drops of water  
> _Clouds are made of tiny drops of water, floating high in the sky._  
> _Wind can push them into big shapes._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that clouds are made of tiny drops of water._

_A great shape comes out of the cloud. It looks like a lion._  
**Simba**: Father?

**Mufasa**: One sad day is not all of you.  
**Mufasa**: Go home, my son. People who love you are waiting.  
_Then the clouds are only clouds._  

#### `a23-14-clouds-done`

_Simba stands still in the wind._  
_Rafiki does not hurry him._

_Behind them, the little pool lies calm and round._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): name a circle  
> _The pool is round. Which shape is round?_  
> - ✅ A circle → Yes! A circle is round, with no corners.
> - A square → A square has four corners. The round pool is a circle.
> - A triangle → A triangle has three corners. The round pool is a circle.
> _For grown-ups: Named the circle as the shape of the round pool._

> - Turn blue → Grass does not turn blue. With water it grows green.

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, ask): sound can bounce back as an echo  
> _The roar bounced off the hills and came back. What is that called?_  
> - ✅ An echo → Yes! An echo is a sound that bounces back. Try it in a big room!
> - A shadow → A shadow is made by light. A sound that bounces back is an echo.
> - A rainbow → A rainbow is made by light and rain. A sound that comes back is an echo.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sound that bounces back is an echo._

## A24-3. Baloo’s Lessons

- `a24-03-s1`: Join Mowgli at Baloo’s lessons. · _The glade is by the fallen tree. Bring your Nubbin._
- `a24-03-s2`: Learn the Master Words from Baloo. · _Say them slowly, in the right voice._
- `a24-03-s3`: Practise the calls with Baloo. · _Growl for hunters. Whistle for birds. Hiss for snakes._

#### `a24-03-glade`

_Time passes. Mowgli is seven now._  
_He is quick and brown._  
_Baloo sits on a fallen tree with his eyes half shut._  
**Baloo**: Sit down, all three of you. The Law is old, and long.  
**Mowgli**: I am bored. You have taught me for ever!  
**Baloo**: I am a sloth bear. I love ants, fruit and honey!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): a sloth bear eats ants, fruit and honey  
> **Baloo**: I am a sloth bear.  
> **Baloo**: What do I like to eat: ants and honey, or pizza?  
> - ✅ Ants and honey. → Yes! Sloth bears dig for ants and love honey.
> - Pizza. → Ha! No pizza in the jungle. Ants and honey for me!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a sloth bear digs for ants and loves honey and fruit._

**Baloo**: Be polite to the bees. Say sorry to a bat you wake.  
_Your Nubbin looks at Baloo, the bees and the bat. Its eyes cross!_  

**Choices**

- **Listen hard and say each one back.**
    - **Baloo**: A guest who listens. Good!
- **Whisper to Mowgli that you are bored too.**
    - **Baloo**: I heard that. Bears hear everything.

#### `a24-03-glade-done`

**Baloo**: First, the Strangers’ Call. You give it before you hunt on someone’s land.  
**Baloo**: It means: may I, please?  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): asking first shows respect  
> _Baloo says: ask first._  
> _What do you do before you go into a friend’s house?_  
> - ✅ Ask first. → Yes! Asking first is polite.
> - Run in without a word. → We ask first. It shows we care.
> _For grown-ups: Understood that asking before using someone else’s space shows respect._

**Mowgli**: Why ask? I am hungry!  
_Your Nubbin tiptoes politely across the glade._  

#### `a24-03-words`

**Baloo**: Now the Master Words. They matter most of all.  
**Baloo**: Say them for the hunters. Say them for the birds.  
**Baloo**: Say them for the snakes.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clapping the syllables of a name  
> _Clap the parts of the bear’s name. Ba-loo._  
> _How many claps? Two!_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:baloo`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the two syllables of Baloo._

_Mowgli gabbles them. Baloo gives a gentle cuff._  
**Mowgli**: Ow! You always hit me!  
**Mowgli**: I hate you!  
**Bagheera**: He wants you safe, little brother.  
**Baloo**: You and I are family, all of us, under the same sky.  
_That is the Master Word. Say it with a growl, a whistle, a hiss._  

**Choices**

- **Say the words slowly.**
    - You say them in a deep voice. Baloo closes his eyes.
    - That is praise.
- **Ask Baloo why the words work.**
    - **Baloo**: Because everyone keeps them. That is what a law is.
- **Sit beside Mowgli.**
    - You sit and say nothing. Soon Mowgli stops sulking.

#### `a24-03-words-done`

_Your Nubbin puffs up. It gives a small hiss._  
**Baloo**: That is not wrong! The snakes might like that.  
**Mowgli**: Baloo hit me. Then he praised Nubbin.  
**Mowgli**: It is not fair.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): saying “I feel cross” in words  
> _Mowgli is cross. What could he say to Baloo with words?_  
> - ✅ “I feel cross. That hurt.” → Yes! Telling someone how we feel helps.
> - “I hate you!” → That can hurt. “I feel cross” is kinder and clearer.
> _For grown-ups: Practised using words to say “I feel cross” instead of shouting something hurtful._


#### `a24-03-calls`

**Baloo**: Now we practise. I am the jungle!  
_Baloo hides behind a bush._  
_He is a bad bird, a bad snake, a bear._  
**Mowgli**: He is the worst bird in the world!  
_Your Nubbin hisses at the bear and growls at the bird._  
**Baloo**: Growl. Whistle.  
**Baloo**: Hiss. Growl.  
**Baloo**: Whistle. Hiss.  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): patterns: growl, whistle, hiss, growl, whistle, ...  
> **Baloo**: Growl, whistle, hiss, growl, whistle... what comes next?  
> - ✅ Hiss. → Yes! The pattern goes round and round.
> - Growl. → Listen again: growl, whistle, hiss. Next is hiss.
> _For grown-ups: Found the next item in a repeating pattern._


#### `a24-03-calls-done`

**Baloo**: Enough. The cub knows it.  
**Baloo**: The guest is learning.  
_Your Nubbin hisses at a stick insect. The insect does not move._  
**Baloo**: A snake has no ears you can see.  
**Baloo**: It feels your feet on the ground.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): snakes feel the ground through their bodies  
> _Snakes have no ears you can see. How do they feel footsteps?_  
> - ✅ Through the ground. → Yes! A snake feels the ground wiggle.
> - Through its tail feathers. → Snakes have no feathers! They feel the ground.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snakes feel footsteps through the ground._


#### `a24-03-complete`

_Baloo lies back with a happy grunt._  
**Baloo**: The Law is like a creeper on a tree. It holds things up.  
_A creeper is a plant that climbs a tree._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, L.2.4, ask): a new word: creeper (a climbing plant)  
> _A creeper is a plant that climbs up a tree._  
> _What does a creeper do?_  
> - ✅ Climbs. → Yes! A creeper climbs and holds on.
> - Swims. → No. A creeper climbs up trees.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a creeper is a plant that climbs._

**Mowgli**: Can I go now?  
**Baloo**: Go. But stay away from the Monkey-People!  
_Mowgli looks away fast._  

## A24-4. The Monkey-People

- `a24-04-s1`: Look for Mowgli under the trees. · _Follow the chattering. Monkeys are never quiet._
- `a24-04-s2`: Watch for Chil the kite. · _Look up! Chil circles in the sky._
- `a24-04-s3`: Go with Baloo and Bagheera to find Kaa. · _Kaa is on a warm ledge. Speak politely._

#### `a24-04-trees`

_Mowgli rests on Bagheera’s back in the warm sun._  
**Mowgli**: The monkeys are nice to me. They give me nuts!  
**Baloo**: The Monkey-People forget everything. Do not trust them.  
_Mowgli goes red. He stomps away to sulk under a tree._  
_Above him, the leaves whisper. Many grey hands reach down!_  
**Bandar-log**: Hoo hoo! Look how clever we are!  
**Bandar-log**: Ooh, a nut!  
_The monkeys swing up into the trees with Mowgli._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): monkeys live together in groups  
> _Monkeys live together in a big group. Do monkeys live alone, or together?_  
> - ✅ Together. → Yes! A group of monkeys is called a troop.
> - Alone. → Not alone! Monkeys live together, in a troop.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that monkeys live together in groups called troops._

**Mowgli**: Baloo! Bagheera!  

**Choices**

- **Shout for Baloo and Bagheera.**
    - They run! Baloo runs like a rolling rock.
    - Bagheera runs like a shadow.
- **Run underneath and keep watching.**
    - You run. Your Nubbin watches the treetops.
    - Bonk! It walks into a tree.

#### `a24-04-trees-done`

_The monkeys swing along the treetops. They are high and fast._  
_Below, nobody can keep up._  
_Up in the sky, a kite is circling. It sees everything._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): a view from above is like a map  
> _A kite flies high in the sky._  
> _Who can see more: a kite up high, or a mouse on the ground?_  
> - ✅ The kite. → Yes! From high up you see the whole place, like a map.
> - The mouse. → The mouse sees only a little. The kite sees much more.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a view from high above shows the whole place, like a map._


#### `a24-04-chil`

_Mowgli whistles the bird word._  
_High above, Chil the kite tips his wing and swoops down._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, ask): birds have wings to fly  
> _Chil has big wings. What does Chil use to fly?_  
> - ✅ His wings. → Yes! Wings help birds fly high.
> - His tummy. → Wings are for flying! Chil flaps and glides.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that birds use their wings to fly._

**Chil**: You are not a bird. But you know the word!  
**Mowgli**: Watch where they take me! Tell Baloo and Bagheera!  
_Chil swings away, high up into the blue. He keeps watching._  
**Chil**: They have taken him to the old city on the hill.  

**Choices**

- **Thank Chil with the bird whistle.**
    - **Chil**: You whistle like a duck. But you whistle!
- **Turn to Baloo. What now?**
    - **Baloo**: Now I think. Bears think slowly, but all the way down.

#### `a24-04-chil-done`

**Bagheera**: The old city. They are not afraid of us there.  
**Baloo**: They are afraid of one friend. Kaa the snake.  
_(Count who is running to find Kaa: Baloo, Bagheera, you, Nubbin.)_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4  
> _Count the runners on your fingers. Baloo, Bagheera, you, Nubbin._  
> _How many? Four!_  
> Check: `edu:count:runners:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four runners._


#### `a24-04-kaa`

_Kaa lies on a warm ledge in the sun. He has a new skin!_  
**Kaa**: Well, well. Visitors.  
**Kaa**: What brings you here?  
**Bagheera**: The monkeys have taken our man’s cub.  
**Kaa**: Have they.  
_Kaa goes very still. Every monkey in the jungle knows that stillness._  
**Kaa**: The monkeys have been very foolish.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds: K for Kaa and kite  
> _Kaa begins with a sound: k, k, k._  
> _Which begins like Kaa: kite or bear?_  
> - ✅ Kite. → Yes! Kaa, kite: k, k, k!
> - Bear. → Bear begins with b. Kaa and kite begin with k!
> _For grown-ups: Heard the first sound k in Kaa and kite._


**Choices**

- **Say his new skin looks lovely.**
    - **Kaa**: It does! Thank you.
    - **Kaa**: Nobody notices.
- **Keep your Nubbin behind you.**
    - **Kaa**: Wise little guest.

#### `a24-04-kaa-done`

**Kaa**: I will come by my own road. Do not wait.  
_He slides off the ledge. The grass does not even move._  
_On the warm stone lies Kaa’s old skin. It is long and papery._  

> **Lesson** (science, 3-LS1-1, ask): snakes shed their skin as they grow  
> _Kaa left his old skin on the stone. Why?_  
> _Because he grew bigger, or because he was bored?_  
> - ✅ He grew bigger. → Yes! Snakes grow, and slip out of the old skin.
> - He was bored. → Not bored! Snakes grow bigger, so they get a new skin.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snakes shed their skin because they grow._


#### `a24-04-complete`

_You run all afternoon with Baloo and Bagheera._  
**Baloo**: I should have watched him better.  
**Bagheera**: You taught him the Words. He used them.  
**Bagheera**: That was you!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): when something goes wrong it is not all your fault; kind words help  
> _Baloo feels sorry. Bagheera says it was not all his fault._  
> _What helps when we feel bad?_  
> - ✅ A kind word from a friend. → Yes! Kind words help us feel better.
> - Being told off again. → That would make it worse. A kind word helps most.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how kind words from a friend help when we feel sorry about something._

_Your Nubbin rides on Baloo’s back for the last mile._  
_Baloo lets it. He is a gentle bear._  

## A24-5. The Cold Lairs

- `a24-05-s1`: Creep into the old city and find Mowgli. · _Keep to the shadows of the broken walls._
- `a24-05-s2`: Watch while Bagheera and Baloo come in. · _Keep your Nubbin close._
- `a24-05-s3`: Get your Nubbin out of the old city. · _Cover your Nubbin’s eyes. Follow Mowgli out._

#### `a24-05-cistern`

_The Cold Lairs is a lost city on a hill._  
_It is full of ruins._  
_Kings built it long ago. Nobody remembers which kings._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): old places tell us about long ago  
> _The ruined city is very, very old._  
> _Which is old: a ruined city, or a new toy?_  
> - ✅ The ruined city. → Yes! Old places tell us about long ago.
> - The new toy. → A new toy is new! The ruined city is old.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that old buildings and ruins tell us about the past._

**Bandar-log**: We are great! We have a man’s cub!  
**Bandar-log**: Ooh, a nut!  
_They drop Mowgli through the roof of a little house._  
_Inside, cobras! They spread their wide hoods._  
**Mowgli**: You and I are family, all of us, under the same sky.  
_The cobras lower their hoods. Mowgli is safe._  

**Choices**

- **Wave to Mowgli through the window.**
    - **Mowgli**: You came! Is Baloo cross?
- **Stay hidden and watch for Bagheera.**
    - A black shape moves along the wall. Slow, like a cloud.

#### `a24-05-cistern-done`

**Mowgli**: The snakes are fine. I said the Words.  
_The cobras sway softly. A spread hood says: keep back._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): if you see a wild snake: stay calm, step back, tell a grown-up  
> _If you ever see a wild snake, what should you do?_  
> - ✅ Stand still, step back, tell a grown-up. → Yes! Step back slowly and tell a grown-up.
> - Pick it up. → No! Never touch a wild snake. Tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Practised what to do if you see a wild snake: stay calm, step back and tell a grown-up._

_Outside, the moon hides behind a cloud._  

#### `a24-05-fight`

_Bagheera runs up the terrace. Monkeys tumble like skittles!_  
**Bagheera**: Get to the water!  
**Baloo**: I am coming! There are too many!  
_Then thump, thump, the wall shakes. Stones fall in._  
_Through the gap comes Kaa!_  
**Bandar-log**: Kaa! Run!  
**Bandar-log**: Run!  
_The monkeys scatter. Four little ones run past you._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): take away: 4 monkeys, 2 go up the wall, how many are left?  
> _Four monkeys run. Two go up the wall._  
> _The rest run to the trees. How many is that?_  
> - ✅ 2. → Yes! Four take away two leaves two.
> - 4. → Two went up the wall. Four take away two leaves two.
> _For grown-ups: Subtracted 2 from 4 with a story._


**Choices**

- **Cheer quietly behind your hand.**
    - You cheer. Your Nubbin cheers with both hands over its eyes.
- **Kick open the door for Mowgli.**
    - The door gives way. Mowgli climbs out, dusty and safe.

#### `a24-05-fight-done`

_Bagheera climbs out of the water, dripping. He shakes himself._  
_Baloo sits down very suddenly._  
**Baloo**: I am not hurt. I am old.  
**Baloo**: It is different.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): saying what you need when you are tired  
> _Baloo is tired, but he does not say so. What could Baloo say?_  
> - ✅ “I need a rest.” → Yes! Saying it helps friends help us.
> - Nothing at all. → If we say nothing, nobody knows. Saying it helps.
> _For grown-ups: Practised saying “I need a rest” to tell people what you need._


#### `a24-05-dance`

**Kaa**: Now stay, all of you. I will dance the Hunger Dance.  
_Kaa has no legs. He slides in slow loops, round and round._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, ask): snakes slide without legs  
> _Kaa has no legs._  
> _How does Kaa move: does he slide, or does he skip?_  
> - ✅ He slides. → Yes! A snake slides on its tummy.
> - He skips. → Snakes have no legs to skip! They slide.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snakes slide along on their bodies because they have no legs._

_The monkeys feel sleepy. They creep down from the walls._  
_Baloo and Bagheera step forward too, with dreamy eyes._  
**Mowgli**: Do not look! Come away!  
_Mowgli pulls them out. They shake themselves awake._  

**Choices**

- **Cover your Nubbin’s eyes and pick it up.**
    - You lift it with your hand over its eyes. It feels safe.
- **Turn your Nubbin to face you.**
    - It looks at your face. You walk out backwards.

#### `a24-05-dance-done`

_Outside the walls, the moon is clean and bright._  
_Your Nubbin rubs its eyes. It feels shaky._  
_Breathe in slowly, through your nose. Breathe out, through your mouth._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, do): calming down with slow breaths  
> _Take three slow breaths with Nubbin. In, out._  
> _In, out. In, out._  
> _Better!_  
> Check: `edu:breathe:slow:3`
> _For grown-ups: Took three slow breaths to calm down after a scare._


#### `a24-05-complete`

**Bagheera**: You went with the monkeys. We had to come and get you.  
**Mowgli**: I am sorry. I was wrong.  
_Bagheera gives him a long, stern look. Then it is finished._  
**Bagheera**: Jump on my back. We are going home.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): saying sorry and making things right  
> _Mowgli said sorry. How can we make things right when we are sorry?_  
> - ✅ Say sorry and help put it right. → Yes! Sorry and helping puts things right.
> - Walk away and say nothing. → Saying sorry and helping is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about making things right: saying sorry and helping._

_Kaa nods slowly from the moonlit wall._  
**Kaa**: Come and see me, guest. My coils are very warm.  

## A24-6. The Red Flower

- `a24-06-s1`: Find Bagheera and Mowgli under the trees. · _Bagheera lies on a branch in the shade._
- `a24-06-s2`: Go to the village with Mowgli at dawn. · _Wait in the ditch. Mowgli goes in alone._
- `a24-06-s3`: Help Mowgli keep the fire alive. · _Bring dry twigs. Feed it a little at a time._

#### `a24-06-branch`

_Years pass. Mowgli is ten now._  
_He has never lived in a house._  
_Akela is old. Shere Khan has made friends with the young wolves._  

> **Lesson** (science, 3-LS3-1, ask): a black panther is a leopard with dark fur  
> _Bagheera is a black panther: a leopard with dark fur._  
> _What colour is his fur?_  
> - ✅ Black. → Yes! Black as ink. In the sun you can see spots.
> - Pink. → Not pink! Bagheera is black.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a black panther is a leopard, a big cat, with very dark fur._

_Bagheera lies on a branch. His fur is black as ink._  
**Bagheera**: Little brother, Shere Khan has not forgotten you.  
**Bagheera**: Men keep a thing in their huts. The Red Flower.  
**Bagheera**: Fire.  
**Mowgli**: They are my brothers. Why would they want me gone?  

**Choices**

- **Ask Bagheera what Mowgli should do.**
    - **Bagheera**: Fetch the Red Flower, little brother.
- **Look at Mowgli. He is very quiet.**
    - **Bagheera**: Be ready for them, little brother.

#### `a24-06-branch-done`

**Mowgli**: I know where the Red Flower is. I will go now.  
**Bagheera**: Take the guest. Guests are good at carrying things.  
_Long ago, people learned to use fire. It gave them warmth and light._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): people long ago used fire for warmth and light  
> _Long ago, fire helped people._  
> _What does fire give us: warmth, or a cold wind?_  
> - ✅ Warmth and light. → Yes! Fire gives warmth and light.
> - A cold wind. → No! Fire is warm and bright.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that long ago people used fire for warmth and light._


#### `a24-06-pot`

_You lie in a ditch at the edge of the village._  
_It is nearly dawn._  
_A woman puts a clay pot of glowing coals by her door._  
_She goes back in. Mowgli darts out and takes it!_  
**Mowgli**: She looks like me. They all look like me.  
**Villager**: My fire-pot! Where is my fire?  
_The woman looks sad. She has a cold breakfast._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): asking first before taking something  
> _Mowgli took the pot without asking._  
> _What should we do first when we want something?_  
> - ✅ Ask first. → Yes! Asking first is kind.
> - Just take it. → The woman felt sad. Asking first is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about asking before taking something, and how it feels for the person._


**Choices**

- **Leave something on the step.**
    - You leave a smooth stone with a hole. It is a thank-you.
- **Run after Mowgli with the pot.**
    - A neighbour shares her fire with the woman. It is a kind village.

#### `a24-06-pot-done`

_Back in the jungle, Mowgli puts the pot on a flat stone._  
**Mowgli**: If I do not feed it, it will die. Fire eats sticks.  
_Under the ash, a few coals glow red._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): fire needs wood to burn  
> _A fire needs food. What does a fire eat: dry sticks, or water?_  
> - ✅ Dry sticks. → Yes! Fire burns wood. Water puts it out.
> - Water. → Water puts a fire out. Fire eats dry sticks.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a fire needs dry wood to burn, and that water puts it out._


#### `a24-06-feed`

_All day you and Mowgli feed the fire with dry twigs._  
**Mowgli**: Two sticks first. Then one more.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, do): add 2 and 1 to make 3  
> _Mowgli puts in two sticks, then one more. How many sticks is that?_  
> _Count: one, two, three!_  
> Check: `edu:count:sticks:3`
> _For grown-ups: Added 2 and 1 to make 3 sticks._

_Your Nubbin brings a twig. It is a beetle!_  
_It puts it back._  
**Mowgli**: It eats like a wolf cub. Always hungry!  
_A wolf passes and goes the long way round._  
**Mowgli**: He is scared of fire. I am not.  
**Mowgli**: Is that what being a man means?  

**Choices**

- **Tell him you do not know. You are still learning.**
    - **Mowgli**: Good. I like people who still learn.
- **Show him how to blow gently.**
    - The coals glow like a cat’s eyes. Mowgli laughs.

#### `a24-06-feed-done`

_By evening the fire glows steadily._  
_Tabaqui slinks into the clearing, grinning._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): a word for a sneaky walk: slink  
> _Tabaqui slinks. Slinking is a sneaky, quiet walk._  
> _Which is sneaky: slink or stomp?_  
> - ✅ Slink. → Yes! Slink, slink, slink. Show me a sneaky walk!
> - Stomp. → Stomping is loud! Slinking is quiet and sneaky.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that “slink” is a word for a sneaky, quiet way of walking._

**Tabaqui**: The young wolves want Mowgli at the Council Rock. All of them!  

#### `a24-06-complete`

**Bagheera**: Akela missed his hunt tonight.  
**Mowgli**: Then I will go to the Council. With this.  
_He lifts the pot. It lights his face from below._  
**Bagheera**: Stay near him, guest.  
_Fire is useful, and it is serious. Matches are for grown-ups._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): fire safety: leave matches alone and tell a grown-up  
> _If you find matches at home, what should you do?_  
> - ✅ Leave them and tell a grown-up. → Yes! Matches are for grown-ups.
> - Play with them. → No! Fire can be dangerous. Tell a grown-up.
> _For grown-ups: Practised fire safety: leaving matches alone and telling a grown-up._


## A24-7. The Council of Fire

- `a24-07-s1`: Go up to the Council Rock with Mowgli and the fire. · _Keep the pot steady. Sit at the edge._
- `a24-07-s2`: Sit with Mowgli on the rock. · _Sit beside him. You do not need to talk._

#### `a24-07-council`

_Akela lies beside his rock tonight. He is old and tired._  
_Shere Khan walks up and down. The young wolves listen to him._  
**Shere Khan**: Give me the man’s cub!  
**Akela**: Mowgli has been good to us. Please leave him alone.  
_Mowgli stands up with the fire-pot. He tips it out._  
**Mowgli**: Men carry this. So I brought some!  
_The coals light the dry moss. Whoosh!_  
_A bright flame!_  
_The wolves feel the heat. They scramble back, ears flat._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): we feel heat from a fire  
> _The wolves feel the fire before they touch it._  
> _What do we feel from a fire?_  
> - ✅ Heat. → Yes! A fire is hot. We keep back.

## A24-9. Tiger! Tiger!

> _Does it run fast here, or slow?_  
> - ✅ Slow. → Yes! Where a river spreads out, it slows down. That is why we cross here.
> - Fast. → Squeezed into a narrow gap, it runs fast. Spread out wide, it runs slow.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a wide, shallow river flows more slowly._

## A24-12. The Water Truce

- `a24-12-s1`: Walk down the dry river with Mowgli and Baloo. · _Follow the riverbed. Water is left at the Peace Rock._

- `a24-12-s3`: Let your Nubbin drink at the pool. · _Set it down on the bank. It will find a place._

#### `a24-12-dry`

_A year comes when the rain does not. Everything goes brown and dry._

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): plants and animals need water; elephants can dig for it  
> _It has not rained for a long time._  
> _What do plants and animals need to live?_  
> - ✅ Water. → Yes! Every living thing needs water. Hathi digs for it.
> - Sweets. → Sweets are nice! But water is what they need.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants and animals need water to live, and that elephants can dig for it in a dry river._

> - Hot. → It is very cold in the north.

**Matkah**: Oh, look! Our baby is white!

#### `a24-18-search`

**Sea Vitch**: Go away! I was asleep.

> - Boat. → Boat begins with b. Sea and seal begin with s!
> _For grown-ups: Heard the first sound s in sea and seal._

## A26-1. The Wall

#### `a26-01-page`

_Nova’s book falls open. A great brick wall shines in the sun._

**Old Brickmaker**: A river runs beside it. People made their homes near the water.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): a city can sit beside a river, in a place on the map  
> _(Look at the river on the page.) Where is Uruk?_  
> - ✅ Beside a river → Yes! Uruk is beside a river. Water is good for drinking and for growing food.
> - Up on the moon → Not quite! Uruk is on the ground, beside a river. Look at the water.
> - In the middle of the sea → Not quite! It is beside a river, with land all around.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Uruk stood beside a river, in the land that is now Iraq._


**Choices**

    - **Old Brickmaker**: You knock it. A good brick rings!

#### `a26-02-games`

_In the big square, young men run races and carry stones._  
_Nobody looks happy. They look very, very tired._  
**Gilgamesh**: Again! Faster!

_This is Gilgamesh, king of Uruk._

> _What does the tired boy need?_  
> - ✅ A drink and a rest → Yes! Bodies need water and rest to feel better.
> - Another race → Oh no! He needs a rest first. Bodies get tired when they run and run.
> - Nothing at all → He needs something! A drink and a rest help a tired body.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about water and rest as things a tired body needs._


**Choices**

    - You carry him a cup. He drinks it all and smiles.

#### `a26-02-games-done`

_The king does not see. He starts another race._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): noticing how kindness makes someone feel  
> _The boy’s mum smiles at you. How does she feel?_  
> - ✅ Thankful → Yes! She feels thankful. A kind act made her feel warm inside.
> - Cross → Look at her smile. She feels thankful, because you were kind.
> - Sleepy → She might be sleepy! But her smile says she feels thankful.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that being kind helps others feel thankful and cared for._


#### `a26-02-clay`

_She picks up a little wet clay and rolls it in her palms._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): clay is soft when wet and hard when it dries  
> _Wet clay is soft and squishy. What happens when clay dries in the sun?_  
> - ✅ It gets hard → Yes! Clay gets hard when it dries. That is why people made bricks from it.
> - It turns into water → Not quite! Dry clay does not turn into water. It gets hard.
> - It grows legs → Ha! No legs. Dry clay just gets hard.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that clay is soft when wet and hardens as it dries._

_Then she drops it gently, far away in the wild grass._
