- `a26-04-s3`: Bring your Nubbin back from the herd. · _Go slowly. Let your Nubbin come to you._

#### `a26-04-road`

_The trapper comes back with a woman from the city._  
**Shamhat**: Hello! I am Shamhat.  
**Shamhat**: I teach people words and songs.  
_You carry her bundle. It smells of bread and sweet oil._  
_Inside there are two flat loaves and three dates._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add two groups to make five  
> _Two loaves and three dates. How many foods in all?_  
> - ✅ Five → Yes! Two and three make five. Count them: one, two, three, four, five.
> - Four → Let us count together: two loaves, then three dates. One, two, three, four, five. Five!
> - Six → Let us count together: one, two, three, four, five. Five!
> _For grown-ups: Added two and three to make five._

**Shamhat**: I do not want to boss him. I want to be his friend.  

**Choices**

- **Ask how she will do it.**
    - **Shamhat**: I will sit where he can see me, and wait.
- **Tell her your Nubbin ran off with the herd.**
    - **Shamhat**: Then we have the same job, you and I.

#### `a26-04-sit`

_Shamhat sits on a flat rock by the water._  
_You sit a little way off._  
_On the first day, Enkidu peeks from behind a gazelle._  
_On the second day, he comes closer and sniffs the bread._  
**Shamhat**: This is bread. This is my hand.  
**Shamhat**: That is yours.  
_By the fourth day, he sits across from her._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): waiting patiently helps a friend feel safe  
> _Shamhat does not chase Enkidu. She sits and waits._  
> _Why does waiting help?_  
> - ✅ He feels safe and comes when he is ready → Yes! Waiting kindly helps a friend feel safe.
> - Waiting does nothing → Look what happened! Waiting helped him feel safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why patient waiting helps someone feel safe._

**Enkidu**: Hand.  
**Shamhat**: Yes! Hand!  
**Shamhat**: And what is your name?  
**Enkidu**: Enkidu.  

#### `a26-04-sit-done`

_He says it again, louder. Then he laughs a big laugh._  
**Shamhat**: There you are! I knew you were in there.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): words that start with the same sound: hand and hat  
> _Enkidu’s first word was “hand”. Which word starts the same: hat, sun or cup?_  
> - ✅ Hat → Yes! Hand, hat. Huh, huh, huh!
> - Sun → Sun starts with “s”. Hand starts with “h”, like hat.
> - Cup → Cup starts with “k”. Hand starts with “h”, like hat.
> _For grown-ups: Matched the first sound of “hand” with “hat”._


#### `a26-04-coax`

_Enkidu walks to the gazelles, the way he always has._  
_They lift their heads. They sniff._  
_Then they run away._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-2, ask): animals use their noses and eyes to tell who is who  
> _How do gazelles know who is who?_  
> - ✅ They use their noses and eyes → Yes! Animals sniff and look. Enkidu smells like a person now.
> - They read name tags → Ha! No name tags. They use their noses and eyes.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that animals use senses like smell and sight to know each other._

**Enkidu**: Wait! It is me!  
_Your Nubbin has been left behind too. It sits alone in the grass._  
**Shamhat**: Go to yours. I will go to mine.  

**Choices**

- **Call its name.**
    - Your Nubbin thinks about it. Then it runs to you.
- **Sit down in the grass and wait.**
    - You wait. Then there is a warm weight against your side.
- **Hold out a date from the bundle.**
    - Your Nubbin comes for the date and stays for you.

#### `a26-04-coax-done`

_Enkidu sits with his head in his hands. Shamhat sits beside him._  
_She says nothing. After a while, he leans on her shoulder._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): what helps when we feel sad  
> _Enkidu is sad. What helps when we are sad?_  
> - ✅ A friend sitting close → Yes! Sitting close, with no words, can help a lot.
> - Being all alone → Sometimes we want a little quiet. But a friend nearby helps most.
> _For grown-ups: Named sadness and what helps: a friend sitting close._

**Enkidu**: Will it run away from me too?  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words that tell a feeling  
> _Enkidu’s voice is wobbly. Which word tells how he feels: sad, purple or round?_  
> - ✅ Sad → Yes! “Sad” is a feeling word.
> - Purple → Purple is a colour. “Sad” is the feeling word.
> - Round → Round is a shape. “Sad” is the feeling word.
> _For grown-ups: Picked out a word that names a feeling._

## A26-5. Bread and Barley

- `a26-05-s1`: Help the shepherds give Enkidu his first supper. · _Carry the bread and the jugs from the fire._
- `a26-05-s2`: Keep watch over the sheep with Enkidu at night. · _Take a lamp to the sheepfold and stay up with him._

#### `a26-05-bread`

_The shepherds’ camp is a ring of tents and a warm fire._  
**Shepherd**: Sit down, friend! You must be hungry.  
_You set down a round loaf and a jug of barley drink._  
**Enkidu**: What is this?  
**Shamhat**: That is bread. People eat it.  
**Shamhat**: Go on!  
_He takes a tiny bite. His eyebrows jump up._  
_He eats until he is full. Then he sings a song with no words._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): bread comes from a plant that grows grain  
> _Bread is made from flour. Flour is made from grain._  
> _Where does grain start?_  
> - ✅ A plant growing in a field → Yes! Grain grows on plants, in fields, with sun and water.
> - A cloud → Not quite! Grain grows on plants in a field.
> - A rock → Not quite! Grain grows on plants. Plants need sun and water.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that bread starts as a plant growing grain._


**Choices**

- **Clap along.**
    - You clap. The shepherds clap.
    - Your Nubbin hops in time.
- **Break your own loaf with your Nubbin.**
    - Enkidu watches. Then he shares his loaf too.

#### `a26-05-bread-done`

_Afterwards, the shepherds trim his hair. He washes in the stream._  
_He rubs oil on his skin. Shamhat gives him clothes._  
**Shepherd**: Look at him!  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): washing keeps us clean and healthy  
> _Enkidu washed in the stream. Why do we wash?_  
> - ✅ To get clean and stay healthy → Yes! Washing takes away dirt and germs.
> - To make the water dirty → Ha! The water does get dirty, but we wash to get clean.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about washing to stay clean and healthy._


#### `a26-05-night`

_That night the shepherds sleep. Enkidu keeps watch on the wall._  
_Stars shine over the sheepfold._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): stars shine at night  
> _The stars are out and it is dark. Is it day or night?_  
> - ✅ Night → Yes! We see stars at night.
> - Day → In the day the sun shines. Stars come out at night.
> _For grown-ups: Told night from day using stars._

**Enkidu**: I know the wolves. I used to drink beside them.  
_Shadows move at the edge of the grass._  
_Enkidu speaks to them, not in words. They turn and go._  
**Enkidu**: They know whose side I am on now.  

**Choices**

- **Hold the lamp up anyway.**
    - **Enkidu**: That is for the sheep, so they know someone is here.
- **Sit beside him on the wall.**
    - Your Nubbin climbs between you and falls asleep.

#### `a26-05-night-done`

_Five little lambs sleep safe in the fold._

> _For grown-ups: Counted five lambs._

_One morning a traveller walks by. He grumbles about the king who never rests._  
**Enkidu**: Someone should tell the king to stop.  
**Shamhat**: Someone should. Shall we go to the city?  
_Enkidu looks at the sheep, then at you. He nods._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): choosing a kind way to help  
> _Enkidu wants the king to stop. What is a good first step?_  
> - ✅ Go and talk to him → Yes! Talking first is a good start.
> - Shout from far away → Shouting from far away will not help. Talking face to face is better.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about a kind first step when something is unfair._


## A26-6. Ninsun’s Dreams

- `a26-06-s1`: Carry the cups to the queen mother’s hall. · _The palace steward needs help. Take the tray._
- `a26-06-s2`: Stay and hear what Ninsun says about the dreams. · _Stand by the fountain with the tray._

#### `a26-06-cups`

_The palace steward gives you a tray of silver cups._  
_There are five cups on the tray. They shine._  
_Ninsun’s hall is cool and quiet, with a fountain._  
**Gilgamesh**: Mother, I had a dream. A star fell from the sky.  
**Gilgamesh**: I could not lift it. But I loved it.  
_You hold out the tray._  
_He takes one cup and forgets to give it back._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): take one away from five  
> _There were five cups. Gilgamesh took one._  
> _How many are left on the tray?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! Five take away one leaves four.
> - Three → Let us count: one, two, three, four. Four cups are left.
> - Five → One cup is gone. Count the rest: one, two, three, four. Four!
> _For grown-ups: Took one away from five._


**Choices**

- **Wait with the tray until he has finished.**
    - Ninsun’s mouth turns up at the corner.
- **Offer Ninsun a cup too.**
    - **Ninsun**: Thank you. Someone remembers the rest of us drink as well.

#### `a26-06-cups-done`

**Ninsun**: Sit down, my son. You are walking up and down, up and down.  
_Gilgamesh sits at last._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): words that rhyme  
> _Down. Which word rhymes with down: town, cup or sun?_  
> - ✅ Town → Yes! Down, town. They rhyme!
> - Cup → Cup does not sound like down. Town does!
> - Sun → Sun does not sound like down. Town does!
> _For grown-ups: Found a rhyme for “down”._


#### `a26-06-meaning`

**Gilgamesh**: There was an axe in the street. I loved it too.  
**Ninsun**: The star and the axe are the same. They mean a friend.  
**Ninsun**: A friend is coming to you. He will stand beside you.  
**Gilgamesh**: A friend? I have a whole city.  
**Ninsun**: You have a city that is tired of you.  
_Gilgamesh opens his mouth. Then he shuts it again._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what makes a friend  
> _What is a friend?_  
> - ✅ Someone kind to you, and you to them → Yes! Friends are kind to each other.
> - Someone who does what you say → Not quite! A friend is kind, and listens too.
> - Anyone in a crowd → A crowd is lots of people. A friend is someone kind to you.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what makes a friend._


**Choices**

- **Tell him you think she is right.**
    - **Gilgamesh**: Do you? Hm.
    - **Gilgamesh**: You may have seen more of my city than I have.
- **Say nothing, and refill his cup.**
    - He looks at you as if he had just noticed you.

**Gilgamesh**: Stay new. Carry my cups.  
_That night the drum stops early. A thin moon hangs over Uruk._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): the Moon shines in the night sky  
> _A thin moon hangs in the dark sky._  
> _When do we often see the moon?_  
> - ✅ At night → Yes! We often see the moon at night, and the sun by day.
> - Only at lunchtime → The moon shines at night. The sun shines by day.
> _For grown-ups: Linked the Moon with the night sky._

> _Uruk and its road are beside a river. Why do people live by rivers?_  
> - ✅ For water to drink and to grow food → Yes! A river gives people water for drinking and for growing crops.
> - To hide from the sun → Not quite! People live by rivers for water to drink and to grow food.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people settle beside rivers for drinking water and farming._

    - **Enkidu**: Good. So am I.

> _Three people at the gate. Nine people in the square._  
> _Where are there more?_  
> - ✅ In the square → Yes! Nine is more than three.
> - At the gate → Count again: the gate has three. The square has nine. Nine is more!
> _For grown-ups: Compared three and nine to say which has more._

_Gilgamesh strides across the square to a big door._

> _The friends push and pull. What makes something move?_  
> - ✅ A push or a pull → Yes! A push or a pull can make things move, or stop.
> - Wishing very hard → Not quite! Things move when something pushes or pulls them.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that pushes and pulls make things move._

_Then he laughs, and Enkidu laughs too._  
_Enkidu holds out a hand, and the king takes it._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): making up after a quarrel  
> _They pushed, then they laughed. What helps friends after a quarrel?_  
> - ✅ Making up and being kind → Yes! Friends make up, and they are kind again.
> - Staying cross for ever → That would be a long time to be cross! Making up feels better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about making up with a friend after a quarrel._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): telling a friend when you feel scared  
> _Enkidu feels scared. What can he do with a scared feeling?_  
> - ✅ Tell a friend he is scared → Yes! Saying “I am scared” out loud can help.
> - Pretend nothing is wrong → Pretending can make a worry bigger. Telling a friend helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about saying out loud that you feel scared._

> - ✅ The big jug → Yes! The big jug holds more.
> - The little cup → Look again. The big jug is bigger, so it holds more.

**Enkidu**: If you go, I will go. Someone must bring you home.

> - They are bossy → They are being careful. Listening to them helps us stay safe.

## A26-9. Dreams on the Mountain

#### `a26-09-fire`

_Every evening the friends climb a hill. Then you make camp._  
_You gather brush and build a fire. Enkidu builds a little brush shelter._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a fire needs wood to keep burning  
> _A fire needs wood to keep burning._  
> _What should we add to keep it going?_  
> - ✅ More wood → Yes! Wood is the fuel. More wood keeps the fire going.
> - Water → Oh no! Water would put the fire out. We add wood.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a fire needs wood as fuel to keep burning._

_In the night Gilgamesh sits up with a start._  
**Gilgamesh**: I dreamed a mountain fell on me. I am cold all over.  
**Enkidu**: A good dream! The mountain will fall, and we will stand on it.

- **Build the fire up higher.**

- **Put your blanket over the king.**
    - He does not notice. In the morning he will think he dreamed it.

> - He is smiling → Look again: he is not smiling. His face looks worried.
> _For grown-ups: Read a friend’s feelings from a face._

## A26-10. Humbaba

> - Shouting loudly → Shouting can make the thumping faster. Slow breaths help more.
> _For grown-ups: Practised slow breaths to calm a scared feeling._

> - Say nothing, because I am not sure → That is all right too. It is hard to know what is right when you are scared.

## A26-11. Ishtar

- `a26-11-s1`: Fetch warm water for the king to wash. · _Heat water in the palace kitchen. Carry it to the king’s rooms._

#### `a26-11-wash`

_Back in Uruk, Gilgamesh asks for warm water._  
_You carry it up, jar after jar. The room fills with steam._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): hot water makes steam  
> _Hot water makes steam. Is steam hot or cold?_  
> - ✅ Hot → Yes! Steam is hot. Be careful of it.
> - Cold → Not quite! Steam comes from hot water, so it is hot.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that steam comes from hot water and is hot._

_He washes the forest out of his hair and puts on his crown._  
**Gilgamesh**: Do I look like a king who has made a name?  
**Enkidu**: You look like a king who has had a bath.  
_Then the light goes gold and strange. Your Nubbin’s fur stands up._  

**Choices**

- **Hand Enkidu a dry cloth.**
    - He holds it like a shield and peers at the gold light.
- **Put down the jar and stand by the door.**
    - Whoever is coming, you would like to be near the way out.

#### `a26-11-offer`

_The goddess Ishtar stands in the doorway, bright as the evening star._  
**Ishtar**: Gilgamesh, stay with me.

**Ishtar**: You will have everything you want.  
_Gilgamesh shakes his head._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Eco.1.K-2, ask): making a choice between yes and no  
> _Ishtar asks. Gilgamesh gets to decide yes or no._  
> _What do we call picking one thing?_  
> - ✅ A choice → Yes! Picking one thing is a choice.
> - A race → Not quite! Picking one thing is called a choice.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that picking one thing from several is making a choice._

**Gilgamesh**: Everyone you loved ended up sad. Why would I be different?  
**Ishtar**: You will be sorry.

    - You scoop it up. Her robe crackles past like summer lightning.

#### `a26-11-offer-done`

**Gilgamesh**: No. But it was true.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): telling the truth takes courage

> - ✅ Yes, it takes courage → Yes! Telling the truth can be hard, and brave.
> - No, it is easy → Sometimes it is easy and sometimes hard. When it is hard, it is brave.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about honesty as a brave thing._

#### `a26-12-bull`

> _How many children in all?_  
> - ✅ Six → Yes! Two, four, six.
> - Four → Count by twos: two, four, six. Six children!
> - Eight → Count by twos: two, four, six. Six children!
> _For grown-ups: Counted by twos to six._

> - Hiding all alone → Hiding alone can feel lonely. Holding hands helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when we feel scared._

> - Table → A table is a thing. “Whoosh” is the sound word.
> - Green → Green is a colour. “Whoosh” is the sound word.
> _For grown-ups: Picked out a sound word._

#### `a27-02-path`

_Two servants carry the baby in a basket. You follow._  
_The road becomes a path. The path goes up, up, up._  
_The wind blows. Rain falls: pitter, patter!_

> _Rain falls from clouds._  
> _What are clouds made of: tiny drops of water, or sand?_  
> - ✅ Tiny drops of water. → Yes! Lots of tiny drops, floating high up.
> - Sand. → Not sand. Clouds are tiny drops of water, floating high up.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that clouds are made of tiny drops of water, and rain falls from them._

_Your Nubbin holds the basket up from below._  

#### `a27-02-path-done`

_The storm is all around. You cannot see the city now._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, ask): count the three kinds of ground: road, path, stones  
> _First the road. Then the path._  
> _Then the stones. How many kinds of ground?_  
> - ✅ Three. → Yes! Road, path, stones. Three!
> - One. → Count again: road, path, stones. That makes three!
> _For grown-ups: Counted three kinds of ground on the journey._


#### `a27-02-rocks`

> _These are the Alborz, real mountains in Iran._  
> _Are mountains very high, or very low?_  
> - ✅ Very high. → Yes! Mountains are very high.
> - Very low. → Mountains are very high. Look how far up the path goes!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Alborz are real mountains in Iran._

_The old servant is sad. He does not want to leave._  
_He goes. You stay._  
_You and your Nubbin keep the baby warm._  

**Choices**

- **Wrap him in your coat.**
    - He stops crying. He is cross about the coat instead.
- **Hum to him.**
    - You hum. The wind is loud, but he hears.
    - He goes quiet.
- **Hold him, with your back to the wind.**
    - He fits against your chest. He is warm.

#### `a27-02-rocks-done`

_Above you, something very big flies over._  
_For a moment the rain stops, as if a roof had been put up._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, do): sound words: whoosh  
> _Big wings go whoosh! Say it with me: whoosh!_  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-word:whoosh`
> _For grown-ups: Said the sound word whoosh and linked it to what wings sound like._


#### `a27-02-complete`

_The shadow comes again. The wind bends the grass._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): holding a friend helps with a scared feeling  
> _You feel scared. What helps a scared feeling?_  
> - ✅ Hold a friend. → Yes. Being close to someone helps. You are not alone.
> - Hide alone. → Hiding alone can feel lonely. Holding a friend helps.
> _For grown-ups: Named a way to feel better when scared: staying close to someone._

_Then the cloud opens. Something comes down!_  

## A27-3. The Simurgh

- `a27-03-s1`: Hold on to the baby when the great bird comes down. · _Do not let go of the basket._
- `a27-03-s2`: Arrive at the nest on the peak. · _There is nothing to do but be carried._

#### `a27-03-descent`

_A bird comes out of the cloud. She is bigger than a house!_  
_Her feathers shine like a sunset. Her eye is gold._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): wings help birds fly  
> _The Simurgh has wings, a beak and claws._  
> _What do wings help a bird do?_  
> - ✅ Fly. → Yes! Wings help most birds fly.
> - Dig. → Not dig! Wings help most birds fly. Claws can grip.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that wings help birds fly._

_She lands on the rock. The rock creaks._  
_She lifts the baby gently._  
_Then she lifts you too, and your Nubbin._  

**Choices**

- **Shout.**
    - Whoosh! The wind takes your shout away.
- **Hold on, with your eyes open.**
    - Below, the mountain gets small. The storm is a grey floor.

#### `a27-03-descent-done`

_Up through the cloud, and out into the sun!_  
_The sky is big and blue and quiet._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count three clouds  
> _Look down at the clouds. (Count them with me: 1, 2, 3.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:clouds:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three clouds, one number for each._


#### `a27-03-nest`

_The nest sits on the very top of the mountain._  
_It is made of sweet-smelling wood, and it is as big as a cottage._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, ask): describing the colours in a painting  
> _Long ago, painters drew the Simurgh with bright colours and a long, swirly tail._  
> _Which colour would you choose for her? There is no wrong answer._  
> - Gold. → Gold shines like the sun.
> - Blue. → Blue is like the sky above the clouds.
> - Red. → Red glows like a sunset.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a colour for the Simurgh, as painters of old Persian books did._

_Four fluffy chicks crowd close. They are curious!_  
_Your Nubbin stands in front of the baby, arms wide._  
**The Simurgh**: No. Not him.  
**The Simurgh**: He is your brother.  

#### `a27-03-nest-done`

_The chicks pull their beaks back. The smallest sits down with a plop._  
**The Simurgh**: These two are your nestmates too. Make room!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): making room: sharing space with a newcomer  
> **The Simurgh**: What does it mean to make room for someone?  
> - ✅ Budge over and share. → Yes! Sharing space makes friends feel welcome.
> - Keep it all. → Sharing makes room for friends. Try budging over!
> _For grown-ups: Talked about making room for a newcomer, and welcoming someone by sharing._


#### `a27-03-complete`

_The chicks shuffle. A warm gap opens in the middle._  
_You, your Nubbin and the baby squeeze in._  
_A big wing comes down like a blanket._  
**The Simurgh**: Sleep. The storm cannot reach us here.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhymes: wing and sing  
> _Wing rhymes with sing. Which word rhymes with wing: sing or sun?_  
> - ✅ Sing. → Yes! Wing, sing, ring, king!
> - Sun. → Sun does not rhyme. Wing, sing, ring: they end the same!
> _For grown-ups: Practised rhyming: wing, sing, ring, king._

_The chick beside you snores. Snore, snore!_  

## A27-4. The Nest

- `a27-04-s1`: Help the Simurgh feed everyone in the nest. · _Chicks first, then the baby, then you._
- `a27-04-s2`: Keep the baby warm through the cold night. · _Sit with him under the big wing._
- `a27-04-s3`: Keep the chicks from sitting on the baby. · _Lift him out of the way._

#### `a27-04-feed`

_At dawn the Simurgh brings breakfast for everyone._  
**The Simurgh**: You have hands. Share it out.  
**The Simurgh**: Chicks first.

> _Four chicks eat. (Count them on your fingers: 1, 2, 3, 4.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:chicks:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four chicks, one number for each._

_The baby has soft figs and honey._  
**The Simurgh**: Feed the others before yourself. That is the rule.  
_One small fig is left._  

**Choices**

- **Eat the fig.**
    - It is the best fig you ever had. The Simurgh brings you two more.
- **Split it with your Nubbin.**
    - Half each. Nubbin eats its half, and looks at yours.
- **Give it to the smallest chick.**
    - The smallest chick is always at the back. It swallows the fig, very politely.

#### `a27-04-feed-done`

_Your Nubbin is round as an apple. It still wants more!_  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Eco.1.K-2, ask): when there is not enough, share fairly  
> _When there is not enough for everyone, what is a kind way to choose?_  
> - ✅ Share fairly. → Yes! Sharing fairly means everyone gets some.
> - Take it all. → Then others go hungry. Sharing fairly is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what to do when there is not enough: share fairly._


#### `a27-04-night`

_The nights on the peak are very cold. The stars are close!_  
_The baby sleeps between you and your Nubbin, under the big wing._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, ask): feathers trap warm air and keep animals warm  
> _The Simurgh’s wing is warm and fluffy. What keeps you warm at night?_  
> - ✅ A blanket. → Yes! A blanket holds warm air close, just like feathers.
> - An ice cube. → Brr! A blanket keeps warm air close, just like feathers.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that feathers, like a blanket, keep warm air close to the body._

**The Simurgh**: His father left him at the foot of my mountain.  
**The Simurgh**: This one is mine now, until someone is ready to love him.  
_Her heart goes thump, thump, thump._  

#### `a27-04-night-done`

_In the morning, frost is on top of her wings._

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): opposites: cold and warm  
> _Outside her wing is cold. Under her wing is...?_  
> - ✅ Warm. → Yes! Cold outside, warm under the wing.
> - Icy. → Under her wing it is warm and snug. The opposite of cold is warm.
> _For grown-ups: Practised opposites: cold and warm._


#### `a27-04-sitting`

_The chicks love their new brother._

_Flump!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): showing love gently

> _What is a gentle way to show love?_  
> - ✅ A soft pat. → Yes! A soft pat is gentle and safe.
> - A big sit. → A big sit squashes. A soft pat is gentle and safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about showing love gently, with soft hands._

**The Simurgh**: Ha! They will learn.  
**The Simurgh**: Keep minding him.  

#### `a27-04-sitting-done`

> _Who is bigger?_

> - Your Nubbin. → Look again. The chick is much bigger.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two sizes: the chick is bigger and the Nubbin smaller._

    - **The Youth**: Nobody ever said it to me. Is that good?

> - Swimming. → Not swimming! Roads take us from place to place.

    - **A Merchant**: A secret! Secrets travel fast.

_The merchant gives your Nubbin a whole round loaf._

> _What do camels have on their backs?_  
> - ✅ A hump, or two! → Yes! A camel’s hump stores fat for food.
> - Wings. → No wings! Camels have a hump, or two.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that camels have a hump, which stores fat, and can walk far._

> - ✅ A kind story. → Yes! Kind stories make people feel good.
> - A mean story. → Mean stories hurt. Kind stories make people feel good.

## A27-6. Sam’s Dream

> - ✅ Yes, it can. → Yes! Hair often turns grey or white as we grow old.
> - No, never. → It often does! Grey and white hair is common in older people.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that hair often turns grey or white as people age (different from being born with pale hair)._

- **“You can stop carrying him now.”**
    - **Old Servant**: Can I? I will practise.

> - Mud. → Mud is brown. Milk is white, like snow.

> - ✅ A hug. → Yes! A hug and a chat help sad feelings.
> - Hide the feeling. → Sad feelings are allowed. A hug and a chat help.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about sadness at a goodbye, and what helps._


#### `a27-08-feather`

**The Youth**: Do you not want me? I can be smaller.  
**The Simurgh**: I want you always. But another life is good for you.  
_He cries. He has never met people._  
_She gives him one feather from her chest. It is grey and gold._  
**The Simurgh**: Burn it on the day you need me, and I will come.  
_He holds it, and looks at you._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): keepsakes help us remember people we love  
> _The feather helps him remember the Simurgh._  
> _What do you keep to remember someone you love?_  
> - A photo. → A photo is a lovely thing to keep.
> - A toy. → A toy that someone gave you is special.
> - A song. → A song is a good keepsake. You can sing it any time.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keepsakes that help us remember people we love._


**Choices**

- **Tell him his father came back, and he should go.**
    - **You**: He came back. He climbed as far as he could, and knelt.
    - **The Youth**: He came back.
    - He says it again, quietly. Then he stands up.
- **Sit with him, and say nothing until he is ready.**
    - You sit beside him, shoulder to shoulder. You say nothing.
    - It takes a long time. You let it.
    - Then, by himself, he stands up.
- **Ask the Simurgh to make Sam wait one more night.**
    - **You**: Can he have one more night in the nest?
    - **The Simurgh**: One more night.
    - That night he sleeps among the chicks, with the feather in his fist.
    - In the morning, he stands up.

#### `a27-08-feather-done`

**The Youth**: I will go. But I will come back to see you all.  
**The Simurgh**: I know. Keep the feather dry.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): feathers are light because they are full of air  
> _Feathers are very light. Which is lighter: a feather or a stone?_  
> - ✅ A feather. → Yes! A feather is light, and full of air.
> - A stone. → A stone is heavy. A feather is much lighter.
> _For grown-ups: Compared weight: a feather is lighter than a stone._


#### `a27-08-complete`

_The young man says goodbye to each chick in turn._  
_You say goodbye too._  
**The Simurgh**: Take something of the nest home with you.  
_She weaves you a great round nest._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): name the shape: circle  
> _Your new nest is round. Which shape is round: a circle or a square?_  
> - ✅ A circle. → Yes! A circle is round, with no corners.
> - A square. → A square has four corners. A circle is round.
> _For grown-ups: Named a circle as the round shape, with no corners._

> _Someone came back for him._  
> _How does it feel when someone comes back for you?_  
> - ✅ Happy and safe. → Yes! It feels warm and safe.
> - Cross. → Some people feel cross first. Often, safe comes after.

> _Which rolls: a ball or a box?_  
> - ✅ A ball. → Yes! A ball is round, so it rolls.
> - A box. → A box has flat sides. A round ball rolls best.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that round things roll downhill._

_Sam bows low to the great bird._

> - Sun. → Sun begins with s. Zal and zebra both begin with z!
> _For grown-ups: Practised hearing the first sound z in Zal and zebra._

## A27-10. The Shah’s Court

- `a27-10-s1`: Go with Sam and Zal to the Shah’s court. · _Walk behind Zal into the big hall._
- `a27-10-s2`: Help Zal get through his first feast. · _Watch the others, and copy._
- `a27-10-s3`: Sit with Zal while he listens to people’s troubles. · _Stand at his shoulder in the hall._

#### `a27-10-court`

_The Shah is the king. He sits on a throne, in a crown._  
_The court is full of rugs and lamps._  
_Sam tells him everything, even the bad part._  
**Manuchehr**: Champion, look after this one.  
**Manuchehr**: Teach him our ways. How would a nest boy know them?  
_Zal bows, just as the Simurgh bows her head._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): people greet each other in different ways  
> _People say hello in different ways. In Persian, hello is salaam._  
> _How do you say hello?_  
> - I wave. → A wave is a friendly hello!
> - I say hi. → Hi is a friendly hello!
> - I say salaam. → Salaam! A lovely hello, in Persian.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about different ways of saying hello, including the Persian word salaam._


#### `a27-10-court-done`

_The star-readers look at the stars. They say he will be brave and wise._  
**Manuchehr**: I could tell that by looking at him.  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): stars shine at night  
> _Long ago, people watched the stars. When do stars shine in the sky?_  
> - ✅ At night. → Yes! We see stars at night, when the sky is dark.
> - At lunchtime. → Stars are there, but the bright sun hides them. We see them at night.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we see stars at night, when the sky is dark._


#### `a27-10-banquet`

_Tonight there is a feast. There are so many cups and knives!_  
**Zal**: Which one is for eating?  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count five cups  
> _Count the cups on the table with me: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5._  
> Check: `edu:count:cups:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five cups, one number for each._

**You**: I do not know either.  
**Zal**: Then we are equal. We will learn together.  
_Zal waits until everyone is served._  
_Your Nubbin eats a whole dish of rice. Munch!_  

**Choices**

- **Watch the others, and copy.**
    - You copy the man opposite, and Zal copies you.
    - **Zal**: This is like hunting. You keep still and watch.
- **Ask the person next to you.**
    - They are glad to be asked. They explain every knife.
- **Try to stop your Nubbin starting a second dish.**
    - Too late! The Shah laughs, and sends it a third.

#### `a27-10-banquet-done`

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): rhymes: snore and door  
> _Which word rhymes with snore: door or sun?_  
> - ✅ Door. → Yes! Snore, door, floor, more!
> - Sun. → Sun does not rhyme. Snore, door, floor: they end the same!
> _For grown-ups: Practised rhyming: snore, door, floor, more._


#### `a27-10-petitions`

_Sam goes to the wars. Zal looks after Sistan._  
_Every morning, people bring their troubles._

_Zal listens to both sides._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): fairness: everyone gets a turn to speak  
> _Zal listens to both sides. Why is listening fair?_  
> - ✅ Everyone gets a turn. → Yes! Fair means everyone gets a turn to speak.
> - Only the loud one talks. → Fair means everyone gets a turn, loud or quiet.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about fairness: everyone gets a turn to speak._

_He never judges anyone by how they look._  

#### `a27-10-petitions-done`

**Zal**: Tell me if I get one wrong. You are not afraid to.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): telling the truth kindly  
> _A good friend tells the truth, kindly._  
> _How can we say a true thing kindly?_  
> - ✅ Use a soft voice. → Yes! A soft voice and kind words help.
> - Shout it. → Shouting can sting. A soft voice and kind words help.
> _For grown-ups: Practised telling the truth kindly, with a soft voice._

> - ✅ Autumn. → Yes! Spring, summer, autumn, winter.
> - Spring. → Spring comes after winter. After summer comes autumn.

## A27-11. Kabul

- `a27-11-s1`: Be at the feast in Zal’s tents outside Kabul. · _King Mehrab comes at sundown._

- `a27-11-s3`: Answer Rudaba’s questions about Zal. · _Sit with the family and talk._

#### `a27-11-tents`

_Zal camps by the river near Kabul._  
_The king of Kabul, Mehrab, comes to meet him._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): Kabul is a real city in Afghanistan where Persian is spoken  
> _Kabul is a real city. Today it is in a country called Afghanistan._  
> _People there speak a kind of Persian, too._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Kabul is a real city in Afghanistan, where Persian is spoken._

_They like each other at once._  
**Mehrab**: Come and stay in my house. Let us be glad of you.  
**Zal**: Ask me anything else. I cannot say yes.  
_Long ago, a cruel king was in Mehrab’s family._  
_Zal’s father would not like it._  
_Mehrab bows and goes away, sad._  

#### `a27-11-tents-done`

**Zal**: I sent him away with nothing. Will you go after him for me?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): making things right with a kind gift and kind words  
> _Zal feels bad. What can he do to make it kinder?_  
> - ✅ Send a kind gift and kind words. → Yes! Kind words and a gift can mend a sore feeling.
> - Forget about it. → Mehrab might still feel sad. A kind gift and kind words can help.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about how to mend a sore feeling with kindness._


#### `a27-11-gift`

_Zal gives you a wooden box._  
_Inside is a white cloth with a gold edge._

> Check: `edu:trace:shape:rectangle`

**Zal**: Tell him I wanted to come. That part is true.

_Mehrab opens the box. He goes pink._  
**Mehrab**: That is the nicest no I ever had!  

#### `a27-11-gift-done`

**Sindokht**: Sit down, messenger. Have something to eat.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): welcoming a guest  
> _In many homes, a guest is offered food._  
> _In Persian, a guest is a mehman. What can you offer a guest?_  
> - ✅ A snack or a drink. → Yes! A snack shows you are glad they came.
> - Nothing. → Offering something shows you are glad they came.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about welcoming guests, and learned the Persian word mehman._


#### `a27-11-praise`

**Sindokht**: Tell us about this white-haired son of Sam.  
**Mehrab**: He is brave, and he is kind. The white hair suits him.  
_Rudaba is quiet. She listens with her whole self._

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): what a character does shows what they are like

> - ✅ Kind. → Yes! What he does shows he is kind.
> - Unkind. → Feeding others first is a kind thing to do. Zal is kind.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out that a character is kind from what he does._


**Choices**

- **“He feeds everyone else before himself.”**
    - **Rudaba**: Does he? Even at a feast?
    - **You**: Especially then.
- **“A great bird raised him. He still bows like her.”**
    - **Rudaba**: I would like to see that bow.
- **“His hair is white as snow, and it suits him.”**
    - **Rudaba**: Father says so too. I think I would like it.

> Check: `edu:count:questions:7`

> _Zal cannot sleep. Sleep helps our bodies rest._  
> _What helps you sleep: a quiet song or a loud drum?_

> - A loud drum. → Boom! A drum would keep us awake. A quiet song helps.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sleep rests our bodies, and that quiet, calm things help us sleep._


## A27-12. The Rose Garden

- `a27-12-s1`: Watch the maids gather roses across the river. · _Stand on the bank by Zal’s tents._
- `a27-12-s2`: Cross with the page and carry messages. · _The ferry stone is a little way downstream._
- `a27-12-s3`: Bring the wise maid to Zal. · _She wants to see him with her own eyes._

#### `a27-12-roses`

_Across the river is a rose garden._  
_Rudaba’s maids pick roses and put them in their hair._

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, ask): plants need water and sunlight  
> _Roses need water and sunlight to grow. What do roses need: water, or toys?_  
> - ✅ Water and sun. → Yes! Roses drink water and love the sun.
> - Toys. → Roses do not need toys. They need water and sun!
> _For grown-ups: Learned that plants need water and sunlight to grow._

_Zal takes his bow and goes to the water._  
_He shoots one arrow across the river. It lands among the roses._

> Check: `edu:count:petals:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted the five petals of a wild rose._


#### `a27-12-boasts`

> - Talk louder. → Talking louder is hard to listen to. Listening and waiting is polite.

> - My running. → Running fast, or running far. Be proud!

## A27-13. The Rope of Hair

- `a27-13-s1`: Go with Zal to the king’s house at dusk. · _Follow the maid through the dark lanes._
- `a27-13-s2`: Keep watch below while Zal goes up. · _Stand at the corner of the lane._
- `a27-13-s3`: Keep watch until dawn. · _The porter comes round once._

#### `a27-13-dusk`

_At sundown the maid says: come now._  
_Zal follows her down the dark lanes. You come too, to keep watch._  
_Rudaba waits on the roof in the last light._  
_She is tall and calm, like a tree with the moon on it._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): comparing: tall like a tree  
> _Rudaba is tall and calm, like a tree._  
> _What is tall like a tree: a giraffe or a mouse?_  
> - ✅ A giraffe. → Yes! A giraffe is very tall.
> - A mouse. → A mouse is tiny. A giraffe is tall like a tree.
> _For grown-ups: Practised comparing things: tall like a tree._

**Rudaba**: Welcome! Bless you for coming.  

#### `a27-13-dusk-done`

**Zal**: You are up there, and I am down here.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): position words: above and below  
> _Rudaba is on the roof. Zal is on the ground._  
> _Who is above?_  
> - ✅ Rudaba. → Yes! Rudaba is above. Zal is below.
> - Zal. → Look up! Rudaba is above, on the roof. Zal is below.
> _For grown-ups: Used the words above and below to say where people are._


#### `a27-13-roof`

_Rudaba lets her long hair down from the roof._  
**Rudaba**: Take hold and climb!  
_Zal holds it gently. Then he lets go._  
**Zal**: No. That would hurt you.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): choosing the kind and gentle way  
> _Zal said no, because it would hurt her. Which is a kind choice?_  
> - ✅ Being gentle. → Yes! Gentle is kind.
> - Pulling hard. → Pulling hard could hurt. Gentle is kind.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about choosing a gentle, kind way so as not to hurt anyone._

_He makes a loop in a rope and throws it up. It catches!_  

#### `a27-13-roof-done`

_Up on the roof, they hold hands and go in together._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, ask): a problem and a solution: a rope helps us climb  
> _Zal had a problem: how to get up the wall. What did he use?_  
> - ✅ A rope. → Yes! A rope solved the problem.
> - A spoon. → A spoon is too small! A rope helps us climb.
> _For grown-ups: Named a problem (getting up a wall) and its solution (a rope)._


#### `a27-13-watch`

_The night is warm and long. Voices drift from the window._  
_Nubbin sits on your feet, fast asleep._  
_At midnight, a night porter walks round with a lamp._  
_He stops at the rope. He looks up the wall._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): first, next, last  
> _First comes dusk. Next comes midnight._  
> _Last comes morning. What comes last?_  
> - ✅ Morning. → Yes! Dusk, midnight, morning. Morning is last.
> - Dusk. → Dusk is first. The last one is morning.
> _For grown-ups: Put three times of day in order: first, next, last._


**Choices**

- **Step out and say good evening.**
    - He jumps, and says good evening back. You talk about the weather.
- **Nudge your Nubbin.**
    - Nubbin rolls after the lamp. The porter follows it, trying to feed it.
- **Keep very still in the shadow.**
    - He thinks the rope is a vine, and walks on.

#### `a27-13-watch-done`

_In the camp, the morning drums begin._  
_The voices upstairs say: not yet, please, not yet._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): feeling sad when a good time ends

> - The sun. → The sun shines in the day. The moon shines at night.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the moon shines at night, and changes shape through the month._


**Choices**

- **Keep quiet, and let him think.**
    - **Zal**: The days of the month! The moon gets thin, then comes back round.

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 8 to find how many  
> _(Count Ananse’s legs together. Point to each one.)_  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. Eight legs!  
> Check: `edu:count:legs:8`
> _For grown-ups: Counted a spider’s eight legs, one by one._

_Your Nubbin touches a silver thread. It sticks!_  
_The spider pulls it free. He has done this many times._  

#### `a28-01-complete`

**Kwaku Ananse**: I am Kwaku Ananse. You will carry things for me.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: In return, you will see the cleverest thing ever done.  
_Far behind you, the old woman is still telling._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Come! We are going to see the Sky-god.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Walk tall. Not too tall.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): who a story is about (characters)  
> _Every story has someone it is about. Who is this story about?_  
> - ✅ Ananse the spider. → Yes! This story is about Ananse, the spider in the hat.
> - A big brown dog. → There is no dog yet! This story is about Ananse, the spider.
> _For grown-ups: Named the main character of the story, Ananse the spider._

_Your Nubbin follows, stepping where he steps._  

## A28-2. The Sky-god’s Stories

- `a28-02-s1`: Climb Ananse’s thread up to the Sky-god’s court. · _Follow Ananse up the silver line._
- `a28-02-s2`: Stand with Ananse while he asks the Sky-god his price. · _Stay one step behind Ananse._
- `a28-02-s3`: Walk into the forest with Ananse. · _Sit with Ananse on the root and listen._

#### `a28-02-climb`

_Ananse spins a thread straight up into the morning._  
_He climbs it. You climb after him._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: A spider’s silk is made inside its body.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: It comes out of tiny spouts at the back.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): spiders make silk inside their bodies  
> _Spiders make silk in their bodies, and spin it out of tiny spouts._  
> _That is how a spider makes a thread._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that spiders make silk inside their bodies and spin it out of tiny spouts._

**Kwaku Ananse**: Don’t look down!  
_At the top is a court of white cloud. Elders sit on carved stools._  
_At the far end is a light too bright to look at._  
_Rich men are leaving. The Sky-god said no to all their gifts._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Kings could not pay. But I have no money.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Nobody watches a poor spider.  

**Choices**

- **Ask what he means to pay with.**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: With whatever he asks for. Agree first.
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: Work out how afterwards.
- **Unstick your Nubbin from your hair.**
    - It takes a while. An elder watches and nods when it is done.

#### `a28-02-climb-done`

_Ananse straightens his hat. He takes three steps._  
_He bows so low that his hat touches the cloud._  
_You bow too. Bowing says: I respect you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): showing respect to an elder  
> _Ananse bows to the elders. How can we show respect to an elder?_  
> - ✅ Say hello kindly and listen. → Yes! Kind words and good listening show respect.
> - Shout over them. → Shouting is not respectful. Kind words and listening are.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how kind words and good listening show respect for elders._


#### `a28-02-price`

**Nyame**: Kwaku Ananse. You have come a long way for a spider.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Great one, I have come to buy your stories.  
**Nyame**: Kings tried. Towns tried.  
**Nyame**: They could not pay.  
**Nyame**: Bring me four things. Onini, the python.  
**Nyame**: Mmoboro, the hornets.  
**Nyame**: Bring me Osebo, the leopard. And Mmoatia, the fairy.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: I will bring them all!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: And my old mother will come too, to sit on the best stool.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add 1 more: 4 and 1 make 5  
> _(Count the four things on your fingers: python, hornets, leopard, fairy.)_  
> _Then Ananse adds his mother. How many is that?_  
> - ✅ Five. → Yes! Four things and one more makes five.
> - Four. → Four things, and Ya Nsia makes one more. Four and one is five.
> _For grown-ups: Counted four things and added one more to make five._

_Your Nubbin stares at him. So do you._  
**Nyame**: So be it. Go, Kwaku Ananse.  

**Choices**

- **Whisper, “Your mother?”**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: She will love it up there. Very good stools.
- **Say nothing.**
    - Ananse glances at you. He knows what you are thinking.

#### `a28-02-price-done`

_Down the thread, Ananse is humming._  
_You count on your fingers. Your Nubbin counts on its toes._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: My name is Kwaku. Clap it with me: Kwa-ku!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clapping the syllables in a name  
> _(Clap twice as you say it: Kwa, ku. Two claps!)_  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: Two claps. Kwa-ku.  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: That is how my name sounds.  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:kwaku`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the two syllables in the name Kwaku._


#### `a28-02-road`

_At the foot of the thread, Ananse sits on a root._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Eight legs, I have. Two arms, you have.  
_Your Nubbin sits in a puddle of sap. It sticks!_  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Ah. A specialist.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: They call me Kwaku. I was born on a Wednesday!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): Akan day names  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: In Ghana, many families name a baby for the day it was born.  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: Kwaku is a boy born on a Wednesday.  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: Ama is a girl born on a Saturday.  
> _(Do you know your birth day? Tell a grown-up.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that many Ghanaian families give babies a day name, such as Kwaku for a Wednesday boy._

**Kwaku Ananse**: Every child has a day name. What is yours?  

**Choices**

- **Tell him the day you were born.**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: A fine day. Not as fine as Wednesday.
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: But fine.
- **Say you don’t know.**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: Then you can choose one. I would choose Wednesday.

#### `a28-02-road-done`

_Ananse gets up and dusts off his hat._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Python first. He is the vainest.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Vain ones are easy.  
_A python is a big snake. It has no legs._  
_It flicks its tongue, flick, flick! That is how it smells._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): snakes smell with their tongues  
> _A snake flicks its tongue to taste the air. That is how it smells._  
> _(Flick your tongue like a snake!)_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a snake flicks its tongue to smell the air._


#### `a28-02-complete`

_The forest is huge, green and noisy._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: One thing at a time. That is how you eat a whole yam.  
_Big jobs get smaller when we do one bit at a time._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): breaking a big job into small steps  
> _A job feels very big. What helps?_  
> - ✅ Do one small bit at a time. → Yes! Small bits, one at a time, get big jobs done.
> - Give up straight away. → Try one small bit first. Little by little, big jobs get done.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how a big job feels easier when we do one small bit at a time._

_You set off. Your Nubbin follows, with a leaf stuck to its foot._  

## A28-3. Onini the Python

- `a28-03-s1`: Find a long palm branch and some creeper. · _Look on the forest floor. Your Nubbin walks into the creeper._
- `a28-03-s2`: Watch Ananse and Aso argue by the python’s tree. · _Stand by the branch. Keep a straight face._
- `a28-03-s3`: Hold the python’s tail. · _Take the tail end and hold on tight._

#### `a28-03-branch`

**Kwaku Ananse**: We need a palm branch. A long one.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: And creeper for tying.  
_You find a branch. It is longer than a canoe!_  
_Your Nubbin finds the creeper by walking into it._  
_Creeper is a vine. It is bendy and strong._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): a bendy, strong material is good for tying  
> _Which is better for tying a bundle: a stiff stick, or a bendy creeper?_  
> - ✅ A bendy creeper. → Yes! A creeper bends round things, and it is strong.
> - A stiff stick. → A stiff stick will not wrap round. A bendy creeper will!
> _For grown-ups: Compared materials: a bendy, strong creeper ties better than a stiff stick._

**Kwaku Ananse**: Now my wife Aso is coming. We will have a loud argument.  
**Aso**: I always argue with you loudly. I do not need a reason.  

#### `a28-03-branch-done`

_You drag the branch to a great tree._  
_Its roots look like knuckles on a big brown hand._  
_Something long sleeps up in the branches. Hhh, hhh._  
_It is breathing._  
_Tree. Three._  
_Those words rhyme!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): words that rhyme  
> _(Say it: tree, three. They sound the same at the end.)_  
> _Can you think of another word that rhymes with tree? Try “bee” or “me”._  
> Check: `edu:say:rhyme:tree`
> _For grown-ups: Heard and said rhyming words: tree and three._


#### `a28-03-argue`

**Kwaku Ananse**: He IS longer than this branch!  
**Aso**: He is NOT! Anybody can see!  
_They shout and shout. They have had lots of practice._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): settling a disagreement without shouting  
> _Ananse and Aso disagree. What helps most?_  
> - ✅ Check the facts together. → Yes! Looking at the facts together settles it.
> - Shout louder. → Shouting does not settle it. Checking the facts does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about settling a disagreement by checking the facts, not by shouting._

_A head comes down out of the tree, followed by lots of python._  
**Onini**: What is all this noise about my length?  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Settle it for us, Onini. Lie down by the branch.  
**Onini**: Lay the branch down. I will lie beside it.  
_He stretches and stretches. There is still a hand’s width of branch left._  

**Choices**

- **Tell Onini he very nearly has it.**
    - **Onini**: Nearly is not a length a python accepts.
- **Keep a very straight face.**
    - You manage. Your Nubbin does not.
    - It turns to look hard at a tree.

#### `a28-03-argue-done`

**Kwaku Ananse**: Your tail keeps slipping, Onini.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: My helper will hold it, so we can measure you properly.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare lengths: shorter and longer  
> _Onini lay beside the branch. (Look at the picture.)_  
> _Is Onini shorter or longer than the branch?_  
> - ✅ Shorter. → Yes! Onini is shorter. There is branch left over.
> - Longer. → Look again. There is branch left over at the end. Onini is shorter.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two lengths and saw that the python was shorter than the branch._


#### `a28-03-tie`

_You hold the tail end. It is heavy and strong._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Just to measure you properly. Now a bit in the middle.  
_Round and round goes the creeper, nose to tail._  
**Onini**: This is not measuring!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: No. You are very long, though!  
_Your Nubbin ties its own foot into the knot._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, ask): a snake has no legs; it moves with its body  
> _A snake has no legs. How does it move?_  
> - ✅ It slithers. → Yes! A snake slithers, pushing along with its strong body.
> - It hops. → Snakes do not hop. They slither along the ground.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a snake has no legs and slithers using its strong body._


**Choices**

- **Tell Onini you’re sorry.**
    - **Onini**: Sorry, from the one holding my tail.
    - You keep holding it anyway. You feel bad.
- **Pat the python’s nose, carefully.**
    - He looks at you with one cold eye.
    - It is not friendship. But it is not biting either.

#### `a28-03-tie-done`

_Ananse unties your Nubbin’s foot, one strand at a time._  
_Onini is still tied up. He looks cross and a bit sad._  
_Onini feels tricked. Being tricked feels bad._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): naming how someone feels  
> _Onini has been tricked. How does Onini feel?_  
> - ✅ Cross and sad. → Yes! Onini feels cross and sad. Being tricked hurts.
> - Very happy. → Look at his face. Onini is cross and sad, not happy.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feelings of a character who had been tricked: cross and sad._


#### `a28-03-complete`

**Kwaku Ananse**: One! One thing paid, by a spider with no money!  
**Aso**: I saw. I argued.  
**Aso**: You are welcome.  
_Onini goes up the thread to the Sky-god. He is cross all the way._  
_He will be looked after. It is a court, not a kitchen._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): elders listen to everyone so rules are fair  
> _In a village, elders help keep things fair. They listen to everybody._  
> _At the Sky-god’s court, Onini will be listened to too._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that elders keep rules fair by listening to everyone._

**Kwaku Ananse**: Hornets next. Find me a gourd!  

## A28-4. Mmoboro the Hornets

- `a28-04-s1`: Fill a gourd with water for Ananse’s “rain”. · _Take the water gourd to the stream and fill it up._
- `a28-04-s2`: Pour the rain when Ananse says. · _Stand under the nest with the water. Wait for Ananse._
- `a28-04-s3`: Stop up the gourd before the hornets work it out. · _Take the grass plug from Ananse. Close the gourd fast._

#### `a28-04-gourd`

_Ananse cuts the top off a dry gourd._  
_He gives you a second gourd for water._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: The dry one is the house. The wet one is the rain.  
_He holds a big plantain leaf over his head, like an umbrella._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Fill it to the brim!  
_You fill the gourd at the stream. Your Nubbin brings half of one._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare amounts: more and less  
> _Your gourd is full. Nubbin’s gourd is half full._  
> _Which gourd has more water?_  
> - ✅ The full gourd. → Yes! The full gourd has more. Half full has less.
> - The half-full gourd. → Look again. The full gourd has more. Half full has less.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a full gourd with a half-full one and said which held more._


**Choices**

- **Ask why the hornets would believe it’s raining.**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: Because I will tell them. Nobody argues with weather.
- **Offer to hold the leaf.**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: No. The leaf is the costume.
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: I am the actor. You are the weather.

#### `a28-04-gourd-done`

_The nest hangs from a branch like a grey paper lantern._  
_It hums. It hums louder the closer you get._  
_Hornets chew wood into paper. They build the nest from it._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): hornets build paper nests from chewed wood  
> _Hornets chew wood and mix it with spit. It dries into paper._  
> _That is how they build their nest. Clever!_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that hornets make a paper nest by chewing wood._


#### `a28-04-rain`

**Kwaku Ananse**: Now. Pour.  
_You tip the water. Splash!_  
_Ananse taps his leaf. Drum, drum, drum!_  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Rain! Rain, Mmoboro!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: You will be soaked!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Come into my dry gourd. It is lovely in here.  
_The humming changes. Buzz, buzz, BUZZ!_  
_The hornets pour into the gourd, like smoke going down a chimney._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.4, do): sound words (drum, splash, buzz)  
> _(Say the sounds: splash! drum, drum, drum! buzz, buzz!)_  
> _Sound words make a story noisy and fun._  
> Check: `edu:say:sound-words:drum-buzz`
> _For grown-ups: Said sound words from the story: splash, drum and buzz._


#### `a28-04-stopper`

_Ananse holds out a plug of twisted grass. His legs jiggle._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Now! Now, now, now!  
_A hornet’s head pokes out. It goes back in._  
_Your heart goes thump, thump. It feels fast._  
_A slow breath helps you stay calm._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, do): a slow breath to stay calm  
> _(Breathe in slowly, then out slowly, three times.)_  
> _Calm hands can close a gourd. Now you are ready._  
> Check: `edu:breathe:slow:3`
> _For grown-ups: Took three slow breaths to calm down when things felt hurried._


**Choices**

- **Jam the stopper in.**
    - It goes in with a squeak.
    - The gourd buzzes in your hands, like a pot coming to the boil.
- **Let your Nubbin close it.**
    - Your Nubbin sits on the hole. It is about the right size.
    - You slide the grass in under it, carefully.

#### `a28-04-stopper-done`

_One last hornet lands on your Nubbin’s nose. It stings!_  
_Your Nubbin’s eyes go wide. Then they go narrow._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Two!  
_Two things are paid: the python and the hornets._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away: 4 take away 2  
> _The Sky-god asked for four things. Ananse has two._  
> _How many more are left?_  
> - ✅ Two. → Yes! Four take away two leaves two: the leopard and the fairy.
> - Four. → Ananse has two already. Four take away two is two more to find.
> _For grown-ups: Solved a take-away problem: 4 things asked, 2 paid, so 2 left._


#### `a28-04-complete`

_Ananse dances on eight legs, with the gourd over his hat._  
_The hornets go up to the Sky-god. They are fine._  
_Your Nubbin’s nose has a small red bump._  
_It is cross with the gourd, the hornets and the sky!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words for feelings  
> _Your Nubbin is cross about its nose. Which word is a feeling word?_  
> - ✅ Grumpy. → Yes! Grumpy is a feeling word. Your Nubbin is grumpy.
> - Square. → Square is a shape. A feeling word is grumpy, glad or sad.
> _For grown-ups: Picked out a feeling word (grumpy) to say how a character feels._

**Kwaku Ananse**: Leopard next. For a leopard, we dig.  

## A28-5. Osebo the Leopard

- `a28-05-s1`: Help Ananse dig a pit across the leopard’s path. · _Dig where Ananse scratched a line. Cover the hole with sticks and leaves._
- `a28-05-s2`: Come back to the pit at dawn. · _Rest at Ananse’s house. Go back to the path at first light._
- `a28-05-s3`: Carry the bundle to the foot of the thread. · _Take the front. Your Nubbin takes the tail._

#### `a28-05-pit`

_Ananse finds the leopard’s path. The paw prints are big._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Dig here! Deep enough for a leopard to sit and think.  
_You dig. Your Nubbin digs a little hole of its own._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Now put sticks across the top. Then leaves on the sticks.  
_The sticks go over the hole. The leaves go on top._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): positions: on top, under  
> _The hole is under the sticks. Where are the leaves?_  
> - ✅ On top. → Yes! The leaves are on top of the sticks.
> - Under the hole. → The leaves are on top of the sticks. The hole is underneath.
> _For grown-ups: Used position words (on top, under) to describe a covered hole._

_Now it looks like a path. You must remember where it isn’t!_  

#### `a28-05-pit-done`

**Kwaku Ananse**: Now we go home and sleep.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Leopards walk at night. That is when the hole will work.  
_Leopards have spots. They are good at climbing trees too._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): leopards are mostly active at night  
> _When do leopards like to walk about?_  
> - ✅ At night. → Yes! Leopards mostly hunt at night, in the dark.
> - Only at noon. → Leopards mostly walk about at night, when it is dark.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that leopards are mostly active at night._


#### `a28-05-fall`

_In the night: crash! Thump!_  
_A long, low growl._  
_At first light you creep back. The pit has a leopard in it!_  
**Osebo**: Who dug a hole in my road?  
_Osebo is spotty and magnificent. He is very embarrassed._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: My poor friend! Who would do such a thing?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): telling the truth  
> _Ananse dug the hole. But he says, “Who would do such a thing?”_  
> _Is that telling the truth?_  
> - ✅ No. He is fibbing. → Yes. Ananse is pretending. Telling the truth is better.
> - Yes. It is all true. → Ananse dug it himself! He is pretending. The truth is better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about the difference between pretending and telling the truth._


**Choices**

- **Look anywhere but at the pile of earth.**
    - You look at the sky, and so does your Nubbin.
    - The pile of earth is right behind you, being obvious.
- **Ask Osebo if he’s hurt.**
    - **Osebo**: Only my pride. Which is worse.

#### `a28-05-web`

**Kwaku Ananse**: Let me help you out. I am wonderful with ropes!  
**Osebo**: You? Help?  
**Osebo**: You are a spider.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Exactly. Put your arms through this loop.  
_The web goes round and round and round._  
_The tree springs up and Osebo goes with it._  
_He is wrapped, cross and not hurt._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): spider silk is strong, and some of it is sticky  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: My silk is very strong, for something so thin.  
> **Kwaku Ananse**: Some of it is sticky, to catch flies.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that spider silk is strong for its thinness, and that some of it is sticky._

**Osebo**: Spider! When I get out of this!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Yes, yes. Everyone says that.  

**Choices**

- **Tell Osebo the Sky-god keeps a fine court.**
    - **Osebo**: Then the Sky-god can come and untie me himself.
- **Say nothing, and take the heavy end.**
    - Osebo looks at you upside down.
    - He seems to think better of you for not explaining.

#### `a28-05-web-done`

_The bundle is heavy and very cross. You carry the front._  
_Your Nubbin carries the tip of the tail._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare weights: heavier and lighter  
> _The leopard bundle is heavy. The tail tip is light._  
> _Which does your Nubbin carry?_  
> - ✅ The light tail tip. → Yes! The tail tip is light, so Nubbin can carry it.
> - The heavy middle. → The heavy middle is too much for a Nubbin. It carries the light tip.
> _For grown-ups: Compared heavy and light, and worked out which part a small Nubbin could carry._

_Your Nubbin gets stuck to the web. It goes up the thread, stuck!_  
_Ananse unpicks it, bit by bit._  

#### `a28-05-complete`

_Osebo goes up to the Sky-god. He is alive and very cross._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Three! Python, hornets, leopard.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Now the hard one. Nobody sees a fairy unless she wants to be seen.  
_Ghana has hot green forest in the south and drier grassland in the north._  
_Leopards live in places like these._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): places have different land: forest and grassland  
> _(Point to the green part of the map.) Ghana has forest in the south._  
> _What grows in a forest?_  
> - ✅ Lots of trees. → Yes! A forest is full of trees.
> - Only sand. → Sand is for deserts and beaches. A forest is full of trees.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Ghana has forest in the south and grassland in the north._


## A28-6. Mmoatia and the Gum Doll

- `a28-06-s1`: Carve a small doll for Ananse’s trap. · _Take the wood and knife from Ananse. Carve at the table._
- `a28-06-s2`: Hide by the odum tree and watch who comes. · _Crouch behind the big root. Keep still until dusk._
- `a28-06-s3`: Choose what to do while Ananse fetches rope. · _Go to the fairy under the odum tree._

#### `a28-06-doll`

**Kwaku Ananse**: Carve me a doll. A small one, with a face and arms and legs.  
_You carve. It comes out round-headed and solemn, with its arms held out._  
_Its head is a circle. Its body is a rectangle._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): name shapes: circle  
> _The doll’s head is round. Which shape is round: a circle or a square?_  
> - ✅ A circle. → Yes! A circle is round, like the doll’s head.
> - A square. → A square has corners. A circle is round, like the doll’s head.
> _For grown-ups: Named a circle as the round shape, using the doll’s head._

_Your Nubbin sits up straighter._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Lovely. Now the gum.  

#### `a28-06-doll-done`

_Ananse paints the doll with gum, thick and shiny._  
_Gum is sap from a tree. It is sticky._  
_Your Nubbin touches it. Stuck!_  
_It takes both of you to pull it free._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): sorting by how things feel: sticky or not  
> _Which one is sticky: gum or a feather?_  
> - ✅ Gum. → Yes! Gum is sticky. It holds on to things.
> - A feather. → A feather is soft and light, not sticky. Gum is sticky.
> _For grown-ups: Sorted things by a property: gum is sticky, a feather is not._

_Ananse sets a bowl of mashed yam in the doll’s lap._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Now we hide. Very quiet.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: You especially.  

#### `a28-06-fairy`

_You hide behind a root until dusk._  
_Something small comes down from the odum tree. It is Mmoatia, a fairy._  
**Mmoatia**: Little one, may I have some of your yam?  
_The doll says nothing. Mmoatia eats the yam._  
_Yum._  
**Mmoatia**: Thank you. I said thank you.  
_The doll says nothing._  
**Mmoatia**: When somebody thanks you, you answer!  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying “you’re welcome”  
> _Mmoatia said thank you. What can we say back?_  
> - ✅ You’re welcome. → Yes! “You’re welcome” shows we heard and we are kind.
> - Nothing at all. → Saying “you’re welcome” is kinder. It shows we heard.
> _For grown-ups: Practised answering a thank-you with “you’re welcome”._

_She slaps the doll. Her hand sticks!_  
_Then her other hand sticks!_  
**Mmoatia**: Let go of me!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Rope! Stay there.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: I will fetch rope!  

#### `a28-06-fairy-done`

_Then Ananse is gone._  
_The fairy pulls and pulls. Nothing comes apart._  
_Both of her hands are stuck. One hand._  
_Two hands._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count two hands  
> _(Hold up your hands. Count them: one, two.)_  
> _Two hands, just like Mmoatia._  
> Check: `edu:count:hands:2`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two hands, matching one number to each._

_She stops. She looks straight at your root._  

#### `a28-06-wait`

_It is nearly dark. Far away, a spider is looking for rope._  
**Mmoatia**: You. You are with him.  
_Mmoatia is not crying. She has gone very still._  
_She is scared. Her eyes are big._  
_Your Nubbin looks at her, then at you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what helps someone who is scared  
> _Mmoatia is scared. What helps someone who is scared?_  
> - ✅ Staying close and being kind. → Yes! Staying close and being kind helps a lot.
> - Telling them to hurry up. → Hurrying them does not help. Staying close and kind does.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how staying close and being kind helps someone who is scared._


**Choices**

- **Work one of her hands free.**
    - You loosen the gum with your thumbs. One small hand comes free.
    - **Mmoatia**: Only one?
    - **You**: The other has to stay. It is his story.
    - **You**: But you can have that one back.
    - She opens and closes her free hand.
    - She looks at you for a long time.
- **Wait by your root.**
    - You stay by your root. It is the spider’s story, not yours.
    - **Mmoatia**: I see. Alright.
    - She lifts her chin and waits for the rope.
- **Sit beside her and wait.**
    - You sit down beside her in the leaves.
    - Your Nubbin sits on her other side.
    - She glares at you both. After a while she stops glaring.
    - When the frogs start up, she leans a little on your arm.

#### `a28-06-wait-done`

_Ananse comes back at last with lots of rope. He is puffing._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Four! Four, and my mother makes five!  
_First the python. Next the hornets._  
_Then the leopard. Last, the fairy._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): first, next, last: the order of events  
> _Ananse caught four things, one after another. Which one did he catch first?_  
> - ✅ The python. → Yes! First the python, next the hornets, then the leopard, last the fairy.
> - The fairy. → The fairy was last. The python was first.
> _For grown-ups: Put story events in order using first, next and last._

_Ananse ties the fairy, doll and all. He is careful._  
_She goes up the thread with her chin high._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Tomorrow, the court. Wash.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: You are covered in gum.  
_Your Nubbin is stuck to the yam bowl. It does not mind._  
_Yam grows under the ground. It is a root, full of food._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): some plants grow food underground  
> _Where does a yam grow: up in a tree, or under the ground?_  
> - ✅ Under the ground. → Yes! A yam grows under the ground.
> - Up in a tree. → Not in a tree! A yam grows under the ground.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that yams grow under the ground._


## A28-7. Spider Stories

- `a28-07-s1`: Walk with Ya Nsia up to the Sky-god’s court. · _Find Ya Nsia at Ananse’s door. Go up the thread with her._
- `a28-07-s2`: Stand in the court while Ananse pays the price. · _Stand a step behind Ananse, among the elders._

#### `a28-07-mother`

_Ananse’s mother waits at his door. She wears her good cloth._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): helping an older person  
> _Ya Nsia is old. How can you help her walk?_  
> - ✅ Offer her your arm. → Yes! An arm to lean on is a kind way to help.
> - Run on ahead. → Running ahead leaves her behind. Offering your arm is kinder.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about helping an older person by offering an arm and walking at her pace._


**Choices**

- **Tell her she must be proud of him.**

    - **Ya Nsia**: It is the same face, with a spider.
- **Just give her your arm, and walk.**

#### `a28-07-mother-done`

> _One, two, three, four. Four climbers!_  
> _The last number tells how many._  
> Check: `edu:count:climbers:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four climbers, and understood that the last number counted tells how many there are._

_The old lady goes first. Ananse comes last, practising what to say._  

#### `a28-07-court`

_The elders sit on carved stools in the cloud court._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, notice): carved stools are seats of honour in Akan culture  
> _In Ghana, a carved stool can be a seat of honour for elders._  
> _People take care of their stools, and treat them with respect._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a carved stool is a seat of honour in Akan culture._

_Ananse lays the price on the cloud._  
_The python, the hornets, the leopard and the fairy._

**Osebo**: Spider. I have not forgotten.  
**Nyame**: Kings could not pay. Kwaku Ananse has paid.

_Ananse takes off his hat and holds it to his chest._  
_For once, he says nothing._  

**Choices**

- **Bow, as the elders do.**
    - You bow. Your Nubbin bows too, too low.

    - You are the only one. Then an elder claps, and another.
    - Soon the whole court is clapping.

#### `a28-07-court-done`

**Nyame**: Ya Nsia will stay with us as our guest. She will want for nothing.

_Spider and story both start with the sound sss._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds: sss in spider and story  
> _Spider and story start with the same sound. Is it sss, or mmm?_  
> - ✅ Sss. → Yes! Spider, story: sss, sss.
> - Mmm. → Say them slowly: sss-pider, sss-tory. They start with sss.
> _For grown-ups: Heard the same first sound (sss) at the start of spider and story._

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-1, ask): animals need the right place; snakes like warmth  
> _Snakes need to keep warm. Where would a python like to lie?_  
> - ✅ On a warm shelf. → Yes! A snake gets warm from sunny, warm places.
> - On cold ice. → Ice is far too cold. A snake likes to lie somewhere warm.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that snakes need warm places, so a python likes a warm shelf._

## A28-8. The Box Opens

- `a28-08-s1`: Help Ananse carry the box of stories home. · _Take one end of the box. Go down the thread with Ananse._
- `a28-08-s2`: Watch what happens when Ananse lifts the lid. · _Stay on the step with Ananse._
- `a28-08-s3`: See if Ananse pays what he owes. · _Stay by the empty box on the step._

#### `a28-08-carry`

_The box is heavy. It is warm like bread, and it hums._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Careful! Every story in the world is in there.  
_You carry one end. Ananse carries the other._  

> **Lesson** (maths, 1.G.A.3, ask): sharing a load: halves  
> _Two carry one box. Does each carrier carry the whole box, or half?_  
> - ✅ Half. → Yes! Two carriers share it. Each carries half.
> - The whole box. → Two carriers share the load. Each carries half.
> _For grown-ups: Understood that two carriers share a load, each carrying half._

_Your Nubbin presses its ear to the lid._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Mine. All of them.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: My name on every one.

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps us wait  
> _Ananse finds it hard to wait. What helps us wait?_  
> - ✅ Taking a slow breath. → Yes! Slow breaths and counting help us wait.
> - Peeking anyway. → Peeking is hard to resist. Slow breaths help us wait better.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about things that help us wait, like slow breaths and counting._

_The stories fly over trees, hills and sea, to every place._  
_Stories travel when people tell them._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, SL.K.1, do): telling a story to someone  
> _(Tell a grown-up one little story. It can be about your day!)_  
> _Now your story has travelled, from you to them._  
> Check: `edu:tell:story:grown-up`
> _For grown-ups: Told a short story to a grown-up, passing it on the way storytellers do._
