## A28-9. The Pot of Wisdom

- `a28-09-s1`: Hold the pot while Ananse sweeps up all the wisdom. · _Follow Ananse and keep the pot upright._
- `a28-09-s2`: Watch Ananse try to climb with the pot. · _Stand at the foot of the tall tree._
- `a28-09-s3`: See what happens to the wisdom. · _Stay under the tall tree. Hold out your hands._

#### `a28-09-sweep`

_The forest flickers. For a moment you are back at the fire._  
**Nana Ama**: Long ago, they say, there was a spider called Kwaku Ananse.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): how a story begins: “Long ago, they say…”  
> _Storytellers often start with “Long ago, they say…”._  
> _Does that start a story, or end it?_  
> - ✅ It starts a story. → Yes! “Long ago, they say…” tells us a story is beginning.
> - It ends a story. → Stories end with “the end”. “Long ago, they say…” starts one.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed how a traditional story opening tells listeners that a tale is about to begin._

**Nana Ama**: One day he swept up all the wisdom in the world.  
_Back in the forest, Ananse is sweeping. Wisdom looks like bright dust._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Mine. All of it!  
_Your Nubbin gets swept into the pile. Ananse tips it out._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Not you. You are not wisdom.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: You are luggage.  

#### `a28-09-sweep-done`

**Kwaku Ananse**: Now I will hang it at the top of the tallest tree.  
_The tree is very tall. Ananse is very small._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare heights: taller and shorter  
> _(Look at the picture.) Which is taller, the tree or Ananse?_  
> - ✅ The tree. → Yes! The tree is much taller than Ananse.
> - Ananse. → Look again. The tree is far taller. Ananse is small.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two heights and said which was taller._


#### `a28-09-tree`

_Ananse ties the pot in front of him and starts to climb._  
_Bump! The pot hits the tree._  
_He slides down._  
_He tries again. Bump!_  
_Slide!_  
**Kwaku Ananse**: This tree is badly made.  
_A small spider is watching. It is Ntikuma, his son._  
**Ntikuma**: Father, tie the pot on your back. Then you can climb.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Hmph.  
_Ananse looks at the pot. He looks at his back._  
_He looks at his son._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): listening when a small person has a good idea  
> _Ntikuma is small, but he has a good idea. What should a grown-up do?_  
> - ✅ Listen to the idea. → Yes! Good ideas can come from anybody, big or small.
> - Ignore it. → Ignoring a good idea wastes it. Listening is wiser.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about listening to good ideas, even from someone small._


**Choices**

- **Try very hard not to laugh.**
    - You manage, just. Your Nubbin has its paws over its mouth.
- **Give Ntikuma a small nod.**
    - Ntikuma nods back, very seriously.
    - Two people who were each right about a pot.

#### `a28-09-scatter`

_Ananse sits in the tree with the pot in his lap._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: A small boy knew a thing I did not.  
_He throws the pot down. Crash!_  
_Pitter-patter!_  
_The wisdom flies out like dandelion seeds in the wind._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): wind carries dandelion seeds far away  
> _A dandelion seed has a fluffy top, like a tiny parachute._  
> _The wind blows it far away. Then a new flower can grow._  
> _Whoosh!_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the wind carries dandelion seeds to new places._

**Nana Ama**: That is why there is a little wisdom everywhere. Nobody has it all.  

#### `a28-09-scatter-done`

_The pieces land on ants, frogs and a very surprised goat._  
_None come your way._  
_Your Nubbin holds out its paws anyway. They stay empty._  
_It is a little sad. But it is glad it tried._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): trying is worthwhile even without a prize  
> _Your Nubbin tried, and got nothing. How might it feel?_  
> - ✅ A bit sad, but proud it tried. → Yes! We can feel sad and proud at once.
> - Nothing at all. → Look at its face. It feels a bit sad, and glad it tried.
> _For grown-ups: Named mixed feelings: sad about missing out and proud for having tried._

**Kwaku Ananse**: I would have thought of the back. Eventually.

> _The pot broke into two equal halves. How many halves make a whole pot?_  
> - ✅ Two. → Yes! Two equal halves make one whole.
> - Five. → Two halves make one whole. Count them: one half, two halves.

## A28-10. The Bald Head

- `a28-10-s1`: Go with Ananse and Aso to Aso’s mother’s funeral. · _Walk with them to the family house, where the drums are._
- `a28-10-s2`: Keep an eye on Ananse. He is up to something. · _Follow him round the back of the cooking fires._
- `a28-10-s3`: Help Ananse look dignified. · _Stay close to him in the crowd. It will not work, but try._

#### `a28-10-funeral`

_Aso’s mother has died. She was very old, and everyone loved her._  
_Died means her body stopped working. It will not start again._  
_Her family has come to remember her._  
_The yard is full of drums, food and cousins._  
_Being sad is allowed. People stay close and share food._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): families gather to remember someone who has died  
> _In Ghana, families come together when someone dies. What do they do?_  
> - ✅ Share food and remember her together. → Yes! Being together helps when we are sad.
> - Go away and be alone. → People stay together. Being together helps when we are sad.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that families and neighbours gather to remember someone, and that being together helps when we are sad._

**Aso**: She would have hated the fuss. She would have counted every chair.  
**A Cousin**: Kwaku! Will you eat?  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Eat? Never!  
**Kwaku Ananse**: I will fast out of respect.  
**Aso**: He has never fasted in his life.  

**Choices**

- **Tell Aso you’re sorry about her mother.**
    - **Aso**: Thank you. She was a hard woman, and fair.
    - **Aso**: She would have liked you.
- **Help carry chairs for the guests.**
    - You carry chairs. Your Nubbin carries a stool on its head.
    - Several aunties cheer.

#### `a28-10-funeral-done`

_The drums beat all morning. Boom, boom, boom!_  
_A drum has a skin. When you hit it, the skin shakes._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, do): a drum makes sound when its skin shakes  
> _(Tap a table with your hand. Can you feel it shake a tiny bit?)_  
> _A drum skin shakes, and the shaking makes the boom._  
> Check: `edu:feel:drum-skin:shake`
> _For grown-ups: Felt a tapped surface shake, and learned that shaking makes sound._

_By noon, Ananse looks at every pot like a dog at a gate._  

#### `a28-10-beans`

_Ananse slips behind the cooking fires. A pot of beans bubbles._  
_He scoops up hot beans. He has nowhere to put them!_  
_So he puts them in his hat, and puts the hat back on._  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Ow. Ow.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Ow ow ow.  
_A cousin comes round the corner. Ananse stands very straight._  
_He said he would not eat. Now he is hiding beans._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): keeping a promise  
> _Ananse said he would not eat. Then he took beans._  
> _Is that keeping a promise?_  
> - ✅ No. He broke it. → Yes. He broke his promise. Keeping promises matters.
> - Yes. He kept it. → He said he would not eat, but he did. That breaks a promise.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keeping promises and what it means to break one._


**Choices**

- **Whisper to Ananse to take the hat off.**
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: Take it off? In front of people?
    - **Kwaku Ananse**: With my dignity?
- **Step in front of him, so the cousin can’t see.**
    - You try. Ananse is short, but the steam is tall.

#### `a28-10-dance`

_The beans are very hot. Ananse begins to shake his head._  
_Shake, shake. Shake, shake, shake!_  
**A Cousin**: Kwaku, what are you doing?  
**Kwaku Ananse**: A dance! A hat-shaking dance.  
**Kwaku Ananse**: Very old. Very respectful.  
_Children join in, delighted. Your Nubbin dances too._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): a repeating pattern  
> _The children dance a pattern: clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap… What comes next?_  
> - ✅ Stomp. → Yes! Clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap, stomp. The pattern repeats.
> - Clap. → We just clapped. The pattern goes clap, stomp, so next is stomp.
> _For grown-ups: Continued a repeating clap-and-stomp pattern._

**Aso**: Kwaku. Stop.  

#### `a28-10-dance-done`

_Then the hat comes off on its own. The beans fly everywhere!_  
_Ananse’s head is bare and shiny. Everyone laughs, kindly._  
_Hot beans made the hat hot, and the hat made his head hot._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): heat moves from hot things to cooler things  
> _Ananse’s head is hot from the beans. What would cool it down?_  
> - ✅ A cool, wet leaf. → Yes! Something cool takes the heat away.
> - More hot beans. → More hot beans would make it hotter! A cool leaf cools it.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that hot things warm what they touch, and that something cool takes heat away._

_Ananse hides in the long grass with his hat in his hand._  
**Aso**: Serves him right. Mother would have laughed till she cried.  
_The funeral goes on, warmer than before._  
_People tell the story of the beans._  
_That is why the spider is bald, and keeps to the grass._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): recalling why something happened in a story  
> _In the story, why is the spider bald?_  
> - ✅ The beans were very hot. → Yes! The hot beans in his hat did it.
> - He got a haircut. → No haircut! The hot beans under his hat did it.
> _For grown-ups: Recalled the cause in a “why” story: the hot beans made the spider bald._


## A28-11. Across the Water

- `a28-11-s1`: Follow the page as it turns. See where the spider has gone. · _Touch the corner of the page when it lifts by itself._
- `a28-11-s2`: Sit on the step and listen to the elder. · _Take the space the children made for you._
- `a28-11-s3`: Hear Miss Ivy’s way of telling the gum story. · _Stay on the step until the story is done._

#### `a28-11-yard`

_The page lifts and turns. Now it is a different night._  
_Frogs sing. The air smells of the sea._  
_This is a yard in Jamaica. Jamaica is a warm island._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): Jamaica is a warm island  
> _Jamaica is a warm island in the Caribbean Sea. What would you wear there?_  
> - ✅ A sun hat. → Yes! It is warm and sunny in Jamaica.
> - A snow coat. → Jamaica is warm, not snowy. A sun hat is better.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Jamaica is a warm island in the Caribbean Sea._

_An old woman sits on the step with a cup of tea._  
_Children sit on the steps below. Your Nubbin sits with them._  

#### `a28-11-yard-done`

_One child budges up. There is room for you too._  
_Nobody asks where you came from._  
_Making room feels kind and warm._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): welcoming someone new  
> _A new child comes along. What can we do?_  
> - ✅ Make room and say hello. → Yes! Making room helps a new friend feel welcome.
> - Turn our backs. → Turning away feels lonely. Making room feels welcoming.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about welcoming someone new by making room and saying hello._


#### `a28-11-step`

**A Boy on the Step**: Miss Ivy, tell an Anancy one. Please.  
**Miss Ivy**: Which one have I not told you yet?  
**A Boy on the Step**: You have told us all of them.  
**Miss Ivy**: Then I will tell one again. That is what they are for.  
_She says where Anancy comes from, like saying where a cousin lives._  
**Miss Ivy**: Long ago, people were taken from Africa by force.  
**Miss Ivy**: They were made to cross the sea.  
**Miss Ivy**: That was wrong. They kept their stories, and nobody could take those.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): stories can be kept and passed on through hard times  
> _Miss Ivy says the people kept something nobody could take. What was it?_  
> - ✅ Their stories. → Yes. They kept their stories, and told them to their children.
> - Their houses. → Their stories. Stories travel inside people, so nobody can take them.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people who were taken from Africa kept their stories and passed them on._

_The children nod. They know._  
_This is where the story stands._  

#### `a28-11-step-done`

**Miss Ivy**: Now. Anancy, and the gum.  
_Frogs sing in the dark. They call loudly to each other._  
_Frogs sing so other frogs can find them._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): frogs call to each other  
> _Why do frogs sing at night?_  
> - ✅ To call to other frogs. → Yes! Frogs call so other frogs can find them.
> - To make soup. → Silly! Frogs sing to call to other frogs.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that frogs sing to call to each other._


#### `a28-11-gum`

**Miss Ivy**: Anancy was stealing peas from a farmer’s field. Every night, a few more.  
**Miss Ivy**: So the farmer made a little man of wood, and covered him in gum.  
**Miss Ivy**: Anancy said good evening. The little man said nothing.  
_The children mouth the next part along with her._  
**Miss Ivy**: So Anancy slapped him, and stuck. Then the other hand, and stuck again.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): who gets stuck in this telling of the story  
> _In Miss Ivy’s story, who got stuck to the gum man?_  
> - ✅ Anancy. → Yes! In her story, Anancy got stuck.
> - The fairy. → The fairy was in your story. In Miss Ivy’s, Anancy got stuck.
> _For grown-ups: Compared two tellings of one story and said who got stuck in this one._

_In her story, Anancy got caught. In yours, he was the one catching._  

**Choices**

- **Tell her you heard it the other way round.**
    - **Miss Ivy**: Did you now? Where?
    - **You**: A long way off. The spider made the doll, and a fairy got stuck.
    - **Miss Ivy**: Well. That one is right too.
    - **Miss Ivy**: He gets about, that spider.
- **Just listen to the end.**
    - **Miss Ivy**: And how did he get loose? The same way as always.
    - **Miss Ivy**: He talked.
    - The children cheer.

#### `a28-11-gum-done`

_Your Nubbin looks at its paw. It has stuck to lots of things today._  
_Silk. Sap._  
_Gum. Web._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count four things to find how many  
> _(Count on your fingers: silk, sap, gum, web.)_  
> _One, two, three, four. Four sticky things!_  
> Check: `edu:count:sticky-things:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted four sticky things, one finger for each._

_Four sticky things!_  

#### `a28-11-complete`

_The lamp on the nail hums. Somebody turns the radio off._  
**Miss Ivy**: There are a hundred ways to tell him.  
**Miss Ivy**: Every one is right, if he gets away at the end.  
_Two tellings of one story, on two sides of an ocean._  
_Neither one is wrong._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): respecting that people tell things differently  
> _Two people tell a story in different ways. Can both tellings be good?_  
> - ✅ Yes, both can be good. → Yes! Each teller can tell it their own way.
> - Only one can. → Many tellers can each tell it their own way. Both can be good.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how two different tellings of one story can both be good._

_The page lifts. It begins to turn back._  

## A28-12. Take Some Elsewhere

- `a28-12-s1`: Come back to the courtyard fire. · _Let the page turn back. Find your mat by the fire._
- `a28-12-s2`: Tell the courtyard a story of your own. · _Stand by the stool. You know which story it is._
- `a28-12-s3`: Hear the storyteller’s last story of the night. · _Sit back down on your mat._

#### `a28-12-return`

_The page turns back. It is the courtyard again._  
_The fire is low. The children are sleepy._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a fire needs wood to keep burning  
> _The fire is low. What does it need to keep burning?_  
> - ✅ More wood. → Yes! A fire needs wood to burn.
> - More water. → Water puts a fire out! A fire needs wood to keep burning.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a fire needs wood (fuel) to keep burning._

_Moths flutter by the wall._  
**Nana Ama**: Another story? It is late.  
**Nana Ama**: Long ago, they say, there was a spider… no. I have told enough.  
**Nana Ama**: Somebody else tells one now. You.  
**Nana Ama**: Your turn.  
_Your Nubbin climbs up on the stool beside her._  

#### `a28-12-return-done`

_The children turn on their mats to look at you._  
_Four children sit on the front mat. Four sit on the next mat._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): add within 10: 4 and 4  
> _Four children on one mat. Four on another._  
> _How many children altogether?_  
> - ✅ Eight. → Yes! Four and four make eight.
> - Four. → That is one mat. Four and four more make eight.
> _For grown-ups: Added two groups of four to make eight._

_Everyone waits, just as they waited for her._  

#### `a28-12-tell`

**You**: This one is about a fairy and a doll covered in gum.  
_You tell them about the odum tree, the yam and the thank-you._  
_You tell them how she stuck, and how the spider ran for rope._  
**You**: While he was gone, somebody waited by a root.  
**You**: It was not their story to change.  
**You**: She went up to the sky caught.  
**You**: But she went up with her chin high.  
_The courtyard is quiet. A small boy at the front frowns._  
_That is a good sign._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): retelling events in order: first, then, last  
> _What came first: the fairy ate the yam, or she got stuck?_  
> - ✅ She ate the yam. → Yes! First the yam. Then she got stuck.
> - She got stuck. → She ate the yam first. Then she got stuck.
> _For grown-ups: Retold a story in order, saying what happened first._

**Nana Ama**: Hm. That one is a true one.  
**Nana Ama**: Things get caught. That is how it is.  
**Nana Ama**: I will keep a piece of that. The chin.  

#### `a28-12-tell-done`

_The storyteller keeps a piece of your story, safe._  
_The children whisper it to each other._  
_It feels good when someone listens to you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): listening well to a friend  
> _How can you listen well when a friend is talking?_  
> - ✅ Look at them and wait my turn. → Yes! Looking and waiting shows you care.
> - Talk over them. → Talking over a friend is hard to listen to. Looking and waiting is kind.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how to listen well: look at the speaker and wait for your turn._


#### `a28-12-last`

**Nana Ama**: One more. A short one.  
**Nana Ama**: I heard it from a spider.  
**Nana Ama**: A small round one paid a buttercup for a story.  
**Nana Ama**: The story was one word long. The word was the spider’s name.  
_Your Nubbin sits up straight on the stool._  
**Nana Ama**: The small round one thought it fair. And it was right.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): recalling who did what in a story  
> _Who paid a buttercup for a story?_  
> - ✅ The small round one. → Yes! The small round one paid a buttercup.
> - The leopard. → It was the small round one, with a buttercup.
> _For grown-ups: Recalled who paid a buttercup for a story._

**Nana Ama**: It was a story about someone. That is all stories are.  

#### `a28-12-last-done`

_The children are quiet for a moment. Then they stretch and yawn._  
_Sparks from the fire float up and up._  
_Hot air goes up. It carries the sparks._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): hot air rises  
> _Sparks float up from the fire. Which way does hot air go?_  
> - ✅ Up. → Yes! Hot air goes up, and it carries the sparks with it.
> - Down. → Hot air goes up. That is why the sparks float up.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that hot air rises, which carries sparks upward._

**The Children**: Some come back!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): sharing stories keeps a tradition alive  
> _The storyteller says, “Take some with you.”_  
> _What do we do with a story we love?_  
> - ✅ Share it with someone. → Yes! Sharing a story keeps it alive.
> - Hide it forever. → Stories are for sharing. Telling them keeps them alive.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that sharing stories keeps traditions alive._

## A30-1. The Jewish Town

- `a30-01-s1`: Step into the brown-ink page and find the caretaker’s house. · _Touch the page, then follow the lane to the door with the ring of keys._
- `a30-01-s2`: Carry water from the well with Rivka. · _Rivka knows the way. The well is where three lanes meet._
- `a30-01-s3`: Fetch the bread from Hannah’s bakery. · _The bakery is the door with the warm step. Your Nubbin has found it already._

#### `a30-01-page`

_Nova’s atlas opens at a page of brown ink._  
_There is a steep roof, little houses, and a wavy line of water._  
**Ori**: This is Prague, a city. A wavy line runs right through it.  
**Ori**: (Point to the wavy line.)  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): finding a river on a map  
> **Ori**: A map shows land and water. What is the wavy line of water?  
> - ✅ A river → Yes! The river is called the Vltava. It runs through the middle of Prague.
> - A road → A road is for walking. Water is blue and wavy. It is a river!
> - A roof → The roof is the steep triangle on top. The wavy line is a river.
> _For grown-ups: Read a simple map: found the river, the Vltava, and Prague as a city beside it._

**Ori**: Long ago, people told a story about this place.  
**Ori**: It is a story, not a fact.  
_Rabbi Loew was a real teacher here._  
_The clay man is only in the story._  
_You step into the page._  
_A kind man with a ring of keys waves at you._  
**Avram**: I am Avram. I look after the keys.  
**Avram**: You can be our lodger.  

**Choices**

- **Shake his hand.**
    - **Avram**: A good grip! You will carry water.
- **Ask which key is which.**
    - **Avram**: This one is the big door. This one is the cupboard.
    - **Avram**: This one? I do not know!
- **Take the basket he is carrying.**
    - He lets you take it. He looks pleased that you helped without being asked.

#### `a30-01-page-done`

**Dvora**: Come in, come in! Water first, and then you can rest.  
**Rivka**: I will show you the well! I know the well best of all!  
_Rivka hops from one foot to the other. She cannot wait._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming a feeling  
> _Rivka is hopping and grinning. How does Rivka feel?_  
> - ✅ Excited → Yes! Excited. Her feet cannot keep still.
> - Sleepy → Not sleepy. Sleepy people yawn. Rivka is hopping. She is excited!
> - Cross → Not cross. She is grinning. She is excited!
> _For grown-ups: Named a feeling (excited) from how someone looks and moves._


#### `a30-01-water`

_Rivka walks backwards the whole way, so she can talk to you._  
**Rivka**: That is the study house. That is Hannah’s bakery.  
**Rivka**: Do not look, you will want it!  
**Rivka**: Worn-out books are put to rest in the attic, not thrown away.  
_At the well you fill two buckets. Your Nubbin fills one little cup._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): counting up to 3  
> _You have two buckets. Your Nubbin has one cup._  
> _(Count them on your fingers.)_  
> - ✅ 3 things → Yes! Two buckets and one cup. One, two, three!
> - 2 things → Let us count again: bucket, bucket, cup. That is three!
> - 4 things → Count with me: one, two, three. Three things, not four.
> _For grown-ups: Added 2 and 1 with objects to make 3._

_Plop! Plop!_  
_The water splashes and sparkles._  

#### `a30-01-water-done`

**Dvora**: Good. Now you are guests.  
**Dvora**: Rivka, take them to the bakery before it shuts.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): the first sound of a word  
> **Dvora**: Bakery. Bread.  
> **Dvora**: Both start with the same sound. Which word starts the same: bread or well?  
> - ✅ Bread → Yes! B, b, bakery. B, b, bread. The same sound at the start.
> - Well → Well starts with w. Bakery and bread both start with b!
> _For grown-ups: Matched the first sound b in bakery and bread._

_Rivka grins. She loves the bakery._  

#### `a30-01-bakery`

_Your Nubbin sits on the bakery step._  
_The step is warm, and its eyes are shut._  
**Hannah**: Is this one yours? It has not moved since you came.  
_Behind Hannah, plaited loaves stand in rows, waiting for Friday._  
**Hannah**: Those are for the Sabbath. This is a crust I burnt.  
**Hannah**: It is for you.  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-4, ask): baking cannot be undone  
> **Hannah**: The soft dough went into the hot oven and came out as bread.  
> **Hannah**: Can it turn back into dough?  
> - ✅ No, heat changed it for good → Right! Baking changes dough for good.
> - Yes, it can → Not this time. Once bread is baked, it cannot go back to dough.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that baking changes dough into bread and it cannot be changed back._

_Your Nubbin holds the crust in both paws, as if it were a medal._  

#### `a30-01-complete`

_The loft is small and smells of apples._  
_Across the lane, a lamp still burns in the study house. Someone is reading._  
**Rivka**: That is the rabbi. He reads all night sometimes.  
_Your Nubbin falls asleep with flour on its nose._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): what helps when you are tired  
> _It was a big day. Your Nubbin is tired._  
> _What helps when we are tired?_  
> - ✅ Rest and sleep → Yes. Rest helps bodies feel better.
> - Running faster → Running makes us more tired! Rest is what helps.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about tiredness and that rest helps._

_The study house is one long room full of books and noise._  
_Students sit in pairs, and talk and talk about one page._

> _In the study house, students learn in pairs and talk it out._  
> _How do they learn?_  
> - ✅ Together, with a partner → Yes! Two heads think better than one.
> - All alone and silent → Not here! In this study house everyone talks.
> _For grown-ups: Compared how students learned in the past (talking in pairs) with today._

_At the front sits an old man with a grey beard._  
**Rabbi Loew**: Here is a very old story.

**Rabbi Loew**: So the wise man knew he was only clay.  

#### `a30-02-study-done`

_The rabbi lets the story sit in the room._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): knowing who a story is about  
> _In the rabbi’s story, who was made of clay and could not answer?_  
> - ✅ A clay man → Yes! A man made of clay.
> - A baker → The baker is Hannah. The story was about a man made of clay.
> _For grown-ups: Named the character in a short story._

_It is like bread that must rest before you cut it._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): showing feelings without words

> - ✅ It bounces and smiles → Yes! Faces and bodies show feelings, even without words.
> - It cannot show anything → It can! Smiles, bounces and hugs tell us how someone feels.

## A30-4. The Answer

- `a30-04-s1`: Take the rabbi his supper in the study house. · _Dvora has wrapped it in a cloth. He will forget to eat it._
- `a30-04-s2`: Listen to what the rabbi asks of you. · _He is at the study house door with two men._
- `a30-04-s3`: Light the lantern in Avram’s window. · _The lantern hangs by the door._

#### `a30-04-ask`

_Dvora sends you across the lane with bread and soup._  
_The rabbi sits very still with his hand over his eyes._  
**Rabbi Loew**: I asked how to keep my town safe. That was all.  
**Rabbi Loew**: The answer is: be patient, be careful, be kind, and wait.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): calm waiting  
> _The rabbi has to wait. What can help us wait?_  
> - ✅ Slow breaths → Yes. In through the nose. Out through the mouth. Slowly.
> - Shouting → Shouting makes waiting feel harder. Slow breaths help.
> _For grown-ups: Practised the idea that slow breathing helps while we wait._

_Your Nubbin pushes the soup an inch closer. It is a good suggestion._  

#### `a30-04-ask-done`

_In the morning the bowl is empty._  
_The rabbi is asleep at the table, with his cheek on a book._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): food and sleep help bodies  
> _The rabbi ate his soup and had a sleep._  
> _What do bodies need to stay strong?_  
> - ✅ Food and sleep → Yes! Food, water and sleep keep us strong.
> - Only sweets → Sweets are a treat. Bodies need good food and sleep.
> _For grown-ups: Named food and sleep as things bodies need._


#### `a30-04-helpers`

_By noon the rabbi looks calm. Two men stand beside him._  
_Isaac is broad and quiet. Jacob is thin and quick._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): telling characters apart  
> _Isaac is broad and quiet. Jacob is thin and quick._  
> _Which one is quick?_  
> - ✅ Jacob → Yes! Jacob is thin and quick.
> - Isaac → Isaac is broad and quiet. Jacob is the quick one.

## A30-5. Clay from the River

- `a30-05-s1`: Follow the three of them to the river, at a distance. · _Keep well back. Stop at the willows above the bank._
- `a30-05-s2`: Let your Nubbin help, if they will have it. · _Your Nubbin has made up its own mind. Stay on the bank._

#### `a30-05-follow`

_You follow at a distance, through the sleeping lanes, out to the river._  
_The river is wide and dark, and it talks to itself._  
_You stop in the willows. Your Nubbin holds on to your trouser leg._  
_Below you, three people kneel on the mud with their sleeves rolled up._  
_They dig clay out of the river bank with their hands._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, ask): places give people what they need  
> _The three people take clay from the river bank._  
> _Where does the clay come from?_  
> - ✅ From the river bank → Yes! Rivers leave soft clay on their banks.
> - From the sky → Not from the sky. The clay is in the mud by the river.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that people use what a place gives them, like clay from a river bank._


**Choices**

- **Go a little closer.**
    - You go one tree closer, and stop.
    - It feels like walking into a quiet room.
- **Stay where you are.**
    - You stay in the willows. Your Nubbin looks up at you, thinking.

#### `a30-05-clay`

_The clay on the ground makes a shape: a head, shoulders, two long arms._  
_It is as long as a door._  
_The three people smooth it, like making bread._  
_The wind dries the clay._  
_Isaac carries water up from the river in cupped hands, but it is slow._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): clay is soft when wet and hard when dry  
> _Wet clay is soft. What happens when the wind dries it?_  
> - ✅ It gets hard → Yes! Dry clay is hard. Wet clay is soft.
> - It gets bigger → It does not grow. Dry clay gets hard, so it needs water to stay soft.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that clay is soft when wet and hard when dry._

_Your Nubbin runs down the bank, fills its cheeks, and trots back._  
_Splish! It wets the clay, very carefully._  
_Then it goes again, and again._  

#### `a30-05-clay-done`

_Near dawn Isaac carries your Nubbin up the bank himself._  
_It is muddy up to its ears._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): feeling proud after helping  
> _Your Nubbin helped all night. How might it feel now?_  
> - ✅ Proud → Yes! Helping can make us feel proud.
> - Grumpy → It might be a bit tired, but helping usually feels proud.
> _For grown-ups: Named the feeling of pride after helping._

**Isaac**: Go home. He knows you are here.

> **Lesson** (literacy, L.2.4, ask): the meaning of mind  
> _Rivka was minding the lantern. What does it mean to mind a lantern?_  
> - ✅ To look after it → Yes! To mind something means to look after it.
> - To shout at it → No shouting. To mind something means to look after it.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that mind can mean look after._

_You put a blanket over her._  
_Your Nubbin curls up on the end of it._

#### `a30-07-chores`

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): life in the past and today  
> _In Prague long ago, people fetched water from a well._  
> _Where does your water come from now?_  
> - ✅ From a tap → Yes! Most of us turn on a tap. Long ago, people carried water.
> - From a cloud, by hand → Rain comes from clouds, but at home water comes through pipes to a tap.
> _For grown-ups: Compared how people got water long ago (a well) and today (a tap)._

**Avram**: Told to sweep the step, he sweeps the step. Only the step!

_Your Nubbin bails with its cheeks, which does not help at all._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): taking away  
> _The barrel holds 3 buckets. Yossele poured 5._  
> _How many buckets too many?_  
> - ✅ 2 → Yes! Five take away three is two.
> - 3 → Let us count: five buckets, take away three. Two are left over.
> - 5 → Five is how many he poured. Take away the three that fit: two too many.
> _For grown-ups: Took away 3 from 5 in a story about buckets._

_Then the rabbi says, “Stop,” and Yossele puts the bucket down._

## A30-9. Fridays

> - Racing → No racing! It is a day of rest, after all the hurrying on Friday.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Sabbath is a day of rest that begins on Friday evening._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.His.2.K-2, ask): the Sabbath as a day of rest

> - ✅ A day of rest → Yes! A day to rest and be together.
> - A day of work → No work on the Sabbath! It is a day of rest.
> _For grown-ups: Reinforced that the Sabbath is a day of rest and being together._

_Shmuel thinks about this, and nods, and eats his bread._

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): stars come out at night  
> _Three stars are out, and the Sabbath is over. When do we see stars?_  
> - ✅ At night → Yes! Stars shine all day, but we only see them when the sky is dark.
> - At lunchtime → The Sun is too bright at lunchtime. We see stars when the sky is dark.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we see stars when the sky is dark, at night._

_The rabbi, Isaac and Jacob carry the clay up the lane on a door._

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): treating old books with respect  
> _The attic is where worn-out holy books are put to rest._

> - ✅ People respect them → Yes! People treat words they love with respect.
> - There is no room → It is about respect, not room. People treat special books with care.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that worn-out holy books are kept respectfully, not thrown away._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): what helps a sad friend

> - Tell them to hurry up → Hurrying does not help. Sitting beside them does.

> - Pretending we do not miss them → Missing someone is a big feeling. It helps to say it, and to tell stories.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about what helps when we miss someone: feelings are allowed, and stories keep them close._

    - You sit on the corn, and so does your Nubbin. Xquic laughs.

#### `a31-05-complete`

**Xmucane**: Well. You are my son’s wife, then.  
**Xmucane**: Come in. It is cold.  
_She puts a log on the fire. She gives Xquic the good stool._  
**Grandmother**: That is how grandmothers say sorry.  
**Granddaughter**: You never give me the good stool!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): saying sorry and making it better  
> _Xmucane said sorry by giving the good stool. How can you say sorry?_  
> - ✅ Say sorry, and help to fix it → Yes. Words and kind actions together say sorry best.
> - Run away → Running away leaves the sorry feeling stuck. Saying sorry and helping works better.
> _For grown-ups: Practised how to say sorry with words and kind actions._

**Grandmother**: You never carried a net of corn.  

## A31-6. The Older Brothers

- `a31-06-s1`: Meet the twins. · _Wait by the house until two boys come down the hill._
- `a31-06-s2`: Watch the older brothers climb the tree. · _Stand well back from the tree._
- `a31-06-s3`: Wait with Xmucane by the door. · _Stand by the door and watch the trees._

#### `a31-06-born`

_Twins are born on the mountain: Hunahpu and Xbalanque._  
_They are loud from the first minute._  
**One Monkey**: Put them outside! We are busy!  
**Grandmother**: The twins grew up outside, with blowguns. And very cheeky!  
_Years pass in one breath. Two boys come down the hill._  
**Hunahpu**: Hello! A guest, and a guest’s guest!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds  
> _Hunahpu starts with “h”. (Say it: h, h, Hunahpu.)_  
> _Which of these starts with “h” too?_  
> - ✅ Hat → Yes! Hunahpu, hat. Both start with h.
> - Sun → Sun starts with “s”. Hunahpu and hat both start with “h”.
> - Ball → Ball starts with “b”. Hunahpu and hat both start with “h”.
> _For grown-ups: Matched a first sound (“h” in Hunahpu and hat)._

_Your Nubbin and the twins are friends at once._  

**Choices**

- **Say hello.**
    - **Hunahpu**: Good. Are you hungry?
    - **Hunahpu**: Nobody here eats till our brothers eat.
- **Ask about the blowguns.**
    - **Xbalanque**: A long tube. You blow, and a clay ball pops out at a target.

#### `a31-06-tree`

**Hunahpu**: We found lovely birds up that tree. Somebody taller should look.  
**One Artisan**: Fine. Artists can climb.  
_The two older brothers climb up. Then the tree begins to grow!_  
**One Monkey**: It is getting bigger! Why?  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): positions: above and below  
> _The brothers are up in the tree._  
> _Are they above the ground, or below it?_  
> - ✅ Above the ground → Yes! Up in the tree is above the ground.
> - Below the ground → Below is under the ground. The brothers are up in the tree, above it.
> _For grown-ups: Used the position words above and below._

**Xbalanque**: Tie your cloths behind you, and you can climb down!  
_They do. The ends of the cloths turn into curly tails!_  

**Choices**

- **Laugh.**
    - Your Nubbin falls over backwards. That is how it laughs.
- **Ask if they are all right.**
    - **Hunahpu**: They are fine. Look.
    - **Hunahpu**: They have never been happier in a tree.

#### `a31-06-laugh`

_The brothers swing off into the trees as monkeys._  
**Xmucane**: Where are my older boys?  
**Hunahpu**: Do not laugh when you see them, Grandmother.  
_They swing back, with long arms and curly tails and very serious faces._  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): monkeys use arms and tails to swing and hold on  
> **Grandmother**: Monkeys swing with their long arms.  
> **Grandmother**: In Guatemala, spider monkeys use their tails like a fifth hand!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that monkeys’ arms and tails help them climb, and spider monkeys grip with their tails._

**Xmucane**: I am not laughing. I am not.  
_She laughs! They swing back up into the trees._  
**Grandmother**: Do not be sad for them. They still paint and play flutes up there.  

**Choices**

- **Try not to laugh too.**
    - Your face goes red. Your Nubbin does not even try.
- **Wave to the monkeys.**
    - One waves back, upside down, and plays three notes on a flute.

#### `a31-06-complete`

_That night there is flute music in the trees._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): kind laughing and unkind laughing  
> _Which is a kind laugh?_  
> - ✅ Laughing together at something funny → Yes! Laughing together is kind.
> - Laughing at someone who is crying → That would hurt. A kind laugh is a laugh together.
> _For grown-ups: Told a kind laugh (together) from an unkind laugh (at someone who is hurt)._

**Xmucane**: Did I do that?  
**Xbalanque**: You laughed, Grandmother. They are happy up there.  
**Hunahpu**: Also, it was funny.  
_Xmucane gives the twins supper first, for the first time._

## A31-8. Zipacna and Earthquake

- `a31-08-s1`: Help the twins make a crab that is not a crab. · _Gather leaves, red flowers and a flat stone._
- `a31-08-s2`: Watch Zipacna go after the crab. · _Hide up on the edge of the ravine._
- `a31-08-s3`: Dig wet clay from the riverbank. · _The clay is at the bend of the river._

#### `a31-08-crab`

**Grandmother**: Seven Macaw had two sons. Both bigger, and both worse.  
**Grandmother**: Zipacna was unkind to the Four Hundred Boys, and they died.  
**Grandmother**: That means their bodies stopped working. In the story, they became stars.  
**Grandmother**: Zipacna loved crabs. That was his weak spot.  
_You gather broad leaves and red flowers._  
_Xbalanque finds a flat stone for the shell._  
_Your Nubbin finds a stick for a claw._  
**Xbalanque**: Best crab I have seen that is not a crab!  

> **Lesson** (art, K.G.A.2, do): name a shape: circle  
> **Xbalanque**: Look at the crab’s shell. It is a circle.  
> **Xbalanque**: Round and round!  
> _(Tap the round shell. What shape is it?)_  
> Check: `edu:tap:shape:circle`
> _For grown-ups: Named a circle in the shell of a crab they helped build._


**Choices**

    - Now the crab is looking at you.

#### `a31-08-zipacna`

_Zipacna comes down the river, big and hungry._  
**Zipacna**: A crab? Where?  
**Hunahpu**: Down there, under the mountain.  
_He squeezes in under the mountain to reach it._  
_Then the mountain settles with a long, slow sigh._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): Guatemala has many mountains and volcanoes  
> **Grandmother**: Guatemala has many mountains. Some of them are volcanoes.  
> **Grandmother**: The K’iche’ highlands are high up in the mountains.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that Guatemala has many mountains and volcanoes, and that the K’iche’ highlands are high up._

**Grandmother**: Zipacna stayed there a very long time. He never carried mountains again.  
_Your Nubbin takes its stick back, very carefully._  

**Choices**

- **Keep very quiet.**
    - You are so quiet you can hear your Nubbin thinking about the stick.
- **Pat the mountain.**
    - The mountain does not seem to mind.

#### `a31-08-earthquake`

**Grandmother**: The second son was Earthquake. He stamped, and mountains shook loose.  
**Xbalanque**: He is hungry. We need clay.  
_You dig wet clay from the riverbank. It is soft and squishy._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, ask): wet clay is soft; dry clay is hard  
> _Wet clay is soft and squishy._  
> _What happens to clay when it dries in the sun?_  
> - ✅ It goes hard → Yes! Dry clay goes hard. That is how pots are made.
> - It stays squishy → Wet clay is squishy. When it dries, it goes hard.
> _For grown-ups: Found out that wet clay is soft and dry clay is hard._

_The twins coat a roast bird all over in clay._  
**Earthquake**: That smells good! Is that for me?  
_He eats it and sits down. He is very sleepy now._  
_The ground still shakes a little when he turns over in his sleep._  

**Choices**

- **Wash the clay off in the river.**
    - Your Nubbin does not want clean paws. It prints them everywhere.
- **Put your ear to the ground.**
    - Far down, very faint, there is a snore.

## A31-9. The Rat

- `a31-09-s1`: Help the twins clear the garden. · _Go to the garden and keep watch with the dove._
- `a31-09-s2`: Wait in the garden at night. · _Hide behind the bush with the twins._
- `a31-09-s3`: Take the water jar to Xmucane at the river. · _Take it slowly._

#### `a31-09-tools`

_The twins should clear a garden. Their tools do it for them!_  
**Hunahpu**: Hoe, dig! Axe, chop!  
_A dove sits on the fence as a lookout._  
_In the morning the garden is a forest again. Every tree is back!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-1, notice): seeds wait in the soil for water and light, then grow  
> **Grandmother**: Seeds can sleep in the soil for a long time.  
> **Grandmother**: When rain and sun come, they wake up and grow!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that seeds in the soil grow when they get water and light._

**Hunahpu**: What? Who did this?  

**Choices**

- **Let your Nubbin help the hoe.**
    - It holds the handle and gets dragged round the garden.
- **Keep watch with the dove.**
    - The dove nods at you, one lookout to another.

#### `a31-09-night`

_That night you hide behind a bush with the twins._  
_At midnight the animals come: the puma, the jaguar, the deer, the rabbit._  
_They tell the trees to stand up again, and the trees do._  
_Hunahpu catches a rat by the tail and holds it up, gently._  
**Rat**: Do not eat me! I know a secret!  
**Rat**: Your dad’s ball and gloves are up in your gran’s roof!  
**Rat**: I want food for ever. That is my price.  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): a fair swap: both sides get something  
> _The rat gives a secret. The twins give food._  
> _Is that a fair swap?_  
> - ✅ Yes, both get something good → Yes! A swap is fair when both sides get something good.
> - No, nobody gets anything → Both get something: the rat gets food, and the twins get the secret.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a swap is fair when both sides get something good._


**Choices**

- **Tell the rat it is a fair price.**
    - **Rat**: A fair price! You hear that?
    - **Rat**: The guest says fair.
- **Let your Nubbin say hello.**
    - Your Nubbin touches noses with the rat. The rat sneezes.
    - That counts.

#### `a31-09-roof`

**Hunahpu**: Grandmother, this chilli sauce is hot! We need water!  
_Xmucane goes to the river with the big jar._  
_You follow with a small one._  
_A mosquito lands on her jar and makes a tiny hole._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, ask): spot a problem to solve  
> _The jar has a hole, and the water runs out._  
> _What problem must we solve?_  
> - ✅ Stop the hole, so the water stays in → Yes! First we must stop the hole.
> - Pour the water faster → Faster does not stop the leak. We must stop the hole.
> _For grown-ups: Named a problem to solve (a leaking jar)._

**Mosquito**: Pardon me. So sorry.  
**Mosquito**: Pardon.  
_Water pours out of the hole! Everyone helps._  
_At home, the rat chews a cord._  
_Down falls a bundle: a ball and gloves._  
**Xbalanque**: Father’s.  

**Choices**

- **Bring the rat a share of your own lunch too.**
    - You give the rat half your tortilla.
    - It looks at you for a long time.
    - **Rat**: You. I will remember you.
- **Leave it to the twins.**
    - **Xbalanque**: From now on, rat, you eat what we eat.
    - **Xbalanque**: Nobody chases you out of the corn.
    - **Rat**: For ever is a good length.
- **Ask the rat to come with you to Xibalba.**
    - **Rat**: Xibalba? Me?
    - **Rat**: There are owls down there.
    - **Rat**: Fine. But I am riding on your Nubbin.

## A31-10. The Summons

- `a31-10-s1`: Follow the message to the ballcourt. · _Go with the louse. It is not quick._
- `a31-10-s2`: See the twins plant their corn, and choose where you will be. · _Stand by the hearth while they plant._

#### `a31-10-relay`

_The owls come to Xmucane’s door with the lords’ message._  
**Xmucane**: Go and tell my grandsons, little louse. Quickly!  
_The louse is not quick. A toad gives it a lift, inside its mouth._  
_Then a snake gives the toad a lift._  
_Then a falcon gives the snake a lift._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): what happens first, next, last  
> _The louse rode in the toad. The toad rode in the snake._  
> _Who gave the very last lift?_  
> - ✅ The falcon → Yes! The falcon gave the last lift, carrying the snake.
> - The toad → The toad gave the first lift. The falcon gave the last.
> _For grown-ups: Followed the order of events in a story: first, next, last._

_At the ballcourt, out pops the snake. Then the toad._  
**Toad**: The louse is fine. It is just a bit stuck.  
**Louse**: Your grandmother says come home. The lords say come down.  

**Choices**

- **Thank every messenger in turn.**
    - The falcon looks embarrassed. The louse bows.
- **Try not to laugh at the louse.**
    - **Louse**: Laugh if you like. I got here, did I not?

#### `a31-10-corn`

_Before they go, each twin plants an ear of corn in the house._  
**Hunahpu**: Look at these every day, Grandmother.  
**Xbalanque**: If the corn goes dry, we are in trouble.  
**Xbalanque**: If it stays green, we are doing well.  
**Xmucane**: And if it does both?  

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): plants need water and sun to stay green  
> _Corn stays green when it has what it needs. What does a plant need?_  
> - ✅ Water and sunshine → Yes! Plants need water and sunshine to stay green.
> - Toys and a hat → Plants do not need toys. They need water and sunshine.
> _For grown-ups: Said that plants need water and sunlight._

**Hunahpu**: Then we are being clever.  
_The twins pick up their father’s gear. Your Nubbin looks at you._  

**Choices**

- **Stay with Xmucane and watch the corn.**
    - **Xmucane**: Oh. You do not have to.
    - She moves her stool over, so there is room for yours.
- **Go down with the twins.**
    - **Xbalanque**: Good. Bring the little one.
    - **Xbalanque**: We need someone who can fetch.
    - **Xmucane**: Look after them. And look after yourself.

#### `a31-10-complete`

_In the morning the twins walk off down the road, bouncing their father’s ball._  
_Behind them, two ears of corn stand green in the house._  
**Grandmother**: Now. Which way did you go?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): what helps when we wait  
> _Staying and going are both brave. Waiting can be hard._  
> _What helps when we wait?_  
> - ✅ A job to do, and a friend beside us → Yes. A job and a friend make waiting easier.
> - Sitting alone and worrying → Worrying alone is heavy. A job and a friend help us wait.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when we have to wait: a job and a friend._

_The page waits, as if it is listening._  

## A31-11. The Crossroads

- `a31-11-s1`: Follow the news of the road to the crossroads. · _Go with the twins, or wait with Xmucane._

#### `a31-11-road`

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Geo.2.K-2, notice): where roads cross is a crossroads, and a map shows roads from above  
> **Grandmother**: Where roads cross, that place is called a crossroads.

> - It does not matter → Names matter. When we say a name, the person feels noticed.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why saying someone’s name is kind._

## A31-12. The Houses

- `a31-12-s1`: Spend the night in the Dark House, or sit up with Xmucane. · _Stay close to the light, or the corn._
- `a31-12-s2`: Go through the other houses, or do the house’s work. · _Carry pine cones, or fetch water and look at the corn._

#### `a31-12-dark`

_The lords send the twins to the Dark House._  
_They get a torch and two little candles._  
**Lords of Xibalba**: Keep them lit all night. Give them back whole in the morning.  
_It is as dark as a cupboard with the door shut._  
**Hunahpu**: So we do not light them.  
_Hunahpu ties a red feather on the torch._  
_In the dark, it looks like a flame!_  
_Xbalanque puts a firefly on each candle. They glow on, off, on._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, notice): we see things when there is light; fireflies make their own light  
> **Grandmother**: We can only see when there is light.  
> **Grandmother**: The guard saw a glow, so he thought the torch was lit.  
> **Grandmother**: Fireflies make their own light inside their bodies. It does not burn!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that we see things when there is light, and that fireflies make their own cool light._

_A guard looks in, sees the glow, and goes away._  

**Choices**

- **Help catch the fireflies.**
    - You catch one in your cupped hands. It glows, pleased to help.
- **Let your Nubbin hold the torch.**
    - It holds the torch very upright. The feather does not burn.

#### `a31-12-dark-done`

_Not burnt at all._  
**One Death**: How?  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.2.3, ask): how characters feel at what happens  
> _How does the lord feel when he gets the candles back?_  
> - ✅ Surprised → Yes! His mouth falls open. He is surprised.
> - Sleepy → He says “How?” His mouth falls open. He is surprised.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out how a character feels from what he says and does._

**Hunahpu**: Good morning!  

#### `a31-12-houses`

**Grandmother**: Then four more houses. Each one was a puzzle: Razor, Cold, Jaguar and Fire.  
_In the Cold House, frost is on the walls._  
_The twins build a fire of pine cones._  
_In the Jaguar House, the jaguars pace._  
_The twins give them bones, and the jaguars lie down._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS4-1, notice): jaguars are big cats that live in forests  
> **Grandmother**: Real jaguars are big cats. They live in warm forests, in Guatemala and nearby.  
> **Grandmother**: They are good swimmers, too!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that jaguars are big cats that live in forests and can swim._

_In the Fire House, the fire roars and does not hurt them._  
_Your Nubbin carries pine cones for the fire, one at a time._  
**Hunahpu**: Every house, and we are still here!  

**Choices**

    - The fire smells of pine and somewhere better.

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): naming a feeling  
> _The creature looked lost. How does lost feel?_

> - Happy → Lost is not happy. It feels scared and alone. A friend helps.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named the feeling of being lost._

**Pixel**: Did you see? It wasn’t angry. It was lost.

- **Tell Sonic it looked lost.**
    - **Sonic**: Lost things still splash. Thanks, though.
- **Look down the drain.**

- **Say nothing.**

#### `pa1-03-sonic-done`

_Sonic is gone, fast as he came._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-ESS2-3, ask): water takes the shape of its container  
> **Pixel**: The creature poured down the drain. Why can water do that?  
> - ✅ Water flows and fits any shape → Yes! Water is a liquid. It flows and fits any hole.
> - Water is hard → Ice is hard. Water flows. It fits any hole it finds!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that liquid water flows into any shape._

_The police roll up their tape._

> - Big → A plum fits in your hand. That is small!

## PA1-4. The Light

- `pa1-04-s1`: Follow the pink light. · _It waits for you down the quiet street._
- `pa1-04-s2`: Sit by the pool with Tikal. · _Sit on the warm stone, quietly._

#### `pa1-04-follow`

> **Lesson** (science, K.MD.A.2, ask): warm and hot  
> _Warm like a hand, or hot like a lamp. Which is safe to touch?_  
> - ✅ Warm like a hand → Yes! Warm is safe. Hot can burn. We don’t touch hot lamps.
> - Hot like a lamp → Hot lamps can burn. Warm, like a hand, is safe to touch.
> _For grown-ups: Your child told warm from hot._

**Pixel**: There’s no button for this. It isn’t me.  
_Your Nubbin reaches up. The light dips to be touched._

#### `pa1-04-follow-done`

_The city sounds go out, like a candle._

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, ask): listening for sounds  
> _Close your eyes. What can you hear now? (Wait for an answer.)_  
> - ✅ Birds singing → Yes! Tweet, tweet. Birds. The city is gone.
> - Cars and sirens → Not any more! Listen. Tweet, tweet. Birds.
> _For grown-ups: Your child listened for a sound in the story._

**Pixel**: Keeper? The screen’s gone gold. Where are you?  

#### `pa1-04-shrine`

_Around it are pools of clear water, full of Chao._  
_A girl sits with her feet in the pool. She has long braids._  
**Tikal**: Oh! A visitor. And a little one. Sit down quietly.  
**Tikal**: I’m Tikal. Your little one looks like a cousin of ours.  
_Then the water rises. It is the water creature._  
_It is not lost now. It stands tall and watches over the Chao._  
**Tikal**: Don’t be afraid. That’s Chaos. It looks after them.  
**Tikal**: Some say it’s a monster. It isn’t. It just worries the most.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): worrying about someone  
> **Tikal**: Chaos worries about the Chao. Who worries about you?  
> - ✅ The grown-ups who love me → Yes. Worrying is a kind of loving. Chaos loves the Chao.
> - Nobody → Someone does! The grown-ups who love you. Worrying is a kind of loving.
> _For grown-ups: Your child talked about who looks after them._


**Choices**

    - You bow. Chaos lowers its head, just a little.
- **Ask Tikal what it is.**
    - **Tikal**: It was a Chao once. The jewel’s light changed it.
- **Watch your Nubbin.**
    - Your Nubbin floats to Chaos’s feet. Chaos turns it the right way up.

#### `pa1-04-shrine-done`

_The gold comes back. The birds go quiet._  
_You are in the street, with your hand on a wall._

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): short and long times  
> **Pixel**: Nine seconds, or all afternoon. Which is longer?  
> - ✅ All afternoon → Yes! An afternoon is hours. Nine seconds is a blink.
> - Nine seconds → Count to nine. Done already! An afternoon is much longer.
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared a short time with a long one._

> - ✅ Kind and calm → Yes. First kind, long ago. Lost came after. Something happened.
> - Lost → The pool was long, long ago. First kind, then lost. Something happened.

> - Three → One tail, and one more. Hold up one finger, then another. Two!

> - Grab the tools and run → Grabbing would not help. Watch, wait, and pass things.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about how to help someone busy._

> - ✅ Brrrm → Yes! Brrrm is a happy engine. Say it: brrrm!
> - Cough → A cough is a poorly engine. Brrrm is a happy one. Brrrm!

> _You get down behind the bench. Can you make yourself small? (Try it!)_

> - Jump up and shout → Not now. Curl up small behind the bench, and wait.

## PA1-6. The Shattered Emerald

- `pa1-06-s1`: Visit the floating island. · _Tails flies you there. Climb the steps._
- `pa1-06-s2`: Help Knuckles find the green pieces. · _Look in the ferns on the left._

#### `pa1-06-island`

_High in the sky floats a whole island! Tails flies you there._  
_In the middle is a shrine with steps. On top, the big green jewel._  
_Someone sits on the steps with his arms folded, glaring._  
**Knuckles**: Who let you up here? Nobody comes up here.  
**Knuckles**: I’m Knuckles. I guard the Master Emerald. Don’t touch it. Don’t lick it.  
_Your Nubbin, who was about to lick it, sits down._  
**Knuckles**: …It can stay. It looks like a Chao. Chao lived up here once.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): rules keep things safe  
> _Knuckles says: don’t touch, don’t lick. Why does he have rules?_  
> - ✅ To keep the jewel safe → Yes. The jewel is precious. Rules keep precious things safe.
> - Because he is mean → Not mean. He is a guard. Rules keep precious things safe.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about why a rule exists._

_Then the sky goes dark! The jewel flashes. The steps shake._  
_Water rises out of the jewel and strikes it. Crack!_  
_The jewel breaks into a hundred green pieces. They fly everywhere._  
**Dr. Eggman**: Splendid work, Chaos! Enjoy your swim, Knuckles!  
_The island tips, slowly, like a big ship. Then it falls._  

#### `pa1-06-island-done`

_You hold the steps and hold your Nubbin._  
_SPLASH! The island lands in the sea, with a long sigh._  
_When the spray settles, it floats. Everyone is fine._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): floating  
> _The island floats on the sea. What else floats? (Think of bath time.)_  
> - ✅ A boat, or a duck → Yes! Boats and rubber ducks float. Stones sink.
> - A stone → A stone sinks, plop. Boats and ducks float on top!
> _For grown-ups: Your child named something that floats._

**Pixel**: You’re all right? Good. My hands are shaking out here.  

#### `pa1-06-shards`

**Knuckles**: Great. A hundred pieces, everywhere.  
**Knuckles**: Without the jewel, the island stays down. Guarding it is my job.  
_He kicks a stone. He stares at the jungle. He does not move._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): a big job feels smaller with help  
> _Knuckles has a big job and feels stuck. What helps?_  
> - ✅ A friend to help look → Yes! A big job feels smaller with a friend.
> - Kicking more stones → Kicking stones doesn’t find pieces. A friend helping does!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that help makes a big job smaller._

**Pixel**: He’ll be ages. Look how much jungle there is.  
_Your Nubbin trots into the ferns. It comes back with a green piece!_  
**Knuckles**: …How did it do that?  
**Pixel**: Nubbins are good at finding green things.  
**Knuckles**: Fine. Small one, you’re with me. Keeper, keep up.  

**Choices**

- **Search with Knuckles.**
    - **Knuckles**: You take the left. I’ll take the right. Shout if you find one.
- **Ask about his people.**
    - **Knuckles**: Echidnas. There was a whole clan. Now there’s me.
    - **Knuckles**: Anyway. Pieces. Left side.

#### `pa1-06-shards-done`

_By sunset you have a sack of green pieces._  
_Knuckles counts them twice and scowls. That is how he says thank you._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.4, ask): counting again to check  
> _Knuckles counts the pieces twice. Why count twice?_  
> - ✅ To check the number is right → Yes! Counting again checks you got it right.
> - Because he forgot how → He didn’t forget. Counting again checks the number is right.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that counting again checks an answer._

**Knuckles**: Not all of them. Not yet. But it’s a start.  

#### `pa1-06-complete`

_Knuckles gives your Nubbin the smallest piece to hold._  
_He takes it back. Then he gives it again._  
**Knuckles**: Just for tonight. Don’t lose it. That piece is a bit of my home.  
_Your Nubbin sleeps holding it. In the morning it gives it back._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): giving something back  
> _Your Nubbin gives the piece back without being asked. Why is that good?_  
> - ✅ It was lent, not given → Yes! When something is lent, we give it back. That builds trust.
> - It didn’t like it → It liked it! But it was lent, so it goes back. That builds trust.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that lent things go back._

#### `pa1-09-big`

**Big**: He swallowed a shiny green stone. Then he grew a tail!  

> **Lesson** (science, 3-LS1-1, ask): frogs and tails  
> _Froggy grew a tail. Do grown-up frogs have tails?_  
> - ✅ No, only tadpoles do → Yes! Baby frogs are tadpoles with tails. Grown frogs have none.
> - Yes, long ones → Grown frogs have no tails. Only baby tadpoles do. Froggy is being odd!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that tadpoles have tails and grown frogs do not._

**Pixel**: A green stone. Another jewel. And a tail like the water creature’s?  
**Big**: He jumped in the river. I’ve been fishing for him all day.  
_Your Nubbin sits by Big. Big pats its head with one big finger._  
**Big**: You can help. But you have to be quiet.  

#### `pa1-09-big-done`

_Big gives you a spare rod._  
_On the end is a little rubber bug with a bell. Ting!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, ask): what makes a sound  
> _Ting! The little bell rings when it shakes. Why?_  
> - ✅ Shaking makes it wobble and ring → Yes! Wobbling, shaking things make sound. Ting!
> - It is singing → Bells don’t sing. Shaking makes them wobble, and wobbling makes sound!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that shaking makes sound._


#### `pa1-09-fish`

_You sit on the bank beside Big. The river slides by, slow._  
**Big**: Froggy likes it when you’re still. If you wiggle, he hides.  
_Big is very good at being still. Your Nubbin is excellent._  

> **Lesson** (health, CASEL: Self-management, do): being still  
> _Can you be as still as Big? Hands in your lap. Count to ten._  
> Check: `edu:sit:still:froggy`
> _For grown-ups: Your child practised being still for a count of ten._

**Pixel**: This is the slowest game ever. I love it.  
_Dragonflies come and go._  
_The bell rings once. Ting. Then it doesn’t._  

**Choices**

- **Keep waiting.**
    - You keep still. After a while, waiting feels easy.
- **Try another spot.**
    - **Big**: Nope. This is the spot.
    - You put the rod back down.

#### `pa1-09-fish-done`

_Something green climbs out and sits on your Nubbin’s foot._  
_It has a long, wobbly tail, clear as water._  
**Big**: FROGGY!  
_Froggy jumps back in the river. Splash! Big is still beaming._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sound: F  
> **Big**: Froggy starts with fff. What else starts with fff?  
> - ✅ Fish, fox, foot → Yes! Fff: fish, fox, foot, Froggy!
> - Cat, cup → Cat is c-c-c. Fff is fish, fox, foot, Froggy!
> _For grown-ups: Your child found words that start with F._

**Big**: He’s all right. He’s being silly. I always find him.  

#### `pa1-09-complete`

**Pixel**: A frog with a watery tail. The water creature has been near here.  
**Big**: That big water fella? I saw him. He was looking for something.  
**Big**: Same as me. I know that look.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): understanding someone else’s feeling  
> _Big says “I know that look.” How does he know how Chaos feels?_  
> - ✅ He is looking for a friend too → Yes. Big misses Froggy. So he understands missing someone.
> - He read it in a book → No book! Big misses Froggy, so he understands missing someone.
> _For grown-ups: Your child noticed someone understanding another’s feeling._

## PA1-10. Pachacamac

- `pa1-10-s1`: Go back with the light. See who has come. · _Stand at the bottom of the steps._
- `pa1-10-s2`: Choose where to stand with Tikal. · _Up by Tikal, or down with the Chao._

#### `pa1-10-council`

_The pink light finds you by the river. It is in a hurry._  
_At the shrine it is evening. Torches burn on the steps._  
_A crowd stands below the altar, in feathers and beads._  
_At the front is a big echidna in a tall headdress. Tikal’s father._  
**Pachacamac**: Our neighbours have walls and spears. We have prayers.  
**Pachacamac**: With the jewels’ power, nobody could ever threaten us again.  
_The warriors bang their spears. The Chao stop playing and look up._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): loud voices can be scary  
> _The spears bang. The Chao stop playing. How do the Chao feel?_  
> - ✅ Worried → Yes. Loud, cross noises make small ones worried. A cuddle helps.
> - Excited → Not excited. Loud, cross noises make small ones worried. A cuddle helps.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named how loud, cross noises feel._

**Tikal**: Father. Please. The jewels aren’t for that. Grandmother said…  
**Pachacamac**: Your grandmother is gone, Tikal.  

#### `pa1-10-council-done`

_The warriors go quiet._  
_Tikal looks round. She sees you at the bottom of the steps._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.1, ask): top and bottom  
> _Tikal is at the top of the steps. Where are you?_  
> - ✅ At the bottom → Yes! Tikal is at the top. You are at the bottom.
> - At the top → Tikal is at the top. You are down at the bottom, looking up.
> _For grown-ups: Your child used the position words top and bottom._


#### `pa1-10-stand`

**Tikal**: The Chao live here because it’s peaceful. Take the power, and it won’t be.  
**Pachacamac**: Peace is a word for people who haven’t been attacked yet.  
**Tikal**: Then let us be those people, as long as we can.  
_Her father’s face does not change. He decided long ago._  
**Pixel**: He’s not listening, is he? Not really.  
_Tikal is shaking. She does not step back._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): being brave while scared  
> _Tikal is shaking, but she does not step back. What is that called?_  
> - ✅ Being brave → Yes! Brave is doing the right thing even when you’re scared.
> - Being silly → Not silly. Brave is doing the right thing even when you’re scared.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that brave means scared and doing it anyway._


**Choices**

- **Climb up and stand beside her.**
    - You climb up and stand next to Tikal, so she isn’t alone.
    - Her father looks at you like a fly. Nothing changes.
    - **Tikal**: Thank you.
- **Stay down with the Chao.**
    - You stay with the Chao. Your Nubbin climbs into your lap.
    - Tikal looks down at you all, and her shoulders come down a little.

#### `pa1-10-stand-done`

**Pachacamac**: At dawn we take what the jewels can give. Tikal, stand aside.  
_He goes. The warriors go. The torches go with them._  
_The shrine is very dark._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-2, ask): light and dark  
> _The torches have gone. Why is the shrine dark now?_  
> - ✅ The light went away → Yes! No light means dark. We need light to see things.
> - Someone shut their eyes → Eyes are open! The torches left. No light means dark.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that we need light to see._


#### `pa1-10-complete`

**Tikal**: He wasn’t always like this. He used to carry me on his shoulders.  
**Tikal**: You being here doesn’t change anything. I know that.  
**Tikal**: I’m still glad. Isn’t that strange?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): company helps even when it can’t fix things  
> **Tikal**: You can’t fix it, but I’m glad you’re here. Does company help?  
> - ✅ Yes, you feel less alone → Yes. Some things can’t be fixed. Company still helps.
> - No, only fixing helps → Fixing is good. But company helps too: you feel less alone.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that company helps even when nothing can be fixed._

_Chaos sinks into the pool. Its glow lights the water from underneath._  
**Pixel**: Keeper. I don’t want to watch the next part.  
**You**: Neither do I.  

## PA1-11. The Egg Carrier

- `pa1-11-s1`: Fly up to the big ship with Tails. · _Stay close to Sonic and Tails._
- `pa1-11-s2`: Take the ship’s Chao to the lifeboats. · _Up two decks, on the left._

#### `pa1-11-board`

_Back in the city, a huge flying ship fills the sky. Red and gold._

**Sonic**: In, find Amy, out. Easy. Stay close. Don’t press any red buttons.  
_Tails drops you on the deck. Whoosh! Sonic is gone at once._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): two feelings at once  
> **Pixel**: I love it AND I hate it. Can you feel two things at once?  
> - ✅ Yes, you can → Yes! Excited and scared at the same time. That’s normal.
> - No, only one → You can! Excited and scared at the same time. That’s normal.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that two feelings can come at once._

_Your Nubbin stays tucked inside your jacket._  

#### `pa1-11-board-done`

_Down a ladder, past a door marked EGG STORAGE._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Literacy, ask): first letter: E  
> _EGG. What letter does “egg” start with? (Point to the sign.)_  
> - ✅ E → Yes! E for egg. E, e, egg. Eggman starts with E too!
> - G → G is in the middle: e-g-g. The first letter is E. E for egg!
> _For grown-ups: Your child found the first letter of egg._

_You hear something you didn’t expect up here: Chao!_  

#### `pa1-11-garden`

_There is a Chao garden inside the ship. Plastic grass. A plastic tree._

> **Pixel**: You carry two Chao. Three follow your Nubbin. How many is that?  
> - ✅ Five → Yes! Two and three make five. Five Chao on the way!
> - Four → Let’s count. Two in your arms: one, two. Three more: three, four, five!
> _For grown-ups: Your child added two and three._

**Pixel**: Every one of them, Keeper. Not one stays behind.  

**Choices**

- **Carry them two at a time.**

- **Let your Nubbin lead them.**
    - Every Chao follows your Nubbin, like ducklings.

#### `pa1-11-garden-done`

_The last Chao is in the last lifeboat. You pull the lever._  
_It floats down under a parachute with Eggman’s face on it._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): parachutes catch air  
> _The parachute opens wide. Why does the lifeboat float down slowly?_  
> - ✅ The big parachute catches the air → Yes! A big open parachute catches air and slows the fall.
> - Eggman’s face is magic → Not magic! The big open parachute catches air and slows the fall.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that parachutes catch air._

**Pixel**: The parachutes have his face on them. I can’t believe it.

_Chaos rises from a tank. It is huge now, with big clawed arms._  
_It isn’t looking at Eggman. It is looking at the empty Chao garden._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): how it feels not to know  
> **Pixel**: Chaos thinks they’re gone. If it knew they were safe, how would it feel?  
> - ✅ Better → Yes. Knowing they are safe would help it feel better.
> - Angrier → Not angrier. Knowing they are safe would help it feel better.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about what another character does not know._

_Sonic is there, with Amy holding the bird. You stay by the hatch._  

#### `pa1-11-chaos-done`

_There is a long, splashy fight. You peek through your fingers._  
_At the end, Chaos pours away over the side, still looking back._

> **Amy**: I saved the bird! Is it all right to feel proud?  
> - ✅ Yes, you did a kind thing → Yes! Feeling proud of a kind thing is lovely.
> - No, be quiet about it → You can say it! Feeling proud of a kind thing is lovely.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that pride in kindness is fine._

## PA1-12. Gamma

**Dr. Eggman**: Because I SAID so! Go to the scrap room.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): asking why is allowed  
> _Gamma asks “why?” Eggman says “because I said so.” Is asking why good?_  
> - ✅ Yes, asking why helps you choose → Yes! Asking why helps you choose what is right.
> - No, just do as you’re told → Asking why is good! It helps you choose what is right.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that asking why helps good choices._

_Eggman stamps off. Gamma stands alone. Then it walks the other way._

_Gamma walks to a row of robots in their charging beds._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.G.A.2, ask): same shape, different colour  
> _Same shape, different colours. Are the robots still the same shape?_  
> - ✅ Yes, colour doesn’t change shape → Yes! Red or blue, a square is still a square.
> - No → They are! Colour doesn’t change shape. Red or blue, same shape.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that colour does not change shape._


#### `pa1-12-birds`

_Gamma opens a little door on the first robot’s back._

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): what birds need  
> _The bird flies free. What does a bird need to be happy?_  
> - ✅ Sky to fly in, food and water → Yes! Birds need room to fly, and food and water.
> - A tiny cage → A tiny cage is sad for a bird. It needs sky, food and water.
> _For grown-ups: Your child named what a bird needs._

**Amy**: They run on birds? Oh, poor Gamma.  
_Gamma looks at your Nubbin for a long moment._  
**E-102 Gamma**: You and the small one. Leave this ship. This unit has work to do.

    - It turns back to its brothers.

    - **E-102 Gamma**: Negative. There are more of them. Go.
    - It says it kindly.

> - Cotton wool → They look fluffy, but clouds are tiny water drops, floating high up.

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): happy-sad tears

## PA1-15. Perfect Chaos

- `pa1-15-s1`: Get up high when the water comes. · _The stairs on the side of the bank._
- `pa1-15-s2`: Carry Chao and people up to the roof. · _Up the stairs and down again._

#### `pa1-15-flood`

_In the morning, the sky over the city turns dark green._  
_Out of the sea rises Chaos. It keeps rising. Taller than the hotel!_  
_Eggman’s ship zooms at it. Chaos swats it away like a fly._  
**Dr. Eggman**: That… was not in the plan!  
_Then the water comes. A whole sea, walking into the city._  
**Pixel**: Get up high. Keeper, now. Find a roof.  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): high ground when water comes  
> **Pixel**: Water is coming. Where is the safe place?  
> - ✅ Up high → Yes! Water stays low. Up high is safe. Up the stairs!
> - Down low → Water goes to low places. Up high is safe. Up the stairs!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that high ground is safe from water._

> - Up → Water can’t climb! It always runs downhill. Down the steps, splash.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that water runs downhill._

> _Slow as a falling petal. What falls slowly: a petal, or a stone?_  
> - ✅ A petal → Yes! Light, wide things like petals float down slowly. Stones drop fast.
> - A stone → A stone drops fast, thud. Light petals float down slowly.
> _For grown-ups: Your child compared how a petal and a stone fall._

**Sonic**: So… you two are going?
