#### `s10-letter-told`

_Morning. Gran Hazel has died._  
_That means her body stopped working. It won’t start again._  
_Under the signpost stone is a letter from Gran._  
**Gran Hazel**: “Don’t make a big fuss. Well, maybe a little fuss.”  
**Gran Hazel**: “You kept my three rules. Here is one more.”  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): add 1: three and one more make four  
> _Three rules, and one more. How many rules now?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes. Three and one more make four. (Count them on your fingers: one, two, three… four!)
> - Three → Three, and then one more. Let’s count up: one, two, three… four!
> - Five → Let’s count: one, two, three rules. One more makes four.
> _For grown-ups: Added one more to three to make four._

**Gran Hazel**: “Show up. Every morning. Same sticky gate.”  
**Gran Hazel**: “I love you. I always will. Love, Gran.”  
_Your friends are already at the gate. Waiting for you._  
_You read the letter to them. Clover cries._  
_Byte checks his shoelaces. Untied!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): being together helps when we are sad  
> _Everyone is sad together. Crying is all right._  
> _Being together helps. So does a little smile._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that sharing sad feelings with friends helps._


#### `s13-letter-given`

_You fetch the letter from its tin box. Down the lane you go._  
_Corvin is by the stile. He keeps rubbing his cold hands._  
**Corvin Vale**: Hazel’s grandchild. Twice in one evening.  
_You hold out the letter. He sees the writing and stops._  
**Corvin Vale**: That’s my father’s writing.  
_He reads it slowly. Then again, even slower._  
**Corvin Vale**: “Nobody will count.”  
_He puts it in his pocket, right over his heart._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): feeling two feelings at once  
> _Corvin’s dad said “I love you” at last. How does Corvin feel?_  
> - ✅ Sad and glad, both at once → Yes. He’s sad his dad waited so long. He’s glad he said it. We can feel two feelings at once.
> - Only cross → Maybe a little. But look: his hand is on his pocket. He’s sad and glad, both at once.
> _For grown-ups: Saw that someone can feel sad and glad at the same time._

**Corvin Vale**: Thank you. I don’t know what else. Thank you.  
_He goes on down the lane. You go back up to Hazel._  

#### `s13-letter-nomoss`

_You open the letter. It is short._  
**Aldous Vale**: Dear Corvin.  
**Aldous Vale**: I worked all the time. I never stopped. Not once.  
**Aldous Vale**: I was too busy to say the most important thing.  
**Aldous Vale**: I love you. I should have said it every day.  
**Aldous Vale**: If you ever want to stop, come and sit by the river.  
**Aldous Vale**: Sit as long as you like. Nobody will count.  
**Aldous Vale**: Love, your dad.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): saying “I love you” to the people we love  
> _“I love you.” Three small words. They feel big when we hear them._  
> _(Ask: who could you say “I love you” to today? Wait for an answer.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard a kind letter from a dad to his son, and thought about who they could say “I love you” to._

**Old Tobin**: “Nobody will count.” He counted everything. And then that.  
**Old Tobin**: It isn’t mine to decide. What shall we do with it?  

**Choices**

- **Keep it for Corvin. Give it to him when his hands are warm.**
    - You fold it up and put it in your coat, by Hazel’s notebook.
    - **Old Tobin**: Yes. Cold hands can’t hold a thing like that.
    - **Old Tobin**: You’ll know when. Your grandmother always knew when.
- **Ask Tobin to burn it in the stove. Some things end with the person.**
    - **Old Tobin**: That’s a real answer. I’ve thought it too.
    - **Old Tobin**: He wrote lots of letters, and burned them. This would be the last.
- **Read it out loud at Aldous’s grave, and leave it there.**
    - **Old Tobin**: Read out loud, and left with Aldous. Yes.
    - **Old Tobin**: Nobody ever read Aldous a letter. This is a way to remember him.

#### `s13-settled-burned`

_The mill’s old stove still works. Tobin lights it._  
_You stand well back and watch. Fire is for grown-ups._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, notice): staying safe near fire  
> **Old Tobin**: Stoves and fires are hot. Only grown-ups light them.  
> **Old Tobin**: Children stay back, a big step away. That keeps us safe.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that only grown-ups light fires and that children stay well back from stoves._

_The letter catches. Then it’s gone, quick as a blink._  
**Old Tobin**: There. The last one.  
_Tobin sits on the step with you till the stove is cold._  
_Nobody counts how long._  

#### `s13-settled-grave`

_Aldous is buried under the trees by the river._  
_It’s autumn. A yellow leaf falls on the stone. Then another._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): autumn: leaves change colour and fall  
> _Yellow leaves are falling from the trees. What time of year is it?_  
> - ✅ Autumn → Yes! In autumn, many trees drop their leaves.
> - Summer → In summer the leaves are green, and they stay on. Falling yellow leaves mean autumn.
> - Spring → In spring, new green leaves grow. Falling yellow leaves mean autumn.
> _For grown-ups: Connected falling yellow leaves with autumn._

_Moss sits on the stone and shuts his eyes._  
_You read the letter out loud, slowly._  
**Moss**: He was never still enough to be read to. This is for remembering him.  
_You put the letter on the grave, under a flat stone._  
_Tobin takes his hat off. Then he forgets why, and puts it back on._

#### `s19-warmth-sable`

_Two days after the Long Night. Snow everywhere. Very quiet._  
_Sable sits at the top of the garden. She hasn’t eaten her breakfast._  
_She stares up at the high snowy hill._  
_Beside her floats Moss’s pale light. It leans that way too._  
_Up in the white snow there is a tiny red dot._  

> **Lesson** (art, do): spotting a colour: red  
> _Red on white is easy to spot. Like a berry in the snow._  
> _(Find something red near you. Point to it!)_  
> Check: `edu:find:colour:red`
> _For grown-ups: Spotted red against white, and found something red nearby._

_Sable looks at you. Then the hill. Then you._  
**You**: All right. We’ll ask Marina.  

#### `s19-climb-sable`

_First light. Marina ties a rope to you. Sable won’t have a rope._  
_She trots ahead, a grey shape on the white snow._  
_Moss’s pale light floats by her shoulder._  
_Crunch, crunch, crunch. Your boots sink in._  
_Sable is so light, she doesn’t sink at all._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): heavier and lighter  
> _You sink in the snow. Sable doesn’t. Who is heavier?_  
> - ✅ Me! → Yes! You’re heavier, so you sink. Sable is light.
> - Sable → Look at the footprints. Yours are deep. Hers are tiny. You’re heavier!
> _For grown-ups: Compared weight by looking at deep and shallow footprints in snow._

**Marina**: She’s not stopping! Is she always like this?  
**You**: Only when it matters.  

#### `s19-hollow-sable`

_Near the top, a rock leans over, like a hand over a cup._  
_Under it there is no snow. The rock is dry and a little warm._  
_On a flat stone sits a tiny red light. Smaller than your fingernail._  
**Marina**: I’ll wait up on the edge. Shout if you need me.  
_Sable stops. The fur on her back stands up._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): reading feelings from an animal’s body  
> _Sable’s fur stands up. How might she feel?_  
> - ✅ A bit scared → Yes. Animals show feelings with their bodies. She’s a bit scared. We can sit close to help her feel safe.
> - Hungry → Maybe! But look at her fur, standing up. She feels a bit scared.
> _For grown-ups: Read an animal’s body to guess how she felt._

_Moss’s pale light settles by the red one. Two little lights._  
_You remember what Moss said. Sit still, for a long time._  

#### `s19-question-sable`

_After a long time, the red light grows a tiny bit bigger._  
**Cinder**: Are they safe?  
_Moss would know what to say. You say it for him._  
**You**: Not just safe. They’re well.  
**Cinder**: Well. Well is better. I didn’t know.  
_Then the light sees Sable. Grey from her ears to her tail._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): first sounds: s  
> _Sable. Snow. Stone. Sorry. Listen: s-s-s!_  
> _Which one starts with s too?_  
> - ✅ Sun → S-s-sun! Yes!
> - Moon → M-m-moon starts with m. S-s-sun starts with s!
> - Tree → T-t-tree starts with t. S-s-sun starts with s!
> _For grown-ups: Heard the “s” sound at the start of Sable, snow and stone, and found another s word._

**Cinder**: Oh, little one. I held them too tight, long ago. I’m so sorry.  
_Sable walks up to the warm stone. She leans on it._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): showing love and forgiveness without words  
> _Sable leans on the stone. That is her way of saying “it’s all right”._  
> _Leaning close is a way to show love._  
> _For grown-ups: Saw that we can show forgiveness and love without words, by being close._

**Cinder**: She came to me. Nobody made her. She forgives me.  
**Cinder**: Keeper, am I forgiven by the others too?  

**Choices**

- **“You’re forgiven.”**
    - **You**: You’re forgiven.
    - The light goes warm, like a fire with the kettle on.
    - **Cinder**: Oh. I thought being forgiven would be heavy. It’s light!
    - Sable breathes out, long and slow. The light warms her nose.
- **“That’s theirs to say. But you’ll be remembered.”**
    - **You**: That’s theirs to say. But you’ll be remembered.
    - **Cinder**: Remembered. That’s what I should have asked for.
    - **Cinder**: Will you tell them I loved them? Not only what I did?
    - **You**: All of it.
    - Moss’s pale light glows brighter, once. Like a nod.

#### `s19-fade-sable`

_You stay. Sable stays by the stone. So does Moss’s light._  
_The red light gets smaller and smaller. Slowly. Gently._  
**Cinder**: Little one. It isn’t cold.  
_Sable shuts her eyes._  
_Then the light is gone. Cinder has died._  
_There is only the flat stone, and the wind._  
**You**: That is fading done right. Not frozen still. Let go.  
_Sable stays curled by the stone a long time. You let her._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): feeling sad when someone dies, and what helps  
> _Sable is sad. You might feel sad too. That’s all right._  
> _Staying close together helps. So does remembering._  
> _(Give your grown-up a hug, if you like.)_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard plainly that Cinder died, and that feeling sad is all right; closeness and remembering help._


#### `s19-warmth-alone`

_Two days after the Long Night. Snow everywhere. Very quiet._  
_You look out of the window, with a warm drink._  
_Up on the snowy hill, there’s a tiny red dot!_  
_You look away. You look back. It’s still there._  
_Moss would want to see it. But Moss has died._  
_You miss him. You pull on your boots._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): missing someone, and what helps  
> _You miss Moss. Missing someone is a sad feeling. What can help?_  
> - ✅ Talking about them → Yes. Talking about someone we miss keeps them close. (Who do you miss? Wait for an answer.)
> - Never saying their name → Saying their name is all right. Talking about them helps us feel close.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about missing someone who has died, and how talking about them can help._

**You**: Marina knows the way. Let’s ask her!  

#### `s19-climb-alone`

_First light. Marina ties a rope to you. She checks it twice._  
_Then she checks your socks. Two pairs!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 4: two pairs make four  
> _A pair is two. Two pairs of socks! How many socks?_  
> _(Count them on your fingers together: one, two, three, four.)_  
> **Marina**: Four socks. Two on each foot. Toasty!  
> Check: `edu:count:socks:4`
> _For grown-ups: Counted two pairs of socks and found there were four._

_Crunch, crunch, crunch. The snow sounds like biting toast._  
**Marina**: Lovely wind! It makes your cheeks tingle!  
**Marina**: What are we looking for?  
**You**: Something warm.  
**Marina**: Up here? Well. You’re Hazel’s. I won’t ask.  

#### `s19-hollow-alone`

_Near the top, a rock leans over, like a hand over a cup._  
_Under it there is no snow. The rock is dry and a little warm._  
_On a flat stone sits a tiny red light. Smaller than your fingernail._

_You go in on your own. You sit down near the light._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): knowing who can help when you feel a bit scared

> - Nobody → Look up! Marina is on the edge, with the rope. A grown-up is near. You can shout for her.
> _For grown-ups: Remembered that a trusted grown-up was close by and could help._

_You remember what Moss said. Sit still, for a long time._

_After a long time, the red light grows a tiny bit bigger._

**You**: Yes. Badly. But they love it!

#### `s24-tea-moss`

_Gran Hazel died. Her flower grows here, so we remember her._

_Nova sits down by the flower. Her big bag stays on her back._

**Nova**: Is there tea? I always say no. Today I’ll say yes, please!

#### `s24-tea-sable`

_Look! The flowers on the hill are open, all at once._  
_This one is Gran Hazel’s flower. It’s a bit untidy, like her._

> _Moss has turned his back. How might he feel?_  
> - ✅ Sad, or upset → Yes. Turning away can mean “I’m upset.” Giving him time helps.
> - Happy and silly → Look again: back turned, not looking. He seems upset. Giving him time helps.

#### `s24-lantern-corvin`

**Nova**: Can we take Gran Hazel’s lantern? And light it up high, at sunrise?

_It is Sunday, so Corvin is by the pond._  
_He takes Gran Hazel’s lantern off its hook, very carefully._  
_He trims the wick, so the flame will burn nicely._  
**Corvin Vale**: For the sunrise, on the far hill.  
_He gives it to you. He holds on for a moment._  
**Corvin Vale**: Bring it back lit.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): looking after things you borrow  
> _Corvin lends you the lantern. What do we do with borrowed things?_  
> - ✅ Look after it, and give it back → Yes. Looking after it, and bringing it back, keeps a promise.
> - Keep it forever → Borrowed things go back! Looking after them, and returning them, is kind.
> _For grown-ups: Your child talked about looking after borrowed things and giving them back._


#### `s24-stowaway-knows`

_The cart goes up the hill road. Clip-clop, creak._  
_Nova puts her big bag on. The cart goes, “Groan!”_  
_Under the cover, something says, “Ow!” Then, “Nobody heard that.”_  
_Up pops a girl in big wellies, with a sash of badges._  
**Tilly**: It’s you! You played my dragon game!  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): noticing how someone feels  
> _Tilly sees you. How does she feel?_  
> - ✅ Happy to see a friend → Yes! Her face lights up. Seeing a friend feels good.
> - Scared → Not scared! She’s smiling. She’s happy to see a friend.
> _For grown-ups: Your child noticed a character’s happy feeling._

**Tilly**: I’m a stowaway. You can’t send a stowaway home. That’s the rule.

#### `s24-bun-moss`

_It’s all right to talk to someone we miss. Lots of people do._

#### `s24-eternal-watch`

_Your Eternal sits on the hill, where it always sits._

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): goodbyes are not forever  
> _The Eternal stays at home. Will you see it again?_  
> - ✅ Yes, when we get home → Yes! Goodbye isn’t forever. It will be waiting for you.
> - No, never → Don’t worry! It stays right here. It will be waiting when you get home.

#### `s24-bird-collector`

_Up high, you walk into a cloud. It is misty and cool._  
_You put Fern’s five buns on a rock. Then there are fewer!_  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.2, ask): take away 1 from 5  
> _Fern packed five buns. Someone took one! How many are left?_  
> - ✅ Four → Yes! Five take away one is four. (Count four fingers.)
> - Six → Six would be one more. Somebody took one away! Hold up five fingers. Fold one down. Four!
> _For grown-ups: Your child took one away from five with fingers._

_A huge bird stands in the mist, with a bun in its beak._  
_It is taller than Nova. It has stripes and long, long legs._  
**Tilly**: Oh! He’s beautiful! He’s called Sir Reginald.  
_Gulp! The bun goes all the way down._  
_The bird steps forward, then back. It is shy._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-3, notice): shy animals need slow, quiet people  
> _Shy animals get scared by fast moves and loud noises._  
> _Slow and quiet helps them feel safe._  
> _For grown-ups: Your child heard how to be gentle around a shy wild animal._

**Nova**: Don’t grab. Be gentle and slow.  

**Choices**

- **Hold out a bun on your flat hand.**
    - You hold out a bun. The bird looks at your hand, and steps back.
    - Nova holds out a bun too. The bird goes to Nova instead.
    - **Tilly**: It doesn’t come to you. That’s funny.
    - You think of your quiet grey Nubbins at home. You feel a bit sorry.
- **Sit down and wait for it to come to you.**
    - You sit and wait. The bird stays far away.
    - Nova sits down too. After a long time, the bird goes to Nova.
    - **Tilly**: It doesn’t come to you. That’s funny.
    - You think of your quiet grey Nubbins at home. You feel a bit sorry.

#### `s24-nest-waited`

#### `s24-shelf-moss`

_Moss slept on your shoulder all the way up. Now he wakes._  
_He looks and looks, and doesn’t say anything for a long time._  
**Moss**: I sat on that hill for years, looking at this one.  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): far-away things look small  
> _From up here, is Moss’s hill near, or far away?_  
> - ✅ Far away → Yes! Far away. That’s why it looks so tiny.
> - Near → It looks tiny because it’s far away. Near things look big.
> _For grown-ups: Your child noticed that far-away things look smaller._

**Moss**: I never once looked back the other way.  
**Moss**: She’d have liked this. She’d have talked all the way through it.  

#### `s24-shelf-sable`

_Sable walked two steps ahead of you, all the way up._  
_She waited for you at every bend._  
_Now she sits on the rock, looking at the Grove._  
_The sun shines on her. She is still grey. But she looks warm._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-PS3-1, ask): sunlight warms things  
> _The sun shines on Sable. Does she get warmer, or colder?_  
> - ✅ Warmer → Yes! Sunlight warms things up: rocks, grass, and Sable.
> - Colder → Sunshine makes things warmer. Feel a sunny window sometime!
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that sunlight warms things._

**Nova**: Your turn.

#### `s24-home-eternal`

_You walk back down the hill, slowly._  
_Fairweather comes too. She holds Nova’s arm._  
**Augusta Fairweather**: Fifty years up there. I hope somebody kept my room!  
_Your Eternal is waiting on the cottage step. Hello!_  
_That night you light Gran Hazel’s lantern and open the book._  
_Look! Little notes in pencil, on every page. Gran Hazel wrote them!_  
_She read all of Nova’s stories, and wrote what she thought._  
_Nova stays three days. She says yes to tea every time._  
_Then off she goes. Her bag is so light now!_  
_At the top of the hill she waves. Goodbye, Nova! See you soon!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): retelling a story in order: first and last  
> _What happened first, on this big adventure?_  
> - ✅ Tea on the hill → Yes! First tea, then the lantern, the cart, the bird… and last, the sunrise.
> - The sunrise → The sunrise came last! First was tea on the hill, with Nova.
> _For grown-ups: Your child retold what happened first and last in the story._


#### `s24-home-corvin`

_Corvin is by the pond when you get home._  
_He sees the lantern. It is still lit!_  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): keeping a promise  
> _Corvin said, “Bring it back lit.” Did you?_  
> - ✅ Yes, we did! → Yes! You kept your promise. Keeping promises helps people trust you.
> - No → Look: it’s still glowing! You kept your promise. That helps people trust you.
> _For grown-ups: Your child talked about keeping a promise._

**Corvin Vale**: Good.  
_He hangs it back on its hook, all by himself._  

#### `s24-lecture`

_The museum is full! Even the Nubbins brought chairs._  
**Professor Delve**: A talk today! Every sign in this museum must be true.  
**Augusta Fairweather**: People said I was fibbing. I wasn’t. The bird is real.  
**Augusta Fairweather**: But I won’t say where she lives. That’s my whole talk. Thank you!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS3-3, ask): keeping wild animals’ homes safe  
> _Why won’t Fairweather say where the nest is?_  
> - ✅ To keep the birds safe → Yes. If nobody knows, nobody can bother the chicks.
> - She forgot → She didn’t forget! She keeps it secret, so the birds stay safe.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that keeping a nest secret can keep wild birds safe._

_Professor Delve hangs a new sign. It says Fairweather was right._  
_Everyone claps. Clap, clap, clap!_

#### `s25-storm-nosable`

_Later that week, your Nubbin finds the toy on the windowsill._  
_It sniffs it. Atchoo! Then it runs off after a moth._  
_Not yet, then._  
_Then, one night, a big storm comes. Boom! Crash!_  
_Your Nubbin can’t settle. Its ears are flat._  
_It is scared of the loud bangs._  
_Flash! The lightning lights up the toy on the windowsill._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when you feel scared  
> _Your Nubbin is scared of the storm. What could help it?_  
> - ✅ Something soft to hold → Yes! Something soft and cosy to hug can help us feel safe.
> - Being told to stop it → Being told off doesn’t help a scared feeling. Something soft to hug helps more.
> - Being left all alone → Being alone can feel scarier. A hug, or something soft to hold, helps more.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what helps when someone feels scared: comfort, and something soft to hold._


#### `s25-page-found`

_You tell Clank. He does a happy spin._

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being a good neighbour

> - ✅ Wave and say hello → Yes! Good neighbours wave, say hello and help each other.
> - Hide from each other → That’s not very friendly! Good neighbours wave and say hello.
> - Shout over the wall → Shouting isn’t kind. Good neighbours wave and say hello.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about being a kind neighbour._


#### `s25-byte`

> - ✅ His umbrella → Yes! An umbrella keeps the rain off. Pitter-patter on top.
> - A sunhat → A sunhat is for sunny days. An umbrella keeps off the rain.
> - A spoon → A spoon is far too small! An umbrella keeps off the rain.
> _For grown-ups: Matched rainy weather to what keeps us dry._

> _What soaks up water best?_  
> - ✅ A towel → Yes! A towel is soft and thirsty. It soaks up water.
> - A spoon → Water runs right off a spoon. A towel soaks it up.
> - A stone → A stone soaks up hardly any. A towel soaks up lots!
> _For grown-ups: Found out that some materials, like towels, soak up water._

#### `s25-coda-wild-button`

_Spring is here! Flowers open on the hill._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): seasons: flowers open in spring  
> _Flowers are opening. Which season is it?_  
> - ✅ Spring → Yes! In spring, flowers open and new leaves grow.
> - Winter → In winter it is cold, and most flowers sleep. Flowers open in spring.
> - Night-time → Night isn’t a season! Spring is the season when flowers open.
> _For grown-ups: Linked flowers opening to the season of spring._

#### `s26-door-thrums`

_Whoosh! The wind lifts the ivy like a curtain._  
_Under it is a round iron knob. And a door!_  
_The old wall hums. Hmmmm. It’s the Thrums!_  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-PS4-1, do): sounds are made by vibrations  
> _(Hum like the Thrums. Hmmmm. Touch your lips. Feel the tickle?)_  
> _(That tickle is a tiny shake. Sounds are made of tiny shakes.)_  
> Check: `edu:hum:feel:lips`
> _For grown-ups: Hummed and felt the tiny shaking that makes a sound._

**The Thrums**: Good morning, Keeper. Yes. That is a door.

#### `s26-ramp-1`

_First evening. Dusty digs out the top step._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, do): steps and a slope: two shapes for going down  
> _Steps go down in bumps. A ramp is one long, smooth slope._  
> _(Make steps with your hand: bump, bump, bump.)_  
> _(Now make a long, smooth slope. Wheee!)_  
> Check: `edu:show:hand:steps-and-slope`
> _For grown-ups: Showed the difference between steps and a smooth slope with their hand._

**Linnet**: That’s not a ramp. That’s a hole!  
**Dusty**: Give it time.  
_Linnet sits at the top. She says where each bit of earth goes._  
_She is right every time._  

#### `s26-ramp-2`

_Second evening. The ramp is nearly done._  
**Linnet**: Too steep! I’d zoom straight into the rose bush!  
**Dusty**: I walked down it fine.  
**Linnet**: YOU walked. Make it longer.  
_Dusty makes it longer. It takes all evening._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, ask): compare: steep and gentle  
> _Which ramp is safer: a short steep one, or a long one?_  
> - ✅ The long one → Yes! Longer means less steep. Slow and safe.
> - The short steep one → Steep is too fast! Longer is less steep, and safer.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a steep slope and a gentle one and chose the safer._

_Linnet was right._  

#### `s26-ramp-3`

_Third evening. The ramp is finished. Long and smooth._  
_Linnet goes down it all by herself. Whoosh!_  
_She doesn’t say a word. She touches the green rose._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): quiet can be a happy feeling  
> _Linnet doesn’t say anything. How do you think she feels?_  
> - ✅ Happy → Yes. Sometimes happy is very quiet.
> - Cross → Not cross now! Look at her hand on the rose. Quietly happy.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that someone can be happy without saying anything._

_Dusty leans on the spade, smiling._  

#### `s26-lift-1`

_Next evening, Sparks lifts Linnet down again._  
_Front and back. Never the sides. Just as Linnet said._  
**Sparks**: Smooth! Like a little, rude generator!  
**Linnet**: Thank you.  
_Linnet says thank you every time. Every single time._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): wanting to do things by yourself  
> _Saying thank you is kind._  
> _But Linnet would like to go down on her own._  
> _(Is there something you like to do all by yourself?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Talked about things they like to do by themselves._


#### `s26-lift-2`

_Second evening. Sparks is late._  
_Linnet waits at the top of the steps. And waits._  
**Linnet**: I don’t mind.  
_She minds. She pulls ivy leaves off the wall._  
_She lines them up. Small, bigger, biggest._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.MD.A.2, do): put three things in order of size  
> _(Show small with your hands. Now bigger. Now BIGGEST!)_  
> _Small, bigger, biggest. Just like Linnet’s leaves._  
> Check: `edu:order:leaves:size`
> _For grown-ups: Put sizes in order: small, bigger, biggest._

**Sparks**: Sorry! Sorry! I’m here!  

#### `s26-lift-3`

_Third evening. Sparks lifts Linnet down, then has to go._  
**Sparks**: I’ll be back to lift you up!  
**Linnet**: What if you’re not?  
**Sparks**: Then I’ll be back later!  
_Linnet doesn’t answer. She goes to the green rose, far from the steps._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): name a worry  
> _Linnet is worried. What is she worried about?_  
> - ✅ Getting stuck down here → Yes. She has to wait for someone to lift her up. It’s hard when you can’t come and go when you want.
> - The robin → Not the robin! She’s worried about getting stuck down here.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out what a character was worried about, and why._


#### `s26-tobin-bench-cellar`

**Old Tobin**: This reminds me! Hazel’s grandchild came down the mill cellar with me!  
**Old Tobin**: Six levels deep! Giant eels! Rats in hats!  
**You**: Four levels. The eels were grumpy. Nobody had a hat.  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.C.6, ask): more and fewer: six and four  
> _Tobin says six levels. You say four. Which is more?_  
> - ✅ Six → Yes! Six is more than four. Tobin made the story bigger!
> - Four → Count up: four, five, six. Six is more. Tobin made it bigger!
> _For grown-ups: Compared six and four and found which is more._

**Old Tobin**: That’s the boring version!  
_Tobin watches Linnet dig. She doesn’t tip._  
**Old Tobin**: I kept a door shut once, for a long time. It got heavy.  
_He sits and watches her until it’s dark._  
_On the way out, Tobin pats the old wall._  
**Old Tobin**: My old boss used to say: plant a rose where your worry sits.  
**Old Tobin**: Then the worry has to move somewhere else!  

#### `s26-snowdrops-lifted`

_Linnet’s tracks stop at the door._  
_Linnet is at the top of the steps. They are deep in snow._  
**Linnet**: I’ve been here an HOUR! I can see the snowdrops from here!  
**Linnet**: Everyone who lifts is somewhere else.  
**Linnet**: I’m not the problem. These silly steps are!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, ask): find the real problem before fixing it  
> _What is the real problem here: the snow, or the steps?_  
> - ✅ The steps → Yes! The steps are the problem. A ramp fixes it.
> - The snow → The snow makes it harder. But the steps stop her every day. A ramp fixes it.
> _For grown-ups: Worked out that the steps, not the person, were the problem to fix._

**You**: Then let’s make a ramp. Now. You tell me where.  
_You dig in the snow. Linnet is the boss._  
**Linnet**: Longer! Not steeper. LONGER!  
_The ramp is done. Down goes Linnet. Whoosh!_  
_Snowdrops! Little white flowers, all round the bench._  

#### `s26-complete-post`

> _(What shared places do you visit? A park? A library?)_

> - ✅ Winter → Yes! Snow comes in winter, when it’s cold.
> - Summer → Summer is warm. Snow means winter!
> _For grown-ups: Matched snow to winter._

**Dusty**: I’m making a bench from the old steps. For your Grove.  
**Dusty**: And this is my digging apron. It’s yours now.

#### `c12-wall-garden`

_Gran Hazel walks past the old wall. She stops._  
_The door is open! She has never seen it before._  
_She goes in slowly, down the ramp._  
_Roses. Snowdrops. A bench. A robin!_  
_Hazel stands still for a long time. She doesn’t say anything._  
_She picks a little red rosehip. She puts it on her coat._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a rosehip is a rose’s fruit, with seeds inside  
> _A rosehip is a rose’s fruit. Seeds grow inside it._  
> _First a flower. Then a fruit. Then seeds!_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a rosehip is the fruit of a rose, with seeds inside._

_On the way out, she pats the post. Gently._  

#### `end-moss-sleeps-garden`

_Moss faded. That means he died. His body stopped, and won’t start again._  
_His flower grew on the hill, by his flat stone._  
_Linnet says its seeds will go over the old wall._  
_Into his patch by Hush’s bench. Where the white pebble is._  
_The robin will help, she says._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-LS2-2, notice): birds carry seeds to new places  
> _Birds eat seeds and berries. They drop the seeds in new places._  
> _That’s how plants travel!_  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that birds help plants spread by carrying their seeds._

_So Moss’s flowers will grow in both places. He is remembered._  

#### `end-epi-garden`

_The door in the old wall is never locked now._  
_Linnet comes every summer. She tells everyone where to dig!_  
_In June, Hush’s roses all come out at once._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-1, ask): June is in summer  
> _The roses come out in June. Which season is that?_  
> - ✅ Summer → Yes! Here in the Grove, June is summer. Warm and sunny.
> - Winter → Winter is snowy. June is summer, when roses come out.
> _For grown-ups: Matched the month of June to summer._

_Pink and red and white. Like a party!_  

#### `end-epi-garden-cold`

_The door in the old wall is open._  
_But your Nubbins don’t go in. They sit outside, very still._  
_Linnet came one summer. She looked at them for a long time._  
**Linnet**: Why don’t they play?  
_Being safe is not the same as being happy._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): safe and happy are not the same  
> _(What makes you feel happy, not just safe?)_  
> _(Playing? Friends? Running about outside?)_  
> _For grown-ups: Talked about what makes them happy, as well as safe._

_The door is still open. The roses are still waiting._  

#### `s27-row-sold`

_Look out of the shed window. You can see the pens._  
_Each pen has a grey runner. They stand very still._  
_At the end is one looking down the valley, towards the Grove._  
_You know that one. It used to be yours._  
_You sold it to Corvin in the spring. Now it has a 9._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): missing someone, and saying so  
> _It’s all right to feel sad, or sorry, or both._  
> _Missing someone shows you love them._  
> _For grown-ups: Talked about missing someone, and feeling sorry._

_Hob comes along with two buckets, whistling._  

#### `s27-words-sold`

**Fern**: My word is SOMEBODY’S. Every Nubbin is somebody’s.  
**Clover**: Mine is WARM. Everybody needs to feel warm.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, ask): hearing rhymes  
> _WARM. Which word rhymes with WARM?_  
> - ✅ Storm → Yes! Warm, storm. They sound the same at the end.
> - Cat → Warm, cat… no. Listen: warm, storm. Storm rhymes!
> _For grown-ups: Listened for a word that rhymes with warm._

**Luna**: Mine is HOME. Everything grows towards home.  
**Byte**: Mine is “statistically above average”!  
_Spindle looks at Byte’s word for a long, long time._  
**Sparks**: Too long for a fence, Byte. Sorry!  
_Then Spindle points at the runner at the end of the row._  
**Sparks**: She wants its real name. Not the number.  
_You tell her the name you gave it when it hatched._  
_Spindle writes it small, to practise._  

#### `s27-midnight-shield`

_In the middle of the night, a light comes on in Corvin’s window._  
_Corvin sits and watches you. All night long._  
_He watches your lantern. He watches your hands._  
_He thinks you are the one writing. He never sees Spindle._  
_Spindle works on and on, thread by thread._  
_Spindle is your secret._  
_Near morning, his light goes out. Spindle ties the last thread._  

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, do): putting times of day in order  
> _(Put them in order: evening, the middle of the night, morning.)_  
> _First evening. Next the middle of the night. Last, morning!_  
> Check: `edu:order:night:evening-midnight-morning`
> _For grown-ups: Put evening, midnight and morning in order._


#### `s27-home`

_In the morning, everyone comes up to the fence._  
_The whole long fence says HOME. Big white letters!_  
**Fern**: HOME! She must have run out of fence!  
**Mr Tull**: I came for the runners that didn’t win. But not that one.  
**Mr Tull**: Everybody knows its name. I can’t sell it. Good day!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, notice): names matter: everybody knows this one  
> _Mr Tull won’t take a runner that everybody knows by name._  
> _When people know your name, they look out for you._  
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how being known by name helps people look out for each other._

_Mr Tull drives away over the hill. His cart is empty._  
_Hob says its real name. The name you gave it._  
**Corvin Vale**: It was yours once. Two hundred Shells. That’s what I paid.  

**Choices**

- **Pay the two hundred Shells.**
    - You count the Shells into Corvin’s cold hand.
    - **Corvin Vale**: Paid. It’s yours.
    - Hob opens the pen. Your Nubbin steps out.
    - It walks to you, slowly, all the way.
    - It leans on your leg, just like when it was little.
    - It’s coming home.
- **Let everyone pass a hat.**
    - **Sparks**: A hat! Who’s got a hat?
    - Everyone puts in some Shells. Fern puts in a button!
    - **Fern**: It’s a very good button.
    - Corvin counts it all. Two hundred Shells. And a button.
    - He puts the button in his pocket.
    - Hob opens the pen. Your Nubbin steps out.
    - It walks to you, slowly, all the way.
    - It leans on your leg, just like when it was little.
    - It’s coming home.

#### `s27-gate-sold`

_You come to the Grove gate._  
_Your old Nubbin bumps the bottom bar with its nose._  
_It remembers! The gate sticks. Lift and push!_  

> **Lesson** (literacy, SL.K.1, do): talking about a memory of home  
> _Your Nubbin remembers home._  
> _(What do you remember about your home? Tell me one thing.)_  
> Check: `edu:say:remember:home`
> _For grown-ups: Talked about a memory of home._

_It sits by the gatepost and looks, and looks._  
_The painted 9 will wash off by spring._  

#### `s27-carry-clank`

_Clank comes too. He loves ladders._  
**Clank**: I can’t climb! I have one wheel! But I’m VERY good at steady!  
_Sparks puts up her long ladder._  
_Clank holds the bottom. He doesn’t wobble one bit._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): everyone can help in their own way  
> _Clank can’t climb. But he can help in his own way._  
> _Everybody can help with something._  
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how everyone can help in their own way._

_Your Nubbin climbs up, step by step, and gets the egg sac._  
**Clank**: Steady. Steady. Quiet steady.  
_Down it comes, holding the sac very gently._  
**Sparks**: Take it to the Grove shed. The top shelf is warm.  

#### `s27-carry-wisp`

_Something grey drops down from a beam. It’s Wisp!_  
_Wisp has a torn ear. He likes warm things._  
_He puts his ear on the egg sac. It’s warm from the sun._  
**Wisp**: mine. warm. mine.  
**You**: It’s Spindle’s. But you can keep it warm for her. All winter.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): looking after something that belongs to someone else  
> _The egg sac isn’t Wisp’s. What can he do?_  
> - ✅ Look after it for Spindle → Yes. He can keep it safe and warm for her. That’s kind.
> - Keep it for ever → They’re Spindle’s eggs. Wisp can look after them for her, and that’s kind.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about looking after something that belongs to someone else._

**Wisp**: keep it warm. yes.  
_Wisp carries it down, very gently, in his mouth._  
_He keeps it under the cottage step all winter._  
_Spindle waves two legs at him. That means thank you._  

#### `s27-spring`

_It’s spring! The snow has gone._  
_In the Grove shed, the egg sac opens._  
_Out come baby spiders. Hundreds! Each one is tiny._  
_They climb up to the top of the gate._  
_Each one lets out a silky thread. Whoosh! The wind lifts them away._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): baby spiders float away on silk threads  
> _Baby spiders are called spiderlings._  
> _The wind catches their silk threads. Away they float, to new homes._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that baby spiders float away on silk threads in the wind._

_Three baby spiders stay._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _(Count the spiders who stay: one, two, three.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:spiders:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three._

_Next morning, there’s a tiny web in the shed window._  
_It says EVENING. You laugh, and say “Evening!” back._  
_We will always remember Spindle._  

#### `s27-spring-wisp`

_It’s spring! The snow has gone._  
_Under the cottage step, the egg sac opens._  
_Wisp sees the baby spiders first. He watches them very carefully._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a spider’s life cycle: egg, spiderling, spider  
> _First an egg. Then a tiny spiderling. Then a big spider, like Spindle._  
> _Then the big spiders lay eggs, and it starts again._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard the life cycle of a spider: egg, spiderling, spider._

_They climb on his nose. He doesn’t mind one bit!_  
_They climb up to the top of the gate._  
_Each one lets out a silky thread. Whoosh! The wind lifts them away._  
_Wisp watches them go. Then he goes back under his step._  
_Three baby spiders stay. Next morning, a tiny web says EVENING._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _(Count the spiders who stay: one, two, three.)_  
> Check: `edu:count:spiders:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three._

_We will always remember Spindle._  

#### `s28-null-minder`

_Byte’s front room. A big clock sits on the shelf. Tick, tock._  
_Null sits in a little bed under it. Null waits for the bell._  
**Byte**: That’s Null. It’s on a timetable. It’s going very well.  
_Parcel bows. Null doesn’t look. Null only watches the bell._  
_So Parcel climbs in beside Null. It waits for the bell too._  
_Byte’s face goes pale. That means white and worried._  
**Byte**: No. Null isn’t mine. It’s borrowed. That isn’t fair on Null.  
_Byte lifts Parcel out, gently. Then he looks at the clock._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): being fair to animals  
> _Null waits all day for a bell. Is that fair on Null?_  
> - ✅ No. Null wants to play → Yes. Nubbins need to play and run about. Byte is starting to see that.
> - Yes, clocks are fun → Clocks can be fun. But Null needs to play, not just wait.

#### `s28-grue-back-weed`

_Pixel fixes the watch. Tick, tick, tick! It works better than before._  
_Knock, knock. It’s Mr Grue, holding a kitchen chair._  
**Mr Grue**: I’ve come for the marmalade. Not the party.  
**Mr Grue**: Your chairs are too low. I brought my own.  
**Mr Grue**: You weeded round my tree as if it mattered.  
_Parcel bows to Mr Grue, very low. That is Parcel’s way of saying sorry._  
_Mr Grue gets his watch back. He moves his chair to the front._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): saying thank you  
> _Mr Grue came back to the party. What can we say to him?_  
> - ✅ Thank you for coming! → Yes. A thank-you makes a grumpy neighbour feel welcome.
> - Go away! → Oh, that would hurt his feelings. “Thank you for coming” is kinder.
> - Nothing at all → He might think we don’t want him. A thank-you tells him we do.
> _For grown-ups: Practised saying thank you, and making a grumpy neighbour feel welcome._

#### `s31-midnight-wisp`

_Just after midnight, a thin grey animal creeps out._  
_One of his ears is torn._

**Tam**: Is that him?  
**Nettie**: That’s a thief.  
_It’s Wisp. He licks his lips and slips back under the hedge._  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): taking without asking is not fair; sharing with the hungry is kind  
> _Wisp took the apple without asking. Was that fair?_  
> - ✅ Not fair, but he was hungry → Yes. Taking isn’t fair. But Wisp was hungry. We can share with hungry animals.
> - Yes, fair → Taking without asking isn’t fair. But hungry animals need food, so we can share.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about fairness: taking without asking, and sharing with someone hungry._

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): what helps when someone is cross  
> _Nettie is very cross. What might help her?_  
> - ✅ Listen and say sorry → Yes. Listening and saying sorry help cross feelings get smaller.
> - Laugh → That might make her crosser! Listening and saying sorry help more.
> - Walk away → She might feel alone. Staying, listening and saying sorry help.
> _For grown-ups: Chose listening and saying sorry as ways to help a cross friend._

#### `a02-15-which-monk`

**Choices**

- **Point at the one on the left.**
    - **Monkey**: Ha! You see? The luggage-carrier knows me.
    - **Monkey**: Ha! You see? The luggage-carrier knows me.
    - They say it together, with the same grin.
    - **Monkey**: That settles nothing, Cousin’s keeper. I am sorry I asked.
- **Point at the one on the right.**
    - **Monkey**: There! Somebody with eyes at last.
    - **Monkey**: There! Somebody with eyes at last.
    - Both bow. Both bows are exactly as deep.
    - **Monkey**: That settles nothing, Cousin’s keeper. I am sorry I asked.
- **Say it plainly: “I can’t tell. I won’t pretend I can.”**
    - Both Monkeys open their mouths. Then neither says a word.
    - **Monkey**: Good. Guessing is how you lose a monk.
    - **Sandy**: Then we ask the one who does know.

**The Ivory Merchant**: You are free, Sinbad. I am sorry I have nothing to give you.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, notice): seeing kindness can change our minds  
> _The master watched the gentle herd. It changed his mind._

> _For grown-ups: Heard that noticing kindness can change our minds._

**Young Sinbad**: You are giving me home. That is plenty.  

#### `a06-15-quay-kept`

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, notice): feeling words: content  
> _Sinbad is poor, but he is content._

> _For grown-ups: Learned the feeling word “content”._

**Choices**

#### `a06-15-street-kept`

> _The porter shared what he had._

> _For grown-ups: Heard that sharing a meal shows someone they matter._

#### `a06-16-telling-nothing`

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): waiting is hard, and things help  
> _Sinbad waited a whole dry season, and then the rains._  
> _That is a long wait!_

> - Shouting “Is it time yet?” → Waiting is hard, and that is okay. Doing something nice helps the time go by.

#### `a11-20-complete-sat`

_Christopher Robin and Pooh walk off together._  
_You do not follow. This part is theirs._  
_Your Nubbin turns round three times in the grass, and sits._  
_A flat round is left, like the one by Eeyore’s step._  

> **Lesson** (science, K-ESS2-2, notice): flattened grass shows where an animal has sat  
> _When an animal sits or sleeps in grass, it leaves a flat round._  
> _Signs like this tell us who has been there. Scientists call it a clue._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that flattened grass is a clue that an animal has rested there._

_A boy and his Bear are playing in that ring of trees._  
_The page closes gently, like a door nobody bangs._  
_You are back in the Grove, with the atlas on your knee._  
_By the stream is a little bridge. One place is worn smooth, for sitting._  

#### `a11-margin-hazel`

_The atlas lies open at the last page of the Forest._  
_Beside the ring of trees is a note in the margin, in soft pencil._  
_You know the writing. It is Gran Hazel’s._  
_It says: Read this to the little one, the summer they stayed._  
_They asked where Christopher Robin went._  
_Somewhere, I said. Not away._  
_At the bottom is one letter: H._  
_Maybe you remember a little: a lap, a voice, a turning page._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, notice): writing things down keeps people close  
> _Gran Hazel wrote this note a long time ago. And it still reaches you._  
> _A note, a drawing or a letter can keep someone close._  
> _You can make one too._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a note or drawing can keep someone close._

_Your Nubbin climbs into your lap. You sit with the page._  

#### `a12-01-ember-forgiven`

_Your Nubbin carries a little lantern. In it is Cinder’s ember, small and red._  
_It burns steady. Grandmother holds her hands out to it._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): a fire gives heat and light  
> _A little fire gives two things. Which two?_  
> - ✅ Warmth and light → Yes! A fire gives warmth and light.
> - Ice and snow → Ice and snow are cold! A fire gives warmth and light.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a fire gives warmth and light._

**Grandmother**: Now that’s a good little fire. Bring it up; the eaves get cold.  

#### `a12-01-ember-remembered`

_Your Nubbin carries a little lantern. In it is Cinder’s ember, small and red._  
_It flickers now and then, as if remembering. It never goes out._  

> **Lesson** (science, notice): flames flicker when air moves  
> **Grandmother**: A flame flickers when air moves. A lantern keeps it safe.  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that flames flicker when air moves._

**Grandmother**: That one has a story in it. Bring it up; the eaves get cold.  

#### `a12-04-kept`

_The white sledge doesn’t pass you. It stops right beside you._  
_The driver looks down. Her face is ice, lovely and still._  
**The Snow Queen**: You keep things too.  
_She says nothing about the stone in your pocket._  
_She opens her white bearskin. It is soft and very quiet inside._  
_Nothing would hurt there. But nothing would be warm, either._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): feelings are part of you  
> _Is it okay to keep your feelings, even the sad ones?_  
> - ✅ Yes. They are part of me → Yes. All your feelings are part of you. That is okay.
> - No. I should feel nothing → Feelings are allowed. The hard ones get easier with a hug.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keeping all our feelings, including the hard ones._


**Choices**

- **“No.”**
    - **You**: No, thank you.
    - She looks at you a moment longer, without anger. Then she drives on.
- **Say nothing. Step back.**
    - You step back, out of reach of the fur.
    - She almost smiles. Then she drives on.

#### `a12-10-free-night`

_The robber girl comes to you first, holding your sleepy Nubbin._  
**The Robber Girl**: There. I gave it back. Nobody made me.  
**The Robber Girl**: If I can give one back, I can give two.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): doing the right thing on your own  
> _The robber girl gave the Nubbin back by herself. That was…_  
> - ✅ Kind and honest → Yes. She chose to do the right thing, with nobody making her.
> - Silly → Giving back what is not yours is kind and honest, not silly.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about choosing to do the right thing without being made to._

**The Robber Girl**: Bae, I’m untying you. Carry this girl to the Snow Queen’s.  
_Bae leaps for joy. The robber girl lifts Gerda onto his back._  
**The Robber Girl**: Here are your boots. I’m keeping the muff. It’s too pretty.  
**The Robber Girl**: Take Mother’s big mittens. They reach your elbows.  
**The Robber Girl**: Two loaves for the road. And don’t cry. Look happy!  
**Bae**: Climb on behind her, lodger. You weigh less than a sack of salt.  
**The Robber Girl**: Run! And look after her!  

**Choices**

- **Wave goodbye to the robber girl.**
    - You wave. She doesn’t wave back, but she watches until you are gone.
- **Nod to her, as one equal to another.**
    - You nod. She nods back, once, hard, like shutting a box.

#### `a12-12-ember-forgiven`

_The Finnish woman stops. She looks at the lantern and its steady ember._  
**The Finnish Woman**: That was a fierce fire once.  
**The Finnish Woman**: Now it only keeps someone warm. That’s the right size for a fire.  
_She warms her hands at it, as if greeting someone._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): only grown-ups handle real flame  
> _A real flame is hot. Who should look after it?_  
> - ✅ A grown-up → Yes. Grown-ups look after fire. The lantern keeps the flame safe.
> - Any child → Fire can burn. Leave it to grown-ups, and keep your distance.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that grown-ups look after real flames._


#### `a12-12-ember-remembered`

_The Finnish woman stops. She looks at the lantern and its flickering ember._  
**The Finnish Woman**: That was a fierce fire once.  
**The Finnish Woman**: Now it only keeps someone warm. That’s the right size for a fire.  
_The ember flickers while she looks. It doesn’t go out._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): things and people can change  
> _The ember was fierce once. Now it is gentle. People can change too._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that people, like the ember, can grow gentler._


#### `a12-13-wait-forgiven`

_You unroll the reindeer skin and sit. Your Nubbin sets its lantern down._  
_Cinder’s ember burns steady. It isn’t much of a fire, but it’s enough._  
_The cold comes to the edge of its light and stops._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): warmth spreads from a fire  
> _Warmth spreads from a fire. We sit close, but not too close._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that warmth spreads out from a fire._

_There is no wind. Just the quiet, the bush and the red berries._  
_You count the berries. Then you count again. A different number!_  
_You don’t know how long. You will be here when it’s over._  

**Choices**

- **Count the berries again.**
    - So many berries! Your Nubbin points at one you missed.
- **Hum Gerda’s rose tune, under your breath.**
    - You hum quietly. Your Nubbin hums it back, a beat behind.
- **Just sit.**
    - You just sit. It turns out you are good at it.

#### `a12-13-wait-remembered`

_You unroll the reindeer skin and sit. Your Nubbin sets its lantern down._  
_Cinder’s ember flickers now and then, as if remembering. It never goes out._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a lantern shields a flame from the wind  
> _Wind can blow a flame out. A lantern keeps the flame safe and still._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a lantern shields a flame from the wind._

_It keeps you both from freezing. That is all it does now._  
_There is no wind. Just the quiet, the bush and the red berries._  
_You count the berries. Then you count again. A different number!_  
_You don’t know how long. You will be here when it’s over._  

**Choices**

- **Count the berries again.**
    - So many berries! Your Nubbin points at one you missed.
- **Hum Gerda’s rose tune, under your breath.**
    - You hum quietly. Your Nubbin hums it back, a beat behind.
- **Just sit.**
    - You just sit. It turns out you are good at it.

#### `a12-14-prayer-kept`

_Gerda says her prayer. Her breath turns to smoke, then to bright figures._  
_They clear the road. She walks on, quickly and bravely._  
_Then some snowflakes turn, and run along the ground towards you._  
_They reach the skin and stop. Then they part, like a door opening._  
_In your pocket, the stone hums. It sounds pleased._  
_The road is open. Nothing would stop you._  
_You could walk in. You know how welcome you would be._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): keeping a promise  
> _The road is open, but you promised to wait. What do you do?_  
> - ✅ Keep my promise and wait → Yes. Keeping a promise is a strong and kind thing to do.
> - Go in anyway → Gerda must do this part alone. Waiting is how you help.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about keeping a promise when something tempting is offered._


**Choices**

- **Sit back down.**
    - You sit down on the skin. After a while the snowflakes close the road.
    - The stone goes quiet. Your Nubbin climbs back into your coat.
- **Turn your back on the road.**
    - You face the way you came. The snowflakes close up like a door.
    - The stone goes quiet. Your Nubbin climbs back into your coat.

#### `a12-17-rider-night`

_Birds sing. The forest has green buds. A horse comes out of it._  
_On it rides a girl in a red cap. It is the robber girl!_  
**The Robber Girl**: I got bored at home. I’m off to see the world.  
_Two wood pigeons ride on her saddle, and they are not tied._  
**The Robber Girl**: They’re not tied any more.  
**The Robber Girl**: Mostly.  
**The Robber Girl**: So this is Kay. Was he worth running to the world’s end?  
**Gerda**: How are the prince and princess? And the ravens?  
**The Robber Girl**: The prince and princess went abroad. The old raven died.  
_The raven’s body stopped working. He was very old._  
**The Robber Girl**: His sweetheart wears a black thread on her leg, to remember him.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): when someone dies, and remembering  
> _When someone dies, their body stops working, and it does not start again._  
> _It is okay to feel sad. We can remember them, and talk about them._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard what death means in plain words, and that sadness and remembering are okay._


**Choices**

- **Say you’re sorry about the raven.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: Don’t be. He had a good job and all the scraps he wanted.
- **Admire her red cap.**
    - **The Robber Girl**: It’s a good cap. You can’t have it.

#### `a12-18-pocket`

**Grandmother**: Lodger. Why is your hand always on your pocket?  
_You look down, and it is. You hadn’t noticed._  
**Grandmother**: Kay held his burning-glass tight, all last winter. I would not see that again.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): noticing our habits  
> _Why is it good to notice what our hands and bodies are doing?_  
> - ✅ So we can choose what to do → Yes. Noticing gives us a choice.
> - It is not good → It is useful. When we notice, we can choose.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how noticing our habits lets us choose._


**Choices**

- **“Habit.”**
    - **Grandmother**: A habit is only a thing we have stopped noticing. So notice it.
- **“Something I’m keeping.”**
    - **Grandmother**: Keeping is fine. Just be the one doing the keeping.
- **Say nothing. Take your hand out of your pocket.**
    - You take your hand out. Grandmother holds it until it is warm.

#### `a12-18-complete-night`

_A wood pigeon lands on the roses. Nothing ties it, and it stays._  
_It might be one of the robber girl’s. Either way, it chose this._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): freedom and friendship  
> _Nobody tied the pigeon. Why does it stay?_  
> - ✅ It likes it here → Yes. It stays because it wants to. That is how friends are.
> - It is stuck → Nothing holds it. It stays because it wants to.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how friends stay because they want to._

_Your Nubbin, in its red cap, sits beside it. They watch the rooftops._  
_The page settles under your hand, like paper laid flat._  
_You are back in the Grove with Nova’s atlas. A rose petal lies inside._  
_On the cottage windowsill stands a window box with a rose tree._  
_Another stands on the lantern shed across the way. Between them is a plank._  

#### `a13-01-page-clank`

_Nova’s atlas opens. The page is all brown ink._  
_A hill town. A long white road. The sea at the bottom._  
_This story begins with a piece of wood. Just wood!_  
_The ink turns to rain. You, your Nubbin and Clank get wet._  
**Clank**: Announcement: it is steps! This whole country is made of steps!  

> **Lesson** (science, K-2-ETS1-1, notice): a ramp is a way to solve the problem of steps  
> _Steps are a problem for wheels. A ramp is a clever answer._  
> _A ramp is a smooth slope. Wheels can roll up it!_  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that a ramp can solve the problem that steps make for wheels._

_Clank unfolds a ramp that Byte made. It has three boards._  
**Clank**: Unfold, roll, fold up. Byte made me practise forty times.  
_One door is open, with sawdust on the step. In you go._  
**Master Cherry**: Come in! Shut the weather out. And bring your… kettle?  
**Clank**: Announcement: I am Clank! I am a guest! I love it!  
_Master Cherry has a nose like a ripe red cherry._  
**Master Cherry**: I will make a table leg from this old log.  
_He lifts his axe._  
**A Small Voice**: Ow! Not so hard!  

#### `a13-05-coat-clank`

_Geppetto comes home in the snow. He has a new spelling-book._  
**Pinocchio**: Babbo, where is your coat?  
**Geppetto**: I sold it. I was too warm.  
_Pinocchio hugs him tight. He understands._  
**Clank**: He sold his coat. For a puppet that kicked his nose.  
**Clank**: Is that a job?  
**You**: No. It is not a job.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): people do loving things because they care, not because it is a job  
> _Clank asks: is it a job? Why did Geppetto sell his coat?_  
> - ✅ Because he loves Pinocchio. → Yes. Love is not a job. It is something we do for someone we care about.
> - Because it was a job. → Not a job. Nobody paid him. He did it because he cared.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about doing loving things because we care, not because it is a job._

_Clank’s chimney-light flickers. He is thinking about it._  

#### `a13-10-doctors-done-carried`

_The doctors pick up their bags. The cricket goes last, slowly._  
_At the door he stops. He nods to you. A small, neat nod._  
_Then he goes down the stairs._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): a nod can say thank you without words  
> _The cricket nods to you. What is he saying, without any words?_  
> - ✅ Thank you. → Yes! A nod, a smile or a wave can say thank you.
> - Go away. → He is saying thank you, for the hedge. A nod can say a lot.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that a nod or a smile can say thank you._


#### `a13-18-sea-carried`

_Up from the sea comes a wooden puppet, wriggling like an eel!_  
**The Drum Man**: Where is my donkey?  
**Pinocchio**: The sea washed the donkey off. I am a puppet again!  
_Pinocchio swims away, laughing._  
_He swims under your rock and looks up._  
**Pinocchio**: Your cricket was right. I did grow up a donkey.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-awareness, ask): saying “I was wrong” is brave  
> _Pinocchio says the cricket was right. Is it hard to say “I was wrong”?_  
> - ✅ Yes, but it is brave. → Yes! Saying “I was wrong” takes courage.
> - No, it is easy. → For most of us, it is hard. That is why it is so brave.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how brave it is to say “I was wrong”._

**Pinocchio**: Do not tell him I said so.  

#### `a13-19-complete-clank`

_The Tunny carries them to shore. Clank rides on his back._  
_On the sand, Pinocchio helps his babbo sit down._  

> **Lesson** (science, 2-PS1-1, do): metal sinks and wood floats, so Clank rides on the Tunny  
> _Clank is metal. Metal kettles sink. So he rides the Tunny!_  
> _Sort: wood floats, kettle sinks, leaf floats, stone sinks._  
> Check: `edu:sort:float-or-sink:kettle`
> _For grown-ups: Sorted things into floaters and sinkers, including a metal kettle._

**Pinocchio**: Thank you, Tunny. I want a bigger word than thank you.  
_He cannot find one. So he kisses the Tunny on the nose._  
_Clank looks at Pinocchio. Something inside him clicks._  
**Clank**: He does not have the word either.  
**Clank**: Nobody put it in him.  
_Your Nubbin keeps the green bottle. It will not give it up._  

#### `a13-20-hut-carried`

**The Talking-cricket**: Oh, my Pinocchio.  
**Pinocchio**: Oh, my dear little Cricket!  
**Pinocchio**: I am sorry about the mallet. Please forgive me.  
**The Talking-cricket**: I forgive you. I only wanted to remind you.  
**The Talking-cricket**: Be kind to everyone you can. Then someone may be kind to you.  
**The Talking-cricket**: And thank your friend for the hedge.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): saying thank you to someone who helped us  
> _The cricket says thank you to you, for the hedge._  
> _Who helped you this week?_  
> - ✅ Someone helped me. I can say thank you. → Yes! Say thank you, or draw a picture for them.
> - Nobody helped me. → Think again. A grown-up, a friend, a pet. Someone helps us every day.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about who helped them this week and how to say thank you._

_He settles on his beam, and looks at you. That is plenty._  

#### `a13-20-complete-clank`

_Pinocchio jumps out of bed. He is not wood. He is a boy!_  
_Geppetto is well again. He is carving a frame and whistling._  
**Pinocchio**: Babbo! Look at me!  
**Geppetto**: I am looking. I have always been looking.  
_The old puppet leans on a chair. His head is on one side._  
**Pinocchio**: I am glad that is over. I am so glad I am me.  
_Clank rolls down his ramp. He parks beside the old puppet._  
_He does not say anything about it._  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, ask): sitting quietly beside someone is a way to care  
> _Clank sits beside the old puppet, saying nothing. Is that kind?_  
> - ✅ Yes. Being close is kind. → Yes! Sitting close shows we care.
> - No. He should talk. → We do not have to talk. Sitting close can be the kindest thing.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about sitting quietly beside someone as a way to show we care._


#### `a13-20-word`

**Clank**: Did they love this one? The wooden one?  
**You**: Yes. He sold his coat for him.  
**Geppetto**: Before he did a single thing.  
**Clank**: If I stop being useful, will you still love me?  
_Your Nubbin climbs up on his hood. Geppetto puts down his chisel._  
**Clank**: Love. That is the word.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): what love can feel like: being looked after and looked at  
> _Who has shown love to you today?_  
> _(Let your child think and answer.)_  
> - ✅ Someone who cooks for me. → Yes! Feeding someone is a kind of love.
> - ✅ Someone who gives me a cuddle. → Yes! A cuddle is love too.
> - I do not know yet. → That is fine. Love is often small and quiet. Look out for it today.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about the people who show love to us, and the small ways they do it._

**Clank**: Nobody puts it in. Somebody does it to you first.  
_Clank is still a kettle on one wheel. And that is just right._  
**Geppetto**: Take my old bench. The little Nubbin on it is lovely as it is.  
_The page closes softly._  
_You are back in the Grove, with sawdust in your hair._

#### `a13-grove-clank-dusk`

_It is dusk in the Grove. The Nubbins come in from the grass._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): dusk is when day turns to night  
> _Dusk is the time when day turns into night._  
> _The Sun goes down, the sky goes soft, and the first star comes out._

#### `a13-grove-pixel`

_Pixel is at the lantern shed, cleaning Clank’s nose._  
**Clank**: Pixel. You did not put it in.  
**Pixel**: Put what in?  
**Clank**: The word. The one I did not have.  
**Pixel**: I know. I am sorry.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): when someone says sorry, we can forgive  
> _Pixel said sorry. What did Clank say back?_  
> - ✅ “Do not be.” He forgave her. → Yes! Forgiving means letting go, and being kind.
> - He was cross. → He was not. He forgave her kindly.
> _For grown-ups: Noticed that saying sorry and forgiving each other helps friends._

**Clank**: Do not be. Geppetto did not either.  
_Pixel laughs, and puts Clank’s nose back on._  

#### `a13-grove-clank-idle`

**Clank**: Announcement: I am just here.  
**Clank**: Announcement: still just here.  
**Clank**: Not helping. Just here. Both are allowed.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): being together without doing anything is good too  
> _Sometimes friends just sit together. They do not need to play or help._  
> _Being together is enough._  
> _For grown-ups: Heard that being together without doing anything is enough._


#### `a14-corvin-joins`

_Corvin Vale is on the page beside you, in his good coat._  
_He is out of breath._  

> **Lesson** (health, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): breathing speeds up when we hurry, and slows down when we rest  
> _Corvin hurried to get here. When you run fast, what does your breathing do?_  
> - ✅ It goes fast, then slows down when you rest → Yes. Puff, puff! Your body needs more air when you run. Rest, and it slows down.
> - It stops → Breathing never stops. It goes fast when you run, and slow when you rest.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that breathing goes faster when we run and slows down again when we rest._

**Corvin Vale**: I saw the atlas open.  
**Corvin Vale**: There is no gate on a page, so I could not knock.  
**Corvin Vale**: I know a little about the long way home.  
_Your Nubbin walks on ahead. That means he can come._  

#### `a14-14-harbour-shout`

_He wakes in the mist. He does not know where he is._  
**Odysseus**: Where am I? Is this a strange shore?  
_A young shepherd comes along._  
**A Young Shepherd**: This is Ithaca. Even far away, people have heard of Ithaca.  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RF.K.2, do): clap the beats in a word  
> _The island is called Ithaca. It has three beats: Ith-a-ca._  
> _(Clap the three beats together.)_  
> Check: `edu:clap:syllables:ithaca`
> _For grown-ups: Clapped the three syllables in the word Ithaca._

_Odysseus is so happy. But he tells the shepherd a made-up story._  
_The shepherd smiles, and turns into Athena._  
**Athena**: You cannot help being clever, Odysseus. Look! Your harbour, your tree, your hill.  
_Odysseus kneels and kisses the ground._  
**Athena**: Bad guests are in your house. Keep who you are secret, for now.  
_She touches him with her wand. He is an old beggar!_  
**The Beggar**: Well. Nobody will know me now.  
**The Beggar**: And you. Not a word this time, not even a little one.

**The Beggar**: You will not say a word. You never do. I am counting on it.  

#### `a14-16-gate-shout`

_Outside the gate is a heap, and on it lies an old dog._  
_He is thin, and nobody looks after him now._  
**Eumaeus**: That is Argos. He was the best hunting dog.  
_The old dog lifts his head. His nose twitches._  
_He knows! After twenty years, he knows his master._  
_His ears go flat and his tail wags. He cannot get up._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.1.4, ask): words that show feelings: a wagging tail  
> _Argos’s tail wags and his ears go flat. What does a wagging tail show?_  
> - ✅ He is happy → Yes. A wagging tail shows a dog is glad. Argos is so glad to see his friend.
> - He is cross → A cross dog growls. Argos is wagging, which shows he is happy.
> _For grown-ups: Read a dog’s body language: a wagging tail shows he is glad._

_The beggar cannot go to him, or everyone will know._  
_The beggar turns away and wipes a tear._  
**Eumaeus**: Come on, old man.  
_They go in through the gate. He does not look back._

#### `a14-16-sit-corvin`

_You sit beside the heap in the warm sun._  
_Your Nubbin goes up to the old dog, gently._  
_Argos sniffs it. He puts his head down._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): dogs have a very good sense of smell  
> _Argos sniffs. A dog’s nose is very, very good._  
> _How did Argos know his friend?_  
> - ✅ By his smell → Yes. A dog remembers smells for a very long time.
> - By his shoes → The beggar wears rags! Argos knew him by his smell.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that a dog knows loved people by smell, because its nose is very good._

_Your Nubbin lies against his side._  
_Corvin comes out of the gate and sits on your other side._  
_He pats the old dog. His hands are warm now._

_Argos’s tail moves once more in the dust._  
_His eyes are on the gate. He is very tired._  

**Choices**

- **Scratch behind his ears.**
    - His eyes half close. He likes it.
- **Just sit with him.**
    - You just sit. That is enough.
- **Tell him, quietly, that his friend is home.**
    - **You**: He is home. You were right.
    - Argos sighs, a long, happy sigh.

#### `a14-19-aegis-done-corvin`

> - ✅ To warm places, far away → Yes. Many birds fly far away to warm places for the winter.
> - Into the sea → Swallows cannot live in the sea. They fly to warm places on land.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that many birds fly far away to warm places in winter._

**Telemachus**: They are gone. Really gone.

#### `a14-20-bed-shout`

> **Lesson** (science, K-LS1-1, ask): roots hold a tree in the ground  
> _The bed is built round a living olive tree._  
> _Why can you not move a tree?_  
> - ✅ Its roots hold it in the ground → Yes. Roots grow deep and hold a tree tight.
> - It is too sleepy → Trees are not sleepy. Their roots hold them in the ground.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that roots hold a tree in the ground._

_Penelope smiles at you over his shoulder._

> - He cannot find the gate → He found it! He waits because it is polite.

#### `a14-margin-hazel`

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): why something happens: cause and effect  
> _Hazel’s gate sticks on purpose. Why does it stick?_

> - It is broken → It is not broken. It sticks so we can hear who comes.

#### `a18-16-sable`

_You shut the atlas. Under the cottage table, something grey is waiting._  
_Sable. She has the little painted doll between her paws._  
_She holds it very carefully, as if it were an egg._  
_She does not give it back. She does not run._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): being gentle with a shy animal  
> _Sable is shy and slow to trust._  
> _What is a kind way to be with her?_  
> - ✅ Sit quietly and wait → Yes. Sitting quietly and waiting helps a shy friend feel safe.
> - Grab the doll back → Grabbing would scare her. Sit quietly and wait.
> - Shout hello → Shouting would frighten her. Sit quietly and wait.
> _For grown-ups: Chose a gentle way to be with a shy animal: sit quietly and wait._

_She puts her chin down on it and shuts her eyes._  
_Your Nubbin looks at its empty pouch. Then it sits down beside her._  

#### `a19-08-hand-slow`

_You know this moment. You sat still like this with Sable._  
_So you sit very still at the edge of the sand._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): sitting still shows we are no danger  
> _Sitting very still helped Sable, too. Why does sitting still help a scared animal?_  
> - ✅ It shows we are no danger → Yes. Still and quiet says “I will not hurt you”.
> - It makes us sleepy → Not sleepy. Sitting still tells a scared animal we are safe.
> - It makes a lot of noise → Sitting still is quiet. Quiet makes a scared animal feel safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why sitting still and quiet helps a frightened animal feel safe._

_Hiccup comes out of the last line. Toothless is very close._  
_Hiccup lifts his hand slowly. Toothless wrinkles his nose._  
_Hiccup stops. Then he shuts his eyes and turns his face away._  
_He holds out his open hand, and waits._  
_Then Toothless pushes his nose into Hiccup’s hand._  
**Hiccup**: Oh!  
_You did not teach him. He found it himself._  

#### `a19-08-hand-grab`

_You remember Sable running off into the dark._  
_Hiccup comes out of the last line. Toothless is very close._  
_Hiccup lifts his hand slowly. Toothless wrinkles his nose._  
_Hiccup shuts his eyes and turns away. He holds out his open hand._  
_Your Nubbin darts forward. You slow it with a gentle hand._  
_It sits down by your hand, and waits with you._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): slowing down is kinder than grabbing  
> _You slowed your Nubbin, not grabbed it. Why is slow better?_  
> - ✅ Grabbing can frighten → Yes. A slow hand feels safe, but a grab can feel scary.
> - Grabbing is faster → It is faster, but it can frighten. Slow is kinder.
> - It does not matter → It matters! A slow, gentle hand helps us all feel safe.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about why slowing down is kinder than grabbing._

_Then Toothless pushes his nose into Hiccup’s hand._  
**Hiccup**: Oh!

> - Chase him → Chasing frightens animals. Giving space is kind.

> _H is for Hazel. Hazel starts with the sound huh._  
> _Which word starts with huh too?_  
> - ✅ Hat → Yes! Huh-huh-hat. Hazel and hat both start with huh.
> - Cat → Cat starts with kuh. Hazel starts with huh, like hat.
> - Dog → Dog starts with duh. Hazel starts with huh, like hat.
> _For grown-ups: Matched words by their first sound (h for Hazel and hat)._

_Your Nubbin pats the picture of the cave, gently._  

#### `a20-14-bowl-sat`

_You go nearer. Sigyn looks up._

**Sigyn**: You sat with the one who would not cry. I heard.

_For a moment, no drops fall on him at all._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): how help gives someone a rest

> - More work → You shared the work, so she could rest.
> _For grown-ups: Talked about how helping lets someone rest._

**Sigyn**: Thank you.  

#### `a20-14-bowl-walked`

> - The snow → Snow is cold. The glowing pebble is warmer.

#### `a20-16-edge-sat`

_From the edge of the wood you can see a very long way._

> **Lesson** (maths, ELOF: Mathematics Development, ask): near and far  
> _Which is near: the root in Nubbin’s arms, or the far-off ship?_  
> - ✅ The root → Yes! The root is near. The ship is far away.
> - The ship → The ship is far away. The root is near.
> _For grown-ups: Used near and far to compare distances._

#### `a20-17-ember`

#### `a20-17-complete-sat`

_The sun goes over the new land. The talk goes on, slow and easy._

> - “Do you want a hug?” → Asking about a hug is a kind thing to do.
> - “Take your time.” → “Take your time” is a kind thing to say.
> _For grown-ups: Named kind things to say to a sad friend._

#### `a22-01-lamp-flicker`

#### `a22-01-lamp-lit`

> - Yes, a lot → A flame wobbles when air moves. In still air, it stands tall.

_She squeezes your wrist, then lets go._

> - Go alone and say nothing → Going alone with a hurt wing is hard. It is wise to ask a friend.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about asking for help when we are hurt._

#### `a23-11-oasis-rafiki`

#### `a28-10-dance-done-freed`

_Behind Ananse, a small figure laughs into her free hand. It is Mmoatia._  
_She reaches up and tips his hat off._  
_The beans fly everywhere. His head is bare and shiny._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, ask): heat moves from hot things to cooler things  
> _Ananse’s head is hot from the beans. What would cool it down?_  
> - ✅ A cool, wet leaf. → Yes! Something cool takes the heat away.
> - More hot beans. → More hot beans would make it hotter! A cool leaf cools it.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that hot things warm what they touch, and that something cool takes heat away._

**Mmoatia**: A spider caught me once. Fair is fair.  
_Everybody laughs. Hers is the loudest._  

#### `a28-10-dance-done-sat`

_The hat comes off on its own. The beans fly everywhere._  
_Ananse’s head is bare and shiny. Everyone laughs, kindly._  
_Later, he hides in the long grass. Someone small sits down beside him._  
_It is Mmoatia. She says nothing._  
_She lays a cool, wet leaf on his hot head._  

> **Lesson** (science, ELOF: Scientific Reasoning, notice): a cool thing takes heat away from a hot thing  
> _The leaf is cool and his head is hot._  
> _Heat moves into the cool leaf._  
> _That is why a cool leaf makes his head feel better._  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that heat moves from a hot thing into a cool thing, so a cool leaf cools a hot head._

_Ananse says nothing too._  

#### `a28-12-tell-freed`

**You**: This one is about a fairy and a doll covered in gum.  
_You tell them about the odum tree, the yam and the thank-you._  
_You tell them how she stuck, and how the spider ran for rope._  
**You**: While he was gone, somebody worked one of her hands loose. Only one.  
**You**: She went up caught, but with a hand of her own.  
**You**: She used it later, on hats.  
_The children laugh. One claps with one hand on his knee._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, ask): retelling events in order: first, then, last  
> _What came first: the fairy ate the yam, or she got stuck?_  
> - ✅ She ate the yam. → Yes! First the yam. Then she got stuck.
> - She got stuck. → She ate the yam first. Then she got stuck.
> _For grown-ups: Retold a story in order, saying what happened first._

**Nana Ama**: Ha! That one is a clever one.  
**Nana Ama**: One hand free, and the story still holds. I will keep a piece.  
**Nana Ama**: The hand.

#### `a30-09-order-safe`
