#### `a30-10-grow-safe`

_Yossele goes down the lane, shutting every door with his hand flat on it._  
_Each time he moves he is a little taller._  
_The cobbles crack under his feet._  
_He drags Hannah’s cart across the end of the lane. Nobody in, nobody out._  
**Rivka**: He has shut the whole lane in! The rabbi does not know!  

> **Lesson** (social-studies, D2.Civ.8.K-2, ask): fairness: everyone should be free to come and go  
> _Is it fair to shut everyone inside their houses?_  
> - ✅ No, people should be free to come and go → Yes! Fair means everyone can go out and come home.
> - Yes, it is fair → Not fair! Everyone should be able to open their own door.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about fairness: everyone should be free to open their own door._


#### `a30-10-grow-help`

_Yossele does everything at once: sweeping, fetching water, chopping wood._

> **Lesson** (maths, K.OA.A.1, ask): adding to 3  
> _Two brooms snapped and one barrel split. How many things are broken?_  
> - ✅ 3 → Yes! Two and one make three.
> - 2 → Two brooms and one barrel. Two plus one is three.
> - 1 → Count them all: two brooms, one barrel. That is three.
> _For grown-ups: Added 2 and 1 to make 3 in a story about broken things._

**Dvora**: My pots! He is scrubbing them into pieces!

#### `a30-10-ember`

> - Less → A bright light shows more. A dim light shows less.

#### `a30-10-ember-settle`

> - More → Now it is soft and dim, so it gives less light.
> _For grown-ups: Compared a bright and a dim light._

#### `a31-13-rat-court`

_Right behind the rabbit goes the rat. It rode down on your Nubbin’s head!_  
**Rat**: Slow! Is that running?  
**Rat**: I have seen faster cheese!  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): animal sound words  
> **Grandmother**: Rats go squeak, squeak! Listen to the rat.  
> **Grandmother**: Squeak is a sound word. What other animal sounds do you know?  
> _For grown-ups: Used animal sound words (squeak) and thought of others._

_The lords chase it twice as far. That gives Xbalanque twice as long._  

#### `a31-13-bats-stay`

_In the night you wake. Xmucane is already sitting up, looking at the corn._  
_One ear has drooped. Its leaves hang down._  
**Xmucane**: No. No, no.  
_She does not touch it, and she does not cry. She just looks._  
_Your Nubbin climbs into your lap._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): calming a big worry with slow breaths and company  
> _Xmucane has a big worry in the night. What helps most?_  
> - ✅ Slow breaths, and a friend beside her → Yes. Slow breaths and company make a big worry smaller.
> - Shouting into the dark → Shouting can feel good, but slow breaths and a friend calm us down.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that slow breathing and company help with a big worry._

**Xmucane**: Sit with me. Do not say anything.  
_Near dawn, the drooping ear lifts, leaf by leaf._  
**Xmucane**: Oh.  

**Choices**

- **Put your hand on her arm.**
    - She puts her hand over yours and leaves it there.
- **Say nothing at all.**
    - You say nothing. It turns out to be right.

#### `a31-13-game-stay`

_The falcon comes at noon with its feathers every which way._  
**Falcon**: A bat took Hunahpu’s hat! Then a coati brought a squash!  
**Falcon**: And a rabbit ran off with the ball, and everyone chased it.  
**Falcon**: Everything is back where it belongs.  
**Xquic**: Everything?  
**Falcon**: Everything. Both twins are fine.  
**Falcon**: They splatted a squash on the lords!  
**Xmucane**: I saw his corn.  
_Xmucane makes tortillas, far too many, and gives the first to the falcon._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, RL.K.3, do): retell events in order  
> _(Tell the news in order: first the bat, next the coati, last the rabbit.)_  
> Check: `edu:order:story-events:3`
> _For grown-ups: Retold three events from the falcon’s news in order._


**Choices**

- **Give the falcon a seat by the fire.**
    - It sits by the fire with its tortilla. For a falcon, that is cosy.
- **Help with the tortillas.**
    - **Xmucane**: Yours are the wrong shape. Make more.

#### `a31-13-rat-coati-told`

**Falcon**: And a rat fetched the coati.  
**Falcon**: Somebody shared lunch with it once, and it does not forget.  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-1, notice): coatis have long ringed tails and long noses for sniffing out food  
> **Grandmother**: A coati is a real animal of the forest.  
> **Grandmother**: It has a long, stripy tail, and a long nose for sniffing out food.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that coatis have long noses for finding food and a long ringed tail._


#### `a31-13-rat-court-told`

**Falcon**: Oh, and a rat. It rode down in Hunahpu’s pocket.  
**Falcon**: It ran rings round the lords, shouting about cheese.  

> **Lesson** (science, 4-LS1-2, notice): rats have whiskers to feel their way in the dark  
> **Grandmother**: Rats have whiskers on their faces.  
> **Grandmother**: Whiskers help a rat feel its way in the dark.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that whiskers help rats feel their way in the dark._


#### `a31-14-oven-stay`

_The next day, the corn begins to dry from the tips down._  
**Xmucane**: No.  
_By evening both ears are dry, and they rattle when the door opens._  
_Xmucane cries. She does not hide it._  
_You pull your stool up beside hers, and stay._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): staying close to a friend who is crying  
> _Xmucane is crying. What can you do for a friend who is crying?_  
> - ✅ Sit with them and stay close → Yes. Staying close says: I am here.
> - Tell them to stop → Crying is allowed. Staying close helps more than saying stop.
> _For grown-ups: Learned that staying close helps a friend who is crying._

**Xquic**: They said: if it does both, we are being clever.  
**Xmucane**: I know what they said.  

**Choices**

- **Stay beside her.**
    - The fire goes down. You build it up, and you stay.
- **Sit with Xquic instead.**
    - Xquic leans her head on your shoulder. She is frightened too.

#### `a31-14-river-stay`

_One day. Two days._  
_Xmucane gets up each morning, looks, and sits down._  
_Three days. Four days._  
_You bring water and wood. Nobody speaks of the corn._  
_On day five your Nubbin turns your head towards the middle of the house._  
_A green shoot! Then another!_  
_Both ears, green._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.A.1, do): count the days to 5  
> _(Count the days on your fingers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. How many days?)_  
> Check: `edu:count:days:5`
> _For grown-ups: Counted five days on their fingers._

**Xmucane**: Oh, you clever, clever boys!  
**Xquic**: Five days! They always keep their promises.  

**Choices**

- **Laugh out loud.**
    - Your Nubbin runs round the corn three times for no reason.
- **Hug Xmucane.**
    - **Xmucane**: Get off. No.
    - **Xmucane**: Stay there a minute.

#### `a31-15-dancers-stay`

_The corn grows a leaf a day, and Xmucane talks to it._  

> **Lesson** (maths, K.CC.B.5, do): count to 3  
> _A leaf a day!_  
> _(Count three days of leaves: 1, 2, 3. How many leaves?)_  
> Check: `edu:count:leaves:3`
> _For grown-ups: Counted three leaves, one for each day._

**Xmucane**: Eat something. Tell your brother to wear a hat.  
_The falcon lands and looks pleased with itself._  
**Falcon**: Two ragged dancers in Xibalba! They make houses vanish and come back!  
**Xquic**: Two of them?  
**Falcon**: Two. With grins.  
**Xmucane**: Oh, I know those grins.  

**Choices**

- **Ask the falcon to go and look again.**
    - **Falcon**: I was going anyway. I want to see how it ends.
- **Tell the corn the news.**
    - Xmucane does not laugh at you. She adds a bit you forgot.

#### `a31-15-curtain-stay`

_You wait all day. Xquic grinds enough corn for twenty._  
_At dusk the falcon sits on the doorpost, quiet._  
**Falcon**: The lords asked for the wonder to be done to them.  
**Falcon**: The boys did it. The lords did not come back.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): mixed feelings: glad and sad together  
> _Xquic is quiet. She grew up down there, and she knows people there._  
> _How might she feel?_  
> - ✅ Mixed up: relieved and sad → Yes. She can feel relieved and sad together.
> - Only happy → Xquic may be glad it is over. She may be sad for people she knew too.
> _For grown-ups: Thought about how someone can feel mixed feelings at once._

_Outside, the wind goes over the corn on the hill._  
**Falcon**: The rest begged. The boys said: mercy, yes.  
**Falcon**: Greatness, no.  
**Xmucane**: Good boys. Hard, but good.  

**Choices**

- **Look at Xquic.**
    - Xquic is very still. She grew up down there.
- **Look at the corn.**
    - Green and tall. Waiting, like you.

#### `a31-margin-hazel`

_Nova’s atlas lies open at the hall of Xibalba. Two seats are empty._  
_In the margin, in faint pencil, is a note. You know the hand._  

> **Lesson** (literacy, ELOF: Language and Communication, notice): a margin is the empty edge of a page, where readers write notes  
> **Grandmother**: The margin is the empty edge of a page.  
> **Grandmother**: People write little notes there, like a message to the next reader.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the margin of a page is where readers write notes._

_“Two boys who won by being cheeky to grumpy lords. My kind of boys.”_  
_Your Nubbin looks at you, asking if it may laugh. It may._  

#### `a31-16-father-stay`

_The corn is taller than the stools now._  
_The falcon lands on Xmucane’s knee, which it has never done before._  
**Falcon**: They are at the ballcourt, at their father’s place.  
**Falcon**: They are telling him every point.  
**Xmucane**: He always liked to hear the score.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Social and Emotional Development, notice): remembering small things someone liked keeps them close  
> **Grandmother**: Xmucane remembers that her son liked to hear the score.  
> **Grandmother**: When we remember little things someone liked, they stay close in our hearts.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that remembering small things someone liked keeps them close._

**Falcon**: They told him he will be remembered. Called first, before anyone.  
**Xmucane**: Good. That is right.  
_She takes your hand without looking._  
**Xmucane**: Come and sit in the door. It will be morning soon.  

**Choices**

- **Sit in the doorway with her.**
    - The doorstep is still warm. The dark goes on a while longer.
- **Bring your Nubbin out too.**
    - It sits between you, facing east, as if it knows something.

#### `a31-16-rise-stay`

_From Xmucane’s doorway you see dark mountains, with a grey line on top._  
_Behind you, the corn stands up green in the dark._  
_Two lights come up, far away, and climb. One becomes the Sun._  
_The other becomes the Moon._  
**Grandmother**: My gran told me which one is which. One day I will tell you.  
_After them come four hundred little lights._  
_The atlas says: now they are the stars._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, do): the Sun rises in the east  
> **Grandmother**: The Sun comes up in the east. That is where the day begins.  
> _(Point to where the sun comes up in the picture. That is east!)_  
> Check: `edu:point:east:sunrise`
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Sun rises in the east, and pointed to it._

_The first sunlight comes over the mountain and through the door._  
**Xmucane**: There they are. There they both are.  

**Choices**

- **Wave.**
    - After a moment Xmucane waves too, as if nobody is watching.
- **Stay still under her hand.**
    - You do not move, and neither does she. The sun gets on with it.

#### `a31-16-complete-stay`

**Xmucane**: You watched the corn with me. That is the hard part.  
**Xmucane**: The boys only had to be clever.  
_She takes a green stone on a cord from round her own neck._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, notice): waiting with someone is a gift  
> **Grandmother**: Waiting with someone is a big gift.  
> **Grandmother**: You cannot see it, but they can feel it.  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that waiting with someone is a kind gift._

_She ties it on your Nubbin._  
**Xmucane**: For sitting up. Nobody gives you anything for sitting up.  
**Xmucane**: They should.  
_The page goes soft round the edges, like a kitchen full of smoke._  

#### `a31-16-ribbons`

_For a moment the smoke parts, and you are back in the kitchen._  
**Granddaughter**: Look! Two colours sewn down the middle!  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, ask): name the colour in the middle  
> _The ribbon is gold on one side and silver on the other._  
> _What colour is sewn down the middle?_  
> - ✅ Green → Yes! Green stitches join the gold and the silver.
> - Red → Look again: gold, green, silver. Green is down the middle.
> _For grown-ups: Looked closely at a ribbon and named its colours._

**Grandmother**: Somebody sewed that very carefully.  
_Then the smoke closes, and you are back at sunrise._  

#### `a31-17-complete-stay`

_The smoke rises. You are back at your own table, with the atlas open._  
_A black rubber ball is on the floor. Your Nubbin sits on it._  
_Caught in the atlas spine is an ear of corn, still green._  
_It is soft, and it smells like a field after rain._  

> **Lesson** (science, 3-LS1-1, notice): green corn is still growing; later it turns golden and dry, and its seeds can grow again  
> **Grandmother**: Green corn is still growing.  
> **Grandmother**: Later it turns golden and dry. Its seeds can grow into new plants!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that green corn is still growing and that its dry seeds can grow into new plants._

_You hang it from the middle beam of the cottage._  
_Out by the pond, the Nubbins come to look at the new ball._  
_Nobody uses hands._  

#### `a31-grove-byte`

_Byte is by the pond, watching your Nubbin play hip-ball. Its ribbons flap._  
_The sun is going down behind the hill._  
_On the other side, the moon is already up._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, notice): the Moon can be seen in the daytime, so the Sun and Moon can share the sky  
> **Byte**: The Sun and the Moon can be in the sky together.  
> **Byte**: Sometimes you can see a pale Moon in the daytime. Look up and see!  
> _For grown-ups: Learned that the Moon can be seen in the daytime, so the Sun and Moon can share the sky._

**Byte**: Same sky. It was always the same sky.  
**Byte**: I would like that read into the record.  
_He goes back to his notebook._  

#### `pa1-01-clank`

_Clank sits on top of the cabinet. His legs dangle over the screen._  
**Clank**: Announcement: I am the lookout. Lookouts sit on top. I am on top.  
**Pixel**: I said lookouts sit still.  
**Clank**: I am sitting very still. Look how still. The stillest ever.  

> **Lesson** (sel, ELOF: Approaches to Learning, ask): listening to what was asked  
> **Pixel**: I asked Clank to sit still. His legs are swinging. Is he sitting still?  
> - ✅ Not quite! His legs are moving → Right. Still means all of you. Legs too, Clank.
> - Yes, very still → Look at those legs swing! Still means all of you. Legs too.
> _For grown-ups: Your child checked whether an instruction was really followed._

_His legs keep swinging. Bonk. Bonk. One heel hits the screen._  

#### `pa1-17-chao-locked`

_Chaos looks round for the Chao. None on the roofs. None in the streets._  
_Oh! The garden. The gate. The little key you turned._  
**You**: They’re still in there.  
_You wade back through the hotel to the garden. The gate is still shut._  
_The Chao sit up in the trees, wet and very quiet. All safe._  
**Pixel**: Safe isn’t the same as well, is it.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Social awareness, ask): safe and well are different  
> **Pixel**: The Chao were safe, but alone and scared. Is that the same as well?  
> - ✅ No, well means happy too → Yes. Safe is good. Well is safe AND happy, with friends.
> - Yes, same thing → Nearly. Safe is good. Well is safe AND happy, with friends.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about the difference between safe and well._

_You turn the key. Your Nubbin goes in first, and they all climb down._  
_You lead them across the square to the puddle._  
_Chaos looks at them. Its glow goes still, and soft, and warm._  

#### `pa1-18-stood`

**Tikal**: You stood beside me on the steps. In front of all of them.  
**Tikal**: It didn’t change anything. It still mattered.  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): standing by a friend  
> **Tikal**: Standing beside me changed nothing, but it mattered. Why?  
> - ✅ I wasn’t alone → Yes. Being with someone matters, even when it can’t fix things.
> - It didn’t matter → It did! Being with someone matters, even when it can’t fix things.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that standing by a friend matters._

_She squeezes your hand once. It is warm, though it’s made of light._  

#### `pa1-18-cinder-forgiven`

**You**: She was called Cinder. She loved them, and held on too tight.  
**You**: At the end, somebody went up the mountain and found her. She was forgiven.  
_Tikal smiles, slowly, like the sun after rain._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Relationship skills, ask): forgiving  
> _Cinder was forgiven. What does “forgive” mean?_  
> - ✅ To stop being cross and let it go → Yes. Forgiving means letting the cross feeling go. Then everyone can rest.
> - To forget everything → Not forget. Forgiving means letting the cross feeling go. Then everyone can rest.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned what forgiving means._

**Tikal**: Forgiven. Oh, I’m glad.  
**Tikal**: Then she can rest. That’s all the fierce ones want, in the end.  

#### `pa1-18-cinder-remembered`

**You**: She was called Cinder. She held on too tight.  
**You**: We don’t forgive all of it. But we remember ours.  
**Tikal**: Remember. Yes. That’s a kind of keeping too.  
_Your Nubbin finds a red petal from home. It gives it to a Chao._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): colours: red  
> _The petal is red. Can you find something red near you? (Look around together.)_  
> - ✅ I found one! → Red! Like the petal from the hill. Well spotted.
> - Nothing red here → Look again: a book, a cup, a sock? Red is everywhere once you look.
> _For grown-ups: Your child found the colour red._

_The Chao holds the petal up to the light. Its ball becomes a heart._  

#### `pa1-18-last-open-stood`

_The screen shows one last picture: the hotel roof at sunset._  

> **Lesson** (science, 1-ESS1-1, ask): sunset  
> _It is sunset. Where is the sun going?_  
> - ✅ Down, and night comes → Yes! At sunset the sun goes down, and night comes. Morning brings it back.
> - Up → Up is sunrise, in the morning. At sunset it goes down, and night comes.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned what happens at sunset._

_A row of Chao sits along the edge, legs dangling._  
_In one corner, two tiny lights, pink and green, and a little square person._  
**Pixel**: That’s you. It put you in the ending!  

#### `pa1-18-last-open`

_The screen shows one last picture: the hotel roof at sunset._  
_A row of Chao sits along the edge, legs dangling._  
_In one corner, two tiny lights, pink and green, float away side by side._  

> **Lesson** (art, ELOF: Perceptual, Motor, and Physical Development, ask): mixing colours: pink and green  
> _Two lights: one pink, one green. Which one is Tikal?_  
> - ✅ Pink → Yes! Tikal is the pink light. Chaos glows green.
> - Green → Green is Chaos. Tikal is the pink light.
> _For grown-ups: Your child matched colours to characters._

**Pixel**: Every one of them out, and up. Good.  

#### `pa1-18-last-locked-stood`

_The screen shows one last picture: the garden, with its gate wide open._  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Responsible decision-making, ask): open means free to choose  
> **Pixel**: The gate is open now. Why is an open gate nicer for the Chao?  
> - ✅ They can come and go as they like → Yes. Open means they can choose: in, or out. That feels good.
> - It isn’t nicer → It is! Open means they can choose: in, or out. That feels good.
> _For grown-ups: Your child thought about why an open gate is kinder._

_A Chao swings on the gate. Two lights float above the palm tree._  
_Beside them, a little square person who looks a lot like you._  
**Pixel**: Open. They’ve drawn it open. And you’re in it, look.  

#### `pa1-18-last-locked`

_The screen shows one last picture: the garden, with its gate wide open._  
_A Chao swings on the gate, back and forth. Creak, creak._  
_Two lights, pink and green, float up through the glass roof and away._  
**Pixel**: Open. Next time, we leave it open from the start. Deal?  

> **Lesson** (sel, CASEL: Self-management, ask): learning for next time  
> **Pixel**: Next time, we leave it open. Is it all right to do better?  
> - ✅ Yes, that’s how we learn → Yes. Nobody gets it all right first go. We learn, and do better.
> - No, you should never get it wrong → Everyone gets things wrong sometimes. We learn, and do better.
> _For grown-ups: Your child learned that doing better next time is how we learn._
